title: Microplastic removal using upcycled magnetic biochar with experimental data-driven modelling and interpretable machine learning algorithms
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution poses a persistent environmental challenge, and the disposal of spent adsorbents after treatment can generate additional waste. This study developed a circular remediation strategy by upcycling regenerated microplastic-spent adsorbents into magnetic carbon material (MCM) for the removal of polystyrene (PS) microplastics, coupled with interpretable machine learning (ML). Magnetic modification enhanced the surface area and pore characteristics of the material, enabling MCM to achieve approximately 90% PS removal, substantially outperforming unmodified carbon material.

abstract: Flow-accelerated corrosion (FAC) is a major degradation mechanism in piping systems and is significant in fittings such as elbows, where local hydrodynamic conditions vary substantially. abstract: Historical archaeology lies at the intersection of the written word, the spoken word, and material things, yet each dataset documents the past unevenly. abstract: Environmental management has historically depended on sparse field sampling, periodic reporting, and slow regulatory feedback, leaving decision-makers to act on incomplete, delayed, and coarse information in space and time. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a central arena of great-power competition, yet research on how authoritarian regimes construct the related discourses and legitimize their governance of AI has been limited. This study examines how China creates that narrative for international audiences and adapts when an external technological shock unsettles its claims. abstract: Sea ice mechanical properties govern dynamical processes spanning scales from meters to several hundred kilometers. These micro-scale needle arrays can painlessly penetrate the outer skin layer to access interstitial fluid, enabling continuous and real-time monitoring of key biochemical markers such as glucose, metabolites, and disease-related biomarkers. title: Predicting slope instabilities in Salvador, Brazil, using machine learning and georeferenced data
abstract: Municipalities worldwide struggle with slope instability, a particularly pressing issue in cities such as Salvador, Brazil, where rugged terrain, escarpments, and complex geology create a high risk of instability. The complexity of the problem is evident in the variability of terrain properties, the bedrock’s inherited structural features, and anthropogenic action. This range of variables makes it well-suited to machine learning (ML) approaches for instability prediction. abstract: Large parts of the Arctic sea ice form during the winter and melt during the summer. Multi-year ice (MYI) is different: it survives the summer and can last for years. abstract: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. title: Metaverse and AI Open Innovation for Inclusive Sustainable Development: A Knowledge‐Based Perspective
abstract: Sustainable development requires deeper collaboration and innovation than traditional digital tools can offer. This study examines how metaverse platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) enhance knowledge‐based processes to support sustainability outcomes across economic, social, environmental, and technological areas. abstract: La creciente disponibilidad de datos y el desarrollo de técnicas de machine learning están ampliando las posibilidades de la prevención de riesgos laborales, lo que permite avanzar desde un enfoque fundamentalmente reactivo hacia una prevención anticipatoria. abstract: Coastal flood forecasting systems increasingly need to provide not only point-based water-level predictions, but also probabilistic flood extents and impact-relevant information at operational time scales. abstract: Tropical reefs are among the most biodiverse and threatened marine ecosystems and face both local and global stressors. Image-based surveys are increasingly used in reef ecology because they enable rapid data acquisition and storage. abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of complex chemical reactors, especially localized engineering-critical points or regions, remains challenging in process engineering. Although data-driven methods offer computational advantages, the incorporation of domain-specific physical knowledge can further enhance their predictive performance. title: Greenland and Antarctica Dominate Recent Acceleration in Global Mean Sea Level Rise: 1993–2023
abstract: Global mean sea level (GMSL) rise has accelerated over the last three decades, with satellite altimetry indicating an acceleration of 0.07 ± 0.03 mm/yr 2 over 1993–2023. However, the specific contributions of Greenland and Antarctica to this acceleration budget have remained insufficiently quantified. We extend satellite gravimetry estimates of Greenland and Antarctica ice mass changes back to 1993, enabling a comprehensive 31‐year assessment of their contributions to GMSL acceleration and providing an independent record for cross‐validation with other observational and modeling data sets. abstract: Background Stock enhancement has become a widely adopted fisheries management strategy to mitigate ongoing declines in marine fishery resources. The Beibu Gulf is an important region for marine stock enhancement in China, with Acanthopagrus latus (yellowfin seabream) being one of the principal target species. This recreationally, commercially, and ecologically important sparid fish forms a genetically distinct population in the Beibu Gulf but has experienced substantial population declines in recent decades, prompting extensive enhancement efforts. abstract: Treasure Island, a century-old artificial landmass in San Francisco Bay, exemplifies the long-term climate vulnerabilities of reclaimed coastal lands under accelerating sea-level rise. Here we show, using historical records, multi-decadal satellite interferometric synthetic aperture radar, three-dimensional geomechanical modeling, and deep learning projections, that the island is undergoing persistent subsidence (5–11 mm yr −1 ) and lateral sliding (up to 6 mm yr −1 ) at its northwest corner. title: Geoheritage, Sedimentary Controls and Shoreline Change in the Somone Lagoon–Estuary Complex (Senegal): Remote-Sensing and Machine-Learning Projections to 2050
abstract: Lagoon–estuary complexes are dynamic sedimentary archives in which shoreline mobility and human pressure affect both coastal function and geoheritage. We integrate 14 sediment cores, a quantitative assessment of seven geosites (Brilha method), eight Landsat and Sentinel-2 shorelines (1984–2025) analyzed with the Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS), and a Gradient Boosting machine-learning model for the Somone lagoon–estuary complex, Senegal. title: Climate-induced sea-level rise amplifies coastal vulnerability across West and Central Africa
abstract: Coastal Vulnerability Indices are widely applied to identify erosion, flooding, and risk hotspots, yet they are typically formulated as static metrics that overlook temporal variability and limit their utility for anticipatory risk management. Here, we demonstrate that a temporally resolved and impact-validated Coastal Vulnerability Index captures seasonal, interannual, and long-term variability in coastal risk along the West and Central African coasts from 1993 to 2020. abstract: Subsurface marine heatwaves (MHWs) represent hidden thermal extremes that can strongly impact marine ecosystems, particularly when they are large-scale and long-lasting. Although they evolve across time and space, their vertical structure and evolution remain poorly understood because of sparse long-record subsurface observations and the limited application of globally consistent frameworks to characterize them. abstract: This study examines the strengthening of personal data protection and human rights safeguards in Southeast Asia amid accelerating digitalisation, cross-border data flows, and emerging data-driven technologies. Employing a non-empirical legal research design, the study applies normative, doctrinal, and comparative legal approaches to ASEAN instruments and national regulatory frameworks in Indonesia, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar. abstract: Assessing groundwater quality is essential for sustainable water resource management in arid regions, where hydrochemical processes are complex and monitoring resources are often limited. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with transformer-based self-attention mechanisms for multiclass water quality index (WQI) classification. Marine Natural Products for Cancer Therapy: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation
abstract: Cancer continues to impose a major global health burden. Conventional therapies often show poor selectivity, off-target toxicity, and drug resistance, creating an urgent need for new agents. The marine environment covers roughly 71% of Earth’s surface and has fostered metabolites of unparalleled chemical diversity, making the ocean a vital source for anticancer drug discovery. title: Compound environmental events in Washington coastal waters from high-resolution downscaled projections
abstract: Coastal temperate upwelling ecosystems face increasingly frequent and persistent environmental extremes including warming, deoxygenation, and acidification, yet integrated regional assessments of future change remain limited. Here we apply high-resolution statistically downscaled CMIP6 projections (SSP2-4.5, 2017–2060) to Washington coastal waters, combining threshold-based detection to characterize individual and compound event dynamics including ocean warming (surface/bottom marine heatwaves (SHW/BHW)), deoxygenation (hypoxia), and ocean acidification (OA). title: Waterworld: increasing coastal urban waterways and the dilemmas for ecology and society
abstract: Coastal urban expansion has transformed shorelines worldwide, replacing wetlands and floodplains with engineered residential waterways. The rapid proliferation of artificial canals and islands, from Palm Islands in the United Arab Emirates to China's coastal megaprojects, has created a global form of “ocean sprawl”, yet its ecological consequences remain largely unquantified. title: Literature review of wildlife disease surveillance capacity in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations region: status, gaps, and recommendations for national and regional strengthening
abstract: Southeast Asia is a globally recognized hotspot for emerging infectious diseases, yet wildlife disease surveillance (WDS) across the region remains fragmented, under-resourced, and poorly characterized. This review used domains adapted from a Needs Assessment Tool (NAT) for national wildlife health programs as an organizing framework to synthesize evidence from peer-reviewed literature, World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) country profiles and surveillance surveys, and regional network reports to analyze WDS capacity in the ASEAN region. abstract: In light of the technological advancements witnessed worldwide and the accompanying expansion in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies across various fields, numerous legal challenges have emerged, particularly those concerning the transboundary effects of these technologies and the potential risks their use may pose to human rights and international peace and security. title: Bridging the hearing data gap in the endangered Australian sea lion (Neophoca cinerea) through biomechanical modelling
abstract: The endangered Australian sea lion ( Neophoca cinerea ) divides its functional ecology between land (for mating and pup-rearing) and sea (for foraging). Given this amphibious lifestyle, it is susceptible to natural and anthropogenic sound exposure in both air and water. Hearing data for the species are limited to a small sample size (two individuals) of behavioural measurements in air at only a few frequencies, and no underwater hearing thresholds are currently available. title: Earth observations for monitoring wildfire impacts on coastal water quality
abstract: Nearly four billion people depend on coastal ecosystems, where the growing influence of wildfire remains an understudied threat to ecosystem health. Wildfires alter watershed hydrology, mobilizing sediments, nutrients, and contaminants that degrade coastal water quality and disrupt marine habitats long after fires are extinguished. Prior work documents wildfire effects on watershed hydrology and inland water quality, but few studies address what satellites can and cannot observe with respect to the wildfire-to-coast pathway. title: A 1951–1998 Lutao coral Pb isotope record reveals site-specific, marine-integrated anthropogenic Pb pollution signals in the Northwest Pacific
abstract: Coral lead (Pb) isotope records provide multi-decadal perspectives on marine Pb histories, but how individual records represent regional isotope histories remains an important interpretive question. We present a 1951–1998 Pb isotope record from a Porites coral at Lutao, southeast of Taiwan, and compare it with published records from Dongsha and Ogasawara in the Northwest Pacific. title: Impacts of the Boreal Summer Intraseasonal Oscillation on marine heatwaves in the Taiwan Strait
abstract: The Taiwan Strait is a hotspot for frequent and intense marine heatwaves (MHWs) in summer, with severe impacts on local marine ecosystems, yet their underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Recent studies have documented the drivers of MHWs from interannual timescales to long-term changes, while the role of intraseasonal variability is still underexplored. The Boreal Summer Intraseasonal Oscillation (BSISO) is a prominent component of the atmospheric intraseasonal oscillation (ISO) over the tropical Indo-Pacific Ocean. abstract: Underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) are severely affected by propagation delay, limited bandwidth, and constrained node energy. This work presents EXTREPSO, a machine learning framework that combines an Extra Trees Regressor with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for offline hyperparameter tuning of a hop-level energy-efficiency predictor. title: Quantifying Total Shrimp Pond Coverage Using Remote Sensing and a Machine Learning Algorithm: A Case Study in the Ecuadorian Coast
abstract: Remote sensing and machine learning have emerged as powerful tools for monitoring rapid land‐use changes in coastal ecosystems. However, accurately quantifying the spatial extent and temporal dynamics of shrimp aquaculture remains challenging, particularly in regions with complex coastal landscapes such as the Ecuadorian coast. This study aims to develop and apply a reproducible computational workflow to automatically detect and map shrimp ponds using multispectral Sentinel‐2 imagery and machine learning techniques. title: Effect of Kinesthetic Learning Strategies on Promoting Chinese Traditional Culture Literacy of Fifth-Grade Students
abstract: Background and Aims: In recent years, primary school Chinese language classrooms across the country have exhibited issues such as monotonous teaching methods and low student engagement in traditional culture education. Classical Chinese reading classes remain largely teacher-centered, emphasizing content explanation over active engagement, which may limit students’ participation and motivation to learn. abstract: Hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) are Critically Endangered sea turtles generally associated with coral reef systems, foraging primarily on sponges or macroalgaes. Globally, hawksbills have occasionally been documented in seagrass meadows, but there is no specific research showing hawksbills using seagrass meadows as a foraging ground. This study is based in the Republic of Maldives where there has been increased observations of hawksbills in peripheral seagrass habitats including direct observation of foraging behavior. title: Observational data and neural network-accelerated modelling provide valuable insights for glacier thickness reconstruction in High Mountain Asia
abstract: Mountain glaciers provide an irreplaceable water resource in High Mountain Asia, with a significant proportion of water input to rivers coming from glacial meltwater. However, the volume of water held in these glaciers and their evolution over the coming decades is subject to great uncertainty. title: Trace-level determination of multiclass pharmaceuticals in coastal seawater by SPE-UHPLC-MS/MS: Method validation and application to Mediterranean waters
abstract: Pharmaceutical residues in coastal waters are of increasing environmental and regulatory concern, yet their determination remains challenging because of their low concentrations, physicochemical diversity, and matrix complexity. In this study, a solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (SPE-UHPLC-MS/MS) method was developed and validated for the determination of 16 pharmaceuticals across different therapeutic classes in coastal seawater. abstract: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. abstract: This paper proposes a global scour detection framework for monopile foundations across offshore wind farms (OWFs) using vibration data acquired from a single accelerometer mounted on the turbine tower. The proposed framework is designed to address the real-world complexity and heterogeneity of offshore wind systems operating under diverse environmental, geotechnical, and structural conditions across multiple sites. title: Developing and testing an operational workflow for underwater robotic recovery of abandoned, lost, or otherwise discarded fishing nets
abstract: Abandoned, lost or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) has a potential to adversely affect marine fauna and ecosystems, entangling and killing numerous species and causing marine pollution. Traditional ALDFG removal methods, often including diving or creeping, are labour-intensive, time-consuming, costly, and, in the case of diving, may be hazardous due to poor visibility, low temperatures, strong currents, and dangers of entanglement. abstract: Mangrove-fringed coastal areas provide habitat and sediment regulation ecosystem services, increasingly affected by land-use change. title: Machine learning insights into environmental and biological triggers of fumonisin outbreaks in Texas corn
abstract: Contamination of corn with fumonisin mycotoxins (FUM) caused by the fungus Fusarium verticillioides is a recurrent issue in Texas corn production that results in significant economic losses for corn producers. Both prediction and management of FUM outbreaks are challenging due to a lack of information regarding region-specific environmental and biological drivers of contamination. abstract: Turbidites generated by large earthquakes and other geological events are commonly preserved in small, topographically confined basins along active continental margins. Reconstructing flow conditions from these deposits is essential for assessing past hazards; however, existing inverse models have been validated only for unconfined settings, and their applicability to confined basins remains unclear. abstract: Artificial intelligence governance frameworks have proliferated globally, yet three critical gaps persist: the principles-to-practice gap, where ethical guidelines remain abstract without measurable implementation mechanisms; the consumer-centric gap, where frameworks are designed primarily from regulator and developer perspectives while consumers account for only 2.2 percent of the actors represented in AI governance scholarship; and the developing country gap, where sophisticated models presuppose institutional capacities absent in emerging economies. abstract: Tafel polarization analysis can be used to teach corrosion kinetics in upper-division physical chemistry and materials science laboratories, but implementing it through fixed procedures and automated fitting may limit students’ engagement with the underlying electrochemical principles. This work describes a context-based electrochemistry laboratory that integrates a large language model (LLM) as an analytical scaffold rather than a source of ready-made answers. abstract: Ti-6Al-4V is widely employed for use in aerospace, biomedicine and marine engineering applications. abstract: Florida's subtropical climate and diverse coastal habitats support an exceptionally high level of biological diversity. Alien species may be categorized as non-native or invasive, depending on their ecological impacts (Colautti and Maclsaac, 2004;Mooney and Cleland, 2001;National Park Service, n.d.;Schlaepfer et al., 2011). title: Long-term limits on maximum ice sheet thickness around central Antarctic Peninsula nunataks
abstract: Understanding past ice sheet sensitivity to long-term climate cycles is essential to predict future sea-level rise. The Antarctic Peninsula Ice Sheet (APIS) is changing rapidly in one of Antarctica’s fastest warming regions. However, APIS thickness changes are poorly understood because there are limited terrestrial records of deglaciation. abstract: Farmer Producer Organizations are widely promoted to integrate small and marginal farmers into markets, yet the factors that sustain member satisfaction remain unclear. abstract: Accurate estimation of the compression index Cc is important for assessing the settlement behavior of marine clay. abstract: This paper considers the problem of detecting and classifying ground objects in radar images using deep learning methods. The study compares two architectures: a single-stage architecture based on the YOLO detector and a two-stage architecture combining YOLO with an additional classifier. abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have been widely studied because of their data collection and observation across diverse applications. However, the restricted energy resources of sensor nodes (SNs) remain a major challenge for prolonging the network lifetime. abstract: A previsão de secas evoluiu significativamente com a integração de técnicas de aprendizado de máquina (AM), oferecendo maior acurácia e antecedência para sistemas de alerta precoce. abstract: Marine oil spill segmentation using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is hindered by blurred spill boundaries, large variations in target scales, and false positives induced by oceanic look-alike features. abstract: Benthic imagery constitutes a primary data source for studying seafloor habitats, providing rich visual information essential for ecological assessment and marine ecosystem monitoring. abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being rapidly adopted in education, prompting growing interest in its application to Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). abstract: Alpha-thalassemia is a genetically heterogeneous hemoglobinopathy caused by reduced or absent α-globin chain production. Its phenotypic presentation may overlap with other microcytic disorders, and routine hematological parameters alone may not reliably permit identification of the underlying α-globin genotype. abstract: La inteligencia artificial está transformando la gestión educativa, aunque persiste escasa claridad sobre su aporte al fortalecimiento del liderazgo directivo, particularmente en contextos como el ecuatoriano. title: Growth and internationalization of artificial intelligence and biotechnology startups in Argentina: modalities, motivations, and patterns
abstract: En este estudio se analiza la expansión internacional temprana de startups argentinas de inteligencia artificial (IA) y biotecnología, tanto por la apertura de filiales en el exterior como la migración de la sede legal. A partir de una base de datos de 172 startups y de estudios de caso cualitativos, se observa que la internacionalización es frecuente incluso en etapas tempranas: el 37% de las startups de IA y el 29% de las biotecnológicas tienen presencia internacional. title: Machine-learning reconstruction of ERA5-Land temperature at local administrative units
abstract: Extreme climate impacts are often managed at neighborhood and local administrative scales, yet reanalysis products remain spatially coarse and are not aligned with administrative boundaries such as Census Block Groups (CBGs). This study develops a machine-learning-based change-of-support reconstruction workflow to translate hourly ERA5-Land 2-m air temperature (2000–2024) from its native approximately 9-km grid to CBG areal support across Maryland. title: Present and future of ENSO impacts on the canary current ecosystem
abstract: The Canary Current System (CCS), one of the world's major Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems, sustains highly productive marine ecosystems whose variability is strongly controlled by large-scale climate forcing. Although the influence of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) on the present-day CCS has been documented, it remains unclear how this teleconnection may evolve under anthropogenic climate change. title: Spatial patterns of the bird-related sentiment index and its nonlinear environmental associations: Evidence from social media and explainable machine learning
abstract: As cities become denser and more artificial, encounters with birds are closely tied to how residents perceive urban nature. However, evidence on the spatial patterns and environmental correlates of bird-related emotions remains limited. Taking Shanghai as a case study, this study cleaned 4,142 bird-related Weibo check-in comments from 2022 to 2024. A deep-learning sentiment model was used to construct a bird-related sentiment index, which was linked to 500 m × 500 m grids and examined with climatic, ecological, landscape, and human-activity indicators. title: How can GRACE satellite observations be downscaled into fine-scale groundwater anomalies? A hybrid machine learning and uncertainty quantification framework
abstract: The Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) missions provide terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) at resolutions too coarse for local groundwater assessment. We developed a two-stage framework to downscale monthly GRACE/GRACE-FO TWSA from 0.5° to 0.01° over Rachna Doab, Pakistan, for 2002-2024. Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL) bridged the mission gap. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) first refined TWSA to 0.1°, followed by a feed-forward neural network (FNN) at 0.01°. title: Enhanced skin tone and blood estimation through AI-enabled upscaling of discrete reflectance spectra
abstract: Objective quantification of epidermal melanin content and dermal blood volume is crucial for equitable applications in dermatology and in the evaluation and engineering of optical devices, such as pulse oximeters, where variable amounts of melanin may introduce inaccuracies. Here, we demonstrate a method leveraging diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and a machine-learning framework using fully connected neural networks (FCNNs) to non-invasively estimate melanin and blood indices from sparse data through spectral upscaling. title: Re-examining the relationship between artificial intelligence development and urban per capita carbon emissions within a government–market–public framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) development may be associated with urban emissions through technological applications and interactions among government, market, and public actors, yet city-level evidence remains limited. This study develops a government–market–public (GMP) framework using panel data for 279 Chinese cities from 2013 to 2021. A city-level AI development index combines government policy support, AI-related firms and patents, and public attention. title: Forecasting-enabled microgrid optimization for adaptive renewable energy planning in remote coastal communities
abstract: Remote coastal communities in the Sundarbans of Bangladesh depend on an unreliable distribution grid, yet microgrid planning studies for such sites usually treat demand and renewable generation as fixed inputs and rarely show what forecast quality means for operation. This study examines whether a grid-connected hybrid microgrid can be both least-cost and resilient for 150 households and three community buildings in Dhangmari, and what operational value hourly forecasting adds to such a design. abstract: Laterite mining stands out as a relevant, but understudied, form of disturbance in the coastal hinterland of Karnataka, taking place in iron- and aluminum-rich zones in fragile ecosystems as well as agricultural land. abstract: Overtourism is a pressing issue that has intensified the need to integrate sustainability values into tourism. abstract: This study investigates whether Chinese listed firms’ financial transparency improves with AI. Our main AI measure is AI-related disclosure intensity based on annual report text. abstract: Rapid urbanization in tropical coastal cities has intensified urban heat island effects; however, seasonal dynamics of urban thermal ecological quality and their conditioning mechanisms remain insufficiently explored in South Asian metropolitan environments. This study develops a seasonal explainable framework to predict urban thermal field variance index (UTFVI), identify dominant conditioning factors, and evaluate LULC-specific thermal vulnerability in Chattogram Metropolitan Area (CTGM), Bangladesh, during 2019, 2022 and 2025. abstract: Tiger sharks ( Galeocerdo cuvier ) are apex predators with well-established ecological roles in tropical and subtropical marine ecosystems, yet their spatial ecology in the eastern Atlantic remains almost entirely unresolved. Here we provide the first systematic, comprehensive characterisation of tiger shark habitat use around Boa Vista Island, which hosts one of the Atlantic’s largest loggerhead turtle nesting aggregations, within the Cabo Verde archipelago, a priority area for elasmobranch conservation. abstract: The underwater environment presents unique challenges for robotic vision due to low light conditions and medium interference, which often result in images with low contrast and indistinct textures. abstract: Floods represent a recurrent natural hazard in Mediterranean coastal environments, driven by climate variability, low-lying topography, and land-use change. This study proposes a multi-temporal flood monitoring and susceptibility framework using Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for the Sebkhet Ariana coastal wetland, Tunisia. abstract: Coastal and marine engineering plays a critical role in the blue economy. abstract: The basking shark, Cetorhinus maximus (Gunnerus, 1765), is a large, filter-feeding species in the monotypic family Cetorhinidae and is widely distributed in warm-temperate to cold-temperate waters of the world’s oceans. Here we report an adult male specimen incidentally caught by a commercial bottom trawler in the northern East China Sea (31°50'N; 126°41'E) on 10 February 2025. abstract: Underwater soft robots are promising for safely and adaptively interaction with delicate marine life and fragile objects. Different from previous studies on WCIs, WCIs are examined in shallow and intermediate water depths in addition to deep water. The proximity of the storm track to the coastline also limits the fetch. abstract: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) are an escalating threat to freshwater ecosystems, urban water infrastructure, and public health, particularly in densely populated urban water bodies such as Bellandur Lake. title: Deep learning-based DDoS detection with error-space fidelity learning for cross-distribution generalization
abstract: Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks pose a significant challenge to intrusion detection systems because network traffic characteristics and attack behaviors can change across deployment environments. Conventional deep learning-based DDoS detection methods are commonly evaluated under closed-world assumptions, where training and testing data follow similar distributions, which may overestimate real-world generalization. To address this limitation, this study proposes an error-space fidelity learning framework for evaluating DDoS detector reliability under cross-distribution conditions.

title: Sky-lit stage: lunar and solar rhythms shape the acoustic behaviour of marine mammals and fish
abstract: Rhythmic lunar and solar cycles are well recognised to influence the biology, behaviour, physiology, and ecological adaptations of many terrestrial organisms, yet their effects on marine organisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the influence of lunar and solar rhythms, together with total cloud cover as a light-blocking factor, on the acoustic behaviour of nine vocally active cetacean species, one pinniped species, and one fish species off Antarctica, the sub-Antarctic region, and the west coast of South Africa. title: Defect‐Conditioned Machine Learning for Molecular Passivator Design in Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Dynamic defects, mobile ions, and evolving interfaces remain major obstacles to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics. Molecular passivation can mitigate these losses, but its efficacy is a conditional response rather than an intrinsic molecular property. It depends on defect identity and charge state, molecular conformation, adsorption geometry, interfacial composition, processing history, and operating conditions. title: A multi-method approach to assessing chondrichthyan communities around offshore oil and gas infrastructure
abstract: Offshore habitats of the world’s oceans are increasingly being altered by human activities, particularly where energy extraction and production require infrastructure. These structures provide artificial habitats that marine life grows on and attracts mobile fauna. Certain species of chondrichthyans associate with these structures, although their reliance on these structures is largely unknown. We surveyed chondrichthyan fauna on oil and gas infrastructure and in natural habitats of the Gippsland Basin, south-east Australia over four years for a pre-decommissioning campaign. title: A two-stage Bayesian-optimized XGBoost framework for damage prediction of full-scale ships subjected to underwater explosions
abstract: Underwater explosions can cause catastrophic damage to ships, making rapid and reliable damage prediction essential. A two-stage damage prediction framework is proposed, in which a node-level damage assessment is first conducted to distinguish fractured and non-fractured structural nodes, followed by quantitative prediction of fracture area and plastic deformation. An adaptive Bayesian-optimized XGBoost (BO-XGBoost) model is employed, in which stage-specific objective functions are designed for classification and regression tasks. title: Hidden seagrass policy: align UK land-management schemes with seagrass recovery
abstract: Seagrass recovery in the UK is constrained by interacting terrestrial and marine pressures, including sedimentation, nutrient enrichment, faecal contamination, altered runoff regimes and disruptions to food-web dynamics. Existing UK land-management schemes already fund actions that can reduce these pressure pathways, including buffer strips, livestock exclusion, riparian planting, runoff attenuation, wetland creation, and pesticide-handling infrastructure. However, flexible electronic devices are prone to detaching under dynamic conditions or underwater environments, resulting in inaccurate and delayed signal transmission. title: National-scale estimation of nitrogen runoff loss from paddy rice fields in China using machine learning approaches
abstract: Accurately estimating total nitrogen (N) runoff loss from rice paddies in China is essential for controlling agricultural non-point source pollution and optimizing N management strategies. However, the effects of key controlling factors and national-scale patterns of N runoff loss remain insufficiently understood. Here, we compiled a comprehensive dataset comprising 1154 records of total N runoff loss from Chinese rice paddies and developed six machine learning models, including eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Multi-Layer Percept

title: CoralDB: a comprehensive functional and evolutionary multi-omics database for stony corals
abstract: Stony corals are foundation species of coral reef ecosystems, yet their biology remains insufficiently explored from an integrative multi-omics perspective. Although the rapid accumulation of genomic and other omics resources offers opportunities to understand coral evolution, development, adaptation, and symbiosis, accessing and utilizing these resources remain challenging. title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. abstract: Context—Recruitment has become a multidimensional decision-making process in which organizations must evaluate both qualitative and quantitative candidate attributes simultaneously. While machine iearning (ML) methods are effective for predicting recruitment outcomes and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques provide structured ranking mechanisms, these approaches are commonly applied independently. title: Neural Network Prediction of Cropland Dynamics in the Vitebsk Region Using Google Earth Engine Land-Cover Data
abstract: Accurate prediction of cropland redistribution is important for regional environmental assessment, agricultural planning, and biodiversity-oriented land management, especially in territories where agricultural activity is spatially interwoven with forests, natural vegetation, transport corridors, and protected areas. This study develops and validates a neural-network framework for forecasting cropland dynamics in the Vitebsk Region of Belarus using harmonised land-cover maps prepared in Google Earth Engine from the MODIS MCD12Q1 product for 2001, 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020. title: Towards Generalisable Virtual Sensing: A Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network Approach On Cantilever Beams
abstract: Virtual sensing reconstructs structural responses at uninstrumented locations from a sparse set of physical measurements, enabling structural health monitoring where dense sensor networks are impractical. Conventional model-based methods depend on an accurate representation of the structure. When this representation does not match reality the reconstruction degrades, and restoring accuracy requires recalibration for each unit of a population, making the methodology time consuming. title: Development and validation of an early warning model for secondary spinal epidural abscess in pyogenic spondylitis based on interpretable machine learning: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Secondary spinal epidural abscess (SEA) in pyogenic spondylitis (PS) can rapidly compress the spinal cord or cauda equina, leading to irreversible neurological deficits such as paraplegia. Once formed, it often requires emergency surgical decompression and is associated with significantly poorer outcomes. Therefore, early identification of high-risk patients before abscess formation is of important clinical value. title: Lightweight adaptive multi-frequency sharpening for underwater image enhancement using contrast and noise guided fusion
abstract: The Adaptive Multi-Frequency Sharpening Model (AMFSM) is a lightweight, training-free approach designed to enhance underwater images by mitigating the effects of light absorption and scattering. Based on multi-frequency Gaussian decomposition with an adaptive weighting factor (α) that incorporates a Laplacian-based noise-related indicator, the proposed approach is capable of adapting the degree of sharpening based on the local properties of the image. title: Land use and environmental drivers of nutrients and primary production in 49 inland and coastal saline lakes of semi-arid Türkiye
abstract: Saline lakes are increasingly threatened by climate and anthropogenic pressures, yet comparative assessments of nutrients and primary production in inland and coastal saline lakes remain scarce. We assessed 49 saline lakes across semi-arid Türkiye (21 inland, 28 coastal) to identify the main environmental and anthropogenic drivers of physicochemical variables, including nutrients, primary production, and macrophyte percent volume infested (PVI%). title: Using machine learning to predict suicide risk among veterans: variation by race and ethnicity
abstract: AIMS: Suicide is a leading cause of preventable death among U.S. veterans. Machine learning (ML) prediction is promising, yet most ML models for suicide rely on predominantly non-Hispanic White samples and rarely assess racial/ethnic status. METHODS: We analysed baseline data from the Behavioural Research and Analysis of Veterans' Outcomes (BRAVO) cohort, a national sample of post-9/11 veterans. title: Hydrogeochemical drivers of salinity intrusion in coastal paddy fields: Soil-water interactions and irrigation implications
abstract: Salinity intrusion is a major constraint in coastal paddy agroecosystems, where the dynamic interplay of groundwater, surface water and soil processes determines the quality of irrigation water and crop performance. While previous studies have examined hydrogeochemical processes, soil salinity and crop responses individually, their integration at the field scale remains limited. title: Enhancing equity and resilience in coastal small-scale fisheries: a Confucian ethical perspective on community co-management
abstract: When trying to balance ecological protection with basic community livelihoods, coastal small-scale capture fisheries are facing serious governance challenges related to fairness, food security, and community resilience. Existing studies have focused on protecting rights, community participation, and the use of adaptive learning. However, further clarification is needed of how prioritizing basic needs, allocating responsibilities in light of participants’ differing circumstances, and reflecting on action can be ethically justified within a coherent framework. title: Integrated satellite–AIS–UAV framework for suspected non-cooperative vessel screening in complex estuarine waters
abstract: Maritime surveillance in complex estuarine waters is constrained by incomplete vessel self-reporting, uncertain satellite-AIS association, and difficulties in converting remote-sensing observations into executable verification tasks. Existing satellite-AIS monitoring improves coverage but often lacks integrated treatment of association uncertainty and verification feasibility. title: Linear Time-Series Models Match Deep Learning in Daily Solar Radiation Forecasting for Tropical Indonesia
abstract: Comparisons of deep learning forecasts seldom separate the effect of architecture from that of location or test the networks against linear models that use the same inputs. This study compared LSTM, GRU, and BiLSTM networks with two linear time-series models, dynamic harmonic regression with ARMA errors (DHR-ARMA) and an autoregressive model with exogenous inputs (ARX), for one-day-ahead forecasting of daily solar radiation in five Eastern Indonesian cities using NASA POWER data for 2014–2023, with 2023 as the test year. title: Determination of organic carbon concentrations in marine sediments across different dates by visible and near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: The application of spectral models across different monitoring dates remains a challenge in fixed-point monitoring. Here, we studied the temporal dynamics of the organic carbon concentrations in sediments from the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea with visible and near-infrared spectroscopy using the established spectral models. In this study, 96 surface sediment samples were collected from the same sites in 2020 and 2023. These samples were prepared as dried powder samples, and their total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations were determined. Their visible and near-infrared spectra were also recorded.

title: Data‐Driven Parameterization of Arctic Ocean Turbulent Mixing
abstract: Turbulent mixing may become increasingly important in a changing Arctic Ocean, influencing regional dynamics and global overturning. Arctic turbulence remains poorly characterized due to sparse observations, limitations of conventional parameterizations, and incomplete understanding. We train gradient‐boosted decision trees on global microstructure turbulence data (>5,000 profiles; ∼ data points) to predict turbulent dissipation from more widely available hydrography. abstract: Estuarine delta wetlands are relatively fragile ecosystems, and soil ecological stoichiometry plays an important role in understanding wetland ecological conditions and developing effective restoration and sustainable management strategies. However, the spatial patterns of soil ecological stoichiometric characteristics and their relationships with environmental factors in estuarine delta wetlands remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a physics-guided framework designed for near-real-time (NRT) SLA reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific and retrospectively evaluates it using 2022−2025 HY-2B/C/D observations. title: Forecasting pneumonia hospitalizations under climate change scenarios in Southern Brazil using neural networks
abstract: Pneumonia hospitalizations exhibit seasonal patterns, and climate-informed models can help explore future hospital demand under specified climate trajectories. This study modeled monthly pneumonia hospitalizations in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, using an autoregressive neural network with exogenous climate variables (NNETAR). Hospitalization records from January 2015 to June 2025 were combined with temperature, precipitation, and humidity simulations from MPI-ESM1-2-LR under SSP5-8.5 to generate projections through December 2049. title: Hidden Helpers: How Tiny Viruses Shape the Arctic Ocean
abstract: The ocean is full of invisible life, including countless viruses. Although viruses are often linked to disease, they also play an important role in keeping the ocean healthy and balanced. These hidden helpers control tiny plants called microalgae, recycle nutrients, and shape the ocean’s food chain. The Arctic Ocean may look like a frozen desert, but it is actually one of the world’s virus hotspots. Why are there so many viruses there and what role do they play in this icy world? title: Machine Learning Calibration of Sentinel-3 Significant Wave Height Using Level-2 Features Only: A Two-Stage Approach Validated at 83 NDBC Buoys
abstract: Satellite radar altimetry provides the only global, all-weather record of significant wave height (SWH), but Sentinel-3 Level-2 retrievals retain systematic, context-dependent errors near coasts and at low sea states. We present a two-stage calibration that uses only Level-2 variables: a buoy-weighted isotonic regression removes the scale-dependent bias, and a LightGBM model predicts the residual from waveform-quality and along-track descriptors, with quantile models supplying a per-sample uncertainty. title: Landslide susceptibility assessment in the monsoon-dominated Sikkim Himalayan region using state-of-the-art models
abstract: Landslides are a common life-threatening natural event in the Sikkim Himalayan Region (SHR). The state-of-the-art decision tree (DT), random forest (RF) and deep learning neural network (DLNN) models were employed to assess landslide susceptibility mapping (LSM) in the monsoon-dominated SHR. The major findings of this research highlight that DLNN is the most effective tool for assessing LSM, proving to be more accurate than alternative methods. title: Neurocognitive Applications of AI: Humanware for Mirrored Intelligence
abstract: Humanware represents an emerging paradigm in human cognitive enhancement, extending the AI frontier through integration of human-centered technological interfaces with cognitive learning, metacognition, and adaptive behavioral engagement. Humanware 4.0 advances a human–technology partnership in which intelligent systems function as responsive cognitive scaffolds, facilitating learning, self-regulation, and the progressive development of intellectual capacity. abstract: Hourly reference evapotranspiration (ET0) forecasting plays a critical role in irrigation scheduling, water resource planning, and climate-resilient agricultural management. Short-term multi-horizon forecasting of hourly ET0 remains relatively underexplored, particularly using automated forecasting frameworks and emerging time-series foundation models. abstract: The prediction of football players’ performance is a significant machine learning problem since clubs, analysts and players engaged in fantasy leagues have to evaluate how a player will perform before a game. However, the usefulness of such a model is determined not only by its predictive accuracy on a certain data set, but also by the question whether its features are based only on historical data, whether its predictions take into account positions of players and whether they can be interpreted by the coaching staff and analysts. title: Why progress in multi-objective materials design via machine learning depends on integrated data infrastructure
abstract: Machine learning is transforming materials discovery, yet its impact on multi-objective optimisation remains constrained by the structure and quality of input data. Despite the growing use of advanced predictive models, most studies rely on single-property datasets developed for specific purposes and not designed for cross-domain integration. Fragmented descriptors, inconsistent metadata, and missing values prevent models from learning relationships across properties and material classes, limiting effective optimisation. title: Adaptive Spatial Filtering and Neural Regression Modeling for Enhanced Bathymetric Retrieval in Optically Complex Inland Waters Using PlanetScope Satellite Imagery
abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) in inland waters remains challenging due to the strong spatial variability of optically active constituents and limited optical penetration depth. This study investigates the impact of a proposed Adaptive Spatial Filtering (ASF) approach and nonlinear regression models on bathymetric retrieval from PlanetScope imagery in two optically complex bays of Lake Dąbie, Poland. title: Lake dissolved oxygen profile prediction considering upstream inflow influences: a graph neural network framework integrating channel attention and a hybrid loss function
abstract: Accurate prediction of lake dissolved oxygen profiles (LDOPs) is crucial for early warning of hypoxic events. Existing studies often overlook the complex spatiotemporal dependencies between upstream inputs and in-lake processes, as well as interactions among water quality indicators, thereby limiting model performance in terms of prediction accuracy and interpretability. title: Efficient hybrid quantum-classical neural networks generation for crop yield prediction using sequential satellite images
abstract: A novel approach is introduced that enables the automatic generation of hybrid quantum-classical neural networks using a two-step optimization process, combining multiobjective genetic algorithms specifically designed for time series on satellite images with a subsequent continuous refinement stage of the circuit’s parameters. This strategy provides models with low prediction error and low complexity in terms of trainable parameters. title: Multiscale Characterization of a Deep-Sea Ferromanganese Nodule from the Clarion-Clipperton Zone
abstract: Ferromanganese nodules from the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ) located in the eastern Pacific Ocean between Hawaii and Mexico are enriched in a variety of critical metals. Understanding the spatial distribution of different metals, their partitioning between mineral phases, and pore-size distributions within the nodules can provide helpful insights into their formation mechanism. title: Roadway safety during active wildfires: A machine-learning analysis of crash occurrence and injury severity
abstract: Wildfires create rapidly changing conditions for roadway operations and safety, yet how wildfire-related conditions relate to crash occurrence and injury severity remains insufficiently understood. Using data from 10 California wildfires between 2020 and 2025, this study examines crash occurrence at the roadway segment-day level and injury severity at the crash level through two separate machine-learning analyses. abstract: Spent earth palm oil (SEPO), a high FFA (32.85%) palm refining waste, was converted to biodiesel in steps: a two acid esterification brought the acid value below 2 mg KOH/g, and base-catalysed transesterification yielded 95% conversion, an acid value of 0.4 mg KOH/g, ester content >99.5% and EN 14214 compliance for all parameters measured. abstract: Study region The study focuses on a steep, 4000 m² headwater hillslope within South Korea's Sulmachun Catchment. This monsoon-influenced region receives 1636 mm of annual rainfall (70% during summer) and features sandy loam soils under a mixed forest canopy. title: Blue biomaterials: a comprehensive review of marine-derived decellularized extracellular matrices (dECM) for regenerative medicine
abstract: Considering that oceans cover more than 70% of the Earth’s surface, they are rich in marine resources, providing a large and unique, sustainable resource pool for various research areas. In biomedical science, dECM derived from marine life is becoming an increasingly widely used and promising biomaterial. Compared with dECM derived from terrestrial mammalian sources, materials from marine organisms have lower immunogenicity, simpler structures, and higher usability. abstract: Underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) is attractive for high-speed underwater data transmission, but variations in water turbidity can severely degrade communication performance. This study presents a supervised machine learning approach based on the Coarse K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) algorithm to identify channel turbidity states in real time. abstract: The transition to low-carbon concrete has renewed attention on agro-industrial by-products, yet most investigations address a single supplementary material at a single strength level. In this work, a ternary blended cement concrete in which rice husk ash (RHA) and ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) partially replace Portland cement, reinforced with alkali-treated jute fibre, is developed and characterised across grades M30, M40 and M50 through a coordinated experimental and machine-learning (ML) programme. abstract: Reliable identification of degradation in polymer-based insulating material is essential to ensure the operational reliability of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems. Leakage current (LC) characteristics are widely used as diagnostic indicators to evaluate the surface condition of polymeric insulating materials. abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring is a non-invasive way to observe marine biodiversity where visual surveys are limited, but continuous recordings mix biological clicks with impulsive noise from anthropogenic and non-target biological sources, and their volume makes manual analysis infeasible; methods that do not resolve this mixture produce biased biodiversity estimates. abstract: Coral reefs are increasingly threatened by ocean deoxygenation and acidification, yet the metabolic mechanisms underlying genotype-specific resilience of corals remain poorly understood. We applied MS-based metabolomics to characterize how Acropora cervicornis fragments from five genotypes, originating from the Florida Keys, respond to 10 day exposures to deoxygenation, acidification, or both. abstract: Vertical hydraulic gradients (VHGs) in confined aquifers are routinely ignored when constructing potentiometric surfaces, introducing depth-dependent bias that distorts the apparent horizontal flow field. The resulting inaccuracies propagate into groundwater flow estimates, recharge and discharge calculations, and regulatory decisions. title: Educational Policy Development for Integrating Deep Learning Educational Values in Vocational High Schools: A Philosophical Approach
abstract: This study examines the development of educational policy for integrating deep learning educational values within vocational high schools through a structuralist–hermeneutic framework. Vocational education is expected not only to produce technically competent graduates but also to cultivate critical thinking, professional ethics, and socio-cultural awareness. However, existing policies often prioritize short-term technical competencies and mechanistic assessment systems, limiting transformative learning. abstract: Background Coastal oxygen depletion is a major driver of changes in sediment biogeochemistry and microbial functioning. However, oxygen states vary over space and time, which results in temporal dynamics that are so far under explored. This study examined three sites with differing oxygen regimes across a year to investigate how temporal oxygen variability shapes surface sediment microbial communities and activity. abstract: Many non-human animals produce vocal displays with rhythmic stability. For animals that sing or call underwater, measuring inter-call intervals (ICIs), the time between the starts of consecutive song or call emissions, can be complicated. Sound travels greater distances in the ocean than in air, so underwater recordings often simultaneously capture the vocal displays of multiple individuals. abstract: Suspended sediment concentration (SSC) is a key indicator of river morphodynamics and water quality, yet long-term spatial monitoring remains limited because in situ measurements are sparse and discontinuous. abstract: Ozone (O 3 ) pollution in coastal China exhibits a widespread increasing trend in autumn, coinciding with the active period of typhoons. Here, we analyze autumn O 3 evolution during 63 typhoon episodes over 2014–2023, and illustrate diverse impacts of typhoons on O 3 variations over different coastal regions. abstract: Nonlinear dynamics and deformations of soft robots pose challenges to conventional robot modeling and control. abstract: Mangrove forests are essential in improving coastal resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration. However, they are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures, particularly pollution such as oil contamination, which can induce long-term physiological stress in mangrove vegetation. Yet, monitoring the health of such ecosystems across large areas is difficult due to the scarcity of ground-based data and the spatial resolution-coverage trade-off. abstract: Forests are key terrestrial carbon pools, with carbon density varying across vegetation types. abstract: The U.S. National Water Model (NWM) produces streamflow forecasts for 2.7 million river reaches, generating roughly five terabytes of output daily. abstract: The Eddy-Diffusivity Mass-Flux (EDMF) parameterization provides a unified framework to represent both local (diffusive) and non-local (convective) vertical mixing in the ocean. abstract: Long-term fisheries statistics often underestimate total removals by overlooking small-scale, subsistence, recreational catches, and discards, thereby biasing assessments of fisheries trends and undermining management effectiveness and governance performance. Here, we reconstruct Uruguay’s marine fisheries catches over seven decades (1950-2022), integrating official statistics with expert-based estimates to quantify industrial, small-scale (SSF), subsistence, recreational, and discard components. abstract: Atmospheric organic carbon deposition acts as both a critical terminal sink for air pollutants and a substantial nutrient subsidy to terrestrial ecosystems. A substantial fraction of deposited atmospheric organic carbon reaches terrestrial ecosystems as dissolved organic carbon through precipitation and canopy throughfall. abstract: Nervous necrosis virus (NNV) is a highly pathogenic betanodavirus that causes severe mortality in marine fish. title: Spatio-Directional Extreme Value Analysis of Surface Currents in the Eastern Mediterranean: An Assessment of Uncertainty in the Gulf of Antalya
abstract: Sea surface currents are crucial for navigation and the design of coastal and offshore structures. This study presents a spatio-directional extreme value analysis of surface currents in the Gulf of Antalya in the Eastern Mediterranean, using 20 years (2000-2019) of hourly reanalysis data at 118 grid points for eight flow directions and the omnidirectional series. Annual maxima were fitted with the Gumbel or generalized extreme value distribution (selected by the Bayesian information criterion), while peaks over the 99.5 th percentile were fitted with the generalized Pareto distribution (GPD).

abstract: Enhancing the resilience of energy systems against exogenous shocks and climate change is critical. While the impacts of the artificial intelligence and digital economy are well‐documented, the role of digital government remains underexplored. To address this gap, we investigate the role of digital government in urban energy system resilience by exploiting the 2018 E‐government comprehensive pilot as a quasi‐natural experiment. abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) are persistent environmental contaminants with potential adverse effects on human health, but their involvement in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), gut microbiome analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to AMD. abstract: Low-salinity stress, frequently caused by spring rainfall and estuarine fluctuations, is a major constraint on the large-scale cultivation of marine diatoms and can disrupt their growth, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism. Nitzschia closterium is a marine diatom with high nutritional value and strong potential for producing PUFAs such as EPA and DHA, and it is also widely used as a live feed in aquaculture. title: Ecological consequences of coastal land formation: soil bacterial succession and assembly mechanisms along a reclamation chronosequence
abstract: Tidal flat land formation is a major land-use practice in coastal regions, profoundly influencing soil ecological functions mediated by microbial communities. However, the mechanisms underlying soil bacterial succession during coastal land reclamation remain poorly understood. Here, we examined soil bacterial community dynamics along a 1- to 14-year land formation chronosequence on Hengsha Island in the Yangtze River Estuary. abstract: Production environments strongly influence the health, welfare, and robustness of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ). Challenges related to gill health in particular have emerged as a major welfare and production issue in salmon aquaculture. Suboptimal rearing conditions can disrupt epithelial integrity, alter mucous cell dynamics, impair immunity, and compromise gas-exchange efficiency, ultimately resulting in reduced growth performance and greater susceptibility to disease. abstract: This study develops an AIS-based, time-resolved Port-LCA framework to estimate port-boundary well-to-wake emissions from alternative marine fuels. abstract: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) constitutes a critical but systematically underquantified pathway for nutrient delivery to coastal waters, particularly in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) where coastal aquifers may be contaminated by wastewater and urban runoff. abstract: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising energy storage candidates owing to their high capacity and environmental friendliness. abstract: A new species of Lestidium Gilbert, 1905, Lestidium serengeti sp. nov ., is described based on 20 type and two non-type specimens collected off Tanzania and Kenya. abstract: Identification of standalone predictors of rainfall extremes is crucial for understanding its underlying dynamics and for enhancing early warning systems. abstract: Food waste management remains a major challenge in rapidly urbanising African coastal communities with limited waste infrastructure. This study developed an exploratory AI-assisted decision-support framework for assessing food-waste compost quality in selected coastal communities in Ghana. abstract: To reduce the impact of tropical cyclones (TCs) under uncertain future climate projections, developing TC hazard curves across a range of potential climate scenarios is essential for risk-informed resilience planning in coastal regions. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) risk is commonly managed through frameworks that identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor model-level hazards. abstract: The asthenosphere's mechanical weakness enables plate tectonics, but its origin is debated. Partial melt has been proposed to cause this softening, yet recent studies suggest that the measured viscosity minimum in basaltic melts—an essential control on melt mobility—is an experimental artifact. Using quantum mechanics‐based, machine learning‐accelerated molecular dynamics, we extend simulation timescales by >10 3 and achieve percent‐level precision. title: A Physically Interpretable Dual‐Encoder Cross‐Attention LSTM for Water Level Forecasting in Dam–Tide Interaction Systems
abstract: Predicting the water level in real time in regulated tidal rivers is challenging because upstream dam releases and downstream tidal fluctuations act simultaneously, with their relative dominance shifting within an event. Attention‐based deep learning models for such systems have generally either mixed all forcings within a single encoder, meaning no forcing‐level attribution can be recovered, or distributed attention across variable–lag pairs in a self‐attention stream. title: An institutional climate based on community education and living well
abstract: Introduction: Institutional climate in educational communities is closely associated with communication, participation, and the recognition of shared responsibilities. Objective: To analyze the strengthening of institutional climate through a socio-educational intervention grounded in community education, living well, and the context-sensitive use of information and communication technologies (ICT) and artificial intelligence (AI). title: Enhancing tropical cyclone intensity estimation via multi-scale spatial feature correlation
abstract: Tropical cyclones pose significant threats to coastal regions, necessitating accurate intensity estimates for effective disaster management. Traditional methods that rely on manual feature extraction suffer from subjectivity and limited scalability. This study introduces a multi-scale spatial feature correlation network for tropical cyclone intensity estimation. institutions: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NA ANÁLISE DE REDES DE COAUTORIA
abstract: This paper explores the application of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and bibliometric tools in the analysis of academic co-authorship networks. The central research problem investigates how different GenAI approaches and specialized software compare in terms of pertinence, methodology, completeness, and performance when analyzing co-authorship networks through the use of the same contextualized prompt. title: Intégration pédagogique et didactique responsable de l’IA générative : Enrichissement de la littératie des enseignants de littérature
abstract: To ensure the contextualization of educational content, the education sector is currently seizing opportunities offered by digital technologies, particularly generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Given its significant influence on contemporary social life, the ethical and equitable use of these tools is increasingly recommended. Adopting an innovative approach, Cameroon aims to integrate AI into its education system, recognizing its numerous benefits. title: AI Literacy, Pedagogical Readiness, and Language Teaching Practices among Pre-Service English Teachers
abstract: Prospective teachers now face both new potential and challenges as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly incorporated into education, especially in the areas of instructional design, classroom delivery, assessment, and feedback. The current study looks at future secondary teachers' AI literacy, pedagogical preparedness, and AI-supported teaching methods. The study uses a descriptive survey research design and a quantitative methodology. A standardized questionnaire encompassing AI literacy, pedagogical preparedness, and reported AI-supported teaching methods is used to gather data. The

title: Geological controls on landfill pollution and environmental risk in arid Saudi Arabia: a critical review of hydrogeological, geophysical, geochemical, and remote-sensing evidences
abstract: Landfill pollution in arid environments depends not only on waste composition and engineering controls but also on geological connectivity, vadose-zone properties, groundwater conditions, and episodic recharge. This critical narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed Saudi Arabian evidence through September 2026 and compares it with selected regional and international studies to evaluate how geological setting affects contaminant pathways and the strength of environmental-risk inferences. title: Antimicrobial peptide–drug conjugates: rational design, pharmacological evaluation, and translational perspectives
abstract: Antimicrobial peptide–drug conjugates (APDCs) combine peptide and antibiotic functions within a single covalent construct. APDCs share design features with antibody–drug conjugates, but the field lacks an integrated account of how such conjugates should be designed and evaluated. This review examines that process from scaffold selection to translational precedent. title: Exploring Ethical Controversies in AI-Generated Art Based on Fundamental Principles
abstract: This paper will discuss from a technical standpoint the issues that lie at the heart of controversies over AI-generated art. Rather than ethical and legal debates, it proposes that intuitive public criticism has grasped well the way the generative model fundamentally works. title: Graph-theoretic multi-view feature engineering for interpretable BGP Anomaly detection
abstract: Graph-based and flat statistical feature spaces are both used for operational anomaly detection, yet how complementary they are—and how well detectors built on them transfer across deployments—remains largely untested. We study both questions for Internet inter-domain routing (BGP). We combine a graph-topological view and a statistical view in a multi-view detector and evaluate cross-domain transfer with a factorial design (two autonomous systems, two route collectors) and CORAL domain adaptation over 12 directed transfer pairs. title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid
abstract: BACKGROUND: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear. METHODS: We integrated network toxicology, machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, virtual gene perturbation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, external transcriptomic validation, and qRT-PCR to investigate candidate molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid. title: LLM-agent-based cross-modal retrieval method for detecting clues of ecological environment damage
abstract: Within Ecological Conservation Redline zones, ecological environmental damage caused by non-compliant production and construction activities has become increasingly severe. Existing methods typically leverage remote sensing imagery and deep learning techniques to automatically identify unauthorized construction, or retrieve clues of ecological environmental damage from textual information such as public complaints and official circulars. title: Enhancing Plurigaussian simulation through neural truncation rules
abstract: Purpose Plurigaussian simulation (PGS) is a powerful approach in generating discrete stochastic structures of complex multiphase systems across a range of scales. Originating as an extension of truncated Gaussian simulation, PGS allows for the detailed representation of phase relationships and connectivity. title: A Short Case Study about where Human Consciousness Originates and Whether Love Sustains it
abstract: Where does human consciousness come from? Science and religion have not answered this question; physics and neuroscience often disagree. This paper asks what one Swedish scientist-turned-mystic, Emanuel Swedenborg (1688-1772), reported after 27 years of journeys between physical, spiritual and heavenly worlds. His answer is direct: We do not make life, we receive it, and love is the life we receive. title: Slip Detection for Robotic Grasping with LSTM and TCN: Edge AI Evaluation on Embedded Platforms
abstract: Reliable object grasping is essential for robotic manipulation in real-world environments, such as manufacturing and assembly. Undetected slips can lead to task failure, while effective slip detection enables robots to adapt their grip in real time, improving robustness and safety. In earlier work, we showed that Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can be deployed on edge devices for real-time slip detection, but that study used a manually labelled dataset and reported only accuracy and F 1 scores, which limited comparisons of model–hardware combinations. title: A lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework for identifying dominant precipitation-related predictors in the data-scarce Mekong River Basin
abstract: Study area The Mekong River Basin is a data-scarce transboundary basin where sparse, unevenly distributed, and temporally discontinuous gauge observations hinder reliable precipitation estimation, particularly under strong subregional hydroclimatic heterogeneity. Research focus This study developed a lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework to identify dominant precipitation-related predictors across the basin. Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Engineering resilient environmental microbiomes: from multi-omics early-warning signals to predictive control and functional recovery
abstract: Microbial consortia are used in environmental bioprocesses, particularly wastewater treatment and anaerobic digestion. High performance under controlled conditions does not ensure stability or functional recovery after disturbance or scale-up. This review examines disturbance, destabilization, detection, prediction, intervention, and functional recovery in engineered microbiomes. We distinguish stability, resistance, resilience, recovery, and functional redundancy as distinct but interrelated properties and classify major physicochemical, ecological, operational, and evolutionary disturbances
institutions: M. Akmullah Bashkir State Pedagogical University

title: From Qualitative to Quantitative: A Data‐Driven Error Budget for Satellite Water Vapor Product Bias
abstract: Satellite‐derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) products are widely used for meteorological and climatological research, yet the relative contributions of environmental and observational variables to product uncertainties remain unquantified. Here, we present an explainable machine‐learning framework that integrates extreme gradient boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to establish a data‐driven error budget for satellite PWV product bias. institutions: State Key Laboratory of Remote Sensing Science

title: Fiber Types, Properties, and Vibration Effects in Fiber-Reinforced and Ultra-High Performance Concrete: A Review
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the different types, geometrics and important characteristics of fibers that have been used or proposed for use in fiber-reinforced concrete (FRC) and ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC). The effects of these fibers on the mechanical properties, durability and workability of FRC and UHPC are then outlined. journal: International Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology

title: Disentangling positional change from intensity in the palaeoclimate reconstruction of circulation patterns
abstract: Under ongoing anthropogenic climate change, the impacts of forcing on climate circulation patterns, such as ocean currents and wind belts, are an area of particular scientific interest. Due to the complexity of the system, these subsystem patterns can exhibit multi-dimensional variability such as strength change or feature migration. However, conventional proxy-based reconstructions risk conflating positional shifts with intensity changes, thereby obscuring the true mode of past variability and potentially impeding the accuracy of hindcasts and predictions. title: Advances in Metaheuristics and Learnheuristics (2019–2026): A Comprehensive Review, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
abstract: This review examines more than 150 recent metaheuristics introduced between 2019 and 2026, emphasizing their significant impact and performance in solving complex optimization problems. In the past three decades, more than 500 metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed, with no sign of deceleration, resulting in a vast and growing landscape that makes it increasingly difficult to select, compare, and evaluate the most suitable methods for specific challenges. abstract: Thyroid nodule malignancy classification using ultrasound remains challenging owing to the differences in assessment by TI-RADS among different observers as well as the lack of interpretability in deep learning models. This study proposes a framework that is based on hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture with fuzzy feature optimization and visual explanation. This system combines convolution feature extraction, Transformer modeling, fuzzy membership feature selection, Softmax classifier, and Grad-CAM explanation.
