title: Space Exploration and Human Expansion Beyond Earth: Current Status, Technological Challenges, And Future Prospects
abstract: Space exploration represents one of humanity's most significant scientific and technological achievements, integrating advances in physics, astronomy, aerospace engineering, materials science, robotics, and computational technologies. Since the launch of Sputnik 1 in 1957, space activities have evolved from early orbital experiments and crewed lunar missions into a multidisciplinary enterprise involving planetary exploration, space-based observatories, reusable launch vehicles, commercial satellite infrastructure, and prospective extraterrestrial resource utilization. title: Design and Implementation of an AI-Assisted Teaching Platform for Electromagnetic Information Courses
abstract: Electromagnetic information-related courses serve as a crucial foundational component for majors in electronic information. These courses are characterized by abstract theories, complex formulas, and significant practical relevance. However, traditional teaching methods exhibit notable shortcomings in terms of intelligence, personalization, and interactivity. title: Goby-fry fishery in the Gulf of Guinea: São Tomé local practices and ecological implications
abstract: “Peixinho”, little fish in English, refers to amphidromous gobiid post-larvae that have been captured for nearly a century and a half in the rivers and estuaries of São Tomé and Príncipe. Post-larval gobies represent an important source of animal protein for local communities in São Tomé and Príncipe and a key livelihood for local fishing communities. This study reports the post-larval goby catches and associated bycatch over a seven-day fishing period in the Iô-Grande community on São Tomé Island, with a mean daily catch of 131.3 kg of post-larval gobies. title: When sharper is not better: super-resolution of Sentinel-2 for multi-index emergent macrophyte mapping
abstract: Deep learning super-resolution sharpens Sentinel-2 imagery from 10 m to 2.5 m. Because emergent reed beds are narrow, often filling only one or two 10 m pixels, a sharper image seems likely to help, yet this had not been tested in optically complex lagoon water. We tested it in the Curonian Lagoon, Lithuania. title: Hyperspectral Imaging: Technology, Analysis Methods, Applications and Future Directions—A Review
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) records a near-continuous spectrum at every pixel, producing a three-dimensional data cube that acts as a spectral fingerprint of the imaged material. Once the preserve of remote-sensing specialists, the technique has spread into medicine, agriculture, food inspection, environmental monitoring, forensics, art analysis and defense as sensors have become cheaper and computing more powerful. title: Effects of acute mild-to-moderate hypoxia on auditory working memory in pilots: associations with physical activity and short-window physiological signals
abstract: Objective To investigate how acute hypoxia affects pilots’ auditory working memory (AWM) capacity and maintenance, and to examine the associations of physical activity and short-window physiological features with cognitive performance. Background Auditory working memory is important for processing air traffic control instructions and cockpit communications, yet its sensitivity to acute hypoxia in pilots remains insufficiently understood. title: Mediterranean low-salinity and anoxic sapropel events triggered by Atlantic atmospheric moisture
abstract: The Mediterranean is a saline sea because it exports moisture to the atmosphere1. Over the last million years, however, the Mediterranean has experienced abrupt declines in salinity that have collapsed the deep thermohaline circulation and caused bottom water anoxia each time the Earth has approached perihelion during the northern hemisphere summer2,3. abstract: High‐dimensional (HD) entanglement of photonic spatial modes endows photon pair with greater shared information, enabling secure quantum communication even in noisy environments. However, adequately characterizing HD spatial mode entanglement remains challenging due to the exponential scaling of measurements and data processing complexity. abstract: Abiotic hydrogen (H 2 ) generation from water‐rock interactions is traditionally attributed to iron‐mediated redox chemistry; which fails to explain H 2 release from low‐iron minerals like pure forsterite. Using density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations of olivine surfaces, we identify an alternative, defect‐mediated mechanism. abstract: The study aimed to analyze the relationship between financial education, responsible credit card use, and financial well-being among Ecuadorian consumers through a structural equation modeling approach. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study with an explanatory-predictive scope was conducted. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to credit card holders aged 18 years or older residing in Ecuador, yielding 195 valid responses. title: A multi-step and multivariate financial time series forecasting framework based on ConvLSTM optimized by Island Algorithm
abstract: Multi-scale and multi-indicator financial time series forecasting is a valuable requirement of quantitative analysis and intelligent decision-making. Nevertheless, the current research concentrates on single-step or univariate prediction, which is unable to completely meet the real-life needs of multi-step and multivariate prediction problems in complex financial time-series situations. title: From Readiness to Revenue: Development Pathways, Prospects, Impacts, and Economic Value of Forest Carbon and Blue Carbon Projects in Bangladesh
abstract: Bangladesh has completed most REDD+ readiness requirements and drafted a Carbon Market Framework, but lacks an evidence-based pathway for turning forest and coastal ecosystems into high-integrity carbon projects. Using secondary data from national policy instruments, the Forest Reference Level (FRL), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), crediting standards and published literature, this study synthesised a 23-step project development pathway and modelled mitigation potential and economic value under three scenarios. title: Building Explainable Sales Intelligence Systems: A Product-Oriented Model for Embedding AI Insights into Enterprise Sales Workflows
abstract: While Enterprise sales systems have dashboards to track revenue, customers, and buying trends, reports often require reading between the lines to determine what's good and what's bad before deciding which accounts to focus on. In this research, an explainable Sales Intelligence framework is proposed that transforms transaction-level information into analytical evidence at the customer level and converts it into conversations to support decision-making. title: Covariance-informed spatiotemporal clustering improves the detection of hazardous weather events
abstract: Spatiotemporal clustering can be used to detect weather events in multi-dimensional datasets. This method requires that the resolution of a dataset equivalently resolves variability across space and time, thereby normalizing the dataset for unbiased clustering across three dimensions. title: Secular Melting of Mantle Pyroxenite Records Mantle Dynamics Coupled With Supercontinent Cycles
abstract: Supercontinent cycles dictate Earth's long‐term tectonic and magmatic evolution, yet the variations in the lithologies of the mantle sources of global basalts remain poorly constrained. Tracking the balance between these two source lithologies, peridotite and pyroxenite, is notoriously difficult as extensive fractional crystallization obscures primary mantle signatures in global basalt records. title: Dual-modal terahertz geometric correction for quantitative air-gap detection in GFRP
abstract: Single-modal terahertz nondestructive testing faces inherent bottlenecks in quantifying thin concealed air gaps inside layered composite materials widely used in aerospace and advanced manufacturing. The reflection mode suffers from waveform superposition and interference, which restricts its quantitative accuracy. title: TSU-former seismic data denoising method based on spatiotemporal attention mechanism
abstract: Seismic data are frequently contaminated by severe environmental noise, reducing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and degrading subsequent processing and interpretation. Although U-Net-based deep learning has been widely used for denoising, such networks suffer from local receptive fields and an imperfect balance between noise suppression and signal preservation. title: Advancements in soft actuation for bionic robotic fish: Mechanisms, performance, and applications
abstract: Natural aquatic locomotion relies on the coordinated deformation of muscle groups to generate continuous body-wave propulsion—a paradigm that rigid-link robotic mechanisms struggle to replicate effectively. Soft actuation paradigms offer a compelling alternative, enabling continuous bending, twisting, and undulatory motions that naturally induce reverse Kármán vortex streets for enhanced propulsive efficiency. title: The Role of Automation and Digital Technologies in Improving Australian Freight Efficiency
abstract: Australia moves large volumes of bulk commodities, containers and consumer goods over long distances with a road-dominated freight system, so small gains in cost, time and energy per tonne carried translate into large national benefits. The question addressed here is whether, and under what conditions, automated and digitally enabled operations make Australian freight more efficient. title: Forest pest prediction using a hybrid Random Forest–LSTM model
abstract: Introduction Forest pest outbreaks can substantially affect forest ecosystem stability and pose challenges to forest health monitoring and risk management. However, forest pest monitoring datasets commonly contain a high proportion of zero observations and exhibit pronounced temporal variability, which can limit the predictive performance of conventional machine learning approaches. title: Time-aware evaluation of metaheuristic-optimized support vector regression for permeate conductivity in hybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis desalination
abstract: Machine learning models of desalination plants are often tested on random splits of time-ordered records, which can overstate their accuracy. This study evaluated support vector regression (SVR) tuned by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), the Genetic Algorithm (GA), Bayesian Optimization (BO), and Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for predicting permeate conductivity in a trihybrid nanofiltration–reverse osmosis pilot plant. title: Open-world panoptic segmentation
abstract: Robots need to be able to understand their surroundings in order to operate safely and robustly, and to interact with the surrounding environment. Robots deployed in unconstrained real-world scenarios must additionally be able to deal with novel situations and objects that have never been seen before. In this article, we tackle the problem of open-world panoptic segmentation, that is, the task of discovering new semantic categories and new object instances at test time, while enforcing consistency among the categories that we incrementally discover. title: Solar Energy and Digital Technologies for Sustainable Shrimp Farming: Opportunities, Challenges and Contributions to the SDGs
abstract: The intensification of shrimp farming has increased the demand for reliable energy, continuous water-quality monitoring, and timely farm management. Aeration is a major energy-consuming operation, while pumping, feeding, and environmental surveillance also require dependable electricity. Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems can reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel, but variable solar generation must be coordinated with farm demand, particularly the need for aeration during night-time and periods of low sunlight. title: Prey size and putatively fat-rich prey decline in the southern African Middle and Later Stone Age in the context of the Late Quaternary megafaunal extinctions
abstract: Introduction Where Late Quaternary extinctions were severe, archaeological, climatic, and extinction signals are compressed into short intervals, which makes their causes difficult to infer. Southern Africa offers a longer view because most of its large mammals survived. We tested whether, over a quarter of a million years, the size composition of hunted prey shifted toward smaller species and whether the estimated contribution of fat-rich prey changed. abstract: Conductive cracks can amplify strain signals, but in coating‐type hydrogel sensors, they usually propagate uncontrollably, causing delamination, drift, and failure. Here, a bioinspired ion‐riveted double carbon nanotube (CNT) coating is developed to turn this defect into a crack‐gated impedance amplification mechanism. title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. title: Detecting Temporal Land-Use Regimes in Mediterranean Agricultural Lowlands Using Landsat Time Series and Unsupervised Learning: Evidence from Albania
abstract: Mediterranean agricultural lowlands are undergoing intense land-use transformations driven by climatic variability, agricultural intensification, as well as urban pressure. Despite the availability of long satellite archives, long-term seasonal land-use dynamics and their functional heterogeneity remain insufficiently captured by conventional linear trend analyses. This study proposes a geo-information–driven analytical framework that integrates long-term satellite time series with unsupervised machine learning in order to identify functional land-use regimes beyond linear assumptions. abstract: This paper presents a remote disease detection method for water conveyance tunnels based on a biomimetic visual attention mechanism. To address the challenges posed by uneven disease distribution and complex background textures, the proposed method integrates local distinctiveness features and global rarity features. title: Explainable timber geographic provenance using flame emission spectroscopy dynamics and a transformer model
abstract: The misrepresentation of timber provenance undermines global supply chain transparency and sustainable forest management practices. Although reference forensic approaches, such as stable isotope analysis and chemical and genetic approximations, are reliable, their high cost and complexity hinder their widespread adoption. This work evaluates the feasibility of a high-throughput framework for provenance classification that integrates VIS-NIR flame emission spectroscopy dynamics and an end-to-end deep learning model. abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. title: Placozoan microbiomes reveal divergent trajectories of host dependence among the largely parasitic Rickettsiales
abstract: Rickettsiales are an enigmatic clade of strictly host-associated bacteria with common phylotypes in aquatic habitats. Despite amplicon- and metagenomic sequencing-based observations, the roles of these aquatic Rickettsiales are still unknown, as their genomes contain beneficial and parasitic traits. In placozoans, microscopy-based observations of intracellular Rickettsia-like organisms point to Rickettsiales as common and abundant symbionts. abstract: Precipitation data fusion combines gauge observations with spatially continuous satellite products to improve precipitation estimation. However, representing local precipitation patterns remains challenging in regions with complex terrain and sparse gauge networks. This study proposes a local structural enhancement-based precipitation data fusion (LSE-PDF) framework. abstract: Behavioural monitoring is central to understanding how animals respond to naturally occurring and human‐induced environmental change, yet scalable approaches for behavioural data collection, analysis and interpretation remain limited. Zoological institutions provide a valuable setting for developing and validating automated behavioural monitoring tools, as they encompass complex environments containing wildlife while offering a degree of control relative to conditions in the wild. title: Selection of classification methods and quantification of changes in extent of mangrove forests over 6 years (2019 - 2025) in Ninh Binh province
abstract: Mangrove forests in Ninh Binh Province, a key part of the Red River Delta, provide important ecological services but face significant mapping challenges due to complex land use and tidal dynamics. This study evaluates four classification methods—Traditional RGB, NDVI thresholding, CMRI thresholding, and an Integrated Approach combining spectral bands with vegetation and water indices—using Sentinel-2 imageries (2019–2025) on the Google Earth Engine platform for a coastal area of 23,871.55 ha. abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) confinement enhances the load-carrying capacity of concrete columns. However, predicting the compressive strength of FRP-confined concrete remains challenging due to the complex interactions between concrete properties, FRP characteristics, and confinement parameters. This study develops a machine learning (ML)-based framework for strength prediction by comparing Gene Expression Programming (GEP) and Taguchi-optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (TO-XGB) using an experimental database compiled from the literature. title: Computational aerodynamics for leading-edge inflatable kite design
abstract: Soft-wing kites are morphing, bridled, tensile lifting surfaces used for wind-assisted ship propulsion and airborne wind energy applications. Their swept-back planform, pronounced anhedral, and unconventional leading-edge geometry induce complex aerodynamic behaviour that challenges conventional modelling approaches. For leading-edge inflatable (LEI) kites, pressure-side separation induced by the inflated tubular leading edge renders classical inviscid methods insufficient, thereby necessitating sectional input from higher-fidelity approaches. title: Please Forward this Postdigital Feminist Chain-Letter on Living with AI in Higher Education
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enters higher education within established hierarchies of knowledge and expertise, becoming entangled with judgments about who sounds authoritative and which forms of writing carry weight. Those judgments were gendered, long before GenAI arrived. Drawing on feminist postdigital inquiry and collaborative, experimental approaches to knowledge production, this article reports a chain-letter experiment. abstract: Deep learning (DL) compilers rely on cost models and auto-tuning to optimize tensor programs for target hardware. However, existing approaches depend on large offline datasets, incurring high collection costs and offering suboptimal transferability across platforms. In this article, we introduce TCL , a novel efficient and transferable compiler framework for fast tensor program optimization across diverse hardware platforms to address these challenges. title: Improving rock fragmentation in rock blasting through geomechanical-based burden prediction
abstract: Rock fragmentation is a key determinant of blasting efficiency, excavation productivity, and downstream processing costs in mining and civil engineering. Achieving optimal fragmentation depends strongly on accurate burden ( B ) selection, yet B estimation remains challenging because of the complex interactions between rock-mass characteristics and blasting behavior. title: Physics-informed multi-sensor fusion framework for predicting weld penetration state and mechanistic discovery in CMT welding
abstract: Accurate recognition of weld states is essential for ensuring structural integrity in cold metal transfer (CMT) welding. However, it remains challenging to develop models that are both robust to industrial disturbances and physically interpretable. In addition, the inherent opacity of current data-driven methods often limits their reliability in complex manufacturing environments. This study proposes ASPIS-Net, a robust physics-informed network for interpretable CMT weld-state monitoring. title: A lightweight cross-session EEG emotion recognition network based on high- and low-frequency differential weighting
abstract: Non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) holds promising potential for brain-computer interfaces and neural engineering. However, cross-session distribution shift and the computational overhead of existing models remain major bottlenecks for deployment on wearable devices. To address these challenges, this paper first verifies the effectiveness of full-band features and reveals the complementary patterns between high- and low-frequency features through progressive frequency-band ablation experiments. abstract: Occupational fatigue is a critical safety concern in industrial environments, where substantial inter-worker variability in physiological responses can limit the generalization of conventional fatigue-detection models. This study presents a Domain Adaptation Network (DAN) with Multi-Scale Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) for worker-independent multimodal fatigue classification using physiological and environmental measurements collected from 50 industrial workers during occupational activities. title: A transformer-based super-resolution method: A novel solution for improving the quality of stacked or migrated seismic data
abstract: Seismic data obtained after stacking or migration typically exhibit low dominant frequency, sparse spatial and temporal sampling, and may retain a low signal-to-noise ratio even after stacking. To enhance the resolution of seismic data, a deep-learning-based single-step super-resolution method was proposed that simultaneously performed denoising, interpolation, and frequency extrapolation. title: Opportunities for Ethical AI Integration in Core Infrastructure Administration: Safety Boundaries and Control Frameworks for Autonomous DBAs
abstract: Database administration is one of the oldest and most consequential disciplines in enterprise computing. Databases hold the records on which banks, hospitals, utilities, governments and commercial platforms depend, and the people who administer them have traditionally held some of the most powerful privileges in any organisation. Between 2017 and 2026 the discipline moved from rule-based self-tuning features toward agentic systems built on large language models (LLMs) that can diagnose incidents, rewrite queries, apply patches and change schemas with little or no human involvement. title: “Betwixt and Between”: Science, Subjectivities, and Everyday Conservation
abstract: This article discusses everyday conservation as “betwixt and between” scientific positivism and day-to-day subjectivities of practice. The phrase helps us discuss the lived realities of conservation and combine diverse perspectives that are rooted in practice and/or field-based research. title: Inferring geographic origin in genebank accessions from genome‐wide SNP variation: A barley case study
abstract: Accurate geographic metadata are essential for using genebank accessions in spatial analyses, but many historical records lack precise coordinates or contain uncertain location information. We developed SNP2GPS, a plant-genomics workflow for inferring geographic origin from genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism data and supporting passport metadata curation in barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) collections. title: Influence of service life and system boundary modelling on the life cycle environmental performance of SCM-based concrete
abstract: Cement-intensive concrete production contributes significantly to global emissions, prompting wide use of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) to reduce clinker content. However, the long-term environmental performance of SCM-based concrete is strongly governed by durability, which directly influences service life and maintenance requirements. title: Biomimetic Multifunctional Surfaces: Engineering Intelligent Multifunctionality Through Bioinspired Structures
abstract: Biomimetic multifunctional surfaces hold promising prospects in numerous fields, including aerospace, marine engineering, biomedicine, flexible electronics, and environmental protection. This is primarily attributed to their unique capability for structural regulation and multifunctional synergy. The structures and fabrication strategies of these surfaces play a critical role in their performance and applications. abstract: Monitoring changes in the position of the boundary where marine-terminating glaciers transition from grounded to floating, known as the grounding line, is critical for advancing our understanding of glacier stability. The grounding line is difficult to observe directly but can be inferred from the ice surface tidal-flexure zone. This zone spans from the inland limit of tidal flexure – the hinge line, across the grounding line to the hydrostatic line, where the glacier becomes freely floating. title: Response and stability analysis of soil organic carbon in different ecosystems of China under climate warming gradient scenarios
abstract: Under the background of global warming, the response pattern of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the stability of carbon sinks have received more and more attention. This research adopts the Space-for-time substitution (SFTS) method to build a spatial unit that integrates climate, vegetation and land use factors. title: Wildfire detection near transmission lines using geostationary meteorological satellite data
abstract: Wildfires pose a severe threat to both ecological systems and critical infrastructure, particularly power transmission lines traversing high-risk areas such as forests and grasslands. We focus on wildfire detection near transmission lines in Yunnan Province, China, using geostationary meteorological satellite data from Himawari-8 and Geo-Kompsat-2A (GK2A). abstract: Clouds over the Antarctic Plateau exert a strong influence on the regional radiation budget, yet observations and modelling of their properties remain scarce. Here, 9 years (2012–2020) of ground-based high-resolution spectral radiance measurements from the REFIR-PAD spectroradiometer at Concordia Station (Dome C, Antarctica) are analyzed in synergy with co-located lidar observations. abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies and data dependent operations has increased organizational exposure to cyber threats, privacy breaches, operational disruption, and regulatory noncompliance, strengthening the need for effective cybersecurity risk management, control, and governance. abstract: Species selection and spatial assumptions influence mangrove restoration screening, but their effects on the area available for blue carbon assessment are often difficult to separate. This study combined habitat suitability rules for 11 mangrove taxa with 19 spatial sensitivity scenarios in Soc Trang Province, Vietnam. abstract: Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory-mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision-denied environments. abstract: Purpose: The purpose of the research is to determine the role of digital transformation in increasing the efficiency of enterprises and forming their competitive advantages in the modern business environment. title: Autochthonous dengue outbreak spreading from a holiday site to visitors’ places of residence, Tuscany, Italy, August to October 2026
abstract: Between August and October 2026, 49 autochthonous dengue cases were notified in Italy. Of these, 42 were exposed at a Tuscan coastal holiday site, and diagnosed after returning home, in 14 municipalities across seven provinces. Seven additional cases were identified, six in two areas where viraemic cases returned home and one near the holiday site. Dengue virus serotype 2, lineage 2II_F.1.1.5, was identified. abstract: Purpose: This study develops a Feature-based Drift-Aware Boosted Ensemble (FDABE) framework for effective concept drift adaptation in industrial sensor data streams. abstract: Measuring vertical velocity is crucial for improving our understanding of deep convection. The Convective Core Observations through MicrOwave Derivatives in the trOpics (C2OMODO) mission aims to retrieve vertical velocity using ice‐sensitive microwave measurements acquired at two closely spaced time intervals. title: Volatility-informed representation for time-series clustering
abstract: Time series clustering is a challenging task due to the presence of noise, non-stationarity, and volatility in real-world data. Traditional methods that rely on raw data often fail to capture meaningful temporal patterns. To address this issue, a time series clustering framework called enhanced clustering using conditional volatility (ECCV) is proposed, which systematically integrates conditional volatility (CV) as an alternative feature representation to improve clustering accuracy. abstract: In practical industrial scenarios, bearings predominantly operate under normal conditions, yielding extremely limited data when faults occur. title: China’s carbon neutrality strengthens its photovoltaic potential: Co-benefits for climate action and energy security
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) power is central to China’s carbon neutrality strategy, but the extent to which mitigation reshapes the climate resource base for PV generation remains uncertain. Here we combine Earth system simulations with a 0.1°-resolution deep learning downscaling framework to quantify changes in China’s meteorological PV potential under divergent emission pathways. abstract: Monitoring diverse, dispersed small‐scale invertebrate fisheries remains challenging because taxonomic diversity, informal trade and dispersed harvesting limit sustained programs that can capture standardised data used for catch identification and measurement. Computer vision is increasingly being used to overcome these challenges, but most affordable and accessible single‐camera systems face a trade‐off: close‐range imagery required for high fidelity species identification while increasing parallax error for three‐dimensional specimens. abstract: Coastal wetland systems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures, including land-use change and climate variability, yet their long-term dynamics remain poorly understood. This study assessed land-use and land-cover (LULC) changes within and around iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa, from 2000 to 2025 using multi-temporal Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery and a Random Forest classification framework in Google Earth Engine. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) co‐occur in natural and drinking waters, where they persist, accumulate, and pose risks to ecological and human health. Their mitigation demands integrated detection and remediation beyond single‐function platforms. abstract: Methylparaben (MP) is a widely used preservative in personal care products, foods, and pharmaceuticals, resulting in widespread human exposure through dermal contact, dietary intake, and pharmaceutical use. abstract: Embedded traffic-sign detection must balance accuracy against the compute, memory and power limits of the target platform. abstract: This study assessed the use and perceived effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in inclusive classrooms among public school teachers in the 4th District of Quezon Province during the Academic Year 2025–2026. abstract: This study presents the first comparative optimization of ultrasound-assisted alkaline extraction (UAE) of Zophobas morio protein (ZMP) using response surface methodology (RSM) and an artificial neural network coupled with a genetic algorithm (ANN–GA). title: Integrating Multi-Source Feedback in Computational Design
abstract: In real-world design practice, evaluations rarely rely on a single source of judgment. Designers routinely combine expert opinions, empirical studies, and computational models, each with distinct strengths and limitations. While machine learning offers methods to integrate multiple feedback sources, these approaches remain largely inaccessible to designers without technical expertise. abstract: Endoreplication is a conserved cell-cycle modification in which cells undergo repeated rounds of DNA replication without mitosis or cytokinesis, generating cellular polyploidy. abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) accumulate in marine food webs, yet their long-term behaviour remains poorly resolved in Southern Hemisphere predators. abstract: This study proposes an integrated digital design optimization framework for ship structural engineering that operates directly within an AVEVA Marine product model. abstract: Laizhou Bay is a typical semi-enclosed bay in the Bohai Sea, where heavy metal pollution has become a prominent issue due to industrial, agricultural, and shipping activities within its watershed. abstract: Non-invasive approaches are increasingly important for monitoring wild cetaceans, particularly vulnerable populations inhabiting anthropogenically impacted ecosystems. abstract: This study presents an empirical validation of the Stanford University Interim (SUI) path loss model for Frequency Modulated (FM) signal propagation at 105.5 MHz within the Yenagoa environment, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. abstract: Moisture-electric generators (MEGs) that harvest ambient or physiological moisture offer a promising route to self-powered wearable and deformable electronics. title: From Safeguard Requirements to Assessable Outcomes: A CrossProgramme Framework for Environmental and Social Risk Evidence in Plastic Credit Projects
abstract: A plastic credit certifies an environmental outcome, but the activity it pays for is carried out by people, and what a programme requires by way of evidence that those people are protected is a separable question from what it requires about tonnes. This study scores what the four programmes require on fifteen safeguard domains, at four ascending evidence levels: a written policy, an implementing procedure, a monitored outcome indicator, and independent verification of the outcome. title: Climate suitability of East Asian mangroves for nature-based solutions is limited by climate extremes
abstract: Mangroves represent distinctive coastal ecosystems that offer ecological benefits, notably through their high carbon sequestration rates. However, their resilience to extreme climate events remains uncertain. Here, we investigated the response of mangroves in East Asia to climate variability by employing the remote-sensing derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) as a proxy for canopy greenness. abstract: This study presents an explainable hybrid artificial neural network (ANN)–multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework for wildfire susceptibility prioritization and preliminary response-center candidate generation in Muğla, Türkiye. A matched grid–date case–control dataset comprising 65,020 observations was constructed from FIRMS/VIIRS active-fire detections, common-protocol ERA5 fire-weather variables, and structural environmental predictors. title: Fishing effort inertia governs daily catch-occurrence predictability for Japanese flying squid in Korean waters
abstract: Introduction Daily grid-scale forecasts of catch occurrence are increasingly used for operational planning and to track species redistribution under climate change, yet what sets their predictability limit is rarely quantified. title: Macrofaunal bioturbation modulates microbial metabolic potential in arid mangrove sediments
abstract: Bioturbation by benthic organisms substantially alters the physical and biogeochemical properties of mangrove sediments. Through burrowing and sediment reworking, bioturbators increase oxygen penetration into otherwise anoxic, waterlogged sediments and redistribute organic matter throughout the sediment profile. Although previous studies have shown that bioturbation modifies microbial community composition, its consequences for microbial functional potential remain poorly understood. title: Transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy: Evidence from Japan
abstract: Japan has pledged carbon neutrality by 2050, yet energy production still accounts for 84% of its greenhouse-gas emissions, and only 33.4% (328.48 TWh) of its 2023 electricity generation came from nuclear and renewable sources. This paper asks how Japan's electricity generation can complete the transition from fossil fuels to nuclear and renewable energy. title: A rare type of uranium mineralization in the Husab uranium deposit, Namibia: glimmerite-type uranium mineralization
abstract: The Husab uranium deposit in Namibia is a globally significant alaskite-type uranium deposit that locally hosts glimmerite-type orebodies. The glimmerite occurs in veins with exceptionally high uranium grades. We combined detailed field investigations, petrographic observations, and whole-rock geochemical analyses to characterize the glimmerite-type uranium mineralization. We identified the principal uranium-bearing minerals using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron probe microanalysis (EPMA), and laser ablation–inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS). abstract: The progressive deterioration of reinforced concrete (RC) bridges driven by aging, increasing traffic demands, and aggressive environmental exposure presents significant challenges to structural reliability, infrastructure resilience, and sustainable urban development. This study presents an integrated computer vision–digital twin (CV–DT) framework incorporating Mask R-CNN with a ResNet-50 feature pyramid network (FPN) for automated defect segmentation, structural condition assessment, and comparative environmental risk evaluation. title: Redirecting persulfate-based advanced oxidation from mineralization to oxidative polymerization: Mechanisms, products, and resource recovery for sustainable water treatment
abstract: Persulfate-based advanced oxidation processes (PS-AOPs) are conventionally used to mineralize organic pollutants, but this route demands substantial oxidant doses and releases the converted carbon as greenhouse gas. Organic pollutants can instead be redirected toward oxidative polymerization, forming separable polymeric solids under controlled activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and peroxydisulfate (PDS) by photo, electro, thermal, or catalyst stimulus. title: RadarTrack: Radar-Only Odometry Beyond Doppler Limits
abstract: Accurate ego-motion estimation at extremely slow speeds is crucial in robotic surgery, micro-robotics, wearable sensing, and structural health monitoring (SHM), where motion occurs at millimeter or micrometer scales. Existing IMU, vision, LiDAR, and doppler-based radar methods struggle due to drift, low micro-acceleration sensitivity, or reliance on favorable environments. We assessed urban inundation susceptibility in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region using 895 Amap inundation locations, 895 sampled background locations and 17 conditioning factors. title: Wild Citrullus species: genetic resource for genetic improvement of cultivated watermelon (Citrullus lanatus var. lanatus)
abstract: Sweet watermelon ( Citrullus lanatus var. lanatus ) is a globally important cucurbit crop valued for its sweet, refreshing, and nutrient-rich fruit. Increasing consumer demand for novel watermelon products with enhanced nutritional quality, unique fruit attributes, and improved resilience to environmental stresses has intensified the need for innovative breeding strategies. title: Diagnostic evaluation of high-impact features on intrusion detection performance in wireless sensor networks
abstract: Intrusion detection in WSNs is important to ensure network safety by identifying and counteracting unauthorized behavior. Given the limited resource nature of WSNs, finite energy, limited bandwidth, and processing power, effective and reliable intrusion detection system design is challenging. Machine learning (ML) has recently gained significant attention as an effective means to improve detection rates by recognizing complex and multi-linear patterns within network traffic. title: A hybrid physics–ML framework for integrating groundwater dynamics into land surface modeling: a ParFlow-based demonstration in headwater watersheds of the Pearl River Basin, China
abstract: Three-dimensional groundwater dynamics play a critical role in regulating land–atmosphere interactions, yet resolving three-dimensional subsurface flow processes at large scales remains computationally prohibitive. Here we present a hybrid coupling framework that enables the integration of three-dimensional groundwater processes into land surface modeling at substantially reduced computational cost. abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing with unique word (UW-OFDM) provides a guard interval that is deterministic in nature, offering better spectral efficiency and lower out-of-band emissions than conventional standard Cyclic Prefix structures (CP-OFDM). abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) represent a severe and refractory diabetic complication characterized by persistent inflammatory activation, disordered macrophage phenotypic transformation, and impaired neurotrophic signaling. Although moslosooflavone (MOS) has been verified to possess anti-inflammatory and pro-healing bioactivities in multiple disease models, its underlying multi-target regulatory mechanisms in DFU wound repair remain poorly elucidated. title: Pantoprazole-associated inflammatory bowel disease reporting signals and altered epithelial inflammatory responsiveness: an integrative pharmacovigilance and experimental study
abstract: Background The association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains uncertain. We evaluated PPI-associated IBD reporting signals and explored pantoprazole-related molecular and epithelial inflammatory responses. Methods FAERS reports from 2004 to 2024 were analyzed by disproportionality analysis. title: Generative AI Adoption in Educational Administration: An Extended UTAUT Model with Trust, Privacy Concern, and Institutional Policy Fit
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly promoted as a tool for educational administration and administrative decision-making, yet evidence on why educational leaders adopt it remains scarce, particularly in technical and vocational education. Extending the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) with trust, privacy concern, and institutional policy fit, this study examined the determinants of administrators’ GenAI behavioral intention and use behavior. title: Vertical distribution, optical characterization and automated classification of airborne pollen from in situ measurements
abstract: Bioaerosols, such as pollen grains, play an important role in air quality, human health and atmospheric processes. However, their vertical distribution within the boundary layer remains insufficiently researched. In this study, we investigate the vertical profiles of pollen concentrations between 4–272 ma.g.l. at the Vehmasmäki station in Eastern Finland. title: Integrated Remote-Sensing and Environmental Data Analytics for Predictive Heat-Stress Risk Assessment and Digital Health Monitoring in South Africa
abstract: This paper presents a framework and a preliminary computational demonstration for predictive heat-stress risk assessment and digital health monitoring in South Africa. Heat-stress risk is increasing under climate change, yet location-specific early-warning tools remain scarce, and South Africa's first national climate and health surveillance platform is, in its present phase, oriented towards surveillance and visualisation. abstract: Condition‐monitoring methods commonly provide discrete fault labels, whereas maintenance assessment requires a quantitative representation of damage severity. This paper proposes a quality‐loss‐based degradation‐state assessment framework integrating cross‐speed fault recognition with severity‐weighted loss mapping for planetary sun gears to improve cross‐speed fault identification and provide severity‐aware quantitative support for degradation‐state evaluation and maintenance decision‐making. abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization intensify flood risk in urban agglomerations. Using data from 92 cities in five Chinese urban agglomerations during 2006–2022, this study assesses the capacities supporting urban flood resilience (UFR) through 19 indicators across four dimensions. Spatial analysis, inequality decomposition, obstacle diagnosis and interpretable machine learning are combined to examine resilience patterns and compare five development scenarios. abstract: Sri Lanka's dependence on imported fossil fuels and its abundant aquatic resources have generated increasing interest in algal biodiesel as a sustainable third-generation biofuel. This review critically evaluates the country's potential to develop a commercially viable algal biodiesel sector by synthesizing evidence on ecological suitability, indigenous algal resources, technological readiness, sustainability benefits, and commercialization challenges. title: Persistence revisited: Partitioning rather than media-specific reactivity dominates persistence in the environment
abstract: Current regulation identifies environmentally persistent chemicals often using thresholds defined for single-media half-lives. This approach ignores the large and even dominating impact of multimedia partitioning on the (bio)availability of compounds that undergo degradation, and accordingly may underestimate the chemical lifetimes by orders of magnitude. abstract: In recent years, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has gained considerable attention as an emerging non-thermal food processing method, but its interaction with food proteins remains poorly understood. title: CPT-based reliability analysis of offshore monopile foundations using geology-informed hierarchical Bayesian spatial modelling
abstract: Uncertainty in ground conditions strongly influences the reliability of offshore wind monopiles, yet design practice still treats spatial variability, soil stratification and property-transformation uncertainty in isolation. This paper presents an end-to-end Bayesian framework that carries these ground-related uncertainties from cone penetration test (CPT) data through to a monopile serviceability failure probability. title: Casting-Derived PVA/PDMS Janus Membranes with Stable Photothermal Conversion for Solar Desalination
abstract: Solar photothermal conversion enables water evaporation and purification through localized interfacial heating, offering a sustainable approach for solar energy utilization. However, integrating efficient solar harvesting, continuous water transport, and structural support within a simply fabricated membrane remains challenging. title: Beyond water splitting: integrated electrocatalytic strategies for sustainable hydrogen production
abstract: Renewable electricity is transforming electrochemical hydrogen (H 2 ) production beyond conventional water electrolysis. However, sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics, complex electrode–electrolyte interactions, freshwater scarcity, and catalyst degradation remain key challenges. title: Investigating Seasonality in Sulfate Presence and Radiative Forcing in the North Pacific
abstract: Sulfate aerosols, formed from the atmospheric oxidation of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), contribute to global cooling through both direct and indirect radiative effects. However, uncertainties remain in their seasonal and spatiotemporal distributions along with their radiative impacts, particularly in relation to anthropogenic emissions and downstream burden. abstract: Introduction During early development, marine fish larvae rely on innate immune mechanisms, creating both a period of high susceptibility to disease and a potential window for immunomodulation. abstract: Introduction Takifugu rubripes is an economically valuable marine fish widely cultured around the Bohai of China. Long-term closed breeding and unregulated cross-regional fry trading have resulted in inbreeding accumulation, loss of genetic diversity and extensive population admixture, posing a risk to the genetic health of farmed stocks and hindering the sustainable development of its aquaculture industry. abstract: This study identifies and maps distinct neighbourhood-level trajectories of urban change across nine Spanish cities (Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Zaragoza, Sevilla, Málaga, Murcia, Palma, and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria), using a two-step unsupervised machine learning approach that combines UMAP dimensionality reduction with HDBSCAN density-based clustering. abstract: Background and aims Direct evidence to connect early life metabolism with cardiometabolic diseases in old age is limited due to the rarity of multi-decadal biochemical follow-up studies. To gain deeper insight into metabolic ageing, we conducted a longitudinal study that integrates serial data on clinical biomarkers, metabolomics and clinical events across the human life course. title: A fuzzy logic-based framework to assess the social feasibility of community-based fishery reserves
abstract: Fishery Refuge Zones (FRZs), a spatial management tool for fisheries, are used in Mexico as “Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures” (OECMs). This study introduces the first perception-based framework that uses a fuzzy logic model to evaluate the social feasibility of FRZ implementation in small-scale fishing communities, focusing on community acceptance, NGO/researcher collaboration, and rule compliance. title: IMU-Guided Adaptive Video Stabilization for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
abstract: This study addresses the critical challenge of video stabilization in Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) operating under high-wave and harsh maritime conditions. Conventional stabilization methods often struggle to distinguish erratic vessel motions caused by waves from intentional camera maneuvers, leading to significant image distortion, horizon tilt, and loss of visual data. title: Status and perspective on mechanical and protective properties of PVD MeSiN nitride nanocomposite coatings
abstract: MeSiN nanocomposite coatings have attracted growing interest due to their exceptional combination of high hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance. However, existing studies still lack a comprehensive analysis of their microstructural characteristics, performance metrics, and optimization strategies. This review critically examines recent advances in the fabrication techniques, structure–property relationships, and potential optimization strategies of MeSiN coatings. abstract: Research on nature-specific outdoor learning draws heavily on natural settings in the Global North, leaving school-based engagement with familiar urban ecosystems in Latin America less visible. This cross-sectional study examines the perceptions of 185 students aged 12–17 after a five-day LemonSea Ecuador intervention in three schools in Manta, Ecuador. abstract: In recent years the use of air sensors has rapidly expanded across North America to measure fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), particularly in response to increasing air quality impacts from wildland fire. With the benefit of enhanced spatial and temporal coverage, the scientific community and the public have come to rely on sensor networks as valuable sources of air quality information. abstract: Understanding marine species distribution and habitat use contributes to the development of effective population conservation and management. Biologging, particularly accelerometry, provides valuable insights on individual movement and behaviour. Technical constraints such as the need for tag recovery limit long-term studies of free-ranging fish over large spatial scales, hindering detailed examination of movements over seasonal or annual migrations. title: A theory of spatial simulation in video games: Selective realism and the production of virtual territory
abstract: Video games have become one of the dominant media through which space is experienced, imagined, and learned, yet no general framework accounts for how they simulate territory as an operational system rather than merely as an image. The aim of this article is to explain a recurring pattern: video games distribute geographical fidelity unevenly, enhancing features that support visual clarity, emotional engagement, and playability, while compressing or omitting dynamic processes, systemic interdependencies, and socio-spatial complexity. abstract: Surface slip has shown significant flow control effects on drag reduction and flow field manipulation. However, the slip effects on flow noise characteristics have not been fully understood. abstract: This research addresses a critical gap in MANET security, where secure routing, trust management, energy efficiency, and IDS are often treated separately, leading to suboptimal performance under dynamic and adversarial conditions. Conventional cryptographic methods introduce high computational overhead, while trust- and learning-based approaches often overlook end-to-end security, adaptive routing, and receiver-side intrusion validation. title: Stage equilibrium and spatial differentiation: Characteristics of meteorological disaster emergency management policies in China
abstract: With intensifying global climate change and frequent extreme weather events posing severe challenges to emergency management systems, the quality of policy design directly affects operating efficiency. This study establishes a scientific, quantitative policy evaluation system for meteorological disaster emergency management to provide evidence for enhancing emergency management capabilities. abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are endogenous peptides that play essential roles in pathogen neutralization and the orchestration of innate immune responses. They are widely distributed across diverse species and are evolutionarily conserved. AMPs exhibit broad-spectrum activity against a variety of pathogens, including bacteria and fungi. abstract: The existing manual prior based image dehazing methods are prone to edge smoothing and halo artifacts in non-uniform foggy scenes, while deep learning based dehazing methods improve overall restoration performance, but still have shortcomings in preserving edge details and accurately estimating depth. abstract: Using panel data from 269 prefecture-level cities for the period 2011–2018, this study employs a staggered difference-in-differences design and deep-learning-based text analysis to examine the effects of central environmental inspections (CEPI). abstract: Flood events—whether riverine, coastal, groundwater, or pluvial—can rapidly alter groundwater quantity and quality through accelerated recharge and increased hydraulic connectivity with near-surface pollution sources. Climate change has intensified and is projected to further increase the frequency, depth, and spatial extent of flood events, amplifying existing groundwater vulnerabilities. abstract: Socialanalysis is a social study that examines various existing social phenomena, which ultimately produce a perspective based on existing social problems to be followed up with various activities. abstract: Wind power generation is sensitive to atmospheric variability across seasonal to annual timescales, creating demand for climate information that is both skilful and temporally consistent. Here we develop a hybrid seamless seasonal‐to‐decadal forecasting framework for annual wind speed over the Americas. abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate prediction of functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke can guide clinical decision-making and resource allocation. Prior work has relied predominantly on structured predictors and conventional machine learning, while the ability of large language models (LLMs) to infer modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores from routine clinical admission notes is largely unexplored. title: Design and Preliminary Experimental Characterization of a LowCost ESP32-Based System for Electric Motor Condition Monitoring
abstract: Small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises without digital instrumentation detect incipient faults in electric motors by sight and sound, which leaves no record of the vibration and temperature changes that precede a breakdown. This study designed and preliminarily characterized a low-cost prototype, based on an ESP32 microcontroller, that measures vibration and temperature and classifies the motor state against approximate thresholds derived from the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 10816-1 class limits. title: Parameterized Cloud and Aerosol Processes Modulate the Spatial Distribution of Extreme Fire Weather Over North America
abstract: Cloud and aerosol processes remain among the largest sources of uncertainty in Earth system models because many governing microphysical processes occur at scales smaller than those resolved by global models. These parameterized processes strongly influence energy balance, moisture transport, and cloud properties, which are closely linked to fire‐prone weather extremes. Here, we leverage the perturbed physics ensemble (PPE) within a state‐of‐the‐art Earth system model to investigate how uncertainties in microphysical parameterizations shape extreme fire weather over North America. title: Heterogeneous patterning behavior emerges from human stem cell-based embryo model
abstract: Undergoing complex self-organization, two-dimensional gastruloids derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are a scalable model system to study developmental processes. However, gastruloid heterogeneity has been obscured by technological limitations. A microraft-based assay was developed to screen, sort, and sequence individual living gastruloids expressing germ layer reporters to quantify the emergence of gastruloid variability. title: FRAMING THE SACRED: SAFEGUARDING THE CULTURAL MATERIALITY IN THE VISUAL ETHNOGRAPHY OF THE ABAM NAMING RITE AMONG THE FANTE OF GHANA
abstract: As globalisation and radical religious changes threaten to wipe out the living traditions of Indigenous communities, the protection and preservation of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) has become a very important goal in the twenty-first century. In Ghana’s coastal region, the Fante People of the Edina Ampenyi traditional group, located in the Komenda/Edina/Eguafo/Abirem Municipality in the Central Region of Ghana, West Africa, have a complex ritual system called Abam that helps twins and children born in certain birth orders make spiritual transitions. title: Risk-Based Design, Construction Quality, and Lifecycle Integrity of Hydrocarbon Distribution Pipelines in Saudi Arabia: An Integrated Engineering Framework for Vision 2030
abstract: Hydrocarbon distribution pipelines connect production, processing, storage and end users, yet their integrity is often governed through disconnected design, construction and operating records. This critical review examines research published from 2020 to 2025 to develop an integrated engineering framework applicable to Saudi Arabian liquid and gas networks. The synthesis evaluates corridor hazards, design margins, corrosion, girth weld acceptance, commissioning evidence, risk assessment, inspection and digital monitoring. title: Water resilience in the high Andean basins of Peru and Ecuador: A synthesis of hydrological modeling, cryosphere dynamics, and ecohydrological approaches under climate change (2011–2025)
abstract: The high Andean basins of Peru and Ecuador supply freshwater to approximately 60% and 70% of their respective national populations. However, these systems are increasingly threatened by glacier retreat, land-use transformation, and climate variability, which jeopardize long-term water security. title: Silent inconsistencies at the aggregation stage of Earth observation pipelines: an internal-consistency audit of zonal statistics for local climate zone–based land surface temperature analysis
abstract: Thematic maps generated by machine-learning classifiers, including Local Climate Zone (LCZ) maps, enter quantitative Earth observation science only after geospatial operators aggregate raster observations within the mapped zones. Zonal statistics constitute this interface, yet the internal coherence of their outputs is assumed rather than tested. This study audits it for LCZ-stratified land surface temperature (LST) analysis in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. title: Sex, but not age, drives transcriptome-wide gene expression variation in a turtle with female-biased longevity
abstract: Sexes frequently differ in life-history traits including body size, lifespan, and age at sexual maturity. Organismal aging, the progressive decline in physiological function and cellular resilience over time, is a central component of sex-specific life histories, yet the mechanisms driving sex differences in aging remain largely unresolved. Long-term mark-recapture efforts reveal a striking pattern of female-biased longevity in painted turtles (Chrysemys picta) (lifespan: males = 24 years, females = 48 years). title: The debt burden of tropical cyclones and climate change
abstract: Addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation is expected to require more than $6 trillion in global investment annually by 2035. Yet many countries face significant barriers to accessing this finance, including low or absent credit ratings, large debt burdens, and high borrowing costs. Climate change may further amplify these barriers, creating a "vicious cycle" in which mounting economic losses reduce the capacity of countries to invest in adaptation and mitigation. title: Ship detection using RSE-YOLOv12 with enhanced feature extraction and fusion
abstract: Ship detection in complex maritime scenes is challenged by substantial scale variation, limited details of small targets, and interference from sea surfaces and shoreline backgrounds. Preserving target features during feature extraction and fusion while maintaining inference efficiency remains important for maritime monitoring. To address these challenges, this study proposes RSE-YOLOv12, an enhanced ship detection model based on YOLOv12. title: High resolution spatiotemporal modelling of outdoor temperature for assessment of heat-related health inequalities in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Urban heat exposure is unevenly distributed within cities, often disproportionately affecting socially and environmentally vulnerable populations. In Sub-Saharan Africa(SSA), where warming is occurring faster than the global average, the lack of high-resolution temperature data constrain efforts to characterize exposure patterns and inform epidemiological research and urban heat adaptation. We developed the first ground-based spatiotemporal outdoor temperature surfaces for a major SSA city using an 18-month measurement campaign across the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area, Ghana. title: Optimization of aqueous extraction and antioxidant activities of crude polysaccharides from Hippophae rhamnoides L. fruit: protection against oxidative stress in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Introduction Oxidative stress is a key contributor to chronic disease and aging, and natural antioxidants from edible plants are of growing interest as dietary protective agents. Hippophae rhamnoides L. (sea buckthorn) is a medicinal and edible plant rich in bioactive compounds, and its polysaccharide-enriched fractions have been reported to possess antioxidant properties. However, the extraction conditions and the in vivo antioxidant effects of these fractions remain insufficiently characterized. title: Sampling optimization to estimate fishing effort for small-scale fisheries using high-resolution tracking data
abstract: Small-scale fisheries (SSF, vessels under 12 m) represent approximately 90% of global fisheries and over 80% of the EU fleet, employing around 100,000 people, yet their fishing effort (FE) remains poorly quantified. Unlike large-scale fleets equipped with Vessel Monitoring Systems, SSF tracking is only now emerging following EU legislation mandating electronic tracking by 2030 (EU 2023/2842). title: HelioTR-Atlas couples satellite-retrieved direct irradiance with station-validated topographic thermodynamics for explainable photovoltaic yield mapping in complex terrain
abstract: Terrain-resolved photovoltaic (PV) yield assessment needs an irradiance source whose direct component is retrieved rather than assumed, thermodynamic fields corrected for elevation and validated against ground stations, and an attribution layer explaining why yield departs from irradiance. These are rarely met together. title: Seasonal controls on dissolved rare earth element signatures in large tropical rivers: interplay of monsoonal discharge, lithology, and anthropogenic inputs
abstract: Understanding the geochemical behavior of dissolved rare earth elements (REEs) in large tropical rivers is critical for tracing global silicate weathering and anthropogenic fluxes to the oceans. This study investigates REE dynamics in two major river systems, the Godavari and the Mahanadi, which drain contrasting lithologies (Deccan basalt vs. heterogeneous metamorphic terrains) and discharge into the Bay of Bengal. title: Glycosylation modification of therapeutic peptides: Synthetic strategies, functional regulation and biomedical applications
abstract: Peptide drugs offer advantages such as high target affinity and low toxicity, but their clinical translation is severely limited by inherent drawbacks including susceptibility to proteolytic degradation, rapid renal clearance, poor membrane permeability, aggregation propensity, and potential immunogenicity. Glycosylation modification, with its excellent biocompatibility and tunable physicochemical properties, has emerged as a key strategy for therapeutic peptide engineering. title: Climate-data-driven zoning methodology for building energy code-compliance: A case study of Korean standards
abstract: In building codes and standards, climate zones play a critical role in regulating building energy efficiency and performance. Especially, the climate zone classification directly affects the determination of envelope insulation and the annual heating and cooling energy use. To ensure better building envelope performance in the buildings, appropriate climate zoning framework is essential to assist tailored building energy performance considering the climatic characteristics of each climate region. title: Analysis of the Evolution Characteristics of Drought-Flood Abrupt Alternation in the Pearl River Delta, China
abstract: Drought-flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) is a compound extreme that is particularly consequential in densely populated deltas, yet its long-term behaviour in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) remains poorly resolved. Using the AgERA5 daily gridded precipitation dataset, this study identified DFAA events with the standardized weighted average precipitation (SWAP) index combined with run theory and analyzed their spatiotemporal evolution with the Theil-Sen slope estimator. abstract: Ophelia limacina (Rathke, 1843), originally described from Norway, is the only species of Ophelia Savigny, 1822 recorded from Chinese waters, but these records have never been verified. To clarify the identity of the Chinese Ophelia , specimens from the Chinese coast, from Shandong to Fujian, were examined. title: Developing a Local Ecosystem-Based Fantasy Writing Module to Strengthen Seventh Graders’ Imaginative Thinking
abstract: Contextual resources may help adolescents transform familiar experiences into original fantasy narratives, yet Indonesian-language writing materials in island schools often provide few locally meaningful prompts. This study developed and evaluated a local ecosystem-based fantasy writing module for seventh graders at SMPN 1 Liang, Banggai Islands. Using the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation framework, the research combined expert appraisal, a 10-student limited trial, and a 40-student one-group pretest–posttest trial. title: Nephelometer-based air sensor networks systematically underestimate PM2.5 in dust-influenced West Africa
abstract: Particulate matter air pollution is a major public health burden in West Africa, a region impacted by long-range transport of desert dust and local emissions. Most recent measurement growth has come from optical air sensors that behave as imperfect nephelometers. We present a multi-year measurement campaign of 16 monitoring sites across four major metropolitan regions in Ghana using the QuantAQ Modulair-PM. title: Host-Country Institutional Environment, Strategic Adaptation, and Firm Performance: Evidence from Chinese-Invested Enterprises in Indonesia
abstract: Leveraging the promulgation of the Green Credit Guidelines as a quasi-exogenous policy shock, this study establishes a rigorous quasi-natural experimental framework to empirically examine the causal nexus between green credit policy and green innovation outcomes in renewable energy enterprises. Employing a Difference-in-Differences (DID) methodology on a comprehensive panel dateset spanning 2016–2025, complemented by systematic heterogeneity analyses, mediation effect examinations, and an extensive battery of robustness tests, we uncover several salient findings. title: Awake infant functional MRI for visual neuroscience: reflections from the Foundations of Cognition Project
abstract: Introduction Awake infant functional MRI (fMRI) has considerable potential to provide a window into the function of the developing brain. In visual neuroscience, NeuroAI approaches combining fMRI with computational models, such as deep neural networks, offer powerful tools for characterizing representations along the ventral visual stream (VVS), a hierarchy of cortical regions that subserve object recognition in adults. title: China’s Consumption Geography: A County-level Estimation of Daily Consumption Using Big Data
abstract: Residents’ daily consumption (RDC) levels provide an important indicator of regional development. However, existing research has largely examined consumption patterns either at coarse spatial scales or through localized case studies owing to data constraints, limiting our understanding of fine-grained spatial disparities in consumption. Using Baidu Population Profiling data, this study systematically examines the geography of RDC levels across county-level units in China and explores the socioeconomic factors underlying regional variation in consumption levels. title: The Erosion of Academic Freedom in the United States in the Early Twenty-First Century: A State- and Movements-Based Analysis
abstract: Academic freedom protections for US professors have never been secure, but they experienced an unprecedented erosion in the early twenty-first century. The objective of this article is to analyze why this sea change occurred—and with what consequences. It discusses the policy interventions in the 50 states and the federal government that brought the issue of higher education’s autonomy to a head in 2025. title: Enhancing Physics Learning Through English Journals and Presentation-Based Scientific Reasoning
abstract: This study examines academic literacy integration in an English-as-a-Foreign-Language (EFL) physics classroom through scientific journal reading and presentations. Involving 78 undergraduate students in a Renewable Energy course at Universitas Bengkulu, the research examines how IMRaD-based activities support scientific reasoning, genre awareness, and disciplinary communication. Students formed seven thematic groups focusing on geothermal, biomass, solar, wind, tidal, ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC), and green hydrogen. title: Tracking the herbivory of brown-tailed moth Euproctis chrysorrhoea (Lepidoptera, Erebidae) on annual increment data of montane Caucasian oak forests in Armenia
abstract: Recent decades of global warming have posed a significant threat to all components of montane forest ecosystems, with particularly pronounced impacts at their ecotonal boundaries adjoining arid regions. In this context, the effects of climate change on the response of natural montane Caucasian oak ( Quercus macranthera ) forests to outbreaks of Euproctis chrysorrhoea (Linnaeus), a polyphagous defoliator responsible for relatively short-lived damage in deciduous forest systems, especially those associated with lower elevations and warmer climatic conditions, were examined. title: Connecting landscapes, communities and knowledge: lessons from organizing the INSAKA symposium on participatory conservation
abstract: Participatory conservation is widely endorsed as policy, yet the deliberative platforms through which it is enacted are seldom examined as research objects. This article studies a three-phase international symposium convened in Namibia in November 2025 by the University of Namibia under the INSAKA Consortium. It asks what such a platform reveals about the conditions under which participation in conservation becomes substantive rather than procedural. title: 21st-century strong wind and heavy precipitation hazards in the Asian monsoon region related to mesoscale convective systems: climatology, variability, and trends
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) occur frequently throughout the Asian monsoon region (AMR) and exhibit distinct spatial distribution patterns, often associated with extreme weather events, including heavy rainfall, hail and tornadoes. To assess the hazardous impacts of MCSs and enhance disaster warning and response strategies, this study develops a database of MCSs across the AMR study domain from 2001 to 2023 using half-hourly infrared brightness temperature data and further examines their relationships with weather hazards based on observational data. title: Sown but not harvested: Unharvested annual crop area in Córdoba, Colombia, and its limited association with soils and El Niño-Southern Oscillation phases, 2007-2021
abstract: The share of sown area that reaches harvest is a component of agricultural production, yet the search made for this study found no municipal analysis of it for Córdoba, Colombia. This study aims to measure the unharvested share of annual crop area in the department's 30 municipalities and to examine its association with land capability and with El Niño-Southern Oscillation phases. title: Impact of climate change on surface temperature projections in Colombia’s principal natural regions
abstract: Climate change poses an increasing threat to Colombia, whose five principal natural regions (Andean, Caribbean, Orinoquia, Pacific, and Amazon) exhibit marked climatic and geographical diversity, increasing their vulnerability to rising surface temperatures. Projected temperatures across these regions were evaluated under the SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 scenarios using an ensemble of NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 models. title: Qmes: Quantum meta-learning for encoding selection in quantum kernel methods
abstract: Selecting an effective encoding quantum circuit is a key challenge in quantum kernel methods because different feature maps can lead to different performance. Conventional methods require constructing and evaluating every circuit for each new dataset, making it computationally expensive. We present Qmes, an open-source Python package that automatically recommends circuits through meta-learning. title: Climate Vulnerability to Food Security in a Non-Agrarian Buffer City of Indonesia's New Capital: A Descriptive Study of Balikpapan City
abstract: Balikpapan, a coastal, non-agrarian city serving as the primary logistics and residential hub supporting Indonesia's new capital (Ibu Kota Nusantara, IKN), faces two interconnected challenges: increasing exposure to climate-related hazards and a food system that relies heavily on external supplies for nearly all strategic commodities. abstract: Fascism has re-emerged as one of the most politically charged topics within the humanities and social sciences, and among the general public. Renewed debates over the fragility of liberal democracy and the appeal of authoritarianism, ultranationalism and political violence during periods of socio-economic and political instability have transformed fascism from what many observers once considered a purely historical phenomenon into a contemporary issue of growing concern. title: Characterizing the Composition and Reactivity of Dissolved Organic Matter: New Insights from Complementary Methods
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays important roles in numerous processes in both natural and engineered systems, ranging from carbon cycling to metal complexation to disinfection byproduct formation. Characterizing the composition of this complex mixture, which is comprised of thousands of molecules that vary in time and space, is critical for understanding its role and reactivity. title: Digital economy and urban green development in China: spatial spillovers and spatiotemporal heterogeneity
abstract: China’s transition toward a green economy remains constrained by rising energy consumption and persistently high carbon emissions. As a transformative force reshaping production processes and resource allocation, the digital economy (DE) is increasingly regarded as an important contributor to green development. title: Lightning in global chemistry-climate models: a review of parameterizations, evaluations, and future projections
abstract: Climate models are our main tool to project how global lightning activity may change in a warmer world. However, the spatial and temporal scales involved in cloud electrification are too small to be explicitly resolved, so lightning is typically simulated using empirical relationships with proxy variables such as cloud top height (CTH), convective precipitation, the product of convective available potential energy and precipitation, or upward ice flux.
