title: Clinician Acceptance of Large Language Model–Generated Discharge Summaries
abstract: Importance: Hospital discharge summaries are essential for continuity of care, but fragmented electronic health record (EHR) data can compromise their quality and safety. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for clinical documentation tasks despite limited evidence regarding their performance in health care settings compared with the current standard of care. title: Using resource selection functions (RSFs) to model the movement ecology of invasive predators in the last remaining habitat of the endangered Atlantic whitefish
abstract: Aquatic invasive species are among the top threats to freshwater fishes globally, causing declines in freshwater biodiversity and altering ecosystem functioning. Within Nova Scotia, Canada, invasive chain pickerel (Esox niger) and smallmouth bass (Micropterus dolomieu) have been found to reduce the abundance and diversity of native fishes. title: Drivers, Trade-Offs and Synergies of Food Security under SDG 2: An Integrative Review and Lessons for Malaysia
abstract: Food security is central to Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger), but it is shaped by forces that cut across economic, social and environmental goals. This review aimed to identify the positive and negative drivers of food security, map how SDG 2 interacts with other SDGs, and assess what this evidence means for Malaysia. The integrative review followed Whittemore and Knafl's five-stage method and was reported using PRISMA 2020. title: Checklist of introduced taxa in Romania
abstract: Invasive alien species are a major driver of global biodiversity loss and impose substantial ecological, economic and health costs. Up-to-date, standardised inventories of introduced taxa are a prerequisite for evidence-based biosecurity, for fulfilling reporting obligations under Regulation (EU) No 1143/2014 and the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and for tracking the pace and pathways of biological invasions. abstract: This study examines spatial association networks and associated factors of public sports service supply efficiency across 31 provincial-level regions in China. title: Health, Risk and Adaptation in Extreme Open Water Swimming: A Qualitative Study of Channel Swimmers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Participation in extreme open water swimming, including channel swimming, has increased markedly, yet health research has focused largely on quantifying risks rather than understanding athletes' lived experiences. This study explored how experienced channel swimmers perceive health issues, prevention strategies, and recovery across preparation, performance, and post-swim phases. abstract: La evaluación hidroacústica sustenta las estimaciones de biomasa y distribución de la anchoveta peruana (Engraulis ringens), pero su aceptación entre los usuarios de esa información está poco documentada. Este estudio caracterizó las percepciones de 76 especialistas en gestión ambiental sobre la tecnología hidroacústica y sobre la evaluación del recurso, y las contrastó con la literatura reciente de acústica pesquera. title: Microbial Culture Collections: Living Treasures of the Invisible World
abstract: Microbial culture collections are like a zoo, but instead of animals, they contain tiny living microbes. You cannot see these organisms with your eyes, but they can grow in special containers for many years, with food provided by scientists. Why do we keep the microbes? Microbes help us make medicines, clean the environment, and even make delicious foods such as yogurt and cheese. title: Natural mineral-supported green nanotechnology for oil-water separation and environmental remediation: surface engineering, separation mechanisms and scale-up perspectives
abstract: Natural mineral-derived nanomaterials offer a credible route to lower the cost and environmental burden of treating oil-contaminated water, yet their performance is often reported without a common framework linking mineral chemistry, surface modification, wetting state, pore architecture, operating conditions, and end-of-life risk. This Review critically examines quartz, zeolites, vermiculite, bentonite, kaolin, halloysite, attapulgite, and iron-bearing minerals as granular media, coatings, adsorbents, and membrane building blocks for oil-water separation and broader environmental remediation.

title: Comparative Performance of Oxford Nanopore Duplex and Simplex 16S rRNA Reads for eDNA ‐Based Prediction of Salmon Aquaculture Benthic Impacts
abstract: Environmental monitoring of salmon aquaculture increasingly uses eDNA-based bacterial community profiling, yet the practical value of Oxford Nanopore duplex sequencing remains uncertain due to low yield. We compared full-length 16S rRNA simplex and duplex Nanopore reads for predicting benthic environmental quality (EQ) at 15 Scottish salmon farms. abstract: Introduction Long-term motion records from aids-to-navigation buoys combine nonstationary environmental responses, mooring-state variations, and positioning errors. These components are difficult to separate when tension measurements and damage labels are unavailable. Methods We propose field-residual-preserving environment-conditioned paired-difference learning. title: Youth resilience in Ascension Island: a qualitative social-ecological approach
abstract: Background Resilience has been associated with positive mental health and wellbeing outcomes but has been scarcely studied in young people in remote geographical settings. The aim of this study was to explore resilience in young people living in the remote context of Ascension Island, South Atlantic ocean. abstract: Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis ( Bd ), the causative agent of chytridiomycosis, is one of the most significant emerging infectious pathogens affecting amphibians worldwide. Despite Brazil harboring the greatest amphibian diversity on planet, a comprehensive assessment of the occurrence patterns of Bd across the country remains lacking. abstract: Wetland ecosystems provide essential ecological functions and natural services that contribute to biodiversity conservation, environmental sustainability, and socioeconomic well-being. However, rapid urbanisation and infrastructural development in Rivers State, Nigeria, have placed increasing pressure on wetland ecosystems, creating a need for reliable methods of wetland mapping and monitoring. abstract: The rapid advancement of wearable electronics places ever‐increasing demands on the electrical and mechanical properties of materials. Cellulose offers renewability, low cost, and high durability for green wearables, but its weak electron‐donating ability and poor charge‐transport efficiency limit triboelectric performance. abstract: Water-lubricated polymer bearings are increasingly used in marine propulsion, yet achieving low friction, vibration attenuation, and durable wear resistance in corrosive, particle-contaminated water remains challenging. abstract: High-speed autonomous surface vessels require hull forms that balance resistance, running attitude, hydrodynamic stability, and mission-related constraints. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) supports detailed assessment of planing-hull performance, but knowledge generated by individual parametric studies is rarely reused in subsequent design projects. abstract: Strategies to strengthen regional water security will be essential for navigating a critical 21st-century environmental challenge: securing freshwater supplies against growing demands and increasingly severe climate extremes. This paper assesses the evolution of water security in the historically water-rich U.S. Northeast (NE) and Midwest (MW) to quantify their resilience to severe drought now and in the future. abstract: Against the backdrop of global carbon neutrality, the development targets and spatial distribution of renewable capacity such as wind and solar power are key to achieving the goals of the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). China’s 2035 NDC target specifies that wind and solar installed capacity should strive to reach 3,600 GW, but its spatial distribution involves multiple coupled constraints—resource endowment, integration space, and energy security—and is a typical cross-domain complex decision-making problem spanning the physical and social systems. abstract: Accurate short-term prediction of ship motions is essential for selecting operational areas and time windows, which are critical for maritime safety and operational efficiency. Traditional physics-based methods provide high accuracy but are computationally expensive, limiting their use in onboard applications. title: Integrating vegetation phenology and SWOT-derived surface water dynamics for improved county-scale winter wheat yield prediction
abstract: Winter wheat yield is shaped by crop growth status and surface hydrological conditions. However, remote-sensing approaches based primarily on vegetation index (VI) time series may not fully represent the surrounding surface-water environment in county-scale yield prediction. We integrated growth-stage VI features with surface-water dynamics derived from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission to predict county-level winter wheat yield in Henan Province, China. abstract: AIM: To estimate RSV hospitalisation rates among children ≤ 2 years in New South Wales (NSW), Australia over two decades; to examine how rates varied by age, prematurity and selected co-morbidities and to describe temporal, seasonal and geographic patterns in RSV hospitalisation across NSW. abstract: Fish feeding behavior is a vital predictor of fish activity and well-being in aquaculture, but manual assessment is time consuming, subjective, and hard to generalize. In this study, we propose a label-free framework for fish feeding-related activity discrimination by integrating ensemble object detection, multi-object tracking, trajectory-based feature engineering and domain-adapted contrastive representation learning. abstract: Thermokarst lakes are critical components of Arctic carbon cycling, yet their ice phenology remains poorly characterized at regional scales. We present the first comprehensive analysis of ice-on and ice-off timing across 30 774 lakes on the Alaska North Slope using Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) classified by a Random Forest (RF) model trained using labels derived from Sentinel-2 optical imagery and ERA5 temperature data for the period 2019–2023. abstract: Introduction To address the growing global type 2 diabetes mellitus burden, dietary intervention via dipeptidyl peptidase‐4 (DPP‐4) inhibition provides a viable approach for glycemic control. abstract: A facility receiving mixed plastic waste must decide which part of that waste can generate credits. The decision turns on programme rules rather than on the material, and this study quantifies how far those rules diverge. title: Investigating effects of the macroalga Caulerpa prolifera on transplant success of the seagrass Halodule wrightii to improve restoration
abstract: Introduction Seagrass restoration efforts have been motivated by global decreases in coverage associated with anthropogenic influences on the environment. In the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), FL, USA, seagrass declined by 75% between 2011 and 2021. During this time, abundance of the native macroalga Caulerpa prolifera increased substantially in this system. As restoration efforts began in the IRL, it became apparent that varying abundance of C. prolifera could impact the recovery of seagrass. abstract: Background Endometriosis (EM) is a chronic estrogen-dependent inflammatory disorder characterized by ectopic endometrial implantation and immune dysregulation. Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure has been associated with EM, but the underlying molecular links remain unclear. This study aimed to identify immune-associated molecular targets linking DEHP exposure to EM through integrated immunotoxicogenomic and transcriptomic analyses. abstract: Long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction for maritime traffic monitoring and route planning requires both a prompt response to manoeuvres and control of error accumulation. UnifiedInternalMoE combines a motion-prior residual expert with four temporal predictors in a separate checkpoint for each region and seed. abstract: Introduction Sarcopenia, an age-related disorder characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, is a growing global health concern with limited effective nutritional interventions. title: Does channel pattern matter for SWOT river discharge?
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite estimates river discharge from observed water surface elevation, width and slope. Its algorithms treat each river reach as a single effective channel. About 58% of the 58,790 alluvial reaches in a global channel-pattern dataset have multiple channels, yet it is not clear whether channel pattern affects the accuracy of SWOT discharge. abstract: Due to the uncertainties associated with the traditional decision-making methods for evaluating design and operational parameters of subsea systems, selecting a subsea cooler is extremely challenging and hard. abstract: The German travelers Friedrich W. Hemprich and Christian G. abstract: We provide the first voucher-based review of Ellobium Röding, 1798 (Gastropoda, Ellobiidae) in Vietnam and confirm four species. Ellobium tornatelliforme (Petit de la Saussaye, 1843) is recorded from Vietnam for the first time. We update the distributions and habitat data of E. aurisjudae (Linnaeus, 1758), E. aurismidae (Linnaeus, 1758), and E. chinense (L. Pfeiffer, 1854) based on voucher specimens. An identification key and revised species accounts are provided, establishing a taxonomically verified baseline for future taxonomic, biogeographical, and conservation studies.

title: Updated occurrence, habitat associations, and genomic resources of syngnathids in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia
abstract: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. abstract: Autonomous robots are transforming industries by enhancing efficiency and precision. Compared with rigid robots, soft robots use compliant materials with intrinsic deformability and agility, offering greater adaptability and safer interactions in unstructured environments. abstract: Long-baseline (LBL) time difference of arrival (TDOA) localization in shallow water often suffers from degraded performance when the sound speed is unknown. abstract: This study aims to investigate the multi-target molecular mechanisms through which synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression using an integrated approach of network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. A representative library of traditional and novel SPAs was selected, and their toxicity profiles and carcinogenicity were predicted via ADMETlab 3.0. abstract: Human-AI collaboration is increasingly initiated from the bottom up, as employees independently incorporate artificial intelligence into everyday work before organizations fully institutionalize its use. abstract: Millimeter-wave radar is highly valuable for all-weather autonomous driving perception due to its excellent environmental robustness and range-velocity measuring capability. abstract: Accurate ship trajectory prediction supports encounter-risk screening and vessel traffic services, but latent intent makes future motion multi-modal across temporal scales. abstract: The Holbina–Razim lake system serves as a calibration testbed for satellite-based algal pigment analysis during severe algal blooms (SABs) in deltaic environments. abstract: Remote sensing (RS) classification models have become dominant tools for RS image analysis, achieving state-of-the-art performance in many downstream tasks. abstract: Climate change can redistribute environmentally suitable conditions for Phlebotomus vectors in semi-arid regions, but conventional habitat-suitability models provide limited information on the broader environmental dimensions of future expansion. abstract: Tipping transitions are abrupt reorganisations in which a system leaves one statistical regime for another. By establishing an accurate nonlinear mapping between geomagnetic vectors and spatial coordinates, the proposed method prevents gradient degradation and the consequent decline in accuracy and stability observed in existing geomagnetic matching methods. title: Attack detection in WSN using Taylor Walrus Optimization Algorithm-based Dense Google Forward Harmonic Net
abstract: In the Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), the Sensor Node (SN) transfers the data to Base Station (BS). Attack detection in WSN is critical for protecting accuracy, trustworthiness, and maintaining the confidentiality of sensor information sent to BS. Effective attack identification helps to prevent malicious intrusions, which impacts the network performance, while increasing its longevity by avoiding unnecessary retransmission and node failures. abstract: In recent times, software fault prediction (SFP) has become a crucial task to maintain the quality and reliability of software products in the complex, high-dimensional, and nonlinear data scenario. SFP necessitates a huge volume of historical software metrics data to efficiently identify the hidden patterns, trends, and relations among those metrics. abstract: Reliable image-quality assessment is important in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle surveys because degraded frames can compromise mapping and downstream visual analysis. This paper presents Global-Target Assessment and Regression (GloTAR), a lightweight multi-domain No-Reference Image Quality Assessment framework combining whole-image context with saliency-derived regional evidence and Kolmogorov–Arnold Network layers for compact feature reduction and regression. abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is more popular in transformative technology, and it is employed in healthcare, industrial automation, agriculture, and environmental monitoring. Despite their adaptability, the main challenge within WSNs is node localization, where the accuracy of sensor node position is crucial for the functionality of these applications. Further, existing research often fails to provide optimal solutions under the complex conditions. Thus, this work introduces an Alpha and Beta Horse Herd Optimization (ABHHO) algorithm to address the limitations of the conventional techniques.

title: Time adaptive clinical data driven cardiovascular disease detection using multi-objective features-based residual CapsNet with coordinate attention
abstract: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, primarily caused by blockages in coronary arteries due to plaques or fatty deposits. Early identification and precise diagnosis are crucial for timely treatment, reducing disease severity, improving patient quality of life, and preventing complications. Objective: To develop an advanced, interpretable, and accurate CVD detection framework that addresses limitations in conventional methods related to feature representation and capturing complex relationships within the data. abstract: Concrete subjected to semi‐immersion in sulfate environments exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity in deterioration, particularly in the region above the water line. In this zone, capillary transport and moisture evaporation jointly promote the upward migration and localized accumulation of aggressive ions. abstract: Secondary ice production (SIP) remains a major uncertainty in understanding deep convection because its rates and controlling conditions are poorly constrained. title: Risk-informed decision making for beach nourishment: integrating technical, environmental and operational criteria
abstract: Beach nourishment requires repeated decisions during planning, construction, monitoring, and maintenance. These decisions rely on technical, environmental, and operational information collected throughout the project. However, monitoring results do not always lead to clear management responses, and different indicators may provide conflicting assessments. This study proposes a practical risk-informed framework for operational decision making in beach nourishment projects. abstract: Natural gas consumption (NGC) is an important consideration in energy planning, supply management, and the efficient operation of natural gas distribution systems. Among the meteorological variables affecting NGC, temperature is one of the most widely used predictors because of its close relationship with heating-related consumption. In this study, average NGC per customer in Konya, Türkiye, was predicted using an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) under different input configurations based on Ambient Temperature (AT) and Soil Temperature (ST). abstract: The unprecedented Greenland Ice Sheet melt in summer 2012 provides a natural experiment to evaluate how spaceborne passive microwave brightness temperature ( T B ) responds to extreme melt on diurnal timescales. We analyzed multi-frequency AMSR2 T B from GCOM–W over a northwestern Greenland site (SIGMA–A) and compared the radiometric evolution with in situ snow temperatures and surface energy balance terms derived from automated weather station meteorology. title: Introducing Water Treatment Community College Students to State-of-the-Art Technologies Using Place-Based Case Studies and Real-World Problem-Solving
abstract: Recent technological advances and a rapidly changing environment necessitate frequent updating of postsecondary curriculum materials for students in natural resource management programs. In particular, water quality and quantity challenges worldwide and the critical need to recruit young professionals into water treatment careers require engaging, up-to-date materials for community college programs that train students in drinking water treatment. title: IoT-based multi-sensor data fusion for freshwater ecosystem monitoring: a case study of Lake Tana, Ethiopia
abstract: This paper investigated an efficient real-time data collection mechanism for Lake Tana using sensor fusion and the Internet of Things (IoT). The rapid proliferation of invasive aquatic weeds in freshwater ecosystems necessitates robust long-term monitoring and efficient data acquisition techniques. Smart IoT-based sensor networks enable real-time acquisition of key aquatic parameters, such as pH, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and chlorophyll-a. abstract: Lake Tana, Ethiopia, harbours the world's only remaining cyprinid species flock, making it globally significant for conservation. Yet, these resources face mounting anthropogenic pressures from overfishing and land use changes. We assessed fish assemblage structure and seasonal dynamics in the Gulf of Lake Tana from September 2024 to August 2025 and land use land cover (LULC) changes from 2000 to 2025 using Landsat and Sentinel imagery. abstract: This study evaluated the biomass production of the microalga Scenedesmus acuminatus using aquaculture effluent as an alternative culture medium. The experiment was conducted in a controlled laboratory environment comparing two treatments: cultivation in aquaculture effluent and in a commercial NPK medium. abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar inversion is essential for characterizing subsurface structures. While full waveform inversion is computationally expensive and unstable, optimization-based low-dimensional structural inversion offers a more efficient and robust alternative. abstract: This study applied synthetic biology principles to engineer Saccharomyces cerevisiae with a heterologous astaxanthin pathway, creating a high-yield strain. abstract: Planning renewable-energy expansion at the national scale requires wind maps far more detailed than sparse meteorological networks and coarse reanalysis grids can typically offer. This study introduces PC-SRCNN, a physics-constrained, self-supervised super-resolution framework that lifts ERA5 wind fields over Brazil from a native 0.25° grid to 0.025°, folding in soft regularization terms for horizontal kinematic consistency and the logarithmic vertical wind profile. abstract: Smart tourism has become an important means of enhancing the competitiveness and service quality of theme parks. However, limited research has explored how visitors perceive the importance and performance of specific smart service components in Chinese theme parks. This study assesses tourists' perceptions of smart tourism services at Ningbo Fangte Oriental Dawn using a case study approach, a questionnaire survey, and the Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) framework. title: A lightweight defect grading detection method for quick-frozen dumplings based on improved YOLOv11n
abstract: Fine-grained defect grading and differentiated quality management of quick-frozen dumplings remain challenging in complex industrial environments. To support fine-grained quality evaluation, a defect grading dataset containing four quality levels (normal, minor defect, moderate defect, and severe defect) was constructed. Based on this dataset, a lightweight defect grading detection model, SCSL-YOLO, based on YOLOv11n is proposed. abstract: La producción de hidrocarburos es estratégica para México, por lo que herramientas de pronóstico precisas son fundamentales. abstract: Probabilistic forecasts of Photovoltaic (PV) power are useful only if their intervals remain calibrated at new sites, in new seasons, and with the information available when forecasts are issued. This review asks whether AI models deliver such forecasts. Journal articles from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from OpenAIRE and Crossref. This study compared four original multispectral bands, five vegetation indices, and their combination for segmentation-free, pixel-based Random Forest mapping of healthy and unhealthy Pinus nigra canopies in Bingöl, Türkiye. abstract: Hydrogeological studies with a focus on the cryosphere became numerous during the last years due to the sensitivity of snowfalls to the climate variations. This study investigated the Gran Sasso Range in central Italy, which is a carbonate mountain characterized by rainfalls and snowfalls. A study of stable water isotopes (δ 2 H and δ 18 O) of rainfall, snow, ephemeral and perennial streams and groundwater is proposed to constrain the principal processes involved in the aquifer recharge. title: A Review of Attacks on Hardware Implementations of Cryptographic Algorithms
abstract: With the increase in online data exchange, transactions, and payments, cryptographic techniques for securing communication over networks have become an area of concern. The vast majority of cryptographic algorithm designs are intended to be mathematically secure and resistant to known cryptanalytic attacks. abstract: Away from the conventional Logistic Regression (LR) technique, this study presents a novel Naïve Bayes (NB) integration with Markov Chain (MC) and Cellular Automata (CA) for modelling urban land use change. abstract: Vibrio parahaemolyticus most often causes self-limited gastroenteritis after seafood consumption; deep-seated invasive disease remains uncommon. We describe a fulminant case of necrotizing fasciitis with septic shock caused by the rare sequence type ST859 in a 71-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class B), who had handled raw seafood two days before admission. title: RPDL-YOLO: An efficient YOLOv8 framework for small bird detection in airport airside environments
abstract: Bird intrusions into airport security zones pose significant threats to aviation safety. However, the small size, rapid movement, and irregular flight patterns of birds often result in missed detections and false alarms in vision-based surveillance systems, especially in complex open-sky environments with low contrast and significant background interference. abstract: The critical assessments of computational hit-finding experiments (CACHE) are prospective benchmarking exercises where small molecule ligands predicted for a nominated protein of interest are procured and tested experimentally. abstract: Free-space optical communication is emerging as a cornerstone technology for next-generation wireless networks, driven by the escalating demand for fiber-optic-level data rates in applications ranging from data center interconnects to satellite and deep-space communications. abstract: This article proposes a safe and efficient positioning control method for offshore wind turbine installation vessels (OWTIVs), addressing the challenges posed by unmeasured multi-source disturbances and thruster constraints. First, a prescribed-time composite disturbance observer (PTCDO) is developed to accurately estimate multi-source disturbances. abstract: Vertebrate extinctions are one of the earliest and most conspicuous examples of human-driven environmental change. On continents, large mammals were the most obvious casualties, but many continental bird species went extinct during the same period. A far greater number of island birds disappeared as humans spread to more isolated landmasses. abstract: Flash floods occur frequently in South Africa, causing infrastructure damage, economic losses, and loss of life. Accurate delineation of flood inundation extents is essential for flood risk assessment, disaster management, and mitigation planning. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the height above nearest drainage (HAND) method in delineating flood inundation extents for two flood events in Durban and Mthatha, South Africa. abstract: Compound weather events can have severe societal and ecological impacts, yet their joint spatial–temporal dynamical drivers remain insufficiently understood. Here, we conceptualize spatial–temporal compound extremes as circulation‐driven extremes arising from a specific preferred circulation trajectory that can generate multiple extremes across space and time. title: Pyramid-level training with stain normalization for breast cancer lymph-node metastasis segmentation in whole-slide images
abstract: Whole-slide histopathology images encode metastatic tissue information simultaneously at multiple spatial scales, from fine cellular morphology at high magnification to broad tissue architecture at low magnification. Existing segmentation models commonly operate at a single fixed resolution, leaving complementary information distributed across the whole-slide image pyramid underused. abstract: The rising incidence and impact of natural disasters have thus increased the need for efficient risk transfer solutions. Conventional indemnity insurance contracts tend to inadequately address financial risks associated with natural disasters due to transaction costs, time-consuming claims settlement, and moral hazard. abstract: Surface melt is a key component of Antarctic ice-shelf surface hydrology and an important indicator of atmospheric forcing. The Shackleton Ice Shelf experiences particularly substantial summer surface melt, yet its seasonal evolution and spatial organization remain insufficiently resolved at fine scales. Here, we aim to characterize surface melt variability over the Shackleton Ice Shelf using a 40 m Sentinel-1 SAR record covering the 2015–2023 melt seasons. abstract: The evaluation of informative path planning algorithms for autonomous vehicles is often hindered by fragmented execution pipelines and limited transferability between simulation and real-world deployment. This paper introduces a unified architecture that decouples high-level decision-making from vehicle-specific control, enabling algorithms to be evaluated consistently across different abstraction levels without modification. abstract: Cross-Project Defect Prediction (CPDP) identifies defects in an unlabeled project (target) by using the historical data of other source projects. abstract: Monitoring crowd conditions is a challenge with just CCTV monitors. abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) enables the fabrication of complex polymeric components; however, the tensile performance of printed parts is strongly influenced by processing conditions and can be difficult to predict when only a limited number of experimental observations are available. This study investigates the use of linear interpolation-based data augmentation combined with an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) for predicting the tensile strength of FDM-printed polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified (PETG) specimens. abstract: Maritime technical and vocational education and training (TVET) must reconcile internationally regulated competence, occupational performance, and rapid technological change. abstract: Vision-based fall detection is increasingly relevant to assistive healthcare, rehabilitation, and older-adult monitoring; however, practical deployment requires a favorable balance among detection accuracy, model complexity, and inference efficiency. The current study proposes FGLD-YOLO, a lightweight fall detection model derived from YOLOv10. FasterNet replaces the original backbone to reduce computational overhead, while a Generalized Feature Pyramid Network (GFPN) is incorporated into the neck to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of terrestrial net ecosystem productivity in China during 2001–2020 and its association with potential evapotranspiration
abstract: Introduction Accurately quantifying net ecosystem productivity (NEP) in China’s terrestrial ecosystems is crucial for improving regional and global carbon budget assessments. However, uncertainties remain because of limited spatial and temporal representativeness of observational data and incomplete understanding of environmental factors associated with NEP variability. Methods We compiled monthly observations from 229 eddy covariance flux sites and developed a multi-model selection framework to estimate NEP dynamics across China’s terrestrial forests, grasslands, croplands, and wetlands. title: Contribution of polyethylene fibers on the static and dynamic mechanical properties of lightweight cement‐based materials prepared with Enteromorpha prolifera powder
abstract: This study investigates the effects of polyethylene (PE) fibers on the flowability, density, thermal conductivity, static and dynamic mechanical properties of Enteromorpha prolifera powder (EPP)‐based lightweight cementitious materials. PE fibers were incorporated at volume fractions of 0%–1.0%, and Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar tests were conducted to evaluate mechanical performance under different strain rates. title: DGIM-SAM: dual-kernel gated interaction modulation and spectral adaptive modulation for real-time wildfire detection
abstract: Wildfire detection in unconstrained natural scenes is challenging due to weak fire responses, ambiguous smoke boundaries, and interference from clouds, haze, vegetation, and illumination changes. To address these challenges, we propose DGIM-SAM , a real-time wildfire detection framework that combines dual-kernel gated interaction modulation with spectral adaptive modulation. abstract: Background: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancer classification is the process of identifying and categorizing cancers that occur in the GI tract based on their morphological, histopathological, and molecular characteristics. Existing GI cancer classification systems often struggle with low interpretability and limited generalizability across diverse datasets. This study aims to improve the accuracy of classifying cancer. Six supervised and six unsupervised methods are benchmarked here on two specimens sharing the same eight-channel layout: an isotropic aluminum 7075-T6 plate and a quasi-isotropic AS4/8552 panel with an adhesively bonded stiffener. title: Research Progress on the Coupling Mechanism of Climate Change Mitigation and Carbon Footprint
abstract: The trend of global warming continues to intensify, and carbon emissions generated by human activities keep rising, which has become a key contradiction hindering the sustainable development of ecosystems. Carbon footprint can quantitatively describe the carbon emission intensity of human production and living activities and the resulting environmental pressure. This indicator has a two-way interactive and mutually restrictive coupling feedback relationship with climate change mitigation. title: A consistency-constrained fusion network for audio-visual emotion recognition
abstract: Audio-Visual Emotion Recognition (AVER) from speech and facial expression is a fundamental task in affective computing, yet effectively fusing multimodal features while accounting for both modality consistency and discrepancy remains a challenging problem. Existing approaches either neglect modality discrepancy or model consistency and discrepancy in separate feature spaces. title: Multi-fidelity heteroscedastic Gaussian processes for cavitation wall-load prediction
abstract: Predicting the peak wall pressure generated by a collapsing bubble cluster requires expensive resolved simulations and must account for variations in the initial bubble arrangement. A probabilistic surrogate is constructed by combining heteroscedastic Gaussian-process regression with sparse variational inference and a nonlinear autoregressive link between coarse- and fine-grid simulations. title: Artifact-aware lightweight dermoscopic lesion segmentation with reproducible corruption robustness evaluation
abstract: Automated dermoscopic lesion segmentation is a key step in computer-aided skin cancer analysis, yet lightweight models for resource-constrained dermoscopic image analysis can be unstable when images contain acquisition artifacts such as hair, specular highlights, skin lines, and air bubbles. This paper addresses this problem by proposing an artifact-aware lightweight U-shaped segmentation framework together with a reproducible corruption benchmark for robustness evaluation. title: Toward a Renewed and Broader Pro‐Climate Alliance?
abstract: After decades of increasing greenhouse gas emissions, climate policies, though fragile and hesitant, have finally started producing substantial effects in the late 2010s. These policies had internal weaknesses regarding governance, inequalities, and biodiversity, but the backlash that followed is also the result of deliberate obstruction. abstract: Complete coverage path planning (CCPP) is a core enabling technology for autonomous operation and navigation of mobile robots and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). However, in large-scale and complex environments, due to the lack of directional guidance in population evolution, existing heuristic path planners often suffer from slow convergence, premature trapping in local optima, and excessive turning maneuvers along the planned tour. title: Karst wetland reclamation increases the proportion of inorganic sulfur in total sulfur: associations with sulfate-reducing bacteria abundance and soil enzyme activity
abstract: Karst wetlands are fragile and critical ecosystems for soil sulfur biogeochemical cycling. In this study, six typical land-use types in the Huixian karst wetland of Guilin, southern China, were selected to investigate the variations in soil physicochemical properties, four inorganic sulfur fractions, soil enzyme activities, and sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) abundance across 0–40 cm soil profiles. title: A novel topology-guided adaptive strategy for automated nuclear-cytoplasmic H-score quantification in immunohistochemistry
abstract: Automated quantification of immunohistochemistry (IHC) supports reproducible biomarker assessment, but routine use remains limited by cellular crowding and staining variability. We present a workflow for batch quantification of nuclear and cytoplasmic IHC staining using H-scores, without task-specific model training. title: Cross-Source Validation of Pressure-Ratio-Driven Surrogate Models for Predicting Steam Ejector Entrainment Ratio
abstract: Pressure-ratio-based surrogates provide compact estimates of steam-ejector entrainment ratios (ERs), but internal accuracy does not establish experimental predictive reliability. This study evaluated four original regression configurations using 111 CFD development records and 18 experimental records representing 17 unique conditions in the same ejector geometry. Leave-one-out, input-pair-grouped and subset-holdout evaluations were combined with independent H1 testing, input-coverage analysis and TreeSHAP. title: Mapping 20-years winter wheat dynamics in global primary planting areas using Gaussian mixture models with adaptive thresholds
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of winter wheat is essential for ensuring global food security. Currently, limited research has focused on the global dynamics of wheat over the past decades. In this study, we propose a novel framework to map fractional winter wheat dynamics from 2001 to 2020 at 1 km resolution in key global planting areas from MODIS satellite data, utilizing a flexible Gaussian mixture model (GMM). title: Fungi, Yeasts, and Microalgae use in Petroleum-hydrocarbon Bioremediation: Taxonomic Diversity, Enzymatic Pathways, and Sustainable Applications
abstract: This review aimed to understand the enzymatic mechanisms and diversity of mycobiota, including fungi and yeasts, as well as microalgae, and their applications in degrading hydrocarbon contaminants in soil and aquatic environments. Evidence from 122 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2014 and 2025 was integrated using bibliometric analysis, phylogenetic synthesis based on internal transcribed spacer (ITS) taxonomic markers, and analysis of annotated hydrocarbon-degrading enzymes. title: SHAPE-Net: structure-aware and confidence-guided learning for semi-supervised medical image segmentation
abstract: Remarkable progress has recently been made in semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Nevertheless, issues related to unreliable pseudo-labels and insufficient feature discriminability remain unresolved. To mitigate the aforementioned limitations, a multi-level collaborative structural perception learning network (SHAPE-Net) is proposed based on a teacher-student framework from the perspective of structural consistency, enabling the unified and coordinated optimization of input perturbations, semantic representations and discriminative learning. title: Real-time visual wrinkle segmentation during paper deep drawing
abstract: Paper deep drawing, inspired by the metal forming technique, is investigated as sustainable alternative to plastic packaging, aiming to achieve airtight sealing and versatile design. However, paper’s inherent tendency to form wrinkles complicates the production process, making it difficult to achieve consistent quality. To effectively control the forming of wrinkles, a runtime-optimized algorithm capable of quickly detecting them for precise material flow manipulation is required. title: The Global Lakes Explorer: a basin-to-global scale data visualisation application for the assessment of nutrient emissions to lakes
abstract: Phosphorus and nitrogen are critical plant nutrients, essential for fertiliser production and global food security. However, poor management of anthropogenic nutrient cycles leads to losses associated with pollution of water bodies, driving eutrophication, biodiversity loss, and methane emissions. Addressing these interconnected challenges requires a sustainable, integrated, and, where possible, circular approach across the entire nutrient cycle. title: Restoration 2 : contributing to a “global knowledge commons” for ecosystem restoration
abstract: Restoration knowledge is often weakly connected across global frameworks, formal evidence, local guidance, practitioner experience and monitoring practice, limiting the ability of practitioners and communities to find, evaluate and adapt relevant knowledge without erasing the particularities of place. Here, we argue for an open and collectively governed restoration knowledge commons: a shared infrastructure through which restoration knowledge can be discovered, interpreted, updated and reused under transparent rules. title: Climate-aware photovoltaic technology selection using hybrid BWM–CRITIC, MARCOS, and explainable surrogate modeling
abstract: Selecting photovoltaic (PV) technology for a specific location requires consideration of both local operating conditions and technology-specific characteristics. This study proposes a climate-aware Multi-criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework integrating the Best–Worst Method (BWM), Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC), and Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to COmpromise Solution (MARCOS) for PV technology selection. abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptive object detection (UDA-OD) transfers detectors from labeled source domains to unlabeled target domains, yet mean-teacher methods still suffer from noisy pseudo-labels and cross-domain feature misalignment. Existing prototype-enhanced approaches retain three limitations: single centroids cannot model intra-class multi-modal feature dispersion; discrete fixed-scale extraction causes detection blind spots for extreme-size objects; and coarse prototype matching is vulnerable to degenerate pseudo-label predictions. title: PILOT: Physics-Informed Optimized LightGBM for Edge-Based Predictive Maintenance
abstract: In Industry 4.0 applications, predictive maintenance is one of the frequently used methods for optimizing equipment reliability and maintenance costs. This paper proposes a new framework for edge-based machine fault detection, Physics-Informed Optimized LightGBM for Edge-Based Predictive Maintenance (PILOT), using a public dataset, AI4I 2020. The approach derives physics-informed interaction features from sensor data and uses Optuna to optimize the LightGBM hyperparameters. title: Classification of European free-floating aquatic vegetation (Lemnetea) to the association level
abstract: Aims : To develop a comprehensive, consistent and unequivocal phytosociological classification of European free-floating aquatic vegetation of the class Lemnetea to the association level. Study area : Europe. Methods : We analysed a European dataset comprising 125,029 vegetation plots and applied heterogeneity-constrained random resampling to derive representative subsets. abstract: Lower prediction error on an unseen battery dataset does not necessarily demonstrate transferable degradation learning. A model may better align its prediction level without improving its ability to follow changes in individual cells. This study presents an evidence-gated framework for evaluating cross-dataset battery state-of-health (SOH) transfer. title: Uncertainty-aware open-set transfer diagnosis of rotating machinery via class-wise adaptive decision boundaries and enhanced target clustering
abstract: Open-set transfer diagnosis of rotating machinery aims to classify target samples from shared fault classes while rejecting unseen target classes under domain shifts. Although open-set domain adaptation has been introduced to handle unseen fault classes in the target domain, reliable separation between known and unknown samples remains challenging. title: Multimodal nondestructive evaluation for structural assessment of composite wind turbine blades
abstract: Composite wind turbine blades carry load through laminates, sandwich panels and adhesive joints, where damage can develop beneath an intact surface. Blade geometry, environmental exposure and offshore access constrain inspection. This review compares optical and thermal inspection, ultrasonic and acoustic methods, electromagnetic techniques, and strain and vibration monitoring through their measurement principles and practical limits. title: Hydrodynamics of robotic microswimmers in confinement
abstract: Inspired by seminal work by E. M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a centimeter-sized prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail. title: Multi-scale simulations of wind farm impacts on nighttime near-surface temperature in complex terrain
abstract: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. abstract: Riparian buffers, vegetated waterways, streambank stabilization practices, and floodplain reconnection projects collectively constitute the riparian restoration toolkit through which agricultural watershed compliance programs address nonpoint source nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment, and pathogen loadings from cropland and pasture. title: Metamodel-based methodology for uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity analysis of tailings dam-breach flows
abstract: Tailings dam-breach analyses are essential for flood-hazard assessment, emergency planning and risk estimation, but their results are strongly affected by uncertainties in breach development, released volume and tailings rheology. This study proposes an efficient probabilistic methodology that integrates uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis for tailings dam-breach studies. title: Modeling leakage current in naturally contaminated insulators using linear regression for transmission line diagnostics
abstract: Natural contamination can significantly influence the surface conductivity of high-voltage ceramic insulators and increase the risk of flashover. This study proposes a modeling framework based on multivariate linear regression to characterize leakage current behavior induced by three contamination types: dust, moss, and flashover residues. title: Automatic Detection of Physiological Attributes from Verbal Communication during Time-Critical Medical Events
abstract: In this study, we present a proof-of-concept system exploring the feasibility of automatically capturing physiological values during the primary survey phase of trauma resuscitation-a complex, time-sensitive evaluation of severely injured patients. We developed and evaluated a speech-driven activity recognition system designed to detect and extract key physiological parameters (e.g., age, manual blood pressure, Glasgow Coma Scale) from spoken clinical dialogue in real-time. abstract: A central goal in ecology is to understand the distribution of abundance and species roles in ecosystem functioning among species in communities. The mass ratio hypothesis emphasizes the importance of common taxa, and the diversity insurance hypothesis highlights the potential role of rare taxa. abstract: Autonomous navigation in broken-ice fields faces two key risks: observation uncertainty of ice floes due to sensor noise, and risks of successive collisions and collective jamming from dense ice aggregation. abstract: Battery-driven passenger ferries offer meaningful environmental benefits over conventional propulsion, yet the large-scale lithium-ion systems that make this possible bring with them a set of safety challenges that are still poorly understood in the maritime context. Thermal runaway, flammable gas generation, and the risk of deflagration in confined shipboard compartments cannot be adequately evaluated with the static probability–consequence models that remain standard practice in maritime safety engineering. abstract: Airports have evolved from simple transit points into complex tourism gateways that shape the travel experience and generate significant non-aeronautical revenues. This study provides an innovative perspective by highlighting how each airport’s unique operating context affects the strategies available to airport managers for increasing non-aeronautical revenues while enhancing passenger satisfaction. abstract: Introduction Indoor dust is increasingly recognised as an important medium for human exposure to microplastics and associated chemical contaminants. This study investigated the occurrence and characteristics of microplastics and emerging chemical contaminants in non-residential indoor environments and explored their potential implications for human exposure and food-chain transfer. abstract: The bocachico Prochilodus magdalenae, Colombia's most ecologically and economically important native freshwater fish, has declined sharply under compounding anthropogenic pressures, yet whether climate anomalies compromise its gamete quality remains unexplored. This species shows two annual reproductive peaks (May-July and October-December), offering a natural model for comparing reproductive performance under contrasting climatic conditions. abstract: Optimization of channel capacity in Channel State Information (CSI)-assisted Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems is a critical need for beyond 5G and future 6G wireless communication systems, in which non-linear propagation and time-varying fading channels significantly affect the channel capacity. abstract: This study examines the relationship between aquaculture production, macroeconomic development and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Bangladesh over the period 1973–2024. Using annual time-series data, the study applies the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds-testing approach to investigate both short-run dynamics and long-run relationships among GHG emissions, real GDP per capita, aquaculture production, gross capital formation, trade openness and inflation. abstract: The St. Helens seismic zone is a dextral fault zone in the Cascade Arc upper crust that underlies the Mount St. Helens volcanic complex, in which two earthquakes of magnitude 5 or greater have been recorded since 1960. abstract: Introduction “Alt-text” is a textual substitute for visual information on digital platforms, primarily by users of screen readers. Effective image description is crucial for inclusive, accessible communication; unfortunately, alt-text creation is often limited by the time and skill constraints of the humans writing it. This baseline study aimed to develop an AI-driven method to semi-automate alt-text generation, with minimal expert moderation, for publicly released science images from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory. abstract: Frequent topology changes in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) often result in unstable routing paths, increased energy consumption, and reduced network lifetime. abstract: Purpose of the study: This study aims to identify and analyze the spatial distribution of landslide susceptibility in South Central Timor Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, using Landsat 8 imagery and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) by integrating land cover, rainfall, slope, and soil type parameters. abstract: The diurnal cycle of precipitation serves as a fundamental diagnostic of the climate system's energy budget and hydrological cycle. Yet comprehensive evaluations of both its regular diurnal and irregular intermittent components across multiple satellite and reanalysis products against extensive ground-based observations remain limited. abstract: This study was carried out in the Saraya Department, Kedougou Region, Senegal, where groundwater is heavily used for drinking, irrigation and industrial activities. It aims to determine the hydrochemical characteristics and to identify the main geochemical processes that govern groundwater composition, as well as to assess water suitability for drinking and irrigation. Geochemical diagrams, water quality index, quality parameters such as TDS, total hardness (TH), SAR, Na%, RSC, PI and the Wilcox and USSL diagrams were used. title: The Digital Economy and the Challenge of Sustainable Development in the Arab World (The Experience of the United Arab Emirates)
abstract: The digital economy is considered one of the most important economic resources in the current era. It has contributed to changing traditional economic concepts concerning the definition of economic resources and how they can be used to address existing economic and social challenges. The digital economy relies on human knowledge as the cornerstone of the information and technological revolution and as a means of achieving sustainable development. This research highlights the role of the digital economy in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals in Arab countries, focusing on the United Ara

title: Image watermarking with adversarial attack on secret key networks: From zero-bit to semantic vectors
abstract: Imperceptible watermarks are essential for ensuring authenticity and protecting image creators' rights. While zero-bit watermarking offers strong imperceptibility and robustness, it remains vulnerable to security threats such as counterfeiting and watermark replacement, and its signatures contain no semantic information. To address these limitations, we propose a secure and semantic watermarking framework based on a Secret Key Network (SKN). title: Robotic search and rescue in earthquake-collapsed buildings: capabilities, evidence gaps, and a roadmap for human-multi-robot rescue
abstract: Following an earthquake, rescue robots must search for and assist trapped individuals in complex environments characterized by unstable rubble, narrow cavities, darkness, dust, and unreliable communications. This paper reviews the technical evidence for seven categories of robots within the seven-stage mission chain of search and rescue (SAR) in building collapse scenarios, covering unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs); tracked, wheeled, and reconfigurable robots; quadrupedal robots; snake-like and continuum robots; humanoid and hybrid robots; heavy-duty engineering robots; and casualty evacuation
institutions: Ministry of Emergency Management of the People's Republic of China

title: Risk Assessment and Mitigation for International Multimodal Container Transport Networks Under Compound Flood and Tropical Cyclone Events
abstract: International multimodal container transport networks (IMCTNs) play a critical role in supporting modern logistics systems and global trade, yet they are increasingly exposed to the risk of climate extremes, particularly compound flood and tropical cyclone (TC) events. The cross-modal impact of such events and the resulting systemic risk to IMCTNs remain insufficiently understood. This study proposes a comprehensive methodological framework for assessing and mitigating risks in IMCTNs under compound flood-TC events. title: Co-developing a human wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for small-scale fisheries: The Bahamas’ Nassau grouper fishery as a case study
abstract: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guidance for broader socio-economic monitoring exists, but no single set of indicators fits every fishery; it has to be worked out in context, with the people whose wellbeing is being measured. title: Serum biochemical profiles in the endemic Baikal seal (Pusa sibirica): longitudinal variability under managed care and comparison with free-ranging seals
abstract: Introduction The Baikal seal ( Pusa sibirica ), the world’s only exclusively freshwater pinniped, remains poorly characterized with respect to biochemical physiology. We characterized serum biochemical profiles in managed seals from two managed-care facilities (Primorsky Aquarium, n = 3; Moskvarium, n = 7) and in wild seals sampled during summer ( n = 20), focusing on longitudinal individual variability, exploratory seasonal and sex-associated patterns, longitudinal biochemical patterns across chronological age stages, and animal-level managed–wild differences. abstract: Introduction The bulbs of Allium sativum L. (garlic) are widely used as food or condiment, while they have also been used as a famous traditional medicine since ancient times for the treatment of diarrhea, dysentery, pertussis, tuberculosis and scabies, etc. However, most studies have focused on bulbs, and few studies have focused on the abundant aerial parts, which are usually discarded during the harvest season. title: Vacuum Impregnation of Foods: From Mass Transfer Intensification to Functional Design
abstract: Vacuum impregnation (VI) is a technique for porous foods that intensifies mass transfer by coupling gas expansion under vacuum with liquid imbibition during pressure restoration. During the vacuum step, trapped gases and some native liquids are partially removed from intercellular voids. Thus, when atmospheric or overpressure is restored, a surrounding external solution is driven into the newly available pore space by a pressure gradient, yielding rapid replacement of internal fluids relative to diffusion-limited mechanisms. title: What two decades of environmental-economic accounting reveal about Guatemala's natural capital and governance
abstract: Guatemala is one of the few developing countries to have kept the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) running for more than two decades without interruption. This paper draws together what those two decades produced and what the experience teaches in terms of empirical findings and governance lessons, including the conditions in which SEEA informs policy in a developing country context. abstract: We investigate diffusion-driven instabilities in a modified FitzHugh–Nagumo-type activator–inhibitor system with superdiffusive transport modeled by fractional Laplacian operators with different diffusion orders for the activator and the inhibitor. A linear stability analysis yields explicit expressions for the instability threshold and the critical wavenumber and shows that superdiffusion modifies the band of unstable modes and the characteristic spatial scale of emerging patterns. title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Mindlin–Reissner Plates
abstract: Plate and shell structures are widely used in engineering fields. Rapid response prediction for such structures under complex geometries, heterogeneous materials, and varying loads is important for engineering design, but conventional numerical methods usually require repeated modeling and solution when the physical configuration changes. To address this issue, this study proposes a geometry-aware variational physics-informed neural operator (GA-VINO) for Mindlin–Reissner plates. journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

title: Geospatial multi-indicator assessment of flood risk in a wetland ecosystem, using a PCA-weighted risk framework
abstract: Flood risk in wetland ecosystems is increasing due to hydro-climatic variability, land-use changes, and socio-economic vulnerability, particularly in low-lying regions of South Asia. This study presents a geospatial multi-indicator framework to assess flood risk in the Chalan Beel, one of the largest freshwater wetland ecosystems in Bangladesh. The assessment integrates four major risk components (hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and capacity) using the analytical relationship. title: Remediation of Petroleum-Contaminated Soils Using Coconut Shell-Derived Activated Carbon: A Systematic Review of Adsorption Mechanisms, Comparative Performance, and Field-Scale Challenges
abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon contamination of soil remains a persistent environmental challenge, particularly in oil-producing regions where conventional remediation technologies are often constrained by high cost, secondary pollution, and limited field effectiveness. Activated carbon–based remediation has emerged as a promising alternative; however, existing studies are fragmented across feedstocks and environmental matrices, making it difficult to identify materials with consistent soil-specific performance. title: Prevalence and abundance of pathogens in biofilters of freshwater recirculating aquaculture systems for Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
abstract: The extent to which recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) biofilters contain pathogenic microorganisms is poorly understood. Previous studies have been limited to single facilities, offering little insight into pathogen prevalence across different systems. This study quantified the occurrence of three bacterial and four viral pathogens in 50 freshwater biofilters from 36 commercial RAS across 11 facilities in Norway and the Faroe Islands for Atlantic salmon using quantitative PCR (qPCR). title: Wireless sensor network-based real-time monitoring system for large ship airbag launching: design and field validation
abstract: Traditional monitoring solutions for airbag launching of large ships rely on mechanical pressure gauges with limited spatial coverage, slow response times (from several hundred milliseconds to a few seconds), and an inability to monitor dynamically changing attitude parameters during the launching procedure. This paper introduces a WSN-based real-time monitoring solution that combines IMUs and pressure sensors installed at strategic positions on the ship hull and airbags. title: Context‐Aware Semantic Alignment Detection Transformer (CAS‐DETR): A Efficient Remote Sensing Detection Framework Integrating Adaptive Multiscale Context and Semantic Alignment
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing imagery is a challenging task in computer vision. The main challenge lies in the significant semantic gap between low‐level and high‐level features in deep networks. To address these issues, this paper proposes a context‐aware semantic alignment detection transformer (CAS‐DETR). title: AdaFusionNet: Adaptive Trajectory Prediction of Group Two-wheelers in Interactive Conflict Scenarios for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: The accurate prediction of two-wheeler motion trajectories is essential for ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles (AVs), particularly at crowded intersections in China. Existing trajectory prediction approaches face limitations in representing the diverse motion patterns, dynamic constraints, and group-level behavioral characteristics of two-wheeler riders. This paper proposes an adaptive trajectory prediction framework for two-wheelers by integrating the revised social force model (RSFM) and a spatiotemporal Transformer (STTransformer) module. journal: Journal of Intelligent and Connected Vehicles

title: Astroclimatic signatures in ENSO recurrence across equinoctial orbital asymmetries
abstract: Introduction This study examined the temporal organization of ENSO variability in relation to two Earth–Sun orbital-state descriptors, ΔLP and Fi, over the period 1948–2025. Methods Annual series were analyzed using Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA), Information Theory, partial wavelet coherence (PWC), and multiple wavelet coherence (MWC) as complementary methods. title: TopoToolbox 3, a laboratory for quantitative geomorphology
abstract: TopoToolbox has been widely used to analyze and model landscapes across geomorphology and other geospatial disciplines for the past 15 years. Its documentation and accessible interfaces have made it a valuable resource for teaching and learning quantitative geomorphology while its customizability and efficiency have allowed researchers to use it as a platform for experimentation and implementation of their own analyses and models. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa ha despertado preocupación por un posible reemplazo de la creatividad humana. Sin embargo, más que competir con ella, puede convertirse en una aliada para potenciarla. title: From density to bioenergetics: approaches for estimating fish rearing capacity in freshwater streams
abstract: Fish ecologists and managers have an interest in estimating the efficacy of freshwater habitat restoration, comparing among restoration options and basins. This often boils down to the question: How many fish can this habitat support? The number of fish a habitat can support, termed capacity, has increasingly become the currency for comparing habitats, restoration options, management policies, and is the backbone of many life cycle models. title: Improved residential load forecasting using multi-feature, multi-layer LSTM exploiting trend and periodic patterns in historical data
abstract: Accurate day-ahead forecasting of individual residential electricity demand remains challenging because household consumption is highly variable, nonlinear, and influenced by recurrent behavioral and environmental patterns. This study proposes a multi-input, multi-feature Long Short-Term Memory (MIMF-LSTM) framework for direct 24 hour residential load forecasting at 15 minute resolution. abstract: El objetivo fue evaluar el efecto de una estrategia integrada de análisis predictivo y mantenimiento basado en condición sobre la eficiencia operacional de líneas de producción en empresas manufactureras ecuatorianas. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, aplicado, descriptivo-correlacional y cuasiexperimental, con mediciones antes y después y comparación entre un grupo experimental y otro de control. title: Effects of dietary oils on the growth performance, fatty acid profile, gut and liver histology in murrel (Channa striata) juvenile
abstract: To evaluate the utilization of different dietary oils by juvenile murrel ( Channa striata ), five isonitrogenous (45%) and similar inclusion levels (8%) of selected oils, namely fish oil (FO), soybean oil (SO), mustard oil (MO), rice bran oil (RBO), and groundnut oil (GNO), were used. title: Advanced Process Automation and Distributed Control Systems for Improving Operational Efficiency in Saudi Arabia's Oil and Gas Industry
abstract: Process automation in petroleum facilities is frequently described as a route to efficiency, yet the mechanisms through which distributed control systems (DCS) improve performance remain insufficiently differentiated from supervisory analytics, instrumentation renewal and operational governance. This critical review examines contemporary evidence on regulatory control, distributed economic optimisation, field data acquisition, asset monitoring and cyber physical integrity, with particular attention to Saudi Arabia's upstream and processing assets. title: Collaborative mining enables efficient multi-scale feature compression for machine vision
abstract: Machine-oriented multi-scale feature compression aims to remove task-insensitive redundancy while preserving task-critical semantic and structural information. Existing methods primarily focus on reducing cross-scale redundancy, while intra-scale redundancy within individual feature maps remains insufficiently explored. abstract: Heterogeneous barriers influence pressure support and water entry in offshore stacked reservoirs, but their development implications are difficult to evaluate where well control in the upper zone is sparse. This study integrates drilled barrier interpretation, operation-screened production dynamics, geological monitoring priorities, and reservoir simulation for Zone B and the underlying Zone C of the LFA field. abstract: The rapid advancement and growing accessibility of image generation and editing technologies have heightened the risk of creating and disseminating increasingly realistic tampered images, posing serious threats to identity authentication, digital forensics, public opinion monitoring, and information security. Existing image tampering detectors predominantly exploit texture artifacts, boundary inconsistencies, or frequency-domain traces. title: Petroleum system evolution and hydrocarbon prospectivity of the Anambra Basin and Southern Benue Trough, Southeastern Nigeria
abstract: The Anambra Basin and Southern Benue Trough of southeastern Nigeria constitute a frontier onshore petroleum province within the West African Rift System, yet remain commercially unproven despite seven decades of exploration. This review presents an integrated synthesis of geological, geochemical, and geophysical data to evaluate petroleum system elements, reconcile contradictory interpretations, and identify exploration strategies. title: Two lead-leg knee flexion-extension patterns and their associations with elbow loading in collegiate baseball pitchers
abstract: Lead-leg mechanics may influence baseball pitching performance and elbow loading, but discrete event analyses may overlook time-varying movement strategies. This study used a data-driven full-trajectory approach to identify lead-leg knee flexion–extension patterns and examine their associations with ball velocity and peak elbow varus torque (pEVT) in 224 NCAA Division I pitchers. title: An Event-Driven Edge AI Surveillance System with Real-Time Automated Alerting
abstract: Traditional surveillance networks rely on continuous video recording, which demands immense data storage, consumes high network bandwidth, and serves primarily as a passive forensic tool rather than an active deterrent. While basic motion-activated systems mitigate storage waste, they suffer from critically high false-alarm rates triggered by environmental noise. title: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
abstract: Virus-host association prediction is fundamental to virus-related disease control and phage therapy, yet many existing tools require candidate-host genome sequences, which may be unavailable for some eukaryotic hosts or impractical to search at the scale of large virome studies. We present VHSeek, a supervised virus-host association predictor that integrates DNA- and protein-derived viral representations. title: Contribution of Land Use and Land Cover to Seasonal Variation in Water Quality in the Nyabarongo River, Rwanda
abstract: Water quality degradation in freshwater systems, driven by land use/land cover (LULC) changes and climatic variability, poses a global threat to ecosystems and human health. This study investigates the seasonal impacts of LULC on water quality in Rwanda’s Nyabarongo River using the National Sanitation Foundation Water Quality Index (NSF-WQI) and multivariate statistical analyses. abstract: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. abstract: To address high false alarm rates in infrared small-target detection, where faint target features are easily submerged by complex background clutter and traditional loss functions lack frequency-domain constraints, this paper proposes a lightweight Dual Wavelet High-Frequency Mamba Network (DWHM-Net) built on a symmetric U-shaped encoder–decoder architecture with Mamba backbone.The first core innovation is a Dual Wavelet Feature Enhancement Module(DWFEM). title: Geometry-Guided Optimization for Offshore Wind Farm Collection System Routing via Adaptive Circuit Partitioning
abstract: Offshore wind farm collection system routing requires cost-effective networks that satisfy coupled electrical and geometric constraints. Existing methods often improve topology search or path feasibility separately, relying on restricted candidates, predefined routes, or post-hoc repair to handle crossings, obstacles, irregular boundaries, and export-corridor conflicts. title: Life-cycle assessment and exergy analysis of enzymatic polyethylene terephthalate recycling
abstract: Plastic recycling and upcycling are effective strategies for mitigating plastic pollution. Rapid advances in protein engineering have enabled the optimization of natural polyethylene terephthalate (PET) hydrolases, thereby accelerating the industrialization of enzymatic PET recycling. In this study, process modeling, life-cycle assessment, and exergy analysis were conducted for an enzymatic PET recycling process based on China’s energy structure. abstract: Microphysiological systems (MPSs) have emerged as powerful in vitro platforms that recapitulate human microenvironments with high physiological relevance, enabling studies of disease mechanisms, drug responses, and toxicity. Effective use of MPSs requires not only stable maintenance of the engineered microenvironment but also quantitative and continuous monitoring of dynamic physical, chemical, and biological changes over time. title: Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: A field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals
abstract: Leak detection on pumped transmission mains that cross steep terrain relies on hydraulic signals whose response to a small leak may be comparable to sensor noise. We evaluated five unsupervised methods (PELT with Bayesian and Akaike penalties, Bayesian online changepoint detection [BOCD], an OLS-CUSUM structural-break procedure and a moving-average ±3σ chart) on flow and pressure series recorded every 30 s during seven controlled leak trials (valve setting 3-5% of nominal flow) in two field campaigns on an Andean transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. title: Spatial coherence and input uncertainty in AutoML-tuned gradient-boosting predictions of depth to groundwater as an indicator of groundwater potential
abstract: Groundwater in the semi-arid Zagros foreland of northern Iraq is being withdrawn faster than it is replenished, and identifying where groundwater is most accessible is a precondition for managing that deficit. This study maps groundwater potential in the Karma Soor basin, Kurdistan Region, and compares three gradient-boosted ensemble learners, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost, tuned under identical settings with the Train Using AutoML tool in ArcGIS Pro. title: Renewable energy and digital transformation for sustainable energy transition: The roles of urbanization and economic growth in PM₂.₅ exposure in Poland
abstract: This study investigates the long-run and short-run relationships between renewable energy (RE) consumption, digital connectivity, urbanization (URB), economic growth (EG), and population-weighted PM₂.₅ exposure in Poland over the period 1990–2023. Using annual data, the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) bounds-testing approach is employed to examine the dynamic relationships among the variables. title: Swim2Real: Vision-Language Models for Simulator Calibration of a Soft Robotic Fish
abstract: Calibrating a soft aquatic robot simulator requires matching coupled deformation and propulsion from limited pool recordings. Swim2Real uses a vision-language model (VLM) to compare real and simulated swimming videos and propose updates to 16 simulator parameters.
