title: Evaluation of reanalysis datasets for studying high-elevation meteorological conditions in the Langtang Catchment, Nepal
abstract: Climate reanalysis datasets are widely used in hydro-meteorological and cryospheric research across High Mountain Asia (HMA), where in situ observations are scarce. Here, we evaluate ERA5L, High Asian Refined Analysis (HARv2), Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications (MERRA2), and Climatologies at High Resolution for the Earth’s Land Surface Areas (CHELSA) against near-surface meteorological observations between 3,865 and 5,350 m a.s.l., in the upper Langtang Catchment, Nepal, using statistical metrics and Taylor Skill Score ( TSS ). title: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
abstract: Extreme glacier melt events accelerate mass loss, increase glacier instability, and temporarily increase downstream runoff, potentially alleviating drought conditions. abstract: Glacier thickness and thermal regime control glacier dynamics and long-term evolution, but observations are sparse at regional scales. abstract: Purpose Plastic pollution in water is a global issue. As polymeric materials degrade, micro- and nanoplastics are formed, and release substances used in their production, many of which exhibit estrogenic effects on organisms. The main aim of the study was to investigate the relationship between the concentrations of selected organic compounds, mainly used in plastic production, in the sediments of artificial reservoirs and the land use of their catchments, under varied anthropogenic pressure. abstract: How does audio describe the world around us? In this work, we propose a method for generating images of visual scenes from diverse in-the-wild sounds. This cross-modal generation task is challenging due to the significant information gap between auditory and visual signals. abstract: Winter compound events characterized by freezing temperatures and heavy snow have profound impacts on vulnerable dryland ecosystems. This paper introduces the Urban Ecosystems special issue and outlines the outcomes and future directions emerging from the ninth Urban Biodiversity and Design International Network (URBIO) 2025 conference, held in Perth, Western Australia — the first URBIO conference specifically oriented toward the Australasian context. abstract: [Introduction]: The identification of more-than-human needs has emerged as a central issue in contemporary debates on design, innovation, and sustainability, as it challenges anthropocentric approaches that subordinate animals, plants, soils, and ecosystems to exclusively human interests. title: Urban freight transition strategies: a multi-criteria assessment of diesel truck alternatives
abstract: Purpose Freight transportation has become an important source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly in urban areas where delivery systems are heavily dependent on diesel-powered vehicles. Although a wide range of alternative strategies have been proposed to reduce this reliance, existing studies mainly evaluate these options in isolation and with a primary focus on environmental benefits. abstract: Urbanization, in combination with global climate change, is rapidly transforming freshwater habitats by altering temperature regimes, flow patterns, and habitat structure, often reducing biodiversity and favoring tolerant species. Amphibians are especially sensitive to these environmental changes, yet some species persist or even thrive in urban landscapes. abstract: The holotype of the type species † Palaeoscyllium formosum Wagner, 1857 from the Jurassic of Europe, lacking the cranial region, is herein carefully re-described and re-evaluated to clarify the taxonomic and nomenclatural status of this taxon. abstract: Spinel oxides (AB2O4) have emerged as widely studied non-noble-metal electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction owing to their structural plasticity, versatile cationic valence states, and cost-effectiveness. abstract: Flooding and water reclamation of former underground and opencast workings of the former “Friendship of Nations–Babina Shaft” brown coal mine, has led to the formation of an anthropogenic lake district in Western Poland. The water reservoirs of this lake district are characterized by different origins, multicolored waters, low pH, and high concentration of iron compounds. abstract: This study proposes a hierarchical Bayesian model to estimate regional accommodation availability using high-resolution booking data from an online travel agency. title: Computer Vision Methods for Bridge Surface Damage Detection
abstract: After long-term service, bridges are prone to surface defects such as cracks, spalling, and corrosion. The timely identification and recording of these defects constitute an essential part of bridge inspection and maintenance. Conventional manual inspection relies on close-range visual observation and record keeping by inspectors; this approach carries safety risks when workers operate at height or beneath bridges, and its efficiency and consistency are readily affected by the experience of the personnel and by field conditions. title: Regional-scale field-level estimation and mapping of tillage practices in areas with crop diversity
abstract: The imperative for sustainable agriculture has led to the promotion of conservation tillage practices, which are critical for maintaining soil health and reducing negative environmental impacts. However, the ability to verify the adoption of these practices at a regional scale and with minimal costs remains a challenge, particularly in regions with diverse crop systems. abstract: Introduction Post-harvest fish loss is an important concern in Somalia's fisheries sector, with potential implications for fish quality, livelihoods, food security, and market development. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional mixed-methods survey was conducted with 94 fisheries stakeholders across four Somali fish markets: Mogadishu, Kismayo, Bosaso, and Berbera. abstract: In this study we establish a proof-of-concept workflow for conducting a mutagenesis screen in Macrocystis pyrifera g ametophytes. abstract: Urban pluvial flood responses exhibit substantial temporal and spatial heterogeneity, making event-scale classifications challenging when directly relying on rainfall and water-depth observations. abstract: Mean stream water depth is an important physical component of streams. However, streams have high spatial heterogeneity, making depth determinations challenging. abstract: Growing maritime trade has intensified congestion and environmental pressures in port cities. Existing approaches primarily focus on port efficiency or promote alternative freight transport modes; however, road transport remains dominant, resulting in persistent congestion and emissions on port-access-road. abstract: The increasing availability of shipboard additive manufacturing (AM) enables on-board repair through the rapid fabrication of temporary polymer spare parts. abstract: Bioethanol is a promising renewable fuel that can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: Accurate forecasting of carbon emissions is vital for shaping sustainable environmental policies and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those linked to climate action. title: Port electrification: definitions, pathways, and grid impact assessment
abstract: Ports are increasingly central to decarbonization strategies, but port electrification is defined inconsistently across academic and policy literature. This ambiguity matters because different definitions imply different electricity-demand profiles, peak loads, connection requirements, and grid-upgrade needs. abstract: Soil salinization is a major environmental stress that restricts plant growth and ecosystem productivity in arid and semi-arid regions. abstract: A poluição por microplásticos em ambientes aquáticos representa uma ameaça crescente à vida dos ecossistemas e à saúde pública em todo o mundo. abstract: Negative online reviews make service failures publicly visible and shape prospective guests' perceptions of hotels, with management responses forming part of digital complaint-response interactions. abstract: Background Alpine permafrost-affected soils, particularly in the European Alps, remain poorly understood despite rapid warming and projected vegetation increase at higher elevations. abstract: The global proliferation of diuron [3-(3,4-dichlorophenyl)-1,1-dimethylurea], a persistent phenylurea herbicide and probable human carcinogen, represents a critical environmental challenge in the Anthropocene. title: Moderating Role of Global Financial Integration in the Climate Finance–Digitalisation–Renewable Energy Nexus: Empirical Evidence From Pacific Island Countries
abstract: Pacific Island Countries contribute a negligible share of global greenhouse gas emissions yet face existential threats from climate change. This study examines how climate finance, digitalisation and renewable energy consumption affect carbon dioxide emissions per capita in 11 Pacific Island Countries over 2000–2024, and whether global financial integration moderates these effects. abstract: This paper presents BehaVerify, a verification toolbox for behavior trees (BTs) and Neuro-Symbolic BTs. BTs are a graphical language for planning and sequencing behaviors - similar to extended state machines - and are increasingly used in safety-critical domains. BehaVerify enables users to specify a BT using a Domain Specific Language (DSL) with formal syntax and semantics. title: Cross-scale mapping of aquatic macrophytes and their limnological drivers in a tropical reservoir using UAV and PlanetScope imagery
abstract: This study evaluates the influence of spatial resolution on aquatic macrophyte classification and integrates limnological variables to better understand their distribution in a tropical reservoir. An object-based approach was used to classify high-resolution UAV imagery and PlanetScope imagery. High-resolution UAV imagery significantly improves classification accuracy for structurally fragmented classes, such as floating macrophytes, by reducing mixed-pixel effects and enhancing boundary delineation. title: Border Checkpoint as Literacy Technology
abstract: This paper draws from an array of primary sources, such as the Customs and Border Protection (CBP) periodical Frontline, government documents, and news reports of CBP brutality, to discuss the ways that border checkpoints function as technologies that impart everyday literacies of race, citizenship, and class onto all who move through them. title: An integrated multimodal temporal-graph framework for rare pharmaceutical supply-chain disruption early warning with explainable AI and permissioned governance
abstract: Rare but high-impact disruptions in pharmaceutical supply chains can propagate across multi-echelon networks, threatening medicine availability and operational continuity. Early warning is challenging because positive examples are scarce, network dependencies evolve over time, relevant evidence is multimodal, and regulated multi-partner settings require auditable review. This study evaluates an integrated node-day framework for predicting whether a qualifying disruption condition will occur within a 14-day future horizon. title: Coaxial Monitoring of Meltpool for Laser Powder Bed Fusion Process Control
abstract: Reliable process monitoring is critical for advancing laser powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M), as it provides the process information required for corrective control actions to prevent defects such as lack-of-fusion and keyhole porosity. A promising approach for PBF-LB/M process monitoring is coaxial measurement of light emitted from the meltpool area. abstract: The Nekor Fault is a major NE-SW structure in the Rif-Alboran plate-boundary zone, yet its present-day activity is poorly constrained. We use approximately a decade of Sentinel-1 ascending and descending InSAR observations to evaluate whether contemporary deformation is detectable across the fault corridor and whether its geometry is compatible with active strike-slip kinematics. title: Flood simulation study of the lower tumen river based on a hydrological-hydrodynamic coupled model
abstract: Climate change has profoundly altered global hydrological regimes and significantly intensified the occurrence of extreme flooding. Although discharge constitutes the dominant driver of flood genesis, flood propagation is also strongly controlled by channel and surface roughness conditions. Nevertheless, the magnitude of roughness impacts on flood responses, and their interactive effects with climate change, remain inadequately explored, especially in transboundary river basins with limited observational data. title: DA-DISTA-Net: Degradation-Aware Unfolding Network for Closely-Spaced Infrared Small Target Unmixing
abstract: Deep unfolding networks for closely-spaced infrared small target (CSIST) unmixing are usually trained and tested with a single, known point spread function (PSF). When the PSF at test time differs from the training PSF, their accuracy drops noticeably. We treat unmixing under an unknown PSF as an information fusion problem: the low-resolution observation contains both the target configuration and cues about the blur that produced it, and the second kind of information can be used to steer the reconstruction. title: Equity-aware multi-objective optimization of nature-based solutions for flood susceptibility reduction
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly promoted for flood mitigation, yet how to allocate limited resources while balancing aggregate effectiveness and social equity remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether directing greater mitigation benefits toward socially vulnerable communities necessarily requires substantial losses in overall flood-susceptibility reduction. title: Differentiated Paths to Enhance Tourism Resilience: A Sustainable Perspective
abstract: Enhancing tourism resilience (TR) is vital for absorbing shocks, ensuring sustainability, and boosting regional competitiveness; yet systematic evaluation and tailored improvement strategies remain urgent challenges. This study introduces the “R 2 ICE” framework, comprising RESIS (resistance), RECOV (recovery), CONFI (configuration), INNOV (innovation), and ENDUR (endurance), with a concise 30‐indicator TR evaluation system. title: Predictability Limit of RMM Index Modulated by Diverse ENSO Events
abstract: The Madden‐Julian Oscillation (MJO), a crucial source of subseasonal predictability, experiences El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) modulation whose impacts vary by event type. Using an analog‐based methodology that incorporates a history of dynamical system evolution and epsilon‐based neighborhoods, we quantify how Eastern‐Pacific (EP) and Central‐Pacific (CP) ENSO events distinctly regulate the predictability limit of the real‐time multivariate MJO (RMM) index. title: Regression model analysis for alternatively fuelled transport ships
abstract: The maritime industry is under increasing pressure to develop ships powered by alternative fuels. Early-stage design relies on empirical formulae to estimate initial dimensions and operational parameters, but these models are predominantly derived from conventionally fuelled ships. Alternative fuels such as liquefied natural gas, methanol, hydrogen, and ammonia have lower energy densities, and require larger storage volumes that may affect relationships between principal dimensions, cargo capacity, and performance. title: International Law in a Divided World: The Ideals and Realities of Interdependence
abstract: This paper examines the possibilities for peace in the twenty-first century through the evolving role of international law in an increasingly divided yet interdependent world. It argues that contemporary crises—including war, genocide, authoritarianism, inequality, polarization, and climate change—expose the limitations of the existing international order, while legal responses to these challenges simultaneously demonstrate the enduring power of universal legal norms. abstract: La inteligencia artificial explicable (XAI) agrupa procedimientos orientados a facilitar el examen de predicciones, representaciones y comportamientos de sistemas de aprendizaje automático. Este artículo analiza las principales familias de técnicas, sus ámbitos de aplicación y sus limitaciones, mediante una revisión narrativa estructurada de publicaciones académicas verificables. title: Climate-driven spatio-temporal escalation of wet mass-movement disasters and their socio-economic impacts (1970−2024)
abstract: Mass-movement disasters, including landslides, avalanches, and mudslides, are among the most critical types of geohazards influenced by climate variability and socio-economic exposure. A comprehensive global assessment linking long-term climate trends to mass-movement disasters and their socio-economic impacts remains limited, despite growing evidence of climate-driven intensification of geohazard frequency. title: Review on Formation Mechanisms and Assessment Methods of Business-Level Indirect Economic Losses Caused by Natural Hazards
abstract: Over the past decades, increasingly frequent extreme natural hazards have caused substantial indirect economic losses that propagate through business interconnections. However, existing review studies predominantly adopt macro or meso perspectives and offer limited insight into micro-level loss formation mechanisms and business heterogeneity. To address these gaps, this study systematically reviews the literature up to June 2026 on the formation mechanisms and assessment methods of indirect economic losses to businesses caused by natural hazards. title: Clinical isolation and genomic characterization of Rheinheimera tangshanensis following ECMO decannulation
abstract: Rheinheimera species are widely distributed environmental bacteria that are rarely encountered in clinical microbiology. Although occasional human infections caused by Rheinheimera have been reported, the clinical significance of Rheinheimera tangshanensis remains largely unknown. Here, we report the phenotypic and genomic characterization of a clinical isolate of R. tangshanensis recovered from an ECMO-associated wound. abstract: Cement tile manufacturing is a traditional industry in Iran, yet wastewater-related heavy metal pollution raises sustainability concerns. This study evaluates the environmental pollution using three distinct approaches. (1) The grey water footprint (GWF) quantifies the volume of freshwater required to assimilate pollution, based on net discharged loads and the receiving environment's limitations. title: Impact of spatial representativeness of aerodynamic parameters on urban street-canyon wind simulations
abstract: Accurate simulation of urban wind fields is critical for street-scale air quality modeling, yet remains challenged by the spatial heterogeneity of real cities. Street-network models enable citywide simulations at reasonable cost, and their aerodynamic parameterizations, which are often derived from idealized geometries, must be rigorously evaluated under realistic urban conditions. abstract: History teaching continues to rely heavily on traditional methodologies based on lectures, textbook reading, and memorization, which frequently leads to low student motivation, limited interaction, and difficulties in understanding historical contexts in a meaningful way. title: UniDRE: Universal method for document-level relation extraction with knowledge retrieval and reasoning augmentation on small and large language models
abstract: Document-level relation extraction (Doc-RE) seeks to identify relation triples among entity pairs across different sentences in a document. Unlike sentence-level RE, Doc-RE demands more comprehensive reasoning capabilities. Despite recent advances, most existing Doc-RE methods focus on isolated or partial reasoning abilities, leaving the comprehensive reasoning required for Doc-RE insufficiently explored. abstract: Rapid urbanization and climate variability have substantially altered the hydrological response of urban watersheds, resulting in increased surface runoff, reduced infiltration, and a higher frequency of urban flooding. Understanding these changes is essential for sustainable watershed management and flood risk mitigation. This study evaluates the rainfall-runoff response of the Wakad urban watershed in the Mula River Basin, Pune, India, using the soil and water assessment tool (SWAT) implemented through the QSWAT interface. title: Beyond recycling: A circularity maturity framework for evidence-based assessment of recycled aggregate concrete research
abstract: Recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) is increasingly promoted to reduce construction and demolition waste and reliance on virgin aggregates; however, higher recycled-material use does not necessarily indicate measurable circular-economy progress. This review introduces a Circularity Maturity Framework (CMF) as a study-level evidence-assessment framework for evaluating reported circularity-related evidence in RAC research rather than absolute circularity performance. abstract: This study addresses interfacial adhesion and friction‐induced wear damage in multilayer composites by developing porous fiber‐reinforced damping composites. Five composite configurations were fabricated to distinguish the respective contributions of the rubber interlayer, carboxyl functionalization, and isophorone diisocyanate‐mediated interfacial modification. title: LIGHT AIRCRAFT WING SECTION
abstract: This work presents the aerodynamic and structural analysis of the wing section of a two-seat light aircraft with a maximum take-off mass of 600 kg. The wing is rectangular in plan, with a span of 9.0 m, a chord of 1.4 m and an area of 12.6 square metres, giving a wing loading of 467 N per square metre. The study compares two common light-aircraft airfoils, NACA 2412 and NACA 4415, and then examines a wing box made of a front spar, a rear spar, ribs and skin under the lift load of a symmetric manoeuvre. title: Mudskippers use tail thrusting to help crutching to move on mud of various wetness
abstract: At the water-land interface, amphibious fishes encounter wet flowable substrates made of granular solid-water mixtures, which can stay solid or flow like a fluid. As these substrates become wetter or drier, their yield strength (at which solid-fluid transition occurs) and cohesion (how sticky they are) both change, challenging locomotion. title: The ICOS Ecosystem Station Loobos: a pine forest site exposed to atmospheric pollution
abstract: The Loobos Ecosystem Station (ICOS: NL-Loo) is in a pine forest on sandy soil, the most dominant forest type in the Netherlands. The station was first built in 1995 and the first atmospheric flux measurements were taken in 1997. The station was one of the first in EuroFlux and FLUXNET. Between 2021 and 2023, the station was rebuilt to meet the ICOS standards as an Ecosystem Class 2 station. The initial purpose of the station was to measure fluxes of heat, water and carbon dioxide. title: Distributed Data‐Driven Formation Tracking Control for Heterogeneous UAV Swarms Under Quantized Communication
abstract: Heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms rely on wireless communication for distributed formation tracking, but limited bandwidth and channel congestion necessitate data quantization. Quantization introduces information loss that degrades formation accuracy. This paper proposes a distributed data‐driven quantized control (QC‐MFAC) algorithm for heterogeneous UAV formation tracking under quantized communication. title: From sludge to supper: biosolids as a potential source of microplastics in the food chain
abstract: Microplastics are widely documented as arriving in municipal wastewater from diverse sources such as clothing fibers, tire shreds and cosmetics. Wastewater treatment works typically remove 70–99% of microplastics from the aqueous phase before discharging treated water back to the aquatic environment. However, rather than being eliminated, the microplastic burden is merely transferred to and concentrated in the sewage sludge created by the treatment process. title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. title: Beyond English-only pedagogy: Translanguaging, learner agency, and meaning-making in Malaysian secondary English classrooms
abstract: This study explores the use of translanguaging to support learner agency and meaning-making in Malaysian secondary English as a Second Language (ESL) contexts. The study adopts García and Li Wei's translanguaging approach, situated within Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory. It addresses the relative lack of empirical attention to observed classroom practice at the secondary level. title: Charting the insect biodiversity of southern-central Crete: Insights from a pilot metabarcoding survey
abstract: Among eukaryotes, insects are by far the most diverse organisms on Earth, yet their global decline threatens ecosystem stability. Understanding local and regional biodiversity patterns is critical for conservation planning, ecosystem management, and predicting responses to environmental change, but traditional surveys for assessing insect diversity (e.g., manual collection, morphological identification, and counting) are highly labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often require rare or simply unavailable dedicated taxonomic expertise. abstract: This study presents a contribution to the development of evolutionary fuzzy optimization control for computational intelligence (CI)‐based robust visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) in autonomous mobile robots. title: Next-generation antifungal therapeutics: emerging drug targets, precision strategies, and novel treatment modalities
abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) remain a major global health threat, particularly among immunocompromised patients. Current antifungals that target ergosterol biosynthesis, cell-wall assembly, and nucleic-acid synthesis are increasingly constrained by toxicity, drug-drug interactions, suboptimal pharmacokinetics, narrow spectra, and rising resistance. abstract: As robotic systems move beyond structured industrial settings into less structured domains such as agricultural harvesting, food handling, medical manipulation, and human-robot interaction, conventional rigid grippers face limitations when handling soft, fragile, irregularly shaped, or highly variable objects. abstract: Fusion plasma control requires real-time coordination of multiple actuators under partial observations and model uncertainty. Here we demonstrate predictive control of a fusion plasma on the Large Helical Device using an adaptive digital-twin system that combines data assimilation with physics-based integrated modeling. abstract: Purpose Ferry transport is vital for island economies, yet persistent operational challenges threaten service reliability and sustainability. abstract: To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of Homo sapiens , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and H. sapiens lived in Europe. title: Enhanced jellyfish search-optimized cascaded fuzzy-FOPI control of a three-phase dynamic voltage restorer for power quality improvement
abstract: Power quality disturbances, particularly voltage sags and swells, pose significant challenges to modern distribution networks with increasing penetration of nonlinear loads and renewable energy resources. Dynamic voltage restorers (DVRs) are highly effective custom power devices for mitigating such disturbances; however, their performance depends strongly on the employed control strategy. abstract: Tenacibaculum finnmarkense is an important pathogen of farmed salmon in Norway and Chile, comprising the finnmarkense and ulcerans genomovars. This study aimed to develop a multiplex PCR (mPCR) assay for species‐specific identification of T. finnmarkense and discrimination between its two genomovars using comparative genomics. abstract: Appropriate reliance on autonomy in multi-agent systems requires operators to continuously evaluate and assign leadership among heterogeneous autonomous agents as task demands and environmental conditions evolve. abstract: Coordinated energy management is crucial for the effective operation of integrated multi-energy systems (IMESs), which integrate water, heat, and electricity networks. The primary objectives of this coordination include reducing operational costs, minimizing hazards, and ensuring a reliable supply of energy. title: Exploring India's agroecology landscape for sustainable and transformative agricultural food systems: a systematic literature network analysis
abstract: This study employs a systematic literature network analysis to examine India's agroecology (AE) landscape and its potential to transform agricultural food systems toward sustainability. Although researchers emphasize the relevance of AE, this review reveals persistent challenges, including ecological degradation from input-intensive practices, the exclusion of smallholders and women from access to resources, and limited institutional support for agroecological transitions. abstract: The climate value of Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) hinges on the assumption that CO 2 can be stored permanently. Yet this assumption rests on evidence gathered over decades, while the storage commitment extends across centuries to millennia. abstract: Cold pools, formed under clouds by the evaporation of precipitation, play a central role in maintaining and organizing atmospheric convection. It is suspected that their absence in climate models may lead to significant errors in the representation of convection, such as the premature convection extinction after sunset. abstract: Digital twin irrigation districts rely on stable multiscale 3D representation of terrain and hydraulic objects, but multi-LOD terrain transitions often cause floating, misalignment, and discontinuous dynamic behavior. abstract: The urban environment is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of human health, yet planning tools rely on static, low-resolution surveys that fail to capture people’s granular experience of local environments. We ask whether citizen-sourced, high-resolution data on urban experience can be translated into design-relevant hypotheses for healthier behavior. title: Multiscale monitoring of gully erosion in Northeast China’s black soil region using integrated satellite, UAV, and ground observations: a case study of the Wulagouzi River Basin, Hailun
abstract: Gully erosion is a major threat to cultivated Mollisols in Northeast China, yet its interannual development is difficult to quantify using single-date or single-platform observations. abstract: Degradation of the Amazon rainforest is increasing by expanding human activities, especially unregulated gold mining. However, the high cost and environmental impact of industrial steel fibers have raised concerns, prompting the exploration of sustainable alternatives. abstract: This study examines strategies for reducing the carbon footprint in transregional transport within international trade, with a focus on the Middle and Zangezur corridors. It explores how institutional frameworks, technological solutions, and infrastructure development shape the transition to low-carbon logistics. title: Real estate wealth inequality and exposure to natural disasters with evidence from France
abstract: Most studies measuring inequalities in exposure to climate disasters rely on aggregate income data and focus on residents. By omitting dwellings owned by nonresidents, this approach overlooks half of the housing stock exposed to flooding. Using dwelling-level data covering the entire French housing market, this paper examines how natural disaster risks are distributed across tenants, owner-occupants, and owners of rental, second, and vacant properties. abstract: Long-term meteorological observations are essential for assessing climate change and urban microclimates, but they are often affected by non-climatic change-points such as instrumental updates. This study presents the homogenization of two daily minimum and maximum temperature series in the plain area around Padua, Italy, covering the 1963–2025 period. abstract: Adaptation needs local temperature projections, yet their uncertainty remains large. Historical temperature differences between observations and the model-ensemble mean contain unforced variability, substantially limiting constraints on future local warming. Whether neighboring records strengthen these constraints, and at what spatial scale, remains a key unresolved question. abstract: Corporate governance plays an important role in shaping firms’ accountability, resource allocation efficiency, and long-term sustainability outcomes (Latella et al., 2025; Tan et al., 2017). This study examines the relationship between corporate governance and firm-level green total factor productivity (GTFP) using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms over the period 2012–2023. title: Fire Safety: Stage‐Dependent Fire Behavior, Performance Criteria, and Application‐Based Requirement
abstract: Fire development is inherently stage‐dependent, with material responses and engineering concerns varying across fire scenarios and exposure conditions. Established fire safety engineering (FSE) and performance‐based design (PBD) approaches already connect fire development, test evidence, and mitigation strategies with defined safety objectives. abstract: Introduction The transition to Space 4.0, characterized by the growing participation of private actors, the commercialization of space activities, and intensifying competition over space resources, is fundamentally reshaping the governance of outer space. abstract: Assessing the welfare of sentient animals, where sufficient species-specific knowledge is available, depends on inferring subjective experience from observable proxies of bio-regulatory function. However, the interpretative logic that connects indicators to experience can now be extended by including fresh perspectives based on recently developed teleonomic reasoning. abstract: Ozone pollution control is mainly based on the ozone chemistry sensitivity to precursor emissions. Here, we show that there is strong interfacial ozone exchange between free troposphere (FT) and atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), which renders FT ozone a potential source of surface ozone, but has not been well accounted for in previous ozone controls. abstract: Nanocellulose is a promising renewable material for sustainable food packaging. title: Modelling climate change impacts on river temperatures in two Norwegian catchments
abstract: Study region: Gaula and Nausta are two Norwegian river catchments that differ in size, hydrological setting, and degree of hydropower regulation. Gaula includes regulated tributary sections affected by diversions and reservoir operation, whereas Nausta represents a smaller, largely unregulated western Norwegian catchment. Together, the catchments provide contrasting test cases for assessing climate-change impacts on river discharge and water temperature at management-relevant spatial scales. title: Structural mapping of Mycobacterium leprae to understand pathogenesis and advance therapeutic discovery; a mini review
abstract: Mycobacterium leprae is an obligate intracellular, acid-fast bacillus and the primary causative agent of leprosy (Hansen’s disease), a chronic infection that predominantly affects the skin, peripheral nerves, upper respiratory mucosa, and eyes. Despite multi-drug therapy, more than 200,000 new cases are reported globally each year, reflecting continued transmission in endemic regions. abstract: This study investigates the influence of machining environment—atmospheric versus submerged—on the performance of Abrasive Water Jet Machining (AWJM) of Nimonic-90, focusing on depth of penetration (DOP) and surface quality. The furniture industry's prevailing trend shows low product differentiation that resonates with users' emotional aspects. abstract: A soft gripper can deform around an object, yet deformation by itself tells the operator little about whether that object is held securely. abstract: The Dombo Sayung River in Demak Regency is one of the rivers prone to flooding due to increased flow discharge during the rainy season and the limited capacity of the river cross-section to accommodate water flow. This study aims to analyze the capacity of the Dombo Sayung River cross-sections under the 50-year return period flood discharge (Q50) of 78.96 m³/s using HEC-RAS 6.6 software. title: Geochemical Assessment and Ecological Risk of Heavy Metal Contamination in River Sediments of Pakistan
abstract: Heavy metal contamination of freshwater ecosystems has become a pressing environmental concern in Pakistan, driven by rapid industrialization, unplanned urbanization and the largely uncontrolled discharge of untreated industrial and municipal wastewater. title: Standards Defining Echocardiography Core Laboratory (ECL) in Clinical Practice and Research
abstract: Echocardiography is extensively utilized in both clinical practice and research due to its accessibility. Echocardiography core laboratories (ECLs) adhering to societal guidelines offer superior readings and interpretations compared with the on-site assessments by reducing measurement variability and enhancing study precision. abstract: Deploying hydrodynamic models for real‐time, impact‐oriented forecasting of urban surface water flooding (SWF) remains challenging due to the computational cost and operational complexity of online hydrodynamic simulations. An alternative investigated in this paper is the rapid selection of flood scenarios from pre‐computed catalogues. abstract: The authors propose a method for jointly learning signed twofold graphs and performing signal restoration on multimodal graph signals. Multimodal signals on sensor networks are commonly modeled under the twofold graph assumption (TGA), which represents spatial structure and inter-modality relations as two separate graphs. abstract: This study aims to improve sustainability and environmentally friendly practices in an Irish bakery by reducing carbon emissions and reducing the use of single‐use plastics. Green lean six sigma (GLSS) methodology was utilised to improve sustainability performance. The use of single‐use plastics decreased by 33.9% through the adoption of intermediate bulk containers, the installation of solar panels and the purchase of green electricity, contributing to a 5% reduction in the carbon footprint. abstract: Toxin production by cyanobacteria that cause harmful algal blooms (CyanoHABs) can be influenced by nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P), yet little is known regarding how the macronutrient balance affects their saxitoxin (STX) content. This study aims to examine whether and how the China–Europe Railway Express (CR Express) attracts foreign direct investment (FDI) to connected Chinese cities. title: Comparison of Single- and Bi-Tuned Mass Dampers under Equal Total Auxiliary Mass and Different Dynamic Loads in a Wind Turbine Tower–Nacelle System
abstract: This study compares a single tuned mass damper and a bi-tuned mass damper in a single-degree-of-freedom wind turbine tower–nacelle model. Four configurations are evaluated under the same total auxiliary mass: the classical Den Hartog design, a single damper retuned with the common objective, a bi-tuned damper with equal branch masses, and a bi-tuned damper with a free mass split. The objective combines normalized displacement and acceleration responses over a frequency band around the main natural frequency, and the designs are optimized for total auxiliary mass ratios of 0.02, 0.05, and 0.20.
journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: SatForensics: a transformer-based multi-modal framework for cyber-attack detection, attribution, and chain-of-custody forensics in low-earth-orbit satellite communication networks
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite networks lack public records of labelled cyber-attacks, which makes it hard to evaluate detection, attribution and forensic tools for them. We present SatForensics, a gated multi-modal Transformer that scores each satellite observation for anomalies, attributes injected RF attacks to one of five archetypes (broadband, continuous-wave, swept and pulsed jamming, and Doppler-following spoofing), and records every event in a SHA-256 hash-chained ledger together with a calibrated posterior, a confidence margin and an ambiguity flag. title: New records of Pseudoderma sinicarum and Lithophyllum nagaokaense (Lithophylloideae, Lithophyllaceae, Rhodophyta) from Korea
abstract: The subfamily Lithophylloideae includes non-geniculate coralline algal genera for which taxonomic uncertainty persists due to pronounced morphological plasticity and the limited availability of type-anchored molecular data. Here, we report Pseudoderma sinicarum and Lithophyllum nagaokaense as new records from Korea, identified based on plastid DNA markers (psbA and rbcL) and morpho-anatomical observations. abstract: This study examines the overall strength, dimension, microstructure, fracture surfaces, SEM, EDX, visual/color changes of jackwood under different environmental conditions, including salinity, varnish exposure, and temperature variations, assessing physical and mechanical properties such as volume, microstructure, hardness, and tensile strength. Wood samples are subjected to isochronal and isothermal annealing for varying times and at different temperatures in an atmospheric environment. title: Proteomic insights into sessility and lifestyle evolution in rotifers
abstract: Rotifers are excellent models for studying lifestyle evolution. Within the monogonont rotifers, motile and facultatively sessile species occur across both Pseudotrocha and Gnesiotrocha, whereas obligately sessile lifestyles are confined to Gnesiotrocha. Proteomics offers a valuable approach for elucidating the molecular basis of these lifestyle differences, yet rotifer proteomic studies have been restricted to the model genus Brachionus and some bdelloids, focusing primarily on dormancy, DNA repair, ecotoxicology, and diet. title: Privacidad y seguridad en sistemas de aprendizaje federado: revisión de métodos y desafíos computacionales
abstract: Federated learning enables model training on distributed information without necessarily centralizing raw records. Nevertheless, parameter exchanges, participant coordination, and malicious behavior create threats that do not disappear when data remain at their source. This paper examines privacy and security safeguards in federated learning systems and their computational trade-offs. A structured narrative literature review was conducted through a targeted search of verifiable academic sources and thematic analysis of foundational studies, methodological contributions, and surveys. title: Hierarchical and local detail enhancement for small object detection in aerial images
abstract: Accurate small object detection in aerial images is important for vision-based applications. Detecting unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and birds in airport clearance zones is particularly important for aviation safety. Nevertheless, existing approaches still suffer from pronounced semantic inconsistencies between high-level semantic representations and low-level structural cues during multi-scale feature fusion. title: Minds over matter: addressing the negative impacts of the international commercial wildlife trade on animal wellbeing
abstract: The scale of global commercial trade in wild animals is extensive and expanding. While research has largely focused on conservation impacts, the welfare of animals involved in trade has been largely ignored, despite the large numbers of sentient animals affected. Here, we evaluate three animal species' experiences during their commercial wildlife trade journey, focusing specifically on welfare impacts: bears used in traditional medicine, dolphins for entertainment, and mink farmed for fur production for the fashion industry. title: A Ranging System Integrating Time‐of‐Flight Approach With Optical‐Frequency‐Comb Interferometry for Ultra‐Precise Long‐Distance Measurements
abstract: Time-of-flight (TOF) ranging and pulse interference have been widely applied in high-precision absolute ranging due to high robustness and low ambient noises. However, TOF is typically limited by low resolutions, whereas the absolute lengths determined using the pulse interference method are discrete. In this study, an absolute ranging system integrating TOF with OFC-based interferometric modules was developed. title: When agricultural water reuse subsidies pay for freshwater conservation
abstract: Public funding for agricultural water reuse may expand irrigation supplies without purchasing additional freshwater conservation. Diversion of municipal effluent changes downstream returns, and reuse may proceed without a subsidy. We apply basin accounting, environmental-payment principles, and decision analysis to programs requiring a conservation quantity supported across all admitted scenarios. The assessment distinguishes protected savings caused by a specific subsidy from total project benefits and financing shares. title: Genomic insights into nitrogen metabolism of the heterotrophic nitrifying and aerobic denitrifying bacterium Achromobacter xylosoxidans pf1
abstract: The rapid expansion of aquaculture has exacerbated nitrogen pollution, underscoring the critical need for effective and sustainable nitrogen removal methods. In this study, a heterotrophic nitrification and aerobic denitrification (HNAD) bacterium, designated strain pf1, was isolated from aquaculture pond water and identified as Achromobacter xylosoxidans based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. title: Adopción de la inteligencia artificial en la Educación Superior Latinoamericana: Revisión sistemática y metaanálisis estructural
abstract: El objetivo de esta revisión fue estimar la magnitud combinada de los factores que explican la aceptación y el uso de la inteligencia artificial en estudiantes y docentes universitarios de América Latina y el Caribe, y contrastar qué modelo teórico reproduce mejor la evidencia regional. Se realizó una revisión sistemática conforme a la declaración para la publicación de revisiones sistemáticas y a su extensión para búsquedas, con protocolo registrado antes del cribado. title: A gray-distribution-based adaptive laser stripe center extraction algorithm
abstract: Accurate laser stripe center extraction is critical for high-precision line-structured laser 3D reconstruction. Many existing methods assume that the cross-sectional grayscale distribution of a laser stripe follows a fixed pattern. However, in practical scanning, variations in working distance, object geometry, and surface material lead to significant changes in grayscale distributions across the same stripe, which introduce center localization errors and degrade reconstruction accuracy and robustness. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive laser stripe center extraction method

title: Human-In-The-Loop en ciencia aumentada por IA: Sesgos, vulnerabilidades y evaluación. Revisión de alcance
abstract: La supervisión humana de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la comunicación científica se invoca con frecuencia, pero se desconoce cómo se configura y qué evidencia la respalda. Esta revisión de alcance se preguntó qué configuraciones de supervisión humana, sesgos y vulnerabilidades describe la literatura reciente sobre la coproducción entre humanos e inteligencia artificial en la comunicación científica, y qué implicaciones tienen para la evaluación de la investigación. title: Dynamic Hydrazone Bond Motivated MIM‐Resonator Based Rewritable Dynamic Photonic Paper for Optical Anti‐Counterfeiting and High‐Density Information Dynamic Display
abstract: Herein, a novel aqueous‐environment‐decoded photonic paper with excellent “rewritability” is reported through introducing poly(diacetone acrylamide) (PDAA) brush within metal‐insulator‐metal (MIM) resonators as the intermediate insulating layer. Based on the reversible formation and hydrolysis of the dynamic hydrazone bonds between N 2 H 4 and side carbonyl groups of PDAA chain, the hydrophilicity of the intermediate layer can be modulated, further enabling the photonic paper to exhibit dynamically tunable structural color across the visible spectral range in an aqueous environment. title: Combustion control strategies to achieve low temperature combustion in PCCI engines - A comprehensive review
abstract: Low-temperature combustion (LTC) has emerged as a pivotal solution for modern compression ignition engines, effectively breaking the traditional nitrogen oxide (NOx) and soot emission trade-off. Among LTC variants, Premixed Charge Compression Ignition (PCCI) stands out for its capacity to reduce in-cylinder emissions with minimal structural modifications. This review evaluates alternative fuel integration within PCCI regimes by shifting from isolated, single-variable engine tuning to a unified multi-parameter coupling framework. title: Diffusion–GAT Dual-Channel Framework for Extreme Few-Shot and Noise-Robust Pump Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of main circulation pumps in converter station valve cooling systems is severely challenged by strong electromagnetic interference and extremely limited fault samples. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-informed dual-channel collaborative framework that integrates multi-field coupling priors into both data generation and feature learning. First, feature sensitivity and signal correlation matrices are derived from fluid-mechanical-electrical coupling mechanisms to formulate computable physical priors. title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor-NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness-is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Optimization of solar and wind systems under uncertainty: a review of recent advances in capacity, configuration, and storage planning
abstract: The growing variability and uncertainty associated with renewable energy sources have made optimization under uncertainty an essential component of modern energy system planning. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of optimization approaches applied to solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, and hybrid PV–wind systems, with a focus on capacity planning, storage integration, and system configuration. abstract: Introduction Free-living amoebae (FLA) of the Vahlkampfiidae family are widely distributed in nature, occupying aquatic and terrestrial habitats. The group includes thermophilic amphizoic organisms such as Naegleria fowleri . This study aims to describe natural recreational freshwaters in terms of the presence of thermotolerant vahlkampfiids, sediment microbial communities and climatic/land use features. title: The Influence of AI-Assisted Problem Solving on Decision Quality: Examining the Moderating Role of Cognitive Reflection
abstract: This study examined the influence of AI-assisted problem solving on decision quality and the moderating role of cognitive reflection among university students in Pakistan. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed, with a target sample of 335 undergraduate and postgraduate students from selected public and private universities, including the University of the Punjab, Bahauddin Zakariya University, Government College University Faisalabad, University of Karachi, University of Sindh, University of Peshawar, University of Malakand, and International Islamic University Islamabad

title: Global insights and feasibility evaluation of incineration approach for sustainable waste-to-energy conversion
abstract: The generation of municipal solid waste (MSW) is expected to rise from 2.01 billion tons in 2016–3.40 billion tons by 2050, mostly due to population expansion, urbanization, and industrialization in low- and middle-income nations. The technical, economic, environmental, and social viability of incineration-based waste-to-energy (WTE) is still heavily reliant on local waste characteristics and institutional conditions. title: Synergistic Dual-Modification of Polyurethane Sponge with MIL-53(Al) and Dimethylsilicone Oil for Efficient Oil–Water Separation of Oily Sludge Thermal Washing Wastewater
abstract: Developing highly efficient adsorbents is one of the most feasible strategies to achieve oil-water separation. Conventional sponge adsorbents often suffer from limited capacity, poor cyclic stability, and low selectivity. To overcome these limitations, in this study, we synergistically modified a commercial polyurethane sponge using MIL-53(Al) and dimethylsilicone oil (DMS) via a facile dip-coating strategy, resulting in the M/Si-6@PU sponge. Through the optimization of the synthesis process, the dual-modified sponge evinced a water contact angle of 140° and an oil contact angle of 0° in air.

title: Trust, policy, and teamwork: Missing layers in standards for multi‐agent system interoperability
abstract: Multi‐agent system (MAS) interoperability falls short in three crucial areas: trust, policy, and teamwork . First, we argue that the requirement for trust goes far beyond the basic requirements of authentication. Importantly, accurate trust calibration requires access to robust, verifiable, continuously updated evidence based on experience. Second, we describe the value of digital policy services . title: IA generativa e innovación educativa: Análisis bibliométrico y mapeo científico
abstract: Introducción: Esta investigación analiza la intersección literario-científica entre GenAI (IA generativa) e innovación educativa. Para ello, se usan técnicas bibliométricas y de mapeo científico. El contexto parte de la normalización del uso de ChatGPT, herramienta de IA generativa lanzada en noviembre de 2022. El estudio tiene un triple objetivo: primero, la caracterización de la evolución temporal de la producción científica entre GenAI e innovación educativa. abstract: La formación jurídica todavía no absorbe, de manera sistemática, la rápida difusión de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la práctica judicial y profesional. title: Long-term spatiotemporal assessment of PM₂.₅ in a semi-urban region of Bangladesh using CAMS and MERRA-2 reanalysis data
abstract: Long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is poorly characterised outside South Asia’s major cities, where monitoring is sparse. We assessed PM₂.₅ in Habiganj, a semi-urban district of north-eastern Bangladesh, from 2016 to 2025 using two atmospheric reanalyses, CAMS and MERRA-2. Annual district means ranged from 70.4 to 84.9 µg m⁻³ in CAMS and from 35.0 to 44.2 µg m⁻³ in MERRA-2, 7–17 times the World Health Organization guideline of 5 µg m⁻³ in every year. title: YOLO11-Based Object Detection against Same-Color Backgrounds
abstract: Objects that closely match background color are difficult to localize because chromatic cues weaken and boundaries can be obscured. This study evaluates a YOLO11 baseline using a dataset containing at least 12 object categories and approximately 630 images per category, trained for 100 epochs. Training and validation curves are summarized alongside confidence-based and precision-recall analyses, and an exploratory grayscale-Canny-YOLO fusion path is documented separately from the evaluated baseline. title: Retreating glaciers and snow cover are amplifying summer droughts in the upper Adige River Basin (Italy)
abstract: Snow and glacier meltwater play a critical role in sustaining summer streamflow in mountains and downstream regions. Yet, understanding glaciers' contributions to buffer river streamflow during droughts remains limited and poses major barriers to improve present and future water management within the context of climate change. This study evaluates the contribution of glacier melt to summer flows and its role in mitigating hydrological droughts in the upper Adige River basin (Italy). title: Urban climate dynamics in informal settlements: Spatiotemporal rainfall and temperature variability in Thembelihle, Johannesburg
abstract: Climate change has emerged as a critical contemporary concern, marked by greater variability and severity in weather systems, from extreme heat to drought and intense precipitation. Africa is particularly vulnerable, with urban settlements facing disproportionate risks. This study investigates long-term temperature and rainfall dynamics in Thembelihle, an informal settlement in Johannesburg, alongside broader metropolitan trends, using robust statistical and geospatial methods. title: A comprehensive analytic framework for wave solutions and stability in perturbed Gardner equations
abstract: This work advances the mathematical analysis of the perturbed Gardner equation—a key model for nonlinear waves in plasmas, hydrodynamics, and optics. We introduce the improved modified extended tanh-function method (IMETFM), a robust analytical framework that generates exact traveling wave solutions, including bright/dark solitons, singular solitons, periodic waves, and rational forms. abstract: Against the backdrop of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this paper reviews the literature on improving the energy trilemma. It first elaborates on the background and significance of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, and then discusses in detail the theoretical research on the energy trilemma, energy security and the energy trilemma, energy transition and the energy trilemma, the evolution of the energy trilemma across different regions, measures for improving the energy trilemma, the role of the energy trilemma, and future development directions. title: Accurately assigning coprolites to vertebrate spiral intestine types: A case study from the Kem Kem beds (Morocco, Cretaceous)
abstract: The Kem Kem Group (Morocco) is renowned for its emblematic mid-Cretaceous vertebrate fauna and the high abundance of predators represented amongst its fossil assemblage. In such predators-dominated context, analysing associated fossil faeces may yield valuable insight into the trophic interactions and biotic dynamics existing at that time in this ecosystem. abstract: This study investigates the composition‐dependent mechanical, thermal, and dielectric properties of bioepoxy composites (BECs) incorporating epoxidized rapeseed oil (ERO) as a renewable modifier and granite powder as an inorganic geological reinforcement. The ERO content remains constant at 3.4 wt.%, while the granite concentration increases from 0 to 6.85 wt.% to elucidate the relationships between formulation, microstructure, and functional performance. title: Knowledge Management-Based Digital Inheritance Model for Shadow Play Intangible Cultural Heritage
abstract: Against global digital transformation, shadow intangible heritage suffers cultural knowledge loss and low audience engagement. This study treats shadow play inheritance as a full-cycle knowledge management problem, comparing three mainstream digital carriers: static archiving, immersive VR and mobile interactive platforms. Cross-project statistics and user experiments reveal major flaws of prior schemes: fragmented cultural metadata, passive participation and missing closed knowledge feedback. title: Institutional thresholds in the climate and food availability nexus in South Asia
abstract: Climate shocks interacting with socioeconomic and institutional conditions threaten food availability (FA; per capita dietary energy supply) in South Asia. Yet studies of climate-food security linkages rely largely on linear frameworks that overlook nonlinear responses and institutional heterogeneity. title: Checklist of oribatid mites (Acari: Oribatida) of Israel, with new faunistic records
abstract: Israel lies at the intersection of the Mediterranean, Saharo-Arabian, Irano-Turanian, and Afrotropical biogeographical regions, yet no comprehensive synthesis of its oribatid mite fauna has previously been available. We present the first comprehensive checklist of Oribatida of Israel, combining published records with newly identified material collected in 2023–2024. title: Long-range transported biomass burning aerosols from wildfires observed at Mount Zugspitze
abstract: The release of air pollutants during wildfires (WFs) poses a growing threat to climate, air quality, and public health. In August 2025, an extreme wildfire season affected large parts of the Iberian Peninsula. Measurements of multiple biomass burning indicators were carried out at the high-altitude research station Schneefernerhaus on Mount Zugspitze (2666 m a.s.l.), Germany. abstract: AI systems can lead to discriminatory outcomes. While EU non-discrimination law prohibits discrimination on specific protected attributes, compliance of this legislation by AI decision-making systems implemented in social contexts appears uncertain for several reasons (e.g. AI systems often discriminate subtly and opaquely, making proof of discrimination difficult to obtain). title: Navigating Fire Impacts: Environmental and Socioeconomic Analysis of Wildfires in Los Angeles County
abstract: This study examines the environmental and socio-economic impacts of the 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles County using remote sensing (RS) and geographic information systems (GIS). The research aims to analyze the relationships between land use dynamics, wildfire impacts, and social vulnerability in order to support decision-making processes for post-disaster recovery. title: Regulatory evidentiary closure as a formal framework for citation faithfulness in large language models
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to generate answers with citations in regulatory settings, including compliance review, clinical governance, fiscal assessment, legal interpretation, and institutional risk analysis. Existing work on attribution, retrieval augmented generation, citation evaluation, and sufficient context has clarified when generated claims are grounded in identifiable sources. title: Arctic Puffin Algorithm with local escaping operator for feature selection in high-dimensional datasets
abstract: Large datasets might make data mining more difficult due to their high dimensionality. To minimize the dimensionality of large datasets, feature selection is an essential step that maximizes classification accuracy by choosing the most informative features. In this study, a binary adaptation of the enhanced Arctic Puffin Optimization (EAPO) algorithm, which builds on the Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO) algorithm, is introduced within a wrapper-based framework to identify the optimal subset of features for classification tasks. title: Dispersive relaxation in indium tin oxide contacted silicon oxide memristive devices
abstract: Silicon oxide memristive devices exhibit volatile current transients in addition to non-volatile resistive switching. Such transients are candidate temporary states for neuromorphic systems, but their form depends on coupled processes in the oxide and its electrode interfaces. Here, we characterise the transient measured in devices with indium tin oxide (ITO) top contacts using constant-current stress, held-voltage measurements, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiling of stressed and pristine samples. title: Grid-optimized neural operators (GONOs) for FE-node-consistent thermo-mechanical field reconstruction in electron-beam powder-bed fusion
abstract: High-fidelity finite-element (FE) simulations of electron-beam powder-bed fusion (EB-PBF) provide thermo-mechanical fields but are too expensive for repeated field queries. This work proposes grid-optimized neural operators (GONOs), which couple FE nodal data with structured-grid neural operators through a bidirectional point-cloud–grid transformation. title: YUV20K: a complexity-driven benchmark and trajectory-aware alignment model for video camouflaged object detection
abstract: The development of video camouflaged object detection (VCOD) is currently constrained by the scarcity of challenging benchmarks and the lack of robustness of models in the face of erratic motion dynamics. Existing methods frequently encounter challenges related to motion-induced appearance instability and temporal feature misalignment, particularly in complex motion scenarios. To address the issue of data bottleneck, we present YUV20K, a pixel-level annotated, complexity-driven VCOD benchmark. abstract: Objectives Environmental sustainability remains a central policy concern for economies undergoing structural diversification, particularly in carbon-intensive nations such as Saudi Arabia, yet the influence of banking-sector development remains comparatively under-examined. This study investigates how banking development, renewable energy consumption, and economic growth shape environmental sustainability in Saudi Arabia using both carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and the load capacity factor (LCF). title: Bacterial stability and site-specific homogeneity in urban groundwater under Low-Temperature aquifer thermal energy storage operation
abstract: The bacterial microbiome in groundwater ecosystems is essential for drinking water quality and biogeochemical cycling. Low-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (LT-ATES) systems may influence these communities, yet in situ evidence remains limited. We hypothesized that LT-ATES operation alters groundwater bacterial diversity and community composition. abstract: This paper aims to investigate the various strengthening techniques for restoring the flexural performance of ultra-high-performance fiber-reinforced concrete (UHPFRC) beams with a simulated reduction in tensile reinforcement, represented by removing one or two steel bars to model a simplified condition of reinforcement loss due to corrosion. The strengthening techniques include near-surface mounting (NSM) of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) bars, glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars, and a CFRP plate. abstract: Conventional compression casting of fresh cementitious materials generally requires applying pressure over the entire specimen cross-section, resulting in high loading demands and potential changes in specimen dimensions. This study proposes a novel small-diameter pressure-inlet casting method that introduces additional fresh material into a confined mold to improve material density while maintaining the designed specimen geometry. abstract: Tributaries of the middle Rio São Francisco basin, including the Rio Verde Grande, are important nursery habitats for reproduction of migratory fishes and provide water for economic activities such as agriculture, but the characterization of the fish fauna in these areas remains understudied. title: Cluster Models Confronted with Small Island Developing States: Relevance, Usefulness and Limits of the Marshall, Porter and Schmitz Models
abstract: The cluster concept is applied to Small Island Developing States (SIDS) through models developed and tested in continental settings. These are generally Marshall’s industrial district, Porter’s competitive cluster and Schmitz’s collective efficiency. To varying degrees, these models depend on a critical mass of firms, sufficient spatial density and a deep domestic market. Small SIDS, however, fail to meet all three conditions at once. abstract: To effectively prevent bridge operation and maintenance (O&M) accidents, a hybrid method integrating text mining with Bayesian network theory was adopted to systematically analyze the causal factors of accidents affecting bridge O&M safety and their interrelationships. First, text mining techniques were applied to preprocess data from 226 Chinese bridge O&M accident cases (1999–2025). abstract: EEG-based shared autonomy integrates neural commands with autonomous assistance to improve control reliability under uncertain brain signals. However, EEG commands may exhibit varying confidence levels and conflict with autonomous actions, making dynamic authority allocation a key challenge. This study proposes a conflict-aware, functionally heterogeneous multi-agent shared-control framework with reinforcement-learning-based authority arbitration for semi-closed-loop EEG-based shared autonomy. abstract: Spatially compounding climate extremes are increasingly recognized as a source of climate-related risk, and their risk significance depends on how synchrony affects connected systems. The critical transition occurs when cross-regional synchrony reduces support from places that would otherwise buffer one another through substitution, reserve capacity, mutual assistance or recovery support—a condition we term spatial buffering loss (BL). abstract: This study aims to evaluate service quality and determine improvement priorities at the Savings and Loan Cooperative of PT Swabina Gatra by integrating Service Quality (SERVQUAL) and Importance Performance Analysis (IPA). Unlike previous studies that primarily confirm the existence of service gaps, the novelty of this research lies in its methodological contribution: creating a two-dimensional prioritization framework that combines gap magnitudes with IPA quadrant placements to classify attributes into immediate action, maintenance, or resource reallocation. abstract: Rising demand for housing and infrastructure, slow construction timelines, and the large CO 2 footprint of cement, requires improvements in conventional construction methods and materials. title: Techno-economic assessment of commercial wind turbines for electricity generation in Nigeria
abstract: The main aim of the present paper is to examine the wind energy potential, as well as the performance and economic sustainability, based on mean monthly wind speed data collected from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) and previous scientific studies. In this study, the Weibull distribution function is used to analyze the characteristics of the wind resources of 32 locations in Nigeria. title: SISAL_monv1: a global database of cave monitoring observations
abstract: Cave monitoring is the process of collecting observational data such as microclimate conditions, hydrogeochemistry and water movement in cave systems. The most common motivation is for speleothem science – the reconstruction of past climate and environmental variability from cave formations such as stalagmites. Applications also include the monitoring of potential recharge to aquifers, as well as cave conservation. title: Compound and cascading risks in the context of epidemics and pandemics: A scoping literature review
abstract: Given the extended timelines of epidemics and pandemics, disasters are likely to arise concurrently with the potential to have compounding or cascading effects and feedback loops that could disrupt societal functioning and threaten societal resilience. This scoping review aimed to identify published literature related to the resiliency impacts of compound and cascading events occurring during or resulting in an epidemic/pandemic. title: Advanced reactor designs and technologies for wastewater purification: Bioprocesses and nanotechnology for nutrient and energy sustainability
abstract: The growing impact of anthropogenic activities, including urbanization, agriculture and industrial expansion, has intensified water and environmental pollution, and wastewater treatment has evolved beyond pollutant removal toward the recovery of nutrients, energy and high-value materials. title: Reassessing long-term downward surface solar radiation changes over China based on an integrated satellite record
abstract: Temporal inconsistencies in station records complicate assessments of multidecadal downward surface solar radiation (DSR) changes over China. This study integrates evidence from ground observations, satellite products, reanalyses, and climate-model simulations to reassess DSR changes from 1980 to 2025. Evaluation against independent Surface Radiation Budget Network (SURFRAD) observations guides the integration of CLARA-A3 and CERES EBAF through calendar-month mean–variance adjustment, yielding the CLARES satellite composite. title: Assessment of vegetation water dynamics by comparing microwave remote sensing signals from satellites and field-based GNSS reflectometry
abstract: Monitoring plant water stress and biomass is limited by labor intensive measurements techniques. Observing plant water conditions more broadly is now enabled by microwave remote sensing. Specifically, satellite-based vegetation optical depth (VOD) provides daily observations of vegetation water volume at tens of kilometers. While satellite VOD has been used for many applications, VOD validations have rarely been carried out. title: Diwariskan, Diciptakan, atau Didigitalkan? Tinjauan Sistematis Batik dalam Pendidikan
abstract: Lebih dari lima belas tahun setelah UNESCO memasukkan program pendidikan dan pelatihan batik Indonesia bersama Museum Batik Pekalongan ke dalam Register of Good Safeguarding Practices, belum ada sintesis sistematis tentang bagaimana batik dihadirkan dalam pendidikan: sebagai warisan yang diwariskan, bahan penciptaan, atau objek digital. abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? abstract: Introducción: La inteligencia artificial (IA) se utiliza en psicoterapia mediante agentes conversacionales, programas de terapia cognitivo-conductual, herramientas de procesamiento del lenguaje y sistemas de apoyo al profesional. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are being increasingly integrated into immersive environments and design workflows, providing application prospects in areas such as rapid scene prototyping for non-expert users and scene understanding capabilities for accessibility design. While many workflows that incorporate LLMs in immersive spaces are proposed, such systems can exhibit errors, potentially resulting in frustration, loss of user trust, and compromised user safety. abstract: This study investigated the toxic effects of thiamethoxam (TMX) on the liver and intestine of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) during a 14-day exposure and evaluated the protective potential of dietary luteolin. A total of 180 fish were randomly assigned to six groups (3 replicate aquaria per treatment, 10 fish per aquarium), with n = 7 fish/group sampled for biochemical and histological analyses: a control group, luteolin-treated groups (200 and 400 mg/kg diet), a TMX-exposed group (100 mg/L), and combined TMX plus luteolin groups. title: Long-term ecological effects of altered flow-sediment regimes in the lower yellow river: nonlinear thresholds, channel mediation, and spatial heterogeneity
abstract: Introduction Ecological responses to altered flow and sediment regimes may involve interannual lags, nonlinear responses, and channel mediation, yet these features are rarely integrated into a single assessment framework for the Lower Yellow River. Methods We integrated flow, sediment, and channel records for 1960–2025 with ecological records for 1980–2025 in the Huayuankou–Gaocun and Gaocun–Taochengpu reaches. title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
abstract: Methane emissions account for nearly a third of the Earth’s effective radiative forcing, with methanotrophs playing a critical role in mitigating emissions by oxidising methane in diverse environments. Despite their ecological importance, methanotrophic diversity and environmental distribution remain incompletely characterised due to cultivation challenges, incomplete or low-quality metagenome-assembled genomes, and limited taxonomic resolution in marker gene surveys. title: Meteorological conditions and aerosol-meteorology feedback drive divergent responses of co-occurring PM 2.5 and O 3 pollution to NO x –VOC perturbations in Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei–Shandong
abstract: Co-occurring PM 2.5 and O 3 pollution (Double High Pollution, DHP) is a growing concern, yet its response to emission controls under different meteorological conditions is poorly quantified. Previous studies focused on synoptic-scale classifications or single meteorological variables, largely neglecting aerosol-meteorology feedback. abstract: High-resolution measurements of near-surface temperature are essential for understanding environmental responses to extreme weather events, yet are rarely available from dense, regularly spaced in situ measurement grids. Here, we analyse temperature measurements derived from a dense network of over 3000 nodal seismometers deployed across a 6 km 2 area in North Yorkshire, UK, during the July 2022 heatwave, using data from embedded microcontroller sensors. title: Investigating Factors Influencing Consumer Behavior in Reducing Single-Use Plastic Bag Usage: An Extended TPB Approach
abstract: Plastic pollution remains a major environmental concern, and single-use plastic bags contribute substantially to urban waste. This study examines factors associated with consumers’ intention to reduce single-use plastic bag use and their self-reported plastic-bag reduction behaviour among Retail S customers in Bandung, Indonesia. Drawing on an extended Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) framework, the study examines the roles of attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, convenience, and policy promotion. abstract: Structural health monitoring is increasingly relevant to smart cities because deterioration, changing loads and climatic exposure cannot always be captured through periodic inspection. This review evaluates how embedded sensors, synchronised acquisition, wireless communications, edge analytics and cloud-based infrastructure intelligence can form a trustworthy evidence chain for bridges, buildings and associated urban assets.
