abstract: Plant-associated microbes, collectively known as the phytomicrobiome, strongly influence plant growth, nutrient acquisition, and stress resilience. However, they are often viewed as external agricultural inputs rather than dynamic components of plant adaptation. This review introduces the concept of climate-selected microbiomes as evolutionary solutions shaped by long-term natural and anthropogenic stress. abstract: This study investigates the impact of global risk factors specifically geopolitical risk (GPR), economic policy uncertainty (GEPU), market volatility (VIX), and commodity price dynamics on the monetary stability of Brunei Darussalam. Given the vulnerability of small open economies to external shocks, understanding the transmission mechanism of these risks is critical for maintaining the resilience of the Brunei Dollar (BND) peg. abstract: Habitat manipulation is a recurrent, community-deliverable form of larval source management; however, its association with human malaria infection has rarely been quantified. This cross-sectional analysis, nested within a randomised two-district cluster trial of integrated environmental management, examined associations between eight self-reported habitat management practices and malaria parasitaemia among adults in Ada West and North Tongu, Ghana, between July and December 2024. title: Toward Transferable Descriptors Linking Formation and Environmental Effects of Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter
abstract: Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is increasingly recognized as an active product of plastic weathering; however, its environmental effects remain difficult to compare or predict. A major problem is the absence of variables that can maintain comparable mechanistic meaning across formation and effect studies. abstract: Biocontrol yeasts offer alternatives or complements to synthetic fungicides for managing postharvest fungal diseases. Despite promising antagonistic activity under laboratory conditions, inconsistent performance under practical conditions remains a major limitation. Here, we use ecological fitness operationally to describe a biocontrol yeast’s ability to establish, recover from environmental stress, and persist on fruit under specified handling and storage conditions. abstract: Incomplete combustion of plastic waste is an emerging pathway for forming thermally transformed microplastics (MPs), whose physicochemical identity and ecotoxicological potential in aquatic vertebrates remain poorly understood, as available evidence has focused primarily on the toxicity of their leachates and extracts. abstract: Miniaturization and high integration of 5G electronics, aerospace components, and intelligent devices have caused severe heat accumulation, shortening the service life and degrading the reliability of devices. abstract: This review explores how community-based approaches can offer effective, context-specific strategies that both adapt to and mitigate climate change, while simultaneously advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It interrogates how bottom-up activities have helped strengthen vulnerable populations, especially in climate-affected regions, to be more resilient and achieve a meaningful transition. abstract: Post-harvest losses (PHL) remove a substantial share of the food produced in developing-country agricultural systems, commonly estimated at 20–40 percent for perishables and 10–25 percent for staples, before it reaches a consumer. The dominant policy response has treated PHL as an engineering and logistics problem, funding storage structures, cold chains, and transport upgrades. abstract: Large-scale enterprise environments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous log data from web servers, applications, network devices, and cloud services, making timely monitoring and historical analysis increasingly challenging. abstract: Sustainable engineering materials and lightweight materials have gained demand in the present scenario and have also accelerated the advancement of natural fiber-reinforced polymer composite materials for automotive and load-bearing applications. abstract: El objetivo de este estudio es analizar el uso de memes, imágenes y vídeos como herramientas de propaganda política durante la presidencia de Donald Trump en Estados Unidos. La comunicación política reciente ha experimentado un cambio cualitativo impulsado por la desinformación online, los memes en redes sociales y la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial generativa, que facilita la rápida difusión de contenidos manipulados. abstract: Sensor reconstruction under false-data injection (FDI) is investigated on a control-oriented, reduced-order nonlinear floating offshore wind turbine inspired by the NREL 5-MW rated scale. abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are a promising technology for harvesting ambient mechanical energy, yet their durability is fundamentally limited by friction-induced wear at functional interfaces. Friction in TENGs is inherently paradoxical: It enables charge generation while simultaneously accelerating material degradation. abstract: Individual pitch control (IPC) is commonly used to mitigate periodic blade loads in wind turbines, relying on the multiblade coordinate (MBC). abstract: Nature-based tourism depends not only on ecological assets but also on governance arrangements that shape participation and conservation financing. This Perspective Article examines survey evidence from rural Guayas, Ecuador, to distinguish among perceived environmental problems, organized participation, general support for conservation contributions, personal willingness to pay (WTP), and payment-mechanism preferences. abstract: Nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO 2 ) are major drivers of air pollution and ecosystem damage. title: Analysis of Surface Meteorological Parameters Associated with Wet Days in Maiduguri, Northeastern Nigeria
abstract: Rainfall in the Sudano-Sahelian zone of northeastern Nigeria is confined to a short monsoon season, yet daily relationships between surface meteorological conditions and rainfall occurrence are rarely documented for Maiduguri. This exploratory two-year (2023–2024) diagnostic study examined surface conditions associated with wet days in Maiduguri using daily NASA POWER (MERRA-2-based) estimates of 2-m air temperature, 2-m relative humidity, 10-m wind speed and precipitation for 2023–2024 with a number of samples (n = 731). journal: Journal of Collective Sciences and Sustainability

title: Toward a civil contract of post-photography: AI-Generated humanitarian aesthetics between photojournalism and art
abstract: This article examines how AI-generated (AIG) humanitarian images change the aestheticisation of suffering in photojournalism. Drawing on fifteen semi-structured interviews with Italian photo editors, photojournalists and documentary photographers, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis, it identifies two processes onto which AIG aesthetics is grafted: stockification, through which images of suffering become generic, and artification, through which documentary images are increasingly evaluated according to artistic criteria. title: Advances in microbiome methods for plant-soil interactions in agricultural systems
abstract: Research on plant-soil microbiomes increasingly relies on methods that go beyond characterizing microbial community composition to investigate microbial activity, ecological processes, and plant responses. Traditional cultivation techniques and early molecular fingerprinting laid the groundwork for microbial ecology, while advances in high-throughput sequencing, mass spectrometry, bioinformatics, and single-cell imaging have broadened the scope of microbiome research. institutions: Institute of Soil and Water Conservation

title: Automatic Plant Watering Based on Soil Moisture Sensor and PID Control
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of an automatic plant watering system based on a soil moisture sensor and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control, implemented on an Arduino Uno in the Tinkercad circuit simulator and analysed numerically in Scilab. The objective is to provide a documented and reproducible software-in-the-loop baseline for closed-loop soil moisture regulation. institutions: Sunan Kalijaga State Islamic University Yogyakarta

title: Hydrogeochemical Assessment of Groundwater and Surface Water under Environmental Pressures: Case Study of the Mô Basin, Togo
abstract: This study presents the first comprehensive hydrochemical characterization of water resources in the Mô Basin (central-western Togo) to identify the factors controlling water chemistry, assess water quality for drinking and irrigation, and identify areas most vulnerable to anthropogenic impacts. We collected 150 water samples (132 groundwater samples from 44 boreholes and 18 surface water samples from 6 monitoring stations) across three hydrological periods (low-flow, high-flow, and transition). Physicochemical parameters and major ions were analyzed in accordance with AFNOR standard methods.

title: Lake hydrochemistry and aquatic plant diversity across permafrost landscapes of Yakutia, Eastern Siberia
abstract: Central Yakutia in eastern Siberia is characterized by abundant lakes in permafrost-thaw depressions, named alaas. They constitute the traditional cultural landscape that is home to the indigenous Sakha people, providing critical ecosystem services. This study aims at assessing present-day lake characteristics and exploring their drivers based on lake hydrochemistry and aquatic and terrestrial plant diversity derived from sedimentary DNA in surface sediments. title: Branding visual en la era algorítmica: Autenticidad, participación humana y modelos híbridos
abstract: Este estudio examina cómo la inteligencia artificial generativa transforma la identidad visual de marca y la percepción del consumidor. Mediante un análisis teórico integrado con estudios de caso específicos, se evidencia que el contenido generado por IA activa respuestas ambivalentes: mientras la personalización y eficiencia potencian el engagement, la ausencia de señales humanas erosiona la autenticidad percibida. title: Scale‐Expandable All‐Wood‐Based Hydrogel for Highly Efficient Desalination Enabled by 3D Printing and Array Design
abstract: Fully utilizing all components of waste biomass while enabling scalable structural design remains a critical challenge for solar‐driven interfacial desalination. Herein, we convert waste wood powder into an all‐component wood based (all‐wood‐based) hydrogel (AWH) solar evaporator via one‐step reusable ionic compounds (ICs) composed of ZnCl 2 and CaCl 2 , and through 3D printing and array design, a scale‐expandable pyramid‐structure array evaporator for efficient desalination was realized. title: Towards multi-hazard assessment: a score-based framework for screening and ranking Italian municipalities
abstract: Identifying natural hazard hotspots is essential for disaster risk reduction, yet comparing and aggregating heterogeneous hazards remains challenging due to differences in metrics, spatial-temporal scales, and data availability. This study proposes a transparent, index-based framework for ranking single and multiple natural hazards and identifying multi-hazard hotspots at national and sub-national scales without relying on data-intensive risk modelling. title: Modelo global de evolución de la inteligencia artificial generativa aplicada a los resultados de aprendizaje de estudiantes de educación regular y superior
abstract: Hablar a la inteligencia artificial en la actualidad se ha convertido en un tema relevante en el ámbito de la educación en la que los procesos formativos no volverán hacer los mismos, ya que existe un modelo global de evolución del uso de la inteligencia artificial que inicia en el hogar, escuela y universidad, una secuencia que hace analizar el nivel de conocimiento, uso para actividades educativas, restricciones y promoción, y aprendizaje significativo.Esta investigación titulada “Modelos globales de evolución de la inteligencia artificial generativa aplicada a los resultados de aprendizaje

title: ANALISIS DISTRIBUSI TEGANGAN PADA SAMBUNGAN PIPA HIGH PRESSURE AKIBAT PENAMBAHAN STIFFENER MENGGUNAKAN ANSYS
abstract: High-pressure piping flange connections are susceptible to stress concentration due to geometric discontinuities, which may affect structural integrity. This study aims to analyze stress distribution and evaluate the effects of variations in the number and thickness of stiffener plates on Von Mises stress, stress concentration factor (SCF), and deformation in an ASME B16.5 Class 900 NPS 6 weld neck flange made of ASTM A105 steel. title: Vulnerability Assessments of Road–Rail Multimodal Transport Network With Integrated Coupled Map Lattices
abstract: The coupled map lattices (CML) model has been observed to be adaptable to the cascading failure modeling of transport networks. However, most studies ignore the impact of the node's anti‐risk ability on network performance. This paper proposes an improved CML model to evaluate the node state of the road‐rail multimodal transport network, assess the important nodes' anti‐risk ability, and study the evolution process and vulnerability of the cascading failure under the disturbance of emergencies. title: Inteligencia artificial y gerencia policial: hacia un modelo de corresponsabilidad algorítmica en la toma de decisiones administrativas y operativas en la Policía Nacional de Colombia
abstract: La creciente incorporación de sistemas de inteligencia artificial (IA) en la gestión de seguridad y administración policial está modificando los mecanismos de toma de decisiones, responsabilidad y rendición de cuentas. En este artículo se describen, desde una aproximación crítica y situada, las tensiones éticas, gerenciales y formativas que la IA pone de manifiesto en la Policía Nacional de Colombia. title: A Janus Bilayer Portland Cement‐Based Moisture‐Electricity Generator via Hydrogen‐Bonding Network Regulation
abstract: The ubiquitous interaction between ambient moisture and built environments presents a compelling opportunity for continuous energy harvesting through moisture‐electricity generation (MEG). However, current MEG materials fail to satisfy high‐power demands in buildings because hydrogen bonds, indispensable for the structural integrity of soft carbon‐chain networks, severely restrict water diffusion, and thus bottleneck MEG performance. title: Assessing spatial genetic resilience and enhancement strategies for traditional villages in Liping County, Guizhou, China
abstract: Resilience stands as a central theme within sustainability science, and the resilience of traditional villages and their spatial genes constituting a vital facet of “rural resilience”. This paper applies resilience theory to the study of spatial genetic resilience in traditional villages within China’s ethnic regions. title: Unsupervised Segmentation of Subsurface Delaminations in Large‐Tow Carbon Fiber‐Reinforced Polymer Composites Using Long‐Pulse Thermography
abstract: Large‐tow carbon fiber‐reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites offer cost and manufacturing advantages for large‐scale structural applications; however, tow‐induced structural texture and anisotropic heat diffusion generate strong directional and grid‐like thermal backgrounds that obscure weak delamination responses in long‐pulse thermography. This study proposes an unsupervised framework for segmenting subsurface delaminations in large‐tow CFRP laminates. title: 3D biomanufacturing in tissue engineering: From structural biomimicry to functional integration
abstract: Objectives Three-dimensional (3D) biomanufacturing has emerged as a cornerstone of tissue engineering by recreating physiologically relevant microenvironments. This review aims to integrate scaffold-free self-organization, scaffold-based biomimetic construction, and dynamic bioreactor culture into a unified framework and to chart the transition from structural biomimicry to functional integration. title: Towards biodiversity-relevant chemical risk assessment: insights from SETAC Europe 2025
abstract: A special session entitled “ Biodiversity and chemical hazard/risk assessment: regulatory frameworks, integrative approaches and research for a sustainable future ” was held at the SETAC Europe 2025 Annual Meeting. The session explored how environmental risk assessment (ERA) of chemicals can better support biodiversity protection, drawing on presentations, panel discussions and a live survey of over 100 participants. title: Superionic Al─O─H Compounds With Unconventional Stoichiometries Under Extreme Planetary Conditions
abstract: Extreme pressure and temperature induce novel chemical behaviors, including unconventional stoichiometries and superionic states. Here, by combining crystal structure prediction with first‐principles calculations, we identify two unconventional stoichiometries in the ternary Al─O─H system, AlOH and AlH 3 O 4 , which lie on the convex hull at 300 GPa. title: Alucinaciones en agentes autónomos de IA para ciberseguridad: riesgos operativos y mecanismos de control
abstract: El uso de agentes autónomos basados en modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño en ciberseguridad plantea retos de confiabilidad, especialmente cuando información no verificada orienta decisiones o acciones automatizadas. Este estudio analizó las alucinaciones en estos agentes, su propagación mediante herramientas, sus posibles consecuencias operativas y los mecanismos de control descritos en la literatura. title: Toward structure-specific modeling of cotton/Lycra knit width, density and recovery
abstract: Introduction: Cotton/Lycra ® weft-knitted fabrics are the dominant substrate for stretch apparel, yet manufacturers still lack structure-specific, quantitative rules for predicting how yarn count and elastane denier will shift dimensional stability once fabric leaves the knitting floor. This study establishes such rules across the following three fundamental weft-knitted architectures used in stretch knitwear: single jersey, 1 × 1 rib, and interlock. title: ADCdb 2.0: clinical landscape and ADMET profiles of antibody–drug conjugates
abstract: Systematically characterizing antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) is essential for understanding their therapeutic properties, guiding molecular design, and supporting clinical development. Recently, the expanding clinical landscape of ADCs has generated extensive information on target antigens, therapeutic indications, and clinical trial pipelines, providing a valuable foundation for informing ADC development strategies. title: Can Climate and Environmental SDG Targets Be Met by 2030? A Target–Gap–Pace Framework
abstract: Target–Gap–Pace 2030 assesses whether observed progress is fast enough to meet original climate and environmental Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) commitments by their agreed deadlines. Using United Nations and custodian releases available by August 11, 2026, this paper demonstrate the pace calculations for five access indicators and one energy‐intensity indicator under SDGs 6 and 7. title: Geoeconomic risk and generation costs in Sri Lanka’s hydro-thermal power system
abstract: Introduction: Regulated electricity systems in import-dependent economies face structural vulnerability when global energy crises transmit into domestic generation costs. This paper develops a cost decomposition framework that distinguishes systematic geoeconomic risk driven by oil price, exchange rate, and freight cost shocks from structural risk arising from endogenous generation mix shifts, grounding the analysis in the systematic/unsystematic risk decomposition from Modern Portfolio Theory. title: Satellite-assisted wildfire propagation under environmental uncertainty: Huygens-based front evolution
abstract: Wildfire propagation results from the complex interaction of fuel characteristics, atmospheric and environmental conditions, and terrain topography. This work proposes a satellite-assisted wildfire propagation model that integrates remote sensing observations with a front-propagation approach based on Huygens’ principle. The model combines thermal data, vegetation indices, and meteorological information to estimate directional rates of spread and generate evolving wildfire perimeters. title: An observational study of microbial communities in distressed orchard soil under regenerative management
abstract: This study reports an exploratory, cross-sectional survey of bacterial, archaeal, and eukaryotic soil communities in an approximately 0.35-hectare historically distressed orchard under regenerative management on a regenerative farm in Virginia, USA. Thirteen samples were collected from the distressed area beneath red clover, white clover, fescue, chicory, or common ragweed. 16 S and 18 S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing was used to evaluate the richness and diversity of microbial communities. title: Live bass, fish heads, and bacalao: ethnic supermarkets increase seafood access and strengthen food system resilience in a US urban system
abstract: Ethnic supermarkets serving specific cultural communities have long provided alternatives to mainstream food retail systems; however, their role in seafood diversity and supply chain structure is poorly understood. To characterize product diversity and pricing, we surveyed non-frozen seafood products at supermarkets serving Asian, Black/Latin American/Caribbean, Eastern European, and “mainstream” communities in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA, and conducted interviews with store staff to elucidate seafood procurement systems at different stores. title: Limites de cobertura e desvios de medição na inspeção ultrassônica interna de Risers de perfuração: reanálise de dados experimentais e perspectivas tecnológicas
abstract: Inspecionar risers de perfuração pelo diâmetro interno permite avaliar soldas e espessura de parede sem desembarcar o equipamento, mas os limites de medição e de cobertura dessa inspeção ainda foram pouco quantificados. Para isso, reanalisa dados já publicados, obtidos com ultrassom phased array, difração do tempo de voo e ultrassom convencional, com apoio de um modelo geométrico e de revisão narrativa, sem novos ensaios. title: Sustaining China’s basic medical insurance funds: a multidimensional review of actuarial balance, payment innovation, and system resilience
abstract: Background China’s basic medical insurance scheme covers over 1.35 billion enrollees and is under compound pressure from rapid population aging, rising healthcare costs, and slower economic growth. Whether its pooled funds can remain actuarially and fiscally sustainable has become a central policy question, yet existing reviews have examined single dimensions in isolation and have not reported reproducible search strategies or quantified the composition of the evidence base. title: Analysis of agricultural crop patterns using multi-year satellite-based data: Stability, diversity and change in the Küçük Menderes Basin (2017-2024)
abstract: This study examines the annual agricultural crop dynamics of the Küçük Menderes Basin, located in western Turkey on the Aegean coast, between 2017 and 2024. The main data source for the study consists of annual crop type data provided by the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. Accordingly, using a pixel-based GIS approach, the dynamics of agricultural crops in the basin are explained through three main complementary indicators: Crop Change Frequency, Unique Crop Count, and Dominant Crop & Dominance Ratio. title: A Comprehensive Review of the Cascading Public Health Consequences of Hydrological Disasters: Epidemiological, Toxicological, Nutritional, and Psychosocial Impacts
abstract: Hydrological disasters, primarily floods and tropical cyclones, represent the most frequent and devastating natural hazards globally. Driven by anthropogenic climate change, extreme precipitation events are increasing in both frequency and severity, creating complex public health emergencies that extend far beyond the acute impact phase. This comprehensive review synthesizes current epidemiological, clinical, toxicological, nutritional, and psychological evidence to elucidate the multi-dimensional health impacts of flooding. abstract: Existing signature authentication technologies still face challenges such as complex materials, high costs, and inconvenient operation. In addition, in the field of dynamic optical anti‐counterfeiting, conventional multicolor mechanoluminescence (ML) usually depends on the coexistence of multiple luminescent centers. However, multiple luminescent centers often lead to issues such as spectral instability, energy transfer, and complicated material synthesis. abstract: La zona urbana del cantón Guamote (Chimborazo, Ecuador) elevadas, lluvias intensas y una red de alcantarillado pluvial de tubería PVC construida en 2017. title: From Diagnosis to Development: How Point-of-Care Ultrasound Supports the 2030 UN Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a low-cost, portable diagnostic modality that has rapidly evolved to meet diverse clinical needs in both high- and low-resource settings. This paper explores how POCUS aligns with and advances the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3, but also others such as SDG 4, 5, 8, 10, 11, 14, 15 and 17. title: Research progress on the mechanisms of microbial degradation of antibiotics and attenuation of antibiotic resistance genes during composting
abstract: Antibiotics and their resistance genes (ARGs) commonly coexist in organic solid waste, posing significant ecological and public health risks. Composting is a crucial biological process for mitigating such composite pollution. This review elucidates the microbial mechanisms driving the simultaneous removal of antibiotics and ARGs in composting systems. Specifically, it details how parent antibiotic compounds are transformed through enzymatic degradation and co-metabolic pathways, thereby alleviating selection pressure on drug-resistant bacteria. title: Water Quality Drivers of the Trophic Status in Tasik Kemajuan: Insights from the Trophic Level Index
abstract: Eutrophication is a water quality issue that occurs because of over-enrichment of water bodies. In this study, trophic status of Tasik Kemajuan at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) was determined by Trophic Level Index (TLI) and the relationship of TLI to water quality parameters was assessed. Water samples were taken at three sampling stations weekly for 10 weeks (n = 10) and tested for chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), total phosphorus (TP), total nitrogen (TN), Secchi depth (SD), pH, temperature, and dissolved oxygen (DO). title: Potentials for Sustainable Irrigation in Humid Climate Zones: Building a Case for Sierra Leone's Climate and Ecologies
abstract: Irrigation is conventionally framed as an arid-land technology, yet the fastest relative growth in irrigated area now occurs in humid and sub-humid regions, where rainfall is abundant in total but poorly distributed within the year. This review examined the physical, agronomic, and institutional potentials for sustainable irrigation in humid climate zones and applied the resulting framework to Sierra Leone, a country receiving 1,900–4,000 mm of rainfall annually yet growing a single rain-fed crop on most of its farmland. title: GEOSTATISTICAL EVALUATION AND SPATIAL MAPPING OF STRUCTURAL SOIL FERTILITY IN WUKARI URBAN AREA, TARABA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study evaluates the multivariate and spatial structure of soil fertility in the Wukari urban area, Nigeria, using an integrated geostatistical framework. Seventy soil samples were analyzed for exchangeable bases, organic matter, macronutrients, and salinity indicators. Principal component analysis revealed that the first component (31.6% of total variance) was strongly dominated by exchangeable Ca (0.903), effective cation exchange capacity (0.901), and total exchangeable bases (0.891), forming the basis of a PCA-derived Soil Fertility Index. title: General and professional Electrical Engineering (EE) courses as predictors of success in the licensure examination
abstract: This study investigated the academic performance, core subject competencies, and licensure examination outcomes of Engineering students at an Autonomous University in Central Luzon to determine key predictors of professional success. Using a descriptive-causal design, academic records of recent graduates (N = 4) across General Mathematics, Engineering Sciences and Allied Subjects, and Professional Subjects were evaluated against their outcomes in the Registered Electrical Engineer Licensure Examination (REELE). title: From conventional to digital: the transformation of Quranic learning in Islamic Universities
abstract: The development of information technology has significantly transformed Quranic learning in Islamic universities, shifting conventional face-to-face talaqqi and musyafahah methods into digital models utilizing various online media. This study aims to describe the transformation of Qur’an learning from conventional to digital formats, analyze the role of virtual teachers in this process, and examine its implications for learning quality and spiritual values in Islamic higher education. title: A Stochastic Model of Generative AI’s Impact on Online Information Quality
abstract: The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI (GAI) is fundamentally reshaping online information retrieval and processing, offering great potential but at the same time raising serious concerns about content authenticity and reliability. This paper introduces a novel quantitative approach to analyze the complex information dynamics emerging from the increased use of GAI tools. title: Environmental suitability and high-risk hotspots of Leptospira spp. in southern Chile
abstract: BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease caused by bacteria of the genus Leptospira, widely distributed and of high importance to both public and animal health. In Chile, available studies have mostly focused on pathogen detection, leaving a limited understanding of the environmental factors that determine its distribution. Ecological niche modeling offers a powerful approach to address this gap by identifying the environmental conditions associated with pathogen presence. title: Bipolar Photodetectors: From Mechanisms and Regulation Strategies to Advanced Applications
abstract: Bipolar photodetectors (BPDs) have emerged as promising multifunctional optoelectronic devices because they can generate positive and negative photocurrents under different external stimuli. Compared with conventional unipolar photodetectors, BPDs provide an additional signal dimension through photocurrent polarity, enabling enhanced information encoding, reconfigurable operation, and compact device integration. title: Quantifying the individual and synergistic effects of climate and land-use change on hydrology and sediment using SWAT+ : an ANOVA-based multiscenario analysis across contrasting anthropogenic settings
abstract: Tropical headwater watersheds are sensitive to hydrological and sediment changes associated with climate variability and anthropogenic land transformation. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of climate variability and land-use change on hydrological and sediment responses in two contrasting tropical headwater watersheds of the Western Ghats, India, using an integrated Random Forest–SWAT+ –analysis of variance framework. title: Remote sensing reveals spatially uneven vegetation trends and seasonal rainfall associations in Somaliland from 2000 to 2022
abstract: Dryland vegetation in Somaliland is highly sensitive to rainfall variability, warming, and recurrent drought, yet Somaliland-wide evidence on MODIS-era vegetation–climate relationships remain limited. title: Contour Based Ecological Landscape Restoration in the Torhasan Pond Micro Watershed
abstract: Global climate change and land-use alterations induce hydro-ecological challenges such as increased surface runoff and soil erosion at the watershed scale. This study proposes a contour-based ecological restoration model centered on nature-based solutions for the Torhasan Pond micro-watershed in Çanakkale, Türkiye. Micro-topographic adjustments, vegetative buffer strips, and bioswales were integrated within a holistic landscape framework. title: Spatio-temporal occurrence of small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex, Nepal
abstract: Small carnivores are generally more adaptable to human-dominated landscapes compared with large carnivores, but have received comparatively limited attention. We evaluated the single-season multi-species occupancy and temporal overlap of five small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex (BRC) of Madhesh Province, Nepal using camera-trap surveys during January to February 2023. abstract: Laundering synthetic textiles is a major pathway for microplastic fiber (MPF) release, yet the fabric-level structural and mechanical factors controlling shedding remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated MPF release from eight woven continuous-filament synthetic fabrics, including virgin polyester (PET), recycled polyester (rPET), polyamide (PA), PA/PET, and PA/elastane fabrics with plain, twill, and satin constructions. abstract: Salinity, drought, and heat severely constrain microbial activity in arid soils. This study investigated whether multi-stress tolerance in Bacillus isolated from the rhizosphere of Suaeda vera is associated with a genomic complement of stress-response and plant growth-promoting genes. We isolated 150 bacterial isolates from this rhizosphere soil at saline sites (16–32 dS/m) of Sehb El Mesjoune, central Morocco. These inconsistencies can change screening decisions and can make flexible cross-database corrections fail after transfer. abstract: This study examines the global development of research on integrating ecoliteracy into reading comprehension using a bibliometric approach. It focuses on publication trends, key contributors, influential documents, and thematic structures. Data were retrieved from the Scopus database on March 8, 2026, using a structured search query applied to titles, abstracts, and keywords. abstract: This research investigates the Iraqi Ministry of Oil's efficiency in maximizing gas oil (diesel) production to meet local demand and reduce costly imports. abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aims to summarize the current state of research and global trends in clinical trials related to atherosclerosis through bibliometric analysis. abstract: Cultural heritage assets are exposed to diverse environmental, structural, geological, biological, and anthropogenic threats, yet IoT monitoring strategies remain largely site-specific. This study presents and evaluates the ARGUS framework, a threat-oriented methodology that defines monitoring requirements according to deterioration mechanisms rather than monument typology. abstract: Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro-LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact-mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. abstract: The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. The State of Wildfires project systematically tracks global and regional fire activity, analyses the causes of prominent extreme wildfire events for three focal regions, and projects the likelihood of similar events under future climate scenarios. title: Lifecycle assessment of solar panel integration in residential buildings using electronic monitoring systems
abstract: The proliferation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in residential buildings across sub-Saharan Africa has intensified scholarly interest in their lifecycle environmental performance, particularly in regions characterized by acute electricity deficits. This study conducts a comprehensive lifecycle assessment (LCA) of solar panel integration in residential buildings in South East Nigeria, employing an electronic monitoring framework comprising IoT-enabled sensors, microcontrollers, and cloud-based data platforms to enhance data acquisition precision and lifecycle performance evaluation. abstract: The relationship between formal constitutional recognition and effective implementation remains contested and empirically underexplored, particularly in post-communist legal systems and EU candidate states. While existing comparative environmental law scholarship addresses either single jurisdictions or broad regional surveys, the specific normative-institutional comparison between Albania and Italy two Adriatic neighbours at different stages of EU integration remains unexplored. abstract: Chloride-containing fertilizers, especially those used as accompanying components in nitrogen fertilizers, are widely applied into the soil for agricultural production. abstract: Landslides are a recurrent and increasingly consequential hazard across the Himalaya, where steep terrain, tectonically weakened lithologies, climatic variability, and expanding anthropogenic activity interact to destabilize slopes. title: Characterising the occurrence of monomodal and multimodal ice hydrometeor populations and their fall speeds in midlatitude frontal ice clouds using radar Doppler spectra
abstract: Multimodality in vertically pointing radar Doppler spectra is frequently observed in stratiform clouds, but understanding the microphysical processes causing these signatures, and indeed quantifying their occurrence, remains a challenge. In this study, we utilise Ka-band radar Doppler spectra from 23 deep stratiform clouds observed over Chilbolton, UK. abstract: Purpose of the study: The study aims to (a) identify the impacts of climate change on agricultural production patterns and assess food security in Banggai Regency, and (b) map areas that are vulnerable to climate change based on the regional vulnerability index. abstract: The extent of cyclone damage to crops depends on their condition at landfall and their subsequent recovery. We assessed jute damage and production losses after Cyclone Amphan in 2020 across eight districts of West Bengal, India, using Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 reflectance, crop reference observations and district productivity data. abstract: Accurate, non-destructive diagnosis of crop growth and nitrogen (N) status is important for improving fertilizer management in transplanted rice (TPR) and dry direct-seeded rice (DDSR). abstract: Blue-green spaces (BGSs) are key material carriers for regional ecological resilience under accelerating climate change. abstract: Approximately 40 % of the European Alps consist of karstifiable rock. abstract: Integrated farming systems (IFS) improve resource recycling, livelihood diversification, and climate resilience. abstract: Sustainability indicator systems tell the managers of cultural tourism destinations what to measure, but not what to say, to whom, or through which channel. This study addresses that gap by linking the UNWTO sustainability indicator framework to Integrated Marketing Communication (IMC) theory and applying the combined lens to 74 documented case-indicator observations of sustainability communication in cultural heritage tourism, drawn from more than 30 countries across five world regions. title: Fault-tolerant control on three-tank system using fuzzy brain emotional learning controller
abstract: In this paper, the proposed a fuzzy brain emotional learning controller (FBELC) network is presented as a method for fault-tolerant control. The FBELC network approximates the unknown fault-induced dynamics and system uncertainties. Fault-tolerant control is considered for nonlinear systems subject to a single incipient fault, a single abrupt fault, and the simultaneous occurrence of incipient and abrupt faults. title: Beyond canopy cover: UAV-LiDAR reveals three-dimensional structural divergence and parsimonious candidate diagnostic traits for mangrove monitoring
abstract: Canopy cover is widely used in mangrove monitoring, yet its ability to represent three-dimensional (3D) community structure has rarely been quantified. We used UAV-LiDAR to survey 38 10 × 10 m plots across embanked (BW), tidal-creek (TC), and tidal-flat (TF) habitats on Jinniu Island, China, with TC and TF further pooled as tidally connected habitats (TCH). title: Autonomous Collision Avoidance for eVTOL in Air-Ground Coordination Based on Rule-Constrained Dynamic Velocity Obstacle
abstract: Autonomous collision avoidance for electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft in structured urban low-altitude airspace must satisfy both physical collision-prevention requirements and operational rules. This study proposes a rule-constrained dynamic velocity vector optimization (RC-DVVO) framework. First, urban low-altitude operational rules, including no-fly zones, flight corridors, altitude layers, and speed limits, are decomposed and mapped into a time-varying rule-feasible domain in velocity space. title: Synergistic Molecular Interfacial Bridging and Solvation Structure Regulation for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are hailed as promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost and environmental compatibility. However, their practical deployment is severely hindered by notorious dendrite growth and side reactions, which degrade the plating/stripping reversibility and cycling life. title: The acoustic environment is structured more by place and fine particulate matter more by time across Rhode Island communities
abstract: Environmental comfort in cities is shaped by several exposures at once, yet noise and air pollution are often combined into a single index of environmental quality. We measured the acoustic environment, fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and nighttime illuminance at 144 sites across eight Rhode Island municipalities, sampling each in four day and night session types over 39 measurement days (531 site-sessions). title: Latest Oligocene amphibians from Coderet (France)
abstract: The French locality of Coderet (latest Oligocene, MP30) yielded an astonishing number of amphibian fossil remains. The studied amphibian assemblage from Coderet consists of 8,639 skeletal remains referred to 10 taxa, making it a hot spot for diversity during the Palaeogene. Urodeles are the dominant group, almost 99% of the fossils, represented by the family Salamandridae, including both subfamilies Salamandrinae and Pleurodelinae. title: Mountain carbon budgets miss cryosphere hazard events
abstract: Warming is destabilizing the mountain cryosphere and triggering more frequent hazard events. These hazards mobilize large stores of carbon as well as rock, ice and water. Yet mountain carbon budgets largely overlook this flux, because routine monitoring rarely operates at the time, location and resolution that hazard events demand. We argue that cryosphere hazards should be treated as carbon events and set out how to close the gap. title: Rice-fish symbiosis farmed mode enhances muscle quality of yellow catfish (Pelteobagrus fulvidraco): integrated analysis from the microbiome and metabolome data
abstract: The rice-fish symbiosis is an ecological aquaculture model, which can improve aquatic product quality and farming sustainability. To clarify the effects of rice-fish symbiosis farmed mode (RFFM) on flesh quality, muscle nutritional composition, intestinal microbiota composition and hepatic metabolic profiles of yellow catfish ( Pelteobagrus fulvidraco ), this study compared the muscle nutritional composition, intestinal microbial community and hepatic metabolic phenotype of yellow catfish between rice-fish symbiosis farmed mode (RY) and traditional pond culture system (TY). title: Spatiotemporal evolution and restoration pathways of ecological environmental quality in the Haba River Basin: Spatial associations with climate and human activities
abstract: Assessing ecological environmental quality (EEQ) and its spatial associations with climatic and socioeconomic factors can inform restoration planning in arid river basins. This study integrated the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI), Sen trend analysis, the Mann–Kendall test, and the Optimal Parameters Geographical Detector (OPGD) model to evaluate EEQ dynamics and associated explanatory factors in the Haba River Basin from 2000 to 2022. title: Millimeter‐Scale Single‐Layer RGB Achromatic Metalens via Time‐Simultaneity‐Free Design
abstract: Compact and high‐performance optical components are essential for miniaturizing next‐generation imaging and display systems. While metalenses offer a promising ultrathin alternative to refractive optics, scaling up achromatic metalenses is fundamentally hindered by the trade‐off between aperture size and operational bandwidth. title: Spatial-sensory indicators and sense of presence in virtual reality tourism: evidence from landmark spaces
abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) is becoming a popular way to visit famous places without traveling. However, the specific spatial-sensory qualities that contribute to a user's sense of presence in VR landmark environments are still not well understood. Purpose This study examines six spatial-sensory design indicators derived from the Aesthetic Emotions Scale (AESTHEMOS) and investigates their relationship with users' self-reported sense of presence across six VR landmark environments. title: Beyond membranes: the multifaceted mechanisms of antimicrobial peptides
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides are emerging as critical alternatives to conventional antibiotics, particularly in the fight against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp . While antimicrobial peptides are traditionally known for their membrane-disruptive properties, increasing evidence reveals a broader spectrum of intracellular and molecular actions that remain underexplored. title: Rendezvous optimization method for addressing long-job burst problem in industrial internet of things
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) cells suffer long-job bursts when arrival surges and interdependent tasks push jobs past their time limit. This article presents ROM-RS, a Rendezvous Optimization Method with rule-based Recommendation Scheduling for adaptive task scheduling and resource reallocation. abstract: Currently, the mobile communication system is steadily progressing from the 5G commercial stage to the 6G technology verification stage. The integrated sensing and communication technology, which deeply merges communication transmission with environmental perception, will redefine the service boundaries of the next-generation wireless network. title: The Reuse of High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Plastic Wastes and their Usage with Cerium Dioxide (CeO2) as New Polymer Nanocomposites
abstract: A high density polyethylene (HDPE) plastic was reused and it was used together with cerium dioxide (CeO2) to photodegrade the Roxarsone (ROX, 4-hydroxy-3-nitrophenylarsonic acid). title: The missing Nobels: Mapping the landscape of prestigious scientific prizes
abstract: Prestigious recognition prizes, like the Nobel Prizes, can shape scientists' career decisions and how science is seen. Yet the landscape of such prizes is not well understood. We screen roughly 2,700 international scientific prizes and rank the 99 most prestigious using a novel prestige index. Recognition is unevenly distributed across fields: physics, life sciences, and mathematics are heavily recognized relative to field size, while computer science, engineering, psychology, and the social sciences are under-served. Only three of the 99 prizes target early-career scientists.

title: Spillover effect between oil prices, climate risks, and carbon prices in China: dynamic effects and key drivers
abstract: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and volatile international oil markets, the interdependence among energy prices, climate-risk information, and carbon markets has become increasingly prominent. Clarifying their dynamic spillover patterns is important for climate governance, energy security, and carbon-market risk management. title: When Waste Accumulates: Exploring Community Environmental Awareness amid Limited Waste Disposal Facilities
abstract: Waste accumulation presents an environmental challenge that cannot be understood solely through individual disposal behavior, particularly where waste disposal facilities are limited. This study aims to explore community environmental awareness amid limited waste disposal facilities in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, focusing on how residents understand waste accumulation, perceive environmental responsibility, and respond to infrastructural constraints in their everyday lives. title: Green toads at the Roof of Asia: new distributional and mitochondrial DNA sequence data for the genus Bufotes (Anura, Bufonidae) from the Pamir and adjacent mountain regions
abstract: The Pamir and adjacent mountain systems harbor a diverse assemblage of Eurasian green toads ( Bufotes ), including several polyploid taxa, but their distributions remain incompletely documented in this remote and topographically complex region. New distributional records of Bufotes from the Pamir of Tajikistan and the mountain regions of northern Pakistan are reported, based on field surveys conducted in 2020 and 2025. abstract: Hurricanes of increasing intensity are major disturbances in the southeastern United States, affecting working forests and forest-dependent economies. This study examines employment impacts of Hurricane Michael across the forestry supply chain, including forestry, logging, and wood products industries. title: Green Criminology and Environmental Crime in Albania: Governance Failures, Economic Impacts and EU Conditionality
abstract: Environmental crime represents an important form of environmental harm with ecological, economic, social, and governance implications. This study examines environmental crime through the theoretical lens of green criminology, with particular attention to global patterns and the Albanian context. abstract: The global rise of drug-resistant fungal pathogens, particularly non- albicans Candida species, necessitates the development of novel therapeutic strategies. title: A novel gellan gum-degrading glycoside hydrolase from the hyperthermophile Fervidibacter sacchari
abstract: Fervidibacter sacchari is an aerobic hyperthermophile within the phylum Armatimonadota that degrades various polysaccharides. Its genome encodes 117 putative glycoside hydrolases (GHs), including two assigned to GH family 50 (GH50). In this study, a multidomain GH50 enzyme, Fsa11540Gus, was expressed, purified, and functionally characterized. abstract: Arba Minch, a rapidly growing town in Ethiopia, experienced an 807% increase in built-up areas over the past 25 years. This study investigates the spatiotemporal links between LULC change, LST and NDVI across six continuous temporal framework (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025), which the bi-temporal cannot demonstrate. abstract: Despite improvements in global reporting, Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) monitoring remains constrained by persistent data gaps, structural fragmentation, and the complexity and heterogeneity of the Global Indicator Framework. These challenges highlight the need to define the desirable properties of key SDG indicators that support global comparison and cross‐goal interpretation while preserving essential SDG concepts. abstract: Hybrid nanofluids have attracted considerable attention for advanced thermal-management applications because of their enhanced heat-transfer characteristics compared with conventional single-particle nanofluids. abstract: The objective of this study was to analyze the level of awareness, use, and preference regarding the remote assistance and guidance channels implemented by the Tax Administration Service (SAT) through the Remote Taxpayer Assistance Center (CAREC), as well as to evaluate the reach of digital channels compared to in-person procedures at the Local Taxpayer Services Administration (ALSC). abstract: We use morphological and molecular data to demonstrate that Coleonyx fasciatus , as currently recognized, comprises three divergent lineages. title: Enhancing crop resilience under excess water stress: Physiological adaptations, management strategies and molecular advances
abstract: Recent climatic variability has increased the frequency of waterlogging and flooding events, posing serious threats to crop productivity and food security worldwide. Excess water stress results from prolonged soil saturation, which restricts oxygen availability in the root zone or causes partial to complete plant submergence. abstract: En los ecosistemas virtuales de aprendizaje, la gamificación se ha consolidado como un paradigma relevante para potenciar el aprendizaje. abstract: Why do some national destinations convert their endowments into high international tourist expenditures while similarly endowed destinations do not? abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) está transformando todos los sectores de la sociedad, con un crecimiento exponencial en capacidad y aplicaciones. abstract: Water held in shallow aquifers underpins domestic supply, livestock watering and small-scale irrigation across eastern Rwanda, where surface sources are seasonal and unevenly distributed. abstract: The coupling coordination degree (CCD) is widely used to summarize coordination among production, living, and ecological functions (PLEFs), but a scalar score may conceal important differences in the underlying functional system. abstract: The rapid development of financial technology has transformed the investment landscape by providing retail investors with convenient access to digital investment platforms. Mobile applications, online brokerage services, and digital mutual fund platforms have simplified investment activities by reducing transaction costs, improving accessibility, and providing real-time financial information. abstract: Generative AI now writes Computer-Aided Design (CAD) programs and boundary representations; however, the output that executes or resembles a target need not be dimensionally correct, constrained, or manufacturable. abstract: Agricultural and agro-industrial residues are promising feedstocks for fuels, chemicals and materials, but their renewable origin does not guarantee lower environmental burdens. abstract: Periodontitis is a globally prevalent chronic inflammatory disease strongly associated with specific periodontal pathogens, particularly Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis), which plays a major role in disease progression. Increasing concerns regarding antibiotic resistance and the adverse effects associated with conventional antiseptics have encouraged the exploration of safe, affordable, and naturally derived antimicrobial alternatives. abstract: Ceilometers are established sensors for deriving cloud base height (CBH) from a laser backscatter signal. abstract: In Alpine catchments, extreme weather events and avalanches contribute to alterations in soil characteristics and land use conditions, thereby affecting hillslope stability and increasing erosion‐prone areas. The effects of major natural hazards on land use land cover (LULC) changes and erosion susceptibility remain poorly understood in steep mountainous areas. abstract: Accurate estimation of basement depth is significant in the energy resource exploration and mineral prospecting. Basement depth is inherently controlled by a combination of sedimentation, tectonic subsidence, and geological processes that collectively shape the subsurface architecture. abstract: El crecimiento de la producción científica en educación ha propiciado un aumento significativo de estudios de síntesis, como revisiones sistemáticas, revisiones de alcance y metaanálisis. Este contexto ha generado la necesidad de desarrollar enfoques de síntesis de segundo nivel que permitan integrar la evidencia derivada de estos estudios. En este sentido, las meta-revisiones constituyen una herramienta para analizar de manera global la literatura disponible. abstract: Ecosystem engineers, such as beavers, facilitate other species' survival and growth through habitat modification.Beaver conservation and mimicry is rapidly growing as a restoration tool, but the ability of beaver dams to facilitate other species is poorly understood in many systems.Further, it is unknown if beaver dams uniquely benefit some functional groups (i.e., species with similar traits) more than others.We therefore sought to determine if the richness and abundance of prairie fishes and fish functional groups increased with the construction of beaver dams.We also examined whether functi

abstract: proMGE is a resource of prokaryotic mobile genetic elements (MGEs) that systematically catalogues MGEs from prokaryotes, their intercellular spread, antimicrobial resistance gene carriage, and MGE nesting interactions. abstract: Air pollution can contribute to skin dryness and oxidative damage, highlighting the potential benefits of topical antioxidant formulations. White nusa indah (Mussaenda philippica A. abstract: Objective To establish a multi-tube singleplex qPCR assay for detecting the Corynebacterium kroppenstedtii complex (CKC), the genus Corynebacterium , and other bacteria in pus specimens from patients with granulomatous mastitis (GM). This study develops a scenario-based decision-support framework that links throughput and rail-share assumptions to occupation- and region-specific workforce requirements and a policy-constrained mixed-integer linear programming model. abstract: Alternative oxidase (AOX) is a mitochondrial terminal oxidase that provides an alternative route for electron transfer, contributing to respiratory flexibility and redox homeostasis under stress conditions. In trypanosomatids, AOX displays a highly uneven distribution associated with extensive diversification of mitochondrial electron transport chains (ETCs). abstract: Background Pithecellobium clypearia (PC) is a traditional Chinese medicine with anti-inflammatory effects. However, the preventive efficacy and underlying mechanisms of PC in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain unclear. Objective This study applied an integrated microbiome-metabolomic approach to investigate PC’s pharmacological mechanisms against UC. abstract: Green synthesis of AgNPs by using the extracts from plants is one way of making silver nanoparticles that could be used as an alternative to traditional methods. abstract: A high-precision, non-contact measurement method for ruby balls is proposed by integrating annular dark-field imaging with multi-scale adaptive edge detection. Multi-scale gradient-response fusion and entropy-guided local thresholding are used to improve outer-contour extraction under non-uniform contrast and noise. title: Fluent but Unfounded: A Review of Hallucination in Small Language Models
abstract: Small language models (SLMs), compact generative models ranging from a few hundred million to roughly ten billion parameters, are increasingly chosen for on-device, private and cost-sensitive deployments. Their tendency to produce fluent but unsupported statements is nevertheless rarely treated as a distinct engineering problem. abstract: Efficient soil water movement is essential for improving crop water-use efficiency under drip irrigation, yet the role of Soil Quality Index (SQI) in predicting wetting-front under surface drip irrigation has not been comprehensively studied. This study investigated five land-use systems—bare fallowing for 2 years (BF2), bare fallowing for 3 years (BF3), monocropping (MOC), crop rotation (CR), and fallowing with vegetation (FV)—on soil quality and wetting-front development under surface drip irrigation. abstract: Biomonitoring surveys of Flemish and French rivers revealed two Nitzschia species from the section Lanceolatae that could not be identified with the relevant literature. Examination by light and scanning electron microscopy and comparison with original (type) material of similar species in the Nitzschia frustulum complex ( N. frustulum , N. bulnheimiana , N. costei , N. liebetruthii , and N. fonticola ) justify their description herein as Nitzschia parafrustulum sp. nov . and Nitzschia pseudoeutinensis sp. nov ., respectively. title: Measuring What Matters: Sustainable Performance Indicators and STI’s Role in Achieving the SDGs
abstract: This study examines the pivotal role of Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) organizations in advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and proposes a structured framework to assess their contributions through Sustainable Performance Indicators (SPIs). STI organizations are key enablers of progress in areas such as clean energy, healthcare, education, and climate resilience; however, existing measurement systems often overlook their broader societal and environmental impacts. abstract: The authors (Hill, Harvard Business School professor); Wild (partner at Paradox Strategies), and Tedards (PhD student in organizational behavior at Harvard Business School) contend that today's leaders must be wayfinders, as opposed to pathfinders. title: Degradation problems in energy conversion materials and devices: Efficiency-durability trade-off, interfacial instability, and mitigation strategies
abstract: The transition toward carbon-neutral, sustainable energy systems has intensified the demand for highly durable, efficient energy-conversion materials and devices. However, their practical use is constrained by degradation processes that simultaneously degrade their durability and efficiency. This article provides a critical and comprehensive overview of degradation pathways across diverse energy conversion technologies, including fuel cells, photovoltaics, electrolyzers, photothermal systems, and thermoelectric systems. abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) comfort sessions are increasingly used in residential dementia care, but environment selection remains ad hoc—staff have no systematic way to identify which virtual experience best suits a given resident. abstract: In groundgen airborne wind energy systems that utilise conventional feedback control architecture, the pumping cycle power is largely influenced by four controller set points: reel-out radius, reel-out distance, reel-out winch speed, and reel-in winch speed. abstract: Introduction This study examines the associations between perceived social risk and the tendency toward sports gambling addiction among recreational sports club members in China, with particular attention to the potential indirect role of sports values. abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency's property acquisition ("buyout") program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. abstract: The analysis of stable isotopes has emerged as a pivotal method in paleodietary reconstruction. However, existing methodologies for isotopic data analysis often rely on manual processes that are particularly time-consuming. To address this, we developed SALEM, a standalone, user-friendly application designed to streamline isotopic data processing. abstract: Background The escalating prevalence of resistant bacterial strains, including MDR, XDR, and PDR, poses a major threat to public health. Klebsiella pneumoniae is of primary concern, identified by WHO as a critical priority pathogen in hospital-acquired infections. Therapeutic options were relegated to last-resort antibiotics like colistin, limited by its nephrotoxicity, and tigecycline, which now faces emerging bacterial resistance, raising the need for different treatment options. abstract: Beacon towers were warning and communication nodes in the Ming Great Wall defense system. We developed an interpretable graph learning framework combining a graph attention network (GAT) with random forest (RF) for Yansui Garrison. abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a highly toxic heavy metal with no known biological function in humans. Natural processes and anthropogenic activities release cadmium into air, water, and soil, leading to persistent environmental contamination and increasing the risk of human exposure. Owing to its high bioavailability, long biological half-life, and slow excretion, cadmium progressively accumulates in multiple organs and is associated with a wide range of adverse health outcomes. abstract: The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. abstract: The treatment of highly toxic and refractory phenolic wastewater remains challenging because conventional biological processes can be strongly inhibited at high pollutant concentrations. abstract: The existing lightning risk assessment methods for distribution lines are usually based on lightning monitoring statistical data, and consider terrain conditions and key lightning resistance parameters as quasi-static variables. abstract: Moving persistent extreme precipitation events (PEPEs) can cause severe disasters along their tracks. However, a PEPE typically consists of multiple rain cells that evolve and move differently from one another, rendering the conventional single-center tracking method incapable of capturing their respective characteristics. abstract: Against the backdrop of digital-intelligent integration driving the digital transformation of science popularization, Zhejiang Province leverages its advantages in digital reform to advance the construction of a science popularization communication system from four dimensions: institution, platform, content and collaboration, which has effectively improved citizens’ scientific literacy. abstract: The steering precision and reliability of steer-by-wire (SbW) technologies that replace mechanical linkages with electronic systems can only be improved by the efficient controllers that can deal with the disturbances, uncertainties, and non-linear vehicle behavior of the system. abstract: Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. abstract: Building facade materials are closely associated with urban microclimates, energy consumption, and carbon emissions, yet existing urban building datasets typically capture only building footprints and heights, leaving semantic material information unavailable at the individual-building level. abstract: Underground foundations are essential to the safety of dense urban infrastructure, yet their deterioration and soil–structure interactions are difficult to observe once construction is complete. abstract: Climate change challenges the conservation of island-endemic plants by altering environmental suitability within geographically restricted landscapes. In the Balearic Islands, ecological research has informed the management of endemic flora, and modelling studies offer complementary information about present and future environmental suitability. abstract: Dorsal-ventral (D-V) patterning of the neural tube is essential for neuronal subtype generation during neurodevelopment. abstract: La educación en salud sexual y reproductiva desempeña un papel fundamental en la prevención de infecciones de transmisión sexual y embarazos precoces entre los adolescentes, y la tecnología digital ofrece nuevas vías para la promoción de la salud. abstract: The convergence of the circular economy (CE) and advanced digital technologies has given rise to several overlapping concepts, including Smart Circular Economy (SCE). title: Sustainability by Design in Big Science
abstract: Public investment in Big Science and large-scale research infrastructures increasingly depends on their demonstrated long-term sustainability and societal value. This article argues that sustainability should not be treated as an external constraint imposed on scientific missions, but as a property that can be embedded by design. abstract: Grief is an experience familiar to everyone, given that the core circumstance is loss, and life without loss is as probable as life without energy. abstract: Stable isotope analysis of human bone collagen from Vilnius shows an increase in δ 15 N values from 1500 AD. abstract: Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) offers a pathway to large-scale temporal decoupling of intermittent generation and demand. title: Techno-economic optimization of a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system with an EV charging station at a university campus
abstract: The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in developing economies, combined with the growing imperative to decarbonize campus energy systems, necessitates novel planning frameworks that reconcile grid-interactive microgrid design with probabilistic economic validation. This study presents a techno-economic planning framework for a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) co-designed with an EV charging station at university campus​. title: Advancements in Solar Drying Technology: Enhancing Food Preservation and Solar Power Systems for Sustainable Solutions
abstract: Global food insecurity and escalating postharvest losses, which affect nearly one‐third of total food production, necessitate sustainable preservation technologies aligned with the Food and Agriculture Organization targets and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Solar drying has emerged as an energy‐efficient and environmentally benign alternative to conventional fossil‐fuel‐based dehydration methods. institutions: Vignan's Foundation for Science, Technology & Research

title: Accurate identification of medically important Aedes mosquito species using low-cost imaging and geometric wing morphometrics
abstract: Accurate species identification is crucial to assess the medical and veterinary relevance of a mosquito specimen, but it requires high taxonomic expertise of the respective organism group and well-equipped laboratories. This study aimed to evaluate whether low-cost imaging in combination with geometric wing morphometrics can provide accurate identification of invasive, morphologically similar Aedes species. title: Practical Reflections on Media Communication Empowering Communicative Exchange in Media Marketing
abstract: How to convert communication resources into operating benefits is a problem that needs to be solved in the process of media convergence. Based on the market research industry survey data of CTR, and combined with practical cases from institutions such as China National Radio Media Group, China Central Television, Jiaxiang County Media Convergence Center, this paper studies the specific paths through which media communication promotes media marketing. abstract: This study examines the stabilizing effects of surface-active ionic liquids (SAILs), namely (2-hydroxyethyl)ammonium oleate [2-HEA][Ole], bis(2-hydroxyethyl)ammonium oleate [BHEA][Ole], and tris(2-hydroxyethyl)ammonium oleate [THEA][Ole], on the stability of ZrO 2 by analyzing excess molar volume ( $$V_{m}^{E}$$ ), viscosity ( η ), density ( ρ ), dynamic light scattering, zeta potential, UV-Vis spectroscopy, surface tension, COSMO results, and visual observations over 60 days. title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. title: Experimental Modeling of Blood Loss and Hemorrhagic Shock: Past Achievements, Current Recommendations, and Future Challenges (Review)
abstract: Acute massive blood loss and hemorrhagic shock in severe trauma remain the leading causes of preventable mortality. Despite the impactfull significance of clinical studies, experimental modeling in laboratory animals remains an indispensable for fundamental studies on the pathophysiology of trauma and hemorrhagic shock, as well as for the initial assessment of the efficacy and safety of therapeutic interventions. title: A one-pot asymmetric ERA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay for visual detection of white spot syndrome virus in shrimp
abstract: Introduction White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) threatens shrimp aquaculture. PCR is sensitive but laboratory dependent. Isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a offers an alternative, but one-pot integration is limited by competition between double-stranded amplicons and crRNA for Cas12a. Methods A one-pot assay (OAERA-Cas12a) integrating asymmetric enzymatic recombinase amplification (aERA) with CRISPR/Cas12a was developed. Key parameters were optimized. title: Small Diameter and Decreased Radial Growth Control Pinus palustris Tropical Cyclone Damage in Georgia, USA
abstract: Traditional correlative analyses often struggle to parse the confounding drivers of storm damage in forested systems. To address this limitation, this study utilized a causal inference framework to separate broad observational trends from underlying biological mechanisms. We applied a non-parametric causal forest algorithm to evaluate how diameter at breast height (DBH) and DBH growth rates influenced tree-level damage probabilities in even-aged longleaf pine ( Pinus palustris Mill.) plantations following Hurricane Helene (2024). title: Beyond connectivity: Ecological corridors as socio-ecological governance arrangements
abstract: Ecological corridors are among the most adopted environmental policies to address habitat fragmentation and biodiversity loss, yet the research supporting them is uneven. Spatial and biophysical questions dominate, while the governance, organizational, and distributive processes that determine whether corridors work in practice remain underexplored. Drawing on a social-ecological systems lens, we systematically review 1871 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2025, coded across six analytical dimensions. Two asymmetries stand out. title: Smarter, safer, better: AI upgrades improve the conservation potential of Felixer grooming traps
abstract: Feral cats ( Felis catus ) are among the most damaging predators of native fauna in Australasia and on islands worldwide. Felixer grooming traps automate their control by depositing toxic gel on a passing cat's flank, which the cat ingests through grooming. The Felixer must distinguish feral cats from non-target wildlife and spray the gel within a sub-second window. Here, we tested the gains and limitations of a low-power, greyscale edge-AI vision system across successive upgrades in field-deployed Felixers. title: Spatial and seasonal distribution patterns of wild shrub vegetation along abiotic gradients in Jhelum District, Punjab, Pakistan
abstract: The spatial (habitat-based) and seasonal (phenological) distribution patterns of wild shrub vegetation in Jhelum District, Punjab, Pakistan, are significantly influenced by various abiotic factors. This study aimed to investigate the taxonomic richness, distribution patterns of shrubs in relation to habitat characteristics and environmental gradients in the Jhelum district. Field surveys were conducted from 2019 to 2021 using 120 randomly established transects, and vegetation data were analyzed using classification and ordination approaches. The study area was found to have 28 species of shrub

title: Modelo pedagógico mediado por inteligencia artificial generativa para promover el pensamiento crítico y el aprendizaje significativo en educación media colombiana
abstract: La incorporación de inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación media plantea una tensión entre su potencial de apoyo y el riesgo de sustituir procesos cognitivos esenciales. El objetivo de este estudio fue diseñar un modelo pedagógico mediado por inteligencia artificial generativa que promueva pensamiento crítico y aprendizaje significativo en estudiantes de educación media colombiana, bajo una perspectiva humanocéntrica de Sociedad 5.0. title: Sustainable valorization of tomato grouper Cephalopholis sonnerati skin waste into chrome free leather
abstract: The present study aimed to upcycle tomato grouper ( Cephalopholis sonnerati ) skin waste into high performance leather through a chrome free tanning process. For this purpose, the raw skins of the fish were pretreated with a controlled mild alkaline system of CaCO₃ and NaOH to remove the non-collagenous matrices without affecting the native fiber network. In C. sonnerati skin, the collagen content obtained was 37.31 ± 1.39%. title: Structure-enhanced Benders decomposition for the multi-fleet feeder vehicle routing problem
abstract: : The multi-fleet feeder vehicle routing problem (MFFVRP) coordinates trucks and motorbikes through synchronized replenishment at designated joint nodes, allowing motorbikes to replenish their supplies without returning to the depot. These synchronization requirements complicate the associated mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model and may cause classical Benders decomposition (BD) to explore routing configurations that cannot be extended to feasible synchronized solutions. title: Global Challenges, Local Meaning: Methods and Lessons from a Global Public Health Partnership Measuring the Interplay of Built and Food Environments with Climate Hazards in African Cities
abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are increasing on the African continent, where rapid urbanization, built environments not conducive to healthy diets or active living, and climate-related stressors co-occur as "syndemic hazards" that may interact to amplify NCD risk. We detail the novel concepts and methods employed to quantify these syndemic hazards, co-designed through a global public health partnership of academics collaborating closely with stakeholders in four African cities: Cape Town and Soweto (South Africa), Lagos (Nigeria), and Yaoundé (Cameroon).
