title: Single-isolate resequencing expands the Rhizoctonia solani IBRS16 virome and completes multiple viral genomes hidden in pooled analyses
abstract: High-throughput sequencing has greatly advanced fungal virome exploration, yet pooled analyses can hinder complete genome reconstruction in the case of low abundance viruses. Here, a single isolate of Rhizoctonia solani from a Brazilian collection associated with patch disease on Zoysia japonica was re-analysed independently using Illumina sequencing to refine and expand its virome characterization. title: Detection of IFN-related molecules in early development and transcriptional responses to oral IFNα-expressing yeast in juvenile pearl gentian grouper
abstract: Introduction The interferon (IFN) system is central to antiviral defense in vertebrates, yet its ontogeny and regulation during early development remain poorly characterized in commercially important hybrid groupers. This study investigated the expression dynamics of IFN-related genes and proteins during early developmental stages of pearl gentian grouper ( Epinephelus fuscoguttatus ♀ × E. lanceolatus ♂) and explored the feasibility of oral delivery of IFNα using a recombinant Saccharomyces cerevisiae expression system. title: Three-dimensional CFD simulation of urban drainage confluence flows using a validated Reynolds Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) k-ε turbulence model
abstract: Urban drainage confluences exhibit complex flow dynamics that can induce hydrodynamic instabilities, sediment deposition and localised flooding. In this research, a validated 3D Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) k-ε turbulence model was developed and applied to investigate the influence of change in confluence angle and discharge ratio on flow conditions at an existing urban drainage confluence with a multi-cell box culvert. title: Demography and spatial dynamics of Lycaena helle ([Denis & Schiffermüller], 1775) in an alpine bog: population structure, movement, and environmental drivers (Lepidoptera, Lycaenidae)
abstract: During a study in 2025, our results indicated a large population of Lycaena helle ([Denis & Schiffermüller], 1775) in the study area, an alpine bog, characterized by a male-skewed sex ratio and high survival rates. Individual movements, mostly less than 50 m long, indicate a low connectivity between the three local population cores. title: Phenotype-driven screening reveals a causal role for the cortex in pupil control
abstract: Phenotype-driven forward screening offers a powerful strategy to discover neuronal substrates underlying physical and behavioral traits without prior assumptions. Historically, such approaches have identified many important neuronal circuits using invertebrate model organisms, but application to mammals has remained limited by the lack of appropriate strategies. Here, we quantitatively profiled 56 neurological phenotypic features across more than 200 adult mice when neurodevelopmentally classified neurons were activated or inhibited by chemogenetics. title: Punched zinc-aluminium electrodes for efficient treatment of soap wastewater: Original scientific paper
abstract: This study investigates the efficiency of the electrocoagulation process using punched zinc and aluminium electrodes for the treatment of soap and detergent wastewater. Although the industry generates relatively small volumes of effluent during production, significant environmental concerns arise from its widespread domestic and industrial discharge. The objective was to optimize key operational parameters for maximum chemical oxygen demand (COD) and turbidity removal. title: Developing a Rigid Pavement Performance Prediction Model for Enhancing Maintenance Management of District Roads: A Case of Ubungo District, Tanzania
abstract: Rigid (concrete) pavements built on district roads in Dar es Salaam under the Dar es Salaam Metropolitan Development Project are maintained by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA), which has no locally calibrated tool for predicting their condition. This study developed and validated a performance prediction model for rigid pavements in Ubungo District. A questionnaire survey of 86 practitioners from TARURA, the City Council, contractors and consultants rated twelve technical factors on a five-point scale, and the factors were ranked with the Relative Importance Index (RII). title: Driving sustainable Nora cultural tourism with the BCG economic model: The role of key factors and integration
abstract: This study investigates tourism behavior and patterns, analyzes the causalrelationships of the local economy, and develops a causal relationshipmodel of Nora indigenous cultural tourism in Phatthalung Province,Thailand. title: Digital preservation of multispecies heart morphology using smartphone LiDAR-assisted photogrammetry
abstract: Introduction Fresh biological specimens represent the most realistic material for anatomical study. However, fresh organs are difficult to digitize due to their deformability, moist reflective surfaces, and rapid post-mortem deterioration. These limitations are particularly relevant for the heart, an anatomically complex organ whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture and species-specific variations are challenging to document and preserve. title: Service area extension of PPP-B2b using clock bias prediction based on frequency stability and orbit age-extension
abstract: The PPP-B2b service provided by the BeiDou-3 Navigation Satellite System (BDS-3) enables high-precision real-time precise point positioning (PPP) through corrections broadcast by satellites. However, due to the regional distribution of tracking stations within the operational control system, its service area is mainly limited to the Asia-Pacific region, leading to short correction arcs and data discontinuities near and beyond the service boundary. To extend this capability beyond its nominal service area, this study proposes a service area extension strategy that combines clock bias prediction
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Lost in (green) space: first record of Syedra nigrotibialis Simon, 1884 (Araneae, Linyphiidae) in Germany and Central Europe
abstract: Syedra nigrotibialis Simon, 1884 is a charismatic species of dwarf spider (Linyphiidae) endemic to the Tyrrhenian region, previously only known from relatively few specimens. Here we present the first record of the species in Germany, far from its original range. Several specimens were found in multiple urban green spaces in the city of Stuttgart. We also provide photographs and illustrations as well as a DNA barcode for the species.

title: Succinylation in lung cancer: mechanisms, implications, and clinical perspectives
abstract: As a form of protein posttranslational modification (PTM), succinylation involves the covalent addition of a succinyl moiety to specific residues (predominantly lysine) in proteins through an amide linkage, altering protein activity, stability, and intermolecular interactions. By influencing these molecular properties, succinylation contributes substantially to the control of cellular metabolism, intracellular signaling, and transcriptional regulation. title: The Effect of Service Quality and Digitalization of Betang Mobile Banking on Customer Loyalty Through Customer Satisfaction at PT. Bank Kalteng Sub-Branch of Bahaur
abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of service quality on customer loyalty and the moderating role of banking digitalization through the Betang Mobile application at PT Bank Kalteng, Bahaur Sub-Branch. The study was motivated by increasing competition in the banking industry during the digital era and inconsistent findings from previous research regarding the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty. title: Multi-algorithm based inter-annual flood monitoring and accuracy evaluation over southern Ethiopia using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery and cloud-based APIs
abstract: Flooding along the lower Omo River threatens livelihoods, infrastructure, and ecosystems in Dasenech, southern Ethiopia. This study evaluated multiple flood-detection algorithms and characterized flood events using Sentinel-1 SAR data and Google Earth Engine. Three SAR-based flood mapping algorithms, Change Detection and Thresholding (CDAT), Normalized Difference Flood Index (NDFI), and Root of Normalized Image Difference (RNID), were comparatively evaluated to assess accuracy and temporal consistency in mapping flood extent across the central part of the district. title: A food security landscape framework for understanding energy-based decision-making in wild animals
abstract: Food limitation has long shaped understanding of animal behavior, physiology, reproduction, and population dynamics. Yet food abundance alone does not capture the energetic conditions experienced by wild animals. Resources may be inaccessible, nutritionally inadequate, unpredictable, or unreliable over time, causing individuals in the same habitat to experience very different energetic environments. title: Climate change adaptation for tourism resilience: stakeholder perceptions and critical gaps in Kilimanjaro National Park, Tanzania
abstract: Introduction Climate change poses a significant threat to tourism-dependent protected areas; however, adaptation effectiveness fundamentally hinges on stakeholder awareness, involvement, and perceived efficacy for tourism resilience. Guided by Social Exchange Theory (SET) as an interpretive lens, this study posits that community support for adaptation depends on perceived fairness, transparency, and meaningful participation. title: FAIR NMR: Acquisition, Processing, and Modeling of Time-Resolved NMR Data According to the FAIR Principles
abstract: Time-resolved NMR spectroscopy is a promising method for measuring the concentrations of reactants, intermediates, and products during a catalyzed reaction, which enables mechanistic elucidation. However, the conventional methods of data processing and incomplete metadata reporting in kinetic NMR studies currently hamper cross-laboratory validation and reuse of catalytic data. title: Advances in hazardous waste disposal technologies: Environmental impacts, treatment efficiency, and sustainable strategies
abstract: Hazardous waste generation has increased rapidly due to industrialisation, urbanisation, and technological advancement, creating significant risks to human health, ecosystems, and sustainable development. Effective hazardous waste management requires advanced treatment technologies, strong regulatory frameworks, and sustainability-focused strategies. This review evaluates current treatment and disposal methods, including physical, chemical, biological, and thermal technologies, emphasising their efficiency, environmental impacts, and sustainability. journal: South African Journal of Chemical Engineering

title: Inteligencia Artificial generativa aplicada: Creación de imágenes para la reconstrucción patrimonial especulativa
abstract: La investigación examina cómo los modelos generativos pueden contribuir a paliar vacíos de información en el estudio y la divulgación del patrimonio, no como sustitutos de la evidencia científica, sino como herramientas de exploración visual y reflexión. Se analizan los límites técnicos y conceptuales entre reconstrucción, interpretación e imaginación algorítmica, y las implicaciones epistemológicas y éticas derivadas del uso de IAG en contextos patrimoniales. Mediante casos de estudio de patrimonio escultórico, el artículo evalúa el potencial de la IAG para la formulación de hipótesis visuale
journal: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual

title: Precision oncology 2.0 in advanced colorectal cancer: resistance-state pharmacology and tumor ecosystem remodeling
abstract: Precision treatment in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) has advanced through molecularly selected therapies, but pretreatment genotyping often fails to explain resistance that emerges during therapy. The clinical benefits of targeting resistance-related signaling are evident in BRAF V600E- and KRAS G12C-mutant disease. In the phase III BREAKWATER trial, encorafenib plus cetuximab and mFOLFOX6 extended median progression-free survival from 7.1 to 12.8 months in patients with BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC. title: Potenziale für Naturschutz durch virtuelle Zäune in der Beweidung
abstract: Conservation potential through virtual fences in grazing management // Virtual fencing is an emerging technology with the potential to simplify grazing management and facilitate nature conservation measures on grazed grassland. Based on an approved field trial with cattle and artificial nests, we demonstrate that the use of virtual fences is promising for the protection of ground-nesting birds. In areas protected by virtual fences, the rate of nest trampling was significantly lower compared with unprotected areas. title: Does Breakthrough Innovation in Key Core Technologies Always Enhance Urban Economic Resilience? Evidence From Diverse Resource‐Based Cities
abstract: This study develops a dynamic framework incorporating heterogeneous innovation to examine how breakthroughs in key core technologies affect urban economic resilience in China. A constant elasticity of substitution (CES) function integrates breakthrough and incremental innovation while accounting for their dynamic accumulation and resource allocation. title: Mediating Knowledge: Scholarly Journal Editors as Gatekeepers in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping scholarly publishing, creating both opportunities for efficiency and risks to the integrity of the scholarly record. Journal editors and peer reviewers, along with the entire scholarly publishing apparatus, are navigating unprecedented challenges, including evolving authorship and use policies, the influx of low‑quality or fabricated submissions and imperfect AI detection tools. title: Trajectories of random walks on Markov sources reveal the structure of complex sequences
abstract: We highlight a hierarchical property that is found in many sequences, the property of subunit structure, in which sequence symbols are joined together in tightly knit groups to create new subunits at higher levels of organization. Many sequences have strong connections both between the subunits and within the subunits. We propose an information-theoretic method that reveals hierarchical subunit structure in sequences. title: Assessing the attentional dynamics of Responding to Joint Attention in infancy via online webcam-based eye-tracking
abstract: Responding to Joint Attention (RJA) is a foundational social-cognitive skill that unfolds through a sequence of distinct attentional processes: engagement with a social partner, orienting toward a referent, and sustained attention to a shared point of interest. Traditional assessments of joint attention often rely on aggregate behavioral scores that may not capture this fine-grained temporal structure. title: Beyond the Score: Mapping Local Human Development in Poland with Scalar and Vector-Based Indices
abstract: This study investigates local human development dynamics in Poland by applying a dual-method approach that combines the classic scalar-based Local Human Development Index (LHDI) with a novel vector-based formulation using complex numbers and visual typogram representation. Drawing оn comparative county-level data from 2010 to 2023 and employing bivariate analysis, the research captures both the magnitude of development and internal structural shifts across three core dimensions: health, education, and welfare. title: Agricultural land management practices in the conterminous United States from 1980–2023
abstract: Agricultural land management practices affect environmental variables including water quality, carbon and nitrogen cycles, and greenhouse gas emissions. To better understand agricultural land management practices, we compiled a land management history for the conterminous United States (CONUS) from 1980–2023. We used the National Resources Inventory as the basis for our sample-based approach to impute planting and harvest dates, synthetic N fertilizer and manure N and C application rates and timing, tillage systems and intensity, and cover crop adoption on major commodity croplands. title: Pollution NO2 and C6H6 Dynamics and their Implication for the Fitness-for-purpose of Air Quality Networks. A Case Study in 2005–2022 Madrid
abstract: Air quality monitoring networks are fundamental for assessing pollutant concentrations, evaluating population exposure, and supporting environmental management. Nevertheless, whether their original design remains representative under evolving pollution conditions is rarely evaluated. This study proposes an integrated framework for assessing the long-term effectiveness of air quality monitoring networks using temporal trends, spatial distribution gradients, spatial variability indicators, meteorological analyses, and health-related metrics. title: Crystal-field modulation activates dormant tetrahedral Co sites for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Water activation in the Volmer step is a major kinetic bottleneck in alkaline hydrogen evolution, yet the catalytic potential of many lattice sites remains underutilized. Here, we develop an oxalic-acid-assisted treatment to modulate the surface coordination environment of spinel Co 3 O 4 while preserving its crystalline framework. The optimized U-Co 3 O 4 -2 electrode requires an overpotential of 38 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH and sustains operation for at least 1000 h. title: Integration of Condition Index and Risk Score for Maintenance Prioritization of Educational Buildings A Component Level Case Study at Manado State Polytechnic, Indonesia
abstract: Maintenance of educational buildings is often constrained by limited budgets, incomplete condition data, and the absence of transparent maintenance prioritization procedures. This study developed and applied a maintenance prioritization model integrating the Condition Index (CI) and Risk Score (RS) to assess an operational higher education building at Manado State Polytechnic, Indonesia. A systematic visual condition assessment was conducted using 43 component-level observations across 16 rooms or zones and 12 building element categories. title: Geography education and climate change awareness among secondary school teachers and learners in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon
abstract: By integrating physical and human environmental processes, Geography education is increasingly recognised as an important vehicle for climate literacy. However, evidence on its contribution to climate change awareness and adaptation-oriented learning at school level remains limited. This study examines how Geography teachers and learners in secondary schools in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon, perceive the contribution of Geography education to climate change awareness. title: An Integrated Study of the Spatiotemporal Characteristics of the Impact of China's Digital Economy on the Upgrading of the Sports Industry
abstract: As the digital economy becomes a key driver of global economic growth, China's sports industry is currently undergoing a profound digital and intelligent transformation. Using Stata 18.0 software, this study conducts a comprehensive spatial autocorrelation analysis across 15 provincial-level regions in China from 2020 to 2024. It aims to systematically identify the complex integration patterns between the digital economy and the sports industry, providing robust empirical evidence and a solid theoretical foundation for effective policymaking. title: Circularity, scaling and co-competition in the AI industry: singularity or bubble?
abstract: A partir del lanzamiento masivo de ChatGPT-3.5 en noviembre de 2022, se configuró un ecosistema caracterizado por alianzas multimillonarias que trascienden la dinámica tradicional cliente-proveedor, estableciendo un sofisticado sistema de dependencias mutuas donde cada actor opera simultáneamente como cliente, inversor y competidor. title: Study on the Multi‐Environment Anti‐Aging Performance of Nano‐Textured PTFE – Al 2 O 3 Hybrid FKM Composites
abstract: Fluoroelastomer (FKM) is widely used in aerospace sealing but suffers from synergistic degradation caused by thermal oxidative aging, low temperature embrittlement, salt spray corrosion, and oil swelling. In this study, polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and aluminum oxide (Al 2 O 3 ) hybrid nanofillers were incorporated into the FKM matrix and surface, and tailored microstructures were engineered to fabricate a FKM/PTFE/Al 2 O 3 composite. title: GC–MS Characterization of the Ethanolic Extract of (Ceratonia siliqua L.) Fruit Pulp and Evaluation of Its Antibacterial Activity against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia
abstract: Background: Ceratonia siliqua contains compounds with potential antioxidant and antibacterial activities. Objective: This study aims to characterize the ethanolic extract of Ceratonia siliqua and to evaluate its DPPH radical scavenging activity and antibacterial activity against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. Methodology: The methods included microwave assisted ethanolic extraction, GC–MS profiling and DPPH testing. title: Prolonged static aging of olefin-based inverse emulsion drilling fluids: temperature–time effects on rheology, stability, and filtration
abstract: Synthetic-based drilling fluids (SBFs) formulated as olefin-based inverse emulsions are widely used in deepwater operations, where prolonged static intervals expose the fluid to high temperatures without shear. This study investigated the coupled effects of aging temperature (100–150 °C) and static exposure time (24–168 h) on the rheological behavior, emulsion stability, and filtration performance of an olefin-based synthetic drilling fluid using a Central Composite Design. The response surface models for the Herschel–Bulkley parameters were statistically significant (p≤0.05, R 2 =0.978–0.992)

title: Preparation, structures, physicochemical properties, health benefits, and application in seasonal allergy care: a review on Ribes nigrum L. (blackcurrant) polysaccharides
abstract: Blackcurrant ( Ribes nigrum L.) is a perennial shrub of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae. It has important nutritional and pharmacological value. The fruit of blackcurrant contains anthocyanins, vitamin C, minerals, and dietary fiber, which are widely popular among consumers. Its leaves can be used to treat rheumatism, arthritis, and respiratory diseases. In recent years, with the continuous deepening of research on the chemical composition of blackcurrant, blackcurrant polysaccharides have become a research hotspot due to their complex structure and wide range of health benefits.
institutions: First Affiliated Hospital of Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine

title: Beyond ecological protection: unravelling the Social Matrix and biocultural drivers of heritage tree conservation
abstract: The long-term persistence of heritage trees is shaped by ecological suitability, species traits, land-use pressure, and climate, and may also depend on social arrangements that sustain protection across generations. Yet existing conservation frameworks rarely specify how cultural meaning, governance, knowledge, livelihoods, and collective capacity combine to produce durable stewardship. We conducted a theory-building evidence synthesis of published and selected comparative cases spanning sacred groves, church forests, fengshui forests, heritage-tree governance, and agricultural heritage landsc
journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: A pulmonary air leak model for integrated assessment of pulmonary sealant performance and tissue remodeling
abstract: Pulmonary sealants are used to manage air leakage after lung surgery. Their preclinical assessment requires a defined pulmonary defect and evaluation of both immediate sealing and subsequent tissue responses. This study examined the effect of defect size on airway pressure in a rat pulmonary air leak model and assessed the application of the selected condition to pulmonary sealant evaluation. Small (2–4 mm) and large (8–10 mm) pulmonary parenchymal defects were created in the right middle lobe of mechanically ventilated rats ( n = 6 per group). abstract: To investigate the influence mechanism of water on rock slope stability under different water-content conditions, a high rock slope along a section of the Chongqing–Guizhou Expressway was selected as the engineering case. Initially, field samples were collected and sandstone specimens with varying water content were prepared. title: Institutionalizing Corporate Intelligence in Global Shipping: An AHP-Based Framework for Competitive Intelligence and Counterintelligence
abstract: In the current dynamic threat landscape, the shipping industry is becoming increasingly exposed to disinformation, espionage, and various security and digital risks. This paper utilizes the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to present a structured multi-criteria decision-making methodology for the world-class shipping companies to enhance intelligence operations, drawing primary data from eighteen (18) semi-structured interviews with senior leaders, security and compliance professionals from world-class global shipping companies and state intelligence agencies about current gaps and organizat
journal: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
institutions: Athens University of Economics and Business

title: La protección jurídica contra la discriminación algorítmica en la selección de empleo por parte de las 12 economías más grandes del mundo
abstract: El uso de Inteligencia Artificial en la selección de empleo es capaz de generar sesgos y discriminación. La investigación busca descubrir cómo se produce esta discriminación algorítmica y las soluciones regulatorias adoptadas por las doce mayores economías del mundo. La metodología empleada fue la revisión bibliográfica sobre el tema y documental de los textos normativos de estas economías y el análisis de los datos. title: 2024 Celebration of Research and Scholarship: East Carolina University School of Dental Medicine
abstract: The Celebration of Research and Scholarship (C0RAS), hosted by the East Carolina University (ECU) School of Dental Medicine showcases student, resident, and faculty research, clinical case studies, and scholarly achievements in oral sciences.

title: La inteligencia artificial y los procesos de aprendizaje del emprendimiento en la educación superior colombiana
abstract: El artículo propone analizar la relación entre la percepción, la motivación y las condiciones institucionales del profesorado y la integración de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la enseñanza del emprendimiento, así como el cambio de estas variables tras un periodo académico de capacitación. Para ello, se desarrolla un estudio cuantitativo, correlacional y longitudinal de panel, con muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia, aplicado a 145 docentes de una universidad pública colombiana de educación a distancia (128 en ambas mediciones) y complementado con talleres participativos de triangu

title: Implicaciones regulatorias de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa en la creación visual
abstract: La Inteligencia Artificial Generativa está transformando los procesos de creación visual y el marco jurídico que los regula. De ahí que se analice la normativa europea y española aplicable a la creación visual mediante IA y se proponga un modelo conceptual que facilite la comprensión de las exigencias regulatorias en el proceso creativo. Los resultados ponen de relieve que los creadores visuales con IA Generativa son sujetos responsables en función de su rol funcional, de la originalidad y del grado de control ejercido sobre las herramientas utilizadas
journal: VISUAL REVIEW International Visual Culture Review / Revista Internacional de Cultura Visual

title: Non‐Volatile ReS 2 Optical Sensor for Enhanced Polarization Imaging
abstract: Polarization‐resolved imaging provides rich vectorial information but is limited by memoryless detectors under low signal‐to‐noise conditions. Here, we report a polarization‐sensitive neuromorphic optoelectronic device based on a plasma‐engineered FLG/ReS 2 /FLG heterostructure that integrates intrinsic sensing and memory properties. Moderate Ar plasma‐treated ReS 2 devices exhibited a persistent negative photoresponse with a responsivity magnitude up to 1.5 × 10 3 A W −1 and long‐term optical memory. title: Spatial–Temporal Evolution of Drought–Flood Abrupt Alternation in Inner Mongolia and the Synergistic Influence of Westerlies and Moisture Transport
abstract: Drought–flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) events represent compound hydroclimatic extremes characterized by rapid transitions between drought and flood conditions. However, their spatiotemporal variability and atmospheric circulation mechanisms in Inner Mongolia remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of DFAA events and their associations with the 500 and 850 hPa westerly indices, geopotential height anomalies and moisture transport. title: Aesthetic Experience and Scientific Understanding in Ecological Science: A Relational Framework
abstract: The climate crisis, biodiversity decline, and ecological risks increase the gap between the ability to receive scientific information and the ability to understand relationship structures, interdependencies, and the consequences of actions. The study aims to examine how scientific knowledge is transformed into scientific understanding and the role of aesthetic experience in that transformation. The study applies conceptual and critical analysis with interdisciplinary and relational synthesis. title: Cement-reduced ternary concrete with fly ash and silica fume for irrigation canal structures: computational mix design with single-composition experimental verification
abstract: Irrigation canal linings in Kazakhstan face freeze-thaw cycling, sulfate-bearing water, and abrasive sediment flow, while national programs to rehabilitate more than 14,000 km of canals create sustained demand for lower-clinker concrete. This study computationally designs a cement-reduced ternary binder (CEM I 42.5N, Ekibastuz low-calcium fly ash, and DSF-95 silica fume, 70:20:10 by mass) that replaces 30% of the cement in a plant control mixture (280 vs 400 kg/m3) while preserving total binder content, paste volume, and aggregate skeleton. title: Evaluating the impacts of low-carbon transitions on urban ecological resilience: Quasi–natural experimental evidence from China
abstract: The enactment of the low-carbon city pilot policy (LCCP) plays a pivotal role in strengthening urban ecological resilience (UER) and achieving sustainable urban development. Herein, we used panel data from 282 cities from 2005 to 2022 and applied a multiperiod difference-in-difference model to evaluate the impact of the LCCP on UER. The LCCP significantly enhances UER, guiding cities toward substantially sustainable development. The mechanism analysis suggests that the LCCP influences UER through government environmental governance capacity, enterprise digital innovation, and public environmen

title: An exploration of curriculum complexity and math cruciality for three engineering disciplines across multiple institutions
abstract: Background The sequential structure of the engineering curriculum, along with the central role of math, creates an interconnected system of prerequisite and corequisite requirements and course sequencing, resulting in curricula with high structural complexity in which one course can influence student pathways. Considering complexity and math requirements side‐by‐side can illuminate levers for curricular change. abstract: This study investigates the effects of combined biochar and liquid organic fertilizer treatments on the growth and yield of mung bean (Vigna radiata L.). The experiment was conducted at the Hera Research Center, Faculty of Agriculture, UNITAL, Cristo Rei Administrative Post, Dili Municipality, from February to June 2025. Two treatment factors were evaluated: locally produced liquid organic fertilizer (Lof-nachi) and biochar application rates. title: Sendai virus, a candidate vaccine for the prevention of respiratory virus infections in children: a review
abstract: Background Respiratory viruses including human parainfluenza virus (hPIV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), pose serious, potentially lethal threats to humans, particularly infants and young children. While maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies are advancing to provide transient protection against these viruses, licensed pediatric vaccines are not yet available. title: Advancing dynamic phosphorus prescription models for cassava ( Manihot esculenta ) using a random forest approach
abstract: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) is a key staple crop supporting global food security, yet its productivity is increasingly constrained by declining soil fertility and climate variability. In many cassava-producing regions, phosphorus (P) recommendations rely on static fertilization grids that do not adequately account for site-specific soil and crop response variability. title: AN APPLICATION OF A I-O ECONOMIC IMPACT MODEL TO US FEDERAL LABORATORY INVENTIONS: 2011–2020
abstract: This article provides an input–output-based estimate of the economic impact of U.S. federal laboratory licensing from 2011–2020. Federal laboratory earned royalty data are used to estimate licensed product sales. These estimated sales, plus federal laboratory license income data and Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) data on patterns of production and employment, are then used in the economic‑impact calculations of Gross Industry Output (GO), Gross Domestic Output (GDP) and jobs. title: The Futures Thinking Kite scenario method
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop the Futures Thinking Kite as a scenario method using a visual heuristic to examine four conditional relationships between intervention intensity and desirable outcomes. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper draws on futures studies, systems thinking and research on subtraction. Hypothetical policing and mobility applications frame the discussion; city housing and Australian wetland scenarios extend it. title: Linking evaporitic crust texture to microbial community structure in a hypersaline environment
abstract: Introduction Hypersaline evaporitic environments are considered terrestrial analogues for planetary settings, because they preserve mineralogical and biological signatures formed under extreme salinity, high UV radiation, and arid conditions. However, the relationships between the surface texture of evaporitic crusts and the underlying microbial communities are largely disregarded. title: Population Dynamics in Central Papua Province of Indonesia
abstract: Central Papua Province, one of Indonesia's newest provinces, has a distinctive demographic profile characterized by a substantial Indigenous Papuan (Orang Asli Papua, OAP) population, geographically dispersed settlements, and unequal access to public services. Understanding population dynamics in this region is essential for formulating effective development policies, particularly in education, healthcare, and economic equity. This study examined population dynamics in Central Papua Province by identifying and analyzing key factors influencing demographic changes. The research employed a descr

title: Ultrafiltration for Sustainable Biodiesel Purification. Part 2 – Fouling Mechanisms and Modelling Approaches

title: Physiological and Agronomic Effects of Biofertilizer Applications Under Drought Stress in Rice (Oryza sativa L)
abstract: This study seeks to identify which type of biofertilizer can mitigate the risk of yield decline, effect of interaction between biofertilizer and rice varieties in focussing on the physiological and agronomic of rice such as Soil and Plant Analyzer Development (SPAD) value, Relative Water Content (RWC), Drought Tolerance Index (DTI) and Drought Susceptibility Index (DSI) during drought stress in the reproductive period. title: Ultraviolet-induced photoluminescence discovered in the Mexican hairy dwarf porcupine (Coendou mexicanus), and its potential applications for monitoring in the wild
abstract: Photoluminescence in different organisms has attracted the interest of scientists over the last 10 years. The list of photoluminescent species in mammals is growing annually, largely thanks to specimens found in museums. However, studies of photoluminescence in live, wild animals are scarce. In this study, we describe vivid photoluminescence in the Mexican hairy dwarf porcupine ( Coendou mexicanus ) from the city of Chetumal, Quintana Roo, Mexico. title: Modelling pesticide residues and ecological risks in Kilombero Valley, Tanzania: a SWAT + approach
abstract: Thorough pesticide use in tropical agricultural catchments threatens surface and groundwater quality, yet long-term pesticide transport and ecological risks remain poorly understood in data-scarce regions. This study assessed the long-term distribution and ecological risks of chlorpyrifos, profenofos, cypermethrin, and lambda-cyhalothrin in the Kisawasawa catchment, Kilombero Valley, Tanzania, from 2005 to 2035 using the Soil and Water Assessment Tool Plus (SWAT + ). title: Simultaneous optimization of GPL distribution and GPL volume fraction for frequency-constrained design of AFG-GPL curved beams using MSS-IGP
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization methodology to determine optimal graphene platelet (GPL) distribution patterns and GPL volume fraction (GVF) in axially functionally graded GPL-reinforced (AFG-GPLs) composite curved beams. Existing studies are limited to predefined distribution patterns, restricting GPL-efficient structural design. title: Assessing future eco-hydrological behaviour of a typical Sahelian agro-ecosystem under climate change for the 21st century
abstract: Study Region The Sahel is dominated by a monsoon climate, where most of the population relies on subsistence agriculture. This study focuses on a typical agro-pastoral area in southwestern Niger. Study Focus Significant gaps remain in climate change impact projections in the Sahel. Indeed, capturing the impact of rapid hydrological processes necessitates high temporal resolution scenarios and adapted ecohydrological models, which has rarely been done in Sahel. This study addresses this gap by building climate scenarios at a 30-minute time step, by combining an observational dataset with CMIP6

title: Climate variability and forest fire dynamics in Himachal Pradesh, India
abstract: Forest fires are recognized as a major threat to a significant global challenge for ecosystem stability. In the recent past the state experienced rise in forest fire events. Therefore, the present study provides an overview of forest fire events in Himachal Pradesh, along with its relationship between climatic attributes. The fire events mostly occur during summer and monsoon season. Therefore, the fire data was collected for said seasons from Fire information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) portal from 2004 to 2024. title: Technology-Integrated Applications Used in Mathematics and Technological Competence: Effects on Engagement and Achievement of Public Junior High School Learners
abstract: Technology-enhanced applications can make mathematics more concrete and relevant, but their benefits depend on how extensively and competently teachers use them. This descriptive-correlational study examined the technology-integrated applications used in mathematics and teachers’ technological competence and their effects on the engagement and achievement of public junior high school learners in the Trinidad 1 and Trinidad 2 Districts, DepEd Schools Division of Bohol, in School Year 2025–2026. title: Polydopamine-mediated dual-anchoring of gelatin hydrogel onto bacterial cellulose membranes for durable antifouling and antibacterial ultrafiltration
abstract: Bio-based membranes offer inherent biodegradability and environmental compatibility, but their poor durability remains a major barrier to practical water purification. In this study, we propose a novel bioinspired dual-anchoring interfacial strategy for stabilizing a gelatin hydrogel as a functional layer on bacterial cellulose (BC) through a polydopamine (PDA) interlayer. title: A configurable VR spacecraft simulator enhanced with HMI data in microgravity
abstract: Simulators play a crucial role in the aerospace industry, ranging from simple desktop models to advanced Level D simulators used for pilot training. While most non-gaming simulators focus on crew training and client illustration, there is a notable deficiency in simulators that assist with cockpit design. Current methods primarily utilize standard CAD/CAE software alongside Digital Human Models, which often lack adequate functionality for comprehensive human factor evaluation for design optimization. title: Digital-Twin-Enabled Energy Management for Low-Carbon Port Cities: A Comparative Urban-Intelligence Framework for Genoa, Livorno and Naples
abstract: Ports are increasingly becoming urban cyber-physical systems in which maritime operations, terminal activities, buildings, electricity networks, renewable generation and environmental pressures interact. Energy Management Systems (EMS) can coordinate energy production and consumption, while Digital Twins (DTs) can connect real-time data, simulation and decision support. Yet port digitalisation and port decarbonisation are still frequently treated as separate domains. title: Flexural Behaviour and Ductility of High-Strength Concrete Beams Reinforced with Hybrid BFRP-Steel Bars
abstract: This study investigates the flexural performance of high-strength concrete beams reinforced with hybrid basalt fibre-reinforced polymer (BFRP) and steel bars. Six beams were tested under four-point bending, including four with varying BFRP-to-steel ratios and two reference beams reinforced solely with steel and BFRP, respectively. The main variable was the reinforcement proportion. The experimental program evaluated load-bearing capacity, midspan deflection, crack width, and ductility. title: Single-cell analysis of epithelial transcriptional states identifies stromal associations and candidate targets in colon cancer
abstract: BACKGROUND: Colon cancer progression involves coordinated changes in epithelial cells and the tumor microenvironment, yet the transcriptional organization, associated regulatory programs and candidate vulnerabilities of epithelial cell states remain unclear. METHODS: Multi-cohort single-cell RNA sequencing data were integrated with inferred copy-number variation, pseudotime, regulon and spatial transcriptomic analyses. title: Genetic diversity of bacterial endophytes associated with Crotalaria (Rattlepods)
abstract: Crotalaria is a diverse legume genus valued for its ecological and agronomic roles. However, its associated endophytic microbiome remains minimally characterized. This study examined the genetic diversity and community structure of bacterial endophytes inhabiting domesticated and wild Crotalaria species. Twenty-nine healthy Crotalaria plant samples were analyzed using the culture-independent 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing approach. title: Unravelling drivers of burned area change in southern Ethiopia: climate, vegetation, and dryland development
abstract: African savannas are the most extensively burned regions globally; however, burned area (BA) in these regions has declined in recent decades. Agricultural expansion, infrastructure development, and climate change are commonly cited drivers, but their relative contributions remain contested. Regional-scale analyses are needed to capture spatiotemporal changes, disentangle environmental and anthropogenic drivers, and inform decision-making. title: The Spillover Effect of Institutionalized Opening-up: Evidence from China's Free Trade Zones
abstract: As a reform experimental field for establishing high-level mechanisms facing the external world, fully releasing the spillover effects of the free trade zone is an important task for China to achieve technological leapfrog development at present. This paper takes the establishment of China's free trade zones as a natural experiment, using panel data of 283 Chinese cities from 2012 to 2023, and adopting the multi-period difference-difference method to conduct an empirical study on the technological spillover effects and their influencing mechanisms of free trade zones (FTZs) under the backgroun
journal: International Journal of Economics Finance and Management Sciences

title: Quantum-inspired differential evolution with Elite Perturbation for high-dimensional portfolio optimization
abstract: High-dimensional portfolio optimization is a challenging computational problem due to its large search space, nonlinear objective structure, and practical constraints on asset allocation. To improve the computational tractability of Sharpe ratio-based portfolio optimization, this paper reformulates the original constrained model as an unconstrained single-objective problem by embedding equality and inequality constraints into the objective function through penalty terms. This reformulation simplifies constraint handling while retaining the financial interpretation of risk-return optimization.
institutions: Kobe City University of Foreign Studies

title: Biosurfactants in wastewater treatment: recent advances in agro-waste valorization, production technologies, and environmental remediation
abstract: Industrial, agricultural and municipal effluents are contaminated with a variety of pollutants, including hydrocarbons, heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals and pathogenic microorganisms that have a great impact on the environment and on public health. Typical treatment technologies are expensive, pollute the environment as secondary pollutants, and are not very effective at remediating hydrophobic and persistent contaminants. title: Thermoelastic Wave‐Based Logic for Mechanically Cognitive Materials
abstract: Recent advances in metamaterials and fabrication techniques have revived interest in mechanical computing. Contrary to techniques relying on static deformations of buckling beams or origami‐based lattices, the integration of wave scattering and mechanical memory presents a promising path toward efficient, low‐latency elastoacoustic computing. This work introduces a novel class of multifunctional mechanical computing circuits that leverage the rich dynamics of phononic and locally resonant materials. title: Decomposing five decades of river flow: multiscale discharge variability, wavelet decomposition, and change-point detection in the upper indus basin (1973–2020)
abstract: The Upper Indus Basin (UIB) serves as a critical freshwater source for millions in South Asia, yet exhibits complex hydrological responses to climate change, cryospheric dynamics, and anthropogenic influences. However, wavelet-based and change-point detection methods in glacio-hydrological basins remain constrained by the lack of consensus on optimal wavelet families for snow-glacier melt signatures and insufficient evaluation against seasonal variability and stochastic noise. title: AI and the Responsibility-Bearing Status of Authorship
abstract: Generative AI has sharpened an old question: who, or what, can be an author? The central aim of this paper is to reconstruct the conception of authorship already implicit in copyright law. I argue that copyright encodes authorship as a responsibility-bearing status, constituted by a cluster of conditions: intentional agency, guided control, and relational expression (ACE). title: Pedogenic Controls on Soil Organic Carbon Persistence in Tropical Soils: A Structured Critical Review with a Colombian Outlook
abstract: Tropical soils store large amounts of soil organic carbon (SOC), but the mechanisms governing its persistence vary among mineralogical, hydrological, biological, and geomorphic settings. This structured critical review examines when particular processes become limiting for SOC persistence rather than treating soil-forming factors as universal controls. An auditable corpus of 78 unique records was screened using eligibility and evidence-characterization criteria, with 70 records retained for qualitative synthesis. title: Plume emission rate estimation using Gaussian plumes in remote imaging spectroscopy with SPIIRE
abstract: The detection and quantification of methane and other trace gas emissions using remote sensing with imaging spectroscopy is an increasingly important tool for understanding local, regional, and global emissions. Traditional algorithms for quantifying the emission rate often rely on user-determined, instrument-dependent parameters and arbitrary plume boundaries. In this paper we present a new algorithm to estimate the emission rate based on a statistical inversion of a physical, Gaussian plume model that does not depend on such parameter choices or plume boundaries, termed SPIIRE. title: CLIENTS AWARENESS ON MULTI-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION IN BANKING SECURITY: BASIS FOR A PROPOSED CAMPAIGN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM IN PREVENTING FINANCIAL FRAUD
abstract: This study examined the use of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) in banking security, focusing on the demographic profile, level of awareness, significant relationships, and challenges encountered by clients in preventing financial fraud. The findings revealed that most MFA users were aged 31–40 (34.2%), male (52%), married (57%), and college graduates (61%). Additionally, 45% conducted online banking transactions daily. Clients demonstrated moderate to high awareness of MFA in terms of online banking access, unauthorized access prevention, account recovery, and online fraud protection. Howeve
journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)

title: Colonial legacies shape natural hazards in the Atlantic forests of Brazil
abstract: Natural hazards pose escalating ecological, public health, and economic challenges globally, with tropical regions bearing a disproportionate burden due to climate change and structural inequalities. This paper examines the intersection of European colonialism, deforestation, and contemporary natural hazard vulnerability in Brazil's Atlantic Forest, one of the world's most biodiverse and threatened biomes. title: Inteligencia artificial en la administración de justicia penal: garantías y desafíos constitucionales en Ecuador
abstract: La inteligencia artificial en la justicia penal promete celeridad y apoyo a la decisión, pero puede comprometer la motivación, la defensa, la presunción de inocencia y la imparcialidad judicial. El estudio analizó su uso en la justicia penal ecuatoriana desde las garantías constitucionales. title: Colourful and blooming cities – spatio-temporal proxies of pollinators for citizen science
abstract: Biodiversity monitoring is essential for detecting spatio-temporal changes and conservation effectiveness. Citizen science is expanding and complementing expert-based monitoring, yet its widespread success depends on simple and reliable sampling protocols. Simplified proxies are required in pollinator research to overcome taxonomic limitations, but their reliability remains uncertain. title: Enhancing Sustainability in Transient Crop Planning Through Integrated Forecasting and Optimization Models
abstract: Abstract Agricultural planning for short-cycle crops involves integrating planting and harvesting decisions under temporal and spatial variability in production. This study develops an integrated decision-support framework for transient multi-crop planning that combines complementary production forecasting mechanisms with a multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model. abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and outcomes in microsatellite-stable metastatic disease have improved only modestly despite optimised cytotoxic, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR regimens. abstract: Dental unit waterlines (DUWLs) can develop persistent microbial biofilms due to narrow-bore tubing, low water flow, and repeated exposure to oral contaminants, making effective decontamination an important infection-control measure. abstract: Este estudio explora cómo afrontar los desafíos de aprendizaje en la Generación Z mediante la integración estratégica de tecnologías emergentes para estimular el pensamiento crítico y el interés por las vocaciones científicas. abstract: Intermediate-volatility organic compounds (IVOCs) serve as crucial precursors to secondary organic aerosol (SOA), yet their seasonal variations remain insufficiently characterized, impeding a comprehensive understanding of their atmospheric processing and impacts on air quality. To capture the seasonal dynamics of primary IVOCs and identify the key drivers governing their variability, four-season field campaigns were conducted at an urban site in Yangtze River Delta region. abstract: Engineering hierarchically porous and heterogeneous interfaces is a powerful strategy for obtaining high-performance microwave absorbers, because it simultaneously improves impedance matching and enhances polarization loss. abstract: Groundnut cultivation in seasonally dry tropical landscapes is strongly influenced by soil heterogeneity, landscape position and management constraints, requiring crop-specific land evaluation for sustainable production. abstract: Ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs) are genetically encoded natural products that undergo diverse enzymatic modifications to generate structurally constrained molecules with broad biological activities and substantial engineering potential. title: Research progress of medical bioadhesives: fundamental Theory, clinical applications, and future perspectives
abstract: Medical bioadhesive glues are transforming surgery, trauma care, and regenerative medicine by enabling rapid tissue adhesion and promoting healing. They offer alternatives to sutures and staples, which can prolong operative time, damage tissue, and provoke foreign body reactions. However, clinical translation remains limited by challenges in long-term safety assessment, standardized evaluation, and adaptation to complex surgical settings. Drawing on a comprehensive search of PubMed and Web of Science, this review traces the evolution of bioadhesives from natural materials to biomimetic designs

title: Sequential Development and Adaptive Reuse Processes: From Chamber of Commerce to Sümerbank and Commercial Center
abstract: Historic buildings are vital components of architectural and urban heritage, reflecting a society’s social and cultural values and shaping a city’s identity. Preserving historic buildings that have lost their original function or can no longer meet modern needs is essential for sustaining both the structures themselves and the city’s identity. Adaptive reuse is an important conservation approach that gives new life to historic buildings by assigning them new functions, ensuring their ongoing relevance and sustainability. title: La Inteligencia Artificial Generativa como mediador epistémico en la educación superior: Revisión cualitativa de actores, niveles y tensiones
abstract: Este estudio cualitativo analiza el pensamiento crítico como un proceso dialógico mediado por inteligencia artificial generativa en la formación docente. En lugar de concebir la IA como proveedora de respuestas, se la aborda como un mediador cognitivo orientado a sostener interacciones reflexivas no directivas. A partir del análisis de interacciones con un asistente socrático, producciones académicas, observación participante y autoevaluaciones de 103 estudiantes, se identifican procesos de reformulación argumentativa, suspensión de respuestas inmediatas y construcción progresiva de criterios

title: Visualising Hope: A Multimodal Discourse Analysis of Environmental Culture in UNEP’s 2025 Campaign
abstract: Scientific data is not enough to address global environmental concerns because public responses to global environmental challenges are also influenced by cultural values and communicative practices. Innovative environmental communication is therefore needed to shift from climate anxiety to collective action. abstract: The goal of remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is to accurately distinguish land-surface changes. abstract: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform in next-generation integrated optoelectronics and on-chip/chip-chip interconnection due to its attractive optical property and versatility. abstract: Soil microorganisms mediate nutrient turnover, carbon storage, disease suppression, and plant stress tolerance, yet the evidentiary distance between microbial measurements and agronomic outcomes remains poorly defined. abstract: La rápida incorporación de la inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) en la educación superior está modificando las prácticas mediante las cuales los estudiantes buscan información, construyen problemas, diseñan investigaciones, analizan datos, elaboran argumentos y comunican conocimiento científico. abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) develops through the interaction of long-term environmental injury and biological susceptibility, which activates self-reinforcing networks of chronic inflammation, oxidative and mitochondrial stress, protease–antiprotease imbalance, cellular senescence, impaired tissue repair, and epigenetic/transcriptional reprogramming. abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants of global concern because of their chemical stability, extensive use, and widespread occurrence. abstract: Production constitutes a fundamental concept for describing the power of modern societies to shape and distinguish themselves from their environment. However, beyond being merely descriptive, the concept also orders reality. Continuing the challenge posed to social theory by Jean Baudrillard while also taking seriously Michel Callon’s account of the performativity of economic concepts, I attempt a historical defamiliarization and a critique of the production concept. abstract: The growing emphasis on integrated and digitally enabled public services has not necessarily ensured resilient and equitable service delivery, particularly in local governments facing uneven infrastructure, geographic barriers, and variations in institutional capacity. abstract: Introduction Endometriosis is an estrogen-dependent, chronic inflammatory condition affecting roughly 10% of reproductive-aged women and is characterized by pelvic pain and infertility. abstract: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) has emerged as a critical pillar of climate mitigation efforts, yet its scalable deployment is constrained by capital-intensive investments, regulatory fragmentation, and an absence of standardized site evaluation frameworks. abstract: Este artículo es una reflexión sobre el impacto de la Inteligencia Artificial Generativa (iagen) en la divulgación escrita: en sus lectores, escritores y editores. Además, se tratan otros asuntos como la construcción del conocimiento y la investigación sobre divulgación. abstract: Introduction Home and domestic gardens are multifunctional systems that support biodiversity, food security, sustainable resource use, and human well-being. abstract: Islamic Religious Education (IRE) can foster moderate student character by connecting multicultural values with everyday social experiences. This qualitative ethnographic study examined multicultural education and value internalization at SMAN 1 Haruai, SMAN 1 Upau, and SMAN 1 Muara Uya in Tabalong Regency, Indonesia. abstract: To address the problems of low path planning efficiency and excessive redundant nodes in tomato harvesting manipulators, an improved RRT-APF path planning algorithm is proposed. First, a goal-biased strategy is introduced into the standard Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) framework to reduce search randomness and improve sampling efficiency. abstract: Breast cancer frequently involves the skeleton, but the systemic molecular changes associated with tumor growth in a vertebral implantation model remain incompletely characterized. To compare gut microbiota, metabolite, and tumor-transcriptome profiles between orthotopic breast tumors and tumors established by direct vertebral implantation, and to identify cross-omics associations for hypothesis generation. abstract: Low-speed wind energy conversion systems require an effective power-electronic interface to manage low and fluctuating generator voltages. In this study, a Mamdani fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for regulating the Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) duty cycle of a three-phase synchronous Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (MOSFET) rectifier intended for low-speed wind energy conversion is developed. title: The impact of advanced manufacturing development on industrial land prices: Evidence from Zhejiang, China
abstract: While existing studies have examined the determinants of industrial land prices, limited attention has been paid to how changes in local government competition strategies shape industrial land pricing. Using data from Zhejiang Province, China, this study investigates how the shift in local government strategies – from a “race-to-bottom” to a “race-for-quality” focusing on advanced manufacturing – affects industrial land prices through market-oriented land allocation practices. title: Evapotranspiration and crop coefficient of garlic c.v. Chino Cincomesino (Allium sativum L.) in the peruvian desert
abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum L.) is a crop of great importance due to its high nutritional content, especially in arid regions where water availability is limited by climate change. In this context, efficient water resource management strategies are required to ensure the sustainability of agricultural production. A study was conducted in the Majes Irrigation District (Arequipa, Peru) to determine the crop evapotranspiration (ETc) and crop coefficient (Kc) of the garlic cultivar Chino Cincomesino (A. sativum) using free-draining lysimeters. title: Hybrid diffusion–DE-based 3D UAV deployment for joint coverage enhancement and energy efficiency in IoT networks
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted communication has become a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks, particularly in post-disaster recovery and remote-area connectivity. A major challenge lies in jointly maximizing the coverage of Internet of Things devices (IoTDEs) while minimizing the energy consumption of UAV base stations (UAV-BSs). title: Phenotypic Variation in Body Measurements and Their Associations with Body Condition Score in Bali Cattle
abstract: Body condition score (BCS) and linear body measurements are the two records most often collected at Indonesian cattle breeding stations, yet they are seldom analysed together. This study described the phenotypic variation of chest circumference (CC), body length (BL), body height (BH) and BCS, and quantified the association between BCS and each body measurement in Bali cattle (Bos javanicus) aged 1-2 years at UPTD PTHPT Api-Api, East Kalimantan, Indonesia. abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial generativa en la educación superior reabre una pregunta central: ¿qué significa aprender cuando una herramienta es capaz de explicar, sintetizar y producir respuestas plausibles en tan poco tiempo? abstract: Cost, schedule and quality constitute the core objectives of project management. Accurate cost and schedule control and prediction are critical to the smooth delivery of wind turbine blade R&D projects. As the mainstream tool for integrated project control, the earned value method can identify project deviations and optimize the allocation of duration and cost. abstract: Urbanization alters land surface characteristics and intensifies Surface Urban Heat Island (SUHI) conditions, particularly in rapidly growing urban areas. However, municipality level studies in Kerala linking Land Use Land Cover (LULC) change, Land Surface Temperature (LST), spectral indices, and urban planning remain limited. abstract: Subglacial bed topography is a fundamental boundary condition for ice-sheet flow, basal thermal regimes, and the preservation of palaeoclimate records, yet it remains highly uncertain across Antarctica. We use stochastic simulation methods to generate an ensemble of gridded (500 m) ice thickness and bed elevation near Dome C, and map bed elevation uncertainty accounting for impacts of data availability and basal roughness. abstract: In multiple neural systems, networks of bursting neurons generate and coordinate robust sequential rhythms, such as those observed in central pattern generators (CPGs) that control motor activity. In this paper, we combine electrophysiological experiments and biophysical models of the pyloric CPG to investigate cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting in sequential rhythms. abstract: Coffee agroforestry systems (AFS) are valued for biodiversity conservation, microclimate regulation, and sustainability in tropical agricultural landscapes. In Peru, smallholders cultivate coffee with associated species, yet floristic and structural information is limited for northeastern coffee regions. This study aimed to characterize species associated with coffee along an altitudinal gradient in Amazonas and Cajamarca. abstract: Background The continuum of pregnancy care refers to the uninterrupted sequence of antenatal, institutional delivery care, and postnatal services that safeguard maternal and neonatal health, and ensuring universal access to it is central to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 3. abstract: Access to safe drinking water remains a critical challenge in the Central African Republic (CAR), where basic water access rates stand at approximately 40%. In Bangui, the capital city, water supply depends primarily on the Oubangui River, whose discharge significantly decreases during the dry season, exacerbating water insecurity for an urban population of approximately 1.5 million inhabitants. abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago 1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka) 2 . abstract: Mass-casualty incidents following earthquakes place substantial strain on emergency medical systems, where delays in triage and transportation can directly affect survival outcomes. Many existing studies examine either facility location or operational performance in isolation, which limits their ability to capture how these decisions interact under uncertain conditions. abstract: Identifying the perceptions and opinions held by a population in connection with a social movement can help to understand how well the movement’s intended messages are spreading. A focus on the student population is essential for this understanding, as these individuals represent the future. abstract: Voting behavior, a prevalent form of political participation, lacks a definitive characterisation and exhibits variability across different contexts. abstract: This study explores how pre-service English teachers (PSETs) understand and envision integrating the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into English language teaching (ELT) through Appreciative Inquiry (AI). abstract: SVoro and PrinceCharming were isolated from moist soil on the campus of Winthrop University and isolated on the host bacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis mc 2 155.SVoro has a myovirus morphology and a genome of 155,109 bp, while PrinceCharming exhibits siphovirus morphology and a genome of 67,429 bp.Lysogens could not be raised for SVoro or PrinceCharming, suggesting these are virulent phages.SVoro is classified in the C1 subcluster, and PrinceCharming belongs to the B2 subcluster.

title: Enhancing Bacterial Secondary Metabolite Yields Using Non-Biological Inducers: Blind metabolic engineering
abstract: Bacteria secondary metabolites are widely used in many industries, including pharmaceutical, food, agricultural, and cosmetics. Abiotic stresses are a low-cost and easy approach to enhance the accumulation of these metabolites. On the other hand, rational metabolic engineering strategies are limited by the unknown metabolic burden, incomplete pathway knowledge, and biosafety concerns associated with genetically modified microorganisms (GMMs). This review surveys abiotic stress-driven strategies to boost secondary metabolite production in bacterial strains. It systematically analyzes how key ab

title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research
abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporati
institutions: Chinese Center For Disease Control and Prevention

title: Uso autoinformado de la inteligencia artificial en estudiantes universitarios: Factores asociados y beneficios académicos percibidos
abstract: La incorporación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa en la educación superior ha transformado las prácticas de aprendizaje; sin embargo, aún existe limitada evidencia sobre los factores asociados con una apropiación académica significativa de estas tecnologías. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar los factores asociados con el uso autoinformado académico de la IA y con los beneficios académicos percibidos en estudiantes universitarios. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, de alcance analítico y diseño transversal, con una muestra de 316 estudiantes de diferentes áreas del conocimi
institutions: Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia

title: Navigating Great Power Rivalry: India’s Strategic Hedging amid U.S.–China Competition after the 2020 Galwan Clash
abstract: The rivalry between the United States and China has placed India in a geopolitical dilemma, particularly following the 2020 Galwan Clash. As a middle power, India faces pressure to take sides, raising research questions about how India strategizes to navigate this competition. This qualitative case study analyzes India’s strategy using Cheng-Chwee Kuik’s hedging framework. The author argues that India has chosen to implement an adaptive hedging strategy to maintain strategic autonomy and avoid the risk of being drawn into conflict. title: Laser-Reduced Graphene Oxide Electrodes as a Self-Stabilizing Scaffold for Neat Ionic Liquids in Humidity Sensing
abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) are attractive sensing materials for humidity detection because of their hydrophilicity and their highly tunable physicochemical properties. However, most reported IL-based humidity sensors require an additional immobilization matrix, such as a polymer, nanoparticle composite, or poly(ionic liquid), to stabilize the liquid phase on solid-state electrodes, thereby increasing fabrication complexity. Here, we report capacitive humidity sensors based on neat 1-hexyl-1-methyl-2-(3-pyridinyl)pyrrolidinium methanesulfonate ([HexNic][MeSO3]) directly immobilized within porous laser
institutions: Foundation for Research and Technology Hellas

title: Challenges, opportunities, and policies for dual use innovation
abstract: Intensifying geopolitical tensions have heightened interest in items (knowledge, technologies, artefacts) with both military and civilian applications. A salient yet understudied question is how innovation and policy shape such dual use potential. This study consolidates the literature on dual use by focusing on the innovation-related challenges and opportunities it identifies, as well as the policy approaches proposed to address them. We conceptualize four dual use spheres by considering whether an item's civilian-military transferability is manifest or latent and whether offensive use is for

title: Mechanical and microstructural behavior of clay soil stabilized with lime kiln dust, silica fume, and carpet fibers under freeze-thaw conditions
abstract: This study investigates the stabilization of clay soil for cold climates using industrial by-products and recycled materials. To this end, the effects of lime kiln dust (LKD, up to 10%), silica fume (SF, up to 100% as a replacement of LKD), and waste carpet fibers (WCF, up to 2% by dry weight of soil) were analyzed individually and in combination, focusing on compaction characteristics, unconfined compressive strength (UCS), indirect tensile strength (ITS), and freeze-thaw (F-T) resistance. institutions: Islamic Azad University Central Tehran Branch

title: From E-waste to high-entropy alloys: sustainable critical metal recovery for advanced multicomponent materials
abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) is one of the fastest-growing solid waste streams globally, generating over 62 million tonnes annually by 2022, yet formal recycling rates remain below 25%. Beyond its environmental hazard, e-waste harbours a remarkable concentration of valuable and technology-critical metals, including copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), iron (Fe), gold (Au), palladium (Pd), rare earth elements (REEs), and many others, whose primary extraction through conventional mining carries severe ecological and geopolitical costs. This review examines e-waste as a strategic secondary resour

title: Amplification-free detection of antibiotic resistance in Enterococcus faecium using PNA-FISH
abstract: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) is a major nosocomial pathogen, with antibiotic resistance mediated by the vanA and vanB operons. Rapid and accurate detection of antibiotic resistance is critical for the timely treatment of bacteremia and sepsis. Although imaging-based approaches using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) provide a potential diagnostic solution, detecting mRNAs of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in individual cells remains particularly challenging due to their low copy number and transient expression. Here, we present a peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-FISH
institutions: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

title: Forest carbon farming across a northern European gradient: land-system archetypes for monitoring, reporting and verification, governance and implementation
abstract: Forest carbon farming is increasingly promoted as a complement to emissions reductions, but its feasibility and integrity depend on ecological baseline, land-use opportunity space, governance capacity and monitoring–reporting–verification (MRV) maturity. This comparative scoping review synthesizes evidence from Finland, Ireland and Iceland as three contrasting northern land-system archetypes: a mature boreal production system, a low-forest agricultural adoption system and a degraded restoration system. title: Tourism demand concentration exposes ecological carrying-capacity mismatches in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Tourism growth and ecological protection increasingly overlap in large river-basin corridors, but available visitor statistics rarely provide a continuous, cross-regional series and within-city spatial detail at the same time. We therefore used a long-term tourism-demand/service-concentration proxy (TD) as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, observed visitation. title: Early prediction of clinically important progression in children with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage treated at a high-altitude tertiary hospital: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Early identification of clinically important progression in children with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (tICH) remains challenging, particularly in high-altitude settings. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prediction model integrating clinical, radiological, oxygenation, and coagulation indicators. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 584 children with CT-confirmed tICH admitted between January 2016 and December 2025. title: Policies and Challenges of Post-Disaster Urban and Community Resilience in Makassar City: JEL Classification: Q54, R58, H84, Q56
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze disaster management policies, community adaptive capacity, and collaboration among government, local communities, and stakeholders in strengthening urban and community resilience to post-disaster conditions in Makassar City in a sustainable manner. This study employs a qualitative approach using in-depth interviews, field observations, document analysis, and focus group discussions (FGDs), with data analyzed using NVivo 12 Plus. The findings indicate that disaster management policies in Makassar City encompass mitigation, preparedness, emergency response
journal: Journal of Management and Administration Provision

title: A variable-separation ensemble transport method for Bayesian inference of parametric PDEs
abstract: This paper presents a variable-separation ensemble transport method (VSET) for inferring parameters in large-scale parametric partial differential equations (PDEs). Traditional Bayesian or ensemble-based approaches are often computationally prohibitive, as accurate inference typically requires many expensive partial differential equation (PDE) solves. To this end, we develop a coupled input–output reduction framework that constructs a low-rank approximation of the parameter-to-observable (PtO) map. title: Autoria mediada na era da inteligência artificial generativa: escrita acadêmica multilíngue, agência epistemológica e integridade científica
abstract: Este artigo analisa a Portaria CNPq nº 2.664/2026 à luz dos Estudos da Tradução, da escrita acadêmica multilíngue e das pesquisas sobre interação humano-IA. Por meio de análise teórico-crítica e documental, distingue geração textual, autoria intelectual e responsabilidade epistemológica. Desenvolve a noção de autoria mediada, diferenciando mediações de entrada e de saída e examinando a preservação da agência do pesquisador. journal: Ilha do Desterro A Journal of English Language Literatures in English and Cultural Studies
institutions: Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina

title: Spatial Accessibility and Village Development in Pidie Jaya Regency, Aceh, Indonesia
abstract: Village development is shaped by social, economic, and environmental conditions, including spatial access to essential services. This study examines the relationship between accessibility to educational, healthcare, and economic facilities and village development, measured using the Village Development Index, in Pidie Jaya Regency, Aceh, Indonesia. A quantitative approach combining spatial network analysis and multiple linear regression was applied to 222 villages.
