journal: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Management

title: Digital Adaptation and Green Human Resource Strategy for Sustainable Infrastructure Development
abstract: Sustainable infrastructure development requires organizations to respond simultaneously to digital transformation, environmental sustainability, and changing workforce requirements. However, digital technology adoption alone does not ensure sustainable infrastructure outcomes, while Green Human Resource Management is often examined separately from infrastructure transformation. This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework explaining how Digital Adaptation and Green Human Resource Strategy contribute to Sustainable Infrastructure Development through capability building. journal: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Management

title: Los ámbitos de aplicación del Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial: extraterritorialidad y unilateralismo regulatorio en el Derecho internacional privado europeo
abstract: El presente trabajo ofrece un estudio sistemático y conjunto de los ámbitos de aplicación material, personal, territorial y temporal del Reglamento (UE) 2024/1689 de Inteligencia Artificial desde la perspectiva del Derecho internacional privado. El análisis sitúa el RIA en el marco del unilateralismo regulatorio europeo y sostiene su caracterización como norma de policía que autodelimita su ámbito de aplicación en el espacio a través del artículo 2, desplazando, aunque sin excluir, el método conflictual.Sobre esta base, el trabajo reconstruye los distintos ámbitos de aplicación del Reglamento.

title: Simulation of subtropical courtyard microclimate evolution and optimization algorithm for landscape design based on multi-source remote sensing data fusion
abstract: Subtropical courtyards temper heat and admit light, yet their thermal performance has been hard to quantify at a scale fine enough to guide design. This study builds an end-to-end pipeline, resting on freely distributed satellite products and open code, that fuses multi-source remote sensing, simulates courtyard microclimate evolution, and optimises landscape configuration; it is applied to twenty-four courtyards in Guangzhou, southern China, a humid subtropical (Köppen Cfa) city, observed between 2021 and 2024. title: Modeling the Distribution of the Invasive Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) in the Wetlands of Côte d'Ivoire
abstract: Eichhornia crassipes (water hyacinth) is one of the world’s most invasive aquatic plants, causing severe ecological and socio-economic impacts in freshwater ecosystems, including those of Côte d’Ivoire. This study aimed to assess the current and future distribution of E. crassipes in the wetlands of Côte d’Ivoire. Species occurrence data were compiled, and future distribution projections were generated under two Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs): SSP2-4.5 (intermediate stabilization scenario) and SSP5-8.5 (high greenhouse gas emission scenario) for the 2050 and 2070 time horizons. journal: International Journal of Current Science Research and Review

title: Evaluating the Loss of Indigenous Knowledge and Local Traditions in the Technical World: A PRISMA-ScR-Guided Scoping Review and Comparative Analysis
abstract: Background: Indigenous and local knowledge systems encode centuries of accumulated observation about ecosystems, medicine, food, language, social organisation and ethics. Their erosion under conditions of technological modernity is widely asserted, yet the evidence for it is scattered across ecology, linguistics, anthropology, health sciences, education and digital studies, and is rarely examined as a single analytical problem. title: Comorbidities with Melioidosis in Indian context: A scoping review
abstract: Background and objectives Published literature from endemic countries such as Thailand and Australia identifies diabetes mellitus, alcoholism and chronic kidney disease as primary pre-existing factors for melioidosis. India, often referred as the global diabetic capital, has the predicted highest burden of melioidosis, yet well-designed prospective studies to analyse these risks remain limited. We conducted this scoping review to map the available Indian evidence on comorbidity patterns in melioidosis. title: Spatial Variability in and Geostatistical Mapping of Soil Organic Carbon Stocks Under Contrasting Land Uses in Foumbot, Western Cameroon
abstract: Accurate assessment of soil organic carbon (SOC) distribution is essential for carbon accounting and sustainable land management, yet spatial information remains limited in Central African landscapes. This study evaluated SOC stocks across cropland, grassland, and forest ecosystems in the Foumbot agricultural basin, western Cameroon, at depths of 0–10 and 10–20 cm. Spatial dependence was assessed using semivariograms, while a two-step, land use-based residual interpolation framework was applied. title: Pre-Service Teachers’ Metaphorical Perceptions of the “Faculty of Education Concept”
abstract: This study aimed to determine the metaphorical perceptions of pre-service teachers participating in the pedagogical formation certificate program regarding the concept of the faculty of education using a basic qualitative research design based on metaphor analysis, with a study group of 363 pre-service teachers. title: Automated determination of ground control points for base map production using UAV photogrammetry and Google Earth Engine
abstract: Context—Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry provides high-resolution spatial data for a wide range of mapping applications. However, the appropriate planning and spatial distribution of Ground Control Points (GCPs) and Check Points (CPs) remain critical for achieving reliable photogrammetric results. title: Orthounimodal Distributionally Robust Optimization: Representation, Computation, and Multivariate Extreme Event Applications
abstract: This paper studies a basic notion of distributional shape known as orthounimodality (OU) and its use in shape-constrained distributionally robust optimization (DRO). As a key motivation, we argue how such type of DRO is well suited to tackle multivariate extreme event estimation by giving statistically valid confidence bounds on target extremal probabilities. title: Effect of a biogenic diatomite-based combined fertilizer on spring barley yield and its potential for functional food production
abstract: Background: Biogenic diatomite rocks are widely distributed in the Republic of Armenia and contain amorphous silicon dioxide, apatite, quartz, siderite, goethite, montmorillonite, and other minerals. To increase the availability of the nutrients present in the rock to plants, the material was subjected to acid treatment. title: Biodiversity Risk and Corporate Credit Ratings
abstract: We examine the relation between firm‐level biodiversity risk and corporate credit ratings. We find that firms exposed to biodiversity risk receive significantly lower credit ratings, by approximately 0.9 notches relative to unexposed firms in the same industry. This relation remains robust after accounting for local economic conditions, alternative dimensions of climate‐related risk, firms’ broader environmental and social performance, and firm‐level regulatory intensity, as well as across a range of additional robustness and identification tests. title: First record of Pipunculidae (Diptera) from Uruguay
abstract: Pipunculidae (Diptera) is recorded from Uruguay for the first time. The family is represented in this country by three genera and six species: Clistoabdominalis spinitibialis (Hardy, 1954), Eudorylas spinosus (Hardy, 1948), Tomosvaryella aurata Ale-Rocha, 1996, Tomosvaryella curta Ale-Rocha, 1996, Tomosvaryella longiseta Ale-Rocha, 1996, and Tomosvaryella platensis Ale-Rocha, 1996.

title: Not regionally extinct: Rediscovery of the only European population of Utricularia subulata L. (Lentibulariaceae), in Central Portugal
abstract: Utricularia subulata L., a small annual carnivorous plant, historically known in Europe from only two localities in Central Portugal, was declared Regionally Extinct in 2020. In this paper, we report the rediscovery of U. subulata in Portugal, confirming its continued survival in the Western Palearctic. Morphological examination confirmed the identity and revealed variable spur morphology, supporting the synonymy of the previously described U. subulata var. tridenticulata with the type variety. title: Inteligencia artificial como herramienta pedagógica para la preservación de saberes ancestrales y la enseñanza de la literatura en la formación docente boliviana
abstract: La integración de inteligencia artificial (IA) en la formación docente abre posibilidades para la enseñanza de la literatura y la preservación del patrimonio cultural, pero también plantea desafíos sobre representación, sesgos lingüísticos y control comunitario del conocimiento. El objetivo de este artículo es analizar, mediante revisión documental, las contribuciones y limitaciones de la IA como herramienta pedagógica para recuperar saberes ancestrales y enriquecer las prácticas literarias en la formación docente boliviana. title: The Contribution of Flood Risk Assessments to Risk Management in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
abstract: Floods account for a substantial share of disaster damage, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite the Official Development Aid mobilised between 2000 and 2024 to address flooding in LMICs, damage has not decreased significantly. During this period, the number of flood risk assessments (FRAs) increased exponentially, particularly after 2018. However, literature reviews have paid little attention to this proliferation and the contribution of FRAs to risk management. This study examines the usability of FRAs for risk treatment in LMICs. title: Molecular Determinants of Contaminant Association with PET Nanoplastics Revealed by Atomistic Simulations
abstract: Chemical contaminants associated with nanoplastics can form environmentally pervasive, persistent complexes with potentially toxic effects. Yet, determining which contaminants are most likely to associate with nanoplastics and which molecular determinants govern this phenomenon remains challenging. Here, we used molecular dynamics (MD) to screen and compare the surface association of small-molecule contaminants with polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic particles (PET-NPPs). title: Analysis of Spatial Accessibility of Agritourism Units in Albania through Network Modeling in GIS and Graph Theory
abstract: Agritourism in Albania depends on how easily visitors can reach farms and rural guesthouses from the main cities. This paper measures that accessibility by combining network analysis in QGIS with graph theory. Road data from OpenStreetMap and the OpenRouteService plugin were used to calculate shortest routes, in distance and travel time, from Tirana, Shkodër, Vlorë and Korçë to every known agritourism unit. title: Rhodococcus–norovirus interactions: a hypothesis of affinity-driven viral release from bacterial exopolysaccharides
abstract: Recent findings have revealed that Rhodococcus species bind human norovirus (NoV) particles in clinical stool samples collected from pediatric gastroenteritis cases. This recurring association across independent samples suggests a potentially relevant biological interaction. The binding appears to be mediated by exopolysaccharides (EPSs), which are typically rich in fucose, galactose, and glucuronic acid residues and may structurally mimic histo-blood group antigens (HBGAs), the known cellular receptors for NoV. title: La formación del profesorado en Inteligencia Aritificial: Estudio descriptivo de uso, percepción de competencias y necesidades formativas
abstract: Este estudio analiza la percepción, el uso y las necesidades formativas del profesorado de la Comunidad de Madrid en relación con la inteligencia artificial (IA). Desde un enfoque cuantitativo descriptivo, exploratorio y correlacional, se aplicó un cuestionario en línea a docentes de Educación Infantil a Formación Profesional y se contrastaron ocho hipótesis. title: Los efectos del error algorítmico en la formación de contratos celebrados a través de plataformas digitales operadas por una de las partes
abstract: Este trabajo analiza los efectos del error algorítmico en la formación de contratos celebrados a través de plataformas digitales bajo el Derecho chileno. Sostiene que, pese a la ausencia de una regulación especial, las categorías disponibles permiten hacerse cargo de las consecuencias del funcionamiento defectuoso de un sistema no humano y distribuir sus riesgos conforme a criterios coherentes con los instrumentos de soft law sobre la materia. title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
abstract: Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. title: Biodiversity credit accounting in the Suiyang Administration Branch of Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park based on changes in flagship species habitat suitability
abstract: Introduction Quantifying changes in flagship species habitats and translating them into spatial management priorities are essential for improving conservation management in national parks. Methods This study focused on the Suiyang Administration Branch of the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park. title: Mechanistic insights into the biodegradation of the cobalt-complex azo dye Acid Red 182 by a defined bacterial consortium
abstract: Introduction Metal-complex azo dyes are persistent pollutants that resist conventional treatment. Acid Red 182 (AR182), a 1:2 cobalt-complex monoazo dye, has primarily been treated using physicochemical methods. abstract: The classical habitable-zone (HZ) criterion screens planets by radiative equilibrium alone and omits processes that decide whether a surface stays habitable over Gyr timescales: atmospheric retention (set by mass), climate stability (set by orbital eccentricity), atmospheric loss (driven by stellar activity) and temperature class (set by insolation flux S). title: Pulse-overlap-driven femtosecond laser-induced defect healing in oxygen-deficient amorphous Ga2O3 thin films
abstract: Amorphous Ga 2 O 3 is an ultrawide-bandgap oxide semiconductor combining solar-blind transparency, low-temperature deposition, and large-area processability. However, oxygen-vacancy-related states promote sub-bandgap absorption and non-radiative recombination, compromising the solar-blind selectivity and optical performance of amorphous Ga 2 O 3 films. title: Association of valgus knee alignment with hallux valgus in individuals with knee osteoarthritis in the population based ROAD study
abstract: Hallux valgus (HV) and hallux rigidus (HR) are common forefoot deformities, but their relationships with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and coronal knee alignment remain incompletely understood. This study examined associations between knee alignment, KOA, and the prevalence of HV and HR in a population-based cohort. Data were obtained from the fifth survey of the Research on Osteoarthritis/Osteoporosis Against Disability (ROAD) cohort in Japan. After exclusions, 3,582 knees and feet were analyzed. title: FRUGAL INNOVATIONS AS A PATHWAY TO INCLUSIVE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT ENTREPRENEURSHIP
abstract: This paper examines frugal innovation as a pathway to inclusive and resource-efficient entrepreneurship in widening economies. Building on a structured literature review, the study conceptualises frugal innovation within sustainability and innovation ecosystem perspectives and empirically tests key relationships using survey data from universities/technology transfer offices and start-ups.The results show that only selected mechanisms are statistically supported. title: Del telégrafo a los algoritmos: tecnología en la administración pública de México
abstract: Este artículo es un recorrido por la historia de la relación entre tecnología y gobierno en México, desde los primeros telégrafos del siglo XIX hasta la irrupción actual de la inteligencia artificial generativa (iagen). Examinamos cómo cada innovación tecnológica modificó las formas de gobernar, comunicarse y tomar decisiones dentro del sector público. title: LA DIDÁCTICA DE LA EDUCACIÓN ARTÍSTICA DESDE EL USO DE LA IA
abstract: La didáctica de la educación artística desde el uso de la inteligencia artificial constituye un campo de transformación pedagógica que invita a reconsiderar las formas tradicionales de enseñar, aprender y construir experiencias creativas en los escenarios educativos contemporáneos. title: A Relational and Spiritual Approach to Islamic Religious Education Supervision: A Case Study of Teachers’ Personality Competence at MTs Negeri 1 Sanana
abstract: This study describes Islamic Religious Education (PAI) supervision that combines professional guidance with relational engagement and spiritual encouragement at MTs Negeri 1 Sanana, Sula Islands Regency, Indonesia. It employs a qualitative case-study design and draws on four informants: one PAI supervisor (Informant 1), the madrasah principal (Informant 4), an experienced PAI teacher (Informant 6), and a junior government-contract (PPPK) teacher (Informant 8). title: Path Planning and Adaptive Controller Development for Ship-To-Ship Guided Missiles
abstract: This study presents an integrated guidance, control, and trajectory planning architecture for a ship-to-ship guided missile designed to counter actively maneuvering enemy surface combatants. A high-speed guided missile is modeled with nonlinear six-degrees-of-freedom (6-DoF) dynamics, while the target performs evasive maneuvers. The target’s velocity is estimated via a Kalman filter and used to generate a dynamically updated reference trajectory. title: Reproductive biology of Tyto furcata (American Barn Owl) in Puerto Rico
abstract: Tyto furcata (American Barn Owl) is a widespread species present in many of the West Indies, though its status on the island of Puerto Rico is not well understood. Here we present the first detailed records of nest sites, brood size, and nest fate of Tyto furcata nesting in the island between 2018 and 2024. We documented thirteen nesting attempts at Hacienda La Esperanza Nature Reserve in the municipality of Manatí, and located two additional nests following reported fledgling sightings in Juana Díaz on the south coast west of the Descalabrado River and in Camuy in the north-west. title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
abstract: Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. title: Apropiación docente de inteligencia artificial generativa: revisión bibliográfica de microcredenciales, mentoría y sostenibilidad pedagógica
abstract: La introducción de la inteligencia artificial generativa en el ámbito educativo representa una serie de retos que requieren algo más que una utilización instrumental de las herramientas. En este trabajo se analiza la literatura vinculada a la apropiación del profesorado, la competencia digital, la integración pedagógica, la ética, las microcredenciales, la tutoría reflexiva y la transferencia de la enseñanza a la práctica educativa, prestando especial atención a la educación media superior tecnológico. title: Lexical Text Modelling of Place Identity, Product Identifiers and Review Imaginaries: Pattern Analysis of Wine Quality Assessment in Rural Italy
abstract: Rural quality of life in specialised peripheral or non-urban territories depends not only on material conditions, but also on the symbolic and evaluative processes through which rural places become recognisable, credible, and valued in extra-local markets. This paper examines professional wine reviews as observative judgment infrastructures that translate territorial intangibles into market-readable signals, thereby shaping reputational opportunities in fragile rural economies. title: Child Development Workers’ Practices for Early Identification and Intervention of Children with Developmental Needs
abstract: This study explored child development workers’ practices for early identification and intervention for children with developmental needs, the challenges encountered, and how these challenges shaped their practices in Alburquerque, Bohol, Philippines. A qualitative narrative inquiry design involved nine purposively selected child development workers. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews and examined using William Labov’s narrative framework and inductive thematic analysis. journal: American Journal of Language, Literacy and Learning in STEM Education (2993-2769)

title: Bringing nature-based health prevention into cities: the role and perception of Green Care in Germany
abstract: Germany lags behind other European countries in implementing preventive health measures, particularly in nature on prescription (green prescribing) to support mental health, while countries such as the United Kingdom, have made substantial progress in implementing nature-based interventions. One promising approach is Green Care—ranging from everyday experiences in green and blue spaces to structured nature-based health promotion and therapy—which supports individual health, community wellbeing, and ecosystem restoration. abstract: Latar Belakang- Karakteristik petrofisika batuan reservoir merupakan aspek krusial dalam menentukan kapasitas penyimpanan dan kemampuan pengaliran fluida hidrokarbon. title: Greenwashing and Climate Change Concerns in the Sustainable Development Agenda: Definition, Communication Strategies and Underlying Reasons
abstract: In the tourism and hospitality industry, greenwashing related to the climate is leading to deceptive environmental communication. Mass media play a critical role in providing information and shaping public opinions. Hence, this calls for accountability for greenwashing and its impact on climate change. This study examines 230 online news articles and 50 videos using Gioia's approach to present a multi‐dimensional examination of greenwashing in the tourism and hospitality industry. title: Nested surrogate-based layout and size optimization of composite wingbox structures
abstract: Early-stage aircraft structural design choices strongly influence performance, yet preliminary sizing often relies on empirical methods which may be inaccurate for composite structures and unconventional layouts. This paper presents an automated surrogate-assisted framework for coupled layout and size optimization of composite wingbox structures, demonstrated in a low-dimensional case study. A nested approach optimizes the number of ribs, number of stringers, and spar-cap width in an outer loop, while component sizing is handled by a commercial gradient-based solver in an inner loop. title: A multi-variable threshold approach to landslide prediction: integrating rainfall, soil moisture, and soil texture in Indonesia
abstract: Landslides are one of the most devastating hazards globally, including in Indonesia. To reduce casualties, Indonesia has established the Blueprint of Indonesian Landslide Early Warning System (BILEWS). This system currently relies on rainfall-induced landslide thresholds for issuing the warning signals derived from historical landslide occurrences in Java, Sumatra, and Kalimantan Islands. title: The role of research in analyzing the resilience of critical power infrastructures in blackout scenarios: implications for energy, national, and global security
abstract: Blackouts represent some of the most severe forms of disruption to the operation of modern energy systems, with cascading effects on industry, the economy, public health, communications and information systems, transportation, social order, security, and national well-being. In the context of the energy transition, accelerated digitalization, and the growing interdependence among critical infrastructures, the analysis of energy system resilience is becoming a strategic priority. title: Integración de las TIC en la educación superior: innovación pedagógica, transformación digital y desafíos contemporáneos
abstract: Introduction: The integration of information and communication technologies (ICT) is transforming university environments, yet their presence does not guarantee innovation or improved learning. Objective: To examine the conceptual foundations, pedagogical trends and challenges associated with ICT integration in university teaching and learning. Methodology: A narrative review of academic literature and institutional documents is presented, organised around conceptual, pedagogical and management themes, with critical analysis of theoretical and empirical contributions. title: Sistem Rekomendasi Toko Belanja Daring Berbobot Ditentukan Pengguna dengan Simple Additive Weighting
abstract: Sistem pendukung keputusan (SPK) untuk memilih toko belanja daring umumnya memakai satu set bobot kriteria yang sama bagi semua pengguna, sehingga prioritas pribadi pembeli tidak terwakili. Penelitian ini membangun SPK berbasis web yang menempatkan penentuan bobot pada tangan pengguna dan memakai metode Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) sebagai mesin perhitungan. Sistem dibangun dengan PHP 8.2, kerangka kerja Laravel 12, dan basis data SQLite, dengan logika SAW dipisahkan ke dalam kelas layanan tersendiri agar dapat diuji terpisah dari antarmuka. abstract: Sustainability education requires learners to develop knowledge, values, competencies and action-oriented behaviors, yet existing instruments capture only parts of this construct knowledge in the Sulitest and Assessment of Sustainability Knowledge; consciousness and attitudes in the Sustainability Consciousness Questionnaire and Attitudes toward Sustainable Development scale, rely largely on school-age or Western samples, and offer limited confirmatory evidence of their structure. title: Mitigating water deficit stress in wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) through foliar application of humic acid, fulvic acid, and amino acids during critical growth stages
abstract: Wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) is one of the most important cereal crops and a staple food worldwide. This study evaluated the effects of foliar applications of humic acid, fulvic acid, and amino acids under well‐watered and water‐deficit conditions at three key growth stages on grain yield of the Taktaz wheat cultivar over two consecutive growing seasons. title: FUNCTIONAL MISALIGNMENT OF SECONDARY EDUCATION AUTHORITY IN INDONESIA’S 3T (FRONTIER, OUTERMOST, AND UNDERDEVELOPED) ARCHIPELAGIC REGIONS: A LEGAL AND GOVERNANCE ANALYSIS OF THE TANIMBAR ISLANDS REGENCY
abstract: Background Law Number 23 of 2014 on Regional Government transferred the management of secondary education from district/city governments to provincial governments to standardize services and improve administrative efficiency. In frontier, outermost, and underdeveloped (3T) archipelagic regions, however, the transfer has weakened institutional responsiveness, lengthened administrative chains, and widened educational inequalities. title: Personality without a person: measuring personality in generative AI
abstract: Personality describes relatively stable styles of thinking, feeling, and acting when interacting with the physical and social environment. The stability and reliability of these individual styles plays an important role in our daily lives as we team with various individuals at work and home. Generative AI agents (LLMs) are new additions to our lives, quickly assuming roles that might otherwise have been given to humans though there is little known about the stability and reliability of LLM “thinking” styles or actions. title: ‘When you keep having sleepless nights and suicidal thoughts … ' understanding the mental health impacts of climate change on smallholder farmers in Ghana
abstract: Climate change poses significant risks to the livelihoods and well-being of smallholder farmers, particularly in vulnerable regions such as Ghana. While earlier studies in northern Ghana have explored farmers’ coping strategies and some of the emotional and socio-economic effects of climate-related challenges, less attention has been paid to how climate change risks interact with financial stress and coping mechanisms to influence farmers’ mental health in dryland farming systems. abstract: Introduction To address the lack of collaborative optimization of structural parameters and dynamic responses in a four-finger cable-driven sorting robot, a structural parameter optimization model based on dynamic modeling and the Genghis Khan shark algorithm is proposed. title: La iagogía, una puesta en escena para la personalización en la educación
abstract: El estudio explora la adopción y el valor pedagógico percibido de la IA en educación superior desde estudiantes. En una universidad latinoamericana se aplicó un cuestionario sobre uso, beneficios y tensiones. Se halló alta adopción (94%) y una valoración centrada en la personalización: 81,5% destaca la adaptación del contenido al ritmo y 51,9% la retroalimentación inmediata. abstract: The Fourier Transform Optimizer (FTO) provides a frequency-domain search framework for metaheuristic optimization, but its original spectral operations do not explicitly consider spectral-energy distribution, amplitude–phase-aware information exchange, or multi-resolution spectral manipulation. title: Prevalence of low back pain and associated individual and occupational factors among nurses in Sakaka, Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Low back pain (LBP) is a major public health concern in occupational settings, and nursing practice frequently involves demanding physical tasks that are widely reported to be associated with LBP risks. Regional insights about the burden of LBP and associated factors shall provide evidence to overcome global variations and thereby reduce intervention policy uncertainty. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of work-related LBP and identify factors associated with LBP among nurses working in public hospitals in Saudi Arabia. title: Safety assessment of biological preparations used for bioremediation of water reservoirs: A laboratory study on common carp ( Cyprinus carpio )
abstract: The use of biological preparations for water quality management and bioremediation has become increasingly prevalent. However, despite their widespread application, comprehensive safety data regarding their physiological impact on non-target aquatic organisms remains scarce. This study evaluated the safety of three commercial biological preparations (ACS AQUAQULTURE 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0) for common carp ( Cyprinus carpio ), a key bioindicator and economically vital species. abstract: Introduction Sarcoglycanopathies comprise a subgroup of four muscular dystrophies characterized by progressive muscle weakness and reduced life expectancy. A major challenge in studying these disorders is the broad heterogeneity observed among patients but also among muscles within the same individual. The biological basis of this heterogeneity remains largely unknown. title: The Use of Coconut Fiber as an Echo Absorbing Material in Green Technology-Based Building Renovation (Case Study of Dome Smesco Jakarta)
abstract: The application of green technology in sustainable building renovation requires environmentally friendly materials that provide effective technical performance while enhancing indoor environmental quality and occupant comfort. One of the primary challenges in public buildings is maintaining appropriate room acoustics, particularly by controlling excessive reverberation and improving speech intelligibility. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of coconut coir fiber (cocofiber) as a natural sound-absorbing material in reducing reverberation time and improving perceived acoustic comfort

title: Bacteriophages as indicators of viral risk along the water–food chain: from regulatory uptake to mitigation
abstract: Enteric viruses enter the food chain through water used for drinking, irrigation, and shellfish production. Routine control, however, relies on fecal indicator bacteria, which do not accurately reflect viral persistence and removal. Bacteriophages that infect enteric bacteria share key properties with enteric viruses and have moved from research tools to regulatory parameters. abstract: In magnetically confined nuclear fusion, the achievement of ignition necessitates the tokamak plasma in a high confinement state known as H-mode. A major challenge encountered in the standard H-mode is the abrupt collapse of its ultrathin edge layer. title: Characterisation and assessment of virulence pattern of Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae causing bacterial leaf blight of rice
abstract: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB), caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo), poses a serious threat to rice production in irrigated and lowland ecosystems. During the 2024–25 cropping seasons, a purposive roving survey was conducted across 25 major rice-growing locations in Tamil Nadu (10) Andhra Pradesh (9), Karnataka (3), Kerala (2) and Telangana (1). abstract: Background: National commodity availability can vary differently from domestic production and processed dietary indicators. This descriptive ecological time-series study distinguishes short-term volatility from whole-period dispersion and avoids causal claims. title: Building Disaster Logistics Resilience: Risk Analysis and Development Strategies for the Emergency Logistics Cluster in West Sumatra Province
abstract: Disaster logistics is a critical determinant of effective disaster management, as it ensures the timely, accurate, and coordinated availability, mobilization, and distribution of relief supplies. The complexity of disaster risks in West Sumatra Province, coupled with the substantial need for cross-sectoral coordination, necessitates the development of a more resilient logistics system through the establishment of a Disaster Logistics Cluster. title: Geopolitical tensions and the “New Cold War” in the twenty-first century
abstract: This scholarly article examines the geopolitical tensions that have intensified globally during the first quarter of the twenty-first century and comprehensively analyzes the trends of global confrontation commonly characterized in academic literature as the “New Cold War.” The principal objective of the study is to identify the functional similarities and differences between the bipolar world order that emerged after the Second World War and the contemporary forms of multipolar, geoeconomic, military, and technological competition. abstract: Impact craters are prominent lunar landforms that record impact conditions and subsequent geological modification. abstract: Background Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) is a major etiological agent of dental caries, and pronounced heterogeneity in cariogenic phenotypes exists among different strains. abstract: Despite extensive military operations that weakened the operational capabilities of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and reduced terrorist violence after 2014, the organisation re-emerged as a formidable security threat following the Afghan Taliban’s return to power in 2021. The existing literature has largely focused on external factors, particularly the developments in Afghanistan. abstract: Background: Online consumers assess financial benefits alongside shopping experiences and social considerations as they develop confidence in platforms and sellers. Objective: The study investigates associations between three value dimensions (Economic, Experiential, and Social Value) and trust in platforms and sellers, as well as the links of these two trust constructs with Customer Engagement in Indonesian online commerce. abstract: The silver economy addresses the problems of an ageing population and the associated changes in the economy, social, health and labour market sectors. An ageing population leads to labour shortages and slowing economic growth, pressure on pension and health systems, and deepening poverty and social exclusion. abstract: Climate change is increasingly framed as a driver of human migration, yet migration is not a universal response to climate stress. Many individuals and households remain in place despite climatic, economic, and social risks, raising important questions about why people stay, under what conditions, and with what consequences. This paper undertakes an exploratory review of the literature on human immobility in the context of climate change. abstract: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. This study evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of producing chitosan from Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) shell waste through a conventional chemical extraction process. abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) airborne gravimetry offers high operational flexibility at relatively low cost, making it an important means of rapidly acquiring regional gravity field information. However, the achievable accuracy of UAV airborne gravimetry remains limited by both the accuracy of the navigation solution and the design of the signal processing scheme. title: Designing a next-generation Chikungunya virus vaccine through integrated immunoinformatics and computational approaches
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a mosquito-borne alphavirus that can cause fever, severe joint pain and neurological complications. Although vaccines against CHIKV are available in some regions there is still a need for additional vaccine strategies. In this study we used a computational immunoinformatic approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate from the CHIKV structural polyprotein. title: Environmental drivers of microbial community dynamics in a cool-water aquaponics system
abstract: Aquaponic systems represent an integrated water-efficient approach to food production by combining recirculating aquaculture with hydroponic plant cultivation. Performance and stability of these systems depend not only on fish and plant interactions but also on the structure and function of associated microbial communities, which regulate nutrient cycling and water quality. Microbial communities play a central role in the stability and performance of aquaponic systems, yet the relative importance of temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and environmental drivers remains poorly understood.

abstract: This study investigates how NEOM's official English-language discourse constructs the image of the future city and contributes to Saudi Arabia's nation-branding objectives within the context of Vision 2030. abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound yet understudied impact on energy poverty and clean energy transition among households. Using at least 6000 and up to 12,000 household longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies from 2014 through 2022, this study implements multiple empirical strategies to assess these effects on urban and rural Chinese households. abstract: Dynamic control of molecular transport remains a central challenge in membrane science, because most conventional membranes rely on fixed pore architectures or bulk stimuli such as pH and temperature. Electrotunable membranes offer more direct, programmable electronic control of transport properties. Here, we present electrochemical osmotic (ECO) actuator membranes based on cellulose nanofibril (CNF)-carbon nanotube (CNT) nanocomposites. abstract: This study aims to analyze the development of Cost Recovery Rate (CRR) research on BPJS inpatient services through a systematic literature review approach combined with bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer. title: Integrated spatial decision support system for prioritizing sewer system rehabilitation
abstract: Sewer networks are essential for public health and environmental protection in urban areas, but they are deteriorating due to age, poor maintenance, and population growth. These deteriorations require repair or rehabilitation, but limited budgets force utility managers to prioritize projects. abstract: Southwest China supports a relatively high diversity of freshwater mussels compared to other regions of the country. In this study, a new species, Inversidens haiting Dai & Chen, sp. nov ., from the Longjiang River in Guangxi, is described based on comparative morphology and molecular phylogenetics. abstract: This article examines the role and importance of problem-based learning technology in developing students' critical and logical thinking skills within the modern educational system. It highlights ways to create problematic situations in the educational process, encourage students to conduct independent research, form an analytical approach, and enhance their learning activity. Furthermore, the article analyzes practical methods and pedagogical conditions for implementing elements of problem-based learning into the classroom.

abstract: The Bien Hoa to Vung Tau Expressway is a 53-kilometre route in southern Vietnam connecting the industrial base of Dong Nai to the deep-water port area of Vung Tau, with an estimated investment of 17.8 trillion VND. Economic forecasts for the project were prepared before 2018, and the regional context has changed substantially since then. abstract: The coordination of various stakeholders constitutes a critical component of tourism destination management. This study analyzes the relational structure of tourism stakeholders in the province of Pichincha, Ecuador. The study integrates two levels of observation: territorial networks constructed through interviews and digital relationships recorded on X. The study employed a convergent mixed-method design. abstract: The transition to renewable energy technologies (RETs) is essential for achieving Malaysia’s sustainable development and carbon-reduction goals. Despite various national initiatives, adoption rates in rural communities remain modest. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated behavioural framework that combines the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to explain intentions to adopt renewable energy in rural Terengganu, Malaysia. title: Hydrological and hydraulic modelling for flood control planning in the Mokwa watershed, Nigeria
abstract: Flooding is a recurrent hazard in many data-scarce African watersheds, where limited stream-gauge information constrains event reconstruction and flood-control planning. This study developed an integrated GIS-HEC-HMS-HEC-RAS workflow to characterize the May 2025 flood response of the Mokwa watershed, Niger State, Nigeria. abstract: El data art en X representa una forma híbrida de comunicación que integra datos, estética y narrativa visual, generando debates sobre su legitimidad informativa. Este estudio analiza la percepción del data art mediante análisis temático de conversaciones textuales en X, identificando patrones de opinión y controversias. title: Potential assessment of rooftop photovoltaic in global cities considering economic feasibility
abstract: Rooftop Photovoltaics (RPV) serve as a promising distributed form of clean solar energy utilization, especially in highly dense urban areas. However, the global variation in the economic potential of RPV remains unknown. Here, we integrate the 3D building footprints and electricity demand to assess both the technical and economic potential of RPV at the global scale. The results show that the global technical potential of RPV in urban areas reaches 4048 TWh·yr − 1 , but the economic potential accounts for only 41.8% of the technical potential. abstract: Attribution of climate change to anthropogenic forcing is an important goal in climate science. Regression of local conditions on global temperatures is a popular statistical approach, but whether the uncertainty derived from observations alone can reflect the range of outcomes possible due to internal variability remains unclear. abstract: This study assessed tourists’ perceptions of tourism sites in Siargao Island, Surigao del Norte, Philippines, focusing on tourist attractions, facilities and amenities, accessibility, environmental condition, and service quality, and examined differences across demographic characteristics. abstract: This article examines why and how peasant farmers participate in non-agricultural market exchanges, and the conditions that enable them to do so. abstract: Decarbonizing the maritime industry through shore-to-ship power (cold-ironing) requires robust transactive energy systems. abstract: The development of the Nusantara Capital City (IKN) in Indonesia has spurred economic transformation amidst environmental pressures arising from changes in land use, industrial activity and infrastructure expansion in the surrounding areas. These challenges underscore the crucial importance of environmental management, not only as a consequence of development, but also as a strategic pillar that influences how regional economic activities contribute to the well-being of the community. abstract: Plastics are ubiquitous, and their performance depends on phosphate ester additives used as plasticizers and flame retardants. abstract: Small wetlands are increasingly recognized for their ecological and socio-economic importance, yet their conservation has received less attention than that of large wetlands. Despite growing international discussions, research emphasis, and policy instruments targeting small wetlands remain uneven across regions. abstract: Christian anthropology offers a vision of existence that is metaphysically defensible and deeply attractive. abstract: Static inspection programmes may apply uniform inspection intervals across heterogeneous asset populations, whereas risk-based inspection (RBI) seeks to differentiate inspection priorities according to assessed risk. abstract: Welded joints are critical regions in steel structures where complex microstructures can reduce local ductility and fracture resistance. abstract: Participatory conceptual mapping is widely used in sustainability research to represent stakeholders’ knowledge, concerns, and perceptions of causal relationships within complex social-ecological systems. abstract: Wildfire smoke causes extreme fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) pollution in North America. abstract: Active layer thickness (ALT) is a key indicator of permafrost change, with important implications for soil hydrothermal conditions, carbon feedbacks, ecosystem processes, and cold-region infrastructure. title: Projective Affine Body Dynamics for Multibody Systems
abstract: Multibody systems have widespread applications in diverse fields such as robotics, entertainment, and animation. Their capability to model and simulate intricate interactions among interconnected bodies makes them invaluable in various domains. However, complexity arises with factors like non‐smooth contact handling, nonlinearity in flexible joints, and parallelization challenges. title: Enhancing small-scale target inversion in acoustic full-waveform inversion using an embedded-scattering-point staining algorithm
abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) recovers high-resolution velocity models by iteratively minimizing the misfit between observed and modeled data, but its gradient is computed in the same way as reverse-time migration (RTM) and therefore inherits RTM’s sensitivity to illumination. institutions: China University of Petroleum, East China

title: Mesh‐Free Simulation of Granular Flows by the Improved Explicit Incompressible Moving Particle Method
abstract: This study proposed numerical techniques in the mesh‐free Moving Particle Semi‐implicit (MPS) method to improve pressure field calculation in granular flows. The Explicit Incompressible scheme in the MPS (EI‐MPS) method is employed to solve the pressure Poisson equation, and a re‐corrector time step is further incorporated to update the pressure field. The improved EI‐MPS method is used to simulate granular column collapses, the collision of two granular columns, and a sand impact flow. journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids

title: Impact of Environmental Degradation, Renewable Energy Consumption and Globalization on Green Growth: An Analysis from Asian Countries
abstract: Nations of the world make effort to protect ecologically sustainability to enhance economic growth (GDPg). The improved green technology is obligatory to lessen environmental degradation (CO2) and nurturing green growth. The existing research examines the factors influencing green growth (GRGDP) by utilising data from 1997 to 2024 in Asian countries. For this purpose, green growth index was used as dependent variable. Though, CO2 emission, renewable energy use, globalization and gini index were used as independent variables. Data were drawn from nine Asian countries for the analysis. Regressio

title: STRATEGIES FOR THE SYNERGISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF UNIVERSITY GOVERNANCE SYSTEMS AND STUDENTS’ SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL COMPETENCIES BASED ON MULTIMODAL LEARNING ANALYSIS
abstract: Against the backdrop of higher education governance shifting from “hierarchical control” to “networked co-governance,” students’ social-emotional competencies (SEC) are no longer merely individual psychological variables but have become a core indicator for measuring governance resilience. This paper proposes an “emotion–governance” coupling analysis framework. title: Iterative optimization with partial convergence guarantees on neutral atom quantum computers
abstract: Neutral atom quantum computers (NAQCs) have emerged as a promising platform for solving the maximum weighted independent set (MWIS) problem. However, analog quantum approaches face two key limitations: Constraints of the atomic layout on realizable graph geometries and the absence of performance guarantees. We introduce , a hybrid quantum-classical framework that integrates an NAQC sampler into a classical cutting-plane algorithm. At each iteration, a relaxed linear program (RLP) bounds the MWIS and induces a reduced graph from which independent sets are sampled using an analog quantum sampler

title: Ozone and Thermal Comfort Responses in Signature Urban Microenvironments under Non-typical Weather
abstract: Urban street microenvironments exhibit pronounced heterogeneity in both physical morphology and anthropogenic activity, but ozone pollution and heat stress during non-typical meteorological periods remain poorly understood in these microenvironments. To address this research gap, this study focused on the representativeness of thermal environment and pollution effects, for which two contrasting microenvironments were selected: (Ⅰ) an “urban desertification” area dominated by impervious surfaces, and (Ⅱ) a “traffic-dining” composite pollution belt. Using KZ filtering, regression, and GAM, we fo
institutions: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, Zhongshan Institute
Changsha University of Science and Technology

title: Cytotoxic Effect of Green-Synthesized Chitosan Nanoparticles (CS-NP) using Chenopodium quinoa Willd. Extract Against Lung Cancer Cells
abstract: The synthesis of plant-derived nanoparticles, in particular, constitutes a unique and promising field and is attracting significant interest due to its expanding applications in the healthcare sector. In our study, chitosan nanoparticles (Cs-NPs) were biologically synthesized and characterized using C. quinoa Willd. extract. The synthesized Cs-NPs were characterized by UV-Vis, ZETA, SEM, XRD, and FT-IR analyses. An analysis of the characterization results revealed that the Cs-NPs exhibit a light absorption peak at 250 nm, a surface charge of 22.2 mV, and an average size of approximately 52 nm.

title: βtubulin>GCaMP6s and βtubulin>H2B-GCaMP6s-T2A-mCherry enable pan-neuronal Ca2+imaging and more accurate measuring neural activity in Ciona robusta
abstract: The βtubulin promoter of Ciona robusta has been widely used as a pan-neuronal marker, but it has rarely been applied to imaging neural activity itself.In this study, two Ca 2+ imaging constructs were developed using this promoter: βtubulin>GCaMP6s and βtubulin>H2B-GCaMP6s-T2A-mCherry.Larvae carrying the former showed fluorescence throughout the nervous system, while in the latter, GCaMP6s was co-expressed in the nucleus and mCherry in the somata, enabling ratiometric correction using mCherry as a calcium-independent reference signal.With both constructs, the excitation of neurons could be visu

title: Probable Subacute Thyroiditis Mimicking Levothyroxine Over-Replacement in an Older Woman With Long-Standing Hypothyroidism: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Subacute thyroiditis is rarely described in people already taking levothyroxine, in whom its thyrotoxic phase can mimic over-replacement. A woman in her 70s with primary hypothyroidism of about 15 years' duration and undetermined cause was taking levothyroxine 50 μg daily. A week after a febrile sore throat, she developed anterior neck pain, which a general practitioner treated as a viral illness with analgesics and antibiotics. Palpitations and tremor followed four days later. On presentation, her thyroid was markedly tender. Tests showed thyrotoxicosis with a suppressed thyroid-stimulating h
institutions: All India Institute of Medical Sciences Bhubaneswar
Institute of Medical Sciences and Sum Hospital

title: Dynamic splitting tensile behavior and failure mechanism of hooked-end steel fiber-reinforced rubberized concrete
abstract: Rubberized concrete (RC) has attracted increasing attention owing to its favorable deformability and energy absorption capacity. Introducing hooked-end steel fibers (SF) into RC can enhance its mechanical performance through crack-bridging and end-anchorage mechanisms. This study investigated hooked-end steel fiber-reinforced rubberized concrete (SFRC) with a fixed 10% rubber replacement ratio and 0%–2.0% SF through quasi-static and dynamic splitting tensile tests. Dynamic tests used a split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) combined with digital image correlation (DIC) at strain rates of 3.22–10.

title: On the calibration and monitoring of dual-polarization radar receivers operating at C-band using solar flux reference at S-band
abstract: The solar radio noise accurately measured by terrestrial solar observatories has been proved to be an effective reference for checking the quality of dual-polarization weather radar receivers. The longest, most complete and accurate record of solar spectral irradiance (“flux”, for the sake of brevity) values exists thanks to the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) of the National Research Council (NRC) of Canada, located in British Columbia. institutions: Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology MeteoSwiss

title: Differentiated responses of ecosystem service supply and demand to urbanization across urban–rural gradients: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: Urbanization is closely associated with changes in ecosystem services, but how the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand vary along urban–rural gradients remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand across urban–rural gradients and to provide evidence for landscape planning and sustainable management in rapidly urbanizing regions. We assessed the supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios of four ecosystem services—water yield, carbon sequestration, habitat qualit

title: Brain Circulation, Brain Drain, Diaspora, and Skilled Migration: A Bibliometric Analysis 2006–2026
abstract: The aim of this bibliometric analysis is to examine the scholarly landscape of brain circulation, brain drain, diaspora and skilled migration from 2006 to 2026 based on the intertextual connections present in the literature. The techniques selected for this bibliometric analysis were performance analysis and scientific mapping. Using a seven-stage procedure and the Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases, a total of 759 research articles were analysed to identify the most relevant authors, keywords, and connections amongst scholarly works within this field. title: Integrated flood risk and transport-network resilience in Baghdad using an EHCR–TOPSIS framework
abstract: This study presents an integrated geospatial framework for prioritizing flood risk across Baghdad’s urban road network. The framework combines four dimensions—Exposure (E), Hazard (H), Criticality (C), and Redundancy (R)—using the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). The indicators were derived from widely available datasets, including the SRTM DEM, Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 imagery, CHIRPS precipitation, hydrographic data, and OpenStreetMap roads. At the road-segment level, they describe proximity to flood-prone hydrogeomorphic settings, terrain and hydro

title: WDQAR: a weighted double Q-learning based adaptive routing protocol for flying ad hoc networks
abstract: Reliable routing in flying ad hoc networks (FANETs) faces challenges such as frequent topology changes and unstable links, which are caused by the rapid mobility of UAVs. Existing Q-learning-based protocols still suffer from biased Q-value estimation, slow convergence, and high control overhead. This paper proposes WDQAR, an adaptive routing protocol based on weighted double Q-learning. WDQAR consists of two stages: neighbor discovery and routing. In the neighbor discovery phase, each UAV dynamically adjusts the HELLO message broadcast interval based on link duration and speed, promptly percei

title: Enhanced Congo Red adsorption by chitosan graft polyacrylamide hydrogel incorporating diatomite supported Fe–Ni layered double hydroxide
abstract: This research aimed to enhance the adsorptive properties of chitosan-grafted-polyacrylamide Poly(AAM) copolymeric hydrogels through the incorporation of Fe–Ni layered double hydroxide (LDH)-loaded diatomite. The synthesized adsorbents were characterized using various analytical techniques, including BET, FTIR, XRD, SEM–EDS, and elemental mapping. The results confirmed the successful immobilization of diatomite–LDH within the hydrogel network. Furthermore, BET analysis revealed enhanced porosity of the composites after modification. The adsorption performance of the prepared adsorbents was asse

title: La liquidación del siniestro en el reaseguro a la luz de los Principles of Reinsurance Contract Law (PRICL): riesgo decisorio y gobernanza contractual
abstract: La liquidación del siniestro constituye uno de los ámbitos más relevantes y, al mismo tiempo, menos sistematizados del contrato de reaseguro desde el punto de vista jurídico. Este artículo examina su tratamiento a la luz de los Principles of Reinsurance Contract Law (PRICL), instrumento de soft law de UNIDROIT, proponiendo la categoría del riesgo decisorio como criterio para reconstruir la asignación de responsabilidades entre asegurador directo y reasegurador ante la ausencia de un marco normativo específico. En este contexto, se analiza el alcance de la cláusula follow the settlements, el tr

title: Thickness‐Confined Mo‐VO 2 /CNTs Heterogeneous Composite Films for Synergistic Dynamic Infrared Camouflage and Electromagnetic Protection
abstract: As a typical phase‐change material for adaptive infrared (IR) camouflage, the development of VO 2 is constrained by its inherent “extreme‐emissivity trap”, with modulation limited to a narrow range of 0.9–0.65, and suffers from intrinsically low free‐electron density that precludes coinstantaneous electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding. Here, a multi‐modulation strategy via thickness‐confined Mo‐VO 2 /CNTs composite films is adopted to resolve these issues. title: Aligning trade and energy policies for sustainability in ASEAN: a regression discontinuity design with random forest-based inference
abstract: Reconciling trade liberalization with a low-carbon transition is a central policy challenge for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries. Rapid economic growth in the region has intensified reliance on fossil fuels, despite commitments to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 13 (Climate Action). However, the extent to which trade openness and energy mix composition jointly shape green economic performance remains empirically unresolved in the regional context. title: Experiments targeting EeV neutrinos
abstract: The detection of EeV neutrinos promises to identify the sources of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, thus motivating a wide range of experimental efforts for their detection. This review covers the current and near-future experimental landscape for neutrino observations in the EeV range. This includes concrete progress as well as conceptual introductions, highlighting the advantages of and challenges of each technology. title: Applying the Balanced Scorecard Framework for Strategic Performance Management in Nigerian University Libraries
abstract: University libraries play an important role in supporting teaching, leaZrning, and research in Nigerian university education. However, many continue to face challenges related to inadequate funding, technological limitations, changing user expectations, and weak performance measurement systems. Conventional approaches often emphasize inputs and outputs without adequately demonstrating the library's broader contribution to university goals. journal: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology

title: From forest edges to disciplinary boundaries: ecological patterns and structural analogy
abstract: Introduction Ecological boundaries separate habitats, whereas disciplinary boundaries can separate ways of understanding them. Whether empirical ecological patterns can provide a basis for structural analogy across disciplinary boundaries remains poorly understood. Methods We investigated soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities, enzyme activities, and soil fauna along edge-to-interior gradients at six forest sites spanning an urbanization gradient in Xiamen, China. title: Beyond keratinases: proteomic insights reveals potential oxidoreductase-mediated pathways involved in feather degradation mechanism by Streptomyces sp. G11C
abstract: Feather waste is an abundant keratin-rich byproduct generated by the poultry industry that represents an important environmental challenge due to the recalcitrant nature of keratin. Although keratinolytic microorganisms have emerged as promising biotechnological tools for feather valorization, the molecular mechanisms underlying bacterial keratin degradation remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the cellular and extracellular protein repertoire of Streptomyces sp. title: A angústia do professor universitário: entre a métrica e o eclipse do pensamento
abstract: This article examines the specific anxiety of the contemporary university professor as an intensified expression of the ‘philosophy of anguish’ characterizing the post-Bologna university. Drawing on a theoretical framework that integrates Ortega y Gasset’s vital reason, Byung-Chul Han’s critique of the achievement society, and Lacanian structural reading, it analyzes five constitutive dimensions of this anguish: the split between teaching and research imposed by ranking metrics; the institutional pressure of publish or perish as a systemic rather than individual imperative; the perversity of t

title: Stability analysis and optimal control theory for a class of plant disease models under a fractional derivative
abstract: The present paper focuses on plant disease modeling using the Caputo derivative. To ensure that the problem is biologically well defined, we establish the non-negativity and boundedness of the solutions of the dynamical system. The stability of the equilibrium points is analyzed in detail. journal: An International Journal of Optimization and Control Theories & Applications (IJOCTA)

title: Experimental Study of the Abrasive Flow Machining Process on Surface Finishing and Material Remove Rate of Aluminium Alloy 6061/SiC Nano Metal Matrix Composites
abstract: One of the most important and costly procedures in today's manufacturing sectors is precision surface finishing, especially for parts with intricate geometries and complex internal pathways. Uniform surface finishing in such hard-to-reach areas is made possible by Abrasive Flow Machining (AFM), a sophisticated non-traditional finishing technique. title: Inteligencia artificial, armas autónomas y ciberoperaciones: Una reflexión sobre la convergencia entre el derecho internacional humanitario y el derecho del desarme y sus desafíos para la educación jurídica
abstract: La rápida incorporación de drones, IA (inteligencia artificial), sistemas de armas autónomas y capacidades ciberofensivas en los conflictos armados modernos, con el conflicto Rusia-Ucrania como paradigma tensiona las categorías clásicas del DIH y del Derecho del Desarme. title: The first hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of the Erlian Basin, Inner Mongolia, China
abstract: Hadrosauroidea is one of the most diverse herbivorous dinosaur clades of the Cretaceous, with its early-diverging members well documented from the Lower Cretaceous of East Asia. However, despite yielding abundant Upper Cretaceous dinosaur fossils, the Erlian Basin of Inner Mongolia has never previously yielded hadrosauroid remains from its Lower Cretaceous deposits. title: Reevaluation of Mycobonia and Pseudofavolus (Polyporaceae) with two new species and two new combinations
abstract: Favolus , Mycobonia and Pseudofavolus ( Polyporales , Basidiomycota ) are polyporoid genera with mainly tropical to subtropical distribution. Mycobonia and Pseudofavolus are morpho-anatomically similar, being distinguished by the presence of a poroid hymenophore in Pseudofavolus , while species in Mycobonia are stereoid with projecting hyphal pegs that resemble thin spines. title: Application of the SARIMAX Model for Forecasting the Number of Domestic Ship Departing Passengers at Soekarno-Hatta Port, Makassar
abstract: The number of domestic ship departure passengers at Soekarno-Hatta Port, Makassar, fluctuates seasonally and is affected by weather conditions. This study aims to forecast the number of domestic ship departure passengers at Soekarno-Hatta Port, Makassar, for the next 12 months as supporting information for port operational planning, using a SARIMAX model with monthly rainfall as an exogenous variable. title: High-resolution soil moisture forecasts for drought early warning in Germany
abstract: Drought early warning increasingly relies on high-resolution monitoring, but the skill of daily soil moisture forecasts at lead times of 1–2 weeks driven by real-time meteorological ensembles has rarely been evaluated directly against an operational drought-monitoring framework. The Hydrological Sub-seasonal Forecasting System (HS2S) extends an established national drought-monitoring framework into high-resolution probabilistic soil moisture forecasts up to two weeks ahead for Germany at 0.015 625 ∘ resolution. title: Water Depollution Studies for the Removal of Contaminants Like Pesticides and Fluoride: Application to Real Water Samples
abstract: The ubiquitous use of pesticides in agricultural ecosystems is crucial for pest management, but it can lead to significant environmental contamination, particularly of freshwater resources. We report the successful adsorption efficiency of a glass fiber–ferrite–PANI composite synthesized via an in situ polymerization method using lime juice as a dopant and reaction medium. title: An assessment of integrated nutrient management as a climate-smart approach to sustainable soil health and agricultural productivity
abstract: The rapid increase in global population has significantly intensified the demand for food production, necessitating the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices. Integrated nutrient management (INM) combines inorganic fertilisers, organic amendments and biofertiliser inputs to optimise nutrient availability, whereas conventional systems predominantly rely on excessive chemical fertilisers, which compromise long-term sustainability through soil degradation and environmental pollution. institutions: Banda University of Agriculture and Technology, Banda

title: The knowledge–behavior gap in occupational safety among vocational students during practical training: A literature review of individual, social, and environmental factors
abstract: The gap between occupational safety knowledge and safety behavior remains a concern in vocational practical activities, as understanding safety principles does not always translate into compliance with safety procedures. This study aims to analyze the relationship between occupational safety knowledge and safety behavior and to identify factors associated with this gap in vocational practical activities. title: Ultra-high voltage transmission and corporate ESG performance: evidence from Chinese A-share listed firms
abstract: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship between ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission access and corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies with valid Sino-Securities ESG ratings from 2009 to 2022. title: Tropocollagen‐Locked Amphibian Collagen Matrices for Supramolecular‐Guided Wound Repair
abstract: Supramolecular organization of collagen encodes stage-specific instructive cues, yet this parameter remains largely unaddressed in wound scaffold design. Conventional mammalian collagen undergoes fibrillogenesis during processing, precluding preservation of the pre-fibrillar organization characteristic of early repair. Here, we exploited the exceptional aqueous solubility of amphibian (Rana catesbeiana) type I collagen to generate a tropocollagen-locked matrix (BF-nCol) via controlled 1,4-butanediol diglycidyl ether crosslinking. title: The Philosophical Foundations of Islamic Education in Malay Tradition: An Ontological, Epistemological, and Axiological Analysis
abstract: This study aims to analyze the ontological, epistemological, and axiological foundations of Islamic education in Malay cultural traditions and examine their relevance to contemporary educational practices. Employing qualitative library research with a philosophical hermeneutic approach, the study analyzes Tunjuk Ajar Melayu and Gurindam Dua Belas, supported by scholarly literature on Islamic educational philosophy and comparative cultural traditions. title: Extracellular vesicle-loaded hydrogels for diabetic bone healing
abstract: The bone healing cascade is initiated by an inflammatory response, which in turn mediates regenerative repair and culminates in the restoration of bone tissue. An imbalanced immune response during the early stage of bone regeneration disrupts the healing cascade, delaying bone healing and compromising therapeutic outcomes. Diabetes induces oxidative stress and inflammation, disturbs bone metabolism, increases the risk of infection, decreases bone scaffold efficacy, and hinders bone defect repair. title: Container Throughput across Eastern Mediterranean Ports: National Renewable Integration, Carbon-Price-Weighted Trade Exposure, and Logistics Infrastructure, 2005-2023
abstract: Eastern Mediterranean container ports operate across heterogeneous energy, logistics, and regulatory environments, yet comparative evidence on their association with throughput remains limited. This study examines container throughput, National Renewable Integration (NRI), logistics infrastructure, and carbon-price-weighted trade exposure (CPTE) across five countries from 2005 to 2023. title: Demographic ageing and household energy poverty in China: the moderating roles of digital access and social capital
abstract: Background As demographic ageing progresses, increasing attention has been paid to ensuring access to basic energy services for households with older members and understanding their potential vulnerability. Household energy affordability is essential for maintaining basic living standards, health, and well-being. Existing studies have examined the relationships between population ageing, household life cycles, and household energy poverty. title: Exclusive quark and gluon dijet production as probes of GPDs at collider energies
abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. title: Estimating differential short-term air pollution impact on cause-specific mortality from multiple pollutants
abstract: Background Air pollution concentration-response functions—the risk estimates from epidemiological models used in health impact assessment —are typically non-local, apply to different concentration ranges, and use broad measures of exposure and outcome like single pollutants and all non-external cause mortality. title: Development of an aerial transect survey for non‐breeding waterfowl in bottomland hardwood forest
abstract: Airplane‐based, low‐altitude aerial surveys are the standard monitoring framework for waterfowl populations in North America. Designing representative, precise, and efficient aerial surveys remains a core challenge for the management community, and critical scientific evaluation of such monitoring programs is necessary among growing safety concerns and shrinking budgets. title: Development of a Condition Prediction Model for Rigid Pavement Roads in Mountainous Areas: A Case of the Magila–Magoroto Road in Muheza District, Tanzania
abstract: Rigid pavement roads in mountainous areas deteriorate rapidly under the combined effects of steep terrain, heavy rainfall, unstable slopes and expansive soils. On the Magila–Magoroto road in Muheza District, Tanzania, these stresses are aggravated by the reactive maintenance approach applied by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA), which results in emergency repairs, prolonged closures and rising costs. title: Panel Surface Segmentation in Thermal Photovoltaic Images Using YOLO11n-Seg and Its Assessment as a Preprocessing Step for Thermal Analysis
abstract: Reliable separation of photovoltaic (PV) panel surfaces from their background is an early preprocessing step for temperature-based inspection of PV systems. This study addresses the automatic segmentation of PV panel surfaces in thermal solar-panel images using YOLO11n-Seg, a lightweight instance segmentation model. title: The Impact of Credit Risk Management on the Profitability of Commercial Banks in China
abstract: Banking institutions' credit risk management policies is having a dramatic effect on their financial performance, particularly in the upcoming markets in various markets in China. In China, the credit growth rates, and shifting regulations, have affected the way financial institutions act and behave. title: Climate-related dysphoria: a proposed research agenda
abstract: Climate change threatens mental health, but its contribution to everyday changes in mood remains difficult to distinguish from seasonal routines and other stressors. I propose climate-related dysphoria (CRD) as a provisional dimensional framework for affective worsening during adverse environmental exposure and improvement as exposure diminishes. abstract: This work investigates nonlinear fractional oscillatory dynamics governed by memory-dependent Stuart-Landau oscillator networks (SLNM) formulated through the Erdelyi-Kober (EK) fractional operator. To obtain analytical-computational solutions, the homotopy recursive iterative method (HRIM) is developed. abstract: Prior research has examined social capital, leadership, knowledge management, and innovation largely in separation, and it has often treated business performance as if it were sustainable competitive advantage. abstract: Introduction One of the benefits of chitosan for broilers is positive effects on growth performance, intestinal morphology and gene expression profiling. abstract: The nutrition transition, originally described by Popkin in 1993, tracks the shift from traditional to industrialised dietary patterns and is widely used to explain rising non-communicable disease burdens globally. Importantly, the framework situates dietary change within broader social, economic, and environmental systems rather than individual behavioural choices. abstract: A tendency to pay limited attention to plants, often described as “plant blindness”, can lead to failing to recognise their biological, ecological and societal importance. This opinion paper argues that botanical education should be an integral part of environmental education and sustainable development, not a narrowly specialised branch of biology. abstract: Regulatory uncertainty poses complex strategic challenges, but firms' responses to it are often reduced to a binary choice between compliance and noncompliance. This study examines how companies manage regulatory uncertainty when facing changing sustainability reporting requirements, focusing on the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and its partial reversal under the Omnibus I package. abstract: This article reflects on teaching a literature elective for medical students. In this elective, students discuss their embodied experience and its relation to their patients in the hospital in reflective writing assignments. The article explores medical student’s positionality in the hospital and puts it in dialogue with Michel Foucault’s notion of “heterotopia.” This analytical concept makes visible the vast networks of linkages that connect humans and the emergence of an ethics of care informed by the awareness of human relationality. abstract: La vigilancia digital ha desbordado las categorías clásicas del derecho de daños y del consentimiento contractual. abstract: Conventional graphite anodes made by slurry coating (SC) contain disordered, tortuous pore networks that hinder lithium-ion transport, particularly at high charge/discharge rates.
