abstract: Although Arab-Javanese cultural interaction has historically influenced social and religious life in East Java, limited attention has been given to its role in community-level identity formation. This study examines Arab-Javanese cultural acculturation and its contribution to local identity construction in Polowijen Cultural Village, Malang, East Java. abstract: Adoption of climate-smart agricultural (CSA) practices has been widely recognized as a promising and effective approach to minimize the adverse impacts of climate change. However, their adoption among smallholder farmers remains low in developing countries, including Tanzania. abstract: Although urban sports clubs in Surabaya are expanding rapidly, comparative studies examining service quality across different sports branches remain scarce. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, this study investigated how service quality shapes member satisfaction and compared performance across five Surabaya sports clubs based on 114 purposively selected active members. abstract: Alarm calls enable animals to warn conspecifics of imminent threats and coordinate collective responses. abstract: En un contexto de expansión de gobiernos iliberales, el Poder Judicial enfrenta presiones políticas y presupuestarias que amenazan su independencia y legitimidad. abstract: This study examines how firms operating in Lithuania adapted their supply chains to two consecutive disruptions: the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent Russia–Ukraine war with its associated European Union sanctions. abstract: Tenganan village does not yet have a dedicated logo to strengthen its institutional brand awareness. Currently, the use of the Tenganan Pegringsingan Traditional village logo creates ambiguity in how it represents the village’s official visual identity. This research aims to design a distinctive logo for Tenganan village grounded in local wisdom principles to establish a clear and culturally rooted visual identity. This study attempts to develop a local wisdom-based logo design framework that translates cultural narratives into an institutional visual identity for rural and cultural villages.

abstract: Hydroquinone is becoming prevalent in our environment, with significant ecological and health implications. title: A bottom-up social cost of carbon for Latin America: municipality-level heat-mortality damage functions from 30 million daily death records
abstract: Temperature–mortality response functions have been quantified across many climate zones, but for most of the developing world they have not been translated into country-specific economic damages at sub-national resolution. This study estimates bottom-up mortality social costs of carbon (SCC) for five Latin American countries at municipality resolution. We assemble 30 million daily death records across 10 214 municipality-equivalent units in Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Ecuador and Peru (2000–2023) and merge them with the ARCO-ERA5 reanalysis sampled at every unit centroid. title: Terrain, water, and the placement of sacred sites across Nepal's physiographic belts
abstract: Sacred sites are widely observed to occupy distinctive positions in the landscape: near water, on high ground, at the confluence of rivers; yet whether this reflects a measurable siting preference, and whether that preference is the same across varied terrain, has rarely been tested at scale. This research focuses on whether the placement of sacred sites across Nepal is structured by terrain and water once the distribution of population is accounted for, and whether this structure differs between the country's physiographic belts. title: Social-emotional competence profiles and their associations with psychological resilience, social support, and online social interaction needs among Chinese university students
abstract: Social-emotional competence (SEC) supports university adjustment, but variable-centered analyses may obscure how its dimensions combine within students. This cross-sectional study identified sample-specific SEC profiles and examined their associations with psychological resilience, social support, online social interaction needs, and demographic characteristics among 463 students from five universities in Guangzhou, China. title: Public Transport Sustainability Assessment: Trends, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Transportation sector is evolving with innovations, has currently prioritized integration of sustainability to ensure a secured future. Public transportation, designed to provide affordable access to all, has emerged as a prominent option within the framework of sustainability. Various methodologies have been employed to assess sustainability in public transportation. Consequently, there is a need for a comprehensive study to identify the most effective evaluation methodologies, as well as to explore future research opportunities within this domain. abstract: Zinc is an essential trace element, but its discharge above permissible limits from galvanizing, electroplating and related industries makes the selective separation of Zn(II) an important analytical and environmental task. title: Effect of Digital Innovations on the Success of Construction Projects: A Case of Rusizi Port Construction Project

title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
abstract: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae ( Xoo ) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. title: Evaluation of improved ‘Mena’ Teff variety under frontline demonstration in dry-land areas, Northeast Ethiopia
abstract: Teff is an important staple cereal growing in diverse agro ecologies in Ethiopia. Its productivity in dry-land areas however remains below the national and regional averages due to drought stress, limited input use, and reliance on local cultivars. This study therefore evaluated the improved teff variety under the farmers’ field conditions in Wag-lasta area, Northeast Ethiopia, to assess its agronomic performance, economic profitability, and farmer acceptance. abstract: Este estudo avaliou a variabilidade e as tendências anuais e sazonais das temperaturas máxima (Tmax) e mínima (Tmin) do ar em nove estações do sul de Moçambique, com séries de extensões distintas entre 1993 e 2023. title: Event‐Triggered Model‐Free Adaptive Sliding Mode Control of Networked Control Systems Under IDoS Attacks
abstract: An event‐triggered model‐free adaptive sliding mode control (MFASMC) method is investigated in this article for networked control systems under intermittent denial‐of‐service (IDoS) attacks. To address unmodeled dynamics and bandwidth limitations, MFASMC is integrated with an event‐triggered mechanism and formulated within a data‐driven framework. title: Usos mercantiles en el arbitraje comercial internacional: hacia un test de razonabilidad y previsibilidad
abstract: Commercial customs are unwritten rules of conduct that are generally accepted in commercial transactions. Their content is dynamic and their nature imprecise, which leads to identification problems in practice, affecting legal stability. This article aims to analyze the origin, concept, application, and normative character of commercial usages, focusing on Article 28.4 of the Chilean Law on International Commercial Arbitration, Law No. 19,971, considering international arbitration practice. title: Digitalization, Institutional Quality, and Logistics Performance: Structural Complementarity versus Within-Country Dynamics
abstract: Previous cross-country studies of logistics performance have examined digitalization and institutional quality as separate determinants and have reported single panel coefficients that do not distinguish differences between countries from changes within countries. This study examines whether the two factors are complementary and whether their associations with logistics performance differ between and within economies. title: Evaluation of the surface quality and coating integrity of teak (Tectona grandis L.f.) with different finishing systems
abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate and compare the performance of different finishing systems on plantation-grown teak (Tectona grandis) to optimize its aesthetics and mechanical protection. Four topcoats such as nitrocellulose (NC) lacquer, solvent-based polyurethane (PU), water-based polyurethane (PUW) and alkyd varnish (VA) were evaluated in combination with straight, oil (O), and non-grain-raising (NGR) stains on plantation teak. title: Compatibilization and Toughening of PLA Composite via Constructing Dynamic Crosslinked Network
abstract: Preparation of polylactic acid (PLA) materials with good comprehensive performance has always been a popular research direction in this field. In this work, we prepared toughened PLA/poly(4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P4HB) composites with good strength by introducing dynamic transesterification bonds. Torque, infrared spectroscopy, and gel content analyses confirmed the occurrence of the dynamic crosslinking reaction, which greatly improved the compatibility between PLA and P4HB. title: Modelling the impact of consecutive dry and wet events on levee failure and flooding
abstract: Prolonged droughts followed by high river flows can weaken earthen levees before they are hydraulically loaded. Desiccated soils may develop cracks, lower resistance to shear stress and increase susceptibility to concentrated erosion, yet antecedent soil conditions are rarely represented explicitly in flood-risk assessments. This study examines how consecutive dry-wet conditions may affect levee-failure probability and breach-induced flood dynamics. title: Green Growth or Growth First? Carbon Intensity and Provincial Development Paths in Vietnam
abstract: Vietnam has committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 while aiming to reach high-income status by 2045. Whether these two goals can be pursued together depends heavily on what happens inside its provinces, where growth is planned, power plants are sited and industrial parks compete for investment. This paper documents the current situation using newly available satellite- and asset-based emission estimates from Climate TRACE for all 63 pre-2025 provinces (2021–2024), combined with provincial GRDP and population statistics and national series from the Global Carbon Project and the World Bank. abstract: Waste-to-energy (WtE) technology has emerged as an important alternative for addressing the growing challenges of solid waste management while supporting the transition towards renewable and sustainable energy systems. In Malaysia, rapid urbanisation, population growth, industrial development and increasing consumption have contributed to rising municipal solid waste (MSW) generation, placing considerable pressure on existing landfill-based disposal systems. title: Do Biodiversity Disclosures Translate Into Corporate Green Excellence? Exploring From CEO Global Experience Within Sustainable‐Oriented Agreement
abstract: Referring to the IPBES Global Assessment on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services report, global companies have been challenged by calls for global protection of biodiversity and nature. Companies play a crucial role in communicating their protection activities. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effect of biodiversity disclosure on corporate green excellence by considering the moderating role of CEO global exposure. title: Biased Error Attribution in Multi-Agent Human–AI Systems Under Delayed Feedback
abstract: Human decision-making is often influenced by cognitive biases, especially under uncertainty and risk. Prior works have studied biases in single-step decision environments with immediate outcomes or in interaction with a single AI agent. However, less attention has been given to (1) cascaded settings with delayed outcomes, where decision at one step influences future system states and (2) to interaction with multiple AI agents. title: Predicting the potential habitat suitability of Phloeosinus aubei Perris in China using BIOMOD2
abstract: Phloeosinus aubei Perris, a bark beetle of increasing concern in China, poses significant threats to Cupressaceae species in both natural and managed landscapes. This study used 69 spatially thinned occurrence records and 10 environmental predictors with BIOMOD2 to predict its potential habitat suitability under current and future climate scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5). title: Comparative Study of TSLM, SARIMA, and Prophet for Nitrogen Service Daily Revenue Forecasting
abstract: The daily revenue of a nitrogen tire filling service at a gas station fluctuates sharply with vehicle mobility, weekly rhythms, and holiday seasons, which complicates staffing, inventory, and budget decisions. This study determines the most accurate forecasting model for the daily revenue of PT Migas Mitra Sejati by testing three approaches: the Time Series Linear Model (TSLM) as a deterministic trend–seasonal regression, the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) as a stochastic benchmark, and Prophet as an additive decomposition model. abstract: The estimation of radiological risks in soils from selected oil-spill communities in the Niger Delta, Nigeria has been carried out using Sodium Iodide detector dopped with Thallium based on gamma spectroscopy, NaI(TI)Ɣ, followed by mathematical computations. abstract: This research, which employs a quantitative approach, aims to understand the role of business communication as a marketing strategy to support the sustainable development of e-commerce in Indonesia. The research process involved the collection of secondary data and a literature review. A sample of 5 online stores was selected from a total of 25, based on the size of their consumer base. title: Echocardiographic assessment of cardiac function in patients with fontan circulation during 24-hour normobaric hypoxia
abstract: Objective The function of the Fontan circulation depends on a low pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), which can increase under hypoxic conditions and might lead to hemodynamic deterioration. Consequently, prolonged exposure to hypoxia has traditionally been considered too risky, although data are scarce. We investigated whether 24 h of moderate normobaric hypoxia, equivalent to 2,500 masl altitude, is associated with changes in resting systemic ventricular function and mean Fontan pathway pressure (P FP ) in clinically stable, non-fenestrated Fontan patients. title: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Ethanol on Cu3Sn: A First-Principles Study
abstract: Electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction (CO2R) represents a promising strategy for recycling greenhouse gas into valuable chemical feedstocks within a circular carbon economy. Among available catalysts, copper (Cu) remains the only monometallic catalyst capable of producing multi-carbon hydrocarbons at reasonable reaction rates and therefore serves as a foundation for designing more efficient bimetallic CO2R catalysts. title: Independent fern gametophytes from Mt. Jiri, South Korea: morphological and DNA barcode profiles
abstract: Ferns possess two free-living generations, the gametophyte and sporophyte; however, most species are dominated by the sporophyte phase. In some taxa, non-cordate gametophytes can persist independently in the absence of conspecific sporophytes; these are referred to as independent gametophytes. Although independent gametophytes have been documented only in a limited number of fern families, they occur worldwide, particularly in temperate regions, and are generally classified into two categories: obligate and facultative independent gametophytes. title: A fuzzy-driven modified draco lizard optimizer for precise PV model parameter estimation
abstract: This paper introduces a Modified Draco Lizard Optimizer (MDLO) for parameter identification of Photovoltaic (PV) models utilizing diode-based equivalent circuits. In the proposed MDLO, three key enhancements are involved in improving adaptability, efficiency and stability. title: The impact of a polyphenol rich sugarcane extract nutrition intervention on bacterial DNA in plasma in response to exertional-heat stress
abstract: Introduction Exercise-associated bacteraemia is common in response to exertional-heat stress (EHS). The study aimed to examine if a polyphenol rich sugarcane extract (PRSE) nutrition intervention could mitigate increases in bacterial DNA in plasma in response to EHS. Design Randomised controlled trial. Methods Fourteen participants completed two EHS trials. title: Beyond the Masculinity Trap: Reimagining Masculinity in the Kenyan Diaspora
abstract: Masculinity is a socially constructed phenomenon shaped by cultural norms, economic structures, historical forces, and interpersonal relations. Among Kenyan men in the diaspora, it is continually negotiated at the intersection of inherited cultural expectations, migration pressures, and global gender discourses. This article introduces the concept of the masculinity trap, referring to the psychological and social constraints that arise when men are expected to conform to rigid ideals of strength, emotional control, dominance, and provider responsibility. title: Ineficacia de las políticas criminales frente a la extorsión y narcotráfico en Ecuador
abstract: El objetivo del presente artículo es analizar la eficacia de las políticas criminales adoptadas por el Ecuador como respuestas a los fenómenos vinculados a economías ilícitas y crimen organizado como la extorsión y el narcotráfico que han mostrado una mayor resiliencia frente a estas respuestas estatales que buscan mitigarlas. title: 4D Aviation Emission Inventory Data of China estimated with QAR data in 2023 (4D-AEID-2023)
abstract: Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a high-resolution, four-dimensional aviation emission inventory for purely domestic civil aviation flights within mainland China in 2023, built directly from onboard Quick Access Recorder (QAR) measurements covering 4.52 million flights (∼96.8 % of national commercial movements). title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
abstract: A wide variety of highly strained indole-fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd-catalyzed sequential reaction process with di-t-butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. title: Nano‐Scaffolding of Fibrous Skeletons for High‐Strength Icephobic Composites Integrating Wave‐Transparent Functionalization
abstract: The complex operating environments in aerospace engineering pose increasing demands for advanced composites with coupled icephobic‐electromagnetic‐mechanical performance. However, existing materials fail to integrate effective icephobicity, high electromagnetic wave transmission, and practical mechanical strength. To solve the above challenge, a novel multifunctional composite design strategy is developed based on the proposal of nano‐scaffolding of fibrous skeletons (NSFS). title: Preparedness for ISO 21401 Implementation in Tourism SMEs : Readiness, Barriers, Enablers, and Perceived Sustainability Integration
abstract: This study investigates tourism small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) preparedness for ISO 21401 implementation, focusing on associations between individual readiness practices, barriers, enabling factors, and a single self‐reported rating of general sustainability integration. Drawing on self‐reported survey data from 209 European accommodation providers selected through purposive sampling, the study applies descriptive analysis, Analysis of variance (ANOVA), and logistic regression. title: Serious games for disaster resilience: an interpretative synthesis of reported participant perceptions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesize reported participant perceptions of serious games used in humanitarian logistics and disaster-management contexts, focusing on experiential, ethical and cognitive dimensions of learning. Design/methodology/approach An interpretive qualitative synthesis examined 57 empirically distinguishable applications from 46 eligible articles within an initial 59-article corpus (2014–2024). title: SwissPaleodatabase 2.0: an updated palaeoseismological database for Switzerland
abstract: Palaeoseismological databases are important for reconstructing long-term seismic activity in regions where historical and instrumental records of large earthquakes are limited. We present SwissPaleodatabase 2.0, an updated compilation of published geological, geomorphological, archaeological and historical observations with potential paleoseismological relevance from Switzerland and surrounding Alpine regions. title: Analysis of Flatwise Compression Performance of Hourglass Lattice Sandwich Structures
abstract: Composites have emerged as the preferred material for primary load‐bearing structures in the aerospace field owing to their outstanding specific strength, specific stiffness, and structural designability. Traditional composite sandwich structures still face numerous challenges under out‐of‐plane compressive loads. In this study, a novel hourglass lattice sandwich structure is proposed and fabricated based on the interlocking assembly molding process. title: Digital Inclusion in Agribusiness: Access, Capabilities, Market Power and Smallholder Outcomes
abstract: Digital technologies increasingly mediate agricultural advice, input procurement, finance, marketing and coordination across agrifood value chains, yet their availability does not necessarily confer meaningful participation on smallholders or rural enterprises. This critical narrative review examines the mechanisms through which digitalisation may reduce transaction costs and improve decision-making, alongside the socioeconomic, organisational and governance conditions that can reproduce exclusion. title: Optimized hybrid-chemical synthesis with morphology-controlled synthesis of copper-based nanomaterials as a response to emerging fungal drug resistance
abstract: The rapid development of nanoscience and nanotechnology has unlocked new possibilities in biomedicine, particularly in diagnostics, imaging, and targeted therapies. Among various nanomaterials, metallic nanoparticles, especially those based on copper, have attracted growing interest due to their unique physicochemical properties, ease of synthesis, and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. abstract: Introduction Mortality among intubated children in public pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) in lowand middle-income countries remains high, driven in part by gaps in workforce training, team coordination, and standardized processes. We evaluated a low-cost, multidisciplinary digital education and team-based quality-improvement (QI) intervention—a multilingual online curriculum, telesimulationbased team training, standardized airway and handoff workflow tools, and on-site visits—in the PICU of a public pediatric hospital in Cartagena, Colombia. title: A surge-detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in the Pamir Mountains, revealed by daily PlanetScope imagery
abstract: Surge-type behaviour and low-angle glacier detachment are distinct but potentially linked forms of dynamic instability that remain insufficiently documented in small debris-covered mountain glaciers. This study investigates the 2025–2026 event at Dehdal Glacier in the northwestern Pamirs, which we interpret as a surge-detachment sequence, using daily PlanetScope imagery. title: National benchmarking of operational energy and carbon performance in England's NHS estate: determinants and net zero trajectories
abstract: England's National Health Service (NHS) has committed to net zero by 2040 for the emissions it controls directly, but its national totals cannot show whether reductions come from the estate, a cleaner electricity grid, changes in reporting coverage or milder weather. This study uses the mandatory Estates Returns Information Collection (ERIC) to separate these drivers and test whether trusts are on track for 2040. abstract: Stereospermum kunthianum Cham. (Bignoniaceae) is a plant documented in the Senegalese pharmacopoeia and is used as a natural source of remedies in traditional medicine. The aim of this study was to perform a chemical screening and evaluate the anti-inflammatory activity of the hydro-ethanolic extract of the plant's stem bark (HEE) and its fractions in rats. abstract: Bond-exchange reactions (BERs) enable vitrimers to relax stress through dynamic topology rearrangement, yet their mechanical effectiveness depends strongly on network architecture. Here, experimental stress-relaxation measurements are combined with reactive coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations of epoxy–acid networks with systematically varied backbone flexibility and cross-linker length. title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Smallholder Cattle Raisers in Ilocos Norte: Basis For Cattle Production Practices Improvement
abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of 420 smallholder cattle raisers in Ilocos Norte as a basis for improving cattle production practices. A descriptive-correlational research design was used, with data collected through a validated questionnaire covering breeding, feeding, health management, housing, biosecurity, and record-keeping. title: Navigating Green Paradoxes in Hotels: A Multistakeholder Framework and the Role of Managerial Values
abstract: This study develops a context‐sensitive analytical framework for understanding tensions encountered when hotels implement green practices in a developing‐economy destination. Guided by the Resource‐Based View, Institutional Theory, Paradox Theory, and Self‐Determination Theory, the study used a multimethod qualitative design. title: Managed Strategic Competition in China–Japan Relations: Security Dynamics, Techno‐Economic Rivalry, and Implications for ASEAN
abstract: Why has Sino‐Japanese security competition escalated continuously since 2012 yet not crossed the threshold of armed conflict? That competition and cooperation coexist in great‐power rivalries is well established; what remains underspecified is the mechanism sustaining this coexistence within a specific dyad, its scope conditions , and its cumulative, directional character. title: Public discourse on violence in medical settings and its implications for medical students' career resilience: evidence from social media text mining
abstract: Background Violence in medical settings has become a growing concern, yet the potential relevance of this public discourse to the career-development environment surrounding medical students remains underexplored. This study investigates the external discursive environment surrounding medical violence and its potential implications for medical students' professional identity and resilience. Methods This study used computational text analysis of public comments on Sina Weibo about violence in medical settings. Guided LDA was applied to 13,101 comments containing at least one retained vocabulary

title: Intercropping delivers multidimensional benefits in smallholder agrifood systems: the case of taro–cowpea–maize cultivation in South Pacific Island countries
abstract: Introduction Smallholder farming systems in the South Pacific face increasing challenges from climate variability, soil degradation, labour constraints, and poor dietary diversity. Conservation agriculture (CA) has been promoted as a pathway to improve the productivity and resilience of these systems, yet evidence of its economic, social, and climate-adaptation benefits remains limited. Methods This study evaluated a Milpa -inspired taro ( Colocasia esculenta L., Schott)–cowpea ( Vigna unguiculata L., Walp.)–maize ( Zea mays L.) intercropping system in representative smallholder farms in Samoa
institutions: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

title: Consideraciones sistemáticas sobre el blanqueo de capitales y figuras delictivas afines en el ámbito de los criptoactivos
abstract: Este artículo aborda los desafíos que plantea el uso de criptomonedas en la ejecución del blanqueo de capitales. Se analiza cómo estos activos virtuales facilitan cada etapa del proceso de blanqueo y la perpetración de tradicionales delitos previos, como la receptación, la corrupción y el fraude fiscal. Se examina la tipificación del delito de blanqueo en España y se destacan los riesgos emergentes asociados a las finanzas descentralizadas, las ofertas iniciales de proyectos cripto, los tokens no fungibles, los servicios mezcladores, entre otros. title: Estimation‐Driven Model Predictive Control Architecture for Active Suspension Systems Under Road Disturbances
abstract: This research work presents an optimal control architecture for a quarter‐car active suspension system, which integrates a discrete‐time Kalman filter (KF) with a model predictive control (MPC) scheme. The proposed framework aims to enhance ride comfort and vehicle stability by effectively suppressing the impacts of road disturbances, that is, road bumps and pathholes, through a feasible control input. title: Unifying Polar and Hydrophobic Models of Ice Recognition by Antifreeze Glycoproteins
abstract: Antifreeze glycoproteins (AFGPs) enable polar organisms to survive at subzero temperatures by inhibiting ice growth through selective association with specific crystallographic planes. However, the molecular basis of this interaction and its remarkable selectivity remain incompletely understood, and both polar and hydrophobic binding models have been proposed. Here, we combine the synthesis of AFGP variants with high-resolution NMR spectroscopy, antifreeze activity measurements, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the molecular determinants of ice recognition. title: Epidemiological and spatial analysis of bacterial meningitis in Colombia, 2010–2022
abstract: BACKGROUND: National level epidemiological and geospatial analyses of surveillance data are required for bacterial meningitis, integrating demographic, clinical, and environmental proxy variables. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the epidemiology, spatial distribution, and environmental factors associated with bacterial meningitis (BM) caused by mandatory reporting pathogens in Colombia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A longitudinal retrospective study was conducted using data from the National Public Health Surveillance System (SIVIGILA) between 2010 and 2022. title: Reliability-based acceptance criterion for compaction quality control in road construction
abstract: Compaction quality control in pavement construction is commonly governed by statistical acceptance specifications intended to account for construction and testing variability. However, these approaches do not explicitly quantify the reliability of the lot mean and may become increasingly conservative as the number of quality-control tests increases. This issue is increasingly important as intelligent compaction technologies enable the efficient collection of large datasets of lot quality. title: Does climate information improve technical efficiency among organic rice farmers?: insight from Indonesia
abstract: Climate variability poses a growing challenge to organic rice farming because natural-input-based production systems are highly sensitive to weather conditions. This study examines whether access to climate information improves the technical efficiency of organic rice farmers in East Java, Indonesia. Survey data from 250 farmers in Malang and Mojokerto were analysed using a stochastic frontier approach. title: Visualidades algorítmicas y desigualdad estética: El Impuesto Rosa como sesgo de género en la Inteligencia Artificial
abstract: Este artículo examina el Impuesto Rosa como una manifestación de la desigualdad estética y económica dentro de la cultura visual algorítmica. En lugar de tratar la diferenciación de precios basada en el género como una práctica de mercado residual, explora cómo la inteligencia artificial (IA) reproduce códigos visuales feminizados históricamente incrustados en el marketing de consumo. title: Aerodynamic Design and CFD-based Performance Analysis of UAV Wing Ailerons
abstract: The aerodynamic efficiency of wing control surfaces is critical in optimizing aircraft performance. This study focuses on the aerodynamic design of ailerons adhering to military standards (MIL-STD-1797) to enhance their efficiency using hybrid analytical-empirical approach. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)-based analyses of flow characteristics, aerodynamic forces, and efficiency were conducted to identify optimal aileron configurations. title: Distribution and human use shape popularity of threatened plants on Wikipedia
abstract: Increased public awareness is crucial to mitigating the ongoing loss of biodiversity worldwide, and conservation culturomics offers a way to quantify this awareness and its implications for conservation. Large online data repositories provide an opportunity to measure awareness, even for groups such as plants, which receive less attention in global conservation analyses. title: County-level spatial heterogeneity and environmental correlates of human echinococcosis in Xizang, China
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human echinococcosis remains a major zoonosis in Xizang, China, where marked climatic, topographic and landscape gradients may be associated with spatial variation in disease prevalence. We investigated county-level spatial patterns of overall human echinococcosis, cystic echinococcosis (CE) and alveolar echinococcosis (AE), and their environmental associations. title: Single-cell and clinical analyses reveal elevated HAX1 expression and cell-cycle-associated programs during metastatic progression of lung adenocarcinoma, particularly in brain metastasis
abstract: Introduction Metastatic dissemination is a major determinant of poor outcome in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, molecular features associated with distinct metastatic states, particularly lymph node and brain metastases, remain incompletely defined. We investigated the relationship between HAX1 and LUAD metastatic progression. Methods We reanalyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE131907 to characterize HAX1 expression and associated transcriptional programs across normal lung, primary LUAD, advanced tumors, metastatic lymph nodes (mLN), and brain metastases. title: Teaching History Through Local Lenses: A Qualitative Study on the Integration of Pangasinan Local History in Grade 7 Social Studies
abstract: This qualitative case study explored the integration of Pangasinan local history into Grade 7 Social Studies under the MATATAG Curriculum in selected public secondary schools within the Schools Division of Alaminos City, Philippines. The study examined teachers' experiences, instructional strategies, implementation challenges, and promising practices to develop a contextualized instructional intervention. title: Residual-stress distribution in gear journal shafts induced by mechanical roll hardening
abstract: Residual tensile stresses in the surface layer of machined 30CrMoA gear journal shafts readily promote fatigue crack initiation and degrade in-service reliability. To mitigate these stresses, this study investigates a localized mechanical rolling-hardening process for the journal diameter. title: The role of magnesium in the pathogenesis of inflammatory skin diseases: mechanisms, preliminary clinical findings, and research perspectives
abstract: The global prevalence of inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis and psoriasis remains high, and existing therapies have limited efficacy in addressing challenges including disease recurrence and insufficient barrier repair. Exploring modifiable risk factors such as diet and lifestyle is of significant value. As an essential trace element in the human body, magnesium participates in energy metabolism, signal transduction, and immune regulation. title: Empowering ASEAN Mathematics Teachers' STEM Pedagogical Content Knowledge: A Culturally Responsive Pedagogy Framework
abstract: While integrated STEM education is increasingly prioritized across Southeast Asia, mathematics educators in ASEAN frequently face difficulties harmonizing abstract STEM instruction with diverse socio-cultural realities, resulting in fragmented STEM Pedagogical Content Knowledge (STEM-PCK). This study fills this critical gap by constructing and validating a novel framework embedding Culturally Responsive Pedagogy (CRP) into STEM-PCK. title: Pedagogical Strategies Employed by History Teachers for the Effective Integration of Google Earth in Fostering Students' Learning of Historical Sites in Dodoma Secondary Schools
abstract: Instruction regarding historical sites in secondary education often presents significant logistical hurdles, as important heritage locations are frequently remote and inaccessible for routine field excursions.Google Earth offers an interactive geospatial platform that enables educators to virtually pinpoint, navigate, and analyze historical landmarks, terrain, routes, and topographical conditions linked to historical occurrences.This study investigated the pedagogical strategies utilized by history teachers to effectively integrate Google Earth for enhancing students' learning of historical si

title: Cuando la ciencia ocurre en una computadora: química computacional y compuestos bioactivos
abstract: En la naturaleza existen miles de compuestos con potenciales efectos en la salud que requieren ser investigados, sin embargo, debido a su amplia diversidad, esto puede ser un reto que demanda alta cantidad de recursos y horas de trabajo. La química computacional contribuye a la comprensión del comportamiento de grandes cantidades de compuestos bioactivos sin la necesidad de trabajar físicamente con ellos en el laboratorio. title: Multicollinearity Problem in Prediction of Egg Albumen Index and Some Regression Methods
abstract: Research on Japanese quail (Coturnix coturnix japonica) eggs examined factors affecting albumen index prediction and evaluated the multicollinearity problem among egg quality traits. The study included egg weight, egg width, egg length, shape index, and Haugh unit as explanatory variables for predicting albumen index. title: Two new species of Simplicillium from the Lancang–Mekong River basin and a molecular reappraisal of Simplicillium formicae (Cordycipitaceae, Hypocreales)
abstract: The genus Simplicillium ( Cordycipitaceae , Hypocreales ) comprises fungi with diverse ecological lifestyles, ranging from arthropod pathogens to saprotrophs. However, species diversity and taxonomic relationships within this morphologically conserved genus remain incompletely understood. title: Applicable Law in Cross-Border Insurance Contracts and Environmental Liability Insurance in the EU
abstract: Insurance contracts constitute a special category of contracts in private law due to their function in the transfer and management of risk, as well as due to the combination of elements of private law with public regulation of the insurance market. Within the framework of the internal market of the European Union, the development of cross-border insurance has increasingly stimulated the need to clearly determine the law applicable to insurance contracts. title: The relationship between perceived organizational support and occupational stress: a cross-sectional study among clinical nurses in China
abstract: Clinical nurses experience long-term high occupational stress, which has been associated with burnout and turnover and may be associated with impaired nursing quality. Perceived organizational support has been associated with lower stress, while psychological capital and emotional intelligence have been proposed as internal psychological resources. title: Communicating language research to a broader audience: A multidimensional analysis of OASIS summaries and research article abstracts
abstract: Open Accessible Summaries in Language Studies (OASIS summaries), a specialized form of plain language summary in applied linguistics, are increasingly required or encouraged by journals to communicate research to a broader audience. From a register perspective, this study examined and compared the linguistic features of OASIS summaries and research article (RA) abstracts through a multidimensional analysis based on Biber’s (1988) five dimensions. title: Ayurvedic interventions for diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a critical review of clinical evidence and safety
abstract: Background Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is most prevalent microvascular complication of diabetes; guideline-directed medications relieve pain in only a fraction of cases, and no recognized treatment reverses established DPN. The ancient Ayurvedisc texts describe Prameha and Madhumeha as a cluster of somatosensory manifestations and propose two therapeutic strategies: Panchakarma (cleansing practices) and Shamana (palliative medicine). abstract: To clarify the vertical differentiation of aromatic hydrocarbon compositions in shale oil intervals and its implications for favorable-interval evaluation, 64 valid core samples were collected from the Fengcheng Formation interval at 4759.71–5010.67 m in Well Xia 207, northern Mahu Sag, Junggar Basin. title: Engineering properties, durability, microstructural, and sustainability characteristics of concrete made with LECA aggregate as an alternative to conventional coarse aggregate
abstract: The purpose of this research is to examine M25 grade concrete which incorporates unsoaked Light Expanded Clay Aggregate (LECA) as a substitute at 0% – 50% levels. Performance of freshly mixed concrete was evaluated based on slump test. Hardened concrete was tested for density, compressive strength, split tensile strength and flexural strength at 28 days. title: Inverse association between macronutrient quality index and renal cancer incidence: results from the prostate, lung, colorectal, and ovarian cancer screening trial
abstract: Background The quality of dietary macronutrients, as an integrated measure of dietary patterns, has been increasingly recognized for its potential role in cancer prevention. However, prospective evidence regarding its association with renal cancer incidence and mortality remains limited. We conducted a large-scale prospective cohort study using data from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial to investigate the relationships between the macronutrient quality index (MQI) and renal cancer risk and survival. title: Annual report maps for impression management: Weapons of colonialism
abstract: Much has been written about Cecil Rhodes and the British South Africa Company (BSAC), which he established by royal charter to colonize Rhodesia. Based on a unique dataset of 24 maps included in the BSAC annual reports 1891–1924, we show how the BSAC portrayed its activities cartographically to shareholders in London and to the Colonial Office. Maps were powerful tools of imperialism. We adopt visual reasoning and close reading to interpret the maps. abstract: The Neotropical genus Palicourea (Rubiaceae, Palicoureeae) is one of the largest and most complex plant groups worldwide and is classified into several sections. Among these, Pal. sect. Pseudocephaëlis, as defined here, comprises more than 15 described species but lacks a recent taxonomic revision. Based on morphological and molecular evidence, a taxonomic reassessment of the section reveals a new species from the Caribbean lowlands of southern Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and northern Panama, which is here described as Pal. llanurensis . title: A Comprehensive Review of the Sustainability of Carbon Fiber-Reinforced Plastic Composites
abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced plastics (CFRPs) are widely recognized for their exceptional mechanical properties and lightweight nature. However, as concerns about climate change and pollution intensify, the environmental impact of CFRPs has come under increasing scrutiny, spurring research into more sustainable alternatives. Bio-based materials offer a promising approach for producing eco-friendly, degradable CFRPs, with high-performance variants expected to significantly improve sustainability. title: Inequality of Access to Fire Services: An Analysis of Disparity in Response Time in West Bandung Regency
abstract: Fire services are a basic public service whose value depends on how quickly crews reach an incident, yet most studies of fire station planning focus on urban settings and give less attention to regencies that combine dense urban corridors with hilly rural areas. This study examines how response-time disparities reflect unequal access to fire services between urban and rural areas of West Bandung Regency, which factors explain them, and what they imply for equitable basic service policy. title: Predicted range expansion of Desert Mule Deer under future climate scenarios
abstract: The desert mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus crooki) is distributed throughout the southern United States and northern Mexico. As a large herbivore, this subspecies plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance. While its distribution is closely linked to water availability and vegetation type, climate change is increasingly altering these factors and shifting potential habitats. This study aimed to model the current potential distribution of O. h. crooki and predict distribution changes for the 2021–2040 period in relation to bioclimatic factors. title: Estimating agricultural development resilience against hunger in the 21 century
abstract: Achieving the Sustainable Development Goal of Zero Hunger is becoming more difficult because of growing uncertainties such as climate change and geopolitical conflicts. This study develops a global index, Anti-Hunger Agricultural Development Resilience (AHADR), to measure the resilience of agricultural systems against hunger. AHADR fluctuated throughout 2001–2019 but improved overall, whereas regional inequality in AHADR increased. title: Digital inequalities, placemaking and geographical diversity in tweets about Cape Town railways, 2010 - 2022
abstract: Digital placemaking is implicated with power relations and can expose inequities, exclusions and erasures. A longitudinal archive of 5606 tweets geotagged in Cape Town was collected to explore placemaking practices and inequality in commuter posts about rail travel in the city over the period 2010--2022. Named Entity Recognition (NER) identified 1755 tweets from this archive as a record of digital placemaking about the major train lines in Cape Town. abstract: Se propone un marco pedagógico integrador para fortalecer la enseñanza y comprensión de la Estadística Bayesiana en la educación superior. title: La Edad como Determinante de la Confianza del Consumidor: Evidencia Empírica en el Contexto Urbano de Riobamba
abstract: El Índice Confianza del Consumidor (ICC) constituye un indicador adelantado clave para evaluar la estabilidad macroeconómica regional. Este estudio determinó el impacto de la edad sobre las variaciones del ICC en el sector urbano de Riobamba. Mediante un diseño no experimental, transversal y correlacional, se aplicó un muestreo probabilístico a 613 hogares. title: Design and Development of a Prototype Environmental Monitoring and Control System for Poultry Houses
abstract: Monitoring environmental conditions in broiler chicken houses using manual methods is less effective because temperature, humidity, and light intensity measurements must be performed directly and periodically. Inappropriate environmental conditions can affect broiler comfort and growth. Therefore, an efficient monitoring system is needed to measure and display environmental conditions remotely. This study aimed to design and develop a microcontroller- and Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring system for temperature, humidity, and light intensity in a broiler chicken house. title: Detección de eventos de la marcha mediante sensores inerciales y comparación con los eventos obtenidos por el sistema de fotogrametría
abstract: El análisis de la marcha constituye una herramienta objetiva y fundamental para la evaluación de las habilidades motoras en pacientes, ya que diversas patologías pueden alterar los patrones de marcha y afectar directamente la funcionalidad en las actividades de la vida diaria. En este contexto, la identificación precisa de eventos clave, como el contacto inicial (Foot Strike) y el despegue de los dedos (Toe Off), es esencial para el cálculo de parámetros espaciotemporales. title: Climate relevance of water operators’ partnerships: Evidence from the EU-WOP Phase I programme
abstract: Water and sanitation utilities face climate-related pressures together with constraints in infrastructure, finance and institutional capacity. Water Operators' Partnerships (WOPs) are not-for-profit, peer-to-peer collaborations between utilities. However, documented operational improvements do not necessarily demonstrate climate adaptation or mitigation. This study examines how climate relevance is communicated across the 20 assessed WOPs funded under the EU-WOP Phase I programme. title: Biodiversity of mosquito fauna (Diptera: Culicidae) associated with bromeliads in Atlantic Forest fragments in the state of Sergipe, Brazil
abstract: The Culicidae exhibits broad taxonomic diversity and significant ecological importance, especially in phytotelm habitats provided by bromeliads. This study investigated the diversity of mosquitoes associated with bromeliads in two Atlantic Forest fragments in Sergipe State, northeastern Brazil: the Morro do Urubu Environmental Protection Area (Morro do Urubu APA), a more disturbed site, and the Mata do Crasto Private Natural Heritage Reserve (Mata do Crasto RPPN), a more preserved area. title: Using Game‐Based Experiential Learning With Scenario‐Based Assessment to Measure Climate Change Competence Among Adolescent Students in Pakistan
abstract: Many adolescents are unaware of how unsustainable practices reinforce climate change factors. Although game‐based learning (GBL) is acknowledged as effective, assessing climate change competence often relies on self‐report measures that may not capture actual understanding. This study addresses the limited use of GBL for climate change education and overreliance on self‐report assessments. We developed a game‐based experiential learning intervention using a board game simulating real‐world climate factors. title: Thermal Deformation and Structural Response of a Rolling Shutter Fire Door Exposed to Standard Fire Heating: A Coupled Thermo-Mechanical FEM Study
abstract: In this study, the behavior of a fire-resistant shutter door under a furnace temperature reaching 1200 °C during a 120-minute fire test was investigated both experimentally and numerically. In numerical studies, a coupled thermal-structural finite element model was created using ANSYS 2022 R1; temperature distributions were transferred to the structural solution. title: Reconceptualizing Bedulang as Living Heritage: Cultural Governance and Community-Based Tourism in Terong, Belitung
abstract: This study examines the cultural meanings, customary knowledge, and preservation concerns associated with Bedulang and considers their implications for tourism adaptation in Desa Wisata Terong, Belitung. It employs an interpretive qualitative case-study approach centred on documentary analysis of two sources: the 2022 institutional study Hasil Kajian Makan Bedulang published by Lembaga Adat Melayu Belitong (LAMB), and the Universitas Pelita Harapan (UPH) Internal Research Final Report on Bedulang and tourism in Terong. title: Individual elephants, not populations: a practical approach to managing human–elephant interactions in a plantation landscape in southern India
abstract: India holds nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephants, and much of their range is shared with people; negative human–elephant interactions (HEIs) cause approximately 500 human deaths in India each year. Forest department staff and local residents have knowledge of specific individual elephants that are tolerant of people, but this knowledge is rarely used systematically in management. title: Low-frequency industrial excitation induced lateral resonance of high-speed railway bridge: field measurements and coupled dynamic analysis
abstract: This study investigates abnormal lateral vibration of a high-speed railway bridge adjacent to stone-processing plants through field measurements, modal analysis, vibration-propagation analysis, and a flexible pier-foundation coupled vehicle-track-bridge dynamic model. title: A computer-vision-driven dynamic color rendering algorithm for virtual reality and its application in remote art creation systems
abstract: Remote art creation in virtual reality continues to be undermined by three coupled problems: color distortion under transient illumination, tail latency during rapid brushwork, and chromatic divergence across heterogeneous headsets. This study develops a computer-vision-driven dynamic color rendering algorithm and embeds it within a working remote art creation platform. title: ANALYSIS OF WATER QUALITY IN ORNAMENTAL FISH FARMING GROUPS (POKDAKAN) IN PANGKALPINANG CITY
abstract: Water quality is an important factor affecting the success of ornamental fish cultivation, especially in small cultivation containers with high density. abstract: Most research and monitoring activities involving low-cost atmospheric sensors (LC) have traditionally focused on urban environments, where air quality is a pressing concern. However, an emerging area of research is their application in rural landscapes, where land use is a key determinant of climate change and net zero outcomes, directly influencing greenhouse gas emissions, carbon sequestration, and ecosystem functioning. abstract: The recycling of multilayer plastic (MLP) waste is challenging due to the limited miscibility of its polymeric components. abstract: The transition toward a circular economy requires not only technological and regulatory changes but also consumer acceptance of products incorporating recycled materials. While previous research has extensively examined pro-environmental consumption, comparatively less attention has been paid to high-involvement durable goods, where purchase decisions are infrequent and involve substantial financial and functional considerations. abstract: As an alternative to historical enzyme isolation, metagenomic databases (e.g. MGnify) provide information on vast unculturable microbial diversity, including extreme environments, and constitute an enormous source of functional proteins. Conservative mining of these data by close sequence homology alone tends to identify merely different versions of known enzymes. abstract: A series of metal ion–modified ammonium polyphosphates (M‐APPs) were synthesized and employed as acid sources in combination with benzoxazine (Si‐BOZ) and melamine (ME) to construct intumescent flame‐retardant polyoxymethylene (POM) composites. abstract: Este estudio exploró si combinar inteligencia artificial (IA) y aprendizaje cooperativo ayuda a lograr una educación más inclusiva y accesible en lo digital. title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of the jungle cat (Felis chaus) in Israel
abstract: The jungle cat ( Felis chaus ) is a widespread but locally vulnerable mesocarnivore associated with wetlands, riparian corridors and productive lowlands across the Eastern Mediterranean and Southwest Asia. Although the species is regularly recorded in human-modified landscapes, its national record patterns and exposure to road mortality remain poorly understood. abstract: Background Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a relapsing inflammatory dermatosis marked by eczematous eruptions and persistent pruritus, both of which can substantially impair quality of life in children. Although the therapeutic landscape for AD has expanded considerably, satisfactory disease control remains difficult to achieve in some children, while treatment-related adverse effects may further limit long-term acceptability. abstract: La Industria 4.0 se ha convertido en una estrategia mundial para la competitividad empresarial; sin embargo, para su consolidación efectiva es necesario diagnosticar con precisión las capacidades de adopción digital en las organizaciones. El objetivo de este estudio fue diseñar y validar un instrumento de investigación para evaluar el nivel de preparación, adopción y madurez organizacional hacia la implementación de Industria 4.0 en empresas mexicanas. abstract: This paper examines water-related conflicts in the Blue Nile basin through the lens of Barry Buzan and Ole Wæver’s Regional Security Complex (RSC) theory. It argues that riparian states have securitized water as a national security threat due to a growing scarcity in the region, thereby fostering a new water-related security subcomplex focused on the Blue Nile basin. abstract: Los planos, los ángulos y los movimientos de cámara se estudian como decisiones narrativas que organizan el espacio y regulan la información disponible para el espectador. title: Late Triassic Dipnoi from south Gondwana, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Mesozoic lungfishes are often represented in the fossil record by isolated tooth plates, which impose limitations on their taxonomic identification and on the interpretation of their diversity. title: Dilemmas and Breakthroughs in the E-Commerce Transformation of Foreign Trade in the New Era
abstract: With the advancement of the digital economy, the environment of international trade has continued to evolve. The B2B wholesale-oriented model on which traditional foreign trade enterprises have long relied is now facing new pressure, while the rapid rise of cross-border e-commerce has offered enterprises the opportunity to reach overseas consumers directly and has driven a transformation in the modes of foreign trade operation. abstract: Climate change is altering the distribution and ecological dynamics of forest insect pests, necessitating reliable tools for predicting future habitat suitability. abstract: Changes in planted forests (PF) and natural forests (NF) can affect regional temperature and relative humidity (RH), but their relative responses under contrasting water conditions remain unclear. abstract: Interdisciplinary higher education increasingly emphasizes societally engaged learning that challenges disciplinary silos. However, fostering boundary crossing learning remains a challenge. This study explores photovoice as a practice-based method to facilitate interdisciplinary learning, reflexivity, and support students in navigating complex scientific and societal dilemmas. abstract: Breastfeeding is widely recognized as beneficial for child health, yet the relationship between breastfeeding duration and long-term cardiovascular outcomes, particularly blood pressure (BP), remains incomplete. This study aimed to examine the association between breastfeeding duration and blood pressure (BP) among school-aged children in southwest China. abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze the factors influencing resource productivity in the European Union region from a sustainable development perspective using spatial analysis methods. In this way, the feasibility of implementing circular economy principles to enhance resource productivity among European Union countries was assessed. abstract: Introduction Mosquito-borne viral infections are a rising global public health challenge, particularly for pregnant women. abstract: Drawing on upper echelons' theory and legitimacy theory, this study examines whether and under what conditions foreign CEOs enhance green innovation in Chinese firms. abstract: Jane Knight's definition of knowledge diplomacy is deliberately generic, designed to apply across diverse geopolitical contexts and sectors. abstract: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance is fundamental for proper neural circuit function, and its disruption has emerged as a convergent mechanism across multiple psychiatric disorders. Primarily, GABAergic inhibitory neurons play essential roles in regulating network dynamics, necessary for physiological, cognitive and emotional processing. abstract: This study develops a patient-centered interdisciplinary framework for robot-assisted hand and wrist rehabilitation that integrates robotic engineering, physiotherapy, hospital-based social work, and health-service quality assessment. abstract: Whether and how land use change regulates soil microbial communities by shifting soil carbon-nitrogen (C–N) balance remains unclear, even though C–N balance is known to govern microbial community structure and function. abstract: La retroalimentación formativa es una de las principales estrategias pedagógicas para fortalecer los procesos de enseñanza y aprendizaje, pero su efectividad en el rendimiento académico y la autorregulación del estudiante aún se cuestiona. El objetivo fue analizar sistemáticamente la evidencia científica publicada entre 2020 y 2026 sobre la influencia de la retroalimentación formativa en el rendimiento académico y la autorregulación del aprendizaje en diferentes niveles educativos. title: Modelo de gestión para la conservación de vías urbanas en Rocafuerte: estrategias basadas en técnicas de toma de decisiones multicriterio
abstract: The objective of this research was to determine the most economical and technically appropriate alternative for the maintenance of a flexible pavement by integrating functional pavement evaluation and multi-criteria analysis techniques, using Eloy Alfaro Street in the Rocafuerte canton as a case study. The Pavement Condition Index (PCI) methodology was applied to evaluate the pavement's condition. abstract: Objectives: The association between adult height and blood pressure (BP) remains inconsistent across populations. We aimed to evaluate this association in a cohort of clinically healthy adults from Mexico City, Mexico. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of non-diabetic, normotensive adults residing in Mexico City. title: Re-entrant, Strut-Based, and Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Lattice Designs for Cobalt–Chromium Dental Frameworks via Additive Manufacturing
abstract: Background: This study investigates the potential of lattice structures in metal-ceramic frameworks for dental prostheses. Metal-ceramic restorations, used in both implant-supported and tooth-supported applications, often suffer from excessive weight due to their solid structure. Additive manufacturing offers a solution by enabling the creation of lightweight, complex internal geometries. This research comparatively analyzes re-entrant, strut-based, and triply periodic minimal surfaces lattice geometries in the pontic region of 3-unit metal-ceramic frameworks. title: Knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of local communities towards carnivores and their conservation in the human dominated Sirso landscape, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: Carnivores are increasingly recognized as engines of sustainable development because they contribute to ecological integrity, human well-being, and socio-economic sustainability. Understanding local knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions towards carnivores is therefore essential for effective conservation in human-dominated landscapes. Yet these human dimensions remain poorly understood in the Sirso landscape of southern Ethiopia. To address this gap, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 343 households in 2025. title: Pakistan’s missing indigenous satellite launch vehicle and the search for orbital sovereignty
abstract: In the 21st century, outer space has become a decisive domain of national power. Space Race 2.0 is gaining momentum as space barriers are brought down and the launch capability of a state into space has become a criterion of its strategic autonomy. While Pakistan is a nuclear-power state and has a robust ballistic-missile program, it lacks an indigenous Satellite launch Vehicle (SLV). The operational satellites of Pakistan, including EO-3 launched in April 2026, continue to rely on foreign launch providers. title: Multi-scenario interaction design for aerial–ground collaborative operation and maintenance: A case study of underground pipeline robots
abstract: With the rapid rise of the low-altitude economy, the coordination between aerial and ground intelligent equipment has become a critical challenge in urban infrastructure maintenance. This study proposes a Multi-Scenario Adaptive Interaction Design (MSAID) framework for operation and maintenance (O&M) systems integrating low-altitude unmanned platforms and underground pipeline robots. Guided by a human–machine–environment model, the research constructs a multi-scenario collaboration mechanism encompassing routine inspection, emergency maintenance, and remote decision-making. title: Impact of altitudinal climate variability on fruit productivity in the Kumaun Himalaya
abstract: Climate change is altering horticultural productivity in mountain ecosystems, yet region-specific assessments of altitudinal climatic shifts and their impact on fruit yields remain limited. This study examines the long-term climatic trends (1990–2025) across three elevation zones in the Nainital district of the Kumaun Himalaya: Foot Hill (< 600 m), Mid-Hill (600–1200 m), and Mountain (> 1200 m). Climate variations were assessed using the ERA5-Land datasets; we quantified variations in temperature, rainfall, surface latent heat flux, and solar radiation. title: Recent Development and Applications of Peridynamics to Fatigue Failure Analysis: A Critical Review
abstract: Peridynamics (PD) provides a nonlocal framework for modeling fatigue damage and evolving cracks without prescribing their final paths. This review examines how mechanical formulations, cyclic constitutive models, and fatigue laws determine PD predictions across crack initiation, propagation, and total life. Applications to variable‐amplitude loading, interacting cracks, heterogeneous materials, and environmental coupling are assessed. title: CEO overconfidence and the linguistic representation of corporate culture in 10-K filings: evidence from upper echelons theory
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether chief executive officer (CEO) overconfidence is associated with the linguistic representation of corporate culture in mandatory 10-K filings. Drawing on upper echelons theory, we argue that executives' psychological traits surface not only in strategic and financial outcomes but in the language through which corporate culture is communicated to external stakeholders, across the dimensions of control, collaboration, competition, and creation. abstract: Este capítulo presenta un flujo de edición no lineal con Adobe Premiere Pro que conecta la organización de los materiales con la construcción del relato audiovisual. Explica la configuración de proyectos y secuencias, la función de los principales paneles y la clasificación de recursos mediante contenedores. journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social

title: Legume intercropping and legume powder reduce sorghum seed-borne fungal infection and preserve seed quality during storage
abstract: Seed-borne fungal pathogens severely threaten sustainable sorghum production in sub-Saharan Africa, causing poor seedling emergence and significant yield loss. This study investigated how sorghum-legume intercropping affects seed-borne fungal infections and evaluated the efficacy of legume-derived botanical preparations in preserving sorghum seed quality during storage. title: Los Pilares de la Competitividad Empresarial en Bogotá: Un Análisis de la Eficiencia, la Innovación y la Adaptabilidad Organizacional
abstract: Resumen Este artículo examina la relación de asociación entre factores estratégicos y el desempeño organizacional en Bogotá D.C. La investigación se centra en cómo la Eficiencia en la Gestión de Recursos, la Innovación y la Adaptabilidad Organizacional inciden en la productividad y competitividad de las empresas de los sectores financiero, transportista y droguista. El entorno de negocios actual requiere que estas organizaciones optimicen continuamente sus activos, sean ágiles en la innovación y muestren adaptabilidad (Morales Guerrero & Álvarez Aros, 2021). title: Role of Spirulina and plant resins in sustainable edible packaging and smart food preservation systems
abstract: As the world goes circular, there is a growing need for sustainable substitutes of petroleum-based food packaging. The present article explores the potential of biopolymers produced from Spirulina platensis for facilitating the development of novel bioactive packaging materials. Due to their inherent antibacterial and antioxidant properties, the issues discussed herein address the challenges of minimizing plastic waste generation and improving food safety at the same time. title: Ag‐Doped CuO Nanoparticle‐Decorated CuO Nanorod Electrodes for Multifunctional Energy Storage and Nonenzymatic Glucose Sensing
abstract: Herein, CuO nanorods decorated with Ag‐doped CuO nanoparticles were directly synthesized on a FTO substrate using a facile two‐step technique involving hydrothermal growth and dip‐coating deposition. The effect of Ag incorporation on the morphology was examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). title: Adaptive Compound Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings Under Strong Background Noise: A Hybrid Framework Integrating Improved CEEMDAN With VMD Guided‐MCKD
abstract: In practical mechanical systems, the measured fault signals of rolling bearings are often submerged by strong background noise, making it difficult to extract compound fault features. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fault signal processing framework that integrates Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) guided‐Maximum Correlated Kurtosis Deconvolution (MCKD). abstract: Evaluating organizational efficiency, particularly against competitors, is essential for identifying improvement opportunities. This study introduces a novel model to assess the efficiency of container ports using a Network Data Envelopment Analysis (NDEA) approach that accounts for internal port structures. The model defines five functional sections: official, structural, operational, storage, and communicational, with input/output variables based on their interrelations. title: Green hydrogen from curtailment: Real data analysis
abstract: As renewable energy capacity has expanded worldwide, curtailment has emerged as a critical issue owing to transmission constraints and mismatches between generation and demand, resulting in significant energy losses. This study assesses the techno-economic potential of green hydrogen production by utilizing real data of curtailed electricity from wind and photovoltaic sources distributed over more than 2000 km and belonging to a single electrical system. Based on real curtailment data from 100 projects over one year of operation, it characterizes the temporal curtailment patterns and estimates

title: La integración de la inteligencia artificial en el Espacio de Libertad, Seguridad y Justicia: avances en el ámbito de la cooperación judicial civil
abstract: Este estudio analiza la transformación de la cooperación judicial civil en la Unión Europea a través de la digitalización y la inteligencia artificial. El Reglamento (UE) 2023/2844 instaura el principio de digital por defecto para las comunicaciones transfronterizas, apoyado en la infraestructura e-CODEX y el marco de confianza digital eIDAS 2.0. title: Avances en las técnicas de cirugía plástica reconstructiva para el tratamiento de defectos complejos de tejidos blandos. Revisión sistematica
abstract: Introducción: Los defectos complejos de tejidos blandos, caracterizados por la pérdida de cobertura cutánea, volumen y estructuras de soporte, representan un desafío reconstructivo de alta complejidad. Esta revisión sistemática tiene como pregunta guía: ¿cuáles son los avances en las técnicas de cirugía plástica reconstructiva para el tratamiento de defectos complejos de tejidos blandos y qué evidencia respalda su efectividad? title: The earliest representative of the Megaviverra– Civettictis lineage (Mammalia, Carnivora, Viverridae) from the Arabian Peninsula documents Late Miocene dispersal between Asia and Africa
abstract: The Late Miocene fossil record of large viverrids is sparse, limiting understanding of their origin, early evolution, and dispersal. Here we describe Promegaviverra abudhabiensis gen. et sp. nov ., a new large viverrid from the Late Miocene Baynunah Formation of Abu Dhabi (c. 7 Ma, United Arab Emirates), representing the first definitive viverrid from the Arabian Peninsula. title: Comparison of two related Roscoea species with different mating systems demonstrates the importance of confounding evolutionary and ecological factors
abstract: The mating system of plants is a pivotal determinant in shaping genetic diversity and fine‐scale spatial genetic structure (FSGS), with self‐fertilizing species generally demonstrating reduced genetic diversity and more pronounced FSGS compared to outcrossing species. Nevertheless, the extent to which this pattern is modulated by the interplay of population history, microhabitat variability, and seed dispersal mechanisms across different habitats remains insufficiently explored. title: Asymmetric and dynamic effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia
abstract: Climate variability poses escalating risks to agricultural systems in fragile and climate-exposed regions, yet evidence on asymmetric and dynamic production responses remains limited. This study investigates the short-run and long-run effects of climate variability on crop and livestock production in Somalia using annual data for 1989–2021. Crop and livestock production indices from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) are combined with rainfall and temperature data from the Climatic Research Unit (CRU). title: Bank Taxation as Financial Regulation
abstract: After the 2008 Financial Crisis, regulators in the United States and abroad enacted a wide range of policies designed to strengthen the financial system. Despite considering several proposed changes to the tax code, lawmakers almost exclusively relied on other regulatory tools. That inaction was a missed opportunity, and the consequences of that oversight persist. Tax policy is an underappreciated dimension of financial regulation. title: Deterministic modeling of nanofluid stability in high-viscosity biodiesels: a Tri-Coupled Fluid–Acoustic–Particle Framework
abstract: Background The synthesis of stable nanofluids within high-viscosity biofuel matrices is often limited by the complex coupling between fluid rheology and acoustic physics. This study proposes a predictive “Tri-Coupled Fluid–Acoustic–Particle Framework” that numerically integrates fuel physicochemical properties, acoustic impedance matching, and deagglomeration kinetics. title: Disentangling public and private sector uses of open-source intelligence through the analysis of their divergent histories
abstract: The focus of this paper is the assertion that Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) is a term that covers a range of similar but functionally different disciplines. Analysis of the histories of different communities of practice reveals the reasons for these functional differences in a way that may allow for further nuance in the crafting of definitions. This paper tests that theory by comparing the history of public sector OSINT with private sector counterparts in both the commercial sphere and in what is sometimes referred to as the Online Investigative Community.

title: Sparse multi-channel simultaneous seismic impedance inversion in the Laplace–Fourier domain for well-free low-frequency recovery
abstract: Seismic acoustic impedance (AI) inversion is fundamentally ill-posed due to the band-limited nature of recorded seismic wavefields. In frontier exploration areas lacking reliable well controls, establishing an accurate low-frequency background model (typically 0–10 Hz) is difficult. title: Generating Mitigations for Downstream Projects to Neutralize Upstream Library Vulnerability
abstract: Third-party libraries are essential in software development as they prevent the need for developers to recreate existing functionalities. However, vulnerabilities within these libraries pose significant risks to dependent projects. Upgrading dependencies is infeasible when no patched version is available or when downstream projects have strict version constraints. Moreover, repairing the vulnerability proves challenging when the source code of the library is inaccessible. title: Mexican breast cancer consensus. Management of advanced breast cancer
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common neoplasia, with the highest mortality in women worldwide.The 10 th update of the Mexican Consensus on Diagnosis and Treatment of Breast Cancer (2023) is published by its authors in different articles.This article includes the management of advanced breast cancer, the adjuvant systemic treatment, the role of surgery and radiotherapy in metastatic disease, and follow-up after treatment with curative intent.The dissemination of this consensus contributes to the updating and homogeneity of breast cancer management of advanced stages.

abstract: Introduction: Informal caregiving for people with Alzheimer disease creates demands that affect caregiver health in ways not always captured by standard assessment. Objective: To identify caregiver burden profiles based on burden, stress, and executive function, and the contribution of the latter. Methods: Cross-sectional study in 84 informal caregivers of people with Alzheimer disease in Punta Arenas, Chile, assessed with the Zarit Burden Interview, the Stress Coping Questionnaire, the Trail Making Test, and the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Index. title: Immune microenvironmental regulation of odontogenic differentiation in dental pulp stem cells: mechanisms, signaling networks, and regenerative strategies
abstract: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) are a promising cell source for dentin regeneration, but their regenerative behavior is strongly shaped by the local immune microenvironment. This review integrates evidence on immune mediators, immune cell–DPSC interactions, intracellular signaling, and immunomodulatory biomaterials. Particular attention is given to how mediator concentration and exposure duration influence the balance between inflammatory injury and differentiation-associated responses. abstract: Multifunctional conductive textiles are essential components of emerging wearable electronic systems. However, simultaneously achieving high electrical conductivity, long-term environmental stability, textile-compatible manufacturing, and integrated device functions remains challenging.
