title: Didáctica de la educación religiosa escolar en la cultura digital
abstract: This article analyzes how ICT contribute to the development of SRE within the framework of Colombian holistic education. A qualitative study was adopted, combining ethnography and bibliometric analysis aimed at understanding perceptions, trends, and challenges. The findings show that SRE is broadly valued as a pathway for cultivating the religious and spiritual dimensions and for accompanying the search for meaning. abstract: En un contexto empresarial caracterizado por la creciente generación de información, la aceleración tecnológica y la necesidad de responder oportunamente a las exigencias de los mercados, la inteligencia de negocios (Business Intelligence, BI) se ha consolidado como un componente estratégico para la gestión organizacional. title: Minimum wage policy and innovation strategy: Evidence from Chinese industrial firms
abstract: We examine the impact of the minimum wage policy on firms’ innovation strategies. Using a sample of Chinese industrial firms consisting predominantly of manufacturing firms, we find that upon an increase in the local minimum wage, firms adjust their innovation strategies to focus more on process innovation. title: Building an inclusive scientific enterprise: institutional pathways for innovation and equity in Canadian science
abstract: Inclusion and diversity in science are essential to fostering innovation, particularly as the scientific community is increasingly called upon to address global challenges such as climate change, an equitable energy transition, and rising wealth and income inequality. However, the scientific community has come under heightened scrutiny, as shown by declining public trust and persistent gaps in representation and diversity across scientific fields. title: Phenylketonuria worldwide: geographic genotype and phenotype structure, birth prevalence and newborn-screening context
abstract: Phenylketonuria (PKU), caused by phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) deficiency, comprises a continuum from mild hyperphenylalaninemia (MHP) to mild and classic PKU. We characterized the contemporary global geographic and epidemiological landscape of this spectrum using an international genotype-phenotype database and a structured synthesis of birth-prevalence and newborn-screening evidence. The database contained 24,718 unique anonymized individuals representing 4867 distinct biallelic PAH genotypes. title: Chromium pollution and its effects on soil health, microbial diversity, and sugarcane production in the Vellore sugarcane belt: a metagenomic and geochemical assessment
abstract: Disposal of tannery effluent has elevated soil chromium (Cr) across the Vellore sugarcane belt of southern India, yet its integrated consequences for soil health, bacterial communities and sugarcane productivity remain poorly characterised. Specifically, we ask: (a) What is the vegetation and habitat diversity of Caucasian wetlands accompanying travertine-forming springs? title: Aliens hiding in greenhouses: update of scale insects (Hemiptera: Coccomorpha) diversity on botanical gardens of Germany, with six new records for the country
abstract: Botanical gardens provide important services for research, education and the conservation of plant diversity. Many of these activities depend on the movement of plant material, which inevitably includes alien organisms. One such group is scale insects (Hemiptera, Coccomorpha), obligate phytophagous insects with agricultural implications. title: Exploring Small State Offensive Strategies (SSOS) in International Relations: A Conceptual Analysis
abstract: Traditionally seen as passive actors, small states have often relied on defensive strategies in international relations. However, this article challenges that view by exploring how small states can adopt proactive and offensive strategies to influence global affairs. abstract: INTRODUCTION: (Zydus Lifesciences Ltd., Ahmedabad, India), a novel aflibercept biosimilar (Afl-Bs), in treatment-naïve eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular oedema (DME), retinal vein occlusion (RVO) or myopic macular neovascularization (MNV). title: Identifiability and scaling limits of field sap-flow phenotyping: a two-season case study of the vapour pressure deficit response in maize and grain sorghum
abstract: The limited-transpiration phenotype, a plateau in transpiration above a threshold vapour pressure deficit (VPD), is invoked to explain why grain sorghum conserves soil water better than maize. Most evidence comes from controlled environments, where VPD is imposed, and radiation is held constant. We treat a two-season field dataset as a methodological case study and ask whether such a threshold is identifiable from stem heat balance records. title: Bryophyte diversity and community turnover along an elevational gradient in the high-altitude region of Mila Mountain, Xizang, China
abstract: Introduction Bryophyte diversity and community turnover remain insufficiently documented along high-altitude elevational gradients on the Xizang Plateau. We investigated these patterns on the eastern slope of Mila Mountain. Methods We surveyed 146 quadrats (0.25 m² each) across seven sites (4,079–5,230 m a.s.l.), obtaining 1,085 specimen records. title: From Manuscript to Visualisation: A Digital Approach to Medieval Livonian Craft Ordinances
abstract: Medieval Livonian craft ordinances have often been reproduced and examined by researchers, but they have not previously been compiled into a single edition. The digitisation of these sources is not just a matter of access and preservation; it also offers an opportunity for further scholarly analysis by transforming dispersed manuscripts into a structured corpus of data. This corpus enables new forms of comparison, corpus analysis, and visualisation, while also exposing the limits of interpretation in data-driven approaches to the normative sources of medieval towns.

title: Educational attainment and continuing learning engagement as links between parental educational capital and adult happiness across ages in China
abstract: Background Research often examines educational attainment and adult learning separately. Less is known about their joint associations with happiness after family educational background is considered. Age is relevant because opportunities and purposes for learning differ across adulthood. Methods We analyzed 5,162 adults from the face-to-face component of the 2023 Chinese General Social Survey. title: Safety Risk Classification of a Marble Gang Saw Machine Using Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)
abstract: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) was applied to a gang saw machine operating in a marble processing facility in the Aegean Region of Türkiye, where 74 personnel work under a two-shift production system. The analysis aimed to identify and prioritize occupational safety risks associated with the cutting line under actual operating conditions**, focusing on a single high risk production machine rather than on a plant wide assessment. title: A fracability evaluation method for low-permeability sandstone-hosted uranium deposits and its application
abstract: Poor injectability and limited recoverability remain key technical challenges restricting the efficient exploitation of low-permeability sandstone-hosted uranium deposits. Hydraulic micro-fracturing is an effective approach for improving permeability, and fracability evaluation provides a critical basis for selecting favorable ore-bearing intervals for fracturing. title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
abstract: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive. This paper presents Information as a controlled executive within the organogram of duality-immune, autonomous consciousness. title: The Sense of Oblivion: Johann Samuel Stryk’s De Jure Oblivionis and the Lost History of Legal Forgetting
abstract: This article is the first to discuss Johann Samuel Stryk’s 1692 essay on the “law of oblivion” in early modern jurisprudence. title: The Jurisprudence of Institutional Ignorance: When Should the Law Hold Public Authorities Responsible for What They Failed to Know?
abstract: Legal accountability is usually organised around what an institution did, what it knew, or what it ought to have known. Each formulation treats the institution’s state of knowledge as a fact to be discovered, when it is frequently a condition the institution itself produced. Public authorities, regulators, financial institutions and large corporations now decide through information systems they design, fund, staff and prune, so that what such an organization does not know is often the result of choices about what to collect, what to keep, whom to hear and which warnings to send upward. abstract: Since 2019, eighteen NSF Research Traineeship (NRT) awards in quantum information science and engineering (QISE) and adjacent fields have been funded, constituting the largest NSF-coordinated investment in graduate QISE training in the United States. abstract: Introduction Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent late sequelae of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). While total body irradiation (TBI) is an established risk factor, the toxicity of alkylating agent-based conditioning regimens remains poorly characterized. abstract: This study evaluated practical diets containing 10% of selected alternative protein sources, including black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) meal, mealworm meal, Spirulina platensis , Gammarus spp. meal, and glandless cottonseed kernel powder (GCKP), in juvenile guppy ( Poecilia reticulata ). abstract: Background Caffeine has been proposed as a photoprotective agent, but its effects on ultraviolet (UV)-induced photoaging may vary by dose and biological endpoint. This study investigated whether the effects of oral caffeine in a rat model of UV-induced photoaging differed across three doses and multiple biological endpoints. abstract: Seed vigor is a seed-lot property that describes the potential for rapid, uniform emergence and normal seedling establishment across various environmental conditions. abstract: Aim Bradyarrhythmia is a prevalent cardiac disorder often necessitating lifelong pacemaker implantation, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated the role of Peroxiredoxin 3 (PRDX3), a mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme, in the pathogenesis of bradyarrhythmia. Methods A rat model of bradyarrhythmia was constructed. title: From the microscope to high‐performance computing centres, a national effort towards automated data workflows for microscopy facility users in France
abstract: Modern biological microscopy routinely generates large and complex image datasets, including multidimensional, multimodal, and time-resolved acquisitions. While imaging technologies have rapidly evolved, data management infrastructures within microscopy facilities often remain fragmented, relying on heterogeneous local solutions that are difficult to maintain, scale, and integrate with high-performance computing (HPC) centres and public data repositories. abstract: Education on the energy transition is necessary to address the problem of unemployment among students in our country. abstract: Phase change materials (PCMs) offer high latent heat and near‐isothermal heat storage and release, making them attractive for thermal energy storage and regulation. abstract: Extreme climate events impose significant impacts across the Horn of Africa. One way to monitor these is by using novel digital tools to forecast extreme events and climate-sensitive disease outbreaks. However, limited information exists on stakeholder use of such tools. This qualitative study identified key multidisciplinary stakeholders in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda, and conducted a needs assessment and gap analysis. abstract: This study explores how major geopolitical conflicts such as the Russia–Ukraine war, Israel–Palestine conflict, and instability in the Democratic Republic of the Congo affect global trade and economic stability in an increasingly interconnected world. Using a meta-analysis of research studies published between 2020 and 2025, it brings together evidence on how conflicts disrupt trade flows, weaken GDP growth, increase inflation, and destabilize supply chains, investment, and financial systems. title: Variations and influential factors of the seed oxygen isotope ratios across 42 forest plant species
abstract: Oxygen isotope ratios ( 18 O/ 16 O, hereafter δ 18 O) of plant tissues are widely used for various purposes, including paleoclimatic reconstruction, identification of the geographical origin of plant-based products, and understanding plant water use. On the other hand, δ 18 O values of seeds have been rarely measured. abstract: In order to provide access to formal education for all children in the economy, successive governments, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), and public-spirited individuals have contributed in rescuing trafficked children and reintegrate them into the school system. abstract: Introduction Cochlear implants (CIs) can restore speech perception in individuals with severe cochlear hearing loss. However, access to paraverbal cues, such as emotional prosody, remains limited, particularly in electronic communication, where speech is often digitally compressed. Methods This study compares CI users and normal-hearing (NH) listeners in their ability to recognize basic emotions from neutral sentences presented either as uncompressed audio or audio processed using common audio codecs (MP3, SPEEX, AMR-WB), measuring accuracy, response time, and confidence. title: Soft spatial imaginaries as a regional dynamic capability
abstract: Soft spatial imaginaries offer a novel conceptualisation of a regional dynamic capability to adapt to and shape collective action on regional development challenges towards desirable futures. This capability encompasses six dimensions embedded within a time- and region-specific opportunity space: sensing change, seizing opportunities, transforming organisations, boundary organisations, place leadership and continuous activity. abstract: La disponibilidad limitada de materiales didácticos en instituciones públicas de educación inicial de Durán y Guayaquil, Zona 8 de Ecuador, plantea la necesidad de diversificar los recursos narrativos mediante alternativas contextualizadas. Numerous dietary supplements enriched in omega-3 fatty acids were tested in patients with neurodegenerative diseases, as decreased levels of DHA were demonstrated in the central nervous system and plasma of patients and animal models. abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the levels, network structure, and gender differences of positive youth development (PYD) attributes in a sample of rural adolescents in southern China. A total of 3,924 adolescents from five secondary schools were recruited, with 3,753 valid participants included in the analyses after data screening (Male: 43.8%, M age = 15.12). abstract: Managing white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) in prawn farms relies on fit‐for‐purpose in‐house tests (IHTs), for instance, to confirm WSSV infection during disease outbreaks. Selecting and interpreting fit‐for‐purpose IHTs requires robust evidence on their diagnostic accuracy. abstract: Whether evolutionary radiations are primarily driven by ecological or neutral processes remains an unresolved question. The karst-endemic genus Petrocodon, distributed across southern China and northern Indochina, provides a powerful system for testing these alternatives. abstract: Flooding stress (FS) is a major abiotic constraint that negatively affects crop growth and productivity by disrupting photosynthesis, water balance, oxidative homeostasis, and hormonal regulation. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) represent a sustainable strategy for improving crop resilience under waterlogging conditions. abstract: Landau–Kleffner syndrome (LKS) is a rare epileptic disorder characterized by the loss of receptive and expressive language skills following normotypical development. This study aims to design an educational proposal based on playful strategies to promote language development in a 9-year and 5-month-old child diagnosed with LKS. The research adopts a mixed-methods approach using a single-case study design. abstract: Forest humus soil (FHS) harbors highly diverse microbial communities driving carbon transformation, yet genomic resources and strategies underlying lignocellulolysis remain poorly understood. abstract: Soil erosion poses a severe environmental challenge in Ethiopian highlands, threatening agricultural productivity, water quality, and rural livelihoods. This study evaluated soil erosion dynamics over 24 years (2001–2025) in the Muger River Watershed using the revised universal soil loss equation (RUSLE) model integrated with geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sensing. abstract: This study examines the trade–environment nexus in India over 1991–2023, focusing on the scale, composition, and technical effects of trade and testing the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) and Pollution Haven Hypothesis (PHH). abstract: Clean-label processing and reformulation of meat and animal-based foods have received increasing attention in response to consumer demand for simplified ingredient lists and minimally processed products. abstract: Camel farming occupies a growing place in the Mauritanian pastoral economy. abstract: To address the deficiencies of existing railway scheduling schemes—namely, insufficient intelligence, ineffective utilization of multi-source heterogeneous IoT sensor data, and weak real-time dynamic resource allocation capability—this paper reviews the literature and identifies that conventional algorithms suffer from low computational efficiency, poor generalization, and a lack of IoT-oriented multi-agent fusion mechanisms. abstract: The first 1,000 days of life, spanning from preconception through early childhood, represent a highly sensitive developmental window during which nutritional exposures may exert long-lasting effects on health. Optimal nutrition during this period is foundational not only for favorable birth outcomes and infant growth but also for establishing long-term metabolic homeostasis and neurodevelopmental trajectories. abstract: This study examines how geopolitical risk, economic policy uncertainty, and tourism uncertainty are associated with ESG uncertainty across G7 countries using monthly data from November 2002 to February 2025. abstract: Land-use planning is essential for climate adaptation and mitigation, but local authorities often lack decision-support tools that effectively link scientific modeling with place-based knowledge. This paper shares findings from RethinkAction, a project that co-developed an Integrated Assessment Platform with stakeholders across six diverse European regions: semi-arid, island, alpine, temperate, continental, and Atlantic. abstract: When buildings are damaged or destroyed by earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, or armed conflict, asbestos-containing materials embedded in the built environment may be fragmented and mixed with concrete, bricks, soil, and other disaster or conflict-related debris, which is potential health and environmental risks. abstract: MOTIVATION: DNA methylation profiling is widely used for tumour classification, biomarker discovery and the identification of molecular subgroups. abstract: This article examines how conspiratorial climate claims on TikTok are constructed through multimodality, meaning made through visuals, sound, and text, and function as climate obstruction. abstract: The waggle dance reports an outbound flight vector with a ritualized whole-body movement to a location in the environment surrounding the bee colony. abstract: Auxin homoeostasis is a critical determinant of plant growth and environmental adaptation, yet its precise role and regulatory mechanisms in Verticillium wilt resistance remain largely unexplored. abstract: This study integrates the digitalisation and dynamic capabilities literature to examine the relationship between digitalisation, eco‐innovation and internationalisation in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SME). abstract: In recent decades, the international dissemination of contemporary Chinese literature has gained increasing prominence within broader cultural exchange initiatives aimed at enhancing cross-cultural dialog and global cultural presence. abstract: Information operations succeed when a target audience simultaneously clears three conditions—congruence, self-efficacy, and value of information—and the weakest condition, not the average, determines behavioral outcomes. Where current doctrine prescribes processes but cannot predict effects, the Informational Decision Triad equips the Joint Force to forecast whether a message will change behaviors before operations launch and to weigh influence risks with the rigors of kinetic targeting. abstract: La incorporación del talento joven al sector logístico constituye uno de los principales retos estratégicos para las organizaciones, en un contexto fuertemente marcado por la digitalización y el cambio generacional. abstract: In June 2025 and February 2026, the wars involving the United States, Israel and Iran led to content about nuclear war being posted on social media, particularly on TikTok and Instagram. abstract: This research examines how majority members' perceived threat (symbolic and realistic) and tolerance motives (respect and coexistence) relate to their willingness to permit minority practices across two national contexts—Italy ( N = 268) and Türkiye ( N = 220). title: Soil profile characteristics and variability of physical and chemical properties in clove-growing areas of baolan, Indonesia
abstract: This study characterized soil-profile morphology and variability in the physical and chemical properties of clove-dominated mixed gardens in Baolan District, Tolitoli Regency, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. Sampling sites were identified using GIS-based overlay analysis of land use, slope, and elevation, followed by field verification. Of 27 candidate sites, 21 soil profiles were selected across nine villages and nine mapped soil units, at elevations of 5.54–311.39 m and slopes ranging from 0–8% to above 45%. Effective soil depth ranged from 97 to 126 cm, with three to six horizons per profile.

abstract: With the increasing prevalence of diseases associated with gut dysbiosis, such as gastrointestinal diseases, immunological disorders, metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, and cancer, there is a growing need for effective strategies to restore the gut microbiota and promote overall health. abstract: Introduction Migrant children navigate intersecting social systems and oppressions (e.g., racism, poverty) that can contribute to worse health outcomes, including pain. abstract: Positive mental health literacy (PMHL) is an important resource for promoting psychological wellbeing and resilience. Research on teachers’ mental health literacy has, however, concentrated on the recognition of mental illness among in-service teachers; its positive dimension has rarely been examined among pre-service teachers, and never in relation to their motivation for entering the profession. abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AR) in industrial strains of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) poses a critical safety concern, as these microorganisms can serve as reservoirs and vectors for AR within the food chain. LAB isolates obtained from human or animal samples may harbor AR genes as a result of selective pressure from antibiotics. Traditional products derived from pasture-raised animals that do not receive feed additives serve as a possible source of AR-free LAB. title: Improving weather radar rainfall estimates by merging with commercial microwave link data: a fully reproducible, large-scale method intercomparison
abstract: Accurate rainfall estimation is essential for hydrometeorological applications, but capturing the fine spatiotemporal variability of rainfall remains challenging. In this study, we assess the impact of merging commercial microwave link (CML) data with weather radar for quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) using two openly available datasets with contrasting observational densities. We compare multiple merging methods, including kriging with external drift (KED), and derive a block kriging interpolation method to account for the line-average nature of CMLs. title: A new species of Hemiphyllodactylus Bleeker, 1860 (Squamata, Gekkonidae) from northern Vietnam
abstract: A new species of the gekkonid genus Hemiphyllodactylus is described from the evergreen forest in Ba Vi National Park, Hanoi City, northern Vietnam. Hemiphyllodactylus baviensis sp. nov . is distinguished from the remaining congeners by having a unique combination of the morphology and significant sequence divergence. Phylogenetic analyses based on a fragment of the mitochondrial ND2 gene recovered the Ba Vi population as a distinct and well-supported lineage within the clade of the Hemiphyllodactylus typus group. title: Ionospheric scintillation during the recovery phase of the May 2024 superstorm over mid- and low-latitude East Asia
abstract: Observations of strong GNSS scintillation over low- and middle-latitude East Asia during geomagnetic storm recovery phases remain limited, especially those combining multiple GNSS stations, multiple constellations, and ionosonde measurements. This study used GPS, BDS, and Galileo observations from five GNSS stations of the Chinese Meridian Project, together with measurements from three colocated digital ionosondes, to investigate the spatial and temporal evolution of ionospheric scintillation and related F-region structures during the recovery phase of the May 2024 super geomagnetic storm over

title: Vegetation and water level-dependent emission factors for moist to wet bog peatlands in Germany
abstract: Drained peatlands and other organic soils are important sources of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in many countries. They are included in national GHG inventories, which necessitates transparent and consistent upscaling methods. Focussing on moist to wet sites on bog peat without or with low-intensity agricultural use in Germany, we developed an emission model based on published annual carbon dioxide and methane budgets. title: Does ‘Betting‐Style’ Horizontal Ecological Compensation Increase Corporate Financialization? Evidence From the Perspective of Corporate Real‐to‐Virtual Transformation
abstract: ‘Betting‐style’ horizontal ecological compensation (BHEC) is a recent innovation in China's ecological governance, and its effectiveness depends on the response strategies adopted by polluting firms. This study employs a time‐varying difference‐in‐differences model to assess the impact of BHEC on corporate financialization. The results show that BHEC does not push firms from the real economy toward the virtual economy; rather, it curbs corporate financialization. This effect is achieved partly by promoting research and development, thereby redirecting resources away from speculative activities

title: Contrasting microbial and environmental associations link water availability to soil multifunctionality in the rhizosheath and bulk soil of Eremopyrum distans
abstract: Introduction Changes in water availability can alter soil resources and microbial communities, but whether association structures linking water availability to soil multifunctionality (SMF) differ between the root–soil interface and bulk soil remains unclear. Methods We subjected Eremopyrum distans to five water treatments over one growing season and assessed dimension-weighted and threshold-based SMF, together with bacterial, fungal and protistan community attributes, in the rhizosheath and bulk soil. abstract: La composición y el encuadre organizan la información visual y condicionan la interpretación de una escena. El capítulo estudia el encuadre como una selección de lo visible y establece diferencias entre el espacio físico, el representado y el percibido. title: Development of flax/kenaf hybrid epoxy composites incorporating sugarcane biochar with enhanced fire performance for potential electrical conduit applications
abstract: This study examines the effect of sugarcane biochar on the structural, mechanical, thermal, and fire-related behaviour of flax/kenaf/flax hybrid epoxy composites with different weight contents of biochar (0–6 wt%). FTIR analysis shows that chemical structure changes may occur and that there might be interactions between the biochar and the epoxy matrix. title: De vigilar a dialogar: seis herramientas freemium para detectar plagio e IA
abstract: El auge de la inteligencia artificial (IA) ha reconfigurado las prácticas académicas, especialmente en lo concerniente al plagio. Este artículo ofrece un análisis crítico sobre seis plataformas freemium de detección de plagio y contenido generado por ia para determinar su efectividad, sesgos y consecuencias pedagógicas. abstract: Business computer networks are essential tools for ensuring interconnectivity and improving service quality within modern organizations. Technology companies such as Cisco Systems and TP-Link have developed economic models focused on providing connectivity solutions adapted to different business levels, from small offices to large corporations. Cisco Systems is recognized for its business model based on high-performance enterprise solutions, offering equipment such as switches, routers, firewalls, and network management platforms. title: Comparative transcriptome analysis of lodging-resistant factors in rice
abstract: Lodging is a major challenge limiting stable rice production and the use of mechanized harvesting, and stem cell wall composition plays a critical role in determining lodging resistance in rice. In this study, two recombinant inbred lines (RILs), R-33 (lodging-resistant) and R-36 (lodging-susceptible), derived from the same population and exhibiting significant differences in the cell wall component contents (cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin) as well as breaking force in mature stems, were subjected to transcriptome sequencing. title: The cost of personalization: campaign finance and women's representation in Turkey's closed list system
abstract: The increasing personalization of election campaigns shifts the campaign activity and its financing away from parties and onto individual candidates. This paper identifies a critical contradiction in Turkish party law—the candidate-finance gap—in which the campaign finance of political parties is heavily regulated while private contributions to individual candidates go entirely unaddressed, creating a gray zone. title: Implicaciones del clima laboral en la maquila: el caso de la fabricación reynosense de maquinaria
abstract: Objective: Given the intensity of manufacturing activity along Mexico's northern border, this study identifies the determinants and implications of the work climate within the bulk of the machinery and equipment maquiladora subsector in Reynosa, focusing on productivity and employee turnover, through the independent application of a structured interview. title: Soft power or hard currency? Rethinking power characterizations through Qatar's resilience case
abstract: Small states such as Qatar are often characterized through dominant power labels such as soft, smart, or other non-conventional forms of power. This paper examines Qatar’s response to the 2017–2021 blockade to assess the explanatory value of such characterizations under a concrete geopolitical stress. Using a qualitative bounded-case design, this study traces the mobilization, timing, and interaction of soft, material/economic, and security resources in relation to Qatar’s resilience. title: Climate change threatens projected habitat suitability and phytochemical quality of Stachys pilifera Benth: a dual-projection modeling approach
abstract: Climate change poses substantial risks to biodiversity, species distributions, and both the compositional consistency and the concentration of bioactive constituents in medicinal plants. Stachys pilifera Benth., valued for its antioxidant and antimicrobial constituents, may experience shifts in both habitat suitability and chemical quality under future climatic regimes. This study integrates ecological niche modeling with chemotypic analysis to assess how climate change could reshape the geographical distribution and secondary-metabolite composition of S. pilifera . abstract: There is an urgent need for climate action by people in the richer parts of the world, for example, politicians and producers, but also ordinary citizens. Many people are concerned about climate change but remain mainly inactive, many are disengaged and some continue to dismiss climate change. The present study investigates how moral imagination can be used in communication at various societal levels to overcome obstacles to climate action. abstract: The present study was conducted during the Rabi season of 2023–24 to evaluate white rust response in Indian mustard germplasm and perform targeted intron-length polymorphism (ILP) marker screening of selected low-PDI entries. Agronomic traits were also recorded as secondary characterization of the germplasm panel. Sixty Indian mustard germplasm lines along with three checks were evaluated in augmented randomized complete block design (augmented RCBD) with a plot size of 2.4 m 2 and spacing of 30 × 10 cm. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To better characterize the clinical phenotypes and heterogeneity of anti-synthetase syndrome (ASyS), we performed unsupervised cluster analyses using clinical and serological data from the Classification Criteria for Anti-Synthetase Syndrome (CLASS) project database. METHODS: The CLASS database comprised 2,035 ASyS cases and 2,140 comparators with mimicking conditions, namely systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases and/or interstitial lung disease (ILD), contributed by 103 centers worldwide. title: Didactic Design for Teaching Algebra in Secondary School Mathematics to Reduce Students’ Mathematics Anxiety
abstract: Mathematics anxiety, the feeling of worry and fear when engaging in mathematical activities, is an ontogenic obstacle (a psychological barrier for students) that hinders the process of abstraction, particularly in the transition from arithmetic reasoning to formal algebra. This study aims to describe a didactical design based on the Function Machine (a visual medium with an input-process-output pattern) that can reduce Grade VII students’ mathematics anxiety in algebra and to analyze their anxiety levels after implementation. abstract: Pyocyanin, a harmful metabolite and a representative virulence determinant of Pseudomonas aeruginosa , is the target analyte of a novel crayfish-type MMF–SMF–MMF biophotonic sensor introduced herein, which integrates rapid response with long-term operational stability. Pyocyanin detection is important for preventing ecological damage, ensuring food-chain safety, and supporting rapid clinical diagnostics. title: How does social media reshape virtual acculturation? A game-mediated framework for cross-cultural adaptation
abstract: This study examines the social and cultural significance of video games as a major form of entertainment among contemporary youth and investigates how social media-mediated game video consumption shapes the interpretation of foreign game cultures. Drawing on a dataset of game videos and 78,169 Danmaku comments from the Chinese social media platform Bilibili, this study employs a multimodal analytical approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), data modeling, and manual coding to explore how culturally salient meanings are identified, elaborated, and circulated in social media inter

title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis in cirrhotic cardiomyopathy: mechanistic gut-liver-heart axis and nutritional microbiota-targeted interventions
abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is an underdiagnosed cardiac complication of end-stage liver cirrhosis without specific targeted therapies. Gut dysbiosis is hypothesized to act as a modifiable upstream regulator along the gut-liver-heart axis. It may contribute to myocardial remodeling through metabolic, inflammatory, autoimmune, and autonomic pathways, although causal evidence specific to CCM remains insufficient. title: Coupled carbon-nitrogen dynamics and soil stabilization under perennial alley cover cropping in raspberry planting
abstract: Agriculture faces the dual challenge of sustaining productivity and mitigating climate change through soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. The current management practice in perennial raspberry production in the Fraser Valley, British Columbia, Canada, pre-disposes the soil to continual degradation via incessant tillage of the alleys with no C input. title: Leadership and organizational sustainability among NGOs working with displaced populations in Greece
abstract: Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) play a central role in ensuring protection, emergency aid and basic services for displaced populations. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources model, this study aims to generate knowledge about how NGO leaders in Greece interpret job demands affecting fieldworkers and organizational functioning, and how resources are mobilized to mitigate these demands and thereby support sustained humanitarian work. title: Role of Networks in Promoting Economic Resilience to Transport Network Failure During Hazards – A Multidisciplinary Review
abstract: Recent global incidents have underscored the critical role of transport networks in the functioning of economic systems. Despite growing interest in understanding the systemic impacts of transport failures on economic resilience, current research remains fragmented across fields such as economic geography, infrastructure planning, network science, and disaster science. abstract: The Oba-Ile area and environs in Akure, southwestern Nigeria, are underlain predominantly by granitoids of the Precambrian Nigerian Basement Complex. This study integrates field mapping, petrography, whole-rock major and selected trace element geochemistry, chemical weathering indices, and multivariate statistical analysis to constrain their geological evolution and petrogenesis. abstract: Driven by global urbanization and the rise of mass tourism, crowding in high-density tourist cities has become a significant concern in the academic community. However, existing studies often lack a systematic categorization of crowding types, resulting in insufficiently targeted governance strategies. abstract: The biology of Protosmia , a species-poor genus of osmiine bees, is only fragmentarily known. We investigated the nesting biology, pollen hosts, and mating behavior of P. glutinosa in central Italy. Females nested in old brood cells of abandoned nests of Megachile (Chalicodoma) apennina and in small holes in a concrete wall. abstract: Soil amendments are important for improving soil quality and increasing nutrient availability, especially in citrus production systems affected by Huanglongbing (HLB). This study evaluated the effects of humic acid (HA), fulvic acid (FA), and sulfuric acid (SA), applied with or without elemental sulfur (S), on soil pH, nutrient availability, and the performance of HLB-affected citrus trees at two Florida sites. title: Prospects for Effective Socio-Ecological Value Creation in Agri-Business: A Case of Vegpro Kenya Limited
abstract: Background Kenya’s agri-business sector operates under growing pressure to reconcile commercial objectives with environmental and social obligations shaped by national policy and international regulatory frameworks. Despite sector-wide adoption of green strategies, persistent bottlenecks in socio-ecological value creation remain poorly understood. This study examines Vegpro Kenya Limited, a major agribusiness exporter, to explore how policy and institutional arrangements, humane entrepreneurship, and network embeddedness shape an organization’s capacity for sustainable value creation. abstract: Introduction Habitat degradation and conservation gaps severely threaten China's endemic montane birds, yet few studies have integrated habitat suitability with quality assessment. abstract: Wind energy is a rapidly expanding renewable resource that plays a pivotal role in the global transition from fossil fuels to sustainable and low-carbon energy systems. However, its potential application requires understanding its intricate dynamics.. The objectives of the present work are to i) evaluate empirically the hypothesis of nonlinearity, determinism and chaotic behavior of wind speed time series and ii) investigate statistical relationships between different nonlinear parameters. title: Exploring the challenges hindering the effectiveness of pastoral-oriented development in the Hamer district, southern Ethiopia
abstract: Pastoral-oriented development (POD) interventions are widely implemented in Ethiopia’s dryland regions to improve pastoral livelihoods, reduce vulnerability, and strengthen adaptation to environmental and socioeconomic challenges. However, the effectiveness of these interventions varies because of environmental uncertainty, institutional constraints, and limited integration of customary governance structures. abstract: The World Trade Organization (WTO) continues to face a deepening crisis that increasingly threatens both the WTO’s relevance and the stability of global trade. abstract: Introduction Internet addiction is associated with poorer adolescent mental health, including non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and suicidal ideation, but the psychological processes that may link them are not well understood. abstract: Hierarchical Fe 3 O 4 /CCF composites were constructed by anchoring planar anisotropic Fe 3 O 4 nanosheets onto submillimeter‐scale carbon fibers derived from waste coconut coir (CCF) through a solvothermal‐carbonization strategy. This design integrates biomass waste upcycling with planar anisotropy engineering, to overcome the snoek's limit of Fe 3 O 4 and introduce interfacial engineering, resulting in synergistic magneto‐dielectric effects for lightweight ultrabroadband microwave absorption. title: Governance Perception & Policy Outcomes in Rural Bangladesh: Voices from the Margins
abstract: Rural governance in Bangladesh is very much linked with the lived experience of citizens in relation to public institutions and public services in everyday life. This study analyses the perception of citizens on rural governance, looking at the three service areas of health, education and agriculture, and a comparison of perceptions by different socio-economic groups. The study also looks at the perception of governance and trust in institutions, especially disadvantaged citizens' experiences. abstract: Background: Extreme temperatures and other climatic stressors are increasingly affecting population health, even in temperate regions such as Germany. Previous studies have demonstrated associations between extreme heat, cold temperatures, and health indicators, including emergency department visits and mortality. However, most analyses rely on coarse meteorological data and hospital-based outcomes, limiting insights into fine-scale spatial variability and prehospital emergency responses. abstract: Urban Iban who keep longhouse apartments, land rights, or obligations raise two questions: what keeps a household a member of a community it no longer lives in, and who decides when its membership ends? title: Decentralized biorefineries for sustainable biochemical production: Techno-economic insights into agro-residue valorization and rural industrialization
abstract: Lignocellulosic agro-residues are an underutilized source of biomass for sustainable biochemical production, especially in agricultural economies like India. This review critically examines the potential of decentralized biorefineries for the conversion of agricultural residues such as rice straw, wheat straw, sugarcane bagasse, cotton stalks, and coconut biomass to value-added products. title: Functional traits and seed morphometry of native trees across an elevational gradient in the tropical montane forest of the Peruvian Andes
abstract: Tropical Andean montane forests constitute a major biodiversity hotspot threatened by land-use change and climate change, yet substantial knowledge gaps remain regarding seed functional traits of native tree species. This study documented seed morphometric diversity and evaluated multivariate patterns across an elevational gradient in Amazonas, northern Peru. abstract: Electrospinning has emerged as a powerful technique for fabricating nanofibrous materials with high surface area, tunable porosity, and extracellular matrix–like mechanical properties. These unique features have enabled its broad application in biomedicine, particularly in regenerative medicine, wound healing, and drug delivery. title: Enhancing nutrient recycling systems in agricultural engineering: Lessons from Fuxian Lake's sustainable practices
abstract: Agricultural non-point source pollution threatens water quality and soil health, particularly in ecologically sensitive lake basins such as Fuxian Lake, China. This study evaluates an integrated nutrient recycling framework that combines engineered interventions, including biochar–microbial synergies, with adaptive policy incentives and real-time monitoring through an Internet of Things (IoT) sensor network. abstract: This study examines whether the tone of earnings conference calls is associated with investors' subsequent use of firms' mandatory disclosure filings. Using conference call transcripts and EDGAR web traffic data from 2007 to 2016, I find that more positive conference call tone is followed by lower subsequent requests for firms' periodic filings. title: Irrigation regime overrides establishment method effects on water, economic and carbon efficiency in rice (Oryza sativa L.)
abstract: Introduction Improving rice sustainability requires maintaining grain yield while reducing irrigation use and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Crop establishment and irrigation management influence these outcomes through different agronomic and resource-use pathways, but their relative contributions to production efficiency and environmental performance need evaluation. This study compared puddled transplanted and dry direct-seeded rice under contrasting irrigation regimes in irrigated rice production systems of northwestern India. Methods A three-year field experiment (2023-2025) was conducted

title: Attribute-Based Assessment of Adaptive Reuse in a Listed Railway Station: Building and Precinct Scales at Canfranc, Spain
abstract: The Canfranc International Railway Station (Huesca, Spain) opened in 1928 and was listed as a monument in 2002. In 2023 it was converted into a hotel, while the wider railway site was restructured. The aim of this study is to develop and apply an evidence-based attribute-coding framework to document which heritage attributes of a large railway complex are preserved, transformed or replaced by adaptive reuse. The framework is applied through a historical–architectural case study that combines fieldwork campaigns (2010–2023), archival sources and planning documents. Significant attributes are id

title: Sustainable development requirements of international investment in China’s IIAs: the context of the BRI
abstract: Introduction Sustainable development, as a widely accepted principle, has gradually been embedded in the realm of international investment in recent decades. The three intersecting elements of sustainable development—economic development, social wellbeing, and environmental protection—have a close nexus with international investment. This paper aims to examine the sustainable development requirements in China’s current international investment agreements (IIAs), including both bilateral investment treaties (BITs) and free trade agreements (FTAs), and to explore the approaches to integrate sust

title: What is therapy in physiotherapy?
abstract: The physiotherapy profession carries the word therapy in its name, yet has never subjected the concept to serious philosophical scrutiny. Where psychologists have interrogated the psyche, nurses the meaning of care, and sociologists the nature of medicine, physiotherapy has no equivalent tradition. It has taken for granted what therapy is in order to build a literature centered on what physiotherapy does. title: Effects of different biochar types on nitrogen retention, soil properties, and maize growth and yield on sandy loam Alfisols
abstract: Background Declining soil fertility and poor nitrogen conservation constrain maize ( Zea mays L.) production on sandy loam Alfisols of Southwest Nigeria. A field experiment was conducted during the 2023 and 2024 cropping seasons to evaluate the effects of different biochar types on soil properties, NO₃ − –N concentration in collected leachate, and maize growth and yield. title: From landrace diversity to promising germplasm for rabi sorghum breeding: unravelling the multi-environment and multi-trait potential of Maldandi sorghum
abstract: Maldandi is an important genetic resource for post-rainy season (rabi) sorghum improvement in India, yet much of the diversity retained within this landrace complex remains underutilized in breeding programs. The present study evaluated 136 Maldandi sorghum landraces across three contrasting rabi environments—Rahuri, Solapur, and Dharwad—to assess their phenotypic diversity, environmental responsiveness, yield stability, and multi-trait breeding potential. title: Dynamic rural greenway exposure: perceived restorativeness and spatial gaze distribution under two video playback implementations
abstract: Introduction Rural greenways are experienced in motion, yet most evidence on perceived restorativeness comes from static images, and little is known about how presentation speed relates to gaze distribution. Methods We quantified ≈230 km of rural greenway (Liyang No. 1 Highway, China) by semantic segmentation at 2,247 sampling points, classified the route into six study-defined greenway categories, and selected one representative one-minute scene per category (scene and category confounded). title: How Job Crafting Enhances Academics’ Well-Being: The Mediating Role of Work Engagement
abstract: Purpose Academics face intense workloads due to multiple roles, publication pressures, project work, administrative responsibilities, and increasing institutional expectations. The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between job crafting and well-being through work engagement. Design/Methods Data were collected through a survey questionnaire from 336 academics working at universities in Türkiye. The validity and reliability of the scales were assessed through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and the research hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling. R

title: Triphala as an antimicrobial: a critical appraisal of the evidence from metabolites and mechanisms to clinical trials
abstract: Introduction Triphala, an Ayurvedic formulation of three botanical drugs rich in plant metabolites, is proposed as an antimicrobial and as an adjunct against antimicrobial resistance. Earlier reviews catalogue its activity but do not test how well the evidence supports these claims. Methods This critical narrative review appraises the strength and validity of the evidence for the antimicrobial activity of Triphala, from metabolites and mechanisms to clinical trials. title: Post-release establishment dynamics of translocated elephants
abstract: Conservation translocations involve pre-release assessment, release, and post-release evaluation. While pre-release habitat assessments identify suitable recipient areas, post-release establishment depends on how animals locate resources, respond to constraints, and develop stable space use. This is especially relevant for large herbivores, whose movements depend on memory and knowledge of resource distributions and whose establishment can shape ecological function. Release into unfamiliar landscapes limits knowledge of resources and constraints, potentially affecting establishment and translo

title: Capítulo 11. Corrección de color y etalonaje
abstract: Este capítulo diferencia la corrección técnica del color y el etalonaje como procesos complementarios de la postproducción audiovisual. La primera equilibra la imagen y mantiene la continuidad entre planos; el segundo desarrolla su tratamiento expresivo y su identidad visual. A partir del matiz, la saturación, la luminosidad y la temperatura de color, se examina cómo las decisiones cromáticas participan en la caracterización de personajes, la organización temporal y la construcción de atmósferas. Las asociaciones emocionales del color se presentan atendiendo a su contexto narrativo y cultural.
journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social

title: Capítulo 10. Adobe Audition
abstract: El capítulo desarrolla los fundamentos de la postproducción sonora con Adobe Audition, desde la grabación y organización del material hasta la mezcla, la masterización y la exportación. Distingue el trabajo sobre archivos individuales en el editor de forma de onda y la construcción de proyectos en el entorno multipista. La configuración técnica, el control de los niveles de entrada y la conservación de los originales se relacionan con la calidad y la seguridad del proceso. Se explican procedimientos de restauración, captura de perfiles de ruido, diagnóstico, procesamiento dinámico y ecualizaci
journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social

title: “All these teachers is my sons”: a teacher educator’s narrative on Black language, Black authority, and lesson planning for Black LGBTQ+ youth in ELA classrooms
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the challenges to assuming authority as a Black teacher educator and what this means for helping teachers design culturally sustaining ELA lessons for Black LGBTQ+ youth. Design/methodology/approach As a reflective narrative, this paper is grounded in the author’s experiential knowledge as a teacher educator and researcher committed to improving the schooling experiences of Black LGBTQ+ youth. title: From Perception to Action: How CSR , Perceived Regulatory Integrity, and Brand Trust Forge Deeper Consumer Bonds in the Hospitality Industry
abstract: This study investigated the relationships between corporate social responsibility (CSR) perception, perceived regulatory integrity, and brand trustworthiness as well as their combined influence on consumer behavior in the hospitality industry by drawing on the signaling theory. The results demonstrated that positive perceptions of CSR significantly impact perceived regulatory integrity and consumer behaviors, which include customer‐company identification, customer advocacy, and customer citizenship behavior, based on a time‐lagged survey that was conducted with tourists in Pakistan at three in

title: Multi-objective optimisation of start-up scheduling for solar-only Micro gas turbine systems
abstract: Solar-only concentrated solar power micro gas turbine (CSP-MGT) systems face unique start-up challenges arising from coupled electro-thermo-mechanical interactions, including compressor surge risk, receiver thermal inertia, and electrical drive constraints, without the benefit of fuel-based regulation. This study presents a multi-objective optimisation framework for start-up scheduling of a 6 kWe parabolic dish CSP-MGT system, based on a validated transient electro-thermo-mechanical model verified against experimental data from the OMSoP project. title: Evidence-gated integration of microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome data reveals a gap between reproducible signals and cross-layer mechanistic evidence in hepatocellular and colorectal cancer
abstract: Introduction Microbiome multi-omics studies frequently identify microbial, metabolic, and host transcriptional associations, but their reproducibility and support for connected biological mechanisms remain uncertain. We evaluated these relationships in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) using an eight-dimensional, non-compensatory evidence-gating framework. title: From primary care centres to community health governance hubs: how decentralisation is transforming sub-district health promoting hospitals in Thailand
abstract: Inroduction Research on Thailand’s transfer of administrative responsibility for sub-district health promoting hospitals (SHPHs) from the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) to Provincial Administrative Organizations (PAOs) has focused primarily on organisational restructuring, with less attention to how decentralisation is reshaping the operational and community roles of these frontline facilities. title: Engineering Vision: The Comparative Role of 3D Printing and 3D Bioprinting in Corneal Regeneration
abstract: Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. Advances in additive manufacturing have positioned 3D printing and 3D bioprinting as promising platforms for fabricating anatomically informed constructs that may recapitulate key aspects of the cornea's hierarchical architecture. title: Research Deconstruction: A Scalable Model for Faculty to Introduce Research Skills in Lower-Division Science Classes
abstract: Synopsis Background Research deconstruction (RD) is a pedagogical strategy used to promote scientific practices and increase science engagement. This approach introduces students to scientific research by “deconstructing” a research seminar led by an invited faculty speaker over several class sessions. This strategy has been shown to increase students' scientific research skills. title: Wolbachia dominance and host-form-consistent geographic structuring of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome across the Republic of Korea
abstract: Mosquito microbiomes are shaped by host genetic background and by the environment, but separating the two in wild populations is difficult, particularly when a single endosymbiont dominates the sequenced community. We present the first nationwide, complex-specific survey of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome in the Republic of Korea: 16S rRNA gene (V3–V4) amplicon sequencing of 29 pools of the two Korean host forms, Cx. pipiens pallens (cpp) and Cx. pipiens form molestus (cpm), collected between 1 and 15 August 2022 from 23 sites in 22 surveillance regions. title: Assessing the Relationship Between Crisis Management Strategies and Organizational Resilience Among SMEs in General Santos City
abstract: This study examined the relationship between crisis management strategies and organizational resilience among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in General Santos City. Using a descriptive-correlational quantitative research design, the study assessed key crisis management dimensions and their influence on organizational resilience. Data were collected from 331 SME respondents and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation, and regression analysis. title: Evaluación postural de la articulación del hombro: fundamentos anatómicos, hallazgos clínicos patológicos y fuerza de prensión manual
abstract: Introduction: The shoulder joint complex is comprised of the glenohumeral, acromioclavicular, sternoclavicular, and scapulothoracic joints. Objective: To analyze the anatomical basis of postural assessment of the shoulder joint and describe the main clinical and pathological findings that distort anatomical landmarks in shoulder postural assessment, as well as the association between postural alterations and handgrip strength. title: Synthetic biology approaches to overcoming the rhizobium competition problem in legume agriculture
abstract: Rhizobia are soil-dwelling bacteria that infect legume plants, inducing the formation of organs called nodules. Within nodules, rhizobia convert atmospheric nitrogen gas to ammonia, providing the plant with an accessible nitrogen source. Rhizobial inoculation has long been recognized as a tactic for providing nitrogen to legume crops; however, the effectiveness of inoculants is often limited by competition from other soil microbes. title: A scalable tumor-vasculature-on-chip for CAR T cell trafficking and efficacy studies
abstract: Most cellular therapies, like CAR T cells, remain ineffective in solid tumors. This is primarily due to a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), which creates biochemically hostile and often immunosuppressive conditions that limit efficacy of immunotherapies. Besides, cellular therapy efficacy is still often established in traditional 2D cultures that fail to simulate relevant aspects of solid tumor biology. title: Quantifying the relationship between prescribed burning and wildfire severity in south-eastern Australia
abstract: High-severity wildfires can pose a critical threat to society and forest ecosystems. While prescribed burning is widely applied to mitigate these risks, evaluation of its effectiveness at the landscape level remains challenging. Factors hindering these assessments include a lack of spatial data quantifying the amount of fuel treatment within burns, and challenges in controlling for variation in environmental conditions (e.g., weather, topography) that affect wildfire severity. title: Edible oil microencapsulation for food fortification: technologies, encapsulating systems, and functional applications
abstract: Food fortification with edible oils improves diet quality, but presents limitations of oxidative instability, off-flavors, and reduced shelf life, which can be overcome by microencapsulation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in edible oil microencapsulation for food fortification. It evaluates core encapsulation techniques, materials, emulsifiers, and microcapsule properties, highlighting their effects on efficiency, morphology, particle size, and process yield. Furthermore, it synthesizes current evidence on the physicochemical, microbiological, sensory,
journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology

title: Relationships between Management Practices and Production Performance among Smallholder Goat Raisers in Ilocos Norte
abstract: This study assessed the production performance and management practices of smallholder goat raisers in Ilocos Norte. Specifically, it described the respondents’ socio-demographic characteristics, management practices, production systems, production performance, and problems and constraints encountered in goat raising. It also examined the relationships between selected socio-demographic characteristics and management practices, management practices and production performance, and production systems and management practices. title: A farmer-centric analysis of an agri-food transition in the face of potential disruption from cultured meat
abstract: The emergence of cultured meat has been presented as a potentially transformative innovation capable of reducing the environmental impacts of food production and reshaping global protein systems. However, little empirical research has examined how farmers—key actors within agri-food transitions—might respond to this potential disruption. This study explores how UK farmers approach an agri-food transition in the face of disruption from cultured meat and considers the implications for a just agri-food transition. title: Multi-organ damage, organ selectivity, and combined pollution effects of ferroptosis induced by environmental toxins in animals
abstract: Mycotoxins, including ochratoxin A, deoxynivalenol, zearalenone, and aflatoxin B₁, together with heavy metals such as cadmium, lead, and copper, constitute two major categories of environmental contaminants prevalent in livestock feed. These toxicants preferentially target and inflict damage upon the liver, kidneys, and intestines of livestock and poultry, consequently impairing overall production performance. title: Medicinal plant agrobiodiversity, biocultural management, and conservation in a Mixtec indigenous community in Oaxaca, Mexico
abstract: Medicinal plants constitute an important component of agrobiodiversity in Indigenous landscapes, where wild, cultivated, and locally managed resources contribute to household health care, biocultural continuity, and biodiversity conservation. This study characterized medicinal plant agrobiodiversity, therapeutic uses, management practices, and intracultural variation in ethnobotanical knowledge in Santiago Ixtaltepec, a Mixtec Indigenous community in Oaxaca, Mexico. Semi-structured questionnaires were administered to 32 adult household members. After taxonomic standardization and data-quality

title: Gut microbiota regulates glucose metabolism in polycystic ovary syndrome: mechanisms and therapeutic implications
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent endocrine disorders affecting women of reproductive age, characterised by reproductive dysfunction alongside significant metabolic abnormalities. Among these, insulin resistance (IR) is a common and important pathophysiological feature in many women with PCOS and is associated with hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and long-term cardiometabolic complications, although its contribution varies across phenotypes. Accumulating evidence indicates that dysbiosis of gut microbiota contributes to glucose metabolic dysfunction in PCOS

title: MOF‐Based Photothermal Catalysts for Solar Energy Conversion: Design Principles, Mechanistic Insights, and Applications in CO 2 Conversion and Hydrogen Production
abstract: Photothermal catalysis, which couples solar energy harvesting and thermal‐driven surface reactions, has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable energy conversion. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs), with their structural tunability, high porosity, and capability of incorporating active metal sites, have become versatile platforms for constructing photothermal catalysts. This review mainly summarized the recent research progress in MOF‐based photothermal systems, focusing on their structural advantages, design strategies, and mechanistic features in energy‐related reactions. title: How non-native are natives? Individual differences in the oral narratives of adult native speakers of Brazilian Portuguese with different levels of schooling
abstract: As a test of the uniformity of competence assumption—the notion that there is an ideal state of native speaker competence—and to establish how variability in native speakers compares to variability in non-native speakers, this study examined individual differences in morphosyntactic attainment in adult monolingual native speakers of Brazilian Portuguese. title: Hydrophilic–hydrophobic flow-field engineering for passive water management in high-power-density PEMFCs
abstract: Effective water management remains a major limitation to high-power-density proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), where excessive liquid-water accumulation restricts oxygen transport and intensifies concentration losses. This study investigates a spatially engineered hydrophilic–hydrophobic flow-field strategy for passive water management, with particular emphasis on the orientation of surface wettability relative to reactant flow. title: Influence of Technical Vocational Education and Training on Skills Gap in the Masonry Workforce in Moroto District, Eastern Uganda
abstract: This research report aimed to investigate how Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) influences the skills gap of masonry workers in Moroto District, Eastern Uganda. Even though there has been an emphasis on TVET to address the skills gap, the masonry trade continues to experience a significant shortage of skilled workers. This study sought to: (i) identify the effect of TVET on the skill level of masonry workers; (ii) establish the skills gap in masonry; and (iii) assess the influence factors on TVET.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: From Static Structural Coloration to Dynamic Photonics in Metal–Organic and Covalent–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent–organic frameworks (COFs) combine structural tunability, accessible porosity, and chemically responsive interiors, making them attractive photonic building blocks. Yet in framework‐dominated static architectures, porosity can reduce dielectric contrast and increase the structural coherence required for strong macroscopic optical responses, while disorder, scattering, and processing‐induced defects can further weaken color saturation. title: Understanding ‘ Zhanglao zhishiren 長老知事人’ and examining the establishment time of the name ‘Shifang十方’ for the monastery system
abstract: In volume two of the Shishi yaolan 釋氏要覽 [Essential Guide to Buddhist Doctrine], there is an entry titled ‘Shifang zhuchi’ 十方住持. Within this, the phrase zhanglao zhishiren 長老知事人 appears, with both the CBETA edition and the Zhonghua Book Company’s annotated version presenting it as an ‘elderly administrator of a Buddhist monastery’ without any punctuation to indicate there may be two separate entities. title: Medicinal plants in diabetic nephropathy: bioactive compounds, mechanisms, and therapeutic potential
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is known as one of the most critical microvascular complications associated with diabetes mellitus, and is a primary cause of chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease worldwide. Renal injury in DN is primarily driven by persistent hyperglycemia, which sequentially triggers oxidative stress, activation of innate immune signaling pathways, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, accumulation of advanced glycation end products, activation of the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS), and extracellular matrix deposition. title: Unravelling groundwater's role in soil-plant-atmosphere continuum: integrated ecohydrological modelling approach using STEMMUS-SCOPE and MODFLOW 6
abstract: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) models are commonly used to investigate various components' role(s) in ecosystem functioning. Yet, in most SPAC models, groundwater is ignored or at best represented in an over-simplified manner, leading to misunderstanding of its critical role in simulating soil-vegetation dynamics. title: RAZVOJ LJUDSKOG KAPITALA I INOVACIONE AKTIVNOSTI PREDUZEĆA
abstract: Human capital development represents an important foundation for enhancing innovation activities and enabling enterprises to adapt to contemporary changes in the business environment. Continuous investment in employees’ knowledge and competencies contributes to creating organizational conditions conducive to the development and implementation of new business solutions. The aim of this paper is to examine the relationship between investment in employee training and investment in the innovation activities of enterprises in the Republic of Serbia. title: Targeting soluble epoxide hydrolase in cardiovascular diseases: from mechanistic insights to clinical translation
abstract: The cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP) system is a multigene superfamily of enzymes essential for metabolizing both exogenous and endogenous compounds. CYP epoxygenases metabolize various n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) into bioactive epoxy fatty acids (EpFAs), including arachidonic acid (AA)-derived epoxyeicosatrienoic acids (EETs), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-derived epoxyeicosatetraenoic acids (EEQs), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-derived epoxydocosapentaenoic acids (EDPs). title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. title: Scaling laws in machine learning on non-ideal experimental data enable inverse design of radiative-cooling coatings
abstract: Materials informatics increasingly targets multicomponent materials, yet experimental datasets inevitably contain non-ideal variations arising from imperfect uniformity and reproducibility in composition, coating formation, and measurement. Whether machine-learning prediction accuracy scales with amount of data under these conditions remains unclear. Here, we develop an automated platform that produced and optically characterized 11,520 radiative-cooling coatings spanning nine material and processing parameters. title: A Diffusive T-Matrix Unifying the Electric and Magnetic Polarizability Tensors in Conducting Layered Media
abstract: Electromagnetic induction is used to detect and classify buried and submerged objects, such as unexploded ordnance in soil and on the seabed. A small object is commonly described by its magnetic polarizability tensor (MPT), which is independent of its position and of the sensor. The MPT assumes that the surrounding medium does not conduct. In seawater at extremely low frequency, or in clay at kilohertz frequencies, this assumption fails at depths comparable to the skin depth. title: Reconstruction and Forecast of Extreme Waves from a Single Observation
abstract: The state space of a dynamical system can, under suitable conditions, be reconstructed from a single observational time-series through delay-coordinate embedding. However, reconstructing the spatiotemporal evolution of nonlinear water waves from highly sparse measurements remains a considerable challenge. title: Explainable AI for Solar PV Power Forecasting: From Model Selection to Trustworthy, Reproducible Deployment
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is now a standard tool for forecasting the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) plants, yet published accuracy figures are often hard to compare and harder to trust. Many studies validate with random splits, report no reference forecast, and present feature attributions without saying what they can and cannot show. This paper reviews the main families of ML methods for PV power forecasting and resource assessment, from tree ensembles to deep and foundation models, and sets out a reproducible workflow that combines automated model search with explainable AI. title: Wall-to-wall maps of canopy height and aboveground carbon across the Atlantic Forest
abstract: Global canopy height maps are increasingly used to estimate forest carbon, yet their regional accuracy is rarely tested. We present wall-to-wall maps of canopy height (10 m) and aboveground carbon density (30 m) for the Brazilian Atlantic Forest in 2024. Height was predicted by a deep learning network fusing Sentinel-2 reflectance, Sentinel-1 and ALOS PALSAR backscatter and ALOS elevation, trained on 7,179 and tested on 1,793 patches (58,800 km$^2$) from a statewide airborne LiDAR campaign over São Paulo state, Brazil. title: DARWIN: a Geospatial Foundation Model for Marine Intelligence
abstract: We present DARWIN, a geospatial foundation model for marine intelligence. Recent Earth-observation foundation models have concentrated on terrestrial domains. The marine realm poses distinct challenges: missingness, multi-modal physical and biogeochemical variables, sparse labels, and dynamics that are transient, multi-scale, and non stationary over time. title: Towards GPROF V08: A Machine-Learning Framework for Simulating Passive Microwave Observations of Precipitation
abstract: Spatially resolved precipitation retrievals based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can improve precipitation estimates from passive microwave (PMW) observations and will be used to implement the next operational PMW retrieval algorithm for the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission. However, the conventional radiative transfer simulations used to extend the retrieval algorithm to the various sensors of the GPM constellation do not provide the spatial coverage required to train CNN-based retrievals. title: Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
abstract: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically.
