title: Emulating physics-based XCO2 retrievals across OCO-2 viewing modes with compact neural networks
abstract: Operational full-physics retrieval of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide from satellite spectra is computationally demanding. We use singular value decomposition to compress spectra from the Orbiting Carbon Observatory-2 separately by band. Compact multilayer perceptrons use the resulting spectral scores, prior information, and viewing geometry to predict the difference between the full-physics retrieval and its operational prior. Adding the predicted difference to the prior yields an estimate of the retrieved mole fraction. The models were trained on 2015-2019 observa
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories
abstract: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields. Level-rank duality connects the charged sectors of the fermionic construction, where explicit neural observables recover conformal block data and enable the transfer of information about unknown correlators between paired theories. We also show that distinct neural presentations of the same continuum current algebra exhibit different finite-width behavior, with approximation accuracy depending on architecture, regulator, and parameter distribution. institutions: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

title: Collision-Resilient All-to-All Broadcast Scheduling in Underwater Acoustic Networks
abstract: This paper studies all-to-all broadcast scheduling for underwater swarms with collision-resilient physical layers that can decode asynchronously overlapping packets. Propagation-aware collision-free schedulers coordinate packet arrivals but do not account for this reception capability. We first design a data-driven neural reception model that captures per-interferer power and timing effects. The model improves prediction accuracy over SINR baselines while admitting an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. The resulting neural-network-embedded MILP (NN-MILP) optimizes trans

title: Hermitian Positive Definite Neural Networks for Matrix-CFAR Geometric Signal Detection in Nonhomogeneous Clutter
abstract: Matrix information geometry (MIG) detectors exploit the Riemannian geometry of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) matrices to achieve robust object detection in nonhomogeneous clutter. The matrix constant false alarm rate (matrix-CFAR) method is a representative MIG detector that relies on the geometric structures with respect to specific metrics. In most cases, computing representative HPD covariance matrices requires numerical methods, typically involving computationally intensive iterative optimization algorithms. Although explicit formulas are available for certain cases, such as the log-Eu

title: Learning Calibrated and Samplable Predictive Distributions of Surface-Ocean $Δp$CO$_2$ Using Tabular Diffusion Models
abstract: The ocean absorbs almost 30% of anthropogenic CO$_2$ emissions, but quantifying this sink requires estimating surface-ocean CO$_2$ from observations that are sparse in space and time. Most existing machine-learning estimates of this field are deterministic, giving a single value per grid point, with uncertainty approximated post hoc via residuals, ensembles, or prescribed distributions. We instead learn a conditional predictive distribution for each observation: using Treeffuser, a conditional diffusion model with gradient-boosted-tree score functions, we estimate the full predictive distribut
institutions: New York City College of Technology

title: NIRJALA: Draining the Sea out of Gaussian Splatting with Three-Path Optics and Reversible Physics
abstract: Water does not just tint an underwater photograph; it rewrites it. Each pixel mixes attenuated scene radiance, backscattered light, and scene light scattered forward on its way to the camera, and many combinations of scene and water explain the same pixels. Most Gaussian-splatting methods for underwater scenes model only the first two effects and remove the water by dividing by a transmission that decays exponentially with range, so their inversion gain grows without bound. We present NIRJALA (Sanskrit for "without water"), a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that recovers water-free appearance

title: Why do continual physical learners need sleep?
abstract: Sleep is widespread across the animal kingdom, including in organisms without a centralized nervous system. Does learning create a need for sleep, even without biology? To explore this question, we study a disordered spring network trained to perform a sequence of mechanical allosteric tasks through local changes in bond stiffness. We find that continual learning progressively reduces the network's ability to acquire new tasks as individual bonds become increasingly specialized. We identify an exact algebraic relationship between the polarization of bond dominance and the network's remaining l

title: A latent twins architecture for robust clear-sky retrieval from IASI acquisitions
abstract: In recent years, data-driven approaches emerged as alternatives to traditional physics-based retrievals, taking advantage of machine learning techniques such as learnable pseudoinverse, random forests, or deep learning architectures. Classical data-driven models generalize poorly to out-of-sample regimes, as they optimize over finite datasets without incorporating underlying physical laws. This often requires large models and extensive data to achieve reliability. Physics-Informed Neural Networks address this by embedding physical constraints into the learning process, enabling improved extrap

title: A hierarchical graph neural network for efficient particle-resolved prediction of granular flow dynamics
abstract: Graph neural surrogates for granular flow can resolve the motion of individual grains, but propagating information across a large amount of grains requires repeated, costly updates on the full particle graph. This study introduce a Hierarchical Coarse-Grained Graph Neural Network (HCG-GNN) that couples direct interactions between neighboring grains with information exchange on two coarser graphs of occupied spatial cells. In discrete element method (DEM) benchmarks of granular flows down incline planes, HCG-GNN captured key flow characteristics, including front propagation, lateral spreading,

title: QuantAtlas-OM: Taming Neural Spectral Bias in Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Ocean Dynamics
abstract: Autoregressive neural networks exhibit spectral bias in long-horizon spatiotemporal prediction. As rollouts progress, high-frequency details decay, blurring the predicted fields and destabilizing long-range forecasts. Ocean dynamics offer a particularly stringent test because kinetic energy is concentrated in mesoscale eddies and fronts spanning tens of kilometers. This degradation stems from coupling large-scale phase evolution and small-scale energy retention in a shared feature space. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model
abstract: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. HaiRuo pairs two components with a clear division of labour: (1) HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Probing Non-Equilibrium Grain Boundary Dynamics with XPCS and Domain-Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: Grain-boundary (GB) dynamics control the stability, mechanical, and functional response of nanocrystalline materials, but direct experimental access to their slow non-equilibrium motion has been limited. Here we establish X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS), combined with domain-adaptive machine learning, as a quantitative probe of GB dynamics. Temperature- and grain-size-dependent two-time XPCS measurements in nanocrystalline silicon reveal pronounced departures from time-translation invariance, showing that GB relaxation can remain far from equilibrium over experimental timescales.

title: Distribution Shift Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Remote sensing imagery acquired by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) supports wide range of applications; however, deploying machine learning (ML) models on resource-constrained aerial platforms introduces challenges beyond predictive accuracy, particularly when deployment data differ from the distributions observed during training. Such shifts are common in remote sensing due to geographic, sensor, seasonal, and other visual variations. A practical solution is to equip deployed models with mechanisms that detect emerging distribution shifts and support subsequent responsive actions. This paper

title: Fiberpose: state-of-the-art fiber morphometry and instance segmentation with a distance-transform neural network
abstract: Analysis of fibrous structures in SEM images is a routine task in biomedical engineering and materials science. However, most available methods for fiber quantification still rely on classical image binarization followed by simple post-processing. These approaches often produce unreliable results in images with weak boundaries, heterogeneous contrast, and densely packed fibers. Here, we introduce Fiberpose, a framework that reformulates fiber analysis as direct regression of a smooth distance-transform (DT) field, together with a novel set of geometry-based algorithms specifically adapted to t

title: GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
abstract: When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address
institutions: CMCC Foundation - Euro-Mediterranean Center on Climate Change

title: KneeFS-Net: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment with Cross-Domain External Validation
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) grading from radiographs using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale requires expertise that may be scarce. We present KneeFS-Net, a lightweight ordinal grader (0.8 million parameters; 0.33 GFLOPs) combining spatial, Fourier and state-space features with landmark-guided attention. On the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) test set, KneeFS-Net achieved a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.325 and 97.2% within-one-grade accuracy, comparable to models with 9-35-fold more parameters. We evaluated cross-population generalization on two Banglades
institutions: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dua

title: SecDVA: A Maliciously Secure Multi-Party Framework for Data Value Assessment in Modern Machine Learning Data Markets
abstract: Data Value Assessment (DVA) plays a critical role in modern data markets by enabling buyers to evaluate how a seller's data would improve model performance before purchase. However, existing DVA approaches require one party to reveal the data or model, exposing participants to privacy leakage, strategic manipulation, and high deployment costs. These limitations motivate a DVA protocol that is secure, reliable, widely applicable, and efficient enough for practical deployment in modern data markets. In this paper, we present SecDVA, the first maliciously secure multi-party computation (MPC) fram

title: A Novel Iterative Algorithm Incorporating Machine Learning for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck Equations in Three-Dimensional Ion Channel Simulation
abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. institutions: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science

title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation–Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
abstract: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Location Encoding Methods for Species Distribution Modelling
abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of species is a key question in ecology. A variety of solutions, from statistical, traditional machine learning, through to deep learning-based methods have been proposed. These methods take sparse observations for a species of interest as input and aim to generate dense spatial outputs indicating the spatial range of the species. Orthogonal to the choice of statistical model used is the question of what input features are most informative. Thanks to recent developments, the number of options has greatly expanded, with choices spanning different climate v

title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
abstract: System thermal-hydraulics codes such as the System Analysis Module (SAM) close turbulence on coarse meshes with algebraic zero-equation mixing-length models. These models cannot represent the non-equilibrium turbulence, flow separation, and large-scale recirculation of open-cavity advanced reactors. We develop an invariant neural-network eddy-viscosity closure for SAM and apply it to the Molten Salt Fast Reactor (MSFR). The closure predicts the turbulent kinetic energy and timescale of each element from the flow and geometry of its neighbors, without solving turbulence transport equations. The

title: Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation
abstract: South Asian monsoon precipitation depends on the thermodynamic structure of the lower troposphere, but how its ingredients combine to shape precipitation remains unclear, partly because this dependence is nonlocal in the vertical. We use symbolic distillation, which combines neural networks and symbolic regression, to discover interpretable precipitation equations from 21 years of June-August reanalysis data. Neural networks first learn the vertical thermodynamic structure most relevant to precipitation, condensing each variable into a single interpretable feature not tied to a particular vert

title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Niño Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents
abstract: The predictability of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) has historically been linked to large-scale errors in models' initial conditions such as heat content and surface wind stress. Here we demonstrate that these slowly evolving errors may ultimately originate from mesoscale errors in initial oceanic states that are common in current models and ocean observation systems. This hidden source of ENSO forecast uncertainty, in terms of mesoscale ocean-current errors, is convincingly exposed by the conditional nonlinear optimal perturbation (CNOP) method applied to a differentiable ocean AI m
institutions: National Marine Data and Information Service

title: SandBAR: A Band-Asymmetric Architecture for Underwater Image Restoration with Removable Frequency Scaffolding
abstract: Light scattering, absorption and turbidity degrade underwater imagery through complementary frequency tendencies: large-scale, channel-dependent appearance distortions and local high-frequency detail loss. This band asymmetry motivates different forms of restoration for global colour and local structure. Our primary contribution is SandBAR, a novel unified band-asymmetric architecture for underwater image restoration. Rather than treating frequency processing as an isolated module, SandBAR organises the restoration pipeline around band asymmetry at the block, encoder and objective levels. With

title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
abstract: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tract

title: Split-and-Learn: Decoupled Learning for Reactive Transport in Heterogeneous Marine Sediments
abstract: Reactive transport in heterogeneous marine sediments couples flow and multicomponent transport with nonlinear chemistry and evolving porosity and permeability, and its simulation over thousands of years is computationally expensive, especially when uncertain heterogeneity requires many simulations. We develop Split-and-Learn, a framework that keeps the sequential operator-splitting scheme of the full-order model and replaces each stage by a data-driven surrogate with its own structure. title: WaveFlow-UIE: A Single-Pipeline Wavelet-Domain Flow Model for Efficient Underwater Image Restoration
abstract: Underwater image restoration remains challenging because color distortion, scattering, and detail loss affect low- and high-frequency image components differently. Recent diffusion-based methods have shown strong restoration quality, but often rely on multi-stage pipelines and costly iterative refinement. We present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model that directly learns to transform degraded underwater wavelet representations into clean ones. institutions: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

title: ASTRA: ASV Simulator for Transferable Realistic Autonomy
abstract: Autonomy development for marine autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) remains challenging because field testing is costly and difficult to reproduce. Existing marine simulation tools provide mature capabilities in vessel dynamics, robotics integration, and visual rendering, but these strengths are emphasized differently across platforms. This paper presents ASTRA, an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine vehicle dynamics, photorealistic perception, and Robot Operating System (ROS 2) autonomy interfaces within a common environment. ASTRA incorporates a Fossen-styl

title: Residual-Closed-Loop SAGE-Brent Estimation for Unknown-Order Wideband Underwater Acoustic Channels
abstract: Grid mismatch in wideband channel estimation leaves structured cancellation residuals after strong-path subtraction. These residuals generate spurious correlation peaks or mask weak arrivals, turning continuous parameter errors into path-count errors. We propose RC-SAGE-Brent, a residual-closed-loop estimator that jointly refines continuous delay-scale parameters and corrects the unknown-order path set. Within each feedback cycle, ambiguity-constrained alternating Brent searches suppress strong-path cancellation residuals. Candidate validation, resolution-constrained pruning, and full-domain r

title: Who sees the sea? Sea-view potential by façade and floor from cadastral LoD1 models on the Costa del Sol
abstract: Views are among the most valued and least measured attributes of a home. We present an open-data method that estimates the sea-view potential of every free façade of every residential building at three floors (ground, middle and top; other floors take the nearest of them), from cadastral footprints with floor counts and a national terrain model. Run for 158,060 buildings of 21 municipalities on Spain's Costa del Sol in under an hour on two cores, it finds that 52 % of buildings see some sea from their top floor and 36 % have an open view (20° or more). Traced over a LiDAR surface in a pilot, s

title: Where Should Physics Enter? Information, Identifiability and Calibration in Probabilistic Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting
abstract: Advection-diffusion priors are a common way to make neural sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts physics-informed. We test where such a prior must enter a heteroscedastic ConvLSTM to help, using daily NOAA OISST v2.1 for the Bay of Bengal (1982-2024) and a synthetic benchmark on the same grid with known currents of controlled strength. Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services

title: Fusing Multimodal CNN Features with Structurally-Masked Transformers for Hierarchical Sub-Pixel Tree Species Mapping
abstract: Precise forest species mapping using spaceborne hyperspectral data is challenging due to high spectral similarity and the inherent sub-pixel heterogeneity of natural forest stands. While traditional deep learning models exploit spatial context through convolutional architectures, these approaches can introduce noise in fragmented or mixed-species forests. title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
abstract: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. title: A Reliability Study of Explainable AI for Freight Mode Classification
abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to support freight transportation decisions, but their predictions are rarely accompanied by evidence that the associated explanations can be trusted. In this study we investigate explainable machine learning for classifying shipments as Air/Air Charter or Truck/Ocean using the PEPFAR Supply Chain Management System Delivery History dataset, with 5,964 shipment records and 47 input features after cleaning, where freight cost and pack price are excluded as near-proxies of the transportation mode. institutions: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

title: OceanCoder: A Verification-Guided Large Language Model for Automated Simulation Modelling in Ocean Engineering
abstract: Numerical simulation is important in ocean engineering, but model construction requires expert knowledge. Large language models support automated modelling, but code syntax and successful execution alone do not establish whether generated models and results meet engineering requirements. We present OceanCoder, a Qwen3-8B-based large language model for automated simulation modelling in ocean engineering. To address specialised programming requirements and scarce training data, we develop an extensible data construction pipeline producing 12,000 verified supervised fine-tuning (SFT) examples acr

title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered va
institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

title: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
abstract: Marine and offshore engineering text is spread across preprints, open-access journals, encyclopedias and institutional documents, and the amount of it is small by pretraining standards. We ask how far a lightweight language model for marine and offshore engineering can be taken with parameter-efficient adaptation on a single workstation-class device. Starting from the 4-billion-parameter OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct, we train two independent LoRA adapters, each updating 33.0 million of 4.06 billion parameters (0.81%). title: A Quantum Support Vector Regression Framework for Missing Data Imputation in Ship Performance Data
abstract: The Internet of Ships enables vessels to generate vast amounts of data, yet missing values remain a persistent issue. To the best of the authors' knowledge, existing imputation techniques in this domain rely exclusively on classical machine learning. This study investigates quantum support vector regression (QSVR) for imputing missing values in ship performance data. Classical support vector regression and QSVR models based on different quantum feature maps are compared for estimating marine fuel consumption under varying levels of data availability. title: Improving Eddy Detection from Wide-Swath Altimetry with Multimodal Data-Driven Models
abstract: Physically-based eddy detection algorithms usually rely on hard-coded thresholds and constraints that make the detected structures sensitive to small variations in the underlying fields. One way to relax such conditions is the use of machine-learning methodologies that transform the full problem into an optimization process. We present a multimodal, multi-task, data-driven eddy detection framework based on a shallow convolutional U-Net, trained to jointly segment eddy structures and reconstruct the co-located spatial sea surface temperature (SST) anomaly using a dynamically-based reconstructio
institutions: CMCC Foundation - Euro-Mediterranean Center on Climate Change
Nansen Environmental and Remote Sensing Center

title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
abstract: Missing well-log intervals make subsurface reconstruction ill-posed. Existing numerical regression models lack geological prior knowledge to constrain ambiguous inverse mappings. We propose GeoLog-Agent, a knowledge-conditioned generative agent using pre-trained large language models (LLMs) as a source of geological priors. A universal Geo-Harness translates LLM stratigraphic reasoning into formation-anchored petrophysical trajectories, feature-wise linear modulation, and conditional adversarial constraints. institutions: China University of Petroleum, East China

title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
abstract: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
abstract: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
abstract: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. Setting up such a study takes many technical steps, and this work is increasingly done with coding agents, programs in which a language model writes code, runs it and checks the result. We present KELP v1.0, the Kinematic Engine for Lagrangian Particles, a tracker for unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix grids that is built to be operated by such agents. institutions: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

title: Benchmarking the State of AI for Crop Yield Forecasting: A Global Assessment Across Modeling Paradigms
abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting is essential for food security, agricultural policy, and commodity markets. Although statistical, process-based, and machine learning approaches have all been proposed, their relative strengths remain poorly understood due to the lack of large-scale, standardized comparisons. title: Imputing Missing Near-Surface Air Temperature using Graph Attention Networks with Distance-Aware Edge Features
abstract: We introduce a graph attention network for reconstructing near-surface air temperature fields from incomplete observations. The model represents each grid cell as a node connected to its $k$ nearest neighbors, with attention weights that depend on node features, distance, and land-ocean transitions. This graph representation avoids the polar distortions associated with treating the globe as a flat latitude-longitude image, as most deep learning reconstruction methods do. title: Trustworthy Geospatial AI Workflows: Reproducible Maritime Analytics and Forecasting on Open-Source AIS Data
abstract: Publicly available geospatial data provide increasing opportuni- ties for data-driven maritime analytics and predictive modelling. However, their availability does not necessarily imply that the underlying observations are equally suitable for downstream AI applications. Properties of the data source and observation pro- cess, including provenance, reporting regularity, spatial coverage, observation density, and missingness, can affect how geospatial data are interpreted, processed, and ultimately used by predictive models. At the same time, trustworthy geospatial AI requires ana- lytical work

title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance. We introduce TabBioMed, a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning electronic health records, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. title: The MegaWave Radio Surveyor
abstract: Several Decadal-level questions in astrophysics, planetary science, astrobiology, and cosmology can be addressed only at low radio frequencies that are inaccessible from Earth. The MegaWave Radio Surveyor would open this largely-unexplored region of the electromagnetic spectrum with a distributed space-based interferometer to (1) Track space weather events generated by other stars (exospace weather); (2) Detect the magnetically-generated radio emission from exoplanets to probe their interiors and assess the magnetic shielding of their atmospheres; (3) Probe directly the Universe’s evolution du

title: Random Exploration is Random
abstract: Decision making often requires balancing exploitation of familiar options with exploration of uncertain alternatives. One strategy for exploration is random exploration, in which choices become more variable and less tied to the option that currently appears best. However, it remains unclear whether this variability reflects genuine stochasticity or instead a deterministic structure that traditional cognitive models fail to capture. title: HybridCT: ML Accelerated Tomography for Climate Relevant 3D Cloud Observations
abstract: Low-level clouds are one of the largest sources of uncertainty in climate predictions, partly because we lack detailed three-dimensional (3D) measurements of their internal structure. Here, we present HybridCT, a cloud tomographic reconstruction scheme accelerated by machine learning (ML) that recovers 3D cloud extinction directly from passive multi-angle observations. title: From the firm- to the application-level: A new typology of AI use in organisations
abstract: Artificial intelligence is applied in organisations in many different ways. However, the firm-level literature on AI lacks a conceptual framework able to describe that variety. Empirical studies typically examine one dimension of AI use at a time. This paper argues that the difficulty follows from the unit of analysis: a firm may hold many AI applications at once, each with its own novelty, sourcing mode, objective and technology type. title: PARDIG: Global Precipitation Estimates Learned from Sparse Satellite Observations
abstract: Estimating precipitation at the global scale is vital for Earth system science and disaster response, yet observational coverage and measurement precision remain constrained. Existing solutions provide options that trade off desirable traits such as skill, latency, geographical coverage, temporal coverage, and spatial and temporal resolution. We present PARDIG, an artificial intelligence framework based on a spherical graph-mesh transformer architecture that produces near-real-time global precipitation estimates. title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Neural networks are typically programmed through optimization, rather than by explicitly specifying their computations. Recent work on weight-space programming suggests that large language models (LLMs) can instead reason about and manipulate neural-network weights directly. In this work, we show that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets. We investigate three complementary settings using GPT-6 Astra, without gradient-based optimization. First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from z

title: CivilBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Information Integration in Civil Engineering
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), is increasingly applied in civil and structural engineering for disaster assessment, structural analysis, and engineering decision support. However, the extent to which current VLMs possess the reasoning capabilities required for reliable engineering judgments remains unclear. In this work, we introduce CivilBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs in civil engineering and disaster-related scenarios. CivilBench covers three major task families: Sequential Reasoning, Image-base
institutions: Sichuan University of Science and Engineering
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
abstract: Vision models are sensitive to object-background context, yet it remains unclear how recognition changes as the semantic distance between objects and backgrounds increases. We introduce ImageNet-OOC1k, a benchmark enabling graded control of object-background relationships along a continuous consensus visual-semantic dissimilarity axis. This formulation reveals a highly consistent monotonic decline in recognition accuracy across 35 models spanning convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, and vision-language models. title: Advancing a Global Framework for AI Safety and Governance for the Well-being of Humanity
abstract: The Report "Advancing a Global Framework for AI Safety and Governance for the Well-being of Humanity" is an important outcome of the AI Safety and Governance Program of World Internet Conference Specialized Committee on Artificial Intelligence in 2025. This report provides a systematic review of current global explorations and practices in AI safety and governance, identifies key issues that need to be addressed, and draws upon multilateral governance experiences from other domains. Centered on mechanism design, it explores how to build a global AI safety and governance system that ensures saf

title: Vibe synthesis: hierarchical agentic decision-making for intent-driven multistep molecule synthesis
abstract: The ability to construct complex molecules underpins advances in medicine and the molecular sciences. Yet long-horizon multistep synthesis requires decisions to be revised as evidence accumulates across chemically dependent operations, a capability not readily supported by artificial-intelligence tools and automated platforms organized around predefined tasks and hard-coded workflows. Here we propose and demonstrate a vibe synthesis system (VibeSyn), an intent-driven architecture in which hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined molecular objectives and accumulating evidence into adaptive

title: Evaluating AI Musical Creativity: Towards a Quantitative Multi-Dimensional Framework Based on Value, Novelty, and Surprise
abstract: Despite the increasing sophistication of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), research on the evaluation of AI-generated musical creativity remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a quantitative framework for the formalization and evaluation of AI musical creativity. Building on Margaret Boden's theory, which conceptualizes creativity in terms of value, novelty, and surprise, the framework adapts and operationalizes these three dimensions for the musical domain. On the hypothesis that certain aspects of musical creativity can be assessed with a degree of objectivity, a do

title: DaYu-TC: a global-regional nested AI system for tropical cyclone forecasting
abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone intensity forecasts are essential for disaster preparedness, yet persistent intensity underestimation limits the value of artificial intelligence (AI) weather models for predicting these destructive storms. Here we present DaYu-TC, a global-regional nested system that links the preservation of strong-wind and low-pressure signals with high-resolution regional prediction. Its global and regional models share an architecture and extreme-aware training objectives. The regional model combines evolving local states with global forecasts valid at each target time, connectin

title: Hybrid Compression for Memory-Efficient Matrix-Vector Multiplication
abstract: Iterative machine-learning algorithms repeatedly access large real-valued matrices through matrix-vector products, and their performance is limited by memory bandwidth rather than arithmetic throughput. Lossless compression schemes that support computation directly over the compressed data reduce both the data moved and the memory footprint of these workloads. The mm-RePair framework [11] follows this approach by applying the RePair grammar compressor to the Compressed Sparse Row/Value (CSRV) representation of a matrix and performing matrix-vector multiplications directly on the compressed dat

title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework
abstract: The rapid growth of deep learning has driven the deployment of computer vision directly on resource-constrained edge devices. However, the extreme heterogeneity of edge hardware architectures poses major challenges in selecting and designing suitable vision models. This survey bridges the gap between edge hardware constraints, model architectures, and deployment software toolchains. We establish a comprehensive taxonomy classifying edge hardware into three distinct tiers: mid-range devices (GPUs and dedicated NPUs or TPUs), dedicated embedded MPU or SoC processors, and microcontrollers (MCUs).
institutions: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
Ho Chi Minh City University of Science

title: Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone track

title: Global probabilistic forecasting of air pollution at the kilometre scale
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) refers to particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 µm or less. It comes from human activities, such as traffic and industry, and from wildfires, desert dust and gases emitted by vegetation. Short-term exposure to it accounts for about a million deaths a year. Operational forecasts run on grids tens of kilometres wide, which hide the pollution breathed by nearly two hundred million people a day. Machine learning has transformed weather forecasting, but data-driven forecasts of air pollution still blur extremes and lose skill as the air travels. Here

title: Reinforcement learning to design near-perfect acoustic absorbers
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed as a strategy for the multi-objective design of Helmholtz resonators with near-perfect acoustic absorption. The approach formulates resonator design as a sequential decision-making problem in which geometrical parameters are iteratively updated to balance competing objectives, including resonator volume, resonance frequency, and acoustic reflection. A Q-learning algorithm based on a neural network is developed to explore the design space and identify non-dominated solutions, providing a Pareto front of optimal configurations. The acoustic response is eva

title: Learning Temporal Dynamics with Derivative Representations for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Time series forecasting aims to predict the future evolution of complex systems by learning their underlying dynamics from past observations. Despite recent advances in deep learning, Transformers in particular still struggle to capture the temporal evolution of system dynamics. Existing approaches have been largely driven by architectural innovation, with comparatively little attention paid to training strategies that explicitly exploit the temporal structure governing system dynamics. In this work, we introduce DeltaTSF, a dynamics-aware forecasting framework based on discrete derivative rep

title: GPROF V08: Improving Satellite Precipitation Estimates Across a Heterogeneous Constellation of Passive-Microwave Sensors
abstract: Precipitation estimates from the passive microwave observations (PMW) of the Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) mission serve a wide range of scientific, societal, and economic applications. The Goddard Profiling Algorithm (GPROF) is the operational precipitation retrieval used to produce the level-two precipitation estimates for the GPM mission. This study presents GPROF V08 - the most recent version of GPROF and a major update aimed at improving the accuracy of precipitation estimates from the GPM constellation. GPROF V08 replaces the single-pixel Bayesian retrieval scheme used by earlie

title: Cooperative UAV and Ground Station for Robust MEC of Dynamic Aquatic IoT: A Generative AI-Enhanced Approach
abstract: The increasing aquatic Internet of Things (AIoTs) require computational support and coverage in applications such as maritime search and rescue. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can offer low-cost, flexible aerial services, and ground stations (GSs) can provide powerful supports, which can cooperate to help the AIoTs in complex scenarios. However, the collaboration between UAVs and GSs for AIoTs faces challenges of task uncertainties, AIoTs trajectory uncertainties, heterogeneities, and limited computational resources. To address these issues, we propose a cooperative UAV and GS based robust mu
institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: Physics-Spawned Neural Integration of Rotating Shallow-Water Dynamics
abstract: Equation-derived neural integration can execute prescribed dynamics without training, while informative ensemble learning can estimate uncertain parameters and identify governing interactions without requiring differentiability. Together, these approaches motivate Physics-Spawned Informative Networks ($Φ$SpIN), a framework for prescribed and adaptive hybrid dynamical systems. As a first step toward flood modeling applications, we present $Φ$SpIN-SW, its prescribed-physics realization for the rotating shallow-water equations. title: DIAGNO: Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators for Heterogeneous Earth Dynamics Modeling
abstract: Accurate forecasting of Earth's dynamic systems is vital in geophysics, where neural operators offer a powerful data-driven paradigm. Standard operators often treat the Earth as a flat Euclidean plane, introducing geometric artifacts. In contrast, Spherical Neural Operators (SNOs) resolve this mismatch by operating within the spherical spectral space, naturally adapting to spherical geometries. However, for computational efficiency, existing SNOs typically rely on the rotation equivariance assumption. This assumption simplifies the transitions of physical states into isolated spectral modal ev

title: VRLLM: Turning LLMs into Powerful Tabular Classifiers
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on text, but whether pretrained LLMs are effective for large-scale tabular classification remains unclear, as many previous works demonstrate that LLMs' tabular data classification performance falls behind tree-based models or neural architectures designed for tabular data. At Visa Research, we managed to fine-tune a pretrained Llama 3.2 1B LLM on billions of rows of labeled tabular data and make it outperform a wide array of tabular classifiers and even our competitive production deep learning model. For ease of reference, we refer to

title: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization for Multi-Asset Portfolios
abstract: Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) insulates asset allocation from Markowitz covariance ill-conditioning. However, classical tree clustering relies on static pairwise Pearson correlation, failing to capture time-varying, asymmetric downside risk contagion across multi-asset markets. We propose a unified deep graph machine learning architecture: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization (ST-GAT-NCO) for multi-asset tactical allocation. The framework extracts temporal momentum and downside risk dynamics via causal dilated 1D-convolutions, then deploys a

title: vividRGB: Various visual cue detection in RGB photographs with forced focused attention
abstract: Natural photographs contain dense, overlapping structures that can be weakly expressed in feature maps from whole-image vision encoders. We introduce forced focused attention (FFA) and its Python implementation, vividRGB. FFA is an encoder-agnostic inference-time procedure that applies a frozen encoder to enlarged, overlapping local crops, averages inverse-aligned reflections, and reconstructs a feature field in source coordinates. We evaluate 50 high-resolution photographs from grassland vegetation, fungal networks, airborne forests, coral reefs, and phytoplankton microscopy, using DINOv3 ViT
institutions: Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research

title: A high-dimensional spatial-physical coupling operator for generalizable super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows
abstract: Accurate representation of turbulent flows requires simultaneously capturing multi-scale spatial structures and the complex, nonlinear coupling between distinct physical quantities (\textit{e.g.}, velocity components and density). In practice, however, turbulent data are often constrained by low spatial resolution due to hardware limitations and computational costs. While current data-driven super-resolution methods have shown promise by learning mappings via convolutional neural networks (CNNs), they typically treat physical variables as independent channels. title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations
abstract: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Observation-to-observation models avoid this dependence, but most omit the recursive filtering cycle that lets DA systems carry a background state through sparse, irregular observations. We introduce WeatherDreamer, a world model that learns this cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems, without reanalysis. It infers a latent state from observations, carries it

title: Improving Tropical Cyclone Forecasts through Objective Ensemble Track-Error Reduction
abstract: Accurate tropical cyclone (TC) track guidance is essential for warnings, evacuation planning, and risk communication, but outlying members and distinct track scenarios can degrade raw ensemble forecasts. Statistical and machine-learning (ML) methods proposed to improve ensemble guidance are difficult to compare because previous studies often use different forecast systems, basins, periods, and verification methods. Using a common verification framework, this study compares six objective methods (four statistical trimming and two ML methods) with the full ensemble mean for 138 TCs forecast by G

title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models
abstract: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation through time (BPTT), whose computational and memory costs grow with the length of the training window. Laboratoire des Sciences et Techniques de l’Information de la Communication et de la Connaissance

title: Towards Restorative Urban Spaces: An Exploratory Field Study of Nature Videos on Public Multi-Display Signage
abstract: In recent years, multi-display signage (MDS) has become increasingly common in urban stations, plazas, and other public spaces, where it is primarily used to present advertisements and information. Beyond these conventional applications, MDS offers opportunities to shape people's experiences of public environments through spatially distributed and dynamic visual content. Motivated by the potential of mediated nature to support restorative experiences in urban environments, we conducted a nine-day exploratory field study in a free-admission area of a science museum, presenting artificial intell

title: SeasonRainBench: Global Seasonal Precipitation
abstract: Accurate seasonal precipitation forecasts help societies prepare for drought, flooding, and crop failure months in advance. While data-driven methods have made rapid progress in weather and subseasonal forecasting, operational seasonal precipitation prediction still relies on numerical ensemble systems. These systems are computationally expensive and exhibit biases and drift that increase with lead time, motivating more efficient data-driven alternatives. Yet this transition faces three linked challenges: comparing data-driven forecasts with operational ones requires (1) a global benchmark tha

title: Predicting Process-Level Behavior: A Benchmarking Study
abstract: Predictive process monitoring (PPM) typically forecasts the future of individual process instances, hence operating on trace level. Process managers, however, typically operate on process level, e.g., when assigning staff or calculating KPIs. The question is how well such process-level managerial decisions are supported by existing approaches, given that PPM research has so far not focused on process-level predictions. We answer this question through a comprehensive benchmarking study of two process-level prediction tasks: concurrent trace prediction and average throughput time prediction. Acr

title: A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
abstract: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. title: RipBench: A Unified Benchmark for Multi-Level Rip Current Detection, Classification and Segmentation
abstract: Rip currents are a serious and often under-addressed threat to beach safety and the leading cause of coastal drownings worldwide. They are difficult to detect due to their amorphous structure, similarity to the background, and large variability in viewpoints and environments. Despite their dangers and growing interest in automated detection, existing research remains fragmented across datasets, metrics, models, and approaches, leading to an incomplete understanding of model performance. We introduce RipBench, a unified benchmark that enables controlled evaluation of rip current detection spann

title: HYDRA: Proactive Android Malware Drift Adaptation via Hierarchical Graph Contrastive Learning
abstract: Concept drift, driven by the rapid evolution of Android malware, severely degrades the performance of machine learning detectors. Current adaptation strategies are often reactive, responding only after performance has dropped and imposing a significant manual annotation burden, or they are proactive but rely on unstable adversarial training and incomplete, single-level graph representations. To overcome these limitations, we propose \model (Hybrid Drift Adaptation), a proactive adaptation framework that learns drift-invariant representations from hierarchically structured data. \model first mo

title: SkillLens: Action-Guided Dense Visual Dynamics for Proficiency Estimation
abstract: Human proficiency estimation is challenging because skill is a high-level and often subjective property that is not captured by action identity alone. Existing approaches leverage multimodal observations such as ego-exo video, gaze, pose, and inertial signals, but the gap between sensor-level evidence and abstract proficiency labels remains difficult to bridge. We present SkillLens, a proficiency estimation framework that uses atomic action descriptions as temporal guidance, rather than direct semantic supervision, to localize proficiency-relevant windows for dense visual-dynamics extraction.
institutions: Korea Institute of Science and Technology

title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets ($R^2 = 0.96$ with NIMS SuperCon). title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. However, increasing the number of agents or iterations does not automatically translate to producing more diverse or feasible ideas. Agents may converge on similar candidates, propagate unsupported claims through shared memory components and repeatedly apply search strategies that no longer yield any improvements. We introduce Inventa, a framework for automated scientific discovery that employs autonomous research units and verified shared knowledge. Each unit creat

title: Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
abstract: Cross-environment deployment is the central obstacle to practical WiFi sensing: a pipeline reaching 0.89+ top-1 in its training environments collapses to 0.408 under Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation with only K-shot labels. A ceiling analysis shows the collapse is not an alignment problem: the action signal is strong across seen environments (about 0.89 K10), environment identity is decodable from the encoder (0.965), and the failure concentrates in the encoder's extrapolation to the novel environment. title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. title: Calibrate, Don't Retrain: Decomposing the Value of Annotator Disagreement in Cyberbullying Severity
abstract: Machine learning models are often trained on labeled data produced by multiple human annotators. When those annotators disagree, their labels are commonly collapsed into a single majority vote, which discards information about the underlying disagreement. We examine the cost of this practice for cyberbullying severity, a subjective judgment on which annotators disagree heavily. In the corpus we study, all 5 annotators assigned the same severity label to only 4.1% of comments. title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
abstract: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. For 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific tropical cyclones from the 2002-2023 hurricane seasons, we analyze the discussion text and its combination with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields, for forecasting intensity changes at lead times of 24 to 120 hours using three modeling methods. title: A Transferable Pretrained 3D Model for Impedance Inversion with Sparse-Well Prior Conditioning
abstract: Deep-learning-based seismic impedance inversion commonly requires retraining for each target survey, which may generalize poorly beyond the conditioning locations when well control is extremely sparse. We propose a transferable three-dimensional inversion framework that separates offline learning from target-survey deployment. A masked autoencoder first learns seismic structural representations from unlabeled multi-survey data, after which the frozen encoder is incorporated into an inversion network trained on synthetic geological models with sparse-well-derived low-frequency priors. title: Data-driven Reconstruction of the Phase Dynamics for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation Reveals Seasonality and Statistical Synchronization with the Annual Cycle
abstract: In this study, we treat the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) as a rhythmic system periodically forced by the annual cycle. We examine ENSO event seasonality and synchronization between the annual and ENSO cycles. We compute phase time series for both cycles from sea surface temperature data using a data-driven Koopman operator approach. We then use Bayesian inference to reconstruct phase equations describing how the phases of the two oscillators evolve. institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
abstract: Missing wireline logs hinder subsurface characterization. Deep reconstruction networks suffer from gap-boundary steps and cross-basin shifts, while interpolation and Gaussian smoothers struggle with long intervals and outliers. We propose boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion (ST-KF), unifying multiresolution wavelet shrinkage, distance-gated residual prior learning, and closed-form robust Kalman smoothing with learning--inference decoupling. title: Morpho-Spectral Projection Analysis (MSPA) for Plant Spectroscopy
abstract: Plant reflectance spectroscopy across the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared domain encodes foliar biochemical and anatomical traits into contiguous spectral signatures with locally differentiable structure; however, extreme inter-band collinearity and unfavorable sample-to-feature ratios challenge predictive modeling. Conventional dimensionality reduction methods routinely adopted in spectroscopy, are column-permutation invariant: they treat adjacent wavelengths as unordered tabular columns and discard the sequential differential geometry of absorption features. title: HoloGene: Learning to Lift Sliced Spatial Transcriptomics to Holistic 3D Gene Fields
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides spatially resolved gene expression measurements, but most 3D ST datasets are acquired as independently processed 2D sections. Computational approaches span slice registration and integration, explicit or generative interpolation, and coordinate-field modeling. Within the last family, implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a continuous, coordinate-queryable parameterization, but standard isotropic coordinate encodings do not explicitly reflect that serial-section measurements are dense in-plane and sparse along the axial direction. title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
abstract: At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J kg$^{-1}$, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m s$^{-1}$. title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
abstract: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(ξ, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
abstract: Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data. title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
abstract: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance? Its answer separates bad decisions from bad luck. We prove that world models trained on factual transitions cannot answer it on their own, whatever their data or capacity. title: Guarded Swarms in the Loop: A ROS 2/PX4 Digital Twin for Hybrid Digital-Analog Coordination of UAV/UGV Swarms
abstract: Swarms of unmanned aerial and ground vehicles (UAV/UGV) operating in contested environments cannot rely on software alone for physical safety, since the software stack and its networks are part of the attack surface. The Guarded Swarms architecture addresses this by pairing a digital coordination layer, built on Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Nets (TB-CSPN), with an independent analog safety layer that can veto unsafe actuation commands. title: A Homogeneous Benchmark of Exoplanet Mass-Radius Relations
abstract: The mass-radius ($M$-$R$) relation is fundamental to inferring the bulk composition and internal structure of exoplanets. However, published relations remain difficult to compare directly because studies adopt different planetary samples, fitting procedures, and evaluation metrics. We construct a homogeneous, quality-controlled benchmark of 963 exoplanets with dynamically measured masses and transit radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. title: Spatial Extremes on Domains with Physical Barriers
abstract: We propose a model for spatial extremes what realistically accommodates nonconvex domains. Most existing models assume that tail dependence between locations depends only on their separation. Even if extended to be anisotropic or nonstationary, they still cannot accommodate features between points that may mediate the dependence. This assumption limits their applicability in settings where physical barriers like mountains, coastlines, or islands may attenuate or even block dependence in extreme events. title: In-orbit demonstration of object-based change detection applied to the maritime domain
abstract: This article presents the successful in-orbit validation of an object-based change detection pipeline for low latency maritime monitoring onboard the CogniSAT-6 mission. We propose and validate a lightweight, three-phase operational sequence: optimized ground-based dual-acquisition scheduling, real-time onboard AI-based vessel segmentation, and multi-temporal matching. title: WAIVES: Weak-form Asymptotically-unbiased Instrumental-Variable Estimation for SDEs
abstract: Weak-form methods have transformed inference for deterministic dynamical systems. By integrating the governing equations against smooth, compactly supported test functions, they trade noise-amplifying differentiation for noise-attenuating integration, yielding fast and robust estimates. Extending this idea to stochastic differential equations (SDEs) has proven harder, and a consistent single-trajectory formulation in the time domain has remained out of reach. title: The balance of evidence indicates a slowing AMOC
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a critical component of the climate system. Climate models have long predicted a slowing of the AMOC due to anthropogenic forcing, with a risk of passing tipping points in the future. The question of whether the AMOC is already weakening is still somewhat controversial. Continuous monitoring is only available for the past two decades, a period too short to tease apart contributions of natural variability and climate change. title: Worth Another Look: Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. title: Data-Efficient Algal Bloom Segmentation in Freshwater Bodies Using a Three-Stage Transfer Learning Pipeline with Attention-Enhanced Decoding
abstract: Harmful algal blooms threaten water quality and public health, yet automated segmentation of bloom regions in freshwater imagery is limited by scarce pixel-level annotations. We present a transfer-learning pipeline that adapts a Swin Transformer U-Net with SCSE decoder attention from ImageNet-1K to water-body segmentation (RIWA, LaRS) and then to algal blooms, together with a model-assisted annotation protocol that expands the labelled algae corpus from 145 to 655 images. In a single-seed ablation on a 41-image validation split (checkpoint S2-A4 and its variants), corpus expansion is the domin

title: An AI-Based OSSE Framework to Evaluate Learned Physical Consistency: A Multi-Model Study Using FourCastNet, Aurora, Prithvi WxC, and GraphCast
abstract: Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) are a central methodology for evaluating future atmospheric observing systems. We present the first AI-based OSSE framework to test whether different AI weather models can reproduce comparable physical impact from new observations that traditional physics based models generate. We evaluate four distinct architectural AI models on the Charney conjecture that incomplete historical observations can infer the present state of the atmospheric. title: STeP-C: Real-Time Neural Compression for Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing at Scale
abstract: Distributed fiber-optic sensing (DFOS) technologies such as Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) generate continuous, high-resolution spatio-temporal data at rates exceeding hundreds of megabytes per second, creating severe challenges for real-time storage and transmission. While neural compression methods can achieve strong rate-distortion performance on sensing data, prior approaches either require per-segment retraining incompatible with streaming, or have only been validated offline. None have been demonstrated end-to-end on a continuously streaming DAS acquisition system at scale. We presen

title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
abstract: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual

title: Domain generalization and synthetic data in object detection: the enabler, the probe, and the gap
abstract: Object detection models often experience performance degradation when deployed under distribution shifts, caused by for example changes in weather type, operational environment, or object appearance. Domain Generalization (DG) aims to develop models that remain robust under such shifts and generalize well to unseen domains. DG research specifically focused on object detection models is scarce, although these models face additional challenges around localization and multi-scale representations. Synthetic data is a promising tool to support in DG, by enabling large-scale generation of diverse ne
institutions: Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research

title: From State of THE ART to Human Prediction Algorithms
abstract: Human curiosity and longing for the future have driven human progress from ancient times to the present. With the advancement of AI technology, human prediction algorithms have also drawn increasing attention from researchers. However, as AI technology continues to advance, we observe a counterintuitive phenomenon. Take human trajectory prediction algorithms as an example. title: Towards Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow for Climate Downscaling: What Projections Can Certify?
abstract: Statistical downscaling restores the regional detail behind flooding and crop stress, but diffusion and flow-matching generators can produce sharp fields that break the conservation laws of their coarse input. Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow (PC-RF) is a conditional flow-matching downscaler. Its training penalties target wind divergence, negative precipitation, and mass drift from the coarse total, and a projection after sampling removes the last two exactly. title: Scale-Induced Semantic Shift in Visual Prompt Injection Against VLMs and Web Agents
abstract: Visual content in multimedia systems may be resized, compressed, or re-rendered before it is interpreted by a vision-language model. We study a security failure mode in which these transformations change the machine-readable semantics of an image: a textual instruction is not recovered at a $512\times512$ presentation resolution under our evaluation protocol but becomes recoverable after aggressive downsampling. title: Informative Path Planning with Gaussian Processes: Error Bounds, Algorithms, and Benchmarks
abstract: Accurate environmental monitoring relies on Informative Path Planning (IPP) to deploy autonomous systems that maximize information gain. While Gaussian Processes (GPs) provide a robust mathematical foundation for modeling the environment, contemporary IPP approaches remain hindered by heuristic operational constraints and the lack of simultaneous theoretical guarantees for worst-case estimation error and approximation quality. Rather than introducing yet another heuristic, this paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of existing error bounds and algorithms to further develop the mathema

title: Multi-level latent-diffusion adaptation for cross-region point cloud segmentation of ancient terraces
abstract: Automated lidar feature detection from lidar point clouds can support archaeological surveys, but models trained in one landscape may transfer poorly to another because of differences in terrain, vegetation, acquisition characteristics, and feature morphology. We address this problem for cross-region detection of ancient terraces using transductive unsupervised domain adaptation that exploits an unlabelled target survey. title: Solving the Discretised Shallow Water Equations on Distorted Structured Grids with Neural Physics
abstract: This paper presents a method for solving the shallow water equations on highly distorted structured grids using convolution-based operators following the Neural Physics approach. By mapping distorted physical grids to a uniform computational domain with Jacobian transformations, the governing advection and diffusion operators are reformulated in a structured convolutional form.
