title: VWEN: A Curated Small Language Model for Vietnamese Paraphrasing
abstract: We present VWEN, a 0.8B-parameter model for Vietnamese paraphrasing at a requested level of change and for five related tasks: generating several paraphrases, simplification, gist, register transfer and paraphrase judgement. VWEN is Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tuned on about 7k samples chosen by a four-stage pipeline: rules and deduplication, a bidirectional entailment filter, a divergence score that assigns low and high paraphrase levels, and selection for coverage and instruction-following difficulty. title: Technology-Enabled Fuel Supply Chain Resilience: An Integrated Information System for Real-Time Monitoring and Decision Support
abstract: This study evaluates and extends the transactional information system described in an earlier fuel logistics study, focusing on data reliability, monitoring, and decision support. An author-led re-evaluation examined available Delphi and SQL code and compared a reconstructed source-derived baseline (R0) with a revised SQL Server system (R1) across twelve evaluation scenarios. Synthetic transactions and public US energy data were used for technical assessment, while organizational processes and supply delays were simulated. title: An Omnidirectional WECT: Closed-Form Computation of the Directionally Integrated Weighted Euler Characteristic Transform
abstract: The weighted Euler characteristic transform (WECT) and related directional descriptors have become popular, efficiently computable tools for shape analysis across a variety of domains. In practice, however, they are approximated over a finite set of filtration directions, and thus the vectorized descriptor depends on this choice of directions and the rotational orientation of the data. title: Level Up! AI-Driven Challenges and Adaptations to Code Review Practices
abstract: AI can write code faster than humans can review, causing a bottleneck and necessitating changes to code review practices. This bottleneck is hotly debated, giving rise to two extreme and orthogonal imagined futures: one where humans continue to be firmly entrenched in the review process, and one where AI agents merge pull requests entirely without human involvement. Yet, these futures remain rooted in folk wisdom. title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
abstract: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. title: Counting What Matters: Reducing Redundant Object Detections in Overlapping UAV Mapping Imagery for Disaster Response
abstract: UAV mapping flights enable rapid aerial reconnaissance of large-scale incident sites in civil protection. However, the image overlap required for orthophoto generation causes every physical object to be detected multiple times across images, while dynamic objects may be omitted from or duplicated in the resulting orthomosaic. Analysis based on the orthophoto alone is therefore structurally insufficient. We address this by detecting objects on the individual images and merging redundant detections across them. title: Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
abstract: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution. The structural function solves an ill-posed operator equation whose conditional expectation operator need not be injective, and whose solutions need not belong to the hypothesis space. title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes
abstract: Titan is a compelling target for future deep space exploration, while its extreme Earth-Titan distance and complex environment make continuous ground-in-the-loop planning impractical. Existing planning methods, primarily developed for Earth-observation scenarios, have limited generalizability to uncertain deep space conditions and adaptability to time-varying mission states. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization (PCM-PPO) method for Titan autonomous mission planning. title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
abstract: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. title: Statistical Characterization of CME Interaction Responsible for Successive Type II Solar Radio Bursts
abstract: Successive type II solar radio bursts are often considered as diagnostics for the evolution of CME-driven shocks and their interaction with the structured solar corona. However, the physical mechanisms driving these successive type II emissions are not well understood, with prior studies mostly limited to single event. In this work, we provide the first statistical analysis of successive type II radio bursts over Solar Cycles 23, 24 and the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25 (1997-2025). title: PVTSizing 2.0: A Fast and Reliable Analog Circuit Sizing Operator for Agentic EDA Workflows
abstract: Analog circuit design automation requires both coordinated tool execution and efficient numerical search. Large language models (LLMs) offer new ways to organize tool execution, but finding one sizing that satisfies specifications across process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners remains costly. PVTSizing 2.0 addresses these needs through a human-agent workflow built around an independently usable numerical optimizer. title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search
abstract: Attributing short LLM-generated texts to a specific source remains challenging for existing multi-bit watermarking methods, which often require long generations or costly decoding to recover payloads reliably. We propose a codebook-based watermarking scheme that maps an $n$-bit payload to a longer $u$-bit codeword and embeds it during generation through token-level logit biasing. title: FastGRN: Few-Step Generative Refinement Networks
abstract: Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) generate an image by repeatedly re-predicting and refining every token of a discrete latent. They reach high fidelity, but need dozens of Markov steps. We therefore train few-step GRNs on the distribution of their own samples. We use its own uniform-state corruption to perform distribution matching on discrete tokens, which lets a discrete generator learn by backpropagation, and we pair noise with samples in the manner of rectified flow. abstract: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. title: ChronoDossier: Long-Form Personas as Temporal Memory Representations
abstract: Long-horizon agents rely on stored records to recover a person's state as facts change. Reliable answers depend on how facts are recorded, retrieved, and presented to the reader. We treat a long-form persona dossier as a memory representation of a known latent state, an invariant identity plus a timeline of facts, routines, and decision rules tied to life phases. abstract: This work presents Arboreus, a realistic Boreal forest simulator, developed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in Boreal forest environments. Arboreus presents an automated methodology for synthesizing large-scale, data-informed, plausible forest worlds from parametric trees, height-variant terrain, and satellite-informed tree density distributions. abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. abstract: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution. Inoculation prompting can reduce this effect by explicitly eliciting the undesired behavior during training, but recent work shows that the behavior can reappear when evaluation prompts contain cues from the training context. title: It Was Better Not to Know: Digital Recognition, Family Authority, and Postpartum Mental Health in Bangladesh
abstract: Postpartum mental distress affects roughly one in five mothers in low- and lower-middle-income countries, yet recognition and support remain limited where formal mental-health care is scarce, and family relationships govern health decisions. We report a five-month interview study with 20 mothers in urban, urban slum, and rural Bangladesh who had given birth within the previous two years. title: Performance Portability Explained: Insights from accelerating ICON microphysics
abstract: Scientific computing is under increasing pressure to adapt to HPC hardware that is shaped by AI workloads. In these modern ecosystems, extracting reasonable performance without investing major engineering effort is a central issue for domain scientists. Correctness constraints and intricate reference implementations represent further impediments to development. abstract: Radio positioning needs the positions of its anchors, access points, base stations, or reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and manual surveying is costly and error-prone. Calibrating this infrastructure from its own measurements is one estimation problem, studied in at least four communities as self-calibration, auto-positioning, anchor self-localization, network localization, or radio simultaneous localization and mapping. abstract: Frontier AI agents increasingly succeed on realistic, long-horizon tasks and are beginning to improve the systems through which they operate. Yet existing benchmarks often restrict agents to narrow action spaces, use simplified environments, or rely on verification methods that are unreliable for evaluating arbitrary agent-generated systems. We introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark for autonomous AI development with six end-to-end tasks spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration. abstract: Visualizing intermediate representations could help us inspect the reasoning steps underlying a model output. Unified multimodal models offer this opportunity by combining understanding and generation in one architecture. Their image generators can access representations formed while processing text. abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) provides label-free metabolic contrast, but conventional time-correlated single-photon counting requires thousands of excitation pulses per pixel to avoid pile-up distortion, limiting imaging speed and increasing motion artifacts and photodamage. Here, we develop single-pulse analog sampling that combines sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune, frequency-domain estimator for accurate lifetime measurement at low photon counts. abstract: Compliant coatings offer a passive approach to modifying near-wall turbulence and potentially reducing skin-friction drag, but high-fidelity exploration of the coupled parameter space is costly. We develop a two-way coupled resolvent-Galerkin framework for turbulent channel flow over finite-thickness, layered viscoelastic coatings. title: Lost in Read-out: Locating the Image Quality Gap in Vision-Language Models with a Closed-Form Edit
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are widely used as zero-shot image quality assessors, yet their good-vs-poor answers agree only moderately with human opinion. We ask whether these models fail to see quality or fail to say it. Layer-wise probes on five VLMs point to the second: quality is linearly decodable from the vision encoder and still from the last language layer, far better than the answer reveals, and about a hundred labels recover most of it. title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
abstract: We introduce GeoWorld, a controllable and continuously evolving geographic environment platform for LLM agents, and LiveGeo, a benchmark for evaluating reliable decision-making in real-world geographic environments using GeoWorld. Unlike existing evaluations that largely reason and plan over fixed geographic states, GeoWorld is grounded in real-world geographic structure and allows external world states to evolve along their own temporal processes while preserving verifiable state histories. abstract: Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. abstract: Flow-based generative models are trained on a hand-chosen prediction target, such as the velocity, the noise, or the clean data. This choice strongly affects training and sample quality. This study investigates the feasibility of near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) combined with an aquaphotomic approach to discriminate honeydew, monofloral, and polyfloral honey varieties. A total of 45 honey samples collected from various regions of Bulgaria were investigated. The botanical origin of monofloral and polyfloral honeys was verified through melissopalynological analysis, whereas honeydew honey was identified based on electrical conductivity and sugar profile. title: Enhancing maritime domain awareness using latent space representations
abstract: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. title: Towards Operational Efficiency in Maritime Fire Response: A Collaborative Approach Using Smart Technologies and Shared Situational Awareness
abstract: Maritime transportation is the backbone of global trade, yet it faces significant fire safety challenges, particularly in cargo handling. Fires on container ships account for 55% of all maritime fire incidents, with 92.6% originating from cargo, often involving misdeclared dangerous goods (DG). These fires lead to catastrophic consequences, including vessel damage, container loss, and environmental pollution. institutions: Institut de Recherche de l’École Navale

title: RATE: A Regime-Adaptive Temporal Ensemble for Accurate Retail Credit Default Prediction
abstract: How can a credit model keep predicting defaults accurately when the relationship between borrower characteristics and default risk keeps shifting and the patterns it learned steadily become outdated? Estimating the probability that a borrower defaults is a central problem in consumer and mortgage lending. It underpins the pricing, provisioning, and capital decisions of financial institutions worldwide. The task is difficult for three reasons. journal: ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF)

title: BESPORT—Collaborative Innovation for Business and Environmentally Sustainable Ports
abstract: Ports, as crucial hubs bridging between waterborne and road transport, are challenged by the regulatory and industrial need for improving business and environmental operational sustainability. As a Finland-China joint innovation action, BESPORT brings together 11 partners from Finland and China to work collaboratively for joint innovations and employ a holistic approach to addressing the industry’s challenges and need for port electrification, digitalization and automation towards smart and green ports, focusing on next-generation port electric vehicles, on-site multi-energy utilization and ch

title: Approach for Predicting the Content of Heavy Metals in Honey using Spectral Analysis and Regression Methods
abstract: The paper presents an approach for express assessment of the presence and content of heavy metals in honey using NIR spectral data and two basic chemometric regression models. The honey samples 29 in number were previously analyzed, and the values of the specified parameters - arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), and iron (Fe) were obtained. The accuracy of the two chemometric regression methods, PLSR and PCR, for determining the quality parameters of honey samples was assessed. title: ClimInvestBench: Evaluating Agentic Investment Report Generation and Maintenance
abstract: Generated analytical reports can inform financial decisions, so evaluation must check numerical correctness and evidential support as well as content coverage. Existing report benchmarks provide reference reports or grading criteria, but offer limited support for automatically revising expected calculations and written content when evidence is withheld or updated. Testing generation, missing inputs, and maintenance under the same reporting requirements therefore requires additional reference construction. title: Sustaining the Future with Speculative Proposals in Design Training
abstract: This paper examines the pedagogical potential of speculative design to broaden approaches to circular design and sustainability in design education. While circular design is often framed through operational concerns such as materials, efficiency, lifecycle thinking, and resource management, this study explores how speculative methods can support critical reflection on the cultural, social, political, and imaginative dimensions of sustainable futures. title: Digital Twin-Enabled Energy Simulation for Automated Zero-Emission Vessels in Constrained Inland Waterways
abstract: This paper presents a physics-informed energy simulation model, PRISM, developed within the EU-funded FOREMAST project to support sustainable inland waterway transport. FOREMAST promotes a modal shift from road to waterway freight by introducing Small, Flexible, Automated, and Zero-emission (SFAZ) vessels for constrained and ecologically sensitive waterways. PRISM estimates energy consumption along segmented routes, balancing power flow between LiFePO4 batteries and hydrogen fuel cells to optimize range and operational efficiency. title: Cross-Pilot Integration of Automated Logistics: Insights from AutoMoTIF
abstract: In recent decades, automation has emerged as a promising way to address various challenges associated with the growing complexity of freight transport and logistics, while enhancing safety and efficiency in global supply chains. Interoperability is key when automation is introduced; nevertheless, most applications so far are characterized by fragmentation across modes and operational environments. title: Spatio-Temporal Data Management and Enhanced Processing for Urban Heat Island Analysis supported by Digital Elevation Models

title: Depoliticised Sustainability in Fashion Higher Education: Classroom Discourse, Risk, and the Limits of Critique
abstract: This paper examines the de-politicisation of sustainability within fashion higher education, arguing that sustainability is discursively re-engineered into an aesthetic, technological, and personal-responsibility orientation. As a result, sustainability is permitted primarily in non-disruptive and non-antagonistic forms, narrowing pedagogical latitude and limiting the scope for collective critique and political engagement. title: Speaking for Others: A Scoping Review of Entity-Representing Conversational Agents and Interactional Representation
abstract: Conversational agents increasingly communicate from positions associated with organisations, people, cultural artefacts, and more-than-human entities. However, research on these systems remains fragmented across domains, and it remains unclear how an agent’s interaction becomes a form of representation. We introduce entity-representing conversational agents (ERCAs) as a cross-domain lens for examining this relationship. title: From Alerts to Causes: Backtracing of Security Events with Metric Temporal Logic
abstract: The volume of alerts handled daily by analysts in Security Operations Centers (SOCs) has prompted the research community to devise new strategies to aid the triage effort, and ensure that legitimate critical alerts are handled in a timely manner. In this paper, we propose combining an alert correlation engine with log retrieval to reconstruct chains of event logs associated with incoming alerts. This process allows, for an analyst, to automatically obtain an established context for an alert and its neighbours, within the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain model. title: Are Items Answering the Right Questions? A Context-sensitive Approach to Cataloging AI-generated Media
abstract: This study critiques conventional cataloging practices, arguing that describing items based solely on the information they contain overlooks contextual factors that shape meaning and authenticity. Drawing on Walter Benjamin and Jean Baudrillard, this study examines how cultural information objects are detached from their provenance, turning them into self-referent objects, a process intensified by generative AI’s simulation of content and labor. journal: Proceedings of the ALISE Annual Conference

title: A Technology-Driven Maturity Framework for Truck Appointment Systems in Ports
abstract: Truck Appointment Systems (TAS) are essential tools for reducing gate congestion at container terminals (CTs). However, the adoption of these systems and the required enabling technologies varies across CTs. This study presents a five level TAS maturity framework, linking technological capabilities to operational, environmental, and economic performance, to create resilient, decarbonised ports. The methodology follows a sequential logic: insights from the literature review and technology mapping are used to define relevant KPIs, which serve as inputs for the techno-economic evaluation. title: Operational Resilience of Road Systems When Disruptions Arise
abstract: Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly to emerging threats results in cascading risks across the interdependent services like emergency response and healthcare. This research adopts a systems thinking approach to investigate how operational resilience of the road systems can be enhanced during such disruptions. title: From Uniformity to Reform: Fashion, Decadence, and Material Transformation
abstract: This contribution proposes an approach to fashion that considers clothing items as primary sources of knowledge, capable of articulating time and cultural context. Fashion is understood both as material culture and as a symbolic system that questions the relationship between the individual and the collective. As such, it institutionalizes decadence, producing the “new” within a logic that already anticipates its obsolescence. Practices historically rooted in preservation and reuse – particularly in the 18 th and 19 th centuries – acquire renewed ethical relevance in relation to the environment
journal: Springer series in design and innovation

title: Biological Design as an Interdisciplinary Strategy for Solving Sustainability Issues
abstract: This paper explores using biological design as a framework to teach problem-solving in the classroom by integrating it in design inspirations. The field of Sustainability Studies is inherently interdisciplinary and allows for the synthesis of concepts from various fields of study, humanities, social sciences, design, and STEM. Sustainability in innovation is well-recognized in the design world. Designers and engineers are focused on providing low environmental impact in their projects, and design aims are rapidly shifting from Human-centered design to Life-centered design. title: Initial Field Testing of a Small-Scale Hybrid Solar Gas Turbine in a Rural Community
abstract: This paper presents the initial field testing and performance evaluation of a mobile, concentrated solar thermal Brayton cycle power plant (unrecuperated) developed at the University of Pretoria. Designed for rural deployment, the system integrated 42 elliptical facets (totalling 22.6 m² of reflective area) and a helical cavity receiver to concentrate solar energy for cogeneration of electricity and heat. title: From Designing for People to Designing Through Relationships: Relational Interaction Design (RID) in an Indigenous-Led XR Collaboration
abstract: Human-centred interaction design typically begins by identifying people's needs and designing technologies to support them. This paper asks what might change if Interaction Design instead began through relationships. Drawing on a multi-year, Indigenous-led collaboration with my own hapū (clan) in Te Matau-a-Māui (Hawke's Bay) in New Zealand, I reflect on the design of extended reality (XR) possibilities for river and coastline stewardship under climate change. title: Performance-Based Ranking of Building Damage Assessment Methods
abstract: Building damage assessment (BDA) from satellite imagery is evaluated in many different ways: the task is formulated as classification, semantic segmentation or instance segmentation, damage classes differ from one dataset to the next, and results are summarized almost always by a single score, usually a variant of F1, so published results are rarely comparable. This talk introduces a probabilistic theory of performance-based ranking. title: Beyond Model Choice: Designing Maintainable and Source-Grounded LLM Assistants for Academic Advising
abstract: Students increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for academic advice, yet general-purpose models often lack institution-specific knowledge and can provide confident but inaccurate guidance. This creates risks for students and raises design questions about how universities should develop reliable, accountable, and maintainable LLM advising systems. This study evaluates three approaches for incorporating institutional knowledge into LLM-based advising systems: prompting, retrieval, and fine-tuning, compared across three open-weight models producing 48 configurations. title: The 2026 United States and Israeli Military Conflict with Iran: Implications for International Relations, Global Governance and Security
abstract: The 2026 Military Conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran is an example of a local geopolitical shock that can create a domino effect of vulnerabilities in organisations, the economy, energy, transport and security. This problem is described by existing scholarship, on geopolitical risk, systemic propagation, strategic signalling, information uncertainty, energy security and crisis governance. title: UNDERGROUND COAL GASIFICATION: FROM CONCEPT TO COMMERCIAL APPLICATION
abstract: Ensuring a reliable and sustainable energy supply represents one of the most critical environmental, economic and societal challenges of the 21st century. Despite the accelerated transition to renewable energy sources, fossil fuels- especially coal are expected to remain a significant energy component in the foreseeable future. Researches indicates a continued increase in coal demand, underscoring the necessity for more efficient, economically viable, and environmentally acceptable utilization technologies. title: Climate Stories in Conversation: Localising Tuvaluan Storytelling for Relational Climate Engagement
abstract: Climate change is experienced unevenly, yet many engagement approaches prioritise behaviour change and information provision. We explore how culturally grounded storytelling can support relational climate engagement across Tuvaluan and Australian contexts. Through Research through Design, we collaborated with a Tuvaluan co-designer and Australian contributors using cultural sensitisation, localisation, story elicitation, thematic analysis, and iterative prototyping. title: Polar remote sensing in China: advances, integrated observation systems, and future perspectives
abstract: Polar environmental changes affect the surface energy balance, ocean circulation, and global sea level. Constrained by extreme environmental conditions and logistical challenges, traditional in situ observations exhibit limitations in spatial coverage and temporal continuity. Remote sensing supports polar environmental research by providing repeated observations over large areas. title: Diffusion models in atmospheric and oceanic research: a survey
abstract: Diffusion models represent a novel class of generative models with exceptional generative capabilities across various domains, including computer vision and multimodal learning. As research progresses, their applications have increasingly extended to meteorology and oceanography, providing innovative solutions to challenges such as data noise and the rising frequency of extreme weather events. By simulating the noise diffusion process in datasets, they can accurately capture latent patterns and trends, facilitating data assimilation, forecasting, and post-processing. title: Ice–ocean albedo feedback as a key mechanism driving recent Antarctic summer sea-ice decline
abstract: Antarctic summer sea-ice extent has exhibited a remarkable declining trend since 2016, reaching a record minimum in February 2023. This decline could accelerate regional warming, disrupt deep water formation and carbon cycling, and negatively affect Southern Ocean ecosystems. However, the mechanism driving this decline remains incompletely understood. Our analyses of satellite sea-ice data and heat flux calculations suggest that the ice–ocean albedo feedback is one of the key contributing processes to the recent decline. title: Antarctic sea ice variability and monsoonal precipitation: a review of reported teleconnections, associations and uncertainties
abstract: Antarctic sea ice variability is increasingly recognized as a potentially important component of the coupled Southern Hemisphere climate system. Growing observational, reanalysis, and modeling evidence suggests that Antarctic sea ice anomalies are associated with large-scale atmospheric circulation changes that may contribute to climate variability in tropical and subtropical regions. title: A new high-resolution daily mean South China Sea Ocean Reanalysis dataset: SCSORA
abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) ocean reanalysis data are essential for investigating multiscale ocean dynamics in the regional ocean and their impacts on energy transport, marine ecosystems, and climate change. The South China Sea (SCS), as one of the most eddy-active marginal seas in the global ocean, is characterized by complex 3D dynamical processes and frequent extreme ocean events, imposing urgent data demands on the scientific community. title: Vertical Characteristics of Marine Heatwaves in Global Coral Reef Regions
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) threaten coral reef ecosystems worldwide, yet their subsurface characteristics remain poorly understood. Using two high‐resolution ocean reanalysis products spanning 1993–2023, we reveal the global spatiotemporal patterns of subsurface MHWs across coral reef regions. MHW annual days decrease with depth, while their cumulative intensity increase, indicating that deep events are stronger but less frequent. title: Sea ice variability and links to East Siberian permafrost carbon remobilization during the last glacial-interglacial transition
abstract: Sea ice plays a central role in the polar climate system, and its rapid decline in the Arctic over recent decades has altered surface albedo and the exchange of heat and gases between the ocean and atmosphere. Investigations of earlier warming events, such as the Preboreal/Early Holocene (PB/EH, 11–8 kyr B.P.), Bølling-Allerød (B/A, 14.7–12.9 kyr B.P.), and Dansgaard Oeschger event 3 (DO-3, 28–27.5 kyr B.P.), likely hold clues on climate system responses to changes in Arctic sea ice. title: Linking Scaffold Architecture, Ion Transport and Biofilm Formation in Functionalized TPMS Scaffolds Using a Digital Twin Framework
abstract: Periprosthetic infections remain a major complication of orthopedic implants despite advances in antimicrobial surface functionalization. While antibacterial coatings can reduce bacterial colonization, local transport phenomena within porous implant architectures may generate spatially heterogeneous antimicrobial exposure, potentially influencing biofilm persistence. title: Domain landfast sea-ice simulation and forecast in Prydz Bay, East Antarctica in 2016
abstract: Landfast ice near Zhongshan Station critically affects Antarctic navigation, logistical support and expedition safety. A one-dimensional thermodynamic model called Icepack was used to simulate landfast sea ice in the 68–70°S, 72–80°E domain near Zhongshan Station in Prydz Bay from March 2016 to February 2017. Driven by raw, 7 day Global Forecast System (GFS) data, validation showed GFS biases: overestimated downward shortwave radiation and precipitation and underestimated air temperature. Sea-ice thickness simulations were slightly thinner than field measurements, with a mean bias of −14.0 cm.

title: Intelligent Operation and Maintenance of High-End Drilling Equipment for Deep-Sea and Deep-Earth Applications: A Review and Conceptual Framework
abstract: This study provides a technology-level reference for the future development, implementation, and validation of intelligent O&M systems for high-end drilling equipment. Intelligent operation and maintenance systems for high-end drilling equipment provide crucial technological support for addressing the challenges posed by extreme environments in deep-sea and deep-earth drilling and are intended to facilitate the transition from traditional reactive maintenance toward predictive maintenance. This study adopts a narrative technology review approach combined with a conceptual framework synthesis.

title: Coastal ocean properties in the Galápagos upwelling region
abstract: The Galapagos Islands and the Galapagos Cold Pool to their west serve as a biological hotspot due to frequent episodic upwelling of subsurface waters high in nutrients. The region’s primary productivity provides an important base to multiple endemic species within the ecosystem as well as a sink for the anomalously high sea surface pCO2 that also results from the upwelling. In situ observations of near-surface seawater properties collected between the cold pool and the coast of the archipelago are limited, despite interest in the region’s distinctive biological and physical processes. The researcher proposes an innovative econometric model based on natural resource infrastructure using Predictive Analysis embedded in the human-focused, sustainability, and resiliency aspects of the fifth Industrial revolution. title: A study on the 3D printing preparation method of reinforced casings for lithium-ion batteries in energy storage power stations using high specific energy absorption metamaterials
abstract: Additive manufacturing has enabled the development of advanced lattice and metamaterial structures with tailored mechanical performance for energy absorption and lightweight structural applications. In this study, a novel round gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) metamaterial is designed, fabricated 3D printing, and systematically investigated under quasi-static compression loading. A combined experimental and finite element method (FEM) approach is employed to evaluate the mechanical response and validate the numerical model. title: A large ice‐dammed lake in the western Danish North Sea: Deglacial evolution and ice‐margin dynamics
abstract: The Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) ice extent in the western Danish North Sea remains unchartered, which impedes our understanding of the last glacial to Holocene transition in the region. Despite increasing interest in the shallow subsurface of the North Sea, there is still a knowledge gap concerning this transition. In this study, we describe the geological evolution of the southern part of the western Danish North Sea using high‐resolution seismic data, with emphasis on the LGM and the late Quaternary development. title: SWORD-CTRIP mapping (SCM v1.0): a confidence-aware framework for mapping satellite-derived river reaches to gridded routing networks
abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides reach-scale river observations referenced to the vector-based SWORD database. Linking these observations to gridded routing models such as CTRIP requires reconciling differences in river network representation. We present SCM v1.0, a global mapping framework that combines spatial intersection and MERIT Hydro-derived River information with a geometric scoring procedure based on proximity, reach length, and flow-direction alignment. title: The accelerating northward expansion of the South Asian High has slowed regional sea ice melt in the Arctic
abstract: Summer Arctic sea ice affects Arctic shipping, the regional ecological environment, atmospheric blocking highs, and even the subsequent East Asian winter monsoon variability; consequently, the mechanisms governing its evolution have received extensive attention. This study investigates impacts of the South Asian High (SAH) on the slowdown of Arctic regional sea ice melt through diagnostic analyses and nudging experiments. title: Simulated Antarctic iceberg melting occurs primarily within the Southern Ocean mixed layer
abstract: Although iceberg meltwater accounts for nearly half of the freshwater release from the Antarctic ice sheet, most ocean models do not represent the vertical distribution of this meltwater in a realistic way. Here, we investigate the importance of distributing the iceberg meltwater vertically in an ocean model that represents icebergs as Lagrangian particles. title: The Azores plume origin of the New England Seamounts chain
abstract: Age-progressive seamount chains are fundamental archives in revealing the past plate motion and mantle convection. However, for a representative example such as the New England Seamounts chain on the North American Plate, both its plume source and its evolutionary trajectory remain debatable. This long-lasting uncertainty is mainly caused by the absence of quantitative high-resolution constraints on plume dynamics and its interactions with multiple plates. title: Secondary Microseisms' Propagation Effects Highlighted by Joint DAS Observations and Full Waveform Modeling Offshore Sicily
abstract: The use of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) on submarine cables provides new opportunities to investigate the microseism wavefield generated by ocean surface gravity waves at the seafloor, but its interpretation requires understanding how signals propagate through seafloor heterogeneities to reach the cable. Here, DAS data collected on a submarine cable offshore Catania, Sicily is investigated to analyze an episode of enhanced secondary microseism activity originating in the Mediterranean Sea. title: Land Temperature Sensitivity to the Extreme Oceanic Conditions of 2023 in CESM2
abstract: Global mean surface temperature reached unprecedented levels in 2023, alongside record‐high sea surface temperatures and sea ice retreat. However, how land temperature responds to such anomalous oceanic conditions remains unresolved. Using a land‐atmosphere coupled model with prescribed observed sea surface temperature and sea ice conditions in 2023 relative to a 1982–2001 climatology baseline, we quantify this land temperature sensitivity. title: Toward Self-Regulating Oscillating Water Column Systems: State of the Art in Wave-to-Wire Control, Intelligent Adaptation, and Reliability
abstract: Oscillating water column (OWC) wave energy converters operate under variable and nonlinear marine conditions, making advanced control essential for efficient, stable, and reliable energy conversion. This review examines the evolution of OWC control from conventional turbine-level regulation toward predictive, intelligent, adaptive, and fault-aware operation, with emphasis on their contribution to self-regulating systems. title: Winter Barents–Kara Sea ice loss preconditions a summer drought corridor across Eastern Europe and Eurasia
abstract: Droughts are becoming increasingly severe and widespread across Eurasia, with major consequences for agriculture, public health, and regional economies. Although declining Arctic sea ice has been linked to midlatitude climate extremes, the directionality and physical robustness of its relationship with summer drought remains uncertain. Here, we apply a multi-method framework, based on observational data, that integrates statistical analyses with information flow diagnostics, predictive autoregressive models, and physical diagnostics. title: A Sustained High Growth Regime After Collapse of the Arctic Sea Ice Volume Feedback
abstract: We investigate changing Arctic sea ice growth behavior by synthesizing 29 years (1994–2023) of remote sensing products into a sea ice volume budget. By resolving dynamic and thermodynamic terms, we reveal a regime change in growth. Arctic sea ice has undergone a 1,077 (259) km 3 increase in mean winter growth following the 2007/08 winter. title: Assimilation of Mobile Doppler-Lidar Wind Profiles from a Wave Glider for Tropical Cyclone Track Prediction
abstract: Sparse lower-tropospheric wind observations over the ocean remain an important source of uncertainty in tropical cyclone (TC) track prediction. This proof-of-concept case study examines lower-tropospheric wind profiles collected by a wave glider equipped with Doppler wind lidar over the northern South China Sea during Typhoon KRATHON (2024). The quality-controlled profiles were assimilated into the Weather Research and Forecasting model using hourly three-dimensional variational rapid update cycling (RUC). Two 72 h forecasts were compared: a control experiment without the wave-glider observati

title: Seasonal sea ice formation re-establishes the cold halocline layer on the Northeast Greenland Shelf
abstract: Hydrographic changes of the Northeast Greenland Shelf, located along the cold branch of the AMOC pathway, can alter the thermohaline circulation and global climate system. Regardless, the hydrography of the Northeast Greenland Shelf has been historically overlooked. Intra-annual variability remains poorly understood as scarce observations from ice-free periods depict a persistent Cold Halocline Layer (CHL) with near freezing temperatures overlying warmer waters. title: Impact of the Individual Satellite Sea Surface Temperature Observations in the Global Ocean Reanalysis GODAPS2-RA: an Observing System Experiment Approach
abstract: Observing system experiments (OSEs) within Korea Meteorological Administration’s global ocean reanalysis system (GODAPS2-RA) are conducted to assess the impact of individual satellite sea surface temperature (SST) observations: the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2), the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS), MetOp-B Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (AVHRR), and NOAA AVHRR. title: Las oposiciones individuo/estadio y evento/objeto en combinación con ser y estar. Un estudio basado en juicios de preferencia y aceptabilidad
abstract: El presente trabajo busca analizar el comportamiento de las cópulas del español ser y estar en combinación con adjetivos de tipo i-level/s-level, así como con sustantivos eventivos y no eventivos en oraciones locativas. Estudios previos han mostrado que algunas de estas unidades admiten con facilidad una de las cópulas, pero no así la opuesta, lo que permite plantearse si esta asimetría se debe a una representación mental diferente. title: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
abstract: Large-scale circulation waviness shapes day-to-day weather and extremes. During 1989 to 2011, Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes experienced a pronounced increase in wintertime waviness, coinciding with rapid Arctic warming and more frequent cold-air outbreaks. While Arctic amplification was hypothesized to cause this trend via jet weakening, subsequent studies have failed to support this mechanism, leaving the origin unresolved. title: Subsurface marine heat surge produces delayed climate impacts in the North Pacific
abstract: Marine heatwaves are iconic markers of a warming world, yet the climatic feedbacks of extreme warming in the ocean interior remain largely unexplored. Here we identify two subsurface marine heat surges originating in the eastern North Pacific in 2009 and 2013 using Argo observations, ocean reanalysis data, and water parcel tracking. These surges transport significant heat and volume anomalies into the tropics during multi-year, trans-basin migrations. Their downstream signals precede and correlate strongly with the 2015/16 and 2019/20 El Niño events, respectively. Theoretical considerations su
institutions: Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology

title: Revisiting the relationship between sea surface temperature and coral species richness in Japan: nestedness and regional variation beyond temperature
abstract: In Japan, coral species richness has long been known to decline with decreasing winter sea surface temperature (SST). However, recent taxonomic revisions, together with the accumulation of occurrence records from temperate regions, have enabled re-evaluation of this relationship using an updated nationwide database. Although high-latitude coral communities in Japan have long been suggested to form subsets of lower-latitude communities, quantitative tests of this nested structure along a detailed thermal gradient remain limited. Here, we analyzed reef-building coral occurrence records from 1059
journal: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science

title: The implementation and effectiveness of Calving Algorithms in numerical ice models (CalvingMIP)
abstract: Ice calving plays a significant role in ice sheet mass loss. Predictions of future ice sheet mass balance require accurate representations of the calving process in numerical ice models to determine rates of future global mean sea level rise. Whilst calving has recently begun to be implemented in numerical models there has not yet been a systematic investigation into how this implementation compares between different ice flow models. title: Multi-year predictability of hydrography and circulation on the U.S. Northeast Shelf: a dynamical downscaling perspective
abstract: The U.S. Northeast Shelf (NES) is a dynamic and economically important marine ecosystem where temperature and salinity variability are shaped by interactions among large-scale climate variability, Gulf Stream shifts, mesoscale eddies, and local shelf processes. Predicting these variations on multi-year timescales remains a major challenge for current climate systems, as global models at typically 1–2° resolution exhibit poor skills for the NES. title: Dust storms effects on surface-heat flux and sea surface temperature in the Red Sea
abstract: Extreme Dust Days (EDDs) are much more frequent in the southern part of the Red Sea (RS) compared to the northern part during the dust season (March–August) over the period 1980–2024. In this study, MERRA-2 surface heat-flux data and AVHRR SST observations are analyzed to investigate the influence of extreme dust events on surface heat fluxes and associated SST variability in the Red Sea. During this period, an increasing trend in EDD occurrence over the Red Sea is observed. title: Intermediate Water Salinification Counteracts Thermosteric Sea‐Level Rise in the Tropical Southwest Indian Ocean
abstract: Sea level in the tropical Southwest Indian Ocean has risen rapidly during the Argo era, yet whether its mid‐depth halosteric component reflects along‐isopycnal change or isopycnal displacement remains unresolved. Using gridded Argo data for 2004–2023, we decompose steric sea level into thermosteric and halosteric components and partition temperature and salinity trends into heave (isopycnal displacement) and spice (along‐isopycnal change). title: Heatwaves, Boundary Layer Responses, and Modification by Sea Breezes in the Western Mediterranean
abstract: Heatwaves are intensifying across the Mediterranean, yet the processes governing planetary boundary layer responses to extreme heat remain poorly understood, particularly in coastal regions where mesoscale and synoptic circulations interact. Here, we examine the relationship between heatwaves, sea breeze circulations and planetary boundary layer height (BLH) using four decades (1981–2021) of ERA5 reanalysis data and a database of sea breeze occurrences at seven coastal sites across the western Mediterranean. An assessment of seasonal and extreme sea-level variability in the Indonesian Seas derived from new tide-gauge records
abstract: The Indonesian Seas, at the junction of the Pacific and Indian Oceans, exhibit pronounced spatial and temporal sea-level variability. However, a lack of tide-gauge data in the Indonesian Seas limits our understanding of sea-level variability in the region. Here, we assemble and analyze hourly tide-gauge records from 20 sites spanning 2005–2023, including 12 previously unpublished tide-gauge stations obtained from the Indonesian Geospatial Information Agency, to characterise seasonal sea-level variability and extremes. Notably, these 12 stations provide records beyond 2018, which are not public

title: Improved CMIP6 projections of Hudson Bay region navigability using bias correction and route continuity
abstract: Hudson Bay's seasonal sea ice limits maritime access to the Port of Churchill. This study improves on past efforts to project future navigability of shipping routes from Churchill by correcting for substantial model biases, better combining sea ice concentration (SIC) and sea ice thickness (SIT) into calculations, and incorporating a novel path-finding approach that requires continuous navigable routes (rather than relying on spatial domain averages). Linking ridge shapes to the ice thickness distribution via discrete element simulations
abstract: Sea-ice ridges are piles of ice rubble extending into the water and piling up on top of the ice, created by convergent ice motion. Consequently, ridges significantly increase the sea-ice thickness compared to the level ice surrounding them. In continuum sea-ice models, this increase is either represented by an increase in mean ice thickness or by changes in the ice thickness distribution (ITD). The implementation of ITDs requires a sub-grid parametrization of ridging by using a redistribution scheme. title: Sea salt aerosols from blowing snow: contributions to radiative forcing
abstract: The Arctic and Antarctic regions experience significant climate impacts from aerosol–cloud–radiation interactions, yet the role of sea salt aerosols (SSA) emitted through blowing snow remains poorly quantified. We implement a parameterization of blowing-snow SSA production in the TM5 global chemical transport model and the EC-Earth3 global climate model, using atmosphere-only and fully coupled transient (SSP3-7.0, 2015–2051) experiments to assess the contribution of blowing snow to aerosol mass, number, cloud condensation nuclei (CCN), and radiative fluxes in both polar regions. title: CFD Comparison of Marine Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchangers
abstract: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers (STHXs) are critical thermal management components in marine engineering, where design must balance thermal transport against the hydraulic pressure drop and auxiliary pumping power it demands. Marine-specific baffle geometries are rarely evaluated within a single validated framework that jointly addresses thermal performance, dead-zone-driven biofouling risk, nozzle-dominated pressure losses and fabrication-versus-energy cost. This study presents a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) investigation and comparative thermo-hydraulic evaluation of a marine STHX. The
journal: Journal of Naval Sciences and Engineering

title: Spatiotemporal shoreline and sea level dynamics along the Kenyan coast (2000–2024): patterns of erosion, accretion, and spatial autocorrelation
abstract: Shoreline management in the Western Indian Ocean (WIO) is largely informed by small-scale studies with coarse temporal resolution, potentially obscuring fine spatial patterns and interannual dynamics. This study examines spatiotemporal shoreline change along 400 km of the Kenyan coastline from 2000 to 2024 and tests its association with regional sea-level trend and variability, accounting for spatial dependence. title: HSSW Salinity Potentially Modulated by Summertime Preconditioning in Terra Nova Bay Polynya
abstract: High Salinity Shelf Water (HSSW) in Terra Nova Bay, a key constituent of Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW), freshened from 1959 to 2014 before reversing in 2015. Variations in HSSW salinity influence AABW properties, global ocean heat and oxygen distribution. Yet, observations informing salinity trends are primarily collected during austral summer, months after HSSW is formed by wintertime brine rejection in Antarctic polynyas. title: Isolating the influence of aerosols on Arctic cloud radiative effects during a polluted warm air mass intrusion
abstract: Arctic warm air mass intrusions are key to the region's energy balance because they transport large amounts of heat and moisture from lower latitudes. The resulting changes in heat and moisture content influences cloud properties, the thermodynamic structure of the boundary layer, and surface radiation. Warm air mass intrusions can also carry significant amounts of aerosols into the Arctic, including aerosols from anthropogenic sources at lower latitudes, which could influence the radiative impacts of such events. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Wave-dependent mixing effects on hydrodynamic and water quality simulations in Osaka Bay, Japan
abstract: Numerical models are widely used to evaluate water quality dynamics and management measures in enclosed coastal systems. However, the effects of wave-dependent mixing on hydrodynamic and water quality simulations remain insufficiently examined in many regional applications, particularly in highly enclosed bays where tidal currents and estuarine circulation dominate over nearshore wave-driven currents. title: Frequent occurrence of newly formed aerosol particles over wide geographical areas in the Arctic free troposphere and atmospheric boundary layer
abstract: New particle formation (NPF) can impact the Arctic radiative energy budget since this region is particularly sensitive to changes in aerosol particle and cloud condensation nuclei concentrations. Prior measurements have predominantly investigated NPF in the Arctic atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), while vertically-resolved studies on newly formed aerosol particles remain scarce. Here, we present an analysis which suggests that NPF may take place throughout the entire lower Arctic troposphere. title: Teleconnection processes linking snow cover variability over western Siberia to enhanced early-winter cold waves in South Korea
abstract: This study examines thermodynamic teleconnection processes to identify the drivers of the increasing frequency of December cold waves in South Korea over the 46-year study period. By modifying the cold day index and cold wave advisory criteria of the Korea Meteorological Administration, we calculated revised cold day index and applied principal component analysis to extract a representative time series of nationwide cold day variability. title: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
abstract: Since October 2024 the Météo-France operational convective scale model AROME-France has been using a 3DEnVar data assimilation (DA) scheme in order to improve the performance of severe weather prediction. This paper describes the configuration and evaluation of this 3DEnVar scheme. It summarizes the work carried out to configure this scheme in an operational context, with the inherent constraints of numerical robustness, compatible execution times, and of course correct performance of the forecasts produced. title: Coastal Flooding at Large Scales: Fundamentals and Methods Overview
abstract: Coastal flooding threatens lives, infrastructure, ecosystems, and economic activity, making reliable assessments essential for coastal planning and adaptation to sea-level rise. Coastal flood assessments over regional to global scales must reconcile broad spatial coverage with the local processes that control hazardous water levels and inundation. This review examines the physical foundations and methodological approaches used in large-scale assessments, with particular attention to the representation of wave contributions to total water level. title: Future projections of compound events around the Main Hawaiian Islands
abstract: The consequences of overlapping environmental stressors – referred to as compound events – may be more harmful to marine ecosystems than as individual stressors. Using recently conducted submesoscale-permitting future projections for the Main Hawaiian Islands, we present the first assessment of future compound events for Hawaiian waters. Our analysis focuses on surface and sub-surface heat-stress, ocean acidification, and low-oxygen events and is based on three different greenhouse gas emission scenarios. We show that a large fraction of ocean around Hawai'i will be subject to compound events

title: Increasing favorability for intense tropical cyclone activity in the northern South China Sea
abstract: The South China Sea (SCS) is one of the most active marginal seas for tropical cyclones (TCs) worldwide and a key region for TC hazards along the coasts of southern China, Philippines and Vietnam. However, the drivers of long-term changes in intense TC development in this region remain unclear. Here, we show that the number of TCs reaching Category 3–5 intensity has increased significantly, with more occurring in the northern SCS. title: BOWTIE: ship-based measurements of atmosphere and ocean within the moist tropical Atlantic
abstract: As part of BOWTIE (German: Beobachtung von Ozean und Wolken – Das Trans ITCZ Experiment), the German research vessel FS Meteor navigated the moist tropics of the Atlantic Ocean for 40 d in summer 2024, with an east-west trajectory. The journey started in the port of Mindelo, Cape Verde, on 16 August, and finished in the port of Bridgetown, Barbados, on 24 September. The objective was to measure properties of the atmosphere, upper ocean, and air-sea interface within the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), under a variety of wind, convection, and sea surface temperature regimes. title: Gap filling of missing and invalid values in SWOT wide-swath sea surface height data using Attention U-Net
abstract: High-resolution sea surface height (SSH) data are essential for studying mesoscale and submesoscale ocean dynamics. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite, launched on 16 December 2022, provides high-resolution SSH observations over a 120-km swath. However, the 20-km nadir gap and invalid data regions in SWOT Level-3 products create spatial discontinuities, limiting continuous observations of fine-scale ocean processes. To address this problem, an Attention U-Net-based gap-filling model is proposed to fill both the nadir gap and invalid data regions in SWOT wide-swath SSH data

title: Consistent Sea‐Level and Energy Budget Residuals Suggest Enhanced Deep‐Ocean Heat Uptake Since the Mid‐2010s
abstract: The deep ocean (>2,000 m) comprises ∼50% of the total ocean volume and is crucial in Earth's climate system, yet its warming remains uncertain owing to limited observations. We revisit the recently reported non‐closure of the global mean sea‐level (GMSL) budget and show that, despite instrumental corrections, the budget residual has increased since the mid‐2010s. title: Effects of snow redistribution parameterization on simulated snow thickness validated by MOSAiC observations
abstract: Snow plays a critical role in the mass and energy balance of sea ice through its insulating properties and high albedo. Based on observations from the Multidisciplinary Drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate (MOSAiC) campaign, we assess the influence of two Icepack snow redistribution parameterizations, bulk redistribution and blowing snow redistribution, on snow thickness simulations using the Icepack column model. title: Reassessing tsunami evacuation planning in a postdisaster coastal area: a GIS-based study of Baitussalam, Indonesia
abstract: Purpose The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami highlighted the importance of effective evacuation planning in tsunami-prone coastal areas. In the Baitussalam coastal area, Indonesia, postdisaster population growth and rapid residential development have reduced the relevance of tsunami evacuation routes established more than a decade ago. This study aims to reassess tsunami evacuation planning in the Baitussalam coastal area, Indonesia, by updating evacuation routes and identifying suitable final evacuation sites in response to postdisaster population growth and rapid residential development. title: Influence of ocean tides on apparent ground thermal conductivity inferred from thermal response tests
abstract: This study investigated the influence of tide-induced groundwater flow on the thermal performance of deep horizontal ground heat exchangers (HGHEs) installed using horizontal directional drilling (HDD) for ground-source heat pump (GSHP) systems. Heating cable-based thermal response tests (TRTs) were first conducted in three 20 m deep vertical boreholes at coastal sites in Saga Prefecture, Japan. title: Long‐Term Strengthening of the Summer Indian Ocean Subtropical Cell and Its Underlying Mechanisms
abstract: The Indian Ocean Subtropical Cell (STC) is a shallow overturning circulation that links the subtropical and equatorial oceans and plays a key role in redistributing heat. Although strongest during boreal summer, its long‐term evolution remains poorly understood. Using multiple ocean reanalysis and pacemaker experiments, we show that the summer STC has significantly strengthened since 1980 (−0.047 ± 0.010 Sv yr −1 ). title: Modelling the effects of proglacial lake filling and drainage on lake-terminating glacier dynamics
abstract: The rapid retreat of glaciers worldwide is leading to the formation and expansion of proglacial and ice-marginal lakes. Proglacial lakes not only influence glacier dynamics and contribute to accelerated mass loss, but also pose a growing risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), particularly as warming intensifies in polar and high-mountain regions. Despite important feedbacks between glacier behaviour and lake expansion, ice–lake interactions remain understudied compared to ice–ocean processes, introducing considerable uncertainty in projections of future mass loss. Shoreline change and hydroclimatic variability at Ras Al-Katib, Red Sea coast, Yemen: implications for coastal conservation and management
abstract: Ras Al-Katib is a dynamic coastal barrier adjacent to the Port of Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast of Yemen, where shoreline instability may affect coastal infrastructure and navigation. This study quantifies shoreline change along a 5.6-km sector and evaluates its consistency with regional wind and offshore wave forcing. Multi-temporal satellite imagery from 2000, 2010, and 2020 was analysed using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS), while hourly wind data (2000--2020) and ERA5 wave parameters (2001--2020) were assessed, with ERA5 evaluated against buoy observations from 2003--2004. title: Significant offshore rainfall trends during sea-land breeze transition hours
abstract: The understanding of coastal precipitation changes is critical for climate adaptation, yet their diurnal-scale responses to global warming demand robust observational constraints. In this manuscript, using 25 years (2000–2024) of high-resolution IMERG satellite precipitation data, we systematically investigate globally averaged behavior of precipitation trends in coastal and offshore regions, with a focus on diurnal variations and physical drivers. title: Tropical Cyclones Increasingly Reach Peak Intensity Near Continental Landfall
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) typically weaken before landfall after reaching peak intensity over the open ocean. Here we show that this behavior has changed markedly in recent decades. Using global best‐track and reanalysis data sets from 1980 to 2023, we find a significant increase in TCs that intensify within 24 hr of landfall and attain peak intensity at or near the continental coast. Both the frequency and proportion of these events have nearly doubled, with trends concentrated in nearshore regions. title: Along-strike dredging reveals a crust-dominated section at the Marie Celeste Fracture Zone, Central Indian Ridge
abstract: Scarps along oceanic fracture zones provide key tectonic windows into the architecture of oceanic lithosphere. Recent investigations along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (MAR) demonstrate that such scarps can expose both crust- and mantle-dominated sections. However, integrated datasets combining bathymetry, seafloor imagery, and systematic rock sampling remain spatially uneven, limiting direct comparisons among fracture-zone systems. title: Quantifying the near-term response of the ocean CO 2 sink to reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations
abstract: The ocean plays a critical role in sequestering carbon, yet how the air–sea carbon sink will respond to rapid reductions in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations remains a key uncertainty for climate mitigation and carbon accounting. In this study, we utilize the ECCO-Darwin ocean biogeochemistry model to simulate the ocean's response to a range of near-term CO 2 mitigation scenarios which are simulated with reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations. title: Classification of Synoptic Conditions Associated with High-Frequency Sea-Level Extremes in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Classification of synoptic conditions associated with the Mediterranean high-frequency (HF; T < 2 h) sea-level extremes is qualitatively performed. The study encompasses the Adriatic Sea where initial studies of prevailing synoptic conditions associated to HF sea-level extremes were previously done, as well as the Ligurian, Tyrrhenian and Aegean Seas, i.e., seas for which systematic studies of this type are lacking. title: Fractal attractor of the deep convection cycle in the northwest Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Deep convection in the Gulf of Lion is an important ocean mixing process in the western Mediterranean Sea caused by large cooling fluxes at the sea surface. It aids the Mediterranean thermohaline circulation, and promotes phytoplankton blooming. This work investigates the three different periods of the process: preconditioning, deep convecting, and restratification, through the lens of fractal attractor analysis with the local correlation dimension. title: Remote Sensing-Based Identification And Initial Findings Of Seasonal Thermal And Colour Fronts in the Red Sea
abstract: This work investigates the seasonal variability of thermal and ocean-colour fronts in the Red Sea (RS) using daily sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) data derived from the Aqua Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) over 19 years (2003–2021). Although thermal fronts and chlorophyll variability have previously been investigated in parts of the RS, their long-term basin-wide seasonal characteristics have not been consistently quantified using a common detection framework. title: Modeling groundwater salinity evolution and mitigation strategies under stochastic climate forcings in the Comacchio coastal aquifer (Italy)
abstract: Coastal aquifers are increasingly threatened by salinization due to climate change and sea level rise, particularly in low-lying Mediterranean environments where groundwater systems are strongly connected with saline and brackish surface water bodies. This study presents a three-dimensional variable-density groundwater flow and transport model of the Comacchio coastal aquifer (northern Italy), integrating climatic datasets to investigate groundwater future response to climate forcings. title: Average received intensity of a Super-Lorentz beam propagating through oceanic turbulence
abstract: The propagation of a Super-Lorentz beam through Oceanic Turbulence is examined using the extended Huygens-Fresnel principle. The average intensity distributions of the Super-Lorentz beam at the receiver plane are analyzed with respect to the beam's flatness parameter, source size, propagation distance, and ocean turbulence parameters such as relative strength of the temperature and salinity fluctuations and the rate of dissipation of the mean square temperature. title: Salt-Diapir Controls on the Routing of Submarine-Canyon Turbidity Currents and Their Depositional Architecture: Insights from Numerical Modelling
abstract: Salt diapirs are common in the deep-water parts of salt-bearing passive margins, where they reroute the turbidity currents that cross them. Quantitative predictions of how much sediment bypasses a diapir, and where the rest is deposited, remain scarce. We simulate five canyon-fed turbidity currents that meet a single static salt diapir, using a long-term landscape-evolution model. The diapir relief is 0, 100, 200, 250 and 300 m, and the canyon depth is fixed at 200 m. title: Beach and coastal structure impacts of infragravity waves during the late december 2023 swells in Southern California
abstract: A late December 2023 swell in the Pacific impacted Southern California, generating near-record wave heights in the Santa Barbara Channel. We analyze wave conditions and resulting coastal impacts of this event using offshore buoy data, tide gage records, field observations, and numerical modeling. The storm produced significant infragravity (IG; <0.04 Hz) within local harbors. A “sneaker” wave was observed at Ventura on 28 December, overtopping a beach and seawall during high tide and causing sudden flooding over nearby infrastructure. title: Bioregionalization delineates distinct regimes of winter phytoplankton blooms in the Arabian Sea
abstract: Winter phytoplankton blooms in the northern Arabian Sea (NAS) exhibit pronounced spatial variability in timing and magnitude. abstract: Extreme wind analysis commonly assumes stationarity, although climate change may alter the statistical properties of wind extremes. abstract: Offshore solar photovoltaic (PV) systems may broaden renewable-electricity options where coastal demand, land competition and maritime space intersect. title: Unruly waters: local environmental knowledge and the erosion of Holocene stability
abstract: Coastal regions around the world are experiencing accelerated and uneven levels of change in the Anthropocene. These ongoing transformations are not only experienced through sea-level projections, but are lived and narrated in specific places. abstract: The lateral boundaries of ice streams and glaciers, commonly referred to as shear margins, play a key role in the mass balance of ice sheets. Margin migration alters the width of fast-moving ice and thus the force balance that controls ice speed and mass loss. abstract: Deep-sea benthic biodiversity remains underrepresented in climate-risk assessments because transferable indicators for species- and ecosystem-level vulnerability are still limited. abstract: Estimating low‐probability storm surges is essential for flood risk management, yet conventional asymptotic extreme value methods use only a small subset of observations and therefore produce large uncertainty at poorly gauged and ungauged sites. abstract: The northern coast of São Paulo State, Brazil, experienced the most extreme 24-h rainfall event recorded in the country between the afternoon of 18 February and the morning of 19 February 2023, with accumulated precipitation exceeding 600 mm at several rain-gauge stations. abstract: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) has been identified as a necessary complement to industrial decarbonization for climate change mitigation. title: Geomorphic Approach for Beach Downdrift of Fishing Ports and Marinas: Parabolic Model and Software MeePaSoL
abstract: Coastal erosion problems associated with a fishing port or marina on a sandy coast are caused by an imbalance of longshore sediment transport and bay shape formation on downdrift. Regardless of the availability of littoral transport, the tip of its outer breakwater would behave as an updrift control point for an embayed beach to form, by combined wave diffraction-refraction aided by nearshore current circulation. abstract: Two catastrophic rainfall events struck Henan Province, China, on 20 July 2021 and 18 September 2024, producing record‐breaking 24‐hr precipitation totals of 624.1 mm in Zhengzhou and 272.6 mm in Xiayi, respectively. abstract: Active atmospheric water harvesting extracts freshwater from ambient air by cooling it below its dew point, offering a decentralized, infrastructure-light supply for water-scarce regions such as Morocco. This study presents a high-resolution geospatial assessment of the potential, performance, and cost of a vapor-compression atmospheric water generator across Morocco. Understanding the spatial characteristics of tsunami inundation under different wave height scenarios is essential to support hazard assessment and coastal mitigation planning. abstract: The Zero-Degree Level serves as a critical boundary for aircraft structural icing in the presence of supercooled droplets. Understanding its spatiotemporal evolution is crucial for evaluating mid-tropospheric thermal shifts and aviation safety. Using ERA5 reanalysis data (1990–2024) across 38 Greek airports, this study analyses trend dynamics of mean freezing levels and lower-tail cold extremes (25th percentile-Q25) via Mann–Kendall and Sen’s slope methods. abstract: The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and Pacific-North American (PNA) patterns are the most prominent atmospheric teleconnections over the Northern Hemisphere, which are traditionally considered independent of each other. Here we use reanalysis and state-of-the-art climate models to show the emergence of unprecedented coupling between the NAO and PNA in recent decades. abstract: Anticipatory tropical cyclone warning is vital for coastal infrastructure and proactive risk management. However, existing structural tropical cyclone-induced response (TCIR) assessments rely mainly on point estimates from on-site monitoring. Trained on scarce independent cyclone records, these approaches struggle to learn robust representations and cannot quantify predictive uncertainty. abstract: Hazardous chemical leakage and explosions on navigation vessels pose severe threats to underlying underwater tunnel structures. This study adopts the TNO multi‐energy method to determine the overpressure, duration, and effective radius of blast loads induced by vessel‐based chemical explosions. abstract: As a key forage fish in the Arctic, Arctic cod ( Boreogadus saida ) plays a critical role in transferring energy in Arctic marine ecosystems. While understanding Arctic cod population dynamics within the context of a rapidly warming Arctic could provide essential information for regional conservation efforts, it remains elusive. abstract: Understanding monthly-to-annual climate variability is essential for improving climate services. Previous studies show that European summer climate, including temperature and precipitation extremes, is modulated by hemispheric large-scale circulation patterns, which themselves are connected to predictors such as North Atlantic sea surface temperature anomalies. abstract: Co-locating hydrogen production and aquaculture on floating offshore wind platforms requires dispatch policies that jointly optimize energy trading, electrolyzer longevity, and cage water quality—objectives that scalarized reinforcement learning struggles to reconcile. abstract: The performance of polymers produced with fused deposition modelling (FDM) in marine environments is a critical property for their engineering applications. This study investigates the water-ageing behaviour of polylactic acid (PLA), polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG), and carbon-fibre-reinforced PETG (PETG-CF) employing experimental testing and numerical modelling. abstract: Tsunami inundation and run-up heights are essential for studying historical earthquakes, as instrumental records are scarce. Conventional linear tsunami waveform inversion does not account for advection or bottom friction and does not incorporate a moving-boundary condition for coastal inundation and run-up. abstract: Rising global temperatures are steadily altering the frequency, intensity, and spatial distribution of extreme rainfall, with far-reaching consequences for agriculture, water security, public health, and coastal infrastructure — consequences that are especially acute across the climate-sensitive tropics of West Africa. abstract: Using observational and reanalysis data sets, we diagnose summer surface warming trends over Northern Hemisphere mid‐ to high‐latitude land, focusing on hotspots over Eastern Europe–Western Asia, Mongolia–Northern China, and Western North America. abstract: Precise age scales are essential for reconstructing past climate variability at high temporal resolution. abstract: Tropical cyclone (TC) remnants can cause extreme rainfall in coastal cities; however, modulation of these extreme events by urbanization is not well understood. abstract: Wind-power cannibalization, the decline in market value as wind penetration increases, is typically assessed using national averages that can mask important regional differences. abstract: Soil and water bioengineering (SWBE) offers a nature-based approach to slope stabilisation by integrating structural elements with live vegetation.
