abstract: The 2022 South Asian heatwave was among the most extreme events recorded in the past half-century, with temperature anomalies exceeding 6°C in several regions. abstract: Along-strike upper plate heterogeneity is widely observed at subduction margins, but its direct influence on slab geometry and interseismic deformation remains debated. abstract: The pattern of sea surface temperature (SST) warming in the tropics modulates global climate variability. In reanalysis, this transition manifests as a shift in the zonal momentum balance from frictional control to meridional-advection control as the cross-equatorial flow intensifies, once the local Rossby number rises toward unity and the absolute vorticity vanishes. title: An idealised model for the spatial structure of the eddy-driven Ferrel cell in mid-latitudes
abstract: The dynamics of the mid-latitude jet stream and the associated Ferrel cell are fundamentally governed by the life cycle of synoptic-scale baroclinic waves. While numerical simulations and reanalysis have long highlighted the role of turbulent eddy fluxes in regulating the zonal-mean flow, a closed analytical theory that captures the interplay between eddy parameterisation, diabatic forcing, and the resulting circulation remains a challenge. title: Sparse sensor placement for reducing forecast errors in ensemble Kalman filtering
abstract: Designing efficient observation networks for reducing forecast errors is a fundamental challenge in numerical weather prediction. Data‐driven sparse sensor placement (SSP), which selects observation locations based on optimal experimental design, has recently been proposed. However, it targets analysis error reduction and has not been explored for reducing forecast errors. In this study, we develop new SSP methods for reducing forecast errors in the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) by using a tangent linear model approximated by an ensemble forecast. title: Strategic Optimization of Well Types for Co-Production of Gas Hydrates and Shallow Gas Reservoirs
abstract: In recent years, the co-production of natural gas hydrate and shallow gas has been regarded as a promising technical solution to tackle the aforementioned challenges; however, the influence of well-type adaptability of single-wellbore in co-production has been insufficiently studied, hindering the optimization of co-production schemes. In this paper, typical symbiotic reservoirs containing natural gas hydrate and shallow gas in the Qiongdongnan Basin in the South China Sea were selected as research targets. title: Assessing the contribution of extratropical cyclones to river floods that caused property damage in Quebec, Canada
abstract: In the past few decades, the province of Quebec in eastern Canada has experienced widespread and costly flood events, yet the contribution of extratropical cyclones to these floods remains unquantified. This paper presents a methodology for analysing the contribution of extratropical cyclones (ETCs) to 498 fluvial floods that occurred in watersheds in southern Quebec, Canada, between 1991 and 2020, and highlights key characteristics shared by the 200 flood ETCs (storms that contributed to flooding) identified in the study. title: Impacts of Climate Variability on Wetland Ecosystem Provisioning Services in the Diang Sub-Division, East Region of Cameroon
abstract: Wetland provisioning services are vital for rural livelihoods in Sub-Saharan Africa, yet they face severe risks from climate variability and unsustainable resource extraction. This study evaluated the impact of climate variability on wetland provisioning services across five communities in the Diang Sub-Division, East Region of Cameroon. The study integrated 35-year meteorological reanalysis data (1990–2025) with questionnaires administered to 150 service extractors including key informant interviews, and field observations. title: Hydroclimatic Variability and Near-Surface Soil Moisture in South-South Nigeria: An ERA5-Land Assessment of Selected Years, 2000–2020
abstract: Soil moisture is an essential part of the hydrological cycle and connects the atmospheric forcing with the land-surface processes and influences the agricultural productivity, wetland functioning and environmental resilience. This study was conducted to assess the spatial and temporal trends of near surface air temperature, daily precipitation and top layer (0–7cm) volumetric soil moisture across South South Nigeria using the ERA5-Land Hourly reanalysis dataset and zonal statistics in Geographic information system (GIS) for 08 selected reference years (2000, 2003, 2006, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2017

title: Hold me back! Does vegetation density shape the particle-specific fate of microplastics in stream mesocosms?
abstract: Rivers and streams are important conduits for microplastic particles from terrestrial sources to marine environments. Submerged macrophytes are expected to influence microplastic short-term retention by altering local hydrodynamics and trapping microplastics. However, their impact in longitudinal transport processes remains unclear. title: Enhanced influence of the North Pacific Meridional Mode on the western North Pacific tropical cyclones in a warming climate
abstract: Western North Pacific (WNP) tropical cyclone (TC) activity is strongly modulated by the North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM), yet how this influence responds to global warming remains unclear. Using observations and high-resolution atmosphere-only simulations that reproduce the observed NPMM-related environmental and TC responses, we investigate how warming alters the NPMM influence on TC genesis and tracks and the underlying physical mechanisms. abstract: Heterogeneity in the occurrence, amount and distribution of precipitation in mountainous areas is relevant for water resources and stresses the need for high-altitude observations and high-resolution modeling over complex terrain. This work focuses on the analysis of precipitation in the Sierra de Guadarrama, a mountain range at the center of the Iberian Plateau that provides water resources for several million citizens living within it and in nearby cities, mostly Madrid. title: Modelling annual wave-induced loss for floating photovoltaics under realistic weather conditions
abstract: The installed capacity of floating photovoltaics (FPV) is growing, and deployment at more exposed locations, such as larger lakes and nearshore or offshore environments, is increasingly being considered. For FPV systems, the presence of waves will lead to movement of the PV panels, which in turn leads to variations in the incident irradiance. These irradiance variations, both in the average system irradiance and within a string of panels, cause a power loss referred to as wave-induced loss (WIL). title: Lithospheric‐Scale Martian Tectonic Deformation: Defining the Strength Profile Through Parameter Testing
abstract: We incorporate recent data constraints from the 2018 InSight mission into two rheology yielding mechanisms to calculate the plastic (brittle) and viscous (ductile) yield stresses for 30 potential lithospheric scenarios of the Martian lithosphere. Through these calculations, we produce estimates for the depth of the transition from brittle to ductile deformation for each scenario. title: The boundary of nighttime ozone chemical equilibrium as an indicator of local chemistry disturbances in the polar mesopause region
abstract: The nighttime ozone chemical equilibrium (NOCE) is a key assumption widely employed in various applications within the mesopause region, such as retrieving difficult-to-measure characteristics from observational data. Previously, the NOCE boundary criterion was used to analyze its long-term evolution based on SABER/TIMED data, primarily at low and mid-latitudes. This study extends this focus to polar latitudes. title: Spatiotemporal variability of extreme precipitation in Ecuador (1991-2020): wavelet coherence and non-parametric trend analysis by homogeneous zones
abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon exerts a strong influence on precipitation variability in Ecuador, although its spatial impacts at the scale of homogeneous micro-basins and extreme events require more detailed analysis. This study assesses the relationship between ENSO and precipitation across 22 homogeneous zones of Ecuador for the 1991–2020 period. title: Can IO Endorsements Influence Public Attitudes on Issues with Direct Personal Consequences? Evidence from the IAEA’s Safety Verification of Japan’s Treated Water Release
abstract: International organizations (IOs) are often expected to shape public attitudes by providing credible policy information. Yet existing research focuses largely on foreign and security policy, leaving unclear whether IO endorsements influence attitudes on issues with direct personal consequences. This study addresses this question by examining the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) safety verification of Japan’s 2023 treated water discharge—an issue that affects people’s health and food consumption decisions yet requires specialized knowledge to evaluate. abstract: The MAESTRO airborne field campaign took place between 10 August and 10 September 2024 over the North Atlantic tropical ocean near the Cabo Verde Islands. Its goal was to investigate the processes that control the mesoscale organization of clouds with a payload of probes and sensors, as well as vertically and horizontally-pointing radars and lidars. title: Predicting fault development in extensional systems using energy optimization: Implications for graben formation, synthetic vs. antithetic faulting, fault spacing, and the low angle normal fault paradox
abstract: Grabens and arrays of sub-parallel synthetic normal faults are typical geologic structures that develop in extensional systems. However, there is a limited mechanical understanding of the conditions that favor the development of grabens or synthetic arrays of normal faults. In this study, we use energy optimization to predict the vergence, dip, position and spacing of layer-spanning normal faults within an extending layer in numerical models. title: Three roles of evacuation simulation in life-safety-oriented flood disaster management
abstract: Evacuation simulation links physical hazard analysis with human response by assessing whether populations exposed to coastal and riverine flood hazards can reach safety within the available time. However, because evacuation is a collective process emerging from individual decisions made during infrequent and rapidly evolving events, behavioral realism, validation, and transferability remain challenging. title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
abstract: Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. title: Improved Simulation and Projection of Northern Hemisphere Bomb Cyclones in a High‐Resolution Coupled Climate Model
abstract: Bomb cyclones (BCs) are rapidly intensifying extratropical cyclones (ETCs) that pose wintertime hazards. Current low‐resolution climate models underestimate their frequency by ∼30%, causing substantial uncertainties in future projections. Using the high‐resolution Community Earth System Model (HR‐CESM), with 0.25° atmospheric and 0.1° eddy‐permitting ocean resolution, we show that the bias is largely reduced with improved representation of wind structure, upward motion and precipitation. title: Impact of teleconnection patterns on the thermal growing season in Central and Northern Europe
abstract: This study aimed to assess spatiotemporal changes in the thermal growing season (TGS) and its correlation with teleconnection patterns in Central and Northern Europe from 1950 to 2022. title: Shifting Thermal Growing Seasons and Their Relationships with Tree-Ring Chronologies in the Yenice Stream Watershed, Karabük, Türkiye
abstract: Climate change has substantially altered the thermal growing season, with important implications for terrestrial ecosystems, agriculture, and forestry. This study investigated the temporal dynamics of the start of the growing season (SOS), end of the growing season (EOS), and growing season length (GSL) in the climatically sensitive Yenice Stream Watershed, Türkiye, during 1950–2025 and examined their relationships with standardized conifer tree-ring chronologies. title: Dispersion Modeling of the 2021 Eruptive Plumes at Mt. Etna by Coupling WRF‐Chem Model With Ground‐Based and Satellite Remote Sensing Observations
abstract: From 20 December 2020 to 22 February 2022, 66 paroxysmal events occurred at Mt. Etna volcano. Among these, the paroxysms of 4 and 12 March 2021 were investigated by coupling a plume dispersion modeling approach with ground‐based flux measurements and satellite observations. Both paroxysms generated ash‐ and ‐rich plumes reaching heights of ∼11.8 and ∼10.8 km above sea level, respectively. title: Rapid one-pot microwave assisted sample pretreatment and Py-GC–MS for high-throughput quantification of microplastics and phthalate plasticizers in seafood
abstract: Microplastic pollution has emerged as a global environmental threat, as microplastics persist in ecosystems and act as sources and carriers of additives, persistent organic pollutants, and degradation products. Analytical pyrolysis-based methods enable robust mass-based quantification of polymers and associated compounds, but their application often requires labor-intensive pretreatments, especially when analyzing complex biological matrices rich in proteins and lipids. title: Anthropogenic warming intensified the July 2023 North China extreme rainfall event: Roles of moisture transport and convective organization
abstract: In late July 2023, North China experienced a devastating extreme precipitation event, resulting in severe flooding and massive economic losses. While extreme circulation patterns, abundant moisture transport, and local topography have been identified as the key drivers, the specific role of anthropogenic warming remains elusive. abstract: Salt marshes dynamically adapt to a range of environmental boundary conditions and their long-term resilience depends on feedbacks between vegetation, sediment, and hydrodynamics. The vegetation of the pioneer zone, a transitional area located between the tidal flats to the vegetated salt marshes, contains very few species. title: Cross-Stream Thermocapillary Migration of a Droplet in a Confined Oscillatory Flow
abstract: The study of cross-stream migration of droplets in a confined oscillatory flow turns out to be of significant importance in various physiological systems. Although significant exploration has been done on the thermocapillary migration of droplets in a pressure-driven flow, a linear superposition of time-dependent flow oscillations would not be suitable to address the nonlinearity due to channel confinement and interfacial deformation. The present study numerically investigates the role of an externally imposed temperature gradient on the manipulation of droplets suspended in such a flow field.

title: What Controls the Seasonality of Poleward Energy Transport by Intense Extratropical Cyclones?
abstract: Intense extratropical cyclones shape midlatitude weather extremes, but their role in the seasonal cycle of poleward energy transport remains poorly constrained. Here we develop a localized, Lagrangian‐mean moist static energy (MSE) framework that combines objective feature tracking with the Eulerian‐mean MSE budget. title: Experimental and numerical analysis of damage, stability, and seepage in underground anti-scour walls
abstract: To investigate the damage evolution and seepage control performance of underground anti-scour walls under complex hydraulic environments, concrete damage tests were conducted to elucidate the damage deterioration process. Subsequently, a numerical model of the anti-scour wall construction was established to analyze its structural stability and anti-seepage effectiveness under varying degrees of concrete damage and different water levels. title: Contrasting dynamical and thermodynamical pathways shaped the 2024 North-Central Indian heatwave
abstract: An unprecedented heatwave affected North-Central India (NCI) during the 2024 pre-monsoon season, with two connected episodes, against the backdrop of the warmest year on record and Pacific sea-surface temperature conditions favorable for extreme heat. This superposition makes it difficult to determine whether the event was driven by natural climate variability or background influence of global warming. abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric generation coupled systems show promising application potential in seawater desalination and energy harvesting. However, a portion of the heat generated by photothermal conversion is used for interfacial evaporation, while the remaining heat continuously dissipates to the thermoelectric generator (TEG) module and the surrounding environment. title: Performance Investigation of a Solar-Driven Air Gap Membrane Distillation System Coupled with PEM Electrolysis for Sustainable Water and Hydrogen Production
abstract: Freshwater scarcity and the rising demand for clean energy standout as two ofthe most pressing global challenges, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. To tackle these interconnected issues, this study explores an innovative approach utilizing a solar-powered Air Gap Membrane Distillation (AGMD) system integrated with a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolyzer.This hybrid system is designed for the simultaneousproduction of freshwater and green hydrogen. abstract: The partition of lee-wave energy sinks in bottom-intensified flows between dissipation and reabsorption is explored over parameter spaces of lee-wave generation frequency, model viscosity, and topographic Froude number. In addition to reabsorption into the sheared mean flow and explicit dissipation by model viscosity, indirect dissipation due to a nonlinear cascade via parametric subharmonic instability (PSI) is identified as a significant but previously overlooked sink that enhances the role of lee waves in dissipating the balanced circulation. title: Two distinct modes of North American spring temperature evolution shaped by tropical SST regimes and midlatitude circulation
abstract: Abnormal temperature fluctuations during spring can substantially impact vegetation growth, agricultural productivity, and ecosystem stability. However, the physical processes underlying year-to-year variations in the evolution of North American spring temperature anomalies remain poorly understood. Here, we apply Season-reliant Empirical Orthogonal Function (S-EOF) analysis to identify the leading modes of spring temperature evolution over North America. title: Reassessing Ozone Formation: How Photochemical VOC Loss Unmasks Biases in Radical Pathway Diagnosis
abstract: Photochemical loss of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by OH radicals during transport significantly influences their observed concentrations at receptor site. title: Injection strategy optimization for engineered water enhanced oil recovery in carbonate reservoirs
abstract: Carbonate reservoirs commonly exhibit limited oil recovery because of strong heterogeneity, complex pore structures, and unfavorable wettability. This study presents an integrated experimental-numerical framework for evaluating engineered-water flooding and optimizing injection strategies in the heterogeneous WQ1-57 carbonate reservoir. abstract: Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extreme precipitation events, categorizing areas into four risk levels: from no risk to high risk. title: Numerical investigation of heat transfer enhancement and frictional characteristics of rib roughened channels
abstract: One of the primary cooling technologies used for turbine blades is through utilizing structures inside the channel like ribs and fins employed for roughening of the channel. These features erected upstream in the flow channel can help in achieving heat transfer augmentation in the internal cooling process. The present work has been aimed at numerically assessing the effect of ribs on the heat transfer and frictional characteristics of the flow in the channel. title: The last builders of megaliths in the South of the Iberian peninsula? The Bronze Age necropolis of Trafalgar (Barbate, Cádiz, Spain)
abstract: The archaeological excavations undertaken at the Trafalgar tombolo during 2021-2022 led to the identification of a Bronze Age megalithic necropolis. This paper presents an interdisciplinary study, considering chronological, structural, bioarchaeological, and archaeometrical evidence of two megalithic tombs. title: Urban Fog Prediction Based on Aerosol Microphysics and Visibility Parameterization in a High‐Resolution Model
abstract: Accurate prediction of winter fog over Delhi remains challenging because operational numerical models inadequately represent aerosol–fog interactions. To address this, a modified Thompson–Eidhammer (TE) aerosol‐aware microphysics scheme, coupled with a diagnostic visibility parameterization accounting for extinction by hydrometeors, aerosols, and gases, was implemented within the Weather Research and Forecasting model. abstract: To investigate local erosion in split-frame aqueducts under sediment-laden flow, a three-dimensional water–sediment two-phase numerical model was developed using the RNG k–ε turbulence model, the Discrete Phase Model (DPM), and the Neilson–Gilchrist erosion model. abstract: The influence of initial injection velocity on turbulent spray combustion of n-dodecane (C₁₂H₂₆) and n-octane (C₈H₁₈) in a model cylindrical chamber was investigated numerically. abstract: A data set that incorporates native‐footprint observations from the Global Precipitation Measurement Core platform, CloudSat, Atmospheric Infrared Sounder, and Cross‐track Infrared Sounder is constructed which utilizes the similarities and differences between observational capabilities of these platforms. title: Historical population exposure to temperature extremes in Peru: evidence for health adaptation in a changing climate
abstract: Temperature extremes are becoming more common and pose growing risks to population health. However, spatially resolved, population-weighted evaluations are scarce for Latin American countries. We sought to estimate population-weighted exposures across the geographically diverse regions of Peru. Eight health-relevant temperature extreme indices were computed at 0.1° × 0.1° resolution from daily ERA5-Land data for 2000-2025, using the 1961-1990 baseline for percentile thresholds. abstract: Hourly wind series combine diurnal periodicity, synoptic variability, and ocean-atmosphere variability, complicating the interpretation of finite-scale multifractal estimates. We analyze twelve automatic stations in Pernambuco, Northeast Brazil, with a regular hourly calendar, non-overlapping monthly sequences, multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA), and circulation diagnostics. title: Grouting Reinforcement for Thaw Settlement of In‐Service Roads in Permafrost Regions: Adaptability and Key Scientific Issues
abstract: Thaw settlement of in‐service roads in permafrost regions is worsening. It has become a key constraint on the safe and stable operation of cold‐region roads. abstract: Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. abstract: The appropriateness of sandwich composite panels reinforced with glass fibre facesheets and hollow glass microsphere (HGM) foam cores for lightweight structural applications was assessed by experimentally and numerically examining their mechanical and thermal characteristics. abstract: The Trans-Himalaya, located between the Great Himalaya and the Tibetan Plateau, is ecologically fragile and one of the most climate-sensitive regions. title: Annual Atmospheric Δ 14 C Variations in the Subtropics During 1850–1933 CE Linked to ENSO
abstract: The 14 C content of tree‐rings serves as a valuable proxy for inferring past solar activity and environment change. Here we present an annually resolved tree‐ring Δ 14 C record (1850–1933 CE) from eastern China, where Δ 14 C data are rare. The weighted mean deviation between our record and IntCal20 calibration curve is −0.40 ± 0.26‰, revealing no significant regional offset. title: Stable Isotope Insights Into the Trophic Role of the Invasive Atherina boyeri (Atherinidae) in Central Anatolia, Türkiye
abstract: This study aimed to determine the trophic role of the big‐scale sand smelt (BSSS) ( Atherina boyeri ) in Lake Eğirdir, a large freshwater lake in Central Anatolia, Türkiye, using carbon (δ 13 C) and nitrogen (δ 15 N) stable isotope analyses. Although this euryhaline species rarely occurs in freshwater habitats, it has recently expanded into many freshwater systems worldwide, including Türkiye. The species was introduced into Lake Eğirdir approximately 18 years ago and has been associated with the decline of several native fish stocks, primarily due to predation on fish eggs. title: From Watershed Ambitions to Parcel-Scale Retrofits: Rethinking Rain-Gardens in Climate Resilience Planning
abstract: Rain-gardens are widely promoted as nature-based solutions (NbSs) within blue-green infrastructure (BGI), yet their contribution to broader resilience objectives raises questions about how localized projects are governed, maintained, and connected to watershed planning. title: Reduced-order aerodynamic modelling of a lift-plus-cruise VTOL UAV: flight-envelope assessment and load-conserving reconstruction
abstract: A traceable reduced-order design workflow is developed for a 13.85 kg lift-plus-cruise vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The novelty is a verification architecture – not a new lifting-line relation – that couples archived-data reconciliation, flight-envelope falsification, bounded uncertainty and exact load closure in one reduced-order chain. title: Dynamic downscaling vs global forecasts: Impact of meteorological drivers for air quality modelling in complex terrain
abstract: Accurate air quality modelling is crucial for assessing public health risks, particularly in regions with complex terrain. This study investigates the influence of meteorological drivers on the performance of the LOTOS-EUROS chemical transport model by comparing two setups: the standard configuration using operational data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), and a dynamically downscaled setup using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. title: Consistency and boundary sensitivity of size-selectivity estimates for small yellow croaker gillnets: A comparison of SELECT and generalized additive models
abstract: This study evaluated the consistency and boundary sensitivity of size-selectivity estimates for small yellow croaker ( Larimichthys polyactis ) drift gillnets by comparing the parametric Share Each Length's Catch Total (SELECT) framework with a semiparametric generalized additive model (GAM). Catch data from 6,310 fish collected using six mesh sizes (40–65 mm) were analyzed. title: Lake Ice Thickness retrieval using TanDEM-X immediate interferometry
abstract: Knowledge of Lake Ice Thickness (LIT) is essential for understanding the cryosphere and monitoring current climate change impacts. However, accurately retrieving LIT at the desired spatial-temporal scale remains a challenge, as many lakes are in remote regions and LIT is a logistically expensive parameter to measure. Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) provides a novel approach to estimating ice thickness by measuring surface deformations at high resolution. This study used TanDEM-X pursuit mode that offers minimal temporal decorrelation to maintain high coherence for accurate LIT

title: Strong winds in Poland in the 17th century and their consequences, in light of documentary evidence
abstract: The paper presents a detailed analysis of strong winds in Poland in the 17th century, including their frequency, intensity, and impacts on the natural environment, society and economy. The analysis is solely based on available documentary evidence. Preliminary archival research allowed the construction of a comprehensive database of strong winds for Poland for the study period. The 542 weather notes were used to obtain the following information about strong winds: time, location/region, duration, and indexations of intensity, extent, and damage character. title: Equivalent reconstruction and nonlinear contact mechanics of particle-adhered rough sealing interfaces
abstract: Solid-particle adhesion is an important factor contributing to the degradation of sealing interfaces, particularly in particle-laden operating environments such as subsea pressure-retaining coring, offshore oil and gas drilling and production, and pipeline transportation. In this study, an equivalent rough-surface reconstruction model incorporating particle adhesion and a three-dimensional finite-element method (FEM) contact model between the seal ring and the reconstructed particle-adhered surface are established. title: Development of a national-scale rip current forecast for Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Rip currents are dangerous flows in the surfzone of wave-exposed beaches and can take bathers from the shallows into deeper water. They cause hundreds of drownings globally each year and are the leading cause of all beach lifeguard rescues. In New Zealand, with a population of approx. 5 million people, rip currents typically cause 500–1000 lifeguard rescues each year and are attributed to 53 % of all Surf Life Saving New Zealand rescues. journal: Natural hazards and earth system sciences

title: Sistemas Autônomos Submersíveis e a Nova Arquitetura Digital de Defesa Marítima no Século 21
abstract: A robótica subaquática constitui um dos campos de maior relevância da engenharia contemporânea, especialmente diante da crescente necessidade de exploração, monitoramento e utilização estratégica dos ambientes marinhos.

title: Numerical analysis of dynamics between debris flows and wave propagation using multi-layer shallow water equations
abstract: Debris flows are destructive disasters that often cause casualties and property damage, particularly when occurring near residential areas. In reservoir basins, debris flows can reduce effective storage capacity by raising the dead storage level and generate waves that may induce overtopping or structural collapse. Previous numerical studies have applied three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamics or smoothed particle hydrodynamics to analyze debris flow-induced waves. title: Thermal and Phase Behavior of Chloride–Perchlorate Brines on Mars: Insights from the MgCl2–Mg(ClO4)2–H2O System
abstract: Cl-bearing brines (Cl–, ClO4–, ClO3–) are critical to the Martian water cycle because they can extend the liquid water stability under present-day conditions. Natural Martian brines are likely multicomponent mixtures, yet their low-temperature behavior remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the binary MgCl2–H2O and Mg(ClO4)2–H2O and ternary MgCl2–Mg(ClO4)2–H2O systems to constrain cryogenic phase equilibria relevant to Mars. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) experiments are used to characterize phase behavior during controlled cooling–heating cycles

title: The SOLCHECK project: An investigation into the imprints of solar variability across multiple timescales
abstract: The project Solar Contribution to Climate Change on Decadal to Centennial Timescales (SOLCHECK) investigated the influence of solar variability on the atmosphere from the pre-industrial era to the present and future. Variations in solar output ranging from weeks to millennia leave distinct imprints on the climate system. Their assessment is, however, challenging because of limited observations, incomplete representation of feedback processes in climate models, and computational constraints. title: Early assessment of cyanobacteria growth in water reservoirs from high-frequency multispectral active fluorescence
abstract: We demonstrate the use of multispectral active fluorometry for early warning of cyanobacteria growth in water reservoirs by inducing blooms in samples from two drinking water reservoirs, creating nutrient-replete growth conditions. Photosynthetic parameters derived from fluorescence light curves were recorded at high frequency, using light excitation protocols designed to favour light harvesting in cyanobacteria and algae, respectively. abstract: Background and Aims This study examined hydro-atmospheric conditions during the 2007 Attica wildfire period using complementary observations at different time scales. Methods GRACE total water storage anomalies (TWSA), GLDAS-Noah soil moisture storage anomalies (SMSA), daily GNSS-derived precipitable water vapor (PWV) from ten stations, and MODIS FIRMS active-fire data were analyzed. title: A smoothed particle hydrodynamics model for droplet heat transfer and icing on a cold wall
abstract: Heat transfer and phase change of droplets on cold surfaces are important thermophysical processes in aircraft icing and anti-icing. The interaction between a droplet and a cold wall involves coupled thermal transport, interfacial dynamics, and liquid-to-solid phase transition. In this study, a smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) model is developed to investigate heat transfer and freezing of a water droplet on a cold flat wall. title: Physical Constraints on Future Tropical Cyclone Genesis Over the Western North Pacific: A CMIP6 Multi–Model Assessment
abstract: Reliable projections of tropical cyclone genesis frequency (TCGF) under global warming remain challenging. We evaluate three genesis potential indices (χGPI, DGPI, and χMqGPI) over the western North Pacific (WNP) using 22 CMIP6 models under four SSP scenarios, supplemented by HighResMIP simulations under SSP5–8.5. title: Constraints on the lithospheric structure and rheology of northern Chile from 8-year post-seismic deformation following the M w 8.1 Iquique earthquake
abstract: Understanding and modeling the deformation following large earthquakes is essential for characterizing the rheological structure and processes that release post-seismic stress. Here, we measured postseismic deformation over an 8-year period following the 2014 M w 8.1 Iquique earthquake using Sentinel-1 InSAR and GNSS time series in northern Chile and Bolivia. title: Sistema osservativo per le lagune dell'Alto Adriatico
abstract: The lagoons of the Northern Adriatic are highly productive transitional ecosystems, sensitive to climate change and human pressures. Within the PNRR MER project, ISPRA upgraded the observing system: the historical Venice lagoon tide-gauge network was expanded with new stations and inlagoon wave sensors. title: The World's Longest Lake Ice Break‐Up Chronology: Capturing Precise Late‐Winter and Spring Temperatures in Central Scandinavia Since 1693
abstract: Using an assembly of historical documentary sources, from the areas surrounding the lake Storsjön, central Scandinavia, this study establishes the world's longest lake ice break‐up chronology, spanning 1693–2025. The study finds a strong late‐winter and spring temperature signal in ice break‐up dates. The correlation between the ice break‐up chronology and cumulative degree days above 0°C from 1 January–16 May reaches r = −0.88 (1860–1980) and the correlation with mean March–May temperatures is r = −0.82 (1860–2021). title: Environmental Influences on the Distribution of Intense Lightning in Tropical Cyclones During Landfall in China
abstract: Based on lightning data from 84 tropical cyclones (TCs) that made landfall in China from 2010 to 2022, this study investigates the spatial patterns of intense lightning in TCs and their associations with large‐scale environmental conditions. Individual time periods ranking in the top 10% of hourly lightning frequency within 0–100 km and 200–500 km radii from TC center were defined as intense inner‐core (IIC) and intense outer‐rainbands (IOR) samples, respectively. title: Absorbing Aerosols Amplify Vertical Heterogeneity in Cold‐Topped Precipitation
abstract: The vertical structure of precipitation (VSP) links cloud processes to surface rainfall, yet aerosol effects on VSP remain poorly constrained. Combining high‐resolution observations and idealized simulations (May–September, 2015–2023) over eastern China, we show that aerosols reshape precipitation profiles in cold‐topped clouds with storm‐tops above the freezing level (FL). title: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
abstract: Internal climate variability (ICV) represents the intrinsic fluctuations within the climate system. Understanding how ICV varies across regions, seasons, and climatic conditions is crucial for detecting externally forced climate change and assessing future climate risks. It can also provide a useful benchmark for assessing climate model performance and the emergence of anthropogenically forced climate change. title: Warming Trends on the Hurd Peninsula of Livingston Island, Antarctica, Between 2000 and 2024, and Improvements in the Estimation of Air Temperature Using C6.1 MODIS LST Data
abstract: Analysing the spatial and temporal variability of near-surface air temperature (Ta) is essential for assessing climate change, particularly in polar regions such as the maritime Antarctic, where observational studies remain comparatively scarce. In areas with sparse meteorological networks, satellite observations provide a valuable means of extending station-based analyses and generating spatially distributed Ta maps. title: Revisiting the Signal‐to‐Noise Paradox in Climate Predictions: An Extended Mathematical Framework
abstract: The signal‐to‐noise paradox—where climate model predictions correlate more highly with observations than with their own ensemble members—remains a challenge for interpreting predictability. We present an extended theoretical framework explaining the role of different types of model errors in the paradox. Analytical results show, despite the non‐identifiability of the latent parameters, that the paradox arises only when the shared signal is underestimated relative to observations and this underestimation is sufficiently large, rather than from differences in signal‐to‐noise ratios. title: Saharan dust transport and boundary layer entrainment over western Europe: multi-instrument observations and convection-permitting model evaluation
abstract: Long-range Saharan dust transport affects radiation, clouds, and air quality, yet its vertical structure and entrainment into the boundary layer remain challenging to simulate. We investigate four contrasting dust events over southwestern Germany using ground-based lidar, sun-photometer and in situ aerosol measurements, satellite observations, backward trajectories, and ICON-ART simulations. title: A potential emergent constraint on cloud liquid water path adjustments to aerosol–cloud interactions
abstract: Emergent constraints are relationships between an observable in the present-day climate (such as cloud state variables) and an unobservable response (such as adjustments to radiative forcing) of the climate system to a perturbation. Here we present a candidate emergent constraint arising from the relationship across members of a perturbed parameter ensemble (PPE) between the observable present-day cloud droplet number–liquid water path ( N d –ℒ) correlation and the unobservable liquid water path adjustment to anthropogenic aerosol–cloud forcing (RA ℒ ). title: Constraining the hydrogen soil sink and photochemical source: insights from atmospheric H 2 inversions (2003–2023)
abstract: Hydrogen (H 2 ) is expected to become an increasingly important energy carrier during the energy transition, likely leading to higher atmospheric H 2 levels due to losses during production, transport, storage and usage of hydrogen. Multiple studies have shown this could impact atmospheric composition through interactions with the hydroxyl radical. However, the magnitude of this impact remains uncertain due to large uncertainties in the global H 2 budget, particularly in the soil sink and photochemical source. title: A high-speed bionic robot actuated by flow-induced flutter of a folded gradient soft pipe
abstract: This paper proposes a novel actuation mechanism based on high-frequency flow-induced flutter in a gradient-discontinuous soft pipe. The actuator of the bionic fish is inspired by the tentacles of pipe anemones. The actuator consists of a gradient-discontinuous soft pipe with a thin membrane attached to its outer surface. abstract: Atmospheric stability is a major factor in wind turbine response analysis, as it affects the mean wind profile, turbulence characteristics, and wake behaviour. Wind turbine design standards support the use of surface-layer wind profile formulations, such as Monin–Obukhov similarity theory or empirically fitted power laws. abstract: The stability and motion characteristics of air-supported floaters deviate from conventional displacement-type floaters due to the influence of the entrapped air. In particular, air compressibility induces a scale effect that reduces the restoring force below the value predicted by the Froude similarity law in small-scale model tests. title: Global warming extends boreal fire seasons into uncharted territory
abstract: Recent wildfire disasters in communities such as Fort McMurray and Jasper in Canada, and across Siberia, highlight the growing vulnerability of boreal regions to prolonged fire-conducive conditions under a warming climate. Here, we use 5000-year Earth system model simulations to quantify how quasi steady-state global warming alters the boreal fire-season length across North America and Eurasia. title: Validation of PREFIRE mid- and far-infrared radiances during the WHAFFFERS campaign
abstract: Despite containing up to half of the Earth's thermal emission to space, the far-infrared spectral region (FIR, defined here as 100–667 cm −1 or 15–100 µm) has seldom been observed from satellites. This has contributed to substantial uncertainties in the spectroscopy of water vapour, radiative properties of clouds, and surface spectral emissivity; these in turn limit confidence in modelled FIR energy flows. title: Environmental drivers of deforming bedrock landslides in southern Alaska
abstract: Large moving bedrock subaerial landslides pose considerable hazards to people, infrastructure, and environments if they fail rapidly and run out over land or into water bodies and produce damaging waves. Identification of these features across the landscape can determine physiographic and environmental factors that influence landslide occurrence, aiding landslide hazard and risk assessments. Quantifying Thermal Inertia Effect of Permafrost in the Community Earth System Model Version 1.2
abstract: Permafrost's thermal inertia causes permafrost thaw to lag behind climate warming. This is critical for understanding climate sensitivity of permafrost, but has not been well quantified. Using differences between stabilized and transient experiments from the CESM1.2, we quantified thermal inertia effect of permafrost in the Northern Hemisphere. The results show that thermal inertia's effect on ground temperature is not apparent in the shallow layers, but enhances with depth. title: Green infrastructure for urban heat risk reduction: case Saudi Arabia
abstract: Rapid urbanisation in arid megacities produces severe urban heat islands (UHI) that increase building energy demand, degrade outdoor thermal comfort, and amplify carbon dioxide emissions. Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, three of the largest cities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, house a combined population exceeding 12 million inhabitants in climates characterised by extreme summer temperatures that routinely surpass 45 °C. abstract: Sub-annual glacier surface velocity time series are receiving increasing attention as they provide critical information on subglacial hydrology, glacier and ice-sheet instabilities, and responses to external forcing. Regional-to-global scale datasets of glacier surface velocities are based on optical and/or SAR remote sensing images. They are now available worldwide in open access or on demand. title: Climate risk assessment in tropical wetlands through integrated hydroclimatic, land cover, and community knowledge
abstract: Climate-risk assessments in tropical wetlands increasingly combine hydroclimatic and land-cover data, but rarely integrate them with structured community evidence on experienced impacts and adaptation priorities. We address this gap in six communities around the Complejo Cenagoso de Zapatosa, a Ramsar site, and the Morales wetland in the Colombian Caribbean. title: Firm versus flexible green hydrogen supply from an islanded solar–wind–PEM plant in Kuwait
abstract: Existing assessments of green hydrogen in Kuwait report production costs for flexible offtake; however, many industrial consumers require continuous supply, and the incremental cost of providing firm supply has not been quantified for Kuwait. This study determines the optimal configuration of an islanded solar photovoltaic (PV)–onshore wind–proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis plant with compressed-hydrogen storage on Failaka Island, Kuwait. title: Boltysh impact crater, Ukraine: Impact deposits and hydrothermal system
abstract: The 24 km diameter Boltysh impact crater, Ukraine, is a uniquely well‐preserved complex structure that formed soon after the Cretaceous–Paleogene (K‐Pg) boundary. Core 42/11 drilled in 2008 offers insights into the late‐stage processes of crater excavation, modification, and postimpact hydrothermal alteration. The sequence of impactites reflects the original layering of the target; the upper 5 m contains carbonate melts and clasts from the thin Cretaceous cover, whereas deeper impactite layers contain only Proterozoic gneiss and granite clasts. abstract: Offshore pontoon structures and rotating-frame launching systems are subjected to complex loading conditions, necessitating accurate assessment of their nonlinear structural behavior and the load-carrying capacity of critical components to ensure safe and reliable operations. This study presents a nonlinear computational framework for analyzing the stress–strain behavior of offshore pontoon structures subjected to combined internal and external loading conditions. title: Hazard hexagons: the influence of anthropogenic climate change on extremes in regions globally
abstract: The sixth assessment report (AR6) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change presented regional summaries of the scientific knowledge of changing weather extremes and the human influence upon this. The hexagon figures, found in the summary for policymakers, were a key part of this presentation. title: A climatological description of atmospheric CO 2 concentrations
abstract: At regional scales, atmospheric CO 2 concentrations show (i) a global trend, (ii) a seasonal cycle that varies with location and altitude and (iii) inter-annual and synoptic variability. title: Methane in the Asian Monsoon anticyclone and global UTLS behavior observed in ACE-FTS satellite data
abstract: Methane in the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere (UTLS) plays a critical role in atmospheric composition and radiative forcing, yet the processes governing its vertical structure and variability remain poorly understood. Here, we use high-quality satellite observations from the Atmospheric Chemistry Experiment Fourier Transform Spectrometer (ACE-FTS) to characterize the vertical structure and global seasonal behavior of methane in the UTLS, with emphasis on the role of Asian Summer Monsoon (ASM). title: The Heterodyne Wind Lidar Gadget HEDWIG for the German research aircraft HALO: instrument design, wind retrieval and first airborne observations
abstract: The HEterodyne Detection Wind lIdar Gadget (HEDWIG) is a new airborne Doppler wind lidar developed at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) for high-resolution observations of atmospheric wind profiles. The instrument operates at an eye-safe wavelength of 1617 nm. title: Approximate analytical solution for steady seepage and hydraulic gradient containment safety criterion of an underground water-sealed oil storage cavern
abstract: Seepage analysis of the surrounding rock masses is crucial for evaluating the containment property of underground water-sealed oil storage caverns (UWOSCs). abstract: Accurate simulation of extreme rainfall, particularly its intensity and spatial variability, remains a significant challenge for numerical weather prediction. In this study, two numerical approaches: the conventional Fixed‐Time‐step (FT) and the Adaptive‐Time‐step (AT) methods are evaluated to simulate the December 2015 Chennai (India) extreme rainfall event. title: Aspectos físico-químicos da Bacia do Rio Doce: antes e após o rompimento da Barragem de Fundão
abstract: O rompimento da Barragem de Fundão, ocorrido em 2015 no município de Mariana (MG), provocou impactos ambientais significativos na Bacia do Rio Doce, comprometendo a qualidade da água, dos sedimentos e dos ecossistemas aquáticos ao longo da região atingida. abstract: Bioinspired porous concrete with a superhydrophobic surface offers multifunctionality for anti‐icing, anti‐corrosion, and thermal insulation, meeting the adaptable demands of modern infrastructure. However, scalable fabrication of robust hydrophobic microstructures in porous cementitious materials remains challenging. Herein, inspired by the low‐pinning dynamic anti‐wetting of Nepenthes interfaces, an in situ carbonation strategy using CO 2 is developed to construct porous concretes with a dual‐level superhydrophobic energy barrier. Intrinsic rough pores trap air to reduce solid–liquid contact

title: Application of Mobile-DOAS observations for analyzing sub-pixel variability and comparing TROPOMI-derived NO x emissions over the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex
abstract: This study investigates sub-pixel spatial variability in TROPOMI NO2 observations and its impact on the consistency between TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations for the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex in South Korea. Furthermore, NOx emissions are estimated using both datasets and compared with a bottom-up emission inventory. The comparison of co-located TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations shows good correlation (r = 0.86), with TROPOMI data exhibiting a slight underestimation relative to the Mobile-DOAS observations (-8.5%). title: Digital interaction design promotes cultural identification and heritage-related participation intention: Evidence from the Wangchuan ceremony
abstract: The sustainable protection of intangible cultural heritage faces unprecedented challenges due to the process of urbanization and the decline in the participation of the younger generation. Digital reconstruction offers a transformative way for heritage transmission, but its long-term contribution to cultural sustainability remains under-explored. This study examines the relationships among users' perceptions of digital heritage experiences, cultural identification, and heritage-related behavioural intention. On the basis of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the study introduces emotional

title: Seafood Processing By‐Products as Sources of Bioactive Compounds for Nutricosmetic Applications
abstract: Seafood waste is a valuable source of bioactive compounds, which are promising components for next‐generation nutricosmetic products that aim to improve beauty through their antimicrobial, moisturizing, anti‐inflammatory, and antioxidant properties. However, translating these resources into effective nutricosmetic products requires integrating the entire value chain. This review evaluates major seafood‐derived bioactives, with particular attention to their bioavailability, absorption, gastrointestinal stability, systemic delivery, and formulation strategies. title: A study on aircushion-type platform behavior in regular waves in relation with inner free-surface profiles
abstract: This paper presents an experimental and numerical study of simplified aircushion-type platform models, mainly focusing on the internal free surface created by the entrapped air in the chamber. Since the elevation of this free surface significantly affects the motion of the floating platform, investigating its characteristics is of great importance. In this study, to measure and analyze the inner free-surface elevation, both mono- and partitioned-aircushion-type models were tested in regular waves. title: A tale of two European summers: the exceptional north–south divide of 2026
abstract: In the early summer from May to July 2026, there was an exceptionally persistent north–south split between wet, cool conditions in northern Europe and hot, dry weather in Britain and western continental Europe. We associate this with a recurring atmospheric circulation pattern that was at its most extreme in 2026. This pattern has shown a positive trend towards 2026‐like conditions in recent decades, which may be temporary or a manifestation of climate change. Our study provides a basis for further investigation of this important question, with implications for the future of European heatwaves

title: Parametric Gravity Wave Forcings in the Stratocumulus-Topped Boundary Layer under a Prescribed Radiative-Convective Equilibrium
abstract: This work studies the breakup propensity of the stratocumulus-topped boundary layer (STBL) interacting with gravity waves using large-eddy simulation with a uniform vertical grid of 5 m and horizontal spacing of 30 m. A radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) state is constructed to enforce stationarity in the STBL, and the gravity waves are introduced via a vertical momentum forcing mimicking a packet of waves. title: Circulação atmosférica associada aos padrões espaciais dominantes das secas meteorológicas na região Sul do Brasil
abstract: A seca é caracterizada como um período excepcional de escassez hídrica para os seres humanos e ecossistemas. No Brasil, a Região Sul é a segunda com maior ocorrência de estiagens/secas. Assim, o objetivo deste estudo é investigar quais padrões de circulação atmosférica estão associados aos eventos de seca meteorológica na Região Sul, nos meses de janeiro de 1950-2025. Para isso, utilizamos o Índice Padronizado de Precipitação-Evapotranspiração (SPEI-01; Global Drought Monitor), campos atmosféricos (ERA5/ECMWF) e o Índice de Niño Oceânico Relativo (RONI; CPC/NOAA). title: Effect of subcritical fluid shear flow on granular bed strength
abstract: Experiments have shown that subcritical fluid flows can strengthen granular beds in the flow direction, while weakening them in the opposite direction. However, the grain-scale mechanisms for this anisotropy of bed strength remain unclear. Using discrete element method simulations in two and three dimensions, we show that the stress history-dependent anisotropy of bed strength arises primarily from changes in the surface grain positions, which causes variations in the fraction of surface grains that are susceptible to becoming dislodged in different flow directions.

title: Analyses on Drought as a Climate Change Indicator in Turkey
abstract: Precipitation is one of the primary indicators of climate change and plays a critical role in environmental processes. Changes in the amount, distribution, and frequency of precipitation are directly influenced by climatic variations, while precipitation characteristics significantly affect ecosystems, water resources, and regional climate conditions. Therefore, monitoring precipitation and identifying long-term trends through statistical analyses are essential to better understand climate change and its impacts. title: Investigation on the anti-friction performance of ink sac-inspired textures under heavy-load conditions
abstract: The working surfaces of PEEK-coated sliding bearings in wind turbines are highly susceptible to severe friction and wear under specific operating conditions of low-speed and heavy-load. To improve the lubrication at the working interface, this paper proposes a novel textured structure inspired by the ink sac structure of cephalopods, adapted to the operating conditions and substrate materials of wind turbines. We apply an identical statistical pipeline to harmonised census-tract data for two structurally contrasted Spanish regions: the Canary Islands (1388 tracts; 2.10 million inhabitants; WRF 3-km dynamical downscaling) and the Madrid metropolitan area (3117 tracts; 4.29 million inhabitants; ADAPTECCA ESD-Reg

title: Trait-based risk of lost species of the Indo-Australasian Archipelago
abstract: Species for which existence has not been confirmed by photographic, acoustic, or genetic evidence in the last ten years are classified as lost. The process of loss may be analogous in some ways to extinction but is confounded by imperfect detection driven by heterogeneous survey effort. Here, we compile the most complete dataset of lost species of any region globally, for the Indo-Australasian Archipelago, focusing on the Indonesia-Papua New Guinea region. title: Explaining Convection and Instability Scalings in Radiative‐Convective Equilibrium
abstract: In Earth's tropics, stronger radiative cooling enhances convection. Numerical experiments reveal that cloud cover increases nearly linearly with the cooling rate, while updraft velocity remains almost constant. However, atmospheric instability decreases under stronger cooling. We develop a simple two‐layer cloud model to explain how these scalings arise. The cloud cover and updraft velocity scalings follow naturally from mass continuity and an assumption for the dissipation rate. The scaling for instability requires a further closure assumption. title: Mapping heat health risk in Madhya Pradesh and Odisha using a hazard exposure and vulnerability framework
abstract: Rising temperatures and climate change have intensified heat-related health risks, particularly in developing countries like India. Understanding the spatial distribution of heat-health risk is important for planning and mitigation. This study evaluates district-level Heat Health Risk Index (HHRI) patterns across Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, India. HHRI was computed using the IPCC AR5 risk assessment framework by combining hazard, exposure, and vulnerability. title: MSDT v1.0: an open-source multi-method snow drought toolbox
abstract: Snow drought, characterized by anomalously low snow water equivalent (SWE) relative to climatological conditions, has become an increasingly important cryospheric hazard with substantial environmental and socio-economic impacts. Although numerous snow drought identification methods have been developed, existing implementations are typically fragmented into independent scripts and region-specific workflows, hindering methodological consistency, reproducibility, and systematic intercomparison. title: Predicting termite risk to North Korean wooden architectural heritage using climate data
abstract: Termite damage to wooden architectural heritage is a growing concern under climate change, yet no assessment exists for North Korea, where field survey is currently impractical. Framed within the hazard-exposure-vulnerability paradigm of heritage risk assessment, we integrated climate data, GIS-based spatial analysis, a biological model of termite-driven wood decay, and regression analysis to assess risk to 67 heritage sites. abstract: Hongshaquan low-rank coal was biodegraded by Aquamicrobium terrae ( A. terrae ). Dynamic changes of dissolved organic matter (DOM), whose presence dominates biodegradation liquid products, were monitored by a combined technique of excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy-parallel factor analysis (EEM-PARAFAC) and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS). title: Centrifuge analogue modelling of tectonic processes: A review focused on shortening-related systems
abstract: Analogue modelling is a powerful approach for investigating lithospheric deformation and large-scale geodynamic processes. Centrifuge analogue modelling, in particular, has been widely used to analyse various tectonic processes under enhanced gravity conditions. Its main advantage lies in reproducing realistic body-force-driven stress fields, enabling the use of stronger materials and improving the simulation of gravity-driven deformation and brittle-ductile interactions. title: A regional climate modeling investigation of wetland-related coupled hydrologic–atmospheric processes in central South America
abstract: This study investigates how the Pantanal, one of the world’s largest tropical floodplains, modulates local and regional climate in central South America through coupled land–atmosphere processes. Using the RegIPSL regional climate modeling framework, two simulations covering the 1998–2019 period were conducted: one including an explicit floodplain scheme and one without it. title: Social Hallmarks of Human Spaceflight
abstract: Current frameworks of space medicine treat the social environment of a crew as one hazard among five, grouped as isolation and confinement. Population health research, by contrast, has long described the social environment as a set of distinct conditions that act through separate mechanisms, and aging research has organized them as social hallmarks. In this narrative review, we transpose that approach to human spaceflight and propose eight social hallmarks arranged in two tiers. title: Orbital spectroscopy links dust source composition to atmospheric acidity and nitrate
abstract: Mineral dust affects atmospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate, yet its impacts remain uncertain because its mineral composition is poorly constrained. Here we combine NASA EMIT orbital imaging spectroscopy with a satellite-constrained global chemistry model to quantify how source-resolved calcite variability alters aerosol chemistry and optical properties. EMIT-derived calcite improves agreement with airborne observations and reveals contrasts in dust alkalinity. title: Comparison of Ascending and Descending Thermals in Cloud‐Resolving Simulations
abstract: Previous work has examined ascending thermals as building blocks for convective updrafts, but descending thermals in downdrafts remain poorly studied. This study uses a thermal‐based approach to analyze convective drafts in cloud‐resolving simulations of three severe convective storms in Australia. The aim is to characterize and compare ascending and descending thermals (up‐thermals and down‐thermals) in terms of their physical properties and driving mechanisms. title: GIS-based drought susceptibility modelling in the Ashanti Region for environmental sustainability management
abstract: Drought is a major environmental hazard affecting agricultural productivity, water availability, and ecosystem stability in many parts of Sub-Saharan Africa. This study evaluates drought susceptibility in the Ashanti Region of Ghana using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and a multi-criteria decision analysis framework based on the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Seven environmental factors were integrated into the model: temperature, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), Soil Moisture Index (SMI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), slope, elevation, and distance to rivers. title: Wildfire Smoke Drives Enhanced Brown Carbon Absorption in an Urban Atmosphere
abstract: Extreme wildfire smoke can substantially alter urban aerosol loading and optical properties, yet the contributions of black carbon and wavelength dependent brown‐carbon‐like absorption remain poorly constrained in downwind cities. We present continuous observations of equivalent black carbon (eBC) and aerosol optical properties in Montréal, Canada, from July 2022 to July 2023, encompassing the exceptional 2023 Canadian wildfire season. title: Eurasian Subtropical Jet Asymmetrically Links to the Dipole Pattern of Summer Precipitation Anomalies Over Central Asia and Northern China
abstract: The East Asian Subtropical Jet (EASJ), the eastern core of the Eurasian Subtropical Jet (ESJ), plays an important role in mid‐latitude weather and climate. However, the relationship between the summer precipitation anomalies over the entrance and exit of the EASJ remains unclear. Here, we identify a dipole pattern of summer precipitation between Central Asia (CA, entrance) and Northern China (NC, exit). title: CbSDI for Ecological Sustainability and Smart Urban Development in Kigali: An Integrated Approach to Building Resilient Cities
abstract: Urbanization presents pressing challenges for sustainability, requiring cities to balance equity, economic growth, and environmental preservation. Kigali, Rwanda’s capital, has emerged as a model for integrating ecological sustainability with smart city development. This study examines Kigali’s initiatives in green infrastructure, biodiversity conservation, waste management, renewable energy, and sustainable transportation, highlighting their role in enhancing resilience and livability. title: Tendência da estação chuvosa na América do Sul entre 1981 e 2021 para o produto RADS
abstract: A estação chuvosa constitui uma dimensão central da sazonalidade hidroclimática na América do Sul, e suas mudanças podem se expressar não apenas pela variação no volume precipitado, mas também pela reorganização do calendário sazonal. Este estudo analisa as tendências (Mann-Kendall e Sen) de início, término, duração e precipitação acumulada na América do Sul, entre 1981 e 2021, utilizando o produto Rainy and Dry Seasons (RADS), derivado do CHIRPS. abstract: In this study the monthly and annual 2-m air temperature, precipitation and 0–7 cm volumetric soil moisture were validated for six selected coordinate locations within Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo and Rivers states in the South-South Nigeria from January 2000 to December 2025. The 1,872 location-month records were retrieved from the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, with the model ERA5 option. title: Multivariate Gaussian process emulation for multifidelity computer models with high-dimensional spatial outputs
abstract: Risk assessment of hurricane-driven storm surge relies on deterministic computer models that produce outputs over a large spatial domain. The surge models can often be run at a range of fidelity levels, with greater precision yielding more accurate simulations. Improved accuracy comes with a significant increase in computational expense, necessitating the development of an emulator which leverages information from the more plentiful low-fidelity outputs to provide fast and accurate predictions of high-fidelity simulations. title: CFD-Based PMM Maneuvering Derivatives and Turning-Circle Prediction for DTMB 5512
abstract: This study evaluates CFD-based Planar Motion Mechanism (PMM) simulations for identifying the maneuvering hydrodynamic derivatives of the DTMB 5512 benchmark model and transferring the resulting hull model to a system-based turning-circle prediction. Static drift, pure yaw, and yaw-and drift motions were simulated at Fn=0.28 for the configuration with bilge keels. Static-drift forces and yaw moment were compared directly with experimental PMM data and reduced by polynomial regression. title: Spatio-temporal modeling of dengue in Argentina (2009–2025): factors associated with reported incidence, spatial patterns, and implications for prevention planning
abstract: Background Dengue has expanded markedly in Argentina, with Aedes aegypti now established in temperate provinces and successive epidemics culminating in a record outbreak in 2024. Disentangling large-scale inter-annual climate variability from local environmental and socio-infrastructural conditions is essential for targeted prevention, yet few studies have modelled dengue determinants across Argentina’s heterogeneous transmission zones at national scale. title: Mind the birds: Assessing the uncertainty in modelling of urban photovoltaic soiling
abstract: Soiling represents a significant loss mechanism in photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, its quantification is still challenging, especially in urban environments, where modules can be exposed to severe bird droppings. This study evaluates the reliability of different approaches for estimating soiling losses in such conditions, using a one-year experimental campaign based on a dedicated soiling station installed in Split, Croatia, as a reference. Results show that an irradiance-based approach can be used to reproduce the temporal evolution of soiling losses with good accuracy after calibration.

title: Cosmetic Packaging’s Green Transition: Trends, Gaps, and the Complex Cosmetic Macroplastic Packaging Waste Definition
abstract: As the global cosmetic products market continues its rapid expansion, the industry faces an escalating waste management crisis driven by the massive annual production of packaging units used by the industry. This study investigates the strategic shift in scientific research and regulatory frameworks regarding cosmetic packaging waste. Using bibliometric analysis via the bibliometrix R-package and VOSviewer (v.1.6.20), a dataset of 352 Web of Science publications (2005–2025) was analyzed. title: Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
abstract: Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
abstract: Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. title: A novel peridynamics-based enthalpy framework for advective melting and freezing with density-change effects
abstract: Melting and freezing processes frequently occur in the presence of fluid motion and density variation, yet their accurate prediction remains challenging because of the strong coupling among advective heat transfer, unequal liquid and solid densities, and moving solid–liquid interfaces. In this study, a novel peridynamics (PD)-based enthalpy framework for transient heat transfer with solid–liquid phase change and density-change effects is developed and systematically verified. title: Periglacial Landform Distribution and Rock Glacier Dynamics in a Semiarid Andean Headwater Catchment: Estero Derecho Nature Sanctuary, Chile (~30° S)
abstract: Rock glaciers are key components of high mountain environments, especially in arid and semiarid regions, where glaciers are scarce. These ice‐debris landforms may act as resilient ice reservoirs and have growing hydrological importance under climate warming. Despite their potential significance, rock glaciers in the semiarid Andes remain understudied, and the climatic controls influencing their distribution and activity are poorly understood. abstract: Study region La Martre River watershed, in the Mackenzie River Basin, is a discontinuous permafrost watershed in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Accelerated climate warming in northern Canada is driving significant changes in temperature patterns, precipitation, permafrost, and wildfire frequency and severity. These changes have individually been linked to observed increases in annual and winter streamflow, though the underlying drivers and cumulative effects remain complex and poorly understood. title: Stiffness-normalized fiber-reinforced polymer composite repair thickness for corroded steel pipelines: design maps and correlation
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) systems are widely used to repair corroded steel pipes, but the required repair thickness depends strongly on the stiffness level of the FRP layer, particularly its hoop direction modulus. This study developed finite-element (FE)-based repair thickness maps for externally repaired corroded steel pipes using normalized FRP stiffness levels. title: Evaluating Decision Criteria for Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting Retrofits in Institutional Buildings: A Critical Integrative Review
abstract: Rooftop rainwater harvesting retrofits in institutional buildings require evidence on water performance, affordability, constraints, and operations, yet inconsistent boundaries limit transferability. This critical integrative review examines the decision criteria and evidentiary requirements supporting institutional retrofit decisions. A purposive sample of 83 full-text publications, screened from 309 Web of Science records, was systematically evaluated against 24 predefined criteria spanning financial, environmental, technological, structural, innovation, and social dimensions. title: Evaluating the representativeness of aircraft sampling strategies for cloud water content in LASSO simulations over the ARM Southern Great Plains (SGP) Site
abstract: Aircraft observations are widely used to evaluate cloud simulations; however, their inherently localized sampling may not fully represent the domain-scale cloud properties resolved by large-eddy simulations (LES). This study quantifies how aircraft-like sampling strategies influence the representativeness of in-cloud cloud water content (CWC) derived from LES output. title: Implementation of new, asset-specific damage curves for flood risk assessment in wastewater treatment plants: a methodological approach applied to the Metropolitan Area of Barcelona (Spain)
abstract: The frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters have increased in recent decades, posing significant challenges to urban resilience. Sanitation systems, particularly wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), are exposed to flood hazards due to their location in low-lying areas near receiving water bodies. Flood events may cause service disruptions, asset and equipment damage, and associated environmental and economic consequences. abstract: This review evaluates the occurrence and epidemiological trends of major foodborne zoonotic pathogens in the European Union, with particular emphasis on the Republic of Croatia, over the period 2020-2024. Using the One Health framework, data were synthesised from annual zoonosis reports of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), complemented by targeted national and regional studies. abstract: When no streamflow time series are available to calibrate a hydrological model, other information can be used. title: Early Cretaceous Paleomagnetic Constraints on a Smaller Greater India
abstract: The original extent of Greater India is critical for East Gondwana reconstructions. Recent paleomagnetic results suggest a smaller Greater India at ca. 126 Ma, but the single‐polarity data seriously limit their reliability. abstract: Sub-pixel fire characterization is essential for quantifying wildfire energetics, combustion phase dynamics, and their atmospheric impacts from satellite observations. This study presents a series of Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) to systematically evaluate the influence of temperature phase complexity, channel selection, and intra-phase temperature heterogeneity on the performance of a Bayesian retrieval framework. title: Stability and Emissions Characteristics of Syngas and Hydrogen Non-premixed Flames
abstract: Hydrogen-enriched syngas produced by biomass gasification is a promising renewable fuel for low-carbon, high-efficiency combustion systems. This study experimentally investigates the stability, flame structure, and pollutant emissions of non-premixed laminar diffusion flames fueled by pure hydrogen and hydrogen-rich syngas mixtures (H 2 /CO and H 2 /CO/CH 4 /CO 2 ). abstract: Controllable shock-wave fracturing combined with perforation offers a potential approach for unconventional reservoir stimulation, yet the effects of perforation configuration, in-situ stress, and shock-wave loading parameters on rock damage remain unclear. In this study, a three-dimensional finite element model incorporating wellbore and perforation cavities was established using the Holmquist-Johnson-Cook (HJC) constitutive model. title: Validating wind farm parameterizations with offshore SCADA data
abstract: A large-scale validation compared wind farm parameterizations (WFPs) of the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model to multi-year SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) data from six offshore wind farms. Although initially seven WFPs were considered, after preliminary assessment only three distinct ones were retained: the original Fitch (Fitch-O), a physics-derived axial-induction modification of Fitch (Fitch-pAIM), and the explicit wake parameterization (EWP). title: Morphological and phylogenic variability of red snow algae in snowpacks along a glacial valley in Alaska
abstract: Red snow blooms are visually similar but can be composed of different algal species and cell morphologies across sites, and the factors determining this spatial heterogeneity remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated spatial variation in community structure, algal cell size, and morphology along gradients of elevation across a glacier and its forefield in Alaska. abstract: To investigate ground surface settlement patterns during caisson sinking in soft soils, this study systematically examines the evolution of the soil plastic zone and ground surface settlement using field monitoring and three-dimensional numerical simulations. title: A Municipal Flood Early-Warning Framework for Community-Centred Development in Urban Uganda
abstract: Urban flood early-warning services in Uganda face interconnected challenges involving incomplete rainfall records, limited monitoring infrastructure, intermittent power and communications, and fragmented arrangements for warning and response. Guided by the World Meteorological Organization’s (WMO) people-centred early-warning framework and the Sendai Framework for Disaster-Risk Reduction, this paper develops a structured pre-deployment municipal framework linking risk knowledge, monitoring, communication, preparedness and accountable governance.
