title: Mineral dust concentration controlling convective cirrus structure and persistence: a large-eddy simulation study with observational constraints
abstract: Dusty cirrus clouds are optically thick, convectively organized ice clouds that occur during intense mineral dust outbreaks. Previous modeling studies have found a link between mineral dust and convectively generated cirrus, but have been unable to explicitly resolve the associated convective dynamics due to limited spatial resolution. title: Rethinking maturity in disaster recovery modeling
abstract: Disaster recovery modeling has evolved substantially over the past decades, moving from engineering-oriented representations of physical repair toward increasingly sophisticated simulations of complex, interconnected socio-technical systems. Despite these advances, in my assessment, operational use of recovery models within institutional decision-making remains comparatively limited. abstract: Purpose This study explores the multipolar network spatial organization of the regional economy, clarifies its connotation, characteristics and value and provides theoretical and practical support for solving regional economic strategic issues, building a new development pattern and promoting Chinese modernization. abstract: Integrating dihydrogen (H 2 ) into energy mixes requires assessing its viability in underground gas storages (UGS) like deep aquifers. The primary challenge is H 2 consumption by autochthonous microorganisms, leading to site-dependent issues like souring and petrophysical changes. title: Supply chain resilience under geopolitical chokepoint disruption: a multiple case study of the GCC countries during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
abstract: The Strait of Hormuz faces severe geopolitical pressure following the 2025-2026 US-Israel-Iran conflict. Some 20 million barrels of oil per day and 20% of global LNG trade transit this 21-mile chokepoint, yet bypass capacity covers fewer than 28% of these flows. This paper examines how the six Gulf Cooperation Council nations have experienced and responded to this disruption through supply chain resilience theory. title: The impact of extreme weather events on the mental health of vulnerable populations in Africa (The WEMA project): a study protocol
abstract: Background Extreme weather events (EWEs) are increasing in frequency and intensity due to climate change, with adverse effects on physical and mental health and disproportionate impacts on vulnerable populations. Limited evidence on the mental health effects of EWEs in Africa highlights the need for research to inform policy and practice. The WEMA study aims to investigate the impacts of EWEs, such as heat and flooding, on common mental disorders (CMDs) in Burkina Faso, Kenya, Mozambique, and South Africa. title: Soybean meal-induced enteritis in fish: a microbiota-immune-metabolic perspective informed by bibliometric analysis and multi-database validation
abstract: Introduction Fish enteritis is a major health challenge in aquaculture as low-fishmeal feeding strategies become more common. Soybean meal-induced enteritis (SBMIE) is a representative model of diet-induced intestinal inflammation, but evidence remains dispersed across species, feed ingredients, pathological endpoints, and mechanistic approaches. title: Dry-Season Roadside Air Quality and Weather Associations in Agbarho, Niger Delta, Nigeria: A Data-Reconciliation and Exploratory Field Assessment
abstract: Roadside air pollution in rapidly changing Nigerian settlements is shaped by nearby combustion and dust sources as well as local ventilation, yet dry-season measurements from smaller Niger Delta communities remain limited. This study examines a supplied field dataset for 18 described sampling locations and a control site in Agbarho and nearby settlements, Delta State, and evaluates its pollutant–weather patterns after reconciling the raw data table. title: Tree-ring cellulose oxygen isotope reveals summer hydroclimate variability across the East European Plain
abstract: Hydroclimate variability across the East European Plain plays a critical role in regional ecosystems and climate dynamics, yet moisture-sensitive tree-ring proxies remain scarce in this region, particularly at high latitudes where tree-ring width (TRW) and density are primarily controlled by temperature. Tree-ring cellulose oxygen isotopes ( δ 18 O TRC ) have the potential to serve as a useful hydroclimate proxy, but their climatic signal in this region remains poorly understood. title: Precipitation extremes in the Argentine Pampas: Current declining trends and projected intensification under climate change
abstract: Climate change is intensifying precipitation extremes globally, posing challenges to agriculture and water management in vulnerable regions such as the Argentine Pampas, one of the world’s major agricultural zones. This study analyses long-term evolution of precipitation patterns and extremes in the Argentine Pampas to inform agricultural planning, water management and adaptation strategies. We examine spatiotemporal variability across three time periods: present (2010–2024), near future (2025–2039) and far future (2085–2099). abstract: Shape adaptive shape memory alloy hybrid composites (SMAHCs) are composites that incorporate shape memory alloys (SMAs) to realize reversible and continuous shape transformation. Despite the availability of numerous analytical and finite element models for predicting the transient response of SMAHCs, many approaches still exhibit limitations with respect to the electro-thermomechanical coupling and comprehensive experimental validation. abstract: This study investigates the final evolution of the Inner Cordilleran magmatic arc (661–580 Ma) of the Araçuaí-Ribeira Orogenic System (SE-Brazil) focusing on the critical transition from subduction to continental collision between c. 610 and 580 Ma. abstract: To reduce mudflat disturbance caused by hydraulic dredging and facilitate efficient, environmentally responsible mechanized harvesting of buried bivalves, this study aimed to develop an accurate discrete element method (DEM) model for analyzing Mactra veneriformis (M. veneriformis)–machine interactions and optimizing harvesting parameters. title: Weak morphological constraints on species roles and partner identity in a facultative ant–plant mutualism
abstract: Mutualisms contribute substantially to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, yet the factors structuring facultative mutualisms remain poorly understood. Trait-based approaches suggest that functional traits may shape species roles and interaction patterns by influencing resource access, exploitation efficiency, and competitive ability, but whether they constrain partner identity remains unclear. title: Dream4D: Lifting Camera‐Controlled I2V towards Spatiotemporally Consistent 4D Generation
abstract: Generating spatiotemporally consistent 4D content requires joint modeling of high‐fidelity spatial details and realistic temporal dynamics. However, existing methods typically lack world knowledge learned from expansive 4D observations. abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. abstract: Trace elements in quartz are increasingly used to determine fluid sources in hydrothermal systems. This study investigates the applications and limitations of quartz as a source proxy and precipitation style monitor using well-characterized samples from the Schwarzwald, where quartz precipitated from various types of hydrothermal fluids over 330 million years. abstract: Increasing atmospheric temperature is expected to lead to higher moisture-holding capacity and the potential for stronger storms. abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. abstract: Autonomous mobile robots that run lean milk-run routes must keep a safe separation from operators, pallets and aisle boundaries while meeting a fixed delivery cycle. title: Full-range flexural modelling of hybrid-reinforced steel fibre recycled aggregate concrete beams
abstract: Hybrid FRP-steel reinforcement and steel fibre-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (SFRAC) can improve crack control and deformation capacity, but the full-range flexural response of hybrid SFRAC beams remains insufficiently quantified. abstract: We examined the eco-correlates of coloration and patterning in Viperidae, a relatively sedentary group of venomous snakes, focusing on the details of four forms of protective coloration: background matching, disruptive coloration, motion dazzle and aposematism. Using phylogenetically controlled analyses of 331 species, we found speckled and beige vipers are associated with living in desert and grasslands, whereas green vipers are found in trees. abstract: Single piles with caps frequently bear pure lateral loads induced by wind, waves, ship impact and adjacent soil movement, yet quantitative studies on the meso-scale deformation and load transfer of the surrounding soil remain scarce. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the hydrodynamic characteristics of double heave plates, combining forced oscillation experiments with numerical simulations. abstract: In this paper, we revisit the Gutnish si-passive described by Petzell (2024). While Petzell focused on the genesis of the si-passive and its early use during the 19th century, we now follow up how the usage has changed during the 20th and 21st centuries. abstract: Lumbar disc herniation is a common cause of disabling back pain and requires effective treatment strategies; however, conventional fusion devices are highly rigid and can severely restrict vertebral motion. abstract: This study examined how residents of flood-affected neighbourhoods in Ado-Ekiti, Nigeria, explain, experience, and cost flooding and how they adapt; reviewed dated documentary evidence of flood-related disruption to the road network; and assessed what the evidence implies for access to hospitality and tourism services and for tourism resilience in a tourism-aspiring capital city.

abstract: The focus of this study is to provide an all-inclusive wind data characterization for Abakaliki in Ebonyi State of South-East region of Nigeria and to evaluate its potential wind energy generation to ascertain if wind energy could be a practical source of electricity in that region. A 10-years period (2012-2021) wind speed dataset obtained at 10 m anemometer height was collected from Nigerian Meteorological Agency. title: Multimodal public perception of Port City Heritage, a virtual reality study in Amsterdam
abstract: Public perception is recognised as a valuable yet underexplored dimension of architectural heritage conservation. This gap is significant for Port City Heritage (PCH), where many attributes have been rapidly changed through urbanisation. This study proposes a VR-based multimodal approach to examine how the perception of heritage attributes changes from visual attention to interpretation over time. Using Amsterdam’s 17th-century Canal Ring as a case study, 25 participants experienced historical scenes overlaid onto present-day panoramas. abstract: O polo Petrolina-PE/Juazeiro-BA é o principal centro de fruticultura irrigada do semiárido brasileiro, mas os dados públicos sobre produção, clima, água e preços estão dispersos em portais com formato, periodicidade e política de acesso próprios, o que impede cruzá-los de forma reproduzível. title: Beyond Tomorrow—Electrification of Hard-to-Abate Sectors
abstract: Reaching net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors, which today account for 30% of global GHG emissions and include steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, and shipping. title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
abstract: The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. The retrieved moment tensors contain not only double-couple (DC) components but also significant non-double-couple (non-DC) components. abstract: Compact transport vehicles fitted with crane booms require stability assessment beyond nominal payload ratings. This study implements a fully specified rigid-body screening model for 200 kg at 3.60 m, 310 kg at 2.70 m, 450 kg at 1.95 m and 800 kg at 1.13 m horizontal payload reach. title: Reliability-based assessment of plate anchor keying and capacity in spatially variable clay
abstract: Plate anchors are widely used for offshore mooring because of their high efficiency, but their performance depends on ultimate pullout resistance and the keying process, during which upwards movement reduces embedment. Existing analyses mostly consider homogeneous or idealised layered soils, whereas offshore sediments are inherently spatially variable. The unquantified effects of this variability on anchor keying and capacity cause significant design uncertainty. abstract: Urban thermal environments are strongly influenced by urban morphology and land cover, yet the seasonal stability of Local Climate Zone (LCZ)–land surface temperature (LST) relationships in cold-climate cities remains insufficiently understood. In regions with long winters and seasonal snow cover, LCZ-specific surface thermal responses may differ substantially from those observed in temperate cities. abstract: This paper describes a physically-based algorithm for estimating the mass-weighted raindrop diameter ( D m ) and the corresponding Doppler velocities ( V D ) which are the radar reflectivity-weighted terminal velocities of the raindrops. The algorithm exploits the attenuation-corrected radar reflectivity ( Z e ) and the specific attenuation ( k ) observed by Ku- and W-band space-borne Doppler radars and estimate D m assuming a specified drop size distribution DSD. abstract: Simulating urban airflow and pollutant dispersion requires resolving multiscale physical processes, from large-scale meteorological forcing to highly localized building-induced turbulence. To accurately capture these multiscale urban flow fields, this study introduces FluidUrban v1.0, an advanced modelling system built upon the Fluidity solver and centred on a three-dimensional Dynamic Adaptive Mesh Optimization (DAMO) framework. title: Growth of Nanoparticles Driven by Distinct Chemical Composition Leads to Contrasting Hygroscopicity and CCN Potential Across Two Environments Over the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of aerosols and cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) over the remote Tibetan Plateau (TP), yet the chemical drivers and climatic impacts of nanoparticle growth remain poorly understood. title: An Experimental Study on the Response of Passive Piles in Soft Clay
abstract: This paper experimentally evaluates the behavior of model piles in a clayey soil exposed to horizontal ground movement. A custom-designed laboratory apparatus, split into upper and lower components, was developed to simulate pile response under a uniform lateral soil movement profile. The device was designed to permit the upper box to slide over the lower box when a horizontal force is applied. Thus, the soil is divided into two separate zones: a moving upper layer and a stable lower stratum. Several tests were performed using square aluminum tubes of varying dimensions embedded in soft clay.

abstract: Estimating net water withdrawals at the basin scale is often hindered by incomplete or inconsistent direct abstraction data, especially for diffuse uses like irrigation. This study introduces a simple hydrological approach to reconstruct long-term net withdrawals by comparing observed discharge at a basin outlet with a natural discharge estimated from spatially distributed runoff and groundwater recharge. abstract: Blasting excavation of shallow subway cross-passages can generate ground vibrations that affect nearby tunnels and urban infrastructure. abstract: The evolutionary loss of photosynthesis is a central question in plant evolutionary ecology. In orchids, full mycoheterotrophy is generally thought to evolve through partial mycoheterotrophy, yet the role of saprotrophic fungi in this transition remains poorly understood. We investigated nutritional strategies and fungal partners in two leafy Calypsoinae orchids, Cremastra unguiculata and Oreorchis coreana, which occupy early-diverging positions within their respective lineages. abstract: BACKGROUND: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens (Stål), and the white-backed planthopper (WBPH), Sogatella furcifera (Horváth), are both major migratory rice pests in Asia, but their cross-border migration dynamics in southern Yunnan, China, remain poorly understood. abstract: Urban heat is transforming as a major disaster and challenge to urban planners and policy makers. The impacts of urban heat are disproportionate and much severe amongst marginalized communities. Nature-based traditional ecological knowledge has become a vital heat adaptive mechanism for such communities. abstract: The stability problem of thin shallow shells is considered, taking into account geometric nonlinearity and creep of the material. abstract: Air entrapment commonly occurs in pressurized pipeline systems, where discrete air pockets form at fittings, high points, or geometric irregularities, yet are often neglected in practice. abstract: Water deficiency is a critical abiotic stress that negatively affects agricultural productivity and product quality. Biochar (BC) is an effective amendment for improving crop yields and mitigating the adverse effects of stress conditions. Zinc (Zn) also plays a crucial role in plant growth and stress tolerance. abstract: Sinkholes can damage transportation infrastructure, underground systems, and buildings through sudden surface and subsurface failure. abstract: This study investigates the impact of technological innovations on enhancing procurement performance within Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) construction projects in Malaysia. abstract: Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. title: Unified post-necking true stress-strain models for hot-rolled steels
abstract: The use of advanced numerical methods for the simulation and design of steel components and structures has increased rapidly in recent years. The response of elements experiencing large plastic deformations and even fracture can now be accurately captured. For such analyses, the full true stress-strain relationship of the material up to the fracture strain is required. title: Analysis of The Impact of River Discharge on Embankment Stability and Nature-Based Solutions: A Case Study at The CS-9 Cibingbin Site
abstract: River embankments constructed from granular materials excavated during river channel normalization, including gravel, stone, and sand, are particularly susceptible to erosion, seepage, and instability under high-flow conditions. This study examined the effects of river discharge on embankment stability at the CS-9 Cibingbin cross-section in Kuningan Regency, Indonesia, and assessed a hybrid nature-based solution (NBS) incorporating gabion structures and riparian vegetation as a potential stabilization measure. title: Performance of surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma actuators at different ambient conditions
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of the influence of ambient air temperature and pressure on the performance of a surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma actuator. The analysis focuses on key discharge and flow characteristics, including the discharge current, power consumption, electric body force, and the resulting induced airflow. title: Process sequencing in torrefied pellet production: Evidence gaps, performance trade-offs and a decision framework for industrial deployment
abstract: Torrefaction and pelletisation are reviewed as complementary biomass-upgrading operations, yet plant design lacks a defensible basis for deciding which operation should precede the other. This synthesis evaluates torrefy-then-densify (T → P) and densify-then-torrefy (P → T) by separating direct comparisons from single-route experiments and system evidence. abstract: Multiple-point geostatistics (MPS) can reproduce complex geological patterns, but its performance depends on representative training images (TIs). We developed a workflow that converts forward hydrodynamic simulations of braided-river deposition into three-dimensional TIs for reservoir-architecture modeling. Five candidate TIs were reconstructed from time-resolved erosion–deposition increments and classified into channel, mid-channel-bar, floodplain, and bar-margin elements. title: Guided-wave transmission of ultrasonic signals using compressive sensing and time-domain encoding
abstract: The increasing deployment of intelligent structures and embedded sensor networks creates a growing demand for reliable transmission of measurement data in environments where conventional wired and wireless communication methods are ineffective. In metallic and enclosed structures, electromagnetic waves are strongly attenuated, while wired solutions increase system complexity and weight. title: Impact of aerosol absorption and scattering on winter fog lifecycle: insights from NWP simulations over Indo-Gangetic Plains
abstract: The Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP) of India frequently experience widespread and dense winter fog with substantial health and economic consequences. This season also coincides with elevated aerosol loading. This study investigates the influence of aerosols on the development and evolution of dense fog over the IGP using high-resolution numerical experiments. We focus especially on the relative contributions of absorption and scattering to aerosol-radiation interactions (ARI). title: Temperature-dependent tribological performance of HVOF-thermal sprayed FeCoCrNiAl HEA coating deposited on TC4 alloy
abstract: A FeCoCrNiAl high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating was deposited on a Ti-6Al-4 V (TC4) alloy substrate by high-velocity oxygen fuel (HVOF) thermal spraying to enhance its sliding wear performance. Reciprocating sliding tests were conducted from 25 °C to 300 °C, and the temperature-dependent friction behavior, wear morphology, and damage evolution were examined. title: Thermally Altered Pore-Fracture Structures and Water Seepage Behaviors in Shale Characterized by LF-NMR Measurements and Numerical Simulations
abstract: Shale is a tight medium with low porosity and permeability, and fluid seepage takes place across interconnected pores and fractures. Thermal stimulation triggers shale cracking, alters pore-fracture geometry, fluid properties, and seepage rules, so as to boost shale gas output. Most existing studies on shale fluid flow under temperature conditions focus solely on either freeze damage at low temperatures or thermal damage at high temperatures. title: A preliminary study of runoff-generated waste dump debris flow in the mountain cryosphere
abstract: Waste dump debris flows pose significant risks as man-made disasters. The development of large-scale infrastructure in the Tibetan Plateau of China has led to the accumulation of tunnel waste in the mountain cryosphere. To investigate the erosion process and initiation mechanism of waste dump debris flows caused by concentrated runoff in the mountain cryosphere, we examined the erosion characteristics of the Duoxiongla waste dump near Mount Namcha Barwa. title: Characterization of phenotypic and genetic diversity of registered indigenous Mashona cattle in Zimbabwe during periods of political and economic instability
abstract: We characterized phenotypic-and-pedigree-based genetic diversity of registered indigenous Mashona cattle in Zimbabwe during periods of political and economic instability using 14,977 animals born between 1960 and 2025. Coat color was predominantly black (58.4%), followed by red (28.6%). The annual proportion of polled animals increased substantially after 2013, rising from 2.2% in 2013 to 50.6% in 2015 and 46.3% in 2022, a trend consistent with selection for the polled phenotype. title: Soil‐specific correlations between vertical electrical sounding, cone penetration test and multichannel analysis of surface waves for Quaternary alluvium
abstract: The integration of electrical resistivity ( ρ ) from vertical electrical sounding, cone penetration test (CPT) parameters and shear‐wave velocity ( V s ) from multichannel analysis of surface waves provides a comprehensive approach to soil characterization. However, direct empirical correlations linking these three geotechnical and geophysical parameters remain limited in the literature. abstract: To address the deficiencies of traditional sealing walls, such as low construction efficiency, susceptibility to failure, and poor airtightness, this paper proposes a novel sealing wall with equivalent thickness. abstract: Produced water is often used for pressure maintenance and secondary recovery in reservoirs. However, the successful injection of produced water depends on its quality, which is related to the presence of organic and inorganic solids. In this study, four nanotechnology-based treatments were evaluated to restore and/or prevent formation damage associated with a decline in injectivity during the water-injection process. title: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
abstract: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of thermotidal torque on tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising a star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. title: Fast models for blockage and gravity-wave effects on wind-farm power output
abstract: Large offshore wind farms can trigger atmospheric gravity waves, with the associated hydrostatic blockage effect impacting their energy yield. Unfortunately, to date no tools exist that can model this wind-farm–gravity-wave interaction and blockage at a computational cost that is not drastically higher than conventional engineering wake models. title: The evolution of hourly strombolian cycles towards paroxysmal activity at Etna volcano
abstract: Lava fountains are typical of basaltic volcanic eruptions, especially during paroxysms when activity shifts from intermittent Strombolian explosions to sustained high lava discharge often accompanied by ash emission. Cyclic eruptive behaviour –marked by regular variations in explosive intensity and lava fountaining over periods of minutes to hours– has been observed before but rarely captured in the geophysical record. title: Evolution of Spacesuit Pressure Systems: From Gas Pressurization to Mechanical Counter-Pressure Concepts
abstract: The renewed interest in long-duration human exploration missions to the Moon and Mars has highlighted the need for spacesuits capable of ensuring both physiological protection and operational performance. Operational extravehicular activity (EVA) spacesuits rely primarily on gas pressurization, which can impose mobility constraints, increase metabolic cost and contribute to fatigue and musculoskeletal injury risk. title: Environmental disruptions and malaria dynamics: causal evidence from climate extremes and fires in the Amazon
abstract: This study examines the causal effects of droughts, unusually high annual precipitation, and fire exposure on malaria incidence in the Brazilian Amazon using a staggered difference-in-differences approach. Combining municipal-level data from 2007 to 2021, we exploit variation in the timing of exposure to climatic and environmental shocks to estimate their dynamic impacts on malaria outcomes. The results show that droughts and unusually high annual precipitation are associated with reductions in malaria incidence, although the effects are not immediate and unfold over time. title: Verifying finite-element buckling of columns and plates: an educational study with mode transitions
abstract: This educational case study shows, step by step, how analytical solutions verify finite-element buckling eigenvalue models for a pinned-pinned Euler-Bernoulli column and a simply supported rectangular plate under uniaxial compression. abstract: The use of interlocking concrete block pavements has increased in Cuba in recent years, particularly in pedestrian areas and on roads with light to medium traffic, with notable applications in the Mariel Development Zone. However, despite their growing use, there is currently no national standard regulating the structural design of this type of pavement. abstract: The teaching of reading is a foundational component of policies and practices for primary education worldwide. Evidence from international comparative studies showed that where the English language was the medium of instruction in schools, jurisdictions performing at the highest levels in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) and Progress in International Reading Literacy Study (PIRLS) had adopted different approaches to the effective teaching of reading. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive hydrogeochemical characterization of the Matese Massif carbonate aquifer system (Southern Apennines, Italy), based on original field samples collected during the 2018–2020 period. Hydrochemical and isotopic analyses were carried out on 109 groundwater samples (springs and wells) to quantify heat discharge and flux of endogenous carbon (C deep ). abstract: Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. abstract: Poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) used in high-temperature vacuum forming shows strongly temperature-, strain-rate-, and time-dependent behavior requiring reliable thermal and mechanical material properties for the development of manufacturing process based on finite element simulation. In this study, a comprehensive material characterization and constitutive modeling framework was proposed for PMMA under conditions relevant to high-temperature vacuum forming. title: Thermochromic Spectrum‑Selective Photovoltaic Glazing with Building Energy Saving and Adaptive Daylighting
abstract: Semitransparent PV glazing is increasingly adopted in low‑energy buildings, but its high operating temperatures and fixed optical properties limit the improvement of indoor thermal and daylighting conditions. In response to these challenges, this study proposes a thermochromic spectrum‑selective (TC‑SS) PV glazing system that combines visible modulation, near‑infrared reflection, and sky radiative cooling within a single glazing unit to achieve building energy saving and adaptive daylighting. abstract: Nonlinear nudging augments the classical linear nudging (continuous data as- similation) term with a nonlinear feedback that strengthens as the observed error decreases, and yields super-exponential convergence to the true state. In this paper, we study nonlinear nudging for the 3-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with the finite element method, which allows complex geometries and physical boundary conditions. abstract: We develop an intrinsic kinetic moment closure for shallow-water equations on smooth manifolds of arbitrary dimension equipped with prescribed, possibly time-dependent Riemannian metrics. Hamiltonian transport on the cotangent bundle and metric-dependent momentum integration yield balance laws with hydrostatic pressure, bottom topography, a skew-adjoint force, and dissipative bottom friction. abstract: Eddies in rotating turbulence can feed the jets that spawn them, resulting in the negative viscosity phenomenon. Taken alone, a negative viscosity represents up-gradient eddy fluxes and is often referred to as "antifriction" or "antidiffusion". Mathematically, it leads to an ill-posed problem. title: MetacouplingLLM: Integrating geographic adjacency, flow indicators, and LLM-assisted analysis
abstract: The metacoupling framework examines interactions within coupled human and natural systems and between adjacent or distant systems, but its application is constrained by inconsistent geographic classifications and limited standardized quantitative workflows. We present MetacouplingLLM, an open-source Python package integrating adjacency databases, reproducible flow indicators, and large language model (LLM)-assisted qualitative analysis. title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

abstract: Natural ice commonly contains entrapped air, yet its dynamical role during melting remains unresolved. Using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, we show that melt-front-released bubbles activate entrapped air as a mechanical forcing on the liquid. Bubble buoyancy disrupts density-anomaly-induced thermal structure and injects momentum into the melt-controlling boundary layer, producing melt rates more than twice the bubble-free value at percent-level gas fractions. abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. abstract: We extend BK19 the semi-implicit finite-volume solver, to provide access to the quasi-geostrophic (QG) regime within the same compressible framework that already admits soundproof and hydrostatic limits. abstract: Tropical cyclones almost never form within a few degrees of the equator. Their energy source, the heat engine fueled by the warm ocean, is available there as everywhere else. What is missing must be the other ingredient a cyclone needs, absolute angular momentum about the local vertical. abstract: The Global Carbon Budget (GCB), the community reference dataset for the carbon cycle, is reissued annually. The 2025 release introduces several adjustments to the published series that we compare with prior releases starting in 2017. abstract: Vertically resolved budget analyses of frozen moist static energy (FMSE) variance within a cloud-resolving model provide a rigorous perspective on the equilibrium state of deep convective self-aggregation. abstract: Vertical profiles of the refractive-index (RI) structure parameter, $C_n^2$, are required in atmospheric-optics calculations. abstract: African easterly waves (AEWs) drive the synoptic variability of West African monsoon rainfall via intricate two-way interactions with mesoscale convective systems (MCSs). The composite MCS-AEW system is a canonical example of multiscale interactions in the tropical atmosphere, with upscale feedbacks from deep convection driving the evolution of a larger-scale circulation. abstract: This paper presents a two-way coupled fluid--solid interaction framework for granular systems based on the level-set discrete element method (LS-DEM) and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH). The proposed method is mesh-free, fully Lagrangian, and equipped with a seamless description of arbitrary solid shapes. abstract: Construction tasks in hazardous and unstructured environments require both human adaptability and robotic precision, yet existing approaches often treat teleoperation and autonomy as separate control modes. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop control paradigm that enables structured transitions among VR-guided teleoperation, semi-autonomous shared control, and rule-based autonomous execution for contact-rich dual-arm construction tasks. abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. abstract: Earth's atmosphere operates a steam cycle: water evaporates from the surface, expands as vapor, condenses in colder air, and returns as precipitation. abstract: We investigate quantum gate teleportation as a primitive for satellite-enabled distributed quantum computing. abstract: The integrated analysis and optimisation codes used to design nuclear fusion reactors need to become increasingly large scale, multidisciplinary and complex to computationally verify design requirements more thoroughly and earlier in the design process. Though the manner in which the integrated models are coupled can have significant implications for computational efficiency, the structure of couplings typically remains hidden in the implementation of a design framework. title: On the numerical representation of atmospheric Lamb waves in dynamical cores
abstract: Atmospheric Lamb waves are horizontally propagating acoustic waves that are supported by hydrostatic and nonhydrostatic compressible equation sets. They are classically defined in an isothermal atmosphere and generate no vertical velocity. In a dynamical core, the numerical representation of the Lamb wave is sensitive to modelling choices, such as the upper boundary condition and spatial discretisation. title: An Evidence-Based Decision Framework for Retiring Roadside Traveler Information Infrastructure in the Mobile Era
abstract: As mobile traveler-information services expand, transportation agencies must determine whether aging roadside infrastructure can be retired while preserving public access and operational resilience. This study develops an evidence-based decision framework for screening highway advisory radio (HAR) and dynamic message sign (DMS) assets for retirement. The framework integrates carrier-specific connectivity measurements, asset inventories, and documented mobile-message receipts, while separating technical evidence, institutional decision rules, and requirements for subsequent agency review. title: The Stability Frontier of Interacting Binary Stars
abstract: We derive a conservation based dynamical stability frontier for interacting binary stars that distinguishes stationary mass transfer from the restoration of a perturbed contact state. We apply the formalism to conservative white dwarf binaries with direct impact accretion, coupling Roche overflow, stream angular momentum, gravitational radiation, and both stellar spin reservoirs. From the contact equations, we obtain the required orbital return torque, and an exact Jacobian identity yields the restoring gradient and an oscillatory stability boundary in the computed white dwarf domain. title: The role of turbulent jet dynamics on contrail formation from conventional and sustainable aviation fuels
abstract: Large-eddy simulations (LES) coupled with a discretised population balance equation (PBE) are used to quantify the effect of turbulence on the early stages of contrail formation (jet regime) for both conventional (soot-rich) and sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs). SAFs typically have low aromatic content which causes a shift in the dominant nucleation pathway. The contribution from soot (non-volatile particulate matter, nvPM) is reduced, while the contribution from volatile particulate matter (vPM) is increased. title: Darcy plume oscillations at low injection velocities
abstract: We numerically investigate miscible buoyancy-driven Darcy plumes at low injection velocities. Below a critical injection velocity, the steady plume becomes unstable and develops periodic oscillations. Approaching the critical velocity, the oscillation amplitude vanishes while the frequency remains finite at the critical point, consistent with a supercritical Hopf bifurcation, whereas at lower injection velocities increasingly complex dynamics emerge. title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
abstract: This paper presents a computational model integrating transmural drug transport, smooth muscle cell contraction, nonlinear anisotropic material behavior, and residual stresses to investigate the effects of calcium channel blockers~(CCBs) on local stress distributions in atherosclerotic arteries. The balance of linear momentum is coupled with a three-dimensional reaction-diffusion equation for the drug transport. title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
abstract: Coding agents built to repair software now write, test, and repair programs for robots, laboratories, and industrial controllers. Unlike in software engineering, no test suite comes with the code. Whether a program works must be established by running it on a robot, in a physics simulator, or through the policies it helps to train, and such evidence is costly to obtain and can itself be wrong. As these agents take on more physical tasks, how their programs are judged matters as much as how they are written. title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
abstract: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. title: Analytical formulae for planet-planet or moon-moon tides
abstract: Almost negligible among the solar system planets, mutual tides raised by a secondary on another secondary orbiting the same primary may gain increased importance in tightly packed systems, e.g., between the components of close-in exoplanetary systems or between the moons of gas giants. In this work, we derive an analytical formula for the planet-planet tidal potential and for the effect of mutual tides on the rotational and orbital evolution of moons or planets in a coplanar configuration. title: And yet it moves - or does it? Spurious drifts at equilibrium
abstract: When diffusion depends on the state of a system, the drift measured from its trajectories contains a spurious part unrelated to forces. At equilibrium, particles can then appear to sediment, repel each other, even rotate - the same way whether the movie is played forward or backward. Drifts are conditional averages, not currents: they carry meaning only together with a consistently inferred diffusion tensor. Paired with the wrong one, they make passive particles look active. I show how to infer spurious drifts from trajectory moments alone, enabling thermodynamically consistent inference.

title: Precision Muon Physics
abstract: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. title: N -phase flow simulations using X-Mesh and an explicit marker interface representation
abstract: We present a marker-based X-Mesh framework for incompressible N-phase flow simulations with sharp, explicitly tracked interfaces. The interface is represented by Lagrangian marker chains, while the computational mesh is deformed so that selected mesh edges conform to the tracked geometry without changing mesh connectivity. This combination preserves the advantages of body-fitted finite element discretizations while allowing highly distorted and nearly degenerated elements to capture fine interfacial features on relatively coarse meshes without requiring mesh refinement. title: Radial Evolution of a Corotating Interaction Region from a High-Resolution MHD Simulation
abstract: Corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are large-scale structures formed by fast--slow solar wind interaction, playing a crucial role in heliospheric dynamics and space weather. However, the evolution of individual CIRs and their full three-dimensional morphology remain poorly understood. We investigate the radial evolution of a single CIR using a high-resolution simulation combined with a backmapping method. title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
abstract: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

Transferable Data-Driven Hydrodynamic Variability-Based Stability Assessment for Marine Renewable Energy Site Selection: A Case Study in Spanish Waters
abstract: Early-stage planning of floating marine renewable energy infrastructures can benefit from identifying areas with favorable hydrodynamic conditions. Hydrodynamic stability assessment can support the planning of floating photovoltaic systems, offshore wind turbines, and renewable hydrogen production facilities. This study presents a transferable, data-driven multivariate framework that quantifies hydrodynamic variability to identify areas of higher relative hydrodynamic stability for marine renewable energy site selection. title: Dissolved oxygen gradients regulate microbial community assembly, metabolic function, and biogeochemical cycling in the southern Indian Ocean
abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a fundamental determinant in assessing the integrity and resilience of marine ecosystems. However, the influence of DO fluctuations on microbial community assembly, metabolic potentials, and interactions remain unresolved from the open ocean surface to the seafloor, especially in the Ninety East Ridge (NER) region of the southern Indian Ocean. Here, DO profiles from 30 to 1000 m water depths at six stations proximate to the NER were characterized. title: Coral and jellyfish share a mechanism for longer-lasting glow
abstract: Fluorescent proteins derived from coral and jellyfish both use amino acid residues to extend their fluorescent lifetimes.

title: No evidence of elevated mercury in sessile coastal biota exposed to Greenland glacial runoff
abstract: Melting glaciers have been claimed to be a significant and unaccounted-for source of mercury (Hg) in Greenland, raising concerns for communities, ecosystem health, and economics. Here we demonstrate, however, consistently low Hg concentrations in sessile organisms across >100 km spatial gradients and decadal time scales in three Southwest Greenland fjords exposed to glacial melt. Average Hg concentrations ranged 21.6–53.4 ng g −1 dw in the blue mussel Mytilus edulis , <7 ng g −1 dw in the macroalga Fucus vesiculosus , and 5.7–20.2 ng g −1 dw in Ascophyllum nodosum . title: Hydrographic and sea ice gradients shape benthic ecosystem functioning through sediment characteristics and benthic functional structure in Nares Strait, Canadian Arctic
abstract: Rapid changes in Arctic sea ice conditions are altering the quantity, quality, and timing of organic matter reaching the seafloor, thereby reshaping benthic ecosystem functioning. However, the exact mechanisms linking sea ice variability, benthic community structure, and sediment biogeochemical processes remain poorly understood. With its multiple forms and ages of sea ice, Nares Strait in the Canadian Arctic offers a unique natural laboratory for investigating how environmental gradients and benthic community structure jointly regulate benthic ecosystem functioning. title: Education for Sustainable Development in Coastal Environments: An International Service-Learning and Research-Based Learning Case Study
abstract: An international higher education collaboration between the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and the University of La Guajira was implemented to strengthen local capacities for coastal risk analysis in Riohacha (Colombia) through an integrated educational approach that combines Education for Sustainable Development, Service-Learning, and Research-Based Learning. The intervention consisted of a four day, inquiry driven course that linked classroom sessions, computer lab practice, and fieldwork. title: The fate of wastewater-derived pathogenic viruses in estuarine and coastal waters
abstract: Sewage-derived viruses are prevalent in rivers, estuaries and coasts, potentially posing a serious risk to human health. However, their environmental fate remains difficult to predict due to complex hydrodynamic processes and virus-specific behaviours. Our aim was to develop an integrated experimental-modelling framework to quantify viral dispersal, decay, and exposure risk across the river-estuary-coastal continuum. title: Low‐Velocity Impact Response and Damage Characterization of Bio‐Sandwich Composites With Montmorillonite Nanoclay
abstract: The bio‐sandwich composites have higher specific stiffness and lower weight than conventional composites under transverse loads. The sandwich composites with same‐thickness glass fiber/epoxy face sheets and a hemp fiber/epoxy core of varying thickness and montmorillonite nanoclay are fabricated using a stirrer and compression molding. title: A valley system investigation of Holocene coastal change and Irish Sea palaeogeography in Cardigan Bay, Wales, UK
abstract: Of the three substantial areas of postglacial aerial exposure on the Irish Sea shelf (Liverpool Bay, Cardigan Bay and the Bristol Channel), Cardigan Bay is the largest and the one about which we know the least. This article provides the first empirical sea level data for Cardigan Bay since the 1980s. It examines the proposition that the valleys of north Cardigan Bay were subject to a long period of marine influence that is not modelled in current palaeogeographical reconstructions. title: Remote Sensing and GIS Integration for Spatiotemporal Assessment of Environmental Deterioration and Pollution to Support Coastal Lakes Sustainability
abstract: Coastal lakes in the Mediterranean are highly sensitive ecosystems facing increasing pressure from the combined effects of anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study examined environmental changes in five Egyptian Mediterranean coastal lakes: Mariout, Edku, Burullus, Manzala, and Bardawil from 2020 to 2025, including an intermediate dataset for 2022. title: Large-scale monitoring of Earth’s tidal response on the deep seafloor using fiber-optic sensing
abstract: The understanding of the seafloor tidal response in deep-sea environments remains sparse due to the logistical challenges associated with long-term deployment of sensors in such extreme environments. Here, we demonstrate the capability of Distributed Acoustic Sensing technology to monitor tidal deformation in the deep sea. title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
abstract: The ocean biological pump regulates atmospheric carbon dioxide, yet Earth system projections may miss how plankton food-web complexity shapes its response to warming. Here we use a single Earth system model framework with three progressively more complex plankton ecosystems to show that ecological complexity amplifies the climate-driven weakening of future carbon export. abstract: Current and projected ocean conditions under climate change necessitate an understanding of coral holobiont resilience, factors contributing to host survival during marine heatwaves (MHWs), and how corals can recover after MHWs subside. It is especially important to understand how MHWs may interact with local stressors such as nutrient pollution and overfishing. title: Groundwater evolution modeling using multiple dating methods in the Pacific coastal area of Shimokita Peninsula, Japan
abstract: Groundwater age is a key constraint for understanding long-term groundwater flow and evaluating the safety of the geological disposal of radioactive waste. This study reassessed groundwater ages and reconstructed groundwater evolution in the coastal sedimentary sequence of the Rokkasho area, Shimokita Peninsula, northeastern Japan, using multiple environmental tracers. title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
abstract: The growth of marine microbial communities drives ocean biogeochemical cycles, yet the growth rates of individual species remain poorly understood. Copiotrophic bacteria, such as Vibrio species, are thought to live a feast-and-famine existence, as their capacity for rapid growth contrasts with their typically low abundance. title: An integrated shipboard workflow for rapid radiocesium determination in seawater: Validation at open-ocean background levels
abstract: Rapid determination of radiocesium ( 137 Cs and 134 Cs) in seawater is crucial for routine marine monitoring and nuclear emergency response. However, quantifying 137 Cs in the open ocean requires large-volume preconcentration and low-background laboratory analysis, delaying quantification until after a research cruise concludes. title: Summer subsurface temperature variability in the percolation zone of southwest Greenland: high resolution observations of the top meter of firn
abstract: As surface melt affects larger areas of the Greenland Ice Sheet, quantifying the energetic processes governing the near-surface firn becomes increasingly important. This work characterizes subsurface temperature and its temporal variability in the upper meter of firn in the percolation zone in southwest Greenland from two months of observations in summer 2024. We provide novel methods for identifying the snow surface height from high resolution (2 cm and 15 min) temperature string measurements and further correct the observations for apparent biases from solar heating. title: Biogeochemical fluxes and tracers of nutrients and organic matter from urban stormwater and rivers to the coastal ocean of Metro Vancouver, Canada
abstract: Coastal marine ecosystems are increasingly impacted by urbanization-driven changes in land-derived organic matter (OM) and macronutrient inputs. Understanding these impacts requires quantification of inputs and the ability to trace them in the environment. This study quantified stormwater and urban river biogeochemistry in Vancouver, British Columbia (Canada). title: Spatial assessment of chemical contamination and marine litter for cetacean exposure risk in the Pelagos Sanctuary (North-Western Mediterranean Sea)
abstract: The Pelagos Sanctuary (north-western Mediterranean Sea) is a key cetacean conservation area, yet pollution stress there remains underestimated because data are fragmented across matrices and species. The present study developed a geographic information system (GIS)-based framework integrating anthropogenic contamination, including marine litter, and cetacean distributions, to identify areas and species with elevated exposure potential. title: Seasonal reorganization of marine metazoan communities in the Yellow Sea revealed by combined bulk and environmental DNA metabarcoding
abstract: The semi-enclosed Yellow Sea is a temperate continental shelf ecosystem characterized by strong seasonal hydrographic variability and indirect influence from Kuroshio-derived warm currents. Such environmental variability may drive seasonal restructuring of marine communities, yet detecting these dynamics at high taxonomic resolution remains challenging using conventional sampling approaches. title: An integrated pre-development environmental baseline for the NEOM coastal region (Saudi Arabian Red Sea)
abstract: Coastal mega-developments require robust environmental baselines to distinguish natural biogeochemical variability from emerging anthropogenic pressures. Establishing pre-development reference conditions is essential for detecting future impacts on marine ecosystems, yet comprehensive baseline datasets remain scarce in rapidly developing coastal regions. title: Contributions of Hydrochemistry to Identifying the Source of Salinity in the Continental Terminal Aquifer of the Coastal Sedimentary Basin, South Togo
abstract: The Continental Terminal aquifer is a strategic resource for the drinking water supply of Togo’s coastal sedimentary basin, but it has exhibited a concerning salinization in recent years. This study aims to identify the sources of salinity and hydrogeochemical processes that contribute to its mineralization using an integrated hydrochemical approach based on binary diagrams, combined with multivariate statistical analysis and GIS. title: Range Expansion or Northward Shift? Assessing the Spatial Dynamics of the Almaco Jack Seriola rivoliana in the Mediterranean Sea and Eastern Atlantic
abstract: Climate-driven ocean warming is altering the distribution of many marine species, but records at higher latitudes do not necessarily demonstrate a directional shift in the population core. This study evaluates the spatial dynamics of the carangid fish Seriola rivoliana in the Mediterranean Sea and European Atlantic. Morphometric, meristic, and molecular characteristics of new specimens captured in the Strait of Sicily are also described. title: Endogenous deiodinase-mediated conversion of T4 to T3 stimulates calcification in corals
abstract: In vertebrates, thyroid hormones (TH) are synthesized predominantly as the prohormone thyroxine (T4), which is converted into biologically active triiodothyronine (T3) by iodothyronine deiodinases (DIOs). Although iodothyronines have been detected across several invertebrate lineages, their origin, activation mechanisms, and physiological roles, particularly in early-diverging metazoans, remain poorly understood. abstract: This study assessed the structural condition, biodiversity, trophic organization and coral restoration potential of the Water Lily and Emily shipwrecks off Trou aux Biches, between 2017 and 2019. Underwater visual censuses, benthic surveys and coral nursery monitoring were conducted to evaluate the ecological role of the shipwrecks as artificial reef systems. Fish surveys recorded 90 taxa, with total abundance ranging from 22,070 to 31,652 individuals. title: MeshVision: An Integrated Workflow for Underwater 3D Reconstruction and Quantitative Analysis
abstract: This paper presents MeshVision, an open-source software tool for generating georeferenced, scaled, and textured 3D models of underwater environments from still images or video. title: Livelihoods of small-scale fishing communities depend on coastal wetlands
abstract: Small-scale coral reef fisheries are a critical resource supporting the livelihoods and food security of tropical coastal communities. Management of these fisheries is generally focused on adult fish and their associated habitats, ignoring the juvenile and sub-adult phases and their associated habitats. title: Occurrence of potentially harmful phytoplankton and phycotoxins in eastern oysters within a coastal Alabama estuary
abstract: Phytoplankton can affect estuarine organisms through nutrient depletion, physical damage, and phycotoxin production, yet exposure risks associated with changing phytoplankton assemblages remain poorly understood. The eastern oyster ( Crassostrea virginica ), a keystone estuarine species and sentinel of ecosystem health, has experienced unexplained mortality events that have been hypothesized to be linked to harmful phytoplankton exposure. title: ASEAN Regional Payment Connectivity and The Reconfiguration of Financial Dependence
abstract: ASEAN’s efforts to strengthen regional financial autonomy through Regional Payment Connectivity (RPC) have raised questions about how financial dependence is changing within the region. Although RPC aims to reduce reliance on external payment mechanisms, closer regional integration may also create new patterns of asymmetric interdependence. This study examines how ASEAN RPC reshapes financial dependence among member states. title: Assessing River Flood Vulnerability in Niger Delta Coastal Communities: A Hydro-Meteorological Analysis
abstract: Flooding is one of the major hazards in the coastal areas of Niger Delta State, Nigeria, due to the topography and climatic status. This paper examines flood vulnerability in the riverine communities of Rivers, Delta, and Bayelsa States using seven hydro-meteorological parameters: rainfall, sea level rise, river discharge, river flow velocity, temperature, wind speed, and elevation. abstract: This study examined short-term changes in science awareness after undergraduate physics students took part in a virtual reality (VR)-supported photoelectric-effect laboratory at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Malaysia (n = 29), and Universitas Muhammadiyah Makassar (Unismuh), Indonesia (n = 34). abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs in the Eastern Tropical Pacific are increasingly affected by environmental stressors that may compromise coral health and promote disease. However, the health status of coral communities across the Gulf of California remains poorly understood, particularly within the Parque Nacional Zona Marina del Archipiélago Espíritu Santo, where information on coral health and its association with local environmental conditions is limited. abstract: Given the complex nature of Marine Functional Connectivity (MFC) science, MFC experts sit in a unique position to lead discussions on strategies for ocean planning and management that would turn “paper parks” into effective conservation areas. title: The Promoting Effect of Intermittent Fin Oscillation on the Directional Escape Behavior of Robotic Dolphins
abstract: This paper explores how intermittent fin oscillation can enhance the directional escape behavior of robotic dolphins. As underwater robots take on increasingly important roles in areas like marine research, environmental surveillance, and rescue operations, the limitations of conventional propulsion systems such as high energy use and disruptive noise are becoming more apparent. abstract: Coastal fortifications form part of cultural landscapes whose preservation depends on the condition of both the structures and their surrounding environments. This study examines 22 historical coastal fortifications in the Algarve, southern Portugal, by combining documentary research, qualitative observations, historical cartography and geographic information system (GIS) analysis. title: Melanodrymia biconica sp. nov. (Gastropoda, Melanodrymiidae) from hydrothermal vents in the Indian Ocean
abstract: The gastropod Melanodrymia biconica sp. nov. (Melanodrymiidae) is described as a new species from abyssal hydrothermal vent habitats on the Central and Southeast Indian Ridge (Indian Ocean). It is a small species that is characterised by its biconical outline with a rounded peripheral keel and a large spiral chord at the base of the shell. abstract: The Tianzuo Hydrothermal Field (THF) on the Southwest Indian Ridge is a dormant ultramafic-hosted seafloor massive sulfide (UM-SMS) deposit, yet its micro- to nanoscale Au mineralization mechanisms remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrate FIB–TEM, SEM, and EDS analyses to characterize the occurrence and nanoscale textures of Au-bearing phases in THF sulfides. title: Key areas for krill-mediated carbon sequestration in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Antarctic krill plays a key role in the ocean carbon cycle, particularly in carbon sequestration, and also supports an important commercial fishery with around 400,000 tons of krill harvested each year. Yet, the spatiotemporal distribution of the krill-mediated carbon sequestration across the Southern Ocean has been under-investigated. abstract: Fishery-related mortality is a major anthropogenic threat to marine megafauna, and gear-specific estimates are essential for effective conservation management of populations. abstract: Canopy-forming macroalgae, particularly Cystoseira sensu lato species, are key habitat-forming organisms and important indicators of ecological status (ES) in Mediterranean coastal ecosystems. abstract: The One Environmental Health framework recognizes the interconnectedness of ecosystem health, wildlife health and human health when studying environmental pollutants. Microplastics are widespread environmental pollutants with increasing potential to cause adverse health outcomes. Marine mammals, sea turtles and humans are exposed to the same microplastic profiles because we share the environment and routes of exposure, including inhalation and ingestion. abstract: Candidatus Nitrosomaritimum is a widespread genus of ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) in coastal and marine sediments. However, its ecological distribution remains poorly resolved because it is not represented as a distinct genus in the widely used 16S rRNA gene reference databases and lineage-specific quantification tools are lacking. Here, we combined SILVA 16S rRNA gene sequences with sequences extracted from GTDB genomes and metagenome-assembled genomes to reconstruct a refined phylogeny of the family Nitrosopumilaceae. title: Three More Poecilogonous Sacoglossans: Why Is Egg‐Size Dimorphism Generally Rare Except in One Lineage of Sea Slugs?
abstract: Theory and meta-analyses suggest changes from feeding to non-feeding larvae in marine animals may be an adaptation to conditions such as ocean productivity or circulation, but testing such predictions is difficult because intraspecific dimorphism in larval type (poecilogony) is rare. In gastropods, known examples are three caenogastropods and six heterobranch sea slugs, including five of ∼400 species in clade Sacoglossa. abstract: Ensuring access to safe water in coastal Bangladesh is increasingly challenging due to salinity intrusion, climate variability, and limited freshwater infrastructure. However, the interactions among source accessibility, water-use practices, and water quality remain insufficiently understood. This study integrated household survey (N = 1,085), laboratory water-quality assessment, and GIS-based spatial analysis to assess water demand, sources, quality, accessibility, and seasonal practices in three coastal unions of Bangladesh: Chila, Ishwaripur, and Charduany. title: An expert-derived content blueprint for ocean, climate, and biodiversity education in Mexico
abstract: Ocean literacy is central to sustainable ocean stewardship, yet existing frameworks are often too general for context-specific curriculum design. Here, we contribute specifically to the content dimension of ocean literacy by identifying candidate priority topics for basic education in Mexico from the perspective of an expert panel. title: Holocene morphogenesis of an estuary–island system along a structurally influenced passive margin, northern Brazil
abstract: Passive-margin estuaries are commonly interpreted as products of relative sea-level (RSL) fluctuations, whereas their islands are generally explained by internal sedimentary accretion. abstract: This study examines the proposed use of Mediterranean seawater to generate hydroelectric power by directing it into a hyper-arid depression in the Libyan desert. The concept is assessed using a steady-state water-balance approach, in which the incoming seawater flow is limited by the basin’s estimated evaporation rate. The baseline scenario assumes an evaporation rate of 7.2 mm/day, a basin surface area of approximately 7,800 km², a continuous flow rate of 650 m³/s, and an effective hydraulic head of 50 m. abstract: Estuarine areas provide critical ecosystem services by supporting biodiversity, maintaining water quality, and supplying seafood resources. Anthropogenic activities can introduce harmful metals into estuarine systems, potentially threatening these services. abstract: Calcifying macroalgae play critical roles in coral reef ecosystem functioning and carbonate dynamics. However, the metabolic responses underpinning several of their ecological functions remain poorly characterized, particularly in the Red Sea. abstract: Tropical cyclones alter marine habitats and influence the behavior of many marine organisms. Along southeast Florida (USA), green ( Chelonia mydas ) and loggerhead ( Caretta caretta ) sea turtles nest in globally significant numbers from May through October, overlapping the most active months of tropical cyclone occurrence. abstract: The Faculty Management System is a web-based application developed to simplify and automate the management of faculty-related information in an educational institution. Traditional faculty management methods often involve manual paperwork, spreadsheets, and separate records, which can be time-consuming, difficult to maintain, and prone to errors. title: First record and biological data of juvenile Dosidicus gigas in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, eastern Central Pacific Ocean
abstract: The Humboldt squid, Dosidicus gigas D'Orbigny, 1835, is endemic to the eastern Pacific. Knowledge of its biology is largely limited to commercial-sized adults, leaving juveniles scarcely documented. abstract: Providing the best available data to decision makers and advisors is an essential component in evidence led recommendations. This paper presents a framework to provide accessible, quality-assured sediment contaminant data to support a transparent and defensible weight of evidence approach to decision making. We present use cases of the Sediment Management Framework (SMF) app as a tool for accessing collated and quality-checked sediment contaminant data. abstract: Introduction: Costa Rica hosts remarkable marine biodiversity, vital for conserving its marine and coastal ecosystems. However, marine macroalgae remains understudied, especially in the Área de Conservación Guanacaste (ACG). abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) are increasingly used for hydrographic surveying, environmental monitoring, ecological observation, infrastructure inspection, and underwater search. Previous studies often focus on autonomous navigation, vehicle design, platform types, or individual applications, leaving relationships among mission objectives, payloads, platform support, and data products unclear. abstract: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a key organosulfur compound in marine ecosystems, and its microbial metabolism involves multiple biosynthetic and degradative pathways that are difficult to fully resolve using conventional stepwise approaches. abstract: Although understanding of respiratory health in free‐ranging cetaceans has historically been limited, recent advances in drone technology have enabled noninvasive collection of cetaceans exhaled respiratory vapor (i.e., “blow”), offering new opportunities to study cetaceans' respiratory microbiome. This study aimed to collect blow from Tamanend's bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops erebennus ) in the Charleston Estuarine System (CES) to investigate their blow microbiome. abstract: Coastal wetlands serve as ecological security barriers and provide important ecosystem services. They are now under combined pressure from multiple human activities. To address the diverse risk types, complex impact pathways and heterogeneous ecological responses in the wetlands of the Beibu Gulf, Guangxi, this study extended the conventional Relative Risk Model (RRM) by incorporating an explicit exposure–response pathway framework linking risk sources, habitat receptors and ecological endpoints. abstract: The Southwestern Indian Ocean is a hydrographically and geologically complex area featuring prominent upwelling and deep basins separated by mid‐ocean ridges. abstract: Coral reefs are declining globally, and novel solutions, such as cryopreservation, can help secure coral biodiversity and genetic diversity. abstract: The Aegean Sea, a region of the Mediterranean Basin known for its biological diversity, remains largely unexplored in terms of its tardigrade fauna. abstract: Phytoplankton biomass is a vital indicator of ecosystem health, yet its dynamics are increasingly sensitive to thermal variability and large-scale climatic events. abstract: Marine sponges host diverse symbiotic bacteria that produce bioactive secondary metabolites with potential therapeutic applications. The rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens and biofilm associated infections needs new antimicrobial and antibiofilm agents. This study explores the culture-dependent diversity of bacteria associated with the marine sponge Callyspongia fibrosa from the coastal region of Karachi, Pakistan, and evaluates their antimicrobial, antibiofilm and anti-quorum sensing (anti-QS) activities to prioritize isolates with dual functionality. title: Genome of the precious red coral Hemicorallium imperiale provides insights into the molecular basis of axial skeleton formation in octocorals
abstract: Diverse biomineralization strategies of octocorals make these species an important model for understanding the evolution of biomineralization. However, molecular mechanisms underlying biomineralization in octocorals are poorly studied. Precious red corals, which are characterized by their fully calcified axial skeletons and striking red coloration, are ideal for the investigation of the molecular mechanisms underpinning the calcification and pigmentation processes in octocorals. In this study, we generated a high-quality chromosome-level genome of the precious red coral Hemicorallium imperiale
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Metabolomic signature of adiposity in preschool children: findings from the CORALS cohort
abstract: Childhood obesity is increasingly recognized as a condition characterized by excess adiposity and early metabolic dysregulation. However, evidence on metabolomic alterations during the preschool years remains limited. This study aimed to characterize circulating metabolomic profiles associated with body mass index (BMI) and examine their relationships with body composition. This cross-sectional analysis included 1200 children aged 3–6 years from the Childhood Obesity Risk Assessment Longitudinal Study (CORALS), of whom 1110 had complete covariate data. institutions: Spanish Biomedical Research Centre in Physiopathology of Obesity and Nutrition

title: A giant thallus of Ulva fenestrata documented from Pillar Point, California, USA

title: Effect of Recycled Glass Fiber on the Mechanical Properties and Durability of Epoxy Composites in Distilled Water and Seawater
abstract: The increasing retirement of wind turbine blades has created an urgent need for the high‐value utilization of recycled glass fibers. However, the effects of recycled glass fibers on the mechanical performance and long‐term durability of epoxy composites remain insufficiently understood. This study systematically investigated the effects of recycled glass fiber incorporation on long‐term properties of epoxy composites under distilled water and seawater environments at 40°C, 60°C, and 80°C. institutions: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

title: The Sea in the Mosaic Floors of the Roman Empire: Its Role in Cultural Interaction. The Mosaics of the Roman Villa of São Simão, Penela, Portugal
abstract: Over the past ten years of archaeological research, the São Simão Archaeological Site in Penela, Portugal, has revealed the presence of a Roman villa occupied between late 2nd/early 3rd century AD and mid-5th century AD.The remains found bear witness to several reconstructions/renovations in the pars urbana, where twenty-two mosaic panels have been identified to this date, seem to accompany the different architectural reforms, with evident changes in the decorative programmes.The representation of the sea is associated with patterns that remind us of the illusion of the movement of water, the

title: Fish and macrobenthic diversity and community assembly patterns in the Jiuduansha Wetland based on eDNA metabarcoding
abstract: Estuarine wetlands are critical zones of land-sea interaction that play vital roles in maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. As the only remaining natural estuarine wetland in the Yangtze River Estuary, Jiuduansha's fish and macrobenthic diversity and community assembly mechanisms remain poorly understood due to limitations of traditional survey methods in protected areas. We conducted eDNA metabarcoding surveys at 11 sampling sites (6 intertidal zone and 5 riverine sites) in the Jiuduansha Wetland Nature Reserve during May and July of 2023-2024, combined with measurement of envi
institutions: Shanghai Estuarine & Coastal Science Research Center

title: Short spatial mooring-tilt variations from deep Mediterranean observations
abstract: Interaction between energy-abundant mesoscale eddies and internal waves can lead to convection-turbulence generation and may prove important for deep-sea life and circulation. However, the size of scales of interacting flows is not well known. In this paper, a diagnostic tool of tilt is tested near the single top-buoyancy of 40 mooring lines 9.5 m apart horizontally and compared with 50-m scale relative vorticity and waterflow above a 2,500-m deep flat Northwestern-Mediterranean seafloor.
