title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. title: Climate change vulnerability, adaptive strategies, and food security of small-scale fishers in marine protected areas (MPAs) of the Island Garden City of Samal
abstract: Currently, there are no updated assessments on the climate vulnerability and food security status of the communities located near or hosting marine protected areas in Samal. To address this question, we assessed the vulnerability and food security status of small-scale fishing communities located near or at the community-managed marine protected areas (MPAs) in the Island Garden City of Samal, Philippines. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were gathered from N = 90 fisher respondents in barangay Aundanao, Tagbaobo, and Tambo. Fishers were interviewed in community fish landing sites or in th

title: Visualizing Heritage: Culturally Accurate Storytelling in Pakistani Mythology and Folklore
abstract: The research recognizes the power of visuals and imagery in storytelling and acknowledges the importance of cultural accuracy in portraying mythological and folkloric elements. By employing culturally appropriate visuals, this research seeks to foster a stronger connection and familiarity between artists, storytellers, and their audience, ultimately reinforcing cultural identity and shared values in Pakistan. journal: Lahore Institute for Research and Analysis Journal

title: Hidden parasites in diatom blooms: high infection rates of Leptocylindrus danicus by the oomycete Miracula nipponica
abstract: Parasitic fungi and fungal-like organisms are increasingly recognized as key players influencing diatom dynamics and carbon fluxes in aquatic ecosystems; however, their diversity and ecological roles in coastal environments remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the diversity of fungi and fungal-like organisms over an annual cycle, encompassing spring diatom blooms, in Sagami Bay, Japan, using 18S rDNA metabarcoding, and quantified parasitic infection of diatoms during the spring bloom of May 2022 using fluorescence microscopy and single-spore PCR. title: A three‐tier screening pipeline for identifying plant immune inducers and growth promoters from marine microbial metabolite libraries
abstract: BACKGROUND: Plant immune inducers and growth-promoting biostimulants provide promising tools for sustainable crop management, but their development is limited by the shortage of bioactive natural products with agricultural relevance. Marine microorganisms from diverse habitats, including deep-sea environments, represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse secondary metabolites. This study aimed to establish a screening pipeline to identify marine microbial metabolites with plant immune-inducing and growth-promoting activities. title: Seasonal trends in the zooplankton community in the NW Arabian Gulf
abstract: Seasonal trends in zooplankton community composition and abundance were investigated in the Northwestern Arabian Gulf from 2013 to 2016. A total of 72 zooplankton taxa were found: 29 copepod taxa, 18 types of meroplanktonic larvae, 16 non-crustacean taxa, and 9 other crustacean taxa. Copepods dominated the community throughout the year (>65% of total zooplankton abundance), with small copepods such as Paracalanus spp, Acartia pacifica, Oithona spp, and Euterpina acutifrons contributing most of the abundance. title: Apparent Rose Bengal Test Seroreactivity and Geographic Distribution of Reactive Goats from Smallholder Farms in Coastal Ecuador
abstract: Brucellosis is an important zoonotic disease affecting livestock productivity and public health, particularly in smallholder production systems with limited biosecurity practices. This study aimed to estimate apparent Rose Bengal Test (RBT) seroreactivity and describe the geographic distribution of RBT-reactive goats in Membrillal parish, Jipijapa canton, Ecuador. A cross-sectional study was conducted from September to December 2025, including 101 reproductive-age female goats from nine participating smallholder farms. Serum samples were screened using the RBT as a presumptive serological assa
journal: Journal of Animal Health and Production

title: Methane and nitrous oxide concentrations and sea–air fluxes in western Long Island Sound, a eutrophic urban estuary: Hourly to seasonal variability
abstract: Western Long Island Sound is a seasonally hypoxic urban estuary undergoing anthropogenic change, which may influence concentrations and emissions of the potent greenhouse gases methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). To provide a benchmark of current gas distributions in this system, enabling detection of future changes and comparison with data from other estuaries worldwide, we obtained the first water column profiles of dissolved CH4 and N2O concentrations in western Long Island Sound. title: Integrated approach to groundwater quality assessment using hydrogeochemistry and GIS along the Kodaiyar river, Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu
abstract: The Kodaiyar River is an important water source of Kanyakumari and Tirunelveli Districts in Tamil Nadu. The aim of the present research is to use the hydrogeochemistry and water quality of groundwater along the Kodaiyar River to assess the suitability of drinking and agricultural purposes through integrated approach. Totally twenty-five groundwater samples were collected from bore wells and open wells along the river course and near the confluence point of the river. institutions: National Centre for Earth Science Studies

title: Presence of novel mitochondrial haplotypes in Indian Cuvier’s beaked whale, Ziphius cavirostris (Cuvier, 1823)
abstract: The Cuvier’s beaked whale ( Ziphius cavirostris ) is a pelagic marine mammal known for its elusive behavior and ecological importance as a predator in ocean ecosystems. Despite its wide distribution, records from Indian waters remain scarce. Here, we report two strandings of this species along the Tamil Nadu coast in 2024. Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) regions, including the COX region (630 bps) and cytochrome b (CYTB) (464 bps), 16S rRNA (520 bps) and 12S rRNA (420 bps), were sequenced and were found to be of two different haplotypes. title: Direct Visualization of Polarity‐Driven Carrier Redistribution in Two‐Dimensional In/CdS
abstract: The intrinsic polarization field (IPF) in wurtzite semiconductors has long been proposed as a means to regulate carrier migration in photocatalytic and optoelectronic systems. However, direct experimental visualization of polarity‐driven charge separation remains challenging because intrinsic polarization effects are often obscured by competing surface fields and structural heterogeneity, leading to long‐standing contradictions between theory and experiment. institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
abstract: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. title: Heavy Metals in Rice Fields at a Typical Southeast Coastal Industrial Site: Spatial Distribution and Toxicity Centroids with Health Risk Assessment
abstract: This study investigated heavy metals (Cd, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn) in the soil-rice system of Sanming, a typical industrial and rice-growing region in China, to analyze their spatial patterns, sources, and ecological and health risks. Standard deviation ellipses based on the geoaccumulation index (Igeo), single ecological risk index (Er) and comprehensive ecological risk index (RI) were used to visualize spatial disparities of pollution and risk. Cd was the primary pollutant with the widest distribution; its average (Igeo) reached 2.29, and roughly 80% of samples presented moderate to heavy pollution.

title: Study on Retained Bycatch in a Traditional Small‐Scale Sero Trap Fishery in Bone Bay, Indonesia
abstract: Traditional sero fisheries support coastal livelihoods in Indonesia, yet their retained bycatch remains poorly documented. This case study quantified retained‐bycatch composition, catch per unit effort (CPUE) and assemblage structure in four sero units, a small‐scale stationary trap operating in seaweed‐farming, coral‐associated, mangrove and river‐mouth settings in Bone Bay. Over 120 hauls (February–May 2024), retained non‐target catch was classified as commercial bycatch (CB) or low‐value retained bycatch (LVB). journal: New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research

title: Rule-Based Operation of a Grid-Connected Hybrid Power System in Coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Coastal communities in Bangladesh, such as Teknaf in Cox's Bazar, suffer from severe energy insecurity due to a fossil-fuel-dominated grid, long transmission lines, and chronic load shedding. This study aims to design and evaluate a grid-connected hybrid power system to improve local energy reliability, reduce grid dependence, and lower carbon emissions. A 24-hour hourly simulation was conducted using real commercial components: five 95 kW wind turbines (475 kW total), a 78.12 kWp bifacial solar PV array, a 128 kWh LiFePO₄ battery, a 100 kVA diesel generator, and bidirectional grid exchange. title: Compositionally Tuned FeNiMnCuNbAg x High‐Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles With Enhanced ROS Generation and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity
abstract: The development of multifunctional antibacterial nanomaterials is of considerable interest in combating antibiotic resistance and marine biofouling. Herein, Ag‐containing FeNiMnCuNbAgx high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA‐NPs) with tunable composition were synthesized through a non‐equilibrium arc‐discharge plasma strategy. By introducing Nb to stabilize Ag within the alloy matrix, homogeneous HEA‐NPs with adjustable Ag content were successfully obtained. title: Flipping Field Cores to Disentangle Drivers of Peat Decomposition in Drained Coastal Peatlands
abstract: Peatland drainage and rewetting trigger microbial and biogeochemical responses that impact carbon cycling and greenhouse gas emissions. The direction and magnitude of these responses depend on environmental factors and peat characteristics. This study assessed how previously oxygen‐exposed peat responds to rewetting and how deeper anoxic layers respond to further drainage, using a flipped core field experiment as a proxy. title: Southern Ocean Control on the Relationship Between AMOC Slowdown and ITCZ Shift in CMIP6 Models
abstract: Changes in the latitudinal position of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) are governed by changes in the temperature gradient between the northern and southern hemispheres. This raises the concern that a cooling of the northern hemisphere caused by a weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) may shift the ITCZ southwards and cause severe alterations of tropical precipitation. title: Variation in residency and space use among fish species at a bottom-fixed offshore wind farm: Implications for offshore wind–artisanal fisheries coexistence
abstract: The numbers of offshore wind farms (OWFs) are expanding rapidly worldwide, raising concerns about potential interactions between OWFs and coastal fisheries that share marine space. These interactions may be particularly complex in regions dominated by artisanal fisheries, where diverse fishing methods operate within the same waters. Understanding species-specific behavioral responses to turbine structures is therefore critical for evaluating the fishery implications of OWF development. title: Discourse diversity in marine protected area management: A Q-methodology analysis of an Atlantic National Park
abstract: This study applies Q methodology to examine stakeholder discourses on management actions in the marine–terrestrial Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park (Spain). A total of 182 participants from diverse actor groups were surveyed, revealing four distinct discourses: Strict Protection (48%), emphasizing ecosystem protection through visitor quota reduction and restrictions on marine activities; Ecological restoration (13%), focusing on habitat recovery, invasive species removal, and marine pollution control; Education & sustainability (12%), prioritizing environmental education, cultural her

title: Deep-water choruses originate from slope-associated biological aggregations
abstract: Evening biological chorusing of unknown origin has been reported near pelagic waters around the world, including the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. While vertically migrating deep scattering layers have been suggested as a possible source of the chorus, this is difficult to confirm without measurements of the spatial distribution of the bioacoustic sources. title: In vitro activity of a saponin-rich Chenopodium quinoa hull extract against adult Calisgus rogercresseyi
abstract: Caligus rogercresseyi is one of the main parasitic challenges affecting salmon farming in Chile, and its control depends largely on a limited number of chemical antiparasitic compounds. This study evaluated the in vitro antiparasitic activity of a standardized Chenopodium quinoa hull extract against adults of C. rogercresseyi. Adult lice were exposed for 45 min to a concentration gradient in seawater and assessed immediately and up to 48 h after transfer to clean seawater. title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
abstract: Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. title: Review of marine tapeworms (Platyhelminthes: Cestoda) from the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman: diversity, annotated host associations, checklists, and geospatial distribution
abstract: Numerous records of cestodes from diverse marine hosts have been reported from the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman; however, these data remain scattered in the literature. This review compiles and synthesizes available information on the tapeworm fauna of these two water bodies by providing parasite-host and host-parasite checklists. title: Light‐Assisted Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Seawater Electrolysis on a Core–Shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O Catalyst
abstract: Harnessing solar energy to assist water and seawater electrolysis represents a promising strategy to reduce the energy input for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its development remains challenging due to limited integration between light‐responsive catalysts and membrane electrolyzer systems. Here, we report a hierarchical core–shell Co‐P@Cu 2 O catalyst that enables efficient light‐assisted hydrogen evolution and is directly interfaced with an anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer. title: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
abstract: Quantitative analysis of sinkhole collapse hazard requires robust data in both space and time. It also needs a clear understanding of the factors and processes that contribute to observed sinkhole locations and dimensions. In many karst settings, these criteria are difficult to meet because of the millennia-long time scales over which sinkhole populations are generated and because of uncertainties around how geomorphological processes link to sinkhole dimensions. title: In-Process Application of Cellulose Nanofibrils Suited for Molded Fiber Substrates: Spreading during Pulsed Underwater Jet Deposition
abstract: Molded fiber products require PFAS-free technologies that provide oil and grease resistance. Cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) are renewable barrier materials, but conventional coating methods are generally limited to flat substrates and require separate coating and drying operations, restricting their application to three-dimensional molded fiber products. title: Anomalous terrigenous input to the continental margin of tropical western South Atlantic at the Pleistocene-Holocene transition
abstract: Continental slopes off southeastern Brazil preserve key records of terrigenous sediment transfer during the last deglaciation, yet the processes controlling these deposits remain poorly constrained. Here, we analyse four sediment cores to investigate the origin of a distinct terrigenous-rich layer (TM facies) identified across all records. Sedimentological, inorganic geochemical, and geochronological data were integrated to reconstruct the depositional history of this interval. title: Carbon fluxes in rhodoliths, coraliths and artificial substrates on tropical reefs
abstract: Understanding how calcifying benthic systems contribute to short-term carbon dynamics helps assess their role in shallow tropical ecosystems under environmental change. We compared day-to-night relative patterns of net organic carbon production and net calcification in three contrasting functional units from the Colombian Caribbean: rhodoliths, spherical free-living colonies (coraliths) of the coral Siderastrea radians , and colonized artificial substrates mimicking the rhodolith shape. title: Glyphosate and AMPA in a coastal agricultural landscape of Northwestern Mexico: sales, usage, and field-scale impact indicators
abstract: Background Glyphosate (GLP) is the most widely used herbicide worldwide, yet understanding of its environmental impacts and patterns of use remains limited. This study evaluates GLP occurrence within a coastal agricultural landscape in northwestern Mexico by combining water monitoring, sales patterns, usage proxies derived from container census data, and field-use Environmental Impact Quotient (EIQf) metrics. title: Application of linear programming methods and geoinformation technologies to justify the functional zoning of specially protected natural areas
abstract: Ensuring a balance between biodiversity conservation and economic use is a crucial objective for specially protected natural areas, which requires objective methods of land organization. The aim of the study is to develop a methodological approach to the functional zoning of SPNAs based on the integration of geoinformation technologies and linear programming methods. The tools applied include GIS modeling in QGIS (delineation of homogeneous plots, visualization of results) and an adapted transportation problem. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of soil and sediment nematode communities across fluvial and lacustrine environments in a Mediterranean coastal Wetland, Central Chile
abstract: Mediterranean coastal environments are increasingly exposed to environmental pressures, yet their ecological responses remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the structure and functionality of nematode communities in fluvial and lacustrine soils and sediments from a coastal wetland and its tributary in central Chile. Nematode communities responded to spatial gradients and seasonal variation, primarily associated with changes in pH, water content, total organic carbon, and available phosphorus. title: From User Needs to Design Choices: A Method for User-Centered Design of Natural Hazards Visualizations
abstract: Communicating natural hazards forecasts and models frequently relies on visual products such as charts, maps, and infographics. The framework of user-centered design can result in products that meet the needs of their users. While numerous methods exist for the elicitation of users’ needs, there are few published methods for how to translate user needs into concrete choices when designing visual products for natural hazards. title: Structural and linguistic barriers to early warning system accessibility among coastal fisherfolk in a typhoon-prone Philippine province
abstract: Typhoons kill hundreds of people in the Philippines yearly — predominantly in coastal fishing communities where the gap between the existence of early warning systems and their effective reach into vulnerable populations is widest. This study examines why that gap persists by investigating the weather information knowledge, utilization, and perceived outcomes among 320 fisherfolk across 18 barangays in Kawayan, Biliran Province, one of the most typhoon-exposed island municipalities in Eastern Visayas. title: Long-term convergence in global fisheries catch composition across Large Marine Ecosystems: A Bayesian compositional data analysis
abstract: Marine ecosystems around the world have undergone major transformations driven by overfishing, climate change, globalization, and technological advances. These processes have altered not only total fisheries catches, but also the relative composition of what is landed. We assessed whether fisheries catches across Large Marine Ecosystems (LMEs) have become more similar over time from a compositional perspective. title: From performance to protection: how to evaluate technical viability and environmental aspects of biodegradable polymers, study of polyhydroxybutyrate for marine save applications
abstract: The accumulation of persistent plastics in marine environments causes damage in marine ecosystem, being entanglement and ingestion the pathways to mortality effects of 90 % on marine organisms. This highlights the need for materials with reduced ecological burdens to be implemented in products for the marine industry. title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
abstract: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. title: Distinct microbial response to organic matter from nitrogen-starved and virus-infected phytoplankton
abstract: When phytoplankton die they release dissolved organic matter (DOM) that feeds co-occurring heterotrophic bacteria. We show that death due to phage infection and nitrogen starvation result in different changes to the macromolecular composition of Prochlorococcus, a globally abundant marine cyanobacterium, and that the resulting DOM elicits different microbial responses. title: Life cycle assessment of marine biodiversity restoration: Case study of European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis) in Nora Lagoon
abstract: Marine ecosystem restoration is increasingly recognized as a key strategy to reverse biodiversity loss and support the recovery of ecosystem services. However, the environmental burdens generated by restoration activities are rarely quantified. This study investigates whether Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) can support the design and management of environmentally sustainable marine restoration interventions. title: Holocene otoliths reveal recent body-size increase in a non-commercial fish species
abstract: Declines in body size are considered a common response of marine ectotherms to global warming, yet evidence remains inconsistent and is scarce for non-commercial species. Moreover, the lack of pristine, pre-industrial baselines limits our ability to assess whether modern changes exceed natural variability. Here, we reconstruct growth, lifespan and body-size variation in the non-commercial black goby, Gobius niger, over the last 8000 years in the northern Adriatic Sea, using morphometric measurements and sclerochronological age estimates from radiocarbon-dated fossil and modern otoliths. title: Stepwise evolution of composite phenotypes underlies the emergence of photo-endosymbiosis
abstract: Photo-endosymbiosis is a major evolutionary innovation considered to underpin the ecological success of tropical coral reefs. Yet, photo-endosymbiosis is an evolutionary endpoint involving multiple traits. Reconstructing its evolutionary trajectory and the underlying adaptations requires disentangling these traits, but few photosynthetic systems contain this diversity of traits and necessary resources to resolve the evolutionary pathway. title: Bridging technology and justice: reconsidering reverse osmosis for just and sustainable water systems in coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Salinity intrusion in coastal Bangladesh has reduced the reliability of conventional drinking-water sources and encouraged the expansion of reverse osmosis (RO) systems. We examine RO here not simply as a desalination infrastructure but as a socio-technical water service whose outcomes depend on access, governance, energy, infrastructure, and environmental management. title: Signals of broad-scale connectivity and cryptic population subdivision in the silky shark Carcharhinus falciformis
abstract: In highly mobile marine predators, extensive dispersal capacity can mask weak or cryptic population structure. The silky shark ( Carcharhinus falciformis ) is a globally distributed pelagic species characterized by high mobility and complex life-history behaviors. Despite intense fishing pressure throughout much of its range, its population structure and connectivity remain incompletely understood. abstract: Accurate detection of saxitoxin (STX) in marine ecosystems remains severely hindered by matrix interference, demanding robust and reliable sensing platforms. Herein, we report a label-free electrochemical aptasensor for sensitive STX detection based on a target-induced strand displacement and competitive hybridisation strategy. title: Visualization and Quantitative Structural Analysis of Carbohydrate Moieties in Aspergillus niger Biofilms Using Fluorescent-Labeled Lectins
abstract: Aspergillus niger is a filamentous fungus that adheres to different substrate surfaces and forms biofilms consisting of dense hyphal networks embedded in a self-produced gelatinous matrix composed of an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS). The EPS mainly contains exopolysaccharides. The objective of this study was to visualize and assess the different exopolysaccharide structures in this EPS using a combination of two different fluorescent-labeled lectin probes, Erythrina cristagalli (ECA)-FITC and Canavalia ensiformis (Con A)_TRITC. title: Quantifying the role of accelerated sea level rise in the declining health of a biogenic Caribbean mangrove forest
abstract: A recent remote sensing study of the Pitahaya Mangrove Forest (PMF) of southwestern Puerto Rico identified a nearly two decade (2006–2023) long decline in vegetation health, as measured by Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). That study attributed the adverse trend to the combined effects of 1) an increase in the pace of relative sea level rise post-2006 and 2) acute damage from recent weather events, specifically a drought (2015) and multiple hurricane impacts (2017–2022). title: Syntropic infrastructure for regenerative urban metabolic reorganization in an Atlantic island city
abstract: Urban climate vulnerability is increasingly associated with ecological fragmentation, thermal amplification, hydrological disruption, and declining ecosystem functionality across densely urbanized territories. This study proposes syntropic infrastructure as a regenerative urban framework capable of reorganizing ecological, hydrological, and thermal regulation processes through multiscalar spatial connectivity. title: Air cavities as the primary drag-reduction mechanism in a superhydrophobic sphere
abstract: Precise control over air cavity generation in liquids is critical in numerous underwater marine systems, where cavity formation can largely reduce fluid resistance and minimize energy consumption. However, how the instability of the three-phase contact line at the microscopic scale induces the formation of macroscopic air cavities and thereby achieves drag reduction has not yet been fully elucidated. title: Catabolite activator protein and quorum sensing cross-control group behaviors in Vibrio campbellii
abstract: Vibrio species adapt to different niches by sensing and responding to environmental signals such as nutrients, host cues, and quorum sensing autoinducers. Vibrio campbellii uses the master quorum sensing transcription factor LuxR to control the expression of hundreds of genes at high cell density. Furthermore, many gamma-proteobacteria use the global transcription factor catabolite activator protein (CAP) to control numerous physiologically relevant pathways, many of which are also modulated by quorum sensing, such as competence, biofilm formation, and carbon metabolism. title: Optimizing Prefabricated Temporary Housing Selection for Immediate Evacuation of Life-Threatening Informal Buildings in Egypt: A Multi-Criteria Logistical and Climatic Framework
abstract: This research introduces and proposes an integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) model that can be used to find optimal prefabricated structural systems in temporary housing for informal settlement redevelopment projects in Egypt. The framework combines aspects of the three sustainability axes (environmental, social, and economic) and regional spatial requirements to ensure sufficient on-site accommodation and reduce socio-economic disruption due to displacement. title: Using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 data to assess mangrove health in Ha Tinh province
abstract: Mangrove forests are unique ecological systems that consist of tree species that exist solely in saltwater and brackish water and coastal regions of tropical and subtropical areas. They provide important ecological services, protecting the coast from storms and against natural disasters caused by climate change. The research conducted in Ha Tinh Province utilized Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and vegetation indices to determine mangrove locations and assess their forest health status through 3 years of 2022, 2024, and 2026. title: Artificial skyglow at night disrupts chronobiology and physiology in Crassostrea gigas
abstract: Artificial skyglow at night (ASAN) is widespread in coastal environments, with consequences beginning to be highlighted but still understudied. Long-term ASAN field studies are needed to better understand the real challenge that nocturnal light poses to coastal organisms. To fill this gap, we investigated during one year in Arcachon Bay (France), ASAN’s impact on the oysters’ biological rhythms and major physiological parameters: behavior, growth, and gametogenesis. title: Raising mountains for a habitable Earth
abstract: The formation of mountain belts (orogens) elevates rocks above sea level, making them available for chemical weathering and altering the composition of the atmosphere and oceans, which in turn control habitability. Peak-metamorphic pressures recorded by crustal rocks buried in orogens increased between 2.7 to 2.2 and 0.8 to 0.7 billion years ago, indicating that rocks could be buried deeper and that orogens could grow substantially thicker after each of these periods. title: Integrating psychosocial factors with geospatial analytics to assess community climate resilience
abstract: Conventional climate adaptation strategies emphasize infrastructure, hazard modelling, and ecosystem management while underestimating psychological processes that shape how communities perceive and respond to climatic risks. Cognitive appraisal, emotional attachment, and behavioural engagement fundamentally influence preparedness, adaptation, and recovery. This study introduces GeoPsyche Futures , an interdisciplinary framework that integrates psychological indicators with geospatial analytics to map community resilience in a holistic, human entered way. title: Integrative taxonomy and whole genome sequencing of two new isopod species of the genus Notopais Hodgson, 1910 (Crustacea, Malacostraca) from the Southern Ocean
abstract: The genus Notopais Hodgson, 1910 is distributed in the Southern Hemisphere and comprises a total of 11 species. In the present study, we describe two new species of the genus, Notopais cryophila sp. nov. and Notopais polaris sp. nov. using integrative taxonomy. The two species can be easily identified and distinguished from the other Notopais species by the spinal and tubercular pattern on the dorsal surface of their pereonites. abstract: The transport of particles in density-stratified fluids is a ubiquitous feature of natural environments. In the ocean, for example, particles and marine snow move through water columns with pronounced density variations arising from temperature and salinity gradients. Such stratification can significantly modify particle rise or settling rates and promote accumulation near sharp density transitions. title: Little Islandscapes of the Saronic Project 2024–2025: A preliminary report
abstract: This article presents a preliminary report on the first two field seasons (2024–2025) of the Little Islandscapes of the Saronic Project(LISP), an archaeological survey conducted by the Swedish Institute at Athens. The project investigates the long-term dynamics of human activity across the small islands and islets of the Saronic Gulf, focusing on Agistri and nearby uninhabited islets of Doroussa and Panagitsa in autumn 2024 and spring 2025. title: Insensitivity of the North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone to recent ice age cycle climate changes
abstract: The ocean’s oxygen-deficient zones are hotspots of biogeochemical reactions. An important example is water-column denitrification, a process that removes biologically available nitrogen from the ocean. Denitrification discriminates against the heavier nitrogen isotope ( 15 N) in favour of the lighter 14 N, leaving a signal of elevated 15 N/ 14 N ratio in the remaining nitrate. title: Propylene Glycol Alginate Sodium Sulfate (PSS): The First Oral Heparinoid Marine Drug—A Pharmacological and Clinical Review
abstract: Propylene glycol alginate sodium sulfate (PSS) is the first oral heparinoid marine drug, derived from brown algal alginic acid and marketed in 1986. Its core pharmacology, including anticoagulation, lipid-lowering, microcirculation improvement, and neuroprotection, makes it an affordable oral option for chronic ischemic cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. title: Objectscapes on the Frontier: Diachronic Transformations of Fish Iconography in the Mosaics of the Middle Euphrates
abstract: This article investigates the diachronic transformation of fish and marine iconography across the mosaic pavements of the Middle Euphrates basin, spanning the Hellenistic, Roman, and Late Antique periods. Employing the conceptual framework of ‘objectscapes,’ the study examines how circulating visual repertoires actively constituted regional identity and localized artistic agency along the provincial frontier. abstract: Sabkha dynamics in the arid Gulf region may indicate a shallow groundwater effect, but their relationship with groundwater storage has not been quantified. title: Local management shapes meiofaunal communities in Balearic sandy beaches
abstract: Sandy beaches are highly dynamic ecosystems providing essential services, yet they face increasing pressure from coastal exploitation. While macrofaunal responses to human disturbance are well documented, the impacts on communities for ecosystem functioning, such as the meiofauna, remain poorly understood. This study characterizes the meiofaunal communities of nine sandy beaches across the Balearic Archipelago (Mediterranean Sea) to evaluate the influence of beach morphodynamic zones, regional urbanization (Human Influence Index), and local management and protection ( Decret 25/2018 ). abstract: Brinicles are dynamic ice structures that have been proposed as chemically active systems on Ocean Worlds, potentially serving as habitable niches for life. However, experimental studies of their internal microstructures and implications for habitability remain limited. This study examined how brine composition influences the formation of liquid habitats within brinicles and how differences in liquid fraction distribution impact the transport and location of fluorescent microspheres representing cellular proxies. abstract: Pomatomus saltatrix is a highly mobile coastal pelagic fish widely distributed in temperate and subtropical waters that supports important fisheries along the southwestern Atlantic coast. This study investigated spatial variation in the otolith elemental composition of P. saltatrix along the southeastern–southern Brazilian coast by integrating chemical signatures representing different life stages. abstract: Replacing fish meal (FM) and fish oil with sustainable alternatives is a priority for Mediterranean aquaculture, yet effects on fillet mineral composition and metal(loid) safety remain unclear. title: Marine self‐assembling peptide materials promote reduced‐scarring wound healing by modulating the wound microenvironment and cellular crosstalk
abstract: High‐quality skin repair with reduced scarring requires biomaterials that actively orchestrate the wound microenvironment and multicellular interactions. Here, we report an enzyme‐controlled strategy to derive a self‐assembling peptide material (AAPs) from Azumapecten farreri meat proteins. abstract: The Marbled Stargazer, Uranoscopus marmoratus, is redescribed based on five individuals collected from the southeastern Arabian Sea, India. title: The Tiber River Mouth Linear Park: A Landscape-Based Strategy for Flood Adaptation Through Nature-Based Solutions
abstract: Flood vulnerability at the mouth of the Tiber River is increasingly influenced by the interaction of extreme rainfall, fragmented urbanization, surface impermeability, and ecological degradation. This study develops a landscape-based flood adaptation strategy for the lower Tiber River corridor by integrating hydrological analysis with a research-by-design framework and Nature-Based Solutions (NBS). abstract: Spartina alterniflora ranks among the most consequential invasive species in coastal wetlands globally; however, the adaptive strategies enabling its success under relatively phosphorus (P)‐limited conditions remain poorly understood. As nutrient bioavailability fundamentally constrains invasion success, soil P bioavailability constitutes a key determinant of plant growth and reproductive output in coastal wetland ecosystems. abstract: Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. title: Stakeholder perceptions of oyster services: A mixed‐methods approach to mapping services to improve management efficiency
abstract: Coastal zones are multifaceted spaces environmentally and culturally. They are sites of recreation, refuge, spirituality, commercial fishing and habitat for numerous marine organisms, while also providing important regulating services. They are increasingly central to interest in oyster aquaculture as both a food of a more sustainable blue future and a mechanism for climate resilience. title: Integrating fish biology, population genomics, and fishery policies for informed management of interjurisdictional multispecies fisheries
abstract: Coastal fisheries are typically managed within bounds set by political jurisdictions of nations and their provinces. This approach often results in multiple states/provinces managing a single genetically distinct fish population autonomously and typically without coordination. In multispecies, decentralized, and data‐poor fisheries, this can lead to inadequate assessments and fisheries overharvests. abstract: Ion‐selective membranes are widely employed to extract energy and resources from seawater, yet their performance is significantly compromised by divalent ions present in natural seawater. Here, we present a graphene oxide‐based monovalent cation‐selective membrane with high ion selectivity and permeability that can reject divalent ions by leveraging steric exclusion within nanoconfined interlayers. abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. abstract: Spatial visualization is a fundamental cognitive skill for learning, especially in STEM. Traditional tests rely on abstract geometric figures that can hinder performance for individuals with spatial visualization difficulties, potentially underrepresenting their true capabilities. This study presents and validates the Measure of the Ability to Form Spatial Mental Imagery for Adolescents (MASMI-A), a spatial visualization test based on realistic human figures. abstract: Oceanic melting of Antarctic ice shelves plays a key role in ice sheet mass balance and retreat. abstract: The dory snapper, Lutjanus fulviflamma (Forsskål, 1775), belongs to the family Lutjanidae (snappers) and is widely distributed across the Indo-Pacific region. Although snappers are commercially important, little is known about them, and species misidentification is common due to overlapping morphological features. abstract: Spatial structure and movement are common features of marine fish populations, yet many fisheries management systems continue to rely on single‐region stock assessments. When stock‐level catch advice is generated at a broader spatial scale than management implementation, empirical catch allocation strategies provide a way to distribute harvest among regions and fleets. abstract: Ulvan is a sulfated polysaccharide that constitutes a major component of the cell wall of green macroalgae in the genus Ulva and plays an important role in coastal carbon and sulfur cycling. abstract: Tamanend’s bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops erebennus ) are apex predators whose abundance and behavior may reflect seasonality in estuarine food webs. We examined mangrove extent in Tarout Bay, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia, for 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2026 using Landsat surface-reflectance composites and NDVI thresholding, with Sentinel-2 imagery providing contemporary landscape context. abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary α-ketoglutarate (α-KG) supplementation at different levels on growth performance, protein synthesis, and mitochondrial function in juvenile red sea bream ( Pagrus major ) fed low-protein (LP) diets. title: Plastic bag deposition alters the macrofaunal structure and function in mangrove mudflats: temporary refuge or ecological trap?
abstract: Plastic debris is recognised as a persistent anthropogenic stressor in coastal ecosystems; yet few experimental studies have examined its ecological impacts in situ over biologically relevant time scales. We evaluated the effects of plastic bag deposition on sediment conditions and benthic macrofaunal communities in two subtropical mangrove mudflats in Hong Kong over 34 weeks. We analysed the taxonomic and functional differences among the macrofaunal communities found within the folds and on the surface of the plastic bags, in the plastic-covered sediment and adjacent uncovered plots. abstract: Eco-friendly community-based coastal tourism requires the integration of Muslim-friendly service values and digitalization to ensure destination sustainability. title: Paleodietary Stable Isotope Analysis of the Pre‐Hispanic Indigenous Population of La Palma (Canary Islands)
abstract: We study the stable isotopes of the indigenous population (4th–15th century ad ) on individuals from cave burials of the island of La Palma. This approach allows for the study of dietary patterns depending on sites and areas. Further, the isotopic analysis was augmented by use of food percentage reconstruction software (FRUITS), which allowed for a visualization of the amount of potential food sources used by the islanders. title: Short-term effects of high-temperature exposure on shell structure, mantle tissue condition, and cellular immune response in the Fat Horsemussel (Modiolus capax)
abstract: Given their ecological and commercial importance, understanding how bivalves respond to environmental stress associated with climate change, particularly rising seawater temperatures, is essential. abstract: Subduction zones play an important role in the global S cycle, because recycling of altered oceanic crust and overlying sediments transfers different S species, particularly sulfide and sulfate, into the mantle. These affect the S contents, the S isotope composition and possibly the redox conditions in the mantle, as reflected by arc magmas along subduction zones. title: Analyzing Weather Station Reliability During Extreme Precipitation Events
abstract: The Global Historical Climatology Network Daily (GHCNd), maintained by NOAA’s National Centers for Environmental Information, provides archived daily climate observations from over 25,000 stations worldwide. During extreme precipitation events, accurate weather-station observations are crucial for forecasting, climate analysis, and hazard response. title: What can energy become? Energy-to-data and energy-to-material pathways for resource-rich economies
abstract: Resource-rich economies face competing uses of electricity, water, infrastructure and public finance. This article develops Energy-to-Value (ETV) as a bounded screening framework for Energy-to-Data (ETD) and Energy-to-Material (E2Mat) pathways. A structured narrative review distinguishes conversion outputs from development outcomes and financing conditions. abstract: Euryhaline fish pose a challenge when interpreting the fishing habitats utilised in areas where both fresh and saline waters would have been accessible. One such example is the island of Gotland, central Baltic Sea, where archaeological fishbone assemblages often contain euryhaline fish species that could have originated from different habitats. title: Gerontecnología y Visualización de la Información en el Hogar: Una Aproximación Teórica a la Autonomía Proactiva del Adulto Mayor desde la Óptica del Desarrollo Sostenible en México
abstract: Currently, population aging represents a major challenge as it impacts the well-being and independence of older adults, particularly in the home environment. In this regard, both gerontechnology and information visualization make it possible to adapt home spaces for a more autonomous, independent, and safe life. This article analyzes gerontechnology, aging, information visualization, autonomy, and sustainable development from a theoretical-conceptual, analytical, and critical perspective, based on a review of previous research and specialized sources. title: Seasonal and spatial drivers of microbiome structure in the invasive mussel Brachidontes pharaonis
abstract: The rocky intertidal tropical invader, the mussel Brachidontes pharaonis , is known for its resilience and adaptability. However, in the summer of 2016, it experienced mass mortality along the Levantine coast of the Mediterranean, where climate-driven warming and coastal pollution exert significant pressure. Although the species has since reestablished its populations, the role of its host-associated microbiome in mussel health remains poorly characterized. title: Beyond production: Valuing and modelling farmers' practices for ecosystem services provision in Mediterranean olive growing
abstract: The crucial role of ecosystem services (ESs) for both human well-being and biodiversity is becoming increasingly apparent. Consequently, mitigating potential impacts that could jeopardise these services presents a significant challenge in our contemporary world. The Mediterranean basin harbours a wealth of natural ecosystems deeply interwoven with human activities, particularly in the agricultural sector. abstract: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon sources entering these marshes are less well known. abstract: The family Eirenidae comprises common hydrozoans in coastal waters worldwide, yet its phylogenetic structure remains poorly resolved due to limited mitochondrial data. This study reported the first complete linear mitogenome of Eirene lacteoides Kubota and Horita, Citation1992, which is 15,009 bp in length with an AT content of 68.11%, featuring inverted terminal repeat (ITR) sequences. title: Development of an Internet of Things-Based Information System for Monitoring and Controlling Mechanical Equipment
abstract: Mechanical equipment such as electric motors, pumps, compressors, and production machines requires periodic condition monitoring. Manual inspection can delay fault detection, increase downtime, and provide limited historical data. This study aimed to develop an Internet of Things (IoT)-based information system for monitoring and controlling mechanical equipment by measuring temperature, electric current, vibration, rotational speed (RPM), and oil pressure in real time while providing remote control through a relay module. title: Seasonal variation in heteromorphic sperm size in Littorina snails on the Swedish West Coast
abstract: Sperm are among the most morphologically diverse cells in the animal kingdom, with many species producing distinct sperm morphs-a phenomenon known as sperm heteromorphism. Typically, fertilizing eusperm are accompanied by non-fertilizing parasperm, which in some taxa play roles related to sperm competition. In Littorina snails, a genus of marine gastropods, the function of parasperm remains unresolved, but it appears to represent a substantial reproductive investment and thus may change through the breeding season. abstract: The Saint Peter and Saint Paul Archipelago (SPSPA), located in one of the most remote regions of the equatorial Atlantic, is a strategic area for marine science and conservation in Brazil. In this study, we used scientometric methods to characterize the evolution of scientific production, thematic structure, and collaboration patterns associated with research in the archipelago. abstract: Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) aquaculture is increasingly seeking alternatives to marine‐derived ingredients, but the physiological and molecular consequences of fishmeal (FM) replacement remain incompletely understood. This study assessed the effects of two nutritionally equivalent summer diets for Atlantic salmon under simulated Tasmanian summer conditions (18°C): FM and FM‐free (FMF). title: Dietary fish-farming by-products shape the antimicrobial bioactivity of polychaetes and their immunomodulatory effects in fish cell lines
abstract: Marine polychaetes are increasingly investigated for their bioactive potential and for aquaculture sludge valorisation, but the effects of sludge-based diets on their functional properties remain still unknown. Here, we provide the first integrated evaluation of immune-related functionality in a polychaete by rearing Perinereis vallata (Grube, 1857) on diets containing 5%, 10% or 20% salmon aquaculture sludge and assessing enzymatic, antimicrobial and immunomodulatory responses. abstract: Natural gas hydrates are promising clean energy, yet accurate characterization of hydrate‑bearing sediments (HBS) is hindered by diverse hydrate morphologies and non‑uniqueness of single‑physics inversions. Conventional rock‑physics models separate elastic and electrical responses or assume ideal single‑mode hydrate occurrence, failing to reproduce microstructural evolution and physicochemical interactions in natural reservoirs. title: Extreme heat drives opposing patterns of size-dependent survival across microhabitats
abstract: Increasingly frequent and severe heatwaves threaten the persistence of species on Earth. Survival under extreme heat is often attributed to organismal traits, such as body size, yet realized heat exposure also depends on microhabitat. We show that a historical heatwave-which killed over a billion coastal organisms-drove size-dependent survival in an intertidal mussel population, favouring opposite extremes of the size distribution. abstract: Protists, defined as eukaryotes distinct from plants, animals and fungi, comprise much of eukaryotic phylogenetic diversity and perform key ecological functions, yet most lineages remain uncultivated and poorly represented in reference databases. Amplicon-based 18S rRNA gene surveys have transformed protist ecology, but primer bias, PCR bias and marker length can limit recovery of divergent lineages. abstract: Understanding how tourist attractions are distributed across Banjarbaru City, South Kalimantan, can support regional tourism planning. This study examined the spatial patterns of four categories of attractions: natural, human-made, cultural, and geopark. The quantitative study combined GPS coordinate collection, digitization of satellite imagery in Google Earth Pro, and geographic information system (GIS) mapping. abstract: With its geographical location between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean a stretch of approximately 3500 km, Morocco has significant fishery resources. It is one of the leading fish producers on the African continent and plays a leading role in the marine fisheries sector in Africa. As a result, it has one of the highest rates of seafood consumption among Mediterranean countries, consisting mainly of small pelagic species such as sardines, horse mackerel, hake, and anchovies. abstract: In Hawaiʻi, wildfires represent an escalating crisis for communities, with growing impacts to health and human safety, native ecosystems, vital watersheds, and nearshore coral reefs. Despite increased funding for prevention, suppression, and recovery, the threat continues to outpace responses, culminating over the past decade in some of the largest fires in Hawaiʻi's history. abstract: The thyroglobulin (TG) gene is a cornerstone of vertebrate endocrinology, serving as the macromolecular precursor for thyroid hormone biosynthesis. Here, we reconstructed the full-length TG sequence of the sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus), a basal vertebrate of key evolutionary significance, and performed comparative analyses across 50 representative species. abstract: Current acellular pertussis vaccines fail to control the burden of Bordetella pertussis ( Bp ) in the human nasopharynx, a reservoir for transmission. abstract: In this study, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a major greenhouse gas predominantly emitted from agricultural soils via microbial activity, was investigated using a real-time detection approach. title: Las nuevas universidades E l fenómeno de comunidades de aprendizaje en línea
abstract: The paper observes and analyzes the moderated activity of a virtual lear­ning community, which has opera­ted since 2005, mainly through an annual meeting called Education and Free Soft­ware (EduSoL). We try to understand the emergent phenomena of expansive lear­ning through collaboration, to help better understand and develop virtual learning communities. abstract: Animal communities at shallow and upper-slope hydrothermal vents are shaped by vent-fluid conditions, geological setting, substrate composition, and the surrounding shelf ecosystems. abstract: The existence of endocrine disrupting chemical (EDCs), like bisphenol-A (BPA), creates a huge challenge for conventional wastewater treatment plants. The current study aimed to develop a hybrid adsorption-photocatalytic material for efficient BPA removal under UV-A irradiation. abstract: Sembawang Hot Spring is the only publicly accessible natural hot spring in Singapore and has attracted increasing attention because of its geothermal potential. Previous hydrogeological investigations and thermal profiling studies have suggested that the hot spring is primarily recharged by meteoric water; however, long-term geochemical observations are still limited. abstract: The implementation of Law Number 3 of 2024 demands the strengthening of professional, digitalized, and accountable village governance capacities, particularly in coastal areas with dynamic economic potential. title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
abstract: The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs 2,3 . abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are evolutionarily conserved mediators of intercellular communication released by cells into biological fluids and the environment. Despite their increasing relevance in biomedical and veterinary research, knowledge of EVs in marine bivalves remains limited. This study first aimed to optimize protocols for EV isolation from the hemolymph of Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) using density gradient ultracentrifugation (dgUC) or size exclusion chromatography (SEC). abstract: Sewage networks are one of the most critical elements of the urban infrastructure that is fundamental for the protection of public health and environment. This requires not only constant monitoring but also evaluation to ensure that the systems are functioning. Karbala hosts millions of yearly pilgrims which places an enormous hydraulic load on the sewerage system. title: The role of community help in mitigating the behavioral health impacts of disasters: A study of U.S. Gulf Coast residents
abstract: Social buffering, social deterioration, and social mobilization theories have been widely used to understand the role community help and support plays in post-disaster health, but often in isolation. We study these using longitudinal data from residents of the U.S. Gulf Coast, an area frequently hit by hurricanes. abstract: Advanced scintillation materials capable of simultaneously delivering ultrahigh efficiency, exceptional stability, and multifunctional X-ray imaging remain elusive because of intrinsic trade-offs in conventional scintillators. abstract: The results of this study provide new insights into some aspects of settlement and early economic activity on Russia's southern frontier. The authors attempt to reconstruct the key physical and geographic features and patterns of anthropogenic impact associated with land use in a microregion of present-day Tambov Oblast, located at the southern margin of the Great East European Forest and the threshold of the Great Steppe. abstract: Bangladesh’s coastal salt industry depends largely on solar evaporation and is therefore sensitive to rainfall, temperature, sunshine duration and other weather conditions. This study examines national salt production and demand trends, explores associations between salt output and selected meteorological variables, and identifies production constraints reported by salt farmers. Annual secondary data for 2000–2024 were obtained from the Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) and the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD). abstract: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-associated infections highlights the need for alternative strategies to control pathogenic microorganisms. Probiotics have emerged as promising candidates due to their ability to inhibit pathogen growth. However, their potential ways of application in human medicine remain insufficiently understood. title: Integrated stage-specific management across the production cycle of Macrobrachium rosenbergii: effects of broodstock nutrition, larval salinity and biofloc carbon management
abstract: This study evaluated stage-specific management strategies across three successive phases of the Macrobrachium rosenbergii production cycle: broodstock conditioning, larval rearing, and juvenile grow-out. Each phase was evaluated through an independent experiment testing specific nutritional, environmental, or microbial management factors, while together the three experiments provided a coordinated production framework. title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically driven strongly interacting bosons
abstract: The time-averaged spectral function plays a central role in studying the Floquet properties of the many-body fermionic systems. Here, we study the time-averaged spectral function of the periodically driven bosonic systems by providing an exact and rigorous analysis in the strongly interacting one-dimensional limit. The exact analysis reveals that the nonequilibrium Lieb excitations emerge if the underlying steady states form a Floquet-Fermi sea. title: Spatial modeling of historical economic systems in Tibet: A seasonal ritual core–periphery framework
abstract: Core–periphery models have traditionally inferred regional organization from relatively stable distributions of markets, settlements, and administrative centers. This article argues that in pastoral and agropastoral societies, periodic congregation structured by religious calendars may constitute an equally important mechanism of regional integration. Using a georeferenced dataset of 215 Tibetan Buddhist monasteries and 401 documented festivals and public assemblies from Yushu Prefecture in eastern Tibet (historically part of Kham), this study develops the Tibetan Monastic Ritual Economy Model
journal: Historical Methods A Journal of Quantitative and Interdisciplinary History

title: Contextualizing the role of mobula rays in household ‘food security’ and what it means for conservation in East Flores, Indonesia
abstract: Elasmobranch conservation increasingly invokes concerns about ‘food security’, yet the term is often applied without a clear theoretical framework or empirical underpinning. This study addresses this gap by first exploring relevant theories of food security, then applying appropriate theory and methods to empirically examine the role of mobula rays ( Mobula spp.) in the food security of fisheries‐dependent households in East Flores, Indonesia, and exploring the implications for mobula conservation. title: ‘A Colonial Institution’: The Ceylon Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society
abstract: In 1859, fourteen years after its founding, the Ceylon Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society (CBRAS) proudly declared itself to be a ‘colonial institution’. This article assesses this claim, exploring the foundation and early development of the Society, and evaluating the extent to which Britain’s burgeoning nineteenth-century empire in Asia and the scientific networks it sustained assisted fledgling institutions like the CBRAS. title: Hierarchical Networks Dominated by Nonclassical Hydrogen Bonding Enable Robust, Adhesive, Self‐Healing, and Recyclable Elastomers for Liquid‐Metal‐Based Soft Electronics
abstract: Soft electronics require elastomers that combine mechanical robustness, adhesion, self-healing, reprocessability, and stable conductive interfaces, yet integrating these properties remains challenging in mechanically dynamic and aqueous environments. Herein, we develop a supramolecular acrylate elastomer by copolymerizing butyl acrylate, hexafluorobutyl methacrylate, and 1-vinylimidazole. title: Foreign Direct Investment and Environmental Sustainability in South Asia and MENA: The Roles of Trade Flows and Institutional Quality
abstract: This study examines how foreign direct investment (FDI) affects environmental sustainability, considering the role of institutional quality. The study is motivated by poor environmental performance scores in South Asian countries and rising emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and carbon dioxide (CO2) in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, which threaten the United Nations sustainability agenda but have been overlooked in earlier studies. title: Fast and cleanup-free determination of trace elements in highly saline matrices using transient inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (t-ICP-MS)
abstract: Standard ICP-MS (inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry) for trace element analysis in highly saline samples (>1% dissolved salts) suffers from salt deposits, reduced sensitivity, and a shortened service life of components. Conventional remedies such as extensive dilution or matrix separation are time-consuming and prone to contamination. Driven by the analytical requirements of safety assessments for deep geological repositories for radioactive waste in saline regions, we present an automated transient ICP-MS (t-ICP-MS) method adapted for the Agilent 8900 ICP-QQQ. title: Integrating Digital Tools into Agricultural Science Instruction in Secondary Schools: Opportunities and Challenges for Curriculum Developers in Delta State
abstract: This study explored the opportunities and challenges for curriculum developers and educators in integrating digital resources into agricultural science instruction in public secondary schools in Delta State, Nigeria. The present study adopted a convergent parallel mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL). The quantitative strand sampled 280 agricultural science instructors using a stratified proportionate sample across nine Local Government Areas in the Delta North, Delta Central and Delta South senatorial districts, with 268 verified questionnaire returns (95.71% response rate). title: Mapping the endemic Betula borysthenica Klokov in southern Ukraine using open remote sensing
abstract: The dataset includes georeferenced occurrences of Betula borysthenica Klokov. The dataset was compiled as part of the work of NGO "Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group" which aimed to map Betula borysthenica Klokov, based on the interpretation of satellite imagery from Google Earth. The dataset contains occurrences of Betula borysthenica Klokov ("Dnipro birch" in Ukrainian), an endemic species recorded in the Black Sea Biosphere Reserve, Oleshky Sands and Biloberezhzhia Sviatoslav's National Nature Parks, the Kinburn Spit Regional Landscape Park, the Sahy Landscape Reserve and the Berezovi Kolk

title: A TMAH-Chloroform Sample-Preparation Workflow for Nile Red-Based Screening of Microplastics in Animal Feed
abstract: Animal feed is increasingly recognized as an important route of microplastic (MP) exposure in livestock production systems; however, reliable fluorescence-based detection remains challenging because proteins, lipids, pigments, and other organic constituents interfere with fluorescence analyses. This study developed and evaluated a sample-preparation protocol combining tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH) digestion with chloroform (TCM) extraction to reduce matrix interference while preserving the fluorescence characteristics of MP particles prior to Nile Red (NR) staining. title: La cultura en Cuba y en el mundo: americanidad y cubanidad en Alejo Carpentier
abstract: La cultura en Cuba y en el mundo (2003), is a book that brings together conferences by Alejo Carpentier, from 1964 to 1966. The purpose of the article is to detect the meanings of Americanidad and Cubanidad in this work, in addition to exposing the findings of a criticism reading that allowed the identification of its biographical meaning, visualization of sociological relations and its link to the cultural policy of the Cuban Revolution. title: Optimise an After-Treatment System for an Ammonia Dual-Fuel Engine to Meet the Maritime Requirements
abstract: Green ammonia can link renewable hydrogen production with ocean-going ship propulsion, but exhaust control for ammonia dual-fuel engines cannot be judged by carbon reduction alone. Ammonia combustion can still produce nitrogen oxides (NOx), ammonia (NH 3 ) slip, and nitrous oxide (N 2 O). This study builds a steady-state exhaust gas recirculation selective catalytic reduction (EGR-SCR) after-treatment model for the 7S60ME-C10.5-LGIA ammonia dual-fuel main engine. title: Photochemistry of Pyruvate Embedded in Sodium Chloride Clusters
abstract: During the aging of sea-salt aerosols, they undergo acid displacement reactions with inorganic and organic acids, which lead to the enrichment of the conjugate bases in the aerosol. Pyruvate is among the most abundant organic conjugate bases found in aged sea-salt aerosols. Here we study the photochemistry of charged pyruvate-doped sodium chloride clusters to better understand and characterize the absorption spectra and photochemistry of pyruvate in the actinic region. title: Health impacts of water risks through water-borne and vector-borne diseases in informal settlements in the Global South and India
abstract: Informal settlements concentrate overlapping water risks that undermine health, well-being and livelihood security. This review synthesizes evidence on how water scarcity, poor water quality, flooding, infrastructure deficits and governance gaps interact to shape health outcomes in informal urban communities, with particular attention to water- and vector-borne diseases. title: Resilience to Landslides in the Lower Shullcas River Basin under Climate Change
abstract: The lower Shullcas River basin has a medium-high to low level of risk from landslides. This risk is made worse by geological, climatic, and topographic factors. Climate change, especially through intense rainfall and higher temperatures, increases this risk and makes it necessary to use proper mitigation strategies and more efficient urban development plans. Even so, there are still weaknesses in how risk management is integrated among the people and institutions involved in the territory. title: Changing rainfall regimes in India: a district level appraisal
abstract: Background The south west monsoon plays crucial role in shaping the agriculture and economy of India, where majority is still dependent of agriculture for their livelihood. Changing spatio-temporal distribution of the rainfall affects both food and water security of the region which is further exacerbated by the climate change. So, this study aims to assess the changing trend and pattern of the rainfall at district level in India. title: Emerging signals of tourism pressure across waves of touristification in historic Baltic seaside resort cities
abstract: This study examines how emerging signals of tourism pressure developed across successive waves of touristification in the Baltic seaside resort cities of Pärnu (Estonia), Jūrmala (Latvia) and Palanga (Lithuania). A comparative historical methodology interprets archival and documentary sources through six predefined dimensions of tourism pressure and combines them with contemporary tourism indicators. title: Forged by frost, ready for heat: Integration of metabolomics and functional traits investigated along a latitudinal gradient reveals relaxed trade‐offs and enhanced heat tolerance in individuals from cold regions
abstract: Acquiring a critical understanding of how organisms respond to environmental changes requires integrating molecular and whole‐organism perspectives while investigating how latitudinal gradients shape thermal responses. We explored trade‐offs between thermal tolerance and performance in the marine intertidal gastropod Littorina littorea collected from 10 locations across a wide latitudinal gradient in North America. title: Fucoidan in lung cancer treatment: a comprehensive review of therapeutic applications and mechanisms
abstract: Lung cancer is a common malignancy in many countries and places a substantial mortality burden on public health systems worldwide. Despite recent advances in diagnosis and treatment, standard therapies often cause severe adverse effects and lead to drug resistance. These limitations highlight the need for safer and more effective treatment options. Fucoidan, a natural sulfated polysaccharide derived from marine brown algae, exhibits antitumor, antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities, supporting its potential biomedical applications. title: Differences in trace element concentrations and stable isotope values among juvenile Leach’s storm-petrels (Hydrobates leucorhous) from colonies in the North Atlantic
abstract: Seabirds face a host of threats, both at sea and on land causing population declines in up to a third of all species. Chemical pollution is an emerging threat to seabirds, and especially so for storm-petrels. Understanding which populations are most affected can be valuable when establishing mitigation measures, but comprehensive baseline estimates for trace element concentrations are lacking. Mitigating the Degradation of the Upstream Jeneberang Watershed: The Role of Ecological Literacy Moderation on Socio-Ecological Resilience of Farmers
abstract: Land degradation in the upstream Jeneberang watershed continues to increase massively, posing a serious threat to the balance of the catchment ecosystem and the livelihoods of local farming communities. Aim: This study aimed to analyze the distribution profile of biophysically degraded lands, as well as to evaluate and model the interactions among demographic pressure, ecological literacy levels, and the socio-ecological resilience capacity of farmers in the area. title: Characterization of transcriptomic profiles underlying gross morphological changes observed in semelparous pink salmon ( Oncorhynchus gorbuscha )
abstract: Pacific salmon undergo dramatic physiological remodeling during their terminal spawning migration, culminating in reproductive maturation, senescence, and death. To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes, we characterized transcriptomic changes in wild pink salmon ( Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) sampled at three migratory stages (marine, riverine, and spawning ground) and across three tissues central to endocrine regulation and energy metabolism: gonads, head kidney, and skeletal muscle. journal: American Journal of Physiology-Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology

title: First detailed reconstruction of the remipede circulatory system indicates the circumoesophageal vessel ring as a labiocaridan apomorphy
abstract: Remipedia is a taxon of crustaceans, discovered only in 1981, that inhabit anchialine caves. Their phylogenetic position has long been debated, but recent studies increasingly support a placement as the sister group to Hexapoda, positioning Remipedia as a phylogenetic link that facilitates the interpretation of character transformations between 'Crustacea' to Hexapoda. In this context, the cardiovascular system of Remipedia-so far only scarcely described-is examined here. title: Flexible zinc coordination polymer/ethylcellulose composite films for triboelectric nanogenerators: Self-powered corrosion monitoring and cathodic protection
abstract: The development of multifunctional triboelectric materials for simultaneous metal corrosion-state monitoring and self-powered electrochemical anticorrosion systems remains a highly desirable yet challenging objective. In this work, flexible zinc coordination polymer (Zn-CP)/ethylcellulose (EC) composite films (Zn-CP@EC) were employed as triboelectric materials to construct triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) for self-powered for metal corrosion detection and electrochemical protection systems. Different Zn-CP contents were incorporated into EC to fabricate a series of Zn-CP@EC composite films

title: Smart Innovations for Unlocking the Social Potential of Biosphere Reserves
abstract: Biosphere reserves represent important laboratories for testing innovative approaches to sustainable regional development. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to the role of smart innovations, particularly those that combine digital technologies, open data infrastructures and participatory governance. This paper analyses selected examples of smart innovations implemented in European biosphere reserves, with a particular focus on their contribution to the development of social potential in these territories. title: Spatial Patterns of Lipid Composition and Trophic Biomarkers in the Argentine Anchovy ( Engraulis anchoita ) Across Contrasting Shelf Environments
abstract: In continental shelf ecosystems, physical‐biological coupling between hydrographic structures and bottom‐up pathways can generate spatial gradients in prey availability and quality that may influence the lipid quality of small pelagic fish. The income‐breeding Engraulis anchoita on the Northern Argentinean Continental Shelf (NACS) fuels reproduction through active feeding and makes tissue lipid quality closely linked to local oceanographic and dietary conditions. title: Evaluation and Regional Adjustment of the Ultra-High-Resolution GGMplus Geoid Model: A Case Study in Türkiye
abstract: The Global Gravity Model plus (GGMplus) ultra-high-resolution geoid model and its regionally adjusted version, ADJ_GGMplus, are evaluated over Türkiye by comparing them with national geoid models (TG-03 and TG-20) and GNSS/levelling observations. The GGMplus model, with a spatial resolution of approximately 200 meters, offers a significant potential for regional geoid modelling, particularly in topographically and geologically complex areas. title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
abstract: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. title: Skin-Protective and Anti-Photoaging Potential of a Collagen-Based Bioactive Complex in Hs68 Dermal Fibroblasts
abstract: As we age, combined intrinsic and extrinsic aging processes lead to functional and structural alterations in the skin. Supplementation with nutraceuticals combining collagen peptides and plant-derived bioactive compounds represents a potential strategy to maintain skin health. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the skin-protective effects of collagen-based bioactive complex (CBC), which contains marine-derived bioactive peptides and plant-derived bioactive compounds, such as Amla, lingonberry, and other bioactive ingredients.
