title: Cracking, Chloride Transport, and Functional Recovery in Slag-Based Alkali-Activated Materials: A Review
abstract: Slag-based alkali-activated materials can develop favorable initial strength and chloride resistance; however, these properties do not establish their performance after cracking or healing. This critical review examines the activation chemistry, fracture, transport, and recovery across intact, damaged, and healed states. Published evidence is synthesized based on the material scale, exposure history, measured function, and reference conditions. title: Functional resonance analysis of ownership continuity in catchment-scale governance of nature-based solutions
abstract: Graphical abstract shows how continuity of catchment objectives across scales and governance functions supports nature-based solutions. Nature-based solutions (NBS) can support urban flood mitigation, water-quality improvement and climate adaptation, yet their effectiveness at catchment scale depends on coordination across multiple actors, governance functions and spatial scales. This study examines how ownership of catchment-scale objectives is maintained as responsibilities shift during NBS planning, construction and operation. title: Solitary bees: understanding its contribution and prospecting key areas for its use in crop pollination in Brazil
abstract: Animal pollination is a key factor for agricultural production, with bees considered the most important pollinating agents. Despite the high diversity within this group, Apis mellifera is the species most widely used for crop pollination; however, numerous factors have driven the search for alternative pollinators. title: The relationship of simulation frequency with preparedness and early community action in emergencies of earthquake and tsunami disasters in Gampong Alue Naga Subdistrict Syiah Kuala
abstract: Gampong Alue Naga is a coastal area in Banda Aceh City that is vulnerable to earthquakes and tsunamis. This study aimed to determine the relationship between simulation frequency, community preparedness, and initial response actions during earthquake and tsunami emergencies. This study employed an analytical correlational design with a cross-sectional approach. A total of 140 respondents were selected using a purposive sampling technique. title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. title: Habitat imprinting is not associated with reproductive benefits in a long-lived bird of prey
abstract: Multiple mechanisms have been proposed to explain how animals choose their first breeding habitat. In the white-tailed eagle Haliaeetus albicilla, similarity between the natal and settlement habitats and the density of conspecifics seem to be important cues. It is, however, unclear whether these are associated with reproductive performance in the selected habitat. title: IoT Based Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition for Solar Microgrid Operation in Bonny Island
abstract: An IoT-enabled SCADA system was designed and tested for real-time supervisory monitoring of a PV-battery microgrid. The study considered the issues of limited visibility of renewable generation and battery conditions, electrical loading, voltage and frequency excursions, IoT delay, and slow detection of abnormal operating conditions in small-scaled microgrids. title: Restoration of host–Lepidoptera herbivory networks in the endemic Scalesia pedunculata cloud forest of Galapagos
abstract: Introduction Insular ecosystems are highly vulnerable to biological invasions, which disrupt native species interactions. Ecological restoration is a key strategy to reverse these impacts, yet its effects on species interactions remain poorly understood. Lepidoptera larvae (caterpillars) play a crucial role in ecosystem functioning but have received little attention in restoration studies. title: Anoxia selects for high-fitness biofilms and reduces antibiotic susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a growing global health crisis, yet resistance is almost exclusively quantified under aerobic laboratory conditions that fail to reflect the complex microenvironments bacteria encounter during infection. Many clinically important infection sites, such as airways of individuals with cystic fibrosis or chronic wounds, are microaerobic to anoxic. title: Biological parameters of the common eel (Ophichthus remiger) in the tropical Eastern Pacific: Implications for fisheries management and sustainable conservation
abstract: Ophichthus remiger, commonly known as the common eel, is commercially important in Ecuador because Asian markets have high demand. Since industrial fishing began in 2004, no systematic population monitoring has been conducted, limiting understanding of the species' population dynamics and challenging sustainable management efforts. This study provides essential biological parameters of O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil, Ecuador, including size structure, sex ratio, length-weight relationship, and size at first sexual maturity (SFSM), estimated as the median length at sexual maturity (L50). title: Terrain-Conditioned Industrial Expansion and Environmental Trade-offs in a Peri-Urban Corridor: A Two-Decade Geospatial Assessment of the Vasanthanarasapura Industrial Area, Karnataka
abstract: Corridor-led industrialisation has altered peri-urban landscapes across India. Most change-detection studies quantify the area converted but leave unexamined the terrain on which that conversion occurred and the reasons for its location. The present study addresses this gap for the Vasanthanarasapura Industrial Area (VIA) and its 5 km buffer (13°23′-13°30′N; 76°55′-77°05′E) in Tumakuru district, Karnataka. title: Trade and logistics performance of the Middle Corridor with empirical insights from Türkiye
abstract: The Trans-Caspian “Middle Corridor” has become a pivotal element in Türkiye’s Eurasian trade architecture. Adopting an interdisciplinary dual-method design, this study integrates a TOPSIS-based multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework with an augmented gravity model to benchmark the corridor against its Northern rail and Suez-based maritime alternatives. Descriptive transit-time data indicate that the Middle Corridor can cut door-to-door transit time by roughly 50% relative to the Northern route. abstract: In this work, we fabricated PETG/POE/Fe 3 O 4 nanocomposites via melt blending at a fixed 4:6 PETG‐to‐POE mass ratio with varying Fe 3 O 4 loadings, aiming to develop a magnetic–near‐infrared dual‐responsive shape‐memory polymer for 4D printing. title: Assessment of Social Inclusion in Project Determination in Ondo State Nigeria: Optimizing Impact of Projects
abstract: This study set to investigate the extent of societal inclusion in projects determination in Ondo State Nigeria. Existing literature provides insights into the significant of social exclusion in development projects implementation but did not comprehensively interrogate the extent of social inclusion in projects determination in context of Ondo State Nigeria. To bridge the gap, this study is set to assess the extent of social inclusion in projects determination in this State. title: Coexposure to Regulated and Unregulated Organohalogens through Omega-3 Fish Oil Supplements: A Retrospective Screening of Products Purchased in 2014–2017
abstract: Omega-3 fish oil supplements are nutraceuticals widely recommended for long-term daily consumption. title: Morphological analysis of the eye of Eudocimus ruber (Linnaeus, 1758)
abstract: Eudocimus ruber (Linnaeus, 1758), commonly known as the scarlet ibis, is a wading bird widely distributed throughout northern South America and along the Brazilian coast. However, detailed information on the ocular morphology of this species remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to perform a multimodal morphological characterization of the eye and its associated structures in E. ruber. title: Biofilms in drug-coated medical devices: Mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance and perspectives on new approaches
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bacterial biofilms are a major cause of treatment failure in orthopedic implant surgery, contributing to a large proportion of chronic, device-associated infections. Biofilms contain bacteria that are able to survive antimicrobial concentrations 10-1,000-fold higher than the planktonic equivalent, and antimicrobial-coated implants, which are designed to limit this risk, can still be colonized after depletion of the antimicrobial reservoir on the implant. title: Climate change literacy and its implications for older adults: a concept analysis
abstract: Purpose This study analyzed the conceptual structure of climate change literacy by integrating climate-related literacy concepts used across disciplines and explored its implications for older adults’ health. Methods This concept analysis used Walker and Avant’s approach. Five electronic databases—PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, PsycINFO, and Web of Science—were searched from inception to December 2025. title: Quantifying biodiversity and ecosystem service trade-offs to inform forest landscape management under changing conditions
abstract: Forested landscapes provide a wide range of ecosystem services (ES) and support biodiversity, yet both are increasingly threatened by intensive management practices and climate change. Understanding trade-offs and synergies between biodiversity and multiple ES is essential for identifying sustainable forest management strategies. abstract: Background Host-associated microbiota play a central role in maintaining physiological homeostasis and regulating host immune responses. In aquatic organisms, this relationship is particularly dynamic due to continuous exposure to the surrounding environment. While acute viral infections are known to induce dysbiosis, the effects of recurrent sublethal exposures, which better reflect conditions in aquaculture and natural environments, remain poorly understood. title: Co-option of lysosomal machinery for sponge biosilicification
abstract: Biomineralization has evolved repeatedly across animals, resulting in novel strategies for buoyancy, locomotion and defense. title: El dispositivo de evaluación del aprendizaje en la formación inicial del profesorado
abstract: This article examines the learning assessment apparatus in initial teacher education, understood as a network of discourses, forms of knowledge, institutional criteria, and recording practices through which learning is rendered visible and assessable. It seeks to understand how the discursive articulations between the purpose and function of assessment express tensions between formative aspirations and the uses of assessment information reported by teachers. title: Effect of 3D Printing Parameters on the Flexural Performance of Laminated Structures: A Taguchi and ANOVA-Based Approach
abstract: The influence of important fused deposition modelling (FDM) parameters, including infill pattern, printing speed and wall thickness, on the flexural behaviors of multi-layered laminated polymer specimens, was investigated in this study. title: Water Tunnel Design Development Using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) DualSPHysics Analysis
abstract: Water tunnels serve as cost-effective alternatives to wind tunnels for aerodynamic testing, offering key advantages in flow visualization due to higher fluid density and lower required free-stream velocity [1][2]. title: Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles using complex polysaccharide-rich sulphated extract (CPSE) from Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its broad-spectrum antimicrobial and catalytic activity
abstract: The dual global crises of escalating antimicrobial resistance and the environmental hazards of chemical synthesis demand the creation of advanced nanomaterials through sustainable and precisely controlled methodologies. While “green” synthesis offers a promising alternative, it is often limited by a lack of control over key nanoparticle attributes such as crystallinity and stability. title: When is a mistake not a mistake? The value of studying misdirected behaviours
abstract: From male deep-sea squid attaching spermatophores to other males to jewel beetles mating with beer bottles, animals are often observed directing behaviour towards targets or stimuli that, at first glance, may appear ‘incorrect’ or ‘inappropriate’. Such misdirected behaviours, broadly defined as behaviours directed towards targets other than those for which they likely evolved, have attracted researchers' attention for centuries. title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
abstract: Eukaryotic genomes are exposed to numerous sources of DNA damage that impede replication. Only a decade ago, repriming by the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL was identified as a pathway that enables cells to tolerate DNA damage1–4. title: Indicators for tracking progress of effective, representative ecosystem protection
abstract: To halt and reverse rapid biodiversity loss, countries are pursuing the ambitious goals and targets in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) to restore and protect biodiversity in representative networks of protected areas. However, the associated monitoring framework lacks indicators of ecosystem representativeness for Target 3. title: Assessment of Fines Content, Sediment Strength, and Pedestrian Trafficability of a Mixed Sediment Tidal Flat Using X-Band Synthetic Aperture Radar
abstract: This study aims to characterize the fines content, strength, and pedestrian trafficability of a mixed sediment tidal flat in Eliot, Maine, using high-resolution HH polarized X-band TerraSAR-X synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images at low incidence angles (24°). Laboratory testing and a portable free fall penetrometer (PFFP) were used to characterize the soil in terms of fines content, median grain size, moisture content, and undrained shear strength. title: Hydro-chemical characterization and multi-index irrigation suitability assessment of surface water in the Indian Sundarbans
abstract: Agriculture in the Indian Sundarbans depends on surface water for irrigation, yet its quality is governed by complex geo-hydro-chemical processes. title: Wild edible fruits of Mozambique: Biodiversity hotspots and priority species for food security and sustainable development
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Wild edible fruits (WEFs) are an important but underutilised resource for improving food security in sub‐Saharan Africa. In Mozambique, many rural communities rely on these fruits to supplement diets, generate income and cope with periods of food scarcity; yet national‐level knowledge of their diversity has been lacking. This study provides the first comprehensive inventory of WEFs in Mozambique and identifies species and regions of the highest socio‐economic and ecological importance. title: Greedy nearest-neighbor approach to quantify site revisitation: Comparing two sympatric raven species
abstract: A central challenge in movement ecology is to describe ecologically meaningful residence sites from raw tracking data due to heterogeneous sampling frequency and uncertain site boundaries. Here, we develop a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering approach with local reassignment and polygon-based site construction that generates timestamped sequences of site visits for each tracked individual, and apply it to 9 years of global positioning system (GPS) data from two sympatric raven species in the Dead Sea region—the fan-tailed raven () and the brown-necked raven (). title: Exploring How Physical Climate Risks Influence Asset Useful Life Estimation in the Transportation Sector
abstract: Background: The increasing frequency and intensity of physical climate hazards—including floods, extreme temperatures, storms, and rising sea levels—pose significant challenges to the transportation sector, which relies heavily on long-lived, capital-intensive assets. Conventional approaches to estimating asset useful life rely primarily on historical performance data and engineering assumptions, often overlooking climate-related stressors. title: Elevation-Related Variation in Vegetation Richness, Composition, and Forage Productivity during the Dry Season in Silvopastoral Systems of Timor Tengah Selatan, Indonesia
abstract: Tropical semi-arid silvopastoral systems undergo seasonal changes in vegetation and forage availability, but their temporal dynamics across elevation classes in Timor, Indonesia, remain insufficiently documented. This study aimed to evaluate species richness, botanical composition, and available forage biomass across two elevation classes during the dry season and to assess monthly variation and elevation × month interactions. abstract: Bioluminescence, although frequently framed as an ecological curiosity of fireflies, marine macrofauna and glow-in-the-dark fungi, has become a real-world tool for understanding plant biology. Over many decades, firefly luciferase-based reporter systems have facilitated sensitive and quantitative measurements of gene expression, circadian rhythms and signalling in living plants. title: Unboxing Indigenous Community Ritual “Sedekah Turun Ton” as Mitigation Communication to Mitigate Disaster in North Lombok
abstract: This study aims to analyze the forms, meanings, and communicative functions embedded in the Sedekah Turun Ton ritual and its contribution to strengthening community awareness, preparedness, and resilience in facing disasters in North Lombok. The study employed a qualitative descriptive approach conducted in Bayan Village, North Lombok Regency, Indonesia. title: The Influence of Russia's Wheat Export Tax and the War in Ukraine on the Domestic Market: A Synthetic Control Method Approach
abstract: Russia, the world's leading wheat exporter, has implemented a wheat export tax since February 2021. This study examines the impact of the export tax and the war in Ukraine on the integration between Russia's domestic wheat market and the Black Sea export market, as well as its economic consequences for supply chain actors. title: The importance of eventflow sampling for river load estimation of trace contaminants
abstract: The accurate quantification of riverine contaminant loads is essential for assessing mitigation measures, pollution transport to downstream recipients (lakes, seas, countries) and for substance balance model validation. However, monitoring programmes based on regular, low-frequency grab samples often fail to adequately capture high-flow events (hereinafter referred to as eventflow). abstract: As populações de ostras são abundantes nos estuários da costa paranaense e apresentam elevada importância econômica regional. abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, caused by Naegleria fowleri , is a rapidly fatal infection of the central nervous system for which no consistently effective treatment exists. title: Utilization of Sargassum Natans in Sand Crete Block Production for Sustainable Walling Solutions
abstract: Seaweeds are a diverse and abundant group of marine algae that offer a promising sustainable alternative to conventional cementitious materials, which are increasingly associated with high environmental impact. This study investigated the feasibility of incorporating locally sourced Sargassumnatans powder into cement–sandcrete blocks as a bio-based additive for sustainable walling. abstract: Water enters the Ravne 1 tunnel system near Visoko through the ceiling and runs down the walls. It flows out of the main entrance year-round and also out of a service opening, and no standing water forms on the walking floor. This paper reconstructs the floor geometry that carries this water and compares its gradients with drainage practice from antiquity to the present. abstract: Rapid urbanization, increasing electricity demand, and developing environmental challenges have created a pressing need for sustainable and climate-responsive architectural solutions in Bangladesh. abstract: Rushan Pacific oyster ( Crassostrea gigas ) holds a geographical indication status in China and is widely consumed fresh. abstract: A growing body of research has characterized microplastic (MP) assemblages in freshwater systems worldwide, but sources and transport pathways remain difficult to identify. abstract: Background Africa has the highest reported prevalence of Helicobacter pylori , which is associated with peptic ulcer and gastric cancer. abstract: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as an undesirable output. abstract: The functional importance of habitat complexity and heterogeneity has wide-ranging implications for the restoration and protection of wetland habitats. The loss of littoral complexity due to shoreline modifications, water level fluctuations or invasive species may have negative consequences not only for biodiversity but also for ecosystem processes; however, little is known about the role of macrophyte complexity and bathymetric heterogeneity in supporting diverse food webs. abstract: Dimethyl sulfide (DMS) and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) have important microbial-driven roles in global nutrient cycling, chemotaxis and/or climate regulation. Microbial DMSO and DMS assimilation were thought to require their enzymatic reduction to methanethiol. However, reactive oxygen species were recently shown to mediate methane production from DMS and DMSO. abstract: The summer flounder, Paralichthys dentatus, is an ecologically important predator and supports one of the most valuable fisheries along the U.S. Atlantic coast, with commercial landings of about 4,040 metric tons valued at approximately $28 million in 2024. Genomic tools are an important resource to monitor shifts in population dynamics; however, genomic resources for summer flounder remain limited. abstract: Fish population monitoring provides essential information for environmental impact assessment of human activities on aquatic ecosystems and supports sustainable fisheries management. Long-term trends in reproduction of vendace (Coregonus albula), a species sensitive to water quality, were examined by monitoring the density of newly hatched vendace larval subpopulation and phosphorus concentration as an indicator of trophic status of four Finnish boreal lakes. abstract: Blue carbon (BC) ecosystems are increasingly recognised for their roles in climate action, biodiversity conservation and community livelihoods. As interest in their protection and restoration grows, so does the need for capacity development that can support effective project design, implementation and sustained action. abstract: This study assessed urban flood risk in Shomolu Local Government Area (LGA), Lagos State, Nigeria using geospatial techniques. abstract: Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. abstract: Maritime transport, often considered a hard-to-abate segment, is a significant contributor to global greenhouse gas emissions. Deployment of alternative green fuels and propulsion systems is among the most promising ways to defossilise maritime transport. This study presents a techno-economic assessment of alternative fuels and propulsion systems for 2030, 2040, and 2050 using the levelised cost of mobility framework. abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81 Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a crucial component of aquatic ecosystems, influencing pH, metal speciation, and the bioavailability of trace elements. The influence of DOM on water quality depends not only on its concentration but also on its chemical characteristics. To quantify the site density (SD) of organic acid functional groups, a key characteristic of DOM, this study utilized data from over 31,000 water samples collected from 110 watercourses between 1995 and 2024 by Swedish national monitoring programs. title: In silico analysis of arginine and creatine kinases, exploring the coexistence of phosphagens in the cannonball jellyfish Stomolophus sp.2
abstract: The cannonball jellyfish Stomolophus sp.2 is distributed in the southern region of the Gulf of California. At high temperatures, it shows metabolic responses that produce large amounts of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to cope with thermal stress. In addition to mitochondria, phosphagens are suggested as one mechanism for rapid ATP production in this species. title: Repeated Fire Increases Soil Pyrogenic Carbon Storage in Alaskan Tundra
abstract: Pyrogenic carbon in permafrost systems is largely unaccounted for in existing soil carbon inventories and earth system models. We assessed a proxy for pyrogenic carbon along a chronosequence of repeat burns and adjacent, unburned sites in Alaskan tundra. Using Fourier Transformed‐Infrared (FT‐IR) spectroscopy, we quantified aromatic carbon, likely of pyrogenic nature, by aggregating carbon functional groups to create a measure of the relative abundance of aromatic carbon. title: Lithium distribution and sediment provenance in Urmia Lake, northwestern Iran
abstract: Introduction: Urmia Lake in northwest Iran is the world’s second-largest hypersaline lake and has been proposed as a potential Li resource. However, the Li content, sediment provenance, and climatic controls on Li preservation in its sediments remain insufficiently constrained. This study evaluates the geochemical characteristics and resource potential of Li in Urmia Lake sediments. title: Nature-Based Tourism and Mangrove Forest Conservation in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: A Pathways–Pressures–Governance Framework
abstract: Nature-based tourism is widely promoted as a tool for conserving tropical forests, yet evidence that it protects forests is thin and context-dependent. This study examines when nature-based tourism contributes to conserving the Bangladesh Sundarbans, the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest. Research on Sundarbans tourism has emphasised potential rather than forest outcomes, the relevant evidence has been analysed in separate silos, and the post-2022 surge in visitors and forest-edge resorts has not been examined. title: Conserving Colonial Order: A Review of Laws and Policies for Conserving Pacific Salmon in Canada
abstract: Since its emergence, conservation biology has been framed as a discipline focused on preserving biodiversity. Less often acknowledged is that conservation is shaped by cultural assumptions about how, why, when, where and by and for whom it is designed and applied. Failing to recognize these assumptions risks reinforcing unjust systems of power rooted in historical forces that continue to shape present‐day realities. title: Application of SWOT analysis and stakeholder engagement to identify strategic priorities for water resources management in Nunavut
abstract: This study investigates the biophysical, sociocultural, regulatory and institutional dynamics that influence water management in Nunavut, Canada. Twenty-two interviews were conducted, followed by a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) analysis to identify strategic priorities for policymakers to improve Nunavut’s water management system. abstract: Bird-related offshore wind curtailment is increasingly used to reduce collision risk during periods of intense bird migration, but its energy and electricity-market consequences depend strongly on when curtailment occurs. This study combines a historical analysis of Dutch Start/Stop events with a forward-looking electricity-market assessment. abstract: Quorum sensing-driven biofilm formation is a key contributor to the persistence and multidrug resistance (MDR) of pathogenic bacteria, presenting a major challenge in combating infectious diseases. Probiotic quorum-quenching (QQ) bacteria represent a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics by suppressing quorum sensing-dependent virulence in MDR pathogens and simultaneously enhancing fish growth, immunity, and overall health. abstract: We explore examples of how the wave equation (especially when dissipation/attenuation effects are included) and the diffusion equation can intersect across the undergraduate physics curriculum, namely, in E&M, mechanics, and thermal physics. We note both physical and mathematical similarities in problems ranging from fluid mechanics, plasma physics, oceanography, and geophysics. title: Bioinspired trajectory tracking control of an underactuated robotic fish using prescribed-time and prescribed-performance control
abstract: Fish swimming couples rhythmic body deformation, distributed coordination, and environmental interaction to produce propulsion and maneuvering. This study asks how these principles can inspire trajectory regulation for an underactuated robotic fish. A three-joint body-caudal model driven by a coupled central pattern generator is combined with prescribed-performance guidance, a filtered reduced-order observer, and a bounded prescribed-time regulator. title: Impacts of dams’ operation and associated reservoirs on sandbar availability: a socioecological assessment of the Madeira River (Amazon Basin)
abstract: Despite the key role of sandbars in riverine socioecological systems, the impacts of dams on sandbars are overlooked. We analyzed how the operation of the Jirau and Santo Antônio dams and the formation of their reservoirs have impacted the distribution, dynamics, and use of sandbars on the Madeira River, Amazon Basin. We compared sandbar area before, during, and after dam construction across upstream, downstream, and between-dam stretches, using remote sensing data. abstract: Elevated levels of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in aquatic environments pose risks to ecosystem integrity and human health through fish consumption. This study assessed PTE concentrations in water and edible muscle tissues of six fish species ( Labeo rohita, Sperata seenghala, Rita rita, Cirrhinus mrigala, Cyprinus carpio, and Gudusia chapra ) from Rasul Barrage, Punjab, Pakistan, and evaluated human health risks using total and bioaccessible PTE concentrations following simulated gastrointestinal digestion. title: Recent advances in transcriptome research in fishes: A review
abstract: Transcriptomic studies have allowed researchers to examine gene activity across the genome and gain insight into many areas of fish biology. This review, following PRISMA guidelines, synthesizes recent studies on fish development, aquaculture, physiology, immunity, nutrition, toxicology, and evolution. abstract: The present research aims to identify the determinants of the demand for recreational use of a peri-urban freshwater wetland, Deepor Beel, located in the Northeastern region of India. Using the individual travel cost method, primary data were collected from 287 on-site visitors through systematic random sampling, and Poisson count data model were estimated for the annual number of visits under the status quo and under a hypothetical scenario of improved site quality with an entry fee. abstract: Deciphering how microbes co-evolved with early Earth's redox conditions helps us understand life's adaptation to early Earth environments. abstract: Spatial population synchrony, broadly defined as the correlated temporal dynamics of a population metric (e.g. abundance, biomass or growth rates) across sampled areas, is a central theme in ecology. Here, we investigated spatial synchrony in the abundance of 38 fish species from the Jirau Reservoir, a large impoundment in the Amazonian basin, over a decade. abstract: Biological invasions are an increasing threat to Antarctic ecosystems under ongoing climate change and expanding human activity. The non-native fly Trichocera maculipennis has progressively expanded its distribution on King George Island, transitioning from synanthropic populations associated with scientific stations towards natural Antarctic environments. abstract: Urbanization significantly alters watershed runoff, increasing peak flows, reducing base flows, and degrading river ecosystems. abstract: The lack of demographic data for many endemic cold-water fishes limits effective conservation planning in the Trans-Himalayan region. This study presents the first comprehensive assessment of the population dynamics and exploitation status of the monotypic cyprinid Diptychus maculatus Steindachner, 1866, which inhabits the Indus tributaries of Ladakh, India. abstract: This study analyzes global research trends in Atmospheric Water Harvesting (AWH) and reviews the underexplored issue of harvested-water quality. A bibliometric analysis of 332 publications revealed that water quality is the least studied aspect of AWH, limiting assessment of its applications and commercial viability. abstract: This qualitative literature review reexamines the corporate turnaround of PT Pembangunan Jaya Ancol Tbk (PJAA) by integrating contemporary scholarship with its newly available unaudited consolidated statements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. abstract: Discussion about abrupt changes in the Sahara at the end of the African Holocene Humid Period has generally remained qualitative. It provides essential context for understanding the increasing threat landscape, exemplified by a 900 per cent rise in cyber breaches targeting operational technology in ships and ports in 2023. Protein-mediated metabolite exchange across the double-membrane plastid envelope is essential for plant cell function. abstract: Shellfish allergens exhibit significant molecular diversity across crustacean taxa, yet the allergen repertoire of stomatopods remains largely unexplored. abstract: In rural and urban Kenya, reliance on groundwater resources has expanded rapidly to meet the rising domestic and agricultural demands. title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
abstract: Islands account for a disproportionate share of global biodiversity 1 , yet insects, including invaluable pollinators such as bees 2 , remain underrepresented in island biogeography research 3 . Here we present a global checklist of island bees, recording 4,147 species across 305 islands. Although islands comprise only about 6% of the Earth’s land area, they support around 20% of known global bee diversity, and 42% of insular species are endemic, making up around 8% of all known bee species. title: Fault‐Related Structure Revealed From Surface‐Wave Attenuation Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on Dark Fiber
abstract: Blind fault mapping requires dense observations over large areas, and distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) provides a viable solution using dark fibers. Seismic attenuation is sensitive to fault‐related structure but relies on reliable amplitude measurements. In DAS data, amplitudes are distorted by non‐attenuation effects, including non‐uniform coupling and small‐scale heterogeneity, limiting their direct use for attenuation imaging. title: Integrating water temperature, conductivity, and streamflow to assess the impact of watershed dynamics on chattahoochee river in the United States
abstract: Rivers are essential for sustaining human activities, ecological balance, and water supply. However, urbanization remains a major factor ​controlling quality of rivers. Several studies have been conducted to examine hydrological processes and watersheds impacts on river water quality; yet fewer studies have only utilized high-frequency monitoring data or considered few parameters like temperature and conductivity alone to capture the effects of urbanization on water quality dynamics in natural and engineered river systems. title: Changes in subfossil chironomid and cladoceran assemblages along water depth in Swiss lowland lakes
abstract: Aquatic invertebrate remains in lake sediments can potentially be used to provide information on past changes in water depth based on sediment records. However, only limited data are available on the distribution of invertebrate remains across varying water depths in stratified Central European lowland lakes. We analysed fossil chironomid and cladoceran assemblages from surface sediments sampled along ten transects of six Swiss lowland lakes with the aim of exploring the relationship between the distribution of species assemblages of these indicator groups and water depth. title: UAV-derived land surface temperature of Paclele Mici Mud Volcano, Romania
abstract: The Pâclele Mici Mud Volcano, located in Buzău County, Romania, is a unique geological formation characterised by active mud volcanism. This study employs unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with a low-cost thermal sensor to derive high-resolution land surface temperature (LST) maps of the volcano and its surroundings. Using a combination of nadir RGB and Thermal UAV imagery, detailed orthoimage and thermal maps with sub-meter spatial resolution were generated. title: Evaluation of polydopamine-mediated immobilization of antimicrobial compounds on titanium surfaces
abstract: Implant-associated infections remain a major clinical challenge, motivating the development of antimicrobial surface coatings that can prevent bacterial colonization while supporting tissue integration. Here, titanium surfaces were functionalized with polydopamine (PDA) and subsequently coated with three synthetic antimicrobial peptides (GN-2, GN-4, and IDR-1018) or chlorhexidine (CHLX). title: Characterising long-term trends and spatiotemporal dynamics of ambient gamma radiation dose rates alongside exploratory meteorological factors
abstract: Ambient gamma radiation constitutes an important component of environmental background radiation and is crucial for evaluating public exposure. In China, a nationwide survey conducted between 1983 and 1990 established the baseline for ambient gamma air-absorbed dose rates, with a nationwide range of 2.4–340.8 nGy h −1 . However, long-term spatiotemporal variations remain poorly documented due to limited publicly available monitoring data. title: Identification and characterization of unique plastic degrading bacteria from the east Kolkata wetlands
abstract: Plastic pollution is an environmental issue that has been highlighted by scientists and activists for years. While most definitely being cheap to produce and having a myriad of uses, these polymers take anywhere from 20 to almost 500 years to effectively decompose, thus, continuing to remain in the environment for decades when carelessly discarded. As a consequence of weathering forces, they erode into microscopic particles in the environment, eventually contaminating water and food sources, and entering living tissues. title: Mapping soil hydropedological response groups to analyse patterns of observed landslide occurrence at catchment scale in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa
abstract: Landslides are widespread natural hazards, often driven by complex interactions between terrain, hydrology and soil properties. This study investigates the hydropedological characteristics of soils in relation to mapped landslide sites near Port St Johns and Lusikisiki in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. The Soil-Landscape Inference Model (SoLIM) was used to produce a rule-based digital soil map of Hydropedological Response Groups (HRGs) representing soil–water dynamics across landscape positions. title: Hydrogeophysical characterization of heterogeneous aeolian dune deposits through integrated ERT, GPR, sedimentological and hydraulic analyses: the Montgrí dune system (NE Spain)
abstract: Aeolian dune systems commonly exhibit strong multiscale heterogeneity that controls groundwater flow, moisture distribution, and geophysical responses. This study investigates the stabilized continental dune field of Baix Empordà (NE Spain) through the integration of electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), ground-penetrating radar (GPR), grain-size analysis, and laboratory hydraulic measurements. title: Factors Influencing Sports Tourism Development in the Andaman Tourism Cluster
abstract: This research aimed to conduct a confirmatory factor analysis of factors influencing sports tourism development in the Andaman Tourism Cluster and to examine the causal relationships among selected factors—namely sports tourism purpose, participants, settings, and impacts—and their effects on the supportive factors for sports tourism development in the Andaman Tourism Cluster. The sample comprised 540 Thai residents of the Andaman Tourism Cluster, Thailand, including Phuket, Krabi, Trang, Phang Nga, Ranong, and Satun provinces. title: Introgression among major phylogeographic lineages alters phenology and fitness of Klickitat River spring-run Chinook Salmon
abstract: Objective Klickitat River spring-run Chinook Salmon (KRSC) are primarily an interior stream-type lineage stock but have experienced introgression from other Columbia River phylogenetic lineages. We aimed to characterize the genetic stocks present, quantify interlineage introgression, and assess its effects on migration timing and individual fitness to inform genetic management in this system. title: Designing a multi-stakeholder platform to advance sustainable groundwater management: case study of Jaffna Peninsula in Sri Lanka
abstract: Worldwide, aquifer management faces anthropogenic and climatic, social, and groundwater challenges. The Jaffna Peninsula in northern Sri Lanka exemplifies these issues, including overextraction, unregulated pumping, pollution, inadequate financing, and weak governance. Viewing groundwater as a private resource has driven exploitation, with most users prioritizing short-term gain over sustainability. title: Carbon Content and Sequestration of Mangrove Stands and Litter in the Pantai Cemara Mangrove Ecosystem, West Lombok
abstract: Mangrove forests play an important role in climate change mitigation through their capacity to store carbon in biomass. This study aimed to estimate carbon stocks and CO₂-equivalent values in mangrove stands and litter in the Pantai Cemara mangrove ecosystem, Lembar Selatan Village, West Lombok Regency, Indonesia. An exploratory-descriptive approach was employed, with purposive sampling conducted in two clusters, each comprising three observation transects. title: The Role of the “Ornitovo” Museum and Educational Centre in Visitors’ Spatial Cognition and Information Acquisition within the “Ujście Warty” National Park
abstract: The study examines the role played by the Museum and Educational Centre (MEC) in relation to visitors’ spatial cognition, infrastructure evaluation, information acquisition, and self-reported modifications of visiting plans within the “Ujście Warty” National Park (UWNP). The analysis is based on data from 249 structured field interviews conducted in the northern and southern parts of the UWNP, complemented by cognitive maps created by 156 respondents and rank-based evaluations of tourism infrastructure. title: Earth Observation for syntropic climate-adaptive urban planning in Santa Cruz de Tenerife
abstract: Climate adaptation in island cities requires integrated environmental diagnosis to guide ecological regeneration and urban planning. This study develops a framework linking Earth observation and territorial indicators to syntropic planning in Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Ecological connectivity, land surface temperature, runoff potential, soil organic carbon and green-space proximity were integrated on a 250 m grid comprising 1,542 cells with complete data. title: Method for using spectral flow data to predict vortex-induced vibration onset of static structures
abstract: Spectral representations of vortex-shedding behavior, such as airfoil data derived from computational fluid dynamics or experiment, can support the efficient identification of potential vortex-induced vibration onset. However, the use of such data is hindered by the myriad practical considerations required to scale, filter, and rank the risk of overlap between natural frequencies and shedding frequencies. title: Seasonal and spatial dynamics of in-channel water bodies on a river sandbar and associated macroinvertebrate communities
abstract: In-channel water bodies (ICWBs) on river sandbars, including backwaters and riverine ponds shaped by hydrological disturbance, remain poorly understood with respect to their seasonal and fine-scale spatial dynamics. We investigated the environmental conditions and benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages in ICWBs formed around traditional wood-based river training structures ("Seigyu") within a single sandbar in a regulated river in central Japan. title: Temporal Trends in Extreme Precipitation Events in Eight Flood‐Prone US Inland Cities (1981–2023)
abstract: Extreme precipitation is one of the leading drivers of hydrometeorological hazards and urban flood risk across the United States. However, most previous analyses focus on broad geographic scales, often obscuring the local variability and urban microclimate effects critical for understanding risk in metropolitan areas. This study investigates temporal trends in the frequency and magnitude of extreme precipitation events at the HUC12 watershed scale in eight flood‐prone inland US cities for 1981–2023. title: Application of Sentinel-2 Level 1C satellite imagery for Inland Surface water Bodies detection in temperate climates based on water indices
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of selected spectral indices – Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) and Sentinel Water Mask (SWM) – for detecting surface water using Sentinel-2 Level 1C satellite imagery in temperate climate conditions. Analyses were conducted for two study areas in the middle Vistula River basin, including the main river channel, tributaries and small water bodies. title: The spatiotemporal evolution mechanism of enterprise-led organic agriculture: Evidence from Shandong Province
abstract: This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023, we combine spatial statistical analysis, Local Moran's I, two-way fixed-effects regression, and robustness checks. title: An equivalent source method with additional sources for three-dimensional acoustic scattering by gas-filled spheres
abstract: The conventional equivalent source method (ESM) avoids singular integrals in the reconstruction of exterior acoustic fields but can exhibit large numerical errors near characteristic wavenumbers. This study investigates a strategy incorporating additional sources for three-dimensional acoustic scattering, using idealized gas-filled spheres as analytical benchmarks. title: Operations risk management for aircraft engines maintenance, repair, and overhaul
abstract: In the business of military maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO), it is necessary to embark on a risk management process to alleviate difficulties such as business productivity, lack of oversight, wasted resources, disjointed strategy, financial instability, ineffective planning and decision-making, and poor departmental integration. Risk management using Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and a discrete event simulation scheme were investigated in this paper. A bow-tie method was used to collect data from 19 departments. title: Estimating reproductive rates of Fisher (Pekania pennanti) and Northern River Otter (Lontra canadensis) in North Dakota from post-mortem carcasses
abstract: Information about reproduction is a critical component of wildlife species population monitoring, particularly game species. Evidence of reproductive activity from animal carcasses is often used in lieu of direct observations for secretive mesocarnivores. Fisher (Pekania pennanti) and Northern River Otter (Lontra canadensis) have expanded their populations in North Dakota over the past two decades, which has resulted in regulated trapping seasons for the two species. abstract: Objective To examine how governance is conceptualised under transdisciplinary conditions and identify implications for comprehensive health approaches. title: Influence of tile-drainage water on groundwater nitrate concentrations within a saturated riparian buffer zone
abstract: Saturated riparian buffers (SRBs) are edge-of-field conservation practices that divert tile drainage into riparian soils to reduce nitrate delivery to streams, but the long-term response of saturated-zone groundwater to repeated tile-water inputs remains uncertain. This study evaluated 6 years of tile-flow, nitrate-nitrogen (NO 3 -N), and chloride data from an SRB in central Illinois to determine whether tile diversion altered groundwater NO 3 -N concentrations or caused multi-year nitrate accumulation. title: Assessment of heavy metal contamination hotspots in the Ramsar-designated East Kolkata Wetlands
abstract: Urban wetlands worldwide are increasingly impacted by anthropogenic effluents, leading to heavy metal accumulation with significant ecological and human health implications. This study presents an assessment of heavy metal contamination in the East Kolkata Wetlands (EKW), a Ramsar-designated wetland in India where sediment samples from fifteen sites encompassing industrially influenced and peripheral zones were analysed for heavy metals including Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Cobalt, Copper, Lead, Manganese, Mercury, Molybdenum, Nickel, Selenium, Vanadium, and Zinc. abstract: H14 avian influenza viruses (AIVs) are rare, with limited data on their circulation in mainland China. This study investigated the ecological origins and zoonotic potential of H14 viruses in southern China. Active surveillance was conducted in Guangdong (2022–2025). The isolates underwent full-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Receptor binding specificity for avian- and human-type receptors was evaluated using a solid-phase assay. title: Mechanical recyclability and soil-burial degradation of melt-synthesized poly(butylene succinate-co-suberate)
abstract: Bio-based aliphatic polyesters such as poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) offer complementary end-of-life options, but the effect of copolymer composition on mechanical recyclability and degradation under soil-burial conditions remains insufficiently resolved. This study compares mechanical recyclability and soil-burial mass loss of a melt-synthesized PBS copolymer containing 10 mol% suberate (PBS-co-10-SubA) relative to commercial PBS and, for the soil-burial study, neat PBS synthesized in-house. title: Metabolic retraction and virulence gene repertoire expansion in a tropical urban river microbiome under dry-season stress
abstract: Anthropogenic pollution and seasonal flow reduction concentrate untreated organic waste in tropical rivers, yet the coupled response of microbial metabolism and virulence gene repertoires remains poorly understood. title: Relevance of traditional knowledge of food preservation for disaster preparedness and climate change adaptation in Pacific Islands: A case study from Nabuna Village, Koro Island
abstract: Pacific Island communities face significant challenges from climate-related hazards, particularly tropical cyclones, which can disrupt food systems and undermine food security. Traditional Knowledge (TK) provides locally grounded knowledge of environmental conditions, seasonal patterns, food preservation and weather observation, but its transmission and use are changing alongside sociocultural and technological developments. abstract: The expansion of the Linearbandkeramik (LBK; ca. 5400–4950 BCE) represents one of the most significant episodes of prehistoric population movement during the Neolithisation of Europe. Although migration is widely accepted as the principal mechanism of this expansion, the roles of ecological adaptation, population pressure and environmental constraints remain debated. title: Reconstructing Constitutional Recognition of Indigenous Peoples as Justiciable Collective Rights
abstract: Constitutional recognition of Indigenous peoples has expanded across contemporary legal systems, yet it often remains declarative rather than enforceable. This study examines how recognition can be transformed into justiciable rights through a structured constitutional framework. title: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
abstract: Undocumented and poorly known species spanning Linnean and Wallacean biodiversity shortfalls pose a major challenge to conservation due to the uncertainty they introduce. To address this, we developed a novel pluralistic approach that accounts for sampling gaps, spatial patterns, environmental associations, and varying conservation needs simultaneously, using amphibians as a case study. abstract: The epistemologies based on the terra firma framework fall short in interpreting the relationship and transcendence of land and water concerning the river islands ( chars ). abstract: The immediate cause of debris-flow cones formation was the short-lived but intense rainfall on 26 June 2020, which affected catchments of small rivers (ranging from several dozen to 200 km2) located in the Carpathian Foothills (300–500 m a.s.l.). The issue of debris-flow cones formation is presented in the context of the geomorphological effects of flash floods in selected catchments of the middle San River basin during the June 2020 events. abstract: Powerline ignitions lead to disproportionately large fires, accounting for about a quarter of the most destructive fires in California’s history. In response, electric utilities have deployed fire mitigation strategies, including line treatments and strategic de-energization. abstract: As one of the first identified persistent, mobile, and toxic (PMT) substances, melamine poses a potential threat to aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: Patterns of influenza in Iraq: Sentinel surveillance 2021–2025
abstract: Seasonal influenza affects individuals of all age groups and represents a significant global public health concern. In Iraq, influenza surveillance is a part of the national surveillance framework for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). This cross-sectional study described the epidemiological characteristics of ILI/SARI cases and circulating influenza viruses using data from six sentinel surveillance sites across Iraq between November 2021 and December 2025. Demographic and clinical data were collected and respiratory specimens were tested using RT-PCR.

abstract: Plastic products are an intrinsic and pervasive part of modern human life. Generally, people find plastics convenient and affordable, but largely overlook their environmental impacts due to limited awareness. The purpose of this study was to apply audience segmentation using knowledge gap theory to identify the characteristics of segments within the U.S. public with low knowledge and perceptions of the impacts of plastic use. abstract: This research seeks to uncover spatial and temporal trends relating to the food contents of amphorae from Roman Gades, the modern Bay of Cádiz, from the second century BC through the second century AD. Earlier scholarship on amphorae from southern Spain has primarily focused on single sites and highlighted olive oil production. abstract: Citizens, firms and civil-society organisations usually learn of decisions that alter protected areas only through the official record. This article examines how far that record allows outsiders to verify a governance transition at Butrint National Park, Albania's first World Heritage property. In January 2022 the park lost 802.2 ha (8.5 per cent) of its surface. abstract: Governments worldwide have adopted hydrogen strategies to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, yet Japan lacks a comprehensive assessment of domestic hydrogen demand. This study estimates hydrogen demand and associated carbon requirements in industry and transportation using a stoichiometric approach and analyses their spatial and temporal distributions. This paper reviews two forms of photographic angles-only observation: continuous or shutter-segmented trails from passive reflective satellites and timed point images from flashing geodetic satellites. abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a commensal bacterium involved in many healthcare-associated infections, sometimes through the formation of biofilm on invasive vascular devices in intensive care units. abstract: The tilapia hatchery business managed by the Aquafarm Patommo group continues to face several challenges, including unstructured production and financial recordkeeping, limited operational control, and a lack of data-driven decision-making. This community service program aims to strengthen the group's business management capacity through the implementation of a Business Management Information System integrated with a Smart Production System. abstract: Anthrax, caused by Bacillus anthracis, remains a persistent zoonotic threat across African savannas, yet its transmission dynamics are poorly understood in regions with limited surveillance systems. abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens biofuel feedstocks through drought, salinity, temperature extremes, flooding and interacting stressors. abstract: The current methods used to assess recreational fish stocks require substantial time and monetary investment. Constraints become more prevalent in large management zones with numerous waterbodies. The popularity of online angling platforms presents an opportunity for fisheries managers to enhance monitoring effort beyond the scope of what can be achieved in a costly, limited field season. abstract: The groundwater systems near nuclear power plants (NPPs) are critical pathways for possible radionuclide migration, both during normal operation and during accidental events. title: PROGRESS AND INTER-STATE DISPARITIES IN THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS IN INDIA: A DESCRIPTIVE ANALYSIS
abstract: India's composite score on the NITI Aayog SDG India Index rose from 57 in 2018 to 71 in 2023–24. This paper examines whether this national progress has been uniform across goals and states. It has two objectives: to examine the trends in India's overall and goal-wise SDG performance, and to analyse the extent and pattern of inter-state and inter-zonal disparities in SDG attainment. abstract: Anthropogenic soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity and ecosystem health. This study evaluated gypsum, polyacrylamide (PAM; solid and solution forms), biochar, peat, NanoBind (NB), Liquid Fulvic (LF), Liquid Organo Hume (LOH), and Humalite for remediating brine-affected, saline-sodic subsoil. abstract: , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. abstract: Energy devolution in Kenya has progressed unevenly, with many counties yet to complete their County Energy Plans (CEPs), posing challenges for integration into the forthcoming Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP). A key gap lies in translating qualitative, needs-based insights from county planning documents into quantitative inputs for energy demand modelling. abstract: Insect pollination supports biodiversity in natural and agricultural systems. However, increasing beekeeping activity raises concerns about the impacts of managed Apis mellifera on wild bees, already threatened by land-use change, agricultural intensification, pesticides, climate change, and invasive species. title: Estimation and Analysis of Solar Radiation Components on Horizontal and Tilted Surfaces in Jadu City, Libya
abstract: Accurate assessment of solar radiation on horizontal and inclined surfaces is essential for the design and optimization of photovoltaic systems, solar collectors, and solar-based building applications. This study estimates the global, diffuse, and beam components of solar radiation in Jadu, Libya, using a validated mathematical model based on solar geometry and the modified Ångström-type relationship. title: PET Accelerates the Decomposition of HDPE During Co-Pyrolysis: A Non-Additive Interaction from Thermogravimetry to Bench Scale
abstract: Post-consumer polyolefin waste sent to pyrolysis commonly carries poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET), yet yield and kinetic models for such feeds often treat their components as decomposing independently. We tested that assumption by comparing the thermogravimetric response of blends of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and PET with the mass-weighted sum of the pure polymers measured in the same campaign, in single runs at 10, 20 and 50 % PET. title: Listening with others: fostering empathy and relationships with nature through immersive soundscape experiences
abstract: Empathy and nature connectedness provide a key motivational basis for positive conservation behaviour, yet dominant framings treat ‘nature’ as a generalised, abstract category rather than attending to relationships with specific species. Multispecies thinking offers a more relational alternative, but how it might be cultivated in practice remains underexplored. title: Evidence for subglacial flooding in labyrinthine channels on Devon Island, Nunavut, Canada
abstract: Devon Island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago was covered by the thin (<1000 m), cold-to-polythermal based Innuitian Ice Sheet over the course of at least three glacial expansions during the last glacial cycle. As a result, the inland plateau region of the island is incised by abundant subglacial and lateral meltwater channels. Some sets of bedrock-carved subglacial channels on Devon Island bear a striking resemblance to the morphology of The Labyrinth in Antarctica, which formed subglacially by the episodic drainage of a subglacial lake. title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Rhopalaea crassa (Ascidiacea, Aplousobranchia, Diazonidae) and phylogenetic analysis
abstract: In this study, we determined the complete mitochondrial genome of Rhopalaea crassa (Herdman Citation1880), a solitary ascidian belonging to the family Diazonidae. The mitochondrial genome of R. crassa is 15,413 bp in length, containing 13 protein-coding genes, 24 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes. The mitochondrial gene arrangement of R. crassa differs from those reported from previously sequenced Aplousobranchia mitogenomes. abstract: The reasonable layout of functional elements in garden landscape space involves multiple factors, such as the number and area of patches of different landscape types, the degree of landscape fragmentation, and other objectives. There are complex nonlinear interactions between these factors. title: To What Extent Does The Railway Network Cover Africa?
abstract: The railway network is one of the most important infrastructure elements that connects different regions within a country. The extent to which the railway network is able to make a given area economically and socially accessible affects a country's economic performance and development opportunities. abstract: Here, we demonstrate a solvent‐free route to printed carbon electronics based on linseed stand oil, a bio‐derived binder used for centuries in painting and wood impregnation. abstract: Kenya is a frontline country for extreme weather and faces long droughts, flooding and heat waves. This study will focus on the broader, pervasive health risks associated with the reduction or catastrophic withdrawal of health services. Our aim is to determine what extreme weather hazards Kenya faces, and how resulting impacts on the population and health service can be mitigated, creating scalable tools that inform planning. title: Phase-wise variation in soil quality under shifting cultivation in the tropical highland red soils of the Eastern Ghats, India
abstract: Shifting cultivation (ShC) is a prominent land-use pattern in the tropical highlands of the Eastern Ghats. Although ecologically important, the phase-wise ecological and pedological footprint of ShC, particularly its association with soil quality, has received less attention. This study investigated variation in soil nutrient status and soil quality across different cultivation phases of shifting cultivation in the red soils of the Eastern Ghats. abstract: Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene-Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the "white continent" had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mammals. Several discoveries of fragmentary Eocene fossils suggest that Antarctica acted as a land bridge connecting South America to Australia, most notably marsupials. abstract: Groundwater in Himalayan intermontane basins represents a critical freshwater resource, yet the hydrogeological and geochemical controls governing trace metal(loid) mobilization remain poorly understood. abstract: Effective disease surveillance is crucial to predict, identify, and manage disease outbreaks in the shrimp aquaculture. A cross-sectional study was conducted to identify the major viral diseases occurrence in shrimp farms of Kerala. abstract: ABSTRACT Current carotenoid profiling in hen eggs and other functional foods is mostly limited to abundant free pigments, leaving minor and esterified carotenoid derivatives undercharacterized. abstract: The Surif area, located in the northwestern part of the Hebron Governorate, is a significant component of the Mediterranean vegetation in southern Palestine, owing to its diverse topography, climatic conditions, and geological formations, as well as its long history of human land use. title: Integrating transport planning and infrastructure to reduce urban flood risk in Accra, Ghana
abstract: Accra's repeated urban flooding has been predominantly attributed to rainfall variability and inadequate drainage; however, the structural role of transport infrastructure influencing flood exposure remains empirically underexplored. abstract: This research presents the first comprehensive analysis of medieval pottery (10th–13th centuries CE) from Mongolia, focusing on ceramics unearthed from the Medieval Border Systems. abstract: Animals face drastic variations in climatic conditions in their habitats, to which they can adapt. title: Speciation and biogeographical history in the European Alpine System: the radiation of Ranunculus sect. Euromontani (Ranunculaceae)
abstract: High mountain systems provide manifold preconditions for allopatric and sympatric speciation. We hypothesize that allopatric speciation due to geographical isolation of mountain chains, and sympatric speciation via allopolyploidy played major roles for a radiation within Ranunculus sect. Euromontani within the European Alpine System (EAS). title: Profiling insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles stephensi from Kenya using in-country nanopore sequencing
abstract: Background Malaria remains a threatening disease in Kenya, with over 70% of the population at risk of getting infected. Although vector control interventions such as indoor residual spraying and insecticide treated nets have significantly reduced transmission, the emergence of insecticide resistance and spread of invasive species such as Anopheles stephensi threaten these gains. This emphasizes the need for continuous insecticide resistance monitoring to inform NMCPs on the selection and deployment of effective vector control tools. Therefore, we developed a simple and cost-effective nanopore
institutions: Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology

title: Leveraging beaver biology to improve beaver‐related restoration efforts
abstract: Beaver ( Castor spp.) are keystone species with the ability to create wetland habitat, store water, and provide ecosystem services benefiting humans. Thus, interest has grown in restoring beaver populations. While considerable focus has been dedicated to the desirable outcomes of beaver‐related restoration, there has been less emphasis on their biological requirements, including processes such as colonization, demographic growth, and dispersal that underlie beaver establishment and population expansion. To achieve sustainable expansion at the landscape scale, a cycle must be repeated in which
institutions: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service

title: Hazard characterization of Alternaria toxins: filling data gaps on in vitro genotoxicity
abstract: Alternaria toxins are naturally occurring food contaminants with limited and often inconsistent genotoxicity and mutagenicity data. Within the European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC), an OECD-aligned in vitro testing strategy was applied to fill existing data gaps and to characterize the genotoxic potential of major Alternaria toxins using high-purity test materials. Mutagenicity was assessed using bacterial reverse mutation test (OECD TG 471) and SOS/umu assay, while chromosomal damage was assessed using the in vitro micronucleus (MN) assay (OECD TG 487) in TK6

National Institute of Health Dr. Ricardo Jorge

title: Novel insights into the specialized metabolism of the extremophile black yeast Hortaea werneckii and its modulation, unlocking its potential for compound discovery
abstract: Hortaea werneckii is a halotolerant yeast, found in various habitats and which specialized metabolism remains largely unexplored. Moreover, its chemical response to high salinities has not been thoroughly investigated. To address this gap, a large-scale metabolomic study based on HPLC-HRMS/MS was conducted on 64 strains, collected from different habitats worldwide, and cultivated both on saline and non-saline media. The culture media salinity significantly modulated the strains metabolomes, suggesting the yeast exhibits a specific chemical response to high salt concentrations, potentially link
institutions: Institut Des Substances et Organismes de la Mer
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Do rumen microbes use quorum sensing to shape digestion and methane?
abstract: Cattle, sheep, and goats live on plant fiber that they cannot digest themselves. The work is done by the microbes packed into the rumen, which convert that fiber into volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and microbial protein, and along the way, release methane. Bacteria in many other habitats coordinate their behavior by releasing and detecting small chemical signals, a process known as quorum sensing (QS). Where QS operates, it switches on the kinds of collective activity that would matter a great deal in the rumen: attaching to feed particles, building biofilms, secreting enzymes, and cross‐feeding.
institutions: National Center for International Research on Animal Gut Nutrition

title: Cognitive Communities of Interest at Different Scales
RISK PERCEPTION AS A MEDIATOR OF THE EFFECT OF FOREST FIRES AND DESTINATION IMAGE ON TOURIST VISIT INTENTION IN WAY KAMBAS NATIONAL PARK
abstract: Environmental crises such as forest fires frequently disrupt ecotourism sustainability by damaging natural landscapes and altering visitor psychological responses toward travel destinations. This study aims to analyze the mediating role of risk perception in explaining the impact of forest fire incidents and destination image on tourist visit intentions at Way Kambas National Park, uncovering novel empirical insights into post-crisis tourist behavior in protected forest areas. The research applies a quantitative approach utilizing a survey method. Data were gathered through structured question
journal: JELAJAH Journal of Tourism and Hospitality

title: Thermal processing alters physicochemical properties and flavor profiles of marinated sturgeon fillets: marinade-associated volatiles and oxidation-related aldehydes
abstract: Thermal processing strongly affects the physicochemical quality, taste, and aroma of marinated fish products, but how different heating methods alter the physicochemical properties and aroma profiles of pre-marinated sturgeon fillets remains unclear. In this study, steaming (ST), boiling (BO), air frying (AF), and sous-vide (SV) were compared at a core temperature of 72 °C. Among the cooked samples, AF produced the firmest texture and the highest sensory scores for taste, odor, and overall acceptability. BO caused the greatest reduction in total volatile abundance, including marked ethanol los
institutions: Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences
Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: Monogenean Parasites in Farmed Catfish: Pond Type Shapes Infestation Patterns
abstract: Monogeneans are ectoparasitic flatworms that attach to fish skin and gills using specialized haptors, causing epithelial damage, respiratory impairment, and increased susceptibility to secondary infections. Their distribution and severity are influenced by environmental and management factors, including aquaculture system type. This study characterized the biodiversity of monogeneans infecting African catfish ( Clarias gariepinus ) and evaluated variation in infestation patterns across culture container types in relation to host clinical and physiological indicators. Using a descriptive explor
journal: Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences

title: Environmental assessment of combined sewer overflow treatment using a vertical-flow constructed wetland: Freshwater saving, water reuse and carbon sequestration co-benefits
abstract: Climate change, rapid urbanisation, and intense precipitation are overloading conventional urban sewer systems. Constructed wetlands (CWs), as nature-based solutions, offer a sustainable alternative for treating combined sewer overflows (CSOs). This study evaluates the environmental impacts associated with the construction and operation of a vertical-flow (VF) CW system designed to treat CSOs in southern Chile using the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework. Carbon sequestration, an ecosystem service, was also estimated using a wetland-adapted RothC model coupled with a 500-year spin-up initia

title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of migrating wet and dry extremes: structural coherence and land-use associations across India
abstract: Global hydroclimatic extremes increasingly occur as cascading wet–dry sequences, challenging conventional single-hazard management. However, their spatiotemporal migration and associations with land-use patterns remain poorly understood. We present an integrated framework combining the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index, a spatio-temporal density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise algorithm, and phase-wise land-use/land-cover (LULC) exposure analysis to characterize the migration, structural coherence, and persistence of major wet and dry extremes across India

title: Gendered vulnerability and social protection in disaster contexts: evidence from Indonesia
abstract: Disasters are increasingly recognized as drivers of social and economic vulnerability, yet their impacts are unevenly distributed across populations. This study examines gendered vulnerability to disasters and the role of social protection in Indonesia. We linked nationally representative data from the 2023 Survei Sosial Ekonomi Nasional (SUSENAS), covering 894,356 individuals and 139,760 households, with district-level disaster mortality data from the 2024 Village Potential Statistics (PODES). Survey-weighted logistic and ordinary least squares regression models with two- and three-way intera

title: Factors Affecting Landuse/Landcover Changes in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Nigeria.
abstract: Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) change is one of the major environmental and socio-economic issues faced by rapidly developing areas of Nigeria. This research was conducted to identify causes of LULC changes among some selected communities in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Nigeria. Primary and secondary data was collected. Secondary data were gathered by means of questionnaire surveys, interviews with people on site and field observation. Data were presented through table and multiple regression analysis was used for analyzing relationship among changes of LULC with some so
journal: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science

title: Development of a High‐Strength Two‐Component Polyurethane Structural Adhesive for Extreme Cryogenic Environments
abstract: Structural adhesives used in liquefied natural gas (LNG) containment systems must retain reliable load transfer under severe thermomechanical mismatch near the boiling point of methane (approximately −163°C). Here, a series of two‐component polyurethane (PU) structural adhesives was developed using a phenyl‐based diol/diamine chain‐extender combination, an MDI/PM‐200‐based isocyanate‐terminated prepolymer, and silica microparticles. title: Apoptotic activity of crude polysaccharides derived from Spirulina platensis and Chlorella protothecoides in pancreatic cancer cells
abstract: This study investigated the apoptotic activity of crude polysaccharides derived from two food-related microalgae, Spirulina platensis (SP) and Chlorella protothecoides (CP), against pancreatic cancer cells. Crude polysaccharides were prepared from dried microalgal biomass through ethanol treatment, hot-water extraction, ethanol precipitation, acetone dehydration, and drying. SP and CP crude polysaccharides were assessed in BxPC-3 and HPDE cells using a WST-1 assay. publisher: Korean Society for Applied Biological Chemistry

title: Green hydrogen in the energy transition: integrating technology, economics, and deployment through a multi-dimensional framework
abstract: Green hydrogen has emerged as a strategic option for decarbonizing sectors in which direct electrification remains technically or economically constrained. However, technological advances in electrolysis do not necessarily translate into viable large-scale deployment, which depends on broader economic, resource, infrastructure, application, and institutional conditions. This study presents a structured, evidence-based literature synthesis supported by bibliometric analysis to identify the conditions and system-level interactions governing green hydrogen deployment.
