title: A Multivariate Empirical (MVE) simulation approach to modeling sunflower yield risk and productivity under alternative farming practices in Tanzania
abstract: Increasing domestic sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) production is important to Tanzania's efforts to reduce edible oil imports and improve smallholder livelihoods. Yet yields remain low and vary considerably among production systems. This study used a Multivariate Empirical (MVE) model within a Monte Carlo simulation framework to examine yield distributions and production risk under six combinations of seed and fertilizer use. We obtained nationally representative household data from the 2019/20 National Sample Census of Agriculture. The systems comprised local seed with no fertilizer (LS_F0)

title: PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes)
abstract: We present an update to the Phages and Integrated Genomes Encapsidated or Not reference database of DNA viral sequences (viral operational taxonomic units [vOTUs], mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) from global ecosystems. To reflect the inclusion of only virus size-fractionated metagenome- (virome-)derived vOTUs, we reintroduce the database as Phages Encapsidated ONlY.

title: Spatial modelling of the contemporary landscape structure of the Srebarna wetland system
abstract: Влажните зони са сред най-динамичните природни системи, характеризиращи се със сложна пространствена структура и висока чувствителност към измененията на хидроложкия режим.Целта на настоящото изследване е да се разработи и приложи интегриран подход за пространствено моделиране и количествена оценка на съвременната ландшафтна структура на влажната система "Сребърна" към 25 юли 2025 г.Изследването се основава на мултиспектрални сателитни данни Sentinel-2 Level-2A, цифров модел на релефа и данни от CORINE Land Cover (CLC) 2018, интегрирани в ГИС среда.За характеризиране на водните площи и растите

title: Reclaiming lands and waters: Communal conservation in the tropics of Guatemala
abstract: Communal conservation governance is becoming increasingly recognized for its critical importance in recovering and sustaining ecosystems. However, historic and ongoing paradigms of extraction, including those perpetuated by conventional norms in conservation and ecosystem stewardship, continue to undermine Indigenous and communal governance, land rights, and knowledges. To reaffirm prevailing Indigenous rights and wellbeing, Indigenous leaders drove the creation of several international legal and policy frameworks to strengthen Indigenous and communal sovereignty and self‐determination. title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems—from the Internet to the brain—derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length3–6. title: Evaluation of the potential and mitigation strategies of post-liquefaction residual deformations in heterogeneous fill soils through performance-based parametric simulations
abstract: Assessments of liquefaction hazards in heterogeneous reclaimed soils are often limited to safety factor-based triggering analyses (FSliq) without considering the consequences of post-earthquake residual deformation. This study aims to evaluate the reliability of FSliq as a single indicator for representing permanent deformation response, as well as to determine the optimal performance-based design threshold for soil improvement. title: Discovery and characterization of microbial GH18 chitinases exhibiting activity at low temperature from raw chilled prawns
abstract: Endo-chitinases (chitinases, EC 3.2.1.14) catalyze the hydrolytic cleavage of chitin ((1→4)-2-acetamido-2-deoxy-β-D-glucan) and are categorized in glucoside hydrolase (GH) families GH18 and GH19. Here, we report the identification and characterization of two novel cold-tolerant bacterial GH18 chitinases, CBI4 and CBI12, from Aliivibrio salmonicida and Aliivibrio logei, isolated from iced prawns ( Pandalus borealis ) caught in the North Atlantic. title: Fished to the Edge: Severe Overfishing Threatens Fish Stocks in Tanzania's Saline Rift Valley Lakes
abstract: The Saline Rift Valley Lakes (SRVLs) of Tanzania support important inland fisheries, but increasing fishing pressure threatens their sustainability. This study assessed the status of fish stocks in two Tanzanian SRVLs: Lakes Kitangiri and Singida. Data on catches, species composition, catch per unit effort, maturity stages, and length‐based indicators were collected from May to September 2023. Results indicate strong evidence of overfishing, reflected in declining catches and high exploitation rates. title: Bacterial microbiome diversity and geographic variation in cattle-associated Rhipicephalus microplus ticks from the Lao People's Democratic Republic: Insights from 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing
abstract: Background and Aim: The cattle tick Rhipicephalus microplus harbors diverse bacterial communities that may influence tick biology and pathogen ecology. However, information on its microbiome composition and geographic variation in the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) remains limited. This study aimed to characterize bacterial diversity, community structure, and potentially pathogenic bacterial genera associated with cattle-derived R. microplus ticks across three provinces of Lao PDR. Materials and Methods: Thirty adult R. microplus ticks were collected from 15 cattle at six locations

title: Looking South, marching East: the structural decoupling of Italian defence policy (1949–2027)
abstract: Italian defence policy is conventionally described as having turned south. This article asks whether that declaratory priority is matched by the way Italy actually allocates military resources. Drawing on MIDA, an original and openly audited dataset of Italian international missions (1949–2027), it separates three dimensions that existing accounts conflate – the institutional framework of a mission, its functional type, and the level of responsibility Italy assumes within it – and applies an explicit geographical coding rule that distinguishes NATO’s Eastern Flank from the Western Balkans and

title: Isofalcarintriol ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced β-cell dysfunction by targeting MIF to enhance mitophagy
abstract: Insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction are closely associated with impaired mitophagy, forming a core pathological mechanism in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study investigates the role of isofalcarintriol (IFT), a carrot-derived polyacetylene, in regulating mitochondrial function in GDM-related β-cells. Here, we use a high-fat diet-induced C57BL/6 J pregnant mouse model and high-glucose/palmitic acid (HG/PA)-treated MIN6 β-cells; IFT ameliorates hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, promotes β-cell maturation and proliferation, induces mitophagy, and enhances β-cell

title: Corporate Social Responsibility of Fintech in Building Microfinance for Self-Help Groups in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu
abstract: This research paper analyzes the way FinTech-driven Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities develop microfinance models for Self-Help Groups (SHGs), improving financial inclusion and circular economy practice in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, India. With increased digitalization, FinTech companies are more often using CSR funds via NGOs to extend interest-free microloans and digital literacy to facilitate SHG entrepreneurs, both men and women, to handle savings, repayments, and accounting through technology-enabled tools (Dinesh Kumar & Rahini, 2023; Anudevi, 2023). Based on secondary data
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: Ecological and economic impacts of increasing landscape connectivity in highly threatened ecological corridors of Tanzania
abstract: Ecological corridors facilitate the flow of ecosystem goods (e.g., wildlife movements) and services (e.g., water regulation) between protected areas, benefiting farmers and governments. To enhance landscape connectivity, farmers within ecological corridors are often encouraged to make pro-conservation decisions, ideally in a coordinated manner. These decisions, however, come along with costs to farmers (e.g., opportunity and transaction costs) as well as governments (e.g., mobilization and enforcement costs). title: Marketplace Diplomacy: The Political Economy of US–Soviet Sister‐City Relations, 1971–1991
abstract: This article situates US–USSR sister‐city initiatives within the history of Cold War trade and exchange, arguing that municipal twinning functioned not only as citizen diplomacy but also as a semi‐official mechanism for facilitating economic cooperation across ideological boundaries. Drawing on Soviet and American archival sources and periodicals, it demonstrates that Soviet cultural and diplomatic institutions actively courted US corporations, private donors, and municipal actors, challenging assumptions that exchange initiatives were primarily American‐driven. title: Development and Analytical Evaluation of a Silver Nanoparticles Functionalized SDBS Colorimetric Sensor for the Detection of Polystyrene Microplastics
abstract: A rapid colorimetric sensor based on AgNPs functionalized with sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (AgNPs-SDBS) was developed and analytically evaluated for the detection of polystyrene (PS) microplastics. AgNPs were synthesized by NaBH4 reduction and functionalized with SDBS, with 0.5 mM providing the most favorable plasmonic response. Surface modifications were supported by UV-visible, FTIR, TEM, PSA, and zeta potential analysis. Functionalization increased the Z-average from 29 to 46 nm, reduced the polydispersity index from 0.49 to 0.36, and shifted the zeta potential from -22.13 to -30.17 mV.

title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C 19 , C 24 , and C 29 Terpenoids
abstract: The terpenoid substrate analog 14‐ nor ‐farnesyl pyrophosphate (14‐ nor ‐FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18‐ nor ‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18‐ nor ‐GGPP) and 22‐ nor ‐geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (22‐ nor ‐GFPP) by GGPP synthase (GGPPS) and GFPP synthase (GFPPS), respectively. title: Geographic Structuring of Gut‐Content Bacterial Communities in Invasive Blackchin Tilapia ( Sarotherodon melanotheron ) Across Thailand: Site‐Level Environmental Associations and Implications for Invasion Ecology
abstract: The blackchin tilapia (Sarotherodon melanotheron) has rapidly expanded across Thailand, but how environmental conditions relate to its gut microbiota during invasion remains unclear. We examined gut-content bacterial communities at six sampling sites along the Gulf of Thailand using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing of 68 fish, alongside site-level water analyses (one composite sample per site; n = 6) and helminth screening. title: Transmission epidemiology and spatial characteristics of 1305 Chikungunya cases in Guangzhou, China from July to November 2025
abstract: From July to November 2025, Guangzhou, the capital city of Guangdong Province of China, went through a large-scale Chikungunya outbreak that 1305 cases were reported to Guangzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Guangzhou Health Supervision Institute) by November 11. The epidemic presented two waves and was influenced by the public health control measures, population mobility and climate change. institutions: Guangzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Tourist Carrying Capacity on the trail of the Site of Geological Interest ‘Portal do Palmiro’ (paleoburrow ‘Toca do Tatu’), Caminhos dos Cânions do Sul UNESCO Global Geopark (Brazil)
abstract: The Portal do Palmiro trail serves as the primary route to the Toca do Tatu Paleotoca, situated in the municipality of Timbé do Sul, which is part of the Caminhos dos Cânions do Sul UNESCO Global Geopark (CCSUGGp) in Brazil. Following the establishment of the geopark in the area, this location has emerged as a significant attraction for geotourism. Assessing the Tourist Carrying Capacity (TCC) is essential for alleviating the possible environmental consequences associated with visitor activity. institutions: Universidade do Sul de Santa Catarina
Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina

title: Unintended positive and negative consequences of climate adaptation interventions for Australia's native species
abstract: Climate adaptation interventions aim to reduce the vulnerability of biodiversity to climate change, but could have unintended consequences in agricultural landscapes where conservation and production goals intersect. We employed expert elicitation to complement a systematic search of peer-reviewed literature, identifying unintended consequences from climate adaptation interventions implemented for Australian native species in agricultural landscapes. title: Global monitoring of wildlife mortality through participatory science in near‐real time
abstract: Detection of wildlife mortality events is critical for timely conservation and natural resource management. We present an open‐source, web‐based, decision‐support tool that queries, aggregates, and summarizes participatory‐science data from iNaturalist to monitor mortality events worldwide. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using four case studies spanning taxonomic, spatial, and temporal scales. title: Preliminary identification of potential pigmentation-related candidate genes in the albino process of northern snakehead, Channa argus, by integrating whole-genome DNA methylation map and transcriptome data
abstract: Distinct body coloration enhances the economic value of commercially important fish species. In this study, we focused on black and albino C. argus and employed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) to systematically analyze, for the first time at single-base resolution, the differences in DNA methylation profiles across skin tissues between the two types. Supplemented by transcriptome analysis, we identified key genes involved in skin color formation. The proportion of high-quality clean reads obtained in this study exceeded 99%. title: Dose-dependent hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in BALB/c mice
abstract: Microplastics have emerged as pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern regarding their potential adverse effects on mammalian health. However, comprehensive evaluations of the dose-related hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) remain limited. This study investigated the effects of oral exposure to PS-MPs on hepatic and renal function in BALB/c mice. Animals were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 10/group) and orally administered 0 (control), 10, 20, or 30 mg PS-MPs/kg body weight/day for 28 consecutive days. title: Determinants of Climate Vulnerability Under SDG 13: Evidence From Urbanization, Institutions, Democracy, and Environmental Taxes in the EU
abstract: Climate change has increased the vulnerability of societies and economies to environmental risks, making the identification of factors that influence climate vulnerability an important policy issue. In line with Sustainable Development Goal 13 (Climate Action), understanding the factors associated with climate vulnerability is important for developing effective climate adaptation policies. This study examines the effects of urbanization, institutional quality, electoral democracy, and environmental taxes on climate vulnerability in 17 European Union countries over the period 1995–2023. title: Wound atlas of Atlantic salmon skin
abstract: The process of wound healing offers a window into how cells coordinate to maintain tissue integrity, repair damage, and restore tissue function. Wound healing in Atlantic salmon, a species of considerable ecological and economic importance, is a tightly coordinated process involving multiple cellular programmes that eventually lead to scarless repair. Here, we present the first single-nucleus atlas of healing salmon skin wounds, providing a comprehensive view of its cellular organisation over multiple timepoints. title: Dysregulated ASH1L-MUC1-CD133 axis promotes lung metastasis and reprograms the metastatic niche in SPOP-deficient prostate cancer
abstract: Metastasis remains the leading cause of mortality in prostate cancer (PCa). Loss-of-function mutations in SPOP, commonly observed in metastatic PCa, have undefined roles in the metastatic niche. Histone methyltransferase ASH1L plays a crucial role in leukemogenesis and is overexpressed in various solid tumors. abstract: The study aims to determine the aquifer characteristics of Gabasawa and its environs using multi-criteria decision analysis to provide sufficient information on groundwater potential zones. ‎Magnetic, elevation, and electromagnetic data were acquired using Magneto-meter and Audio ‎Magnetotelluric device. title: Spatiotemporal network analysis of synchronization, directional predictive dependence, and robustness in actual evapotranspiration dynamics across Iran
abstract: Long-term monitoring of actual evapotranspiration (ETa) is critical for assessing land–atmosphere water dynamics, yet optimizing monitoring networks requires a deeper understanding of spatial synchronization and predictive dependencies in water-limited environments. Utilizing GLEAM v4 satellite-derived data (1980–2023), we propose an integrated trend–topology–directionality framework to assess ETa variability across Iran. Development of Water Treatment HSSEC System to Support Net Zero Emissions in Maritime Vocational Education: Evidence from Politeknik Pelayaran Sumatera Barat
abstract: This study aims to describe the development process of the Water Treatment HSSEC as an initiative to support the achievement of Net Zero Emission at Politeknik Pelayaran Sumatera Barat. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE development model, which was limited to the analysis and design phases. title: Physicochemical Assessment of Ground Water including Heavy metal in Uttar Pradesh :A Review
abstract: Ground water serves as a critical freshwater asset across Uttar Pradesh alluvial plains, sustaining domestic needs, agricultural production and rural economies. Ground water is the primary source of drinking water for a large population in Uttar Pradesh India. Globally, ground water serves as the primary reservoir for domestic, agricultural and industrial requisites. title: Cremastocephalus (Asteraceae: Vernonieae), a new genus from Madagascar
abstract: Cremastocephalus (Asteraceae: Vernonieae) is described as a new genus from the Central and Eastern phytogeographical regions of Madagascar where it occurs in moist evergreen forests at low to mid‐elevation. It belongs to the subtribe Gymnantheminae by its woody habit, corymbiform capitulescence, deciduous inner phyllaries, tailed anthers, and tricolporate sub‐echinolophate pollen. title: The Gut Microbiota/Gut Brain/BDNF Axis Mediates Ginsenoside Re’s Neuroprotection in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Ginseng, as a traditional medicinal and edible resource, has shown potential in the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, particularly Parkinson’s disease (PD), through its active components, ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe). This study aimed to systematically investigate the neuroprotective effects and molecular underpinnings of total ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe) in a 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) induced PD mouse model, with a focus on gut-brain axis modulation. The results showed that GS and GsRe ameliorated motor deficits, reduced substant

Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: Generalizing the LoD transition space for continuous multi-scale representation using straight skeletons
abstract: Continuous multi-scale representation enables geographic features to evolve smoothly across Levels of Detail, avoiding abrupt transitions between independently generalized datasets. However, existing approaches provide limited support for complex transformations involving different geometric and topological configurations. This study generalizes the LoD Transition Space framework to represent continuous transformations between polygons, polylines, and points. The proposed approach uses straight-skeleton-based geometric primitives to construct continuous 2D + 1D transition volumes and decompose
institutions: Wrocław University of Environmental and Life Sciences

title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods
abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail 'Viviparus' sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. High-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography and microfossil extraction reveal key ecological adaptations: obligate ovoviviparity with up to 16 embryonic shells showing an axial developmental size gradient within the maternal b

title: Experimental and DFT Investigation of Fe-Modified TiO2-MoO3 Heterostructures for Microwave Absorption
abstract: The proliferation of high-frequency radar systems and electromagnetic interference (EMI) has created a growing need for highly efficient broadband radar-absorbing materials (RAM). This study investigates the dual-loss attenuation mechanisms of a novel Fe-doped Ti–Mo oxide heterostructure through experimental synthesis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the successful synthesis of the composite, revealing the coexistence of anatase TiO₂ and α-MoO₃ phases and providing a structural basis for investigating the incorporation of dilute Fe dopants. title: Evolution, convergence, and determinants of tourism eco-efficiency in Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies, 2010–2022
abstract: Tourism eco-efficiency benchmarks rarely place Chinese provincial destinations alongside ASEAN sovereign economies despite overlapping carbon footprints and divergent policy regimes. We assemble a balanced panel of Hainan Province and six ASEAN economies (Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam) over 2010–2022 (91 observations) and combine Super-SBM, rolling-window Malmquist, panel MLE/Tobit, and synthetic control. institutions: Hainan Vocational University of Science and Technology

title: Criminalizing ecocide beyond the Rome Statute: Comparative domestic approaches and lessons for environmental accountability in Bangladesh
abstract: Ecocide is an emerging concept in contemporary international environmental law and international criminal law jurisprudence. It has not yet been recognized as an independent international crime under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. However, the increasing scholarly discourse and domestic legislative initiatives have intensified discussions regarding criminal responsibility for severe environmental harm. title: Reporting the Fleet: News Writing of British Naval Reviews and the Construction of Imperial Identity Frameworks, 1773–1914
abstract: Framing Analysis theory posits that news writing functions as an ideological practice, jointly steered by power structures and media institutions within specific historical contexts, which systematically shapes collective cognition and directs identity formation. From 1773 to 1914, the news writing of British naval reviews constituted a pivotal site for the dynamic construction of imperial identity ideology. During this period, the dominant narrative framework underwent three significant structural transformations: evolving from an emphasis on “Monarchical Supremacy”, progressing to a discours
journal: Journal of History Society and Culture

title: Climate adaptation practices and their determinants among smallholder farmers in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur, Philippines
abstract: Climate change poses a significant threat to agricultural sustainability, particularly for smallholder farmers vulnerable to climatic variability and extreme weather. In the Philippines, recurrent floods and droughts continue to disrupt farm productivity and livelihoods. This study identifies key determinants of climate-adaptive practice uptake among farmers in the Adaptation and Mitigation Initiatives in Agriculture (AMIA) program, examining their socioeconomic characteristics and farming behaviors. Primary data were collected through validated questionnaire-guided interviews. Descriptive sta

title: Dental topographic metrics are not inherently taxon- or homology-free: lessons from a new, large dataset of carnivorous mammals (Carnivora, Hyaenodonta, and Metatheria)
abstract: Dental topographic metrics (DTMs) are a popular tool for studying diet in extinct vertebrates. These methods are thought to be largely taxon and homology-free, allowing for direct comparisons among species with dramatically different dental morphologies. Here, we test this assumption using a new, large dataset of 735 molar series representing 277 carnivorous mammal taxa, focusing on the three most commonly used DTMs: orientation patch count rotated (OPCr), convex Dirichlet’s normal energy (convex DNE), and relief index (RFI). All three metrics are strongly influenced by homology and phylogeny

title: Advocating environment through #SaveRajaAmpat in X: a corpus-assisted discourse study
abstract: Digital environmental advocacy on social media enables users to articulate environmental concerns and negotiate responsibility.this study examines how #saverajaampat functions as a linguistic and discursive resource in digital environmental advocacy, addressing the limited research on hashtag-based movements in this context.it analyses an X corpus of 161,756 tokens collected using Python.using antconc 4.3.1 and van Dijk's socio-cognitive discourse approach, this study investigates ideological polarisation across macro-, meso-, and microstructures within the #saverajaampat discourse.Word lists

title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
abstract: Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeO x electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐cente
institutions: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society

title: The identities of two enigmatic Atlantic Forest trees revealed: A new genus representing an ancient Ebenaceae lineage
abstract: Here we report the discovery of an enigmatic plant lineage from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest that remained unnamed in herbaria for many decades. Phylogenetic analyses based on nuclear ribosomal ITS and plastid regions ( atpB , matK , ndhF , psbA‐trnH , rbcL , trnL+trnL‐trnF , trnS‐trnG ), as well as on the whole plastid genome, revealed that the mysterious plants belong to an ancient lineage sister to the rest of the Ebenaceae. This new lineage is recognized here as a new genus ( Pindorama ) in a new subfamily (Pindoramoideae) within the Ebenaceae, enlarging the circumscription of this family
institutions: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro
Instituto de Pesquisas Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro
Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics

title: Ebselen impairs biofilm-associated infections by targeting ArgR and disrupting arginine homeostasis in Gram-positive pathogens
abstract: Biofilm-associated infections, particularly those caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), pose a major clinical challenge due to enhanced antibiotic resistance and metabolic adaptability. Here, we show that Ebselen, a small organoselenium compound, effectively disrupts mature MRSA biofilms and exhibits broad activity against biofilms formed by diverse Gram-positive pathogens. Using clinically relevant in vivo models, including implant-associated osteomyelitis and catheter-associated urinary tract infection, Ebselen significantly reduced bacterial burden and disease progre

title: Unraveling the Toxicological Mechanisms of PAHs in Respiratory Diseases Using Network Toxicology and Molecular Docking
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are persistent organic pollutants widely distributed in the environment, capable of entering human habitats through multiple pathways. However, the pathogenic mechanisms by which PAHs impact respiratory health remain inadequately understood. We aim to systematically investigate the core molecular mechanisms by which PAHs mediate the onset and progression of respiratory diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchiectasis, asthma, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Network toxicology methodologies were employed to integra
institutions: Hubei Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention

title: In Situ Green Synthesis of Antibacterial Copper Nanostructures on Fabrics for Water Filtration Applications
abstract: Diarrheagenic Escherichia coli is a major global health concern responsible for significant mortality, particularly among young children. Copper nanostructures (Cu-NSFs) exhibit antimicrobial activity against various pathogens; however, practical and stable immobilization remains challenging. In this study, Cu-NSFs were synthesized in situ on poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) cheesecloth, offering a one-step, time-efficient alternative to conventional ex situ nanoparticle incorporation methods. Orange peel extracts and ascorbic acid were effective as both reducing and stabilizing agents, mini

title: Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
abstract: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy-reversible metabolic suppression-may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. Dormant individuals form "seed banks" that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, creating a memory of past ecological dynamics. S
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Accumulation by legalization: the accelerated transformation of California’s drug war agrarianism
abstract: Legalization has profoundly altered the agrarian system of California’s (once) most valuable cash crop: cannabis. For decades, illicit cannabis reaped a ‘prohibition premium’ that kept prices and profits high. Small-scale growers formed an illegalized peasantry concentrated in remote areas of the state, shielded from detection by customary local norms. Legalization eliminated that premium, eviscerated local norms and glutted the market. Overproduction appears set to accomplish what prohibition never did: eradicate the vast majority of cannabis cultivators. In this paper, told through four indi

title: Millipede abundance and diversity decline in response to megafires in Australian temperate rainforest
abstract: Wildfires are increasing in severity, frequency and extent across many biomes. Litter invertebrates such as millipedes are diverse and functionally important in forests, but high‐severity fires incinerate their leaf litter habitat. In 2019–2020, ‘megafires’ burnt almost 10 million ha of vegetation in south‐eastern Australia, including large areas of temperate rainforest, which do not usually burn. We asked: (a) How does fire severity affect millipede abundance, species richness and composition? and (b) How specific are millipede species to rainforest or wet sclerophyll forest? One year after t

title: Risk Analysis for the Alfamart Warehouse Construction Project in Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan
abstract: The operational success and completion performance of a logistics warehouse construction project heavily depend on precise schedule adherence and rigorous budget control. In field execution, however, contractors frequently encounter unpredictable environmental factors that lead to severe schedule overruns and cost inflations. These challenges become particularly acute in large-scale facilities featuring wide-span structural steel framing erected over challenging peat soil geotechnics.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: Is Indigenous knowledge meaningfully represented in the IPCC AR6? A bibliometric meta-analysis
abstract: In recent global climatic and environmental reports, indigenous knowledges (IK) are recognised as essential to comprehending social-ecological systems and multi-scalar climate-society relationships. However, IK and indigenous peoples (IP) continue to be mostly excluded from important and powerful processes such as the UNFCCC and the IPCC reports. In the current (AR7) cycle of the IPCC, it is important to understand whether the last cycle (AR6) meaningfully engaged with IK and IP. Here, we present a multi-tiered bibliometric analysis of the literature cited in the AR6 report ( n = 46 145 citati

title: Out of the cradle: secondary expansion from a source lake is associated with loss of morphological distinctiveness in endemic Kamchatkan charrs ( Salvelinus )
abstract: The contribution of postglacial adaptive radiations to regional freshwater fish biodiversity remains debated. To test whether such radiations can give rise to new populations in neighboring ecosystems, we reconstructed the evolutionary history of the endemic Salvelinus malma assemblage of Lake Kronotskoe (Kamchatka). We traced the dispersal of endemic lineages from the lake into adjacent basins and quantified morphological divergence between lacustrine charrs and their derived populations. Using SNPs from SLAF-seq loci, we analyzed phylogeny, genetic differentiation, contemporary hybridization
institutions: Kamchatka State University named after Vitus Bering
Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution

title: Native plant biodiversity is underrepresented in restored and working grasslands of the Virginia Piedmont
abstract: Despite their high biodiversity and ecosystem service value, temperate grasslands have been disproportionately fragmented and degraded by agricultural expansion, development, disrupted disturbance regimes, and climate change. The native grasslands of the southeastern United States have lost over 90% of their historic range due to these pressures. We surveyed plant communities in 237 high-quality reference, working, fallow, and restored grasslands in the northern and central Piedmont of Virginia to compare the effects of agricultural land use on grassland biodiversity and to determine the effec

title: Ageing imprecision compounds the effects of fishing selectivity, increasing bias in estimates of growth parameters
abstract: Accurately estimating fish growth is critical for fisheries management, but growth parameter estimates are often affected by multiple sources of error. While the independent effects of ageing error and fishing selectivity are well documented, their combined effects remain unknown. This study used a simulation approach to determine how ageing imprecision and selectivity (logistic and dome-shaped) compound when estimating growth parameters across four rockfish (Sebastes spp.) life histories. Results demonstrated that ageing imprecision and selectivity exacerbate biases in growth parameter estima
institutions: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service Alaska Fisheries Science Center

title: Genetic variability within Triatoma sanguisuga complex in North America and the re-description of Triatoma ambigua Neiva, 1911, with specimens from Florida, USA
abstract: Triatoma sanguisuga is the most widely distributed triatomine vector in North America, occurring in at least 23 U.S. states and capable of transmitting Trypanosoma cruzi to humans. Historical morphological variability led to the description of several subspecies, but their taxonomic validity has remained unresolved. We integrated molecular (cytochrome b, n = 58; ITS-2, n = 23) and morphometric (18 characters, n = 82 specimens) data to reassess species boundaries within T. sanguisuga sensu lato. Four species-delimitation methods (GMYC, ABGD, mPTP, hierBAPS) consistently identified four divergen
institutions: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

title: OpenPrescribing Hospitals, an Open Access Analytics Platform for Hospital Medicines Use in England: Development and Implementation Study
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Secondary Care Medicines Data (SCMD) makes detailed data on medicines issued by National Health Service (NHS) hospital trusts in England openly available for the first time. These data provide an opportunity to understand medicine use patterns, highlight variation, and drive improvements in evidence-based practice, prescribing safety, and cost-effectiveness. However, this dataset requires extensive domain and technical knowledge to access, clean, transform, and link to other external sources before it can be used effectively. title: Non-canonical telomere repeat-binding factor 2 control of retinal development
abstract: Telomere repeat-binding factor 2 (TRF2) protects chromosome ends but also regulates extra-telomeric chromatin structure and function. Using zebrafish mutants, we show that complete loss of the gene encoding TRF2 (terfa) spares early retinal progenitor expansion yet later causes catastrophic Müller glia failure, loss of retinal lamination, genome-wide DNA damage and apoptosis. journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
State Key Laboratory of Environmental Geochemistry

title: Building bridges for effective inclusive emergency planning: Averting future crises and fostering resilience in US educational institutions through deaf- and disability-inclusive EOP minimum standards and delivery
abstract: Research on school-based emergency planning demonstrates that deaf and disabled students, instructors, and staff face considerable barriers to accessing potentially life-saving information, training, and response at United States (US) educational institutions. This article discusses the critical role that minimum standards for deaf and disability-inclusive emergency operations plans (EOPs) and individual emergency operations plans (IEOPs) could play in effective emergency planning and response for K-12 schools and institutions of higher education. title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Enhances the Thermal Susceptibility of Staphylococcus aureus in Cocultured Biofilms
abstract: Bacterial biofilms infect medical devices in hundreds of thousands of patients, resist antibiotic treatment, and cost the healthcare industry billions of dollars each year. Generating heat at the biofilm interface is a less-invasive alternative to explantation that has been shown to reduce bacterial populations of common pathogens such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. Most thermal susceptibility studies to date have investigated single-species biofilms. title: WATER LEVEL DYNAMICS AND SPATIAL CHANGES IN RIVER CHANNELS WITHIN THE UPPER DNIESTER BASIN
abstract: For the Dniester basin, assessing the current state of water availability is of crucial importance given its role in forming the water resources of Western Ukraine. Studies on long-term runoff dynamics of the Dniester and its tributaries indicate shifts in the water regime characteristics of the basin’s rivers under modern climate change conditions. A critical decline in water levels in the Dniester basin may pose risks to the functioning of the water management complex and the state of aquatic ecosystems. title: Molecular insights into bacterial Cr(VI) reduction: an eco-friendly and sustainable strategy of Cr(VI) detoxification
abstract: Hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) is a highly toxic, mobile and carcinogenic pollutant released primarily from industries such as tanning, electroplating, mining and metallurgy. Its persistence and bioavailability pose serious risks to human health and ecosystems. Conventional physicochemical methods for Cr(VI) removal are costly and inefficient at low concentrations often producing secondary waste. In contrast, microbial reduction offers an efficient, eco-friendly and sustainable strategy for detoxification. Bacteria convert soluble Cr(VI) into the less toxic and insoluble trivalent form [Cr(III)]

title: Structural basis of the lobster carapace blue colour mediated by an HPR protein
abstract: The chemical basis underlying the dark blue colour of live H. americanus , known as the American lobster, is studied in evolutionary biology and in polyene physical chemistry. Carapace colouration is generated by the antioxidant astaxanthin bound within the carotenoprotein crustacyanin complexes. Here, we present the ex vivo structure of the most abundant α-crustacyanin and β-crustacyanin forms, determined respectively by cryo-electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography to a resolution of 2.75 Å. title: A decision analysis framework for defining time horizon and foreseeable future in Endangered Species Act classifications
abstract: To clarify the listing process for at‐risk species in the United States, we describe a decision analysis framework for considering the future in Endangered Species Act (ESA) classifications—an increasingly relevant task amid accelerating global change. The ESA uses the phrase “foreseeable future” to differentiate endangered, threatened, and not warranted classifications, thus requiring a defined future timeline. institutions: United States Fish and Wildlife Service

title: Nutrient dynamics and bioremediation potential of lignocellulosic biomatrix in climbing perch aquaculture systems
abstract: Cultivating climbing perch, Anabas testudineus , in culture ponds has often linked with eutrophication. Inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus are the major drivers of algal proliferation in such environments. The objective of this study was to assess the use of coconut coir pith, rice husk, and their composite blend (40:60 ratio) as biomatrix in climbing perch ( A. testudineus ) culture systems, with the aim of improving water quality, managing nutrient accumulation, and enhancing fish growth and survival. title: Freeze-drying-induced structural enhancement of graphene quantum dot–modified carboxymethyl cellulose beads for highly efficient cypermethrin removal
abstract: The influence of drying procedures on the pore structure and adsorption performance of graphene quantum dot-modified carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC/GQD) beads for cypermethrin removal has not been sufficiently elucidated. Therefore, hydrogel and cryogel forms of CMC/GQD beads were comparatively evaluated to clarify the effect of oven-drying and freeze-drying on cypermethrin adsorption from aqueous media. title: Natural grass cover enhances microbial network stability via soil metal elements in deep black soil
abstract: Microbial network stability is a critical indicator for assessing the resilience of soil ecosystems under long term agricultural disturbance. However, how different land use types affect microbial co-occurrence network stability across deep black soil profiles remains insufficiently understood. Based on a 12-year long term field experiment, this study employed a high-resolution grid sampling approach to systematically evaluate the effects of representative land use systems, including two conservation managed orchard systems with black horticultural fabric covering and natural grass cover, repe

title: Integrated phytochemical profiling and multi-compartment metabolomics characterize gut-serum metabolic responses associated with Yangpi San administration
abstract: Yangpi San (YPS) is a traditional Chinese food composed of edible and medicinal plants that has been used for centuries to modulate gastrointestinal discomfort, but its phytochemical composition and systemic metabolic responses remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrated UPLC-HRMS-based chemical profiling, multi-compartment metabolomics, and network pharmacology to investigate the metabolic responses associated with YPS administration. title: Ultrasonic-assisted extraction of flaxseed oil with bio-based 2-methyltetrahydrofuran: When thermodynamics meets kinetics
abstract: Conventional flaxseed oil extraction relies on Soxhlet extraction with petroleum-derived solvent n -hexane, a process burdened by long residence times, high solvent demand, and occupational and environmental hazards. Here, we report an ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) using the green bio-based solvent 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF). Under optimized conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:15 g/mL, 5 min, 315 W, no external heating), the UAE/2-MeTHF process gave an oil yield of 0.386 g/g dry mass, i.e. 94 % of the Soxhlet reference (0.411 g g −1 ), while consuming 0.31–0.33 kWh/ 30 g batch

title: Genetic structure, inbreeding and effective population size in an endangered island cockatoo, following management-led recovery
abstract: Island populations are particularly vulnerable to genetic risk. The glossy black-cockatoo Calyptorhynchus lathami halmaturinus has been restricted to Kangaroo Island, South Australia, since the mid-20th century and had declined to a few hundred individuals before management-led recovery. To understand how this population bottleneck might have affected population structure, genetic diversity and inbreeding, we analyzed single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), principally generated from feather samples collected from nestlings during two breeding seasons. title: EVALUATING THE EFFICACY OF SURFACE DISINFECTION BY COMMERCIAL ANTIBACTERIAL WIPES USING EN 16615 METHOD
abstract: Antibacterial and disinfectant wipes are pre-moistened with active compounds, including alcohol, quaternary ammonium chloride, and hydrogen peroxide, to eradicate microorganisms. This study aimed to assess the bactericidal efficacy of four brands of disinfectant wipes and verify the absence of microbial contamination in unused wipes. Unused wipes were evaluated for color change and turbidity in Dey-Engley neutralizing broth to detect any contamination. journal: Journal of Microbiology Biotechnology and Food Sciences

title: Entropic development of the logistics system for agricultural trade in Ukraine: A structural-dynamic dimension of transcendental changes
abstract: The article investigates the entropic development of the logistics system of Ukrainian agro-trade under conditions of transcendence characterized by uncertainty, turbulence, nonlinear transformations, and the emergence of fundamentally new factors influencing economic processes. The study aims to identify the structural and dynamic trends of logistics system development in the context of military challenges, disruption of traditional supply chains, transformation of export routes, and increasing complexity of logistics flows. institutions: Kyiv National Economic University named after Vadym Hetman

title: Multidimensional evaluation of bacterial inoculants for modulating growth, physiology, soil biochemical functioning and productivity of Zea mays under contrasting water regimes
abstract: The aim of the present study was to evaluate five PGP bacterial inoculants (T1–T5) and an uninoculated control (T6) for drought stress mitigation in maize ( Zea mays L. cv. V-412) through indicators such as plant water status, physiological and biochemical processes, nutrient acquisition, soil enzymatic activities and yield. A factorial randomized block experiment was conducted with six treatments under well-watered (80% field capacity) and water-deficit (40% field capacity) conditions. title: Agricultural drought in Ethiopian rainfed cropland: EVI deviations and relation to temporal rainfall availability 2009–2022
abstract: Drought remains a critical threat to Ethiopia’s rainfed agriculture, posing significant risks to food security and livelihoods. This study integrates Earth Observation (EO) data with climate-based indices to assess the spatiotemporal dynamics of agricultural drought across Ethiopia from 2009 to 2022. We analysed MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) 16-day composites alongside Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data (CHIRPS) derived Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) at 1-, 3-, and 6-month timescales to capture short-term rainfall variability and cumulative moisture
institutions: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
abstract: A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the a -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution)

title: Parkin Modulates PFOS Induced Apoptosis via Bax Ubiquitination in Rat Dopaminergic Neuronal Cells
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a group of synthetic compounds known for their high chemical stability and resistance to degradation. Perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) is one such PFAS that has been found to produce mitochondrial stress and neurotoxicity, although the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Parkin, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, is a critical regulator of mitochondrial quality control, and its dysfunction is associated with neuronal vulnerability. title: Dark CO2 fixation via the ethylmalonyl-CoA pathway establishes metabolic parity: A stoichiometric basis for compounding ecosystem shifts
abstract: A central challenge in microbial ecology, particularly in engineered systems, is understanding how competing guilds coexist and why communities deviate from expected stability. Whereas polyphosphate accumulation provides energy and redox buffering in many heterotrophs, how lineages lacking polyphosphate synthesis manage equivalent redox imbalances remains an overlooked question. Using an enhanced biological phosphorus removal system, we integrated quantitative stoichiometry with metaproteomics to resolve alternative metabolic strategies that underpin cellular homeostasis in heterotrophs. title: CYB2-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae exerts effective antibacterial activity via lactic acid accumulation
abstract: Bacterial infectious diseases pose a major threat to human health, and rising antibiotic resistance has complicated treatment. Probiotics are promising alternatives, but their mechanisms remain largely unclear. Here, we screened a randomly selected subset of 1,733 strains from the homozygous diploid Saccharomyces cerevisiae gene-knockout collection (YKOC) and identified CYB2-knockout (CYB2-KO) S. cerevisiae as a strain with potent antibacterial activity. CYB2-KO S. cerevisiae effectively inhibited the growth of pathogenic bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains, and suppressed biofilm

title: Leaf‐Inspired Porous Cement‐Based Solar Evaporator With Integrated Water Transport and Thermal Insulation for Stable Wastewater Purification
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation offers a highly promising sustainable strategy for wastewater purification, while existing evaporators still face challenges such as wet‐state structural instability and the difficulty of simultaneously achieving efficient water transport and thermal insulation. To address these limitations, a plant‐leaf‐inspired biomimetic porous cement‐based evaporator consisting of a carbon black photothermal conversion layer and a porous cement‐based matrix is designed in this work. title: The ergodicity assumption in statistical approaches to climate damages
abstract: Projections of the economic impacts of climate change are essential to determine efficient levels of mitigation and adaptation. One common approach to projections is based on statistical models, regressing historically observed economic outcomes on climate or weather variables, without imposing explicit assumptions about the underlying mechanisms that relate the variables to each other. title: FROM ROAD INFRASTRUCTURE TO TERRITORIAL ASSET: ROUTE TOURISM AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN PORTUGAL’S EN2
abstract: Tourism can play a significant role in revitalizing low-density territories, yet transforming dispersed territorial assets into a coherent and competitive tourism offer remains a complex challenge. This study examines Portugal’s Estrada Nacional 2 (EN2) as a case of route-based tourism and explores how territorial resources, collaborative governance, and digital/gamified visitor engagement can contribute to sustainable territorial development. title: Structural basis of avian-to-human receptor-binding adaptation in H9Ny influenza A virus hemagglutinin
abstract: The receptor-binding specificity of influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) is a major determinant for viral host tropism, enabling interspecies transmission. The molecular determinants for receptor-binding properties of HAs vary among different IAV subtypes. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis on the receptor-binding determinants of IAV subtype H9 HA and found that the receptor-binding characteristics of H9 subtype influenza viruses have exhibited temporal variations over decades. abstract: The secondary imaging optical configuration requires precise registration between the mosaic spectral filter array and the focal plane array of the polarization camera. Micrometer-level registration errors between these two components can cause spectral crosstalk among adjacent pixels, thereby reducing the accuracy of target characteristic measurements. title: Venezuela Frente al ODS 13 "Acción por el Clima": Desafíos y Oportunidades
abstract: Este ensayo analiza la situación de Venezuela frente al Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) 13, relativo a la “Acción por el clima”. Con este propósito, se examinan sus metas, los compromisos asumidos por las instituciones públicas y las capacidades del país para adap­tarse a los efectos del cambio climático. Aunque los informes internacionales señalan que la acción climática es el único ODS que muestra tendencias favorables en Venezuela, se advierte que la disminución de las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero (GEI) no es resultado de una política planificada de transición energética
journal: Revista Venezolana de Economía y Ciencias Sociales

title: Governing Higher Education in Remote Islands: The TASK Framework for Indonesia’s Tanimbar Islands
abstract: Geographical remoteness complicates higher education governance by combining connectivity constraints, limited institutional capacity, high service-delivery costs, and uneven opportunities for students and academic staff. This article develops a context-sensitive governance framework for higher education institutions in Indonesia’s Tanimbar Islands, a remote archipelagic setting. abstract: Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a major foodborne pathogen whose persistence in food-processing environments is strongly associated with its ability to survive under a wide range of environmental conditions and form biofilms on different surfaces. Metabolites produced by beneficial lactic acid bacteria may represent a natural source of antimicrobial and antibiofilm compounds capable of affecting bacterial behavior even at subinhibitory concentrations. title: A novel quantile-weighted ridge parameter for the Weibull regression model: Theory, simulation, and real-data application from Saudi Arabia
abstract: The Weibull regression model constitutes a flexible and widely applied framework for the analysis of positive, right-skewed data in reliability, survival, environmental, and engineering research. In its standard formulation, one parameter governs the mean of the response distribution, while a second controls its dispersion and shape, thereby affording the model considerable flexibility for regression-based inference. title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
abstract: Friction at solid-liquid interfaces is typically interpreted through classical contact mechanics, but molecular origins of gas-bubble friction in aqueous environments remain elusive. Here we report the direct quantification of gas-bubble friction at solid surfaces using atomic force microscopy with nanonewton resolution. We show that bubbles enter a contact-line friction regime only after film-mediated attachment, with static and kinetic responses that reflect contact-line pinning and sliding. title: Multiomics investigation of iron-responsive idiopathic anemia in hybrid (Ictalurus punctatus × I. furcatus) catfish
abstract: Idiopathic catfish anemia (ICA) is an important cause of protracted mortalities in pond-cultured channel ( Ictalurus punctatus ) and hybrid ( I. punctatus × I. furcatus ) catfish. Herein, fish and water samples from spontaneous outbreaks in two non-adjacent identically managed ponds were utilized to investigate potential roles of environmental and intestinal microbiomes, and host transcriptome profiles in ICA. abstract: This study examines tonal variations and changes in the transitional areabetween Southern Thai and Central Thai. title: Fabrication of carbon quantum dots/silver nanocomposite–coated FBG for Pb2 + detection
abstract: In this study, a Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) coated with Carbon Quantum Dots/Silver (CQDs/Ag) nanocomposite has been developed for Pb 2+ detection. CQDs were fabricated using the hydrothermal method, while Ag was synthesized using the Pulsed Laser Ablation in Liquid (PLAL) method, and the two solutions were combined into CQDs/Ag nanocomposite. title: Janus Vapor‐Gap Membrane Coupling Superhydrophobic Evaporation and Superhydrophilic Condensation for Pressure‐Driven Desalination
abstract: Pressure‐driven distillation (PD) has emerged as a transformative technology for harnessing non‐conventional water resources, leveraging hydraulic pressure to accelerate vapor generation and transport across vapor‐gap membranes. Despite its promise, the paradigm of conventional PD is fundamentally constrained by overlooked thermodynamic energy barrier, which severely limits overall process efficiency. title: Vegetational diversity and dissimilarity shape the diversity and composition of tree-dwelling spiders in post-mining regeneration sites in Eastern Amazon
abstract: Ecological restoration in tropical forests is critical for recovering biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, particularly in landscapes degraded by intensive activities such as mining. Clarifying the relationships between plant community attributes and fauna reassembly is important for understanding regeneration processes in early successional stages. We evaluated how plant abundance, species richness, and compositional dissimilarity relate to the diversity and composition of arboreal spider assemblages in post-mining regeneration sites in the Eastern Amazon. abstract: Persistent coal fires can mobilize potentially toxic elements and create long-lasting soil contamination. This preliminary screening study evaluated Cr, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Cd, and Pb in nine composite surface-soil samples from coal-fire, non-combustion reference, and residential zones at the Rujigou mine in northwestern China. abstract: Advanced bifunctional oxygen electrodes that simultaneously boost the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) serve as a core component of reversible proton ceramic electrochemical cells (R‐PCECs) for high‐efficiency energy conversion. abstract: We present a new 1:25,000-scale geological map of the Bonghwa-gun area, South Korea, along the boundary between the Precambrian Yeongnam Massif and the Cretaceous Gyeongsang Basin. The map identifies and redefines previously misclassified Upper Paleozoic metasedimentary units, Triassic porphyritic granite (ca. 217.9 Ma), and Jurassic granites (ca. 184.8 Ma). title: Melatonin and GABA Improve Metabolic and Pancreatic Outcomes in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetic Mice with Selective Benefits of Combination Therapy
abstract: Loss of functional β-cell mass is a critical factor in the pathogenesis of type 1 (T1D) and type 2 (T2D) diabetes, both characterized by chronic hyperglycemia. Melatonin (M) and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA; G) exhibit immunoregulatory properties and have shown potential to preserve or restore β-cell mass in experimental diabetic models. title: Urban greening, planning instruments and heat risk reduction in Lagos, Nigeria
abstract: Urban heat is an intensifying challenge in rapidly growing cities across sub-Saharan Africa, yet the role of planning instruments in managing heat risk remains poorly understood. This study examines the relationship between urban greening, planning instruments, and heat risk reduction in the Lagos Metropolitan Area using a mixed-methods approach, combining geospatial analysis of Landsat imagery (2002, 2013, 2024) with semi-structured interviews with nine planning professionals. abstract: The Chaco-Santiagueña region of South America has long been regarded as marginal to agricultural development, with subsistence systems usually described as mixed foraging and low-intensity horticulture. Here, we present the first integrated stable isotope analysis (δ 13 C and δ 15 N) of human and faunal bone collagen from the Dry Chaco, spanning the last ~1600 years. title: Multidimensional Assessment and Spatiotemporal Evolution of Urban Resilience in the Pearl River Delta Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating globalization and new-type urbanization, urban agglomerations have become major spatial units of socioeconomic activity, making urban resilience increasingly important for regional sustainable development. This study develops a multidimensional evaluation framework for urban resilience encompassing four dimensions: social, economic, environmental, and infrastructure resilience. title: Rehabilitation of Historical Earthen Buildings as an Approach to Cultural Sustainability: Al-Rinad Palace in Tarim, Hadhramaut as a Case Study
abstract: The general objective of this research is to examine the rehabilitation approaches of historical earthen buildings as a basic solution for attaining cultural sustainability, using the case studies of Al-Rinad Palace in Tarim and Wadi Hadhramaut. An architectural inventory that is the expression of the spatial memory of the community is constantly challenged by physical deterioration and functional abandonment. title: Global Research Trends on Omega-3 Fatty Acids in Poultry Nutrition: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Omega-3 fatty acids are important components of poultry nutrition because dietary supplementation can modify fatty-acid composition and enhance the nutritional value of poultry products for human consumption. Although research in this area has expanded substantially, an integrated quantitative assessment of its global development, scientific structure, and emerging themes remains limited. abstract: Food packaging is an important form of culinary infrastructure because it is simultaneously critical to the transportation of food and conveys knowledge about the food within. Taking paper, cardboard and early plastics, and their use for food packaging in Australia from the 1850s to the 1950s, we show how packaging developed as a site of knowledge construction about food safety. abstract: Targeting cellular senescence represents a critical frontier for mitigating diabetic kidney disease (DKD), yet the transcriptional hierarchies governing renal senescence remain incompletely defined. While the E2F family is pivotal in cell cycle regulation, its specific contribution to the senescent phenotype in DKD is unclear. abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporators provide a promising pathway for sustainable desalination and resource recovery from hypersaline brines, yet their performance is often limited by inefficient interfacial energy utilization and salt crystallization fouling. abstract: Background/Objectives: Macrophage extracellular traps (ETs) contribute to host defense but, when excessively produced, participate in chronic inflammation, thrombosis, and tissue injury. title: Spatial distribution and cluster-level associations of cesarean section prevalence in India
abstract: Background Cesarean section (CS) is an essential obstetric intervention for managing pregnancy and childbirth complications; however, its utilization varies substantially across geographical regions. In India, pronounced regional disparities in CS prevalence highlight the need to understand its spatial distribution and the contextual characteristics associated with these patterns. This study examined the spatial clustering of CS prevalence and its cluster-level associations with demographic, socioeconomic, and maternal healthcare characteristics across India. abstract: Predicting ecosystem responses to climate warming requires an understanding of how temperature shapes soil microeukaryotic communities. Here, we exposed protist communities from three paddy field soils to a 5–60 °C gradient in controlled microcosms and analyzed taxonomic and functional communities of protists using high-throughput sequencing. abstract: The present scientific paper represents the result of research and documentation efforts aimed at highlighting the value of the multifarious plant resources within the lowland region of Oltenia. The topic was not accidentally chosen, rather it addresses a genuine need to understand and sustainably use spontaneous biodiversity, on the background of marked climate changes, amplified agricultural activities, and increasingly apparent human pressure on the environment. abstract: Tourism is a leading sector that makes a significant contribution to the national economy. Therefore, tourism management is directed towards sustainability with stakeholder synergy. The main problem in the tourism sector is the lack of synergistic, comprehensive, integrated, and sustainable integration or collaboration between stakeholders. abstract: Spatial heterogeneity and population density are critical determinants of Tuberculosis (TB) transmission, yet their combined spatial-temporal dynamics are not well understood. This study aimed to examine spatial clustering and population density-related patterns of TB incidence in Semarang from 2016 to 2022. title: Aligning ESG Initiatives with Sustainable Development Goals in the Oil and Gas Industry: Policy Perspectives from the Global South.
abstract: The paper analyses whether ESG interventions in the oil and gas sector lead to concrete contributions to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals in resource-dependent economies in the Global South. There is an analysis problem related to the lack of information about whether corporate environmental, social and governance measures improve the environmental situation, people’s lives, the institution’s performance or resource benefit distribution. abstract: Recycling polluted and remediated excavated soils can enhance resource efficiency and replace the use of finite virgin materials. This study evaluates the geochemical suitability of two alternative clay materials: soil washing filter cake (SWFC) and excavated cement-stabilized clay (ECSC) for use in constructed impermeable barriers, alongside conventionally used dry crust clay (DCC) for comparison. abstract: Exploration of Earth’s subsurface environments continues to expand our understanding of microbial diversity and associated mineral deposits, providing valuable analogues for the search for life on other worlds. abstract: Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels, together with an undeformed reference, affect anodized Ti6Al4V ELI. abstract: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. abstract: Upstream oil and gas facilities in Nigeria are workplaces and, at the same time, hazard sources for the communities and ecosystems around them. Occupational safety and health (OSH) and disaster risk reduction (DRR) have nonetheless developed as separate fields with separate laws, metrics and institutions. abstract: O artigo analisa a organização coletiva de motoristas por aplicativo, com foco nas disputas por representação entre sindicatos e influenciadores digitais no contexto da repercussão do PLC 12/2024. Triangulamos 20 entrevistas com motoristas em Belém, observação em grupos digitais e mapeamento de 22 perfis de influenciadores no Instagram. abstract: Fluorite solubility in hydrothermal fluids plays an important role in fluorite mineralization and fluoride transport, yet reliable thermodynamic models at elevated temperatures and pressures remain limited. Here, we developed a Pitzer-based thermodynamic model for fluorite solubility in Na-K-Cl-SO 4 -bearing aqueous solutions at temperatures up to 260 °C and pressures up to 500 bar. title: Landscape and vegetation structure of domestic reindeer winter pastures in southern Yamal
abstract: Winter reindeer pastures in the tundra are spatially heterogeneous systems in which vegetation patterns are closely associated with landscape structure. This study characterises the spatial organisation of vegetation within a tundra winter pasture in southern Yamal using landscape units (urochishches) as the basis for mapping and geobotanical analysis. abstract: The pomegranate ( Punica granatum L .) is a commercially significant fruit, and Iran is one of the most important centers of its origin and diversity of cultivars. Pomegranate peel, which constitutes 40-50% of the total weight of the fruit, is the major agro-industrial waste and a rich source of phytochemicals. title: Occupational solvent exposure and Parkinson’s disease: evidence from PPMI online
abstract: Occupational exposures are increasingly implicated in Parkinson’s disease (PD), but the role of specific organic solvents remains unclear, and solvents are rarely encountered alone. abstract: Gamak virus (GAKV) is a recently identified shrew-borne paramyxovirus belonging to the genus Parahenipavirus , which also includes the zoonotic Langya virus (LayV). abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. CZ‐01179 is a first‐in‐class antibiofilm compound with demonstrated in vitro and ex vivo efficacy when incorporated into polyurethane foam for NPWT. title: Effects of subtropical forest gap size on soil invertebrate diversity are primarily season-dependent and secondarily layer-dependent
abstract: Escalating disturbance is reshaping soil invertebrate communities in subtropical forests, with cascading consequences for belowground processes. Forest gaps of moderate size represent a common form of intermediate disturbance, potentially promote soil invertebrate diversity. However, as disturbances are projected to intensify under ongoing climate change and generate larger forest gaps, the effects of gap size on the diversity of soil invertebrate feeding guilds remain poorly understood. title: Biochar/persulfate-modified biogas slurry mitigates soil N2O emissions: Roles of organic components and microbial nitrogen-cycling potentials

This study used biochar and persulfate to modify organic components in biogas slurry, and assessed the effects of modified biogas slurry (MBS) on N 2 O emissions from purple soil and cabbage growth in a 52-day pot experiment. title: Polycrisis, spatial inequality and places of ‘left-behindness’: an analytical integration
abstract: The relationship between polycrisis and regional and urban inequalities remains under-examined. This conceptual paper addresses this gap by analyzing how intersecting crises shape spatial disparity, with particular emphasis on the European Union context, where territorial cohesion has long been a central policy objective. The paper argues that crises are not isolated phenomena but interacting events that significantly reshape spatial inequalities. Vulnerable regions, cities, and neighbourhoods, often characterised as places of 'left-behindness', experience compounded effects of multiple crises

abstract: This research evaluated the physicochemical properties of selected commercial soaps sourced from prominent markets in north-western Nigeria. abstract: This study aimed to characterize bacterial communities across different gastrointestinal (GI) compartments, including the rumen (liquid and solid fractions), cecum, and rectum in Hanwoo steers fed the same late-fattening diet. A total of 48 digesta samples were collected from 12 Hanwoo steers at slaughter. Bacterial communities were analyzed using metataxonomics targeting the V3-V4 regions of the 16S rRNA gene. abstract: Understanding the metabolic mechanism of Sporomusa ovata is crucial for the practical applications of microbial electrosynthesis systems (MESs), a promising technology to sequester CO 2 . This study aims to investigate the electrosynthesis mechanisms of S. ovata under different cathodic potentials using comparative transcriptomics. abstract: Flow cytometry shared resource laboratories (SRLs) depend on a small cohort of highly skilled specialists whose expertise in the field has developed and grown over time, with institutional and professional support often lacking. To better understand professional identity, responsibilities, and career satisfaction within this workforce, we conducted a 29-question anonymous cross-sectional survey of 277 flow cytometry specialists across 32 countries, two-thirds of whom were in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. title: A self‐amplifying antimicrobial nanoagent: ALASe combines dark toxicity with in situ porphyrin biosynthesis for enhanced antimicrobial photodynamic therapy
abstract: The rise of multidrug‐resistant bacteria demands innovative antimicrobial strategies that combine multiple mechanisms of action. Selenium nanoparticles functionalized with 5‐aminolevulinic acid (ALASe) offer a dual‐action platform, coupling the intrinsic bactericidal activity of selenium with photodynamic toxicity derived from metabolically generated porphyrins. title: Dual-porosity impedance-modulated metasilencer
abstract: Controlling low-frequency noise in ventilation ducts remains challenging with conventional porous materials, whose sound attenuation capability is constrained by the weak tunability of their acoustic impedance. Here, we report a dual-porosity metasilencer that addresses this constraint by embedding a millimeter-scale cylindrical perforation array into melamine foam. abstract: Understanding complex dependencies and extrapolating beyond observations are key challenges in modeling environmental space-time extremes. abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is an abundant and renewable resource that holds immense potential for the production of biofuels and other value-added products. Lignin-modifying enzymes, such as lignin peroxidase (LiP) and manganese peroxidase (MnP), offer a promising solution by selectively modifying lignin, thereby facilitating its degradation and valorization. title: Comparative Assessment of Population Structure and Genetic Diversity With SNPs and Microsatellites: A Case of Endangered Black‐and‐White Snub‐Nosed Monkeys
abstract: Detecting fine‐scale population structure and gene flow barriers is crucial for the conservation and management of endangered species. Many such species have traditionally been studied using microsatellite genotyping; however, genome‐wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) may challenge conclusions made on limited numbers of loci. title: BRIDGING FAITH AND SUSTAINABILITY: MAPPING THE NEXUS BETWEEN HALAL TOURISM AND SUSTAINABLE TOURISM
abstract: This study is grounded in the growing transformation of halal tourism from a concept primarily associated with sharia compliance and Muslim travel needs into a broader discourse linked to sustainable tourism development. However, the literature addressing the relationship between halal tourism and sustainable tourism remains fragmented and lacks an integrated scholarly mapping. This study aims to examine the evolution of the literature, identify the distribution of research characteristics, and explain the conceptual and practical interconnections between halal tourism and sustainable tourism.

This study integrates field observations, petrography, bulk rock major and trace element geochemistry, and in situ mineral chemical analyses to constrain provenance characteristics, depositional conditions and post-depositional element redistribution within this unit. title: Trace‐Metal‐Assisted Flash Synthesis for Fast‐Charging Graphite Anodes
abstract: Graphite has remained the dominant anode material in lithium–ion batteries (LIBs), powering portable electronics and electric vehicles (EVs). However, sluggish Li + diffusion kinetics in natural and synthetic graphite can severely limit charging rates. Overcoming this bottleneck requires the rational design of graphite architectures that enable rapid Li + transport in LIBs.
