title: Effects of adopting improved bread wheat varieties on smallholder farmers’ yields: a case study of Duna District, Central Ethiopia
abstract: Wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) is a key food and cash crop for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia, yet national yields remain low. Adoption of improved bread wheat varieties is widely promoted to boost productivity, but institutional, socioeconomic, and demographic constraints limit uptake. This study examines the determinants of adoption of improved bread wheat varieties and their association with smallholder yields in Duna District, Hadiya Zone. abstract: Township tourism is promoted through social media, search engines, online travel agencies and review platforms, yet digital participation does not guarantee that enterprises will be discovered, trusted or selected. This conceptual article examines how algorithmic gatekeeping and platform power shape the visibility, credibility and market accessibility of township tourism enterprises in South Africa. title: The Interconnectedness of Nature and Displacement in Nayomi Munaweera’s Island of a Thousand Mirrors
abstract: The study explores the intricate relationship between nature, identity, and the immigrant experience through Nayomi Munaweera’s award-winning novel, Island of a Thousand Mirrors. This novel set against the backdrop of the Sri Lankan civil war. This study investigates how Munaweera employs the nature, not only as a physical setting, but also as a profound lens to examine the psychological and emotional impacts of displacement, trauma, and adaptation. abstract: Passive seismic tomography is a widely used method for imaging subsurface structures, relying on natural seismicity sources without the need for artificial sources. Grid‑node parameterisation is a key aspect of subsurface reconstruction in passive seismic tomography. title: Managing trade-offs among energy productivity, yield, and nutrient-use efficiency in rice–greengram rotations under nitrogen management and zinc biofortification in Alfisols
abstract: Rice-based cropping systems in South Asia face declining resource-use efficiency, increasing dependence on external energy inputs, and rising environmental costs from fertilizer-intensive production. The combined effects of integrated nutrient management and zinc biofortification on energetics, nutrient-use efficiency, and carbon efficiency in rice–pulse rotations remain inadequately quantified. abstract: Most patients in nephrology units require hemodialysis three times per week. Among the available vascular access techniques, the buttonhole method offers distinct advantages, including improved patient comfort and consistent cannulation. However, its clinical adoption remains constrained by a markedly increased risk of access-related infections. In this study, we present a novel and biocompatible coating strategy for the BioHole buttonhole medical device based on in-house produced silver nanoparticles. abstract: Precipitation frequency analysis is fundamental for hydrological risk assessment, infrastructure design, and insurance/reinsurance. The Simplified Metastatistical Extreme Value (SMEV) is an approach to precipitation frequency analysis derived from the Metastatistical Extreme Value distribution. abstract: Mouthwash is an effective complementary approach to maintaining hygiene during orthodontic treatment. title: Risk, time and social preferences shape cross-country support for carbon dioxide removal technologies
abstract: Technical innovations that remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere are gaining attention to compensate for the insufficient pace of emissions reductions. Given the scale of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) deployment envisioned, there is a notable deficit in our understanding of the underlying predictors of public support of CDR, particularly in the global South. title: Agricultural Land Use Is Associated With Reduced Soil Health and Multifunctionality in Tropical Wetlands of Cameroon
abstract: Agricultural intensification is increasingly associated with declining soil health and reduced soil‐based ecosystem functioning, particularly in tropical regions. Despite growing global concern, there is limited quantitative understanding of these impacts in the wetlands of Cameroon's Western Highlands. This study provides novel insights into integrating a Soil Health Index (SHI) and ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) framework to assess the effects of varying agricultural intensities on tropical wetland soils in Cameroon. abstract: El turismo de bienestar y salud constituye un nicho emergente del turismo mundial, pero la producción científica sobre el tema y su relevancia para América Latina han sido poco examinadas. The characterization of the yielding behavior and the stress‐dilatancy relationship of very soft clay is the primary objective of this study. abstract: Stable hatchery production of yellowtail requires effective brood stock management, particularly control of vitellogenic progression. Although the absence of males impairs oocyte maturation and ovulation in several fish species, its influence on yellowtail reproduction remains unclear. This study compared female-only and mixed-sex groups over two reproductive seasons, referred to as year 1 and year 2, respectively. title: Photocatalyst Design for Plastic Upcycling: From Polymer Deconstruction to Selective Valorization
abstract: Plastic waste poses a severe threat to our environment, yet represents an abundant and largely underutilized reservoir of chemically processed carbon and embedded energy. Photocatalytic conversion offers a promising route to valorize plastic waste into fuels and value‐added chemicals. However, practical plastic photovalorization remains severely limited by sluggish polymer deconstruction and poor product selectivity. title: Codon-specific translational regulation of eIF2B is associated with salt sensitivity in rice
abstract: Salt stress limits rice productivity, but the relationship between transcriptional and translational responses in salt-sensitive cultivars remains incompletely understood. We integrated RNA-seq, ribosome profiling, translational-efficiency analysis, targeted ribosome profiling, and reporter assays in Huanghuazhan (HHZ) rice. Salt treatment produced extensive transcriptional changes alongside more limited changes in ribosome association. Replicate-aware analysis detected positional differences around annotated start codons, while the overall metagene profile remained similar between conditions.

abstract: The efficient separation of thorium (Th) from chemically similar rare earth elements (REEs) is technically challenging. In this work, a stable coordination polymer (Ni-tfc-CP) was fabricated by adopting the strategy of in-situ incorporation of hydrophobic groups. title: Occurrence and Spatial Variability of Suspected Microplastics and Trace Elements in Highway Drainage Water and Roadside Soils in North Macedonia
abstract: Highway runoff represents an important pathway for the transport of traffic-associated contaminants to roadside environments, while microplastic contamination in road drainage systems remains poorly documented in North Macedonia. The present study provides a field-based assessment of suspected microplastic occurrence and selected trace elements in highway drainage water and adjacent roadside soils in North Macedonia. Long‑term reliance on chemical pesticides has led to increasing problems of resistance, environmental pollution, and food safety. Transgenic insect‑resistant maize offers a new approach for green pest management. title: Agricultural economic responses to ecoclimate teleconnections induced by forest loss
abstract: Forest disturbances are increasing globally, altering vegetation in ways that can affect distant agricultural systems through ecoclimate teleconnections. We examine how large-scale U.S. regional forest loss with C3 grass replacement affects agricultural production and markets. We integrate climate simulations, econometric yield models, and an agricultural sector model to trace impacts from vegetation change through climate anomalies to yields, land allocation, prices, and welfare, while isolating vegetation-driven effects from greenhouse-gas forcing. title: Optimization of gum arabic powder content in Kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites for enhanced mechanical, thermal, dielectric, and moisture-related performance
abstract: The use of sustainable multifunctional composites made from renewable sources is gaining momentum in the field of advanced engineering. A constant kenaf fiber content of 20 wt% was maintained, while gum Arabic powder loading was varied from 0 to 20 wt% (KEG0–KEG20) in the proposed in kenaf fiber-reinforced epoxy hybrid composites. The effects of gum Arabic incorporation on mechanical, thermo-mechanical thermal dielectric, and moisture absorption properties were systematically investigated. The addition of fillers increased the composites’ performance and the effects were the highest at 15 wt%.

abstract: Sustainable management and security of water in Central Asian agriculture is increasingly threatened by climate change. This study investigates the impact of climate change on wheat water consumption in the Tashkent region of Uzbekistan. Evapotranspiration changes were simulated through 2100 using the Penman–Monteith method within the framework of three CMIP6 scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5) based on six GCMs at three meteorological stations: Yangiyul, Pskem, and Almalyk. title: A Self-guided Smartphone App to Support Psychological Adjustment in Long-term Physical Conditions: A Protocol for the Feasibility of a Randomised Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Living with long-term health conditions (LTCs) presents significant challenges, often resulting in psychological distress. Digital cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) can help address these challenges, at scale, yet engagement and retention are often sub-optimal. Orbi is a self-guided CBT app designed to support wellbeing among people living with LTCs. abstract: Mass-loss measurements provide a global measure of corrosion damage but do not capture extreme localized penetration. This study compares CT-derived maximum localized penetration with mass-loss-derived equivalent average penetration for S460, S690, and S960 structural steels subjected to three controlled 5% NaCl exposure regimes. title: A Simple Low-Cost Paper-Based Analytical Device For Detecting Water Hardness
abstract: High water hardness can cause damage to piping systems and negatively impact health. This study aimed to develop a simple, low-cost, and user-friendly paper-based analytical device to detect water hardness levels in the field. The device was developed using a complexation reaction principle with specific reagents, namely a pH 10 buffer solution and Eriochrome Black T (EBT) indicator, immobilized on Whatman filter paper. title: Co-production of knowledge for effective flood risk management
abstract: Flood risks (FR) represent one of the most pressing global challenges, exacerbated by factors such as climate change, urbanization, and land use changes. Effective flood risk management (FRM) faces significant challenges, including the need for robust decision-making, the need to address existing risks, and the need to implement strategies across the disaster risk reduction (DRR) cycle. abstract: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is governed by pore chemistry and confinement, yet the molecular origins of uptake and mobility remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate site-specific water adsorption and transport in two structurally related COFs, TUS-46 and TUS-44, by combining molecular dynamics simulations with humidity-controlled in situ FT-IR spectroscopy. title: Hydrochemical-thermal coupling based on temperature field measurements in a karst spring
abstract: Karst spring systems with thermal anomalies commonly involve complex groundwater circulation, water–rock interaction, and cold–hot water mixing. However, hydrochemical evidence alone is often insufficient to fully characterize groundwater circulation and geothermal processes in highly heterogeneous karst systems. In this study, LBC Spring in northeastern Guizhou Province, China, was selected as a representative karst spring system with stable thermal anomalies and multiple outlets. title: General aviation aircraft as a low-cost altered-gravity platform for water electrolysis research
abstract: Hydrogen and oxygen production by water electrolysis is a key enabling technology for future space missions, but altered gravity can affect gas bubble transport and, consequently, electrochemical performance. In this work, water electrolysis was investigated under reduced-gravity and hypergravity conditions by performing parabolic maneuvers with a general aviation aircraft, representing a low-cost experimental platform. title: A Novel Hybrid Fuzzy IRPA–MEREC-G Framework for Assessment of Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods have made a significant contribution to policy-making and governance. However, many of these methods adopt uniform criteria weights and assume linear satisfaction levels, overlooking real-world policy constraints and the law of diminishing marginal utility. To address these shortcomings, this paper introduces a novel Fuzzy Integrative Reference Point Approach (Fuzzy IRPA) that extends the classical IRPA to a type-1 fuzzy environment using trapezoidal fuzzy numbers. title: The anti-phage defense system GAPS4 is a double-edged sword that sensitizes bacteria to DNA-damaging agents
abstract: The arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages (phages) gave rise to multiple layers of antagonistic mechanisms, many of which remain unexplored. Here, we investigated the widespread anti-phage defense system GAPS4. We found that GAPS4 forms a heterotetrameric complex containing active PD-(D/E)xK phosphodiesterase domains. title: Integrated Life Cycle and Techno‐Economic Assessment of Rice Husk Gasification as a Low‐Carbon Alternative to Coal Power
abstract: As energy demand grows, sustainable solutions are required to mitigate climate consequences and improve energy security. This study includes the comparative life cycle assessment and life cycle costing of electricity production from rice husk gasification and traditional coal power electricity, based on a cradle‐to‐gate system boundary and a functional unit of 1 kWh. The results show that rice husk‐based electricity significantly reduces the environmental impacts compared to coal‐based electricity. title: A 3D‐Printed Model of Human Lactation
abstract: Engineering physiologically relevant breast in vitro models remains challenging due to the gland's complex three-dimensional microanatomy, together with the need for epithelial polarity and hormone responsiveness. To overcome these challenges, fabrication methods are needed that rapidly create alveoli-scale structures with efficient diffusion and sustained hormonal stimulation. title: Systemic mycobacteriosis in Danio rerio (Zebrafish): clinical and histopathological findings
abstract: This case report describes systemic mycobacteriosis in Danio rerio from the FURG zebrafish facility, emphasizing the clinical manifestations and histopathological findings that confirmed infection by Mycobacterium spp. Gross examination revealed nodular and ulcerative skin lesions, while internal evaluation indicated widespread inflammatory involvement compatible with chronic infection. abstract: In the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, the capacity for the repair of photosystem II (PSII) is closely associated with the tolerance of PSII to strong light. However, it remains unclear whether the capacity for PSII repair also contributes to the tolerance of PSII to high-temperature stress. title: Sensory Comfort Across Multisensory XR Prototypes for Autistic Adults
abstract: Multisensory XR may support autistic adults, yet sensory-friendly design often prioritizes less input. We conducted a mixed-methods, counterbalanced within-subjects study with 20 Chinese autistic adults evaluating five complete XR configurations presenting identical science content: text (L1), text with images (L2), click-triggered spatial audio (L3), gradual light and audio (L4), and L4 plus vibrotactile and thermal cues (L5). title: Spatiotemporal patterns of breeding challenge the successive broods model in a migratory butterfly
abstract: Migration is widely recognized as a strategy for animals to track seasonally shifting resources. Yet, seasonal and spatial dynamics of migration are challenging to study, particularly for difficult‐to‐track insects. Among insects, monarch butterflies Danaus plexippus have a well‐documented fall migration, but spring breeding recolonization remains poorly understood, particularly in the western United States. title: Subsea Installation Padeye Design for Pipeline End Termination Using Abaqus Cae
abstract: The oil and gas industry is continuously pushing the boundaries of technological innovation to address the complex challenges associated with operational efficiency and the extraction of vital resources from increasingly hostile environments. This relentless pursuit of advancement necessitates robust engineering solutions for the secure installation of critical subsea infrastructure. abstract: N 6 -isopentenyladenosine (i 6 A) and its derivative 2-methylthio- N 6 -isopentenyladenosine (ms 2 i 6 A) at position 37 are conserved modifications of cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNAs that typically contain the A36-A37-A38 motif. abstract: Vegetation net primary productivity (NPP) is a fundamental indicator of terrestrial vegetation productivity and carbon cycling. However, existing global NPP products may exhibit low biases over parts of the Qingzang Plateau and may not fully capture the pronounced spatial heterogeneity of alpine vegetation productivity, partly because of generalized model parameterization and limitations in representing vegetation thermal responses. abstract: Introduction: Castor oil has long been recognized for its laxative activity and used in traditional medicine for the treatment of constipation. This study aimed to deepen our understanding of how castor oil acts as a laxative using computational modeling and to identify potential candidates for future drug development. abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. abstract: 2-methoxyethanol (methyl cellosolve; MC)is an industrial solvent used in paints, coatings, dyes, and jet fuel anti-icing agents that has been associated with reproductive toxicity. abstract: Introduction. The SARS-CoV-2 virus, which emerged in 2019, continues to circulate globally. New genetic variants of the virus continue to arise, including recombinant forms. Continuous epidemiological surveillance is essential to track circulating and emerging variants, with high-throughput sequencing serving as a primary method for investigating the genetic variability and prevalence of circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. title: Challenges and Pathways for Leveraging China's Digital Economy Toward Common Prosperity
abstract: Against the rapid expansion of China's digital economy, digital technologies have created new opportunities for economic development and improved access to markets and services, but their benefits are not necessarily distributed equally. This paper examines the challenges and pathways for leveraging the digital economy toward common prosperity. abstract: Membrane-aerated biofilm reactors (MABRs) are an energy-efficient wastewater treatment technology based on biofilms grown on gas-permeable membranes. As with most wastewater treatment technologies, MABR biofilms are typically dominated by bacteria. However, here we show that MABRs supplied with high organic carbon loadings can be dominated by filamentous fungi, leading to stiff biofilms. abstract: The Indian House Crow ( Corvus splendens) is a highly adaptable invasive bird that is expanding its range worldwide. Despite its ecological and socio-economic impacts, information on its morphometric traits and body condition in semi-arid environments remains limited. This study quantified morphometric traits and assessed body condition using the Scaled Mass Index (SMI) of a population in Dodoma, Tanzania. abstract: The glycolysis is crucial for the material and energy source of virus infection. However, the role of post-transcriptional modification, particularly N6-methyladenosine (m6A), in regulating virus-induced glycolysis in invertebrate remains unclear. abstract: Textile-derived fibers and particles are increasingly recognized as an important source of human and environmental exposure. While synthetic textile particles have been intensively studied as a major source of micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) pollution, textile emissions in real-world environments are far more diverse and include synthetic, natural and biobased materials. abstract: Bronze sickles are among the most characteristic agricultural tools of the Late Bronze Age (1350 − 800 BC) and provide important evidence for harvesting practices and technological traditions associated with cereal cultivation. Despite their abundance in the archaeological record, most finds consist solely of metal blades, while the organic components that once formed integral parts of these tools rarely survive. title: Seasonal constraints and landscape structure drive space use strategies in Dalmatian Pelicans
abstract: Animals using patchy landscapes often repeatedly visit sites, but changes in the size and internal pattern of their seasonal home‐ranges through the year remain poorly understood. abstract: The increasing environmental concerns associated with petroleum-based plastics have accelerated the development of sustainable, biodegradable packaging materials derived from biodegradable and renewable packaging materials with improved functional properties. abstract: The 2018 Palu earthquake caused extensive land deformation across Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. This study evaluates post-earthquake surface displacement using Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (D-InSAR) based on Sentinel-1 Single Look Complex (SLC) images acquired on 7 June 2018 and 5 October 2018. abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) emissive fluorophores are appealing for biological imaging and sensing applications, particularly in the lower-energy NIR-II region (1000–1700 nm). abstract: Background Climate change is intensifying existing social and environmental inequalities, disproportionately affecting populations with limited access to resources, decision-making processes, and adaptive capacity. abstract: This practice review reflects on two connected planning processes in northern Lazio, Italy, where an external project manager became central to coordination. Drawing on three years of university involvement, contemporaneous observation and process documents, it examines both the enabling and constraining effects of consultant-led planning. abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine childhood immunisation coverage in Vanuatu remains suboptimal, with substantial regional disparities. While supply-side constraints are well recognised barriers to vaccine uptake in the Pacific, other contributing factors remain less understood. abstract: When a randomized intervention in southwestern Uganda offered fully subsidized land titles to agricultural households, the majority of husbands chose to add their wives’ names to the title, a striking result given the persistent gender asymmetry in land ownership across Africa. abstract: Fatty acid composition data reflecting foods as consumed remain limited for many populations. abstract: Climate change affects the timing of seasonal events, potentially impacting plant-pollinator interactions through phenological mismatches. title: A gradual shift in channel dominance on the Karnali fluvial fan in the Himalayan Terai
abstract: Fluvial fans in the Himalayan Terai are critical for water resources and provide key habitats for endangered species, including tigers. On such fans, changes in the dominance of distributary channels imply a shift in the distribution of water and sediment, affecting such habitats. Here, we investigate a recent shift in channel dominance on the Karnali River fan, one of the least human-altered large river systems in Nepal and India. title: Urbanization restructures wetland nitrogen cycling via soil properties and microbial functional communities
abstract: Urban expansion, characterized by growing impervious surface area, severely disrupts wetland ecosystem functions and nutrient cycling processes. However, a holistic understanding of how urbanization affects wetland soil nitrogen cycling and the associated functional microorganisms remains unclear. In this study, the key soil nitrogen cycling processes and their associated core microbial functional genes across 22 wetlands were investigated along a rural–suburban–urban gradient. abstract: The control of defect-induced electron trap levels is crucial for regulating the reactivity of photogenerated charge carriers. Although electron trapping can suppress rapid electron–hole recombination, excessive deep trapping lowers the energy and mobility of photogenerated electrons, thereby reducing their reactivity. Thus, controlling trap depth is essential for improving photocatalysts and other photofunctional materials. However, rational design principles remain limited. abstract: This study investigated a sequential treatment combining ozonation followed by membrane filtration for the removal of organic pollutants from water. Membranes were prepared by incorporating mulberry leaf extract-based green-synthesized iron nanoparticles (FeNPs) into polyacrylonitrile, producing PAN@G-FeNPs membranes with enhanced properties: compact finger-like sublayer, increased surface roughness (17–237 nm), enhanced negative charge (–8.2 to –34.4 eV), and higher hydrophobicity (86.8° contact angle). title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Tetraodon pustulatus Murray, 1857 (Tetraodontiformes: Tetraodontidae)
abstract: The first complete mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) of Tetraodon pustulatus was sequenced, assembled, and annotated. The complete mitogenome is 16,471 bp in length and contains 37 mitochondrial genes, including 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs), two rRNA genes, and 22 tRNA genes, as well as one non-coding control region (D-loop). The overall nucleotide composition is A: 29.41%, T: 23.40%, C: 31.66%, G: 15.53%, with a GC content of 47.19%. title: Perceptions of perennial crops among urban agriculture growers in England
abstract: Given increasing evidence of the unsustainable nature of conventional intensive agriculture, alternative methods of food production must be considered. Urban agriculture (UA) is one proposed mechanism for increasing food system sustainability, given the potential to provide social and ecological benefits while increasing access to nutritious food. In conventional farming, the incorporation of more perennial crops has been proposed to increase sustainability through reduced soil disturbance, increased water retention and supporting higher biodiversity than annual cropping. title: CO 2 fertilization to climate limitation: shifting drivers in a dryland forest
abstract: Dryland forests represent a significant but uncertain component of the terrestrial carbon sink, where rising CO 2 and intensifying drought and heat stress exert opposing controls on carbon and water fluxes. Using ED2.2-hydraulics calibrated against 21 years of flux tower and inventory data from Yatir Forest, an arid pine plantation in Israel, we simulated carbon fluxes, biomass dynamics, and water-use efficiency under current climate and high-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) through 2100 using five general circulation models. title: Network analysis reveals the plant and bird species underpinning nature's contributions to people
abstract: Understanding how biodiversity underpins nature's contributions to people (NCP) is key to assessing nature's role in human well‐being. However, identifying the species involved in NCP supply is challenging, as many species indirectly affect NCP supply through ecological interactions. title: Treatment of steel slag leachates and the synthesis of calcite via carbon dioxide micro-pressure circulating aeration technique: a pilot study
abstract: Steel slag leachate poses significant pollution risks to the surrounding environment. This study proposes a CO 2 -based micro-pressure circulating aeration technique for treating strongly alkaline steel slag leachate. By optimizing experimental research and pilot tests in engineering devices, the calcium-containing wastewater was well treated and met the emission standards. The results show that the effluent of this leachate wastewater treatment project reaches Ca 2+ concentrations of ≤ 80 mg/L, with a pH range of 7.0–7.3. title: DNA uptake and twitching motility are controlled by small RNA Arp through repression of pilin translation in Acinetobacter baumannii
abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is a major opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation. This process is driven by type IV pili (T4P) facilitating horizontal gene transfer and accelerating the spread of antimicrobial resistance. While the transcriptional regulation of T4P is increasingly understood, post-transcriptional mechanisms controlling pilus assembly remain unexplored. title: Effects of 6PPD-Q and its hydroxylated metabolites on mitochondrial function in the rainbow trout cell line RTgill-W1
abstract: The tire rubber-derived contaminant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) exhibits high acute toxicity to salmonid species, yet the toxicological profiles of its hydroxylated metabolites and the underlying mitochondrial mechanisms remain poorly characterized. This study investigated cytotoxicity and mitochondrial responses in rainbow trout gill cells (RTgill-W1) exposed to 6PPD-Q and three mono-hydroxylated metabolites (p‑hydroxy 6PPD-Q, 6PPD-Q-1-OH, and 6PPD-Q-4-OH). title: Historical fur farming of nutria (Myocastor coypus) as an introduction pathway for biological invasion in Central Europe Hungary
abstract: Nutria, also commonly known as coypu (Myocastor coypus), is one of the most widely established invasive mammals in Europe, yet the factors contributing to its early establishment in Central Europe remain poorly understood. The history of nutria farming for fur production in Hungary can be divided into two main phases. In the 1950s and 1960s, large-scale farming was dominant, whereas in the 1980s, small-scale backyard breeding became more prominent. abstract: Background High-quality healthcare resources remain unevenly distributed across China, while cross-provincial care seeking, teleconsultation, and regional medical collaboration are increasingly common. Existing studies have mainly explained regional disparities in terms of resource endowments, geographic proximity, and spatial accessibility, with less attention to network structure, tie formation and persistence, and changes during public health crises. title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
abstract: Parasympathetic nervous system activity, vital for restorative sleep, is influenced by vagal sensory afferents, but how these shape brain-body correlates of sleep remains open. Here we combined vagal sensory neuron (VSN) stimulation in the mouse with EEG/EMG, heart rate, brain-body temperature, noradrenergic locus coeruleus (LC) neuron population activity measures and in vitro synaptic physiology to investigate the effects of VSN activation on sleep-wake states. abstract: Culicoides biting midges play an important role as vectors of various viruses and are associated with public and veterinary health concerns worldwide. However, our understanding of the diversity and distribution of RNA viruses associated with Culicoides biting midges remains limited. Therefore, this study used next-generation sequencing to investigate RNA viruses in Culicoides biting midges collected in Hokkaido, Japan in 2023. title: Compelled Flexibility and Lock‐in to Dispersion? Imperatives in Japan’s Energy Policy
abstract: In the wake of the war in Ukraine, escalating tariff regimes, and instability in the Middle East, rethinking the relationship between energy security and the energy transition has become imperative. This article examines Japan’s energy policy as a critical case in which the pursuit of energy security under severe structural constraints can give rise to a form of “compelled flexibility” that drives the simultaneous pursuit of diverse technological pathways beyond mere industrial preference—an “institutionalization of optionality.” It further identifies a risk inherent in this institutionalizati

title: Clean Thermolysis PMMA Top Layer Enables High‐Efficiency Kesterite Solar Cells
abstract: Regulating the phase evolution during selenization of kesterite (Ag,Cu) 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (ACZTSSe) absorbers is essential for high‐efficiency solar cells, yet it remains challenging because of uncontrolled contact reactions between the precursor film and selenium vapor. Herein, we introduce a poly (methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) blocking layer with clean‐thermolysis characteristics onto the ACZTSSe precursor top surface to precisely control the onset of selenization. title: Protists as an overlooked ecological dimension of antimicrobial resistance in agroecosystems
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in agroecosystems is increasingly recognized as an ecological problem, yet environmental surveillance remains largely focused on resistant bacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). This approach identifies where resistance occurs but provides limited insight into the ecological processes that influence its persistence, selection and dissemination. title: Social Sustainability in Ecovillages: A Systematic Scoping Review of Collective Processes and Contextual Conditions
abstract: Ecovillages merge ecological practices with alternative modes of collective living, but their sustainability cannot be solely attributed to environmental commitments. This systematic scoping review synthesizes findings from 96 publications identified through Scopus and Web of Science. It examines five social process domains—governance and power, conflict and relational dynamics, collective identity, membership and justice, and everyday practices—alongside economic, institutional, and spatial conditions, as well as various formation pathways. abstract: This study conducted a bibliometric analysis of scientific publications on spirituality and sport indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection between 1996 and 2023. A total of 226 publications were analyzed to identify research trends, influential journals and authors, country productivity, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic structures. title: Multi-scale analysis of the agricultural phosphorus cycle in Norway to inform farm, regional, and national resource efficiency strategies
abstract: Ineffective phosphorus (P) management in agriculture raises concerns about resource depletion, supply security, eutrophication, and biodiversity loss. A major barrier to more circular and resource-efficient P management is the spatial imbalance between farms: livestock farms often accumulate surplus P from manure in soil, whereas crop farms typically face P deficits that are met with mineral fertilizers. abstract: Surface layers (S-layers) are paracrystalline protein monolayers that envelop archaea and some bacteria, including Bacillus anthracis. S-layer subunits in B. anthracis are tethered to the underlying cell wall through glycopolymers that are covalently attached to the peptidoglycan (PG) meshwork. abstract: The increasing demand for acetic acid and cellulose has driven the exploration of alternative biological sources beyond plants, including bacterial cellulose-producing microorganisms. The bacterial production of acetic acid and cellulose is a promising alternative to plant-derived cellulose due to its rapid production by bacteria under controlled conditions. Acetic acid bacteria (AAB) and cellulose-producing bacteria are commonly found in fruits, flowers, and various fermented foods. title: Evaluation of marginal and average sectorial GHGs emissions abatement costs using an open-source energy system optimization model: the Italian case study
abstract: To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide marginal abatement costs and sectorial and sub-sectorial average abatement costs with a multi-sectoral energy system optimization model. abstract: Motile cilia drive directional fluid flow essential for mucociliary clearance, cerebrospinal fluid circulation, and left–right body patterning, and their dysfunction causes primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a disorder often linked to defective axonemal dynein arms. title: Urban forests can be ecologically similar to the natural forests for sustaining flower-visitation network structure in highly urbanized South China
abstract: Urban green spaces have been suggested to be the refuge for pollinator conservation amid the negative impacts of urbanization on insect richness and abundance. However, the extent to which urban green spaces are ecologically similar to the "natural" ones remains poorly understood. abstract: Two new species of the 'Mesonoemacheilus guentheri' group are described from the Western Ghats Hotspot, based on morphological and multi-locus molecular data (mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase subunit 1, cytochrome b and nuclear Recombination-Activating Gene 1 sequences). abstract: Bacteriophage (phage) collections are essential resources for studying virus–host interactions in bacterial species. abstract: Context and objective The Northeastern Hill (NEH) region of India, a national priority zone for sustainable agricultural intensification, faces persistently low rice productivity driven by suboptimal nutrient management, highly acidic soils with spatially heterogeneous soil organic carbon (SOC), and increasing climate variability. abstract: Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) has emerged as a promising strategy for solar desalination and water treatment, yet the role of interfacial water in governing energy utilization remains debated. abstract: Fuel terminal siting must reconcile the spatial distribution of demand with service-distance limits, yet applied Center of Gravity (CoG) studies rarely test data consistency or service coverage. abstract: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO 2 -releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. abstract: This study investigated the presence of microplastics in canine semen and their potential associations with conventional semen quality parameters. abstract: The question of the environmental consequences of protectionism has emerged as an urgent issue at the intersection of international political economy and sustainability studies, as the world economy becomes increasingly fragmented into competing trade blocs. abstract: Shaped by privacy imperatives, socio-cultural norms, and seismic experience, introverted Ottoman domestic architecture was frequently characterized in Western travelogues as marked by a ‘lack of aesthetics’ or ‘transience’. title: Severity dynamics of an invasive forest pathogen: Beech bark disease in an unmanaged old-growth forest
abstract: Beech bark disease (BBD) is an invasive insect-pathogen complex causing significant mortality to American beech ( Fagus grandifolia )—one of the most dominant species in temperate forests across eastern North America. BBD disproportionately affects older and larger beech trees, yet the biotic and abiotic drivers of its spread and impacts are not well-defined. abstract: The Neotropical freshwater ichthyofauna harbours exceptional diversity, yet many groups remain taxonomically challenging due to the lack of robust phylogenetic frameworks. The genus Rineloricaria (Siluriformes: Loricariidae: Loricariinae), one of the most species‐rich and widely distributed loricariid genera, exemplifies this issue, with numerous undescribed taxa and cryptic diversity. abstract: Hydrologically isolated water bodies are important features of semi‐arid savannas, yet their seasonal hydrochemical variability and associations with local environmental conditions remain poorly understood. abstract: Variable-speed pumped storage hydropower (VS-PSH) offers long-duration energy storage alongside ancillary services in competitive electricity markets. abstract: Rapid warming and accelerating ecological change across high-latitude (>66° N) terrestrial environments are reshaping greenhouse gas dynamics. abstract: A pyrazolone-based ligand constrains the Zn( ii ) coordination geometry, directing the assembly of a microporous quartz-topology metal–organic framework (MUDEC-4(Zn)) applied to the selective removal of emerging contaminants from water.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel modeling approach for arc routing problems (ARPs) which is easily applied to multiple ARP variants (e.g., capacitated ARPs, multiple depot ARPs, heterogeneous fleets). abstract: Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. title: Rural E-Commerce Warehousing Innovation in China: A Digital, Platform, Collaborative and Green Framework
abstract: Rural e-commerce in China depends on warehouses that can consolidate dispersed orders, handle perishable products and coordinate several logistics providers. This study examines how these functions are organised at county level through a documentary multiple-case study with abductive interpretation. abstract: Antibiotic resistance represents a major global health concern, predicted to become a leading cause of death in the near future. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) have been proposed as a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics due to their multi-target nature and highly conserved bacterial targets, suggesting a less frequent emergence of resistance compared to their conventional counterparts. abstract: Environmental pollution drives major changes in freshwater communities across Europe, often favouring tolerant taxa. In gammarid crustaceans, recent findings suggest that endoparasitic infections—particularly by Acanthocephala—may play a previously underestimated role in this transition. These parasites, which use crustaceans as obligate intermediate hosts, can bioaccumulate pollutants, potentially reducing toxic burdens on the host and enhancing their stress tolerance. abstract: Fish age‐length data are crucial to our understanding of many important processes in fish biology, including growth, mortality, recruitment, and year‐class strength. abstract: Bacteria can spontaneously produce polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), a thermoplastic and biodegradable substance. PHA is the best polymer substitute for plastic made from petrochemicals. Bacterial PHA synthesis reduces dependency on petrochemicals and promotes a circular bioeconomy by producing biodegradable, biocompatible polymers from waste and renewable feedstocks. title: Storage-history-associated differences in the mechanical and interfacial properties of carbon fibers
abstract: Commercially sized carbon fibers may be stored for years before composite fabrication, but information on fibers with long storage histories remains limited. We compared archived T700SC-50C and T700SC-60E carbon fibers with nominal storage durations of 6-23 years. title: Contrasting nutrient limitation is associated with microbial genome size and potential metabolic complementarity in the rhizosphere of Zanthoxylum bungeanum
abstract: Rhizosphere nutrient limitation shapes microbial genome characteristics and functional potential, yet how microbial genomes respond to variation in nutrient availability remains poorly understood. Here, we compared rhizosphere communities from two 10-year-old Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim. plantations established on calcareous karst-derived soil and non-karst yellow soil. abstract: Functional proteins combine molecular recognition, catalytic activity, and structural tunability, supporting applications in pollutant transformation, sensing, resource recovery, and disinfection. abstract: A synthesis of archaeological evidence for the organisation of industrial production in later medieval English small towns is presented. We examine evidence for the undertaking of industry within domestic space, landscapes of industrial specialisation (particularly pertaining to iron production, salt extraction and pottery production), the impact of institutional demand and the relationship between industry and processes of urban growth and decline. abstract: Thiacloprid (TCP) is a neonicotinoid insecticide with high insect toxicity but potential health risks for animals and humans. abstract: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-enclosed nanoparticles that transport bioactive cargo and can modulate host cellular responses. Rhodobacter sphaeroides is a metabolically versatile bacterium whose physiology is strongly shaped by oxygen availability, yet how oxygen-dependent growth states influence EV production, cargo composition, and bioactivity has remained insufficiently defined. abstract: The most vulnerable countries in the world are disproportionately affected by climate change, which poses a serious and existential threat to human security and sustainable development. This vulnerability is best shown by the small, landlocked, mountainous nation of Lesotho in Southern Africa. abstract: Matrix stiffness and fluid shear force are key mechanical cues in ovarian cancer microenvironment that can impact cancer stemness, tumorigenicity and metastasis. abstract: Bio-based foams, often derived from wood pulp, have recently gained attention for their sound-absorbing properties. To avoid increasing wood demand for these potentially high-volume uses, diversification of raw material sources is needed. abstract: Carbon capture technologies have been increasingly demanded to achieve the commitments in the Paris Agreement of capturing 10 Gt CO2 per year. This review examines the many facets of activated carbons for CO2 capture applications. abstract: Los paquetes del lenguaje de programación R se distribuyen principalmente en tres repositorios: CRAN, Bioconductor y GitHub. abstract: Although dioecious plant species often exhibit enhanced stress resilience through dioecious cooperation, the mechanistic basis and key chemical signals underlying this adaptive symbiosis remain poorly understood. abstract: Structured lipids (SLs) are engineered molecules with tailored fatty acid composition and positional distribution, designed to confer specific nutritional, functional, and technological properties. abstract: Invasive alien plant (IAP) species are among the major threats to biodiversity, also in valuable and protected habitats. Understanding the impacts of IAPs on soil biota in these ecosystems is essential for developing effective restoration and management strategies. abstract: Recognising Nature as a subject of rights creates a challenge for environmental governance: translating constitutional ecological obligations into practical environmental assessment. title: Responses of soil nematode communities to anthropogenic forest conversion in the Ukrainian Carpathians
abstract: Soil nematodes are a taxonomically and functionally diverse component of terrestrial ecosystems and are sensitive to environmental change. abstract: Leishmaniasis remains a significant and evolving public health challenge in Algeria, particularly in regions previously considered low-endemic. title: DMT-induced aberrant salience and suggestibility correlate with mystical experiences and positive emotionality
abstract: Paradoxically, psychedelics have long been used as models of both psychosis and therapy. abstract: Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase1/2 (PARP1/2) inhibitors are approved for HER2-negative breast cancer harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations, including TNBC. abstract: Forestry practices in South American wetlands transform native grasslands and forests into monospecific plantations, reducing bird diversity. title: Soil storage and growth media shape culture-based recovery of pyrophilous bacteria and fungi from burned soils
abstract: Increasingly frequent and severe fires worldwide underscore the need to understand how pyrophilous microbes survive, thrive, and drive post-fire ecosystem regeneration. However, characterizing their traits through omics and phenotypic assays is limited by the lack of cultured isolates. title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. abstract: Background Diabetic fracture-associated infection (DFAI) is characterized by impaired immune defense, persistent inflammation, bacterial biofilm formation, and delayed bone repair. abstract: In contemporary hybrid conflicts, cultural heritage is targeted not only through physical destruction but increasingly also through digital manipulation. This study proposes a systematic framework for detecting and analyzing cultural weaponization such as the strategic distortion, reframing, or erasure of cultural narratives, on English Wikipedia, using Ukraine as a case study and combining large-scale revision analysis, semi-automatic LLM-based annotation, and expert validation to trace how contested cultural meanings evolve over time. abstract: Wurfbainia villosa (Zingiberaceae) is an economically and medicinally significant plant in southern China, yet the diversity, taxonomy, and ecological roles of its associated fungi remain poorly understood. Through surveys conducted in Guangdong and Yunnan provinces, we obtained 197 fungal isolates from symptomatic, asymptomatic, dead, and decaying tissues of different parts of W. villosa. abstract: Fog harvesting is an effective and low-cost strategy for meeting part of the water demand in fog-prone areas. However, the efficiency of conventional fog collectors is compromised by limitations in the effective collection and drainage of droplets. In this study, the fog collection efficiency of harp-based polyester multifilament fog collectors fabricated from partially oriented yarns (POY) and fully drawn yarns (FDY) was evaluated. title: Size, morphology and ecology explain interspecific differences in the use of bird bills and legs as thermal windows
abstract: Birds use their bills and legs as thermal windows, increasing near‐surface blood flow to dissipate heat in hot conditions while restricting blood flow to conserve heat in cold conditions. How adept species are at vasomotor control of heat loss via bills and legs may influence their capacity to adapt to a warming climate. title: Listeria monocytogenes in the Genomic Era: Persistence Mechanisms, Disinfectant Tolerance, Virulence Diversity, and Evolving Food Safety Challenges in Ready‐to‐Eat Food Systems
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is a ubiquitous Gram‐positive bacterium and the causative agent of listeriosis, one of the most lethal foodborne diseases, with case fatality rates of 20%–30% in susceptible populations. It grows at refrigeration temperatures, tolerates salt and modified atmosphere packaging, and survives exposure to quaternary ammonium compound (QAC) disinfectants. These traits make it a persistent threat in ready‐to‐eat (RTE) food systems. title: Tunnel junctions polarization engineering in III-nitride heterostructures
abstract: A classical p+/n+ tunnel junction is difficult to achieve in group-III nitride (III-N) semiconductors because of the high activation energy of acceptors. title: Metagenomic insights into the distribution and correlation of antibiotic resistance genes in a municipal wastewater treatment plant in Xi’an, China
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic environments may accelerate the evolution of antimicrobial resistance, with potential risks to ecosystems and public health. Municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) serve as critical reservoirs and hotspots for ARGs. This study employed metagenomic sequencing to investigate ARG distribution, diversity, and seasonal dynamics across treatment units of a WWTP-W in Xi’an, China, during summer and winter, and assessed correlations between ARG abundance and antibiotic concentrations. abstract: A series of fifteen quinoline–tetrazolo phenylhydrazone hybrids was synthesized via a four-step synthetic route involving the preparation of 2-chloroquinoline-3-carbaldehydes, incorporation of the tetrazole moiety, and subsequent condensation with substituted phenylhydrazines. abstract: Human‐induced changes in predator densities affect various aspects of prey biology, yet their consequences for prey nutrition are rarely quantified. We investigated how feral dogs shape the nutritional ecology of the desert lizard Saara hardwickii . In parts of the Thar desert, extremely high feral dog densities create hotspots of elevated predation risk for S. hardwickii . title: β12 borophene as a next-generation platform for PFAS adsorption: a DFT investigation
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) have garnered significant attention owing to their extreme persistence, bioaccumulation potential, and harmful effects on both human health and ecosystems. In the current work, the adsorption capability of the β 12 nanosheet toward toxic PFASs, namely PFAS = PFBA, PFBS, PFOA, and PFOS, was systematically investigated, using density functional theory calculations. abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is associated with increased colonization by adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) and altered intestinal lactate metabolism. Here, we investigated how lactate metabolism shapes host–AIEC interactions using intestinal epithelial cells, macrophages, and a mouse model of AIEC infection. This paper examines the portrayal of adolescent depression and parental psychological control in the Chinese television drama A Little Reunion, focusing on Episodes 37–41 and the character Qiao Yingzi. abstract: Polychromatic luminescent materials have attracted sustained interest owing to the potential applications in high-sensitivity visual optical sensing. abstract: Integrating emergent optical, ionic, mechanical, and electronic functionalities within soft materials enables autonomous electronics, intelligent robotics, and adaptive human–machine interfaces. Here, we introduce photoresponsive piezoionics in eutectogels nanocomposites (NCs) containing photochromic WO 3 nanoparticles (NPs). title: Recent advances in hydrogel-based 3D-printed bioinks for bone regeneration and potential applications in osteoporosis
abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease characterized by impairment of bone remodeling, reduced bone strength, and fragility fractures. Despite active exploration of hydrogel-enabled 3D printing and bioprinting as tools for engineering bone tissue, the therapeutic implications for osteoporosis are still debated since most of the available data derive from general bone defect and osteochondral repair models. title: Solar cell efficiencies and light spectra: From measurements at a specific color temperature to predictions for solar spectrum conditions
abstract: We present a method to predict solar cell efficiencies from laboratory measurements where a solar spectrum is not necessarily available. The trick is to use an incandescent light such as a halogen work lamp. The efficiency measured in this light can be transformed to predictions for solar spectrum conditions. This is because both the incandescent light and the solar spectrum are approximated reasonably well by Planck distributions.

abstract: Advancements in nanotechnology have expanded its prospects as a promising avenue for addressing concerns over environmental remediation, sustainability, and industrial waste management through the development of metal-based nanoparticles. This study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using four varieties of Aster flowers (white, pink, lavender, and violet) and their potential for antioxidants, catalytic, cytotoxic, and in silico molecular docking activities. abstract: Following mid-20th-century agricultural abandonment, European landscapes experienced significant secondary succession. abstract: Bioorthogonal chemistry has transformed molecular imaging by enabling highly selective synthetic labeling of biomolecules in their native habitats. Despite its remarkable success, the chemical space available for multiplexed bioorthogonal imaging remains fundamentally constrained by the limited repertoire of mutually orthogonal reactions. abstract: Protein complexes are central to cell biology and typically verified via a combination of interaction data, complete genome sequencing and comprehensive protein-coding gene predictions for reference eukaryotes. abstract: The Indian pangolin ( Manis crassicaudata ) is an endangered and poorly studied mammal in Pakistan, where limited ecological information constrains effective conservation planning. This study assessed its spatial distribution, relative abundance, habitat characteristics, and anthropogenic pressures in Abbottabad District, Lesser Himalayas, Pakistan, from October 2024 to September 2025. abstract: Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . title: A Fungal Hyaluronate Lyase with a Distinct Catalytic Machinery Expands the Polysaccharide Lyase Landscape
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a major glycosaminoglycan of the vertebrate extracellular matrix whose biological functions depend strongly on its molecular weight. Controlled depolymerization of HA into defined oligosaccharides is therefore of considerable biomedical and biotechnological interest. Although bacterial HA lyases have been extensively characterized, fungal HA-degrading enzymes remain poorly understood, and none has been structurally assigned to a defined CAZy family. abstract: Croton maci (Euphorbiaceae) is described herein as a new species endemic to the restinga ecosystems of Northeastern Brazil. abstract: BACKGROUND: Rapid aging intensifies health equity challenges in China due to growing elderly medical demands. abstract: The Amazon Basin faces mounting socio-environmental pressures that threaten both ecological integrity and food security. We analyzed phloem monoterpene concentrations and composition from four pine species used by the mountain pine beetle across 11 sites in western North America and examined how host species, geography, environment, and monoterpene synthase (mono-TPS) gene variation relate to differentiation among host monoterpenes. title: Everyday treasures: Applying product personalities to design user–product relationships
abstract: This research applies Transactional Analysis, a theory of interpersonal relationships, to identify people's relationships with emotionally attached and frequently used objects in their daily routines. Through two complementary studies, it investigates both the nature of these attachments and their implications for design. In Study 1, thirty semi-structured interviews invited participants to present their favourite objects, explain the reasons for their attachment, and rate the objects' perceived personality attributes and the emotions they evoke. abstract: BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus types 40 and 41 (HAdV-40 and HAdV-41), belonging to the species Mastadenovirus faecale, are among the leading viral causes of acute gastroenteritis in children. Despite their clinical importance, whole-genome data on circulating strains remain limited. This study investigated the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of enteric Mastadenoviruses detected in children with acute gastroenteritis. title: Unpredictable socioecology and the context-dependent expression of religious norms in Mauritius
abstract: Normative decision-making is central to collective action, as it often requires individuals to forgo partial personal gains in order to sustain broader within-group equality. Religious commitment has been theorized to foster normative conduct via beliefs in punitive supernatural agents and participation in collective rituals. Yet effects of such religious commitment on normative decision-making may not operate uniformly across contexts and vary with local socioeconomic conditions. title: Greek views of Russia after the invasion of Ukraine: a far left-right ‘axis of ressentiment’ against the West
abstract: How did Greeks view Russia after the invasion of Ukraine, and why? Based on a 2022 nationally representative survey of 1,578 Greek adults, this paper argues that pre-existing and interconnected left-right ideologies and East-West identities substantially divided the Greek public in their views of Russia. Specifically, there was a positive quadratic relationship between ideology and views of Russia, with supporters of the Greek far left (KKE) and far right (Greek Solution) the most pro-Russian, and centre right (New Democracy) supporters the most anti-Russian. title: High-level organic fertilization selectively reorganizes the soil microbiome across carbon-assimilation pathways and the antibiotic resistome
abstract: Increasing organic-fertilizer input is often expected to strengthen its effects on soil microbial functions, but it may instead redistribute functional potential across microbial groups and pathways. We tested these alternatives using shotgun metagenomics in an eight-year paddy–upland rotation under four fertilization regimes, focusing on the contrast between conventional organic fertilization (OF) and high-level organic fertilization (HOF). title: Electron donor–acceptor hybrid bonding polymers exhibit symmetry breaking and ferroelectricity
abstract: Hybrid bonding polymers chemically integrate supramolecular assemblies and covalent macromolecules and can therefore exhibit synergistic functionalities that can impact mechanical properties, catalytic activity, and robotic behavior, among others. In these materials, structural units are connected through both covalent and noncovalent bonds, and this hybrid bonding nature can lead to alterations in nanoscale morphology and internal ordering relative to purely supramolecular or purely covalent polymer systems. title: Experimental study of thermal, flow, acoustic and energetic performance of synthetic jet actuators with sharp-edged and rounded-edge nozzles
abstract: The objective of this paper is to experimentally investigate how the different geometries of the nozzle edge - rounded and sharp – affect the flow, thermal, acoustic, and energetic performance of a synthetic jet actuator. Both configurations are evaluated under identical dimensionless flow conditions, namely the same Reynolds and Strouhal numbers, and with the same internal diameter of the nozzle, matching these integral flow parameters. title: Functional diversity of GPCR–Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways
abstract: Gustducin (G gust ), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage G gust , and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. title: The rise of refinery margins: The case of the energy tax cut in Germany
abstract: This paper evaluates the temporary reduction in energy taxes implemented by the German government between 1 June and 31 August 2022. Measured against the delivered cost of importing the same fuel from the Amsterdam–Rotterdam–Antwerp (ARA) region, German wholesale prices net of tax rose by 5–6 (gasoline) and nearly 4 (diesel) cents per liter during the cut, corresponding to measured pass-through of 83% and 73%. title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. title: Identification of the SNHG14/hsa-miR-577/CLIC4 ceRNA axis reveals the association of CLIC4 with stromal activation and microenvironment remodeling in colorectal cancer
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a prevalent malignancy with complex molecular regulatory mechanisms. In this study, we analyzed transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and identified differentially expressed mRNAs, miRNAs, and lncRNAs. Using integrative bioinformatics approaches, we constructed a CRC-specific ceRNA regulatory network to screen candidate regulatory molecules involved in CRC progression. title: An impact-embedded framework for product-level circularity assessment: Evidence from railway materials and components
abstract: : The circular economy (CE) is increasingly promoted to improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental impacts, particularly in material-intensive sectors such as transport infrastructure. However, most existing circularity indicators remain material-centric, focusing on material flows and recycling rates while treating environmental impacts separately. title: Battery-free ingestible electronic capsule with programmable high-output soft actuation for active gastrointestinal interventions
abstract: Ingestible capsules have garnered considerable attention due to their high gastrointestinal (GI) transitability and minimally invasive nature. However, constrained by pill-sized dimensions (approximately 2 to 4 cubic centimeters), current ingestible capsules face persistent challenges in achieving both controllable high mechanical output and sufficient onboard power delivery, limiting their capacity for effective in vivo therapeutic interventions. abstract: Transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1) and TAK1-binding proteins (TABs) are critical regulators of innate immune signaling pathways. In this study, TAK1, TAB1, and TAB2 were identified from lampreys (Lethenteron reissneri), their evolutionary characteristics and immune functions were investigated. abstract: In oilwells CO2 reacts with Portland cement, inducing portlandite dissolution and C–S–H decalcification, which reduce compressive strength and increase permeability, thereby compromising zonal isolation and wellbore integrity. title: Fuel efficiency gains, market restructuring and rising fuel consumption in global passenger aviation (1996–2025)
abstract: Fuel or GHG emission efficiency improvements are a key part of aircraft manufacturers’ narratives about their commitment to climate mitigation. However, climate impact depends on absolute emissions, and therefore on the amount of fuel burnt. The latter depends on several parameters, including traffic volumes, distances flown, fleet mix and seat density aboard. This calls for a joint assessment of the combined effect of technological progress, fleet renewal, market restructuring and traffic growth on the fuel consumption. title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. title: Sheep grazing within regenerative perennial systems accelerates soil carbon and nitrogen accrual
abstract: Background Global agricultural intensification and crop-livestock decoupling have reduced soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, weakening terrestrial carbon sinks and altering nutrient cycling. Integrating livestock into cropping systems is a cornerstone regenerative practice, with the potential to enhance carbon and nitrogen storage. Studies used leaves, balsam/storax, resins, volatile oils, and formulations whose chemical differences complicate direct comparison. title: Personalism and the Power of Story
abstract: This essay argues that twentieth‐century Christian personalism found a particularly vital and resilient expression through the mid‐century theological novel. While the personalist movement encompassed diverse philosophical strands, its defense of the human person as an irreducible mystery offered a profound counterweight to modern utilitarian objectification. Drawing upon Graham Greene's The Power and the Glory , this essay illustrates how the psychological depth and relational dynamics of the novel uniquely embody personalism's core tenets. title: Extracellular metabolome and antioxidant phenotypes of coffee-derived non-conventional yeasts
abstract: Cell-free supernatants (CFSs) from non-conventional yeasts (NCYs) contain extracellular constituents potentially associated with biological activity, although their chemical composition remains poorly characterized. This exploratory study investigated the extracellular chemical profiles and antioxidant properties of five yeast isolates recovered from spontaneously fermented Coffea arabica cherries: Kurtzmaniella quercitrusa Lev3, Lev5, Lev11, and Lev13, and Meyerozyma caribbica Lev10. title: 3D DCIP for detection of internal defects in Älvkarleby test embankment dam
abstract: Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) and Induced Polarization (IP) data can be used to detect internal erosion in embankment dams, as they reflect variations in subsurface properties such as water content and soil grain size. This study evaluates the combined use of ERT and IP in a test embankment dam in Älvkarleby, Sweden, constructed with several intentional but undisclosed defects. title: Phylodynamic analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in the Gambia: a 2-year genomic surveillance investigation
abstract: The dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 viral spread are well documented in high income countries. However, limited sequence data in low-and middle-income countries have hampered our understanding of the virus’s spatiotemporal circulation within Sub-Saharan Africa. We used Bayesian phylogeographic inference to reconstruct the origin and migration pattern of SARS-CoV-2 sequenced in The Gambia during the pandemic. abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria underscores the urgent need for alternative antimicrobial strategies. abstract: Objective The management of moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) has advanced considerably with the introduction of B-cell-targeted therapies. title: Early Hydration of Mixtures of MgO and Hydromagnesite
abstract: This work investigates the hydration of mixtures of magnesium oxide (MgO) and hydromagnesite (HY), with a particular focus on the formation of the recently described hydrous carbonate-containing brucite (HCB) phase. Whereas MgO normally hydrates to brucite in aqueous media, the addition of a hydrated magnesium carbonate such as HY promotes the formation of an amorphous brucite-like structure that can incorporate both water and carbon into its interlayers and that exhibits characteristic stacking faults. title: Fragility and loss assessment of a multi-span highway bridge with traceable inputs and verified computation
abstract: Lifetime seismic loss assessments of bridges are commonly demonstrated with inputs a reader cannot trace: damage thresholds fitted to a convenient shape, event rates rising with calendar time, and discount rates without a source. This paper assesses the fragility and seismic loss of a four-span reinforced concrete highway bridge using key inputs traceable to published sources, the structural model, or explicitly declared assumptions, with key computational steps independently checked. abstract: Ferrofluid-based soft robots with extreme deformability have emerged as promising manipulation tools for diverse biomedical applications. Their unique properties to navigate irregular terrains and access otherwise unreachable regions within confined spaces have enabled new opportunities in targeted drug delivery, microfluidic logistics, and lab/organ on-a-chip. title: Preclinical Toxicology of a Succinic Acid Salt of a Polyhexamethylene Guanidine Derivative: Acute and Repeated-Dose Studies
abstract: The growing interest in ocular antiseptics is driven by their broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and potential to mitigate antimicrobial resistance. In a previous study, systemic effects of ophthalmic drops based on succinic acid derivative of polyhexamethylene guanidine (ss-PHMGd) following ocular instillation were investigated in a preclinical model. title: One-step antimicrobial peptide immobilization technique: universal compatibility with clinical bone cements
abstract: This study validates one-step antimicrobial peptide nisin-based modification compatible with clinical cements. Modified cements retain suitable handling and biocompatibility. This low-cost strategy facilitates anti-infective bone cement translation.

title: Segmenting the Geotourist Profile in the Caminhos dos Cânions do Sul UNESCO Global Geopark Based on Motivations: a Categorization Proposal for a New Territory
abstract: Understanding visitor motivations is essential for developing effective geotourism strategies and enhancing the management of UNESCO Global Geoparks. This study analyzes and segments the geotourist profile of visitors to the Caminhos dos Cânions do Sul UNESCO Global Geopark (CCSUGGp), southern Brazil, based on their travel motivations. title: Evolutionary dynamics of the vertebrate Wnt gene repertoire
abstract: The Wnt gene family plays a central role in vertebrate development, yet its evolutionary dynamics across lineages remain largely unexplored. Here, we present the most comprehensive analysis of Wnt gene evolution in vertebrates to date, leveraging a large-scale comparative genomics approach of 38,886 Wnt gene sequences mined from 1,961 species. We first investigate overall patterns of gene retention, duplication, and loss, and then focus specifically on the impact of whole-genome duplications (WGDs). title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
abstract: Climate change mitigation from Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) comes with severe sustainability risks and faces major implementation challenges. Yet, the consequences of missing out on AFOLU mitigation potential for the transition of the energy sector and the achievability of climate objectives are not well understood. Here, using the Integrated Assessment Modeling framework REMIND–MAgPIE, we derive future mitigation pathways under different AFOLU policy portfolios. title: The Outsized Effect of Minute Contaminants on the Physical Properties of H2 as Shown Through the Example of Industrial Forced Draft Burners
abstract: As of today, multiple gaseous H2 quality specifications and a single H2 quality standard (ISO 14687:2025) exist. These specifications allow a varying amount of contaminant gases, including contaminants which have no heating value, such as CO2 or N2. Due to the large difference in the physical properties (e.g. density) between these contaminants and H2, even minute amount of contaminant can change the properties of the mixed gas significantly. For example, allowing 2% CO2 in H2 means that the density increases by approximately 40% and the Wobbe index decreases by almost 20% compared to pure H2.

title: A spatially explicit framework for evaluating resource performance across heterogeneous land-use grid cells
abstract: Resource performance evaluation examines how resource inputs are transformed into desirable outcomes while minimising undesirable consequences. Resource performance is spatially uneven, as resource inputs and outputs vary with the human activities and natural processes associated with different land-use types. Existing evaluations either aggregate performance across administrative units or focus on isolated land-use types. abstract: An indole-based colorimetric and reversible ligand, MPH, was developed for the selective detection of Cu 2+ , showing the molecular logic-gate operation, paper-based detection, and successful application to real samples.

abstract: This article examines how citizens assess multinational enterprises' impacts on local communities to inform justice‐oriented practices towards achieving more just relationships between multinationals and local communities. Using a novel mixed‐methods research design grounded in environmental justice, this research examined the views of the citizens of the Huasco Valley in Chile regarding the impacts of two closed and two operating multinationals on communities. title: Deep karst systems as indicators of transtensional deformation: evidence for a releasing step-over geometry in the Alburni Massif (Italy)
abstract: In the southern Apennines, neotectonic evolution is driven by the interaction between strike-slip and extensional regimes. These processes fragmented the Mesozoic carbonate platforms into structurally distinct massifs. Within this regional framework, the Alburni Massif is a key area for investigating tectonic controls on deep speleogenesis. We focus on the massif’s Central Zone, which hosts the highest concentration of cave entrances and the most developed cave systems. title: Background selection behavior follows ontogenetic color change in Nessus sphinx moth caterpillars (Amphion floridensis)
abstract: Animals have evolved an array of strategies for maximizing background matching camouflage in complex and colorful environments, including color change and background selection. Here we investigate background selection in Nessus sphinx ( Amphion floridensis ) caterpillars, which change color as they grow. Caterpillars transition from green to brown, with some individuals expressing a rare pink phenotype before changing to brown.
