title: Vegetation complexity as a multi-dimensional indicator of soil organic carbon storage, but not nitrogen storage, in dryland ecosystems
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil total nitrogen (STN) are essential for primary productivity and nutrient cycling in terrestrial ecosystems. Although their drivers have been extensively studied, the role of vegetation complexity in regulating SOC and STN dynamics, along with the ecological processes involved, remains insufficiently understood. title: Sanguinarine-glycyrrhizic acid nanodiscs for atopic dermatitis via supramolecular and metabolic reprogramming
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with itching, barrier dysfunction, and immune-metabolic dysregulation. abstract: Peripheral populations often harbor unique evolutionary diversity yet face disproportionate conservation risk. The streamside salamander ( Ambystoma barbouri ) occurs primarily in the Ohio River basin in Kentucky, Indiana, and Ohio, but persists as isolated, disjunct populations in central Tennessee and western West Virginia, where rapid urbanization threatens remaining habitat. abstract: The interdependent relationship between mitochondrial and nuclear genomes is a powerful model for understanding how epistasis shapes the architecture and evolution of complex traits. Once considered a neutral marker, mitochondrial DNA variation is now recognized as critical to phenotypic evolution because of its epistatic interactions and history of coevolution with the nuclear genome. A central challenge in evolutionary genetics is to quantify the relative importance of stabilizing and directional selection shaping complex trait distributions within and among species. abstract: The 90-degree peeling test is widely used to characterize adhesion, with simple analytical solutions provided by Rivlin and Kendall that nearly coincide, implying negligible influence of tape elasticity. However, recent studies indicate that peeling viscoelastic adhesive tapes exhibits rate-dependent toughening, attributed to both the tape viscoelasticity and a single-parameter interfacial assumption, and that considering only uniform axial stress yields results approaching Rivlin’s prediction. title: Geometric compatibility assessment of the integrated edge-ramp model based on architectural traces in Khafre’s pyramid
abstract: The construction of the Pyramid of Khafre presents a challenge: raising over two million cubic meters over asymmetrical bedrock. This study provides a cross-monument evaluation of the Integrated Edge-Ramp (IER) framework, assessing geometric compatibility and logistical consistency in Khafre’s architectural and geological context. A geometric-logistic model includes a base leveling phase with short transitional ramps to compensate for uneven terrain before activating the perimeter system. title: Restoration of weathered sandstone by nonionic surfactant-assisted microbial-induced carbonate precipitation
abstract: Weathered sandstone in cultural heritage sites suffers from water‑induced degradation including cement dissolution and pore coarsening, and conventional repairs induce secondary damage and lack long‑term water‑resistant barriers. This study applied microbial‑induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) using Sporosarcina pasteurii with Triton X‑100 surfactant to lower surface tension, improve penetration, and facilitate uniform in-situ calcite precipitation within the sandstone pores. title: Is the river clean? Comparison between public perceptions and water quality monitoring reveals divergences in the understanding of pollution sources in Arequipa, Peru
abstract: Public perceptions of water quality are crucial in shaping water-related behaviors and management decisions that influence water conditions. Yet these perceptions, formed through social, cultural, and environmental experiences, do not always align with scientific assessments of water quality. This study combines a face-to-face survey of 692 adult residents of Arequipa, Peru, conducted in 2022, with an analysis of river water quality data from the prior decade to examine the congruence between perceived and measured water quality in the city's largest water body, the Chili River. title: Production Optimization and Functional Characterization of Melanin Produced by Halotolerant Bacillus atrophaeus Isolated from a Hypersaline Environment
abstract: Melanin is a naturally occurring dark biopolymer widely distributed in microorganisms, plants, and animals, known for its remarkable physicochemical properties, including ultraviolet (UV) protection and antioxidant activity. In this study, a halotolerant bacterial isolate obtained from the hypersaline environment of Tuz Lake was identified as Bacillus atrophaeus and evaluated as a novel source of microbial melanin. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have shown different effects on soil physical structure, chemistry, and microbial communities. As soils are known to differ in their potential to develop structure, the observed variability in MP effects may be strongly attributed to MPs impact on soil aggregation. Hence, we here address the impact of different MPs on soil aggregation and associated soil functions such as water, carbon, and nutrient storage, and microbial habitat in soils differing in texture and soil organic matter (SOM). title: Matrix‐Specific Consumer Perception of Functional Enrichment in Plant‐Based Milk Alternatives: Evidence From a Cross‐Cultural Sensory Study
abstract: This study investigated matrix‐dependent consumer responses to the functional enrichment of oat and soy beverages fortified with two spray‐dried botanical powders in a study involving 344 participants from Denmark, Poland, and Spain. Six beverages, including fortified variants and non‐fortified controls, were evaluated using hedonic ratings, CATA profiling, purchase intent, after which consumers answered questions related to their background and dietary habits. abstract: Organisms, including humans are naturally inclined to move away from pain and move towards pleasure, making pain one of the most researched topics in contemporary times in the behavioural sciences. Pain is the alarm or symptom that announces that all is not right with the body and is the most common reason that can make an organism or people seek help and medical assistance. title: A century of mosquito diversity and distribution in Haiti and the Dominican Republic (1905–2024)
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases represent a major public health threat, particularly on islands and in resource-limited settings. Hispaniola, the second-largest island in the Caribbean, shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, is highly vulnerable to such diseases due to recurrent extreme climatic events, endemic diseases such as malaria, filariasis and dengue, and challenging socio-economic and political conditions that hinder effective vector control. title: Digital mindfulness in motion: A thematic analysis of user comments on Calm’s Instagram Reels
abstract: Objective: This study examined user comments on Calm’s Instagram Reels to explore how mindfulness-oriented short-form content is publicly received under platform-specific conditions. Methods: This qualitative, inductive study analyzed 2,054 user comments on 87 Reels posted on Calm’s official Instagram account between September 4, 2024, and January 30, 2025. abstract: To maximize the conservation impact of genetic resources, they should be applicable across the full distribution of a species, economically and logistically feasible, and validated for the diversity of sample types collected in the field. This is particularly relevant for large carnivores, which are elusive and wide-ranging, and whose individual movements and population dynamics often transcend administrative borders. title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
abstract: The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally important group of grasses 1,2 . Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition-associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type-specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type-enriched transcriptional programs. title: Changes in time discount rates associated with marriage and childbirth: evidence from Japanese panel data
abstract: Although classical economic models treat time preferences as stable, recent research suggests that they can change in response to life events. However, evidence on anticipated and widely experienced life events, such as marriage and childbirth, remains limited. Using 13-year unbalanced panel data from the Japan Household Panel Survey (2010–2022), we estimate individual fixed-effects models of within-person changes in time discount rates, elicited through a hypothetical choice between two delayed payments, around marriage and childbirth. title: Thermodynamic and Exergetic Analysis of a Two‐Stage Ammonia–Water Absorption Cycle for Simultaneous Power and Refrigeration Generation
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive thermodynamic and exergetic analysis of a novel two‐stage ammonia–water absorption power and refrigeration cycle designed to simultaneously produce mechanical power and cooling. The proposed configuration employs two generators operating at different temperature levels, enabling internal thermal energy recovery and more effective utilization of the supplied heat. title: Hemispherical Descent Imaging – an Observation Concept Capable of Enabling New Planetary Surface Imaging Opportunities
abstract: Planetary surface imaging is an essential source of data for conducting planetary science throughout the solar system. Novel imaging systems and alternatives to the predominant approaches (orbital, flyby and rover-based imaging) can open up new opportunities, both in the possible scientific analyses, and the regions of solar system that can be imaged. title: La (silenciada) obra en favor de la protección del medio ambiente de la Iglesia Católica a través de los pontífices
abstract: Este trabajo analiza la contribución de la Iglesia Católica a la protección del medio ambiente, resaltando cómo su enseñanza ha buscado concienciar sobre el respeto a la naturaleza y la necesidad de una gestión sostenible de los recursos. Además, se destaca su relación con el desarrollo del Derecho Internacional del Medioambiente, particularmente desde la Declaración de Estocolmo de 1972, y la forma en que los pontífices han vinculado la paz con la preservación del entorno. title: A Critical Utopian Gaming Pedagogy Practice to Co-Construct Emergent Senses of Place among Youth
abstract: This case study explores how a Critical Utopian Gaming Pedagogy practice facilitated the co-construction of emergent Senses of Place (SoP) to challenge dominant imaginaries of dystopian futures. The study involved youth from Play Utopia, a gaming club in a marginalized Barcelona neighborhood. Participants co-designed desirable futures through the city-building game Townscaper. A reflexive thematic analysis highlighted SoP through three themes: assemblages of community-centered life, akairotic dislocations grounded in places absent from participants’ lives, and resistance to urban speculation.

abstract: This study investigates the effect of green branding and green value on green customer loyalty through the mediating role of green customer satisfaction among consumers of environmentally friendly packaged mineral water products on the island of Java, Indonesia. Employing a quantitative descriptive research design, data were collected from 400 respondents across six major Javanese cities using purposive sampling and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 3.2.6. abstract: BACKGROUND: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most aggressive breast cancer subtype and is characterized by a high metastatic potential and limited treatment options. TNBC frequently metastasizes to lymphatic vessels and the presence of breast cancer cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes (LNs) is an important prognostic factor. abstract: BACKGROUND: Phrynops geoffroanus (Schweigger, 1812) is a freshwater chelonian widely distributed in South America, playing important ecological roles and commonly maintained under human care in institutions such as zoos. Despite its susceptibility to various diseases, reference values for hematologic and biochemical parameters in this species remain limited, restricting their clinical application. abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a significant indicator gas with considerable application value in atmospheric monitoring, industrial production, and medical diagnosis. abstract: Background Resprouting of native perennial grasses is central to their persistence and to fuel dynamics. Nonetheless, how changing environments influence resprouting success and vigor remains poorly understood for many perennial grass species. abstract: Multiyear droughts (MYDs) are severe drought events with profound impacts on human activities and ecosystems. abstract: Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) bring global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) reporting expectations into nationally situated reporting practices. abstract: Ice and frost accumulation on transparent and outdoor surfaces requires coatings that combine passive protection with active removal. abstract: Agricultural intensification and land abandonment are rapidly transforming traditional Mediterranean olive landscapes, with important consequences for biodiversity and ecological functions. abstract: Renovascular hypertension involves persistent activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, oxidative stress, inflammation, and cardiovascular remodeling. abstract: How plant genomes accommodate selective pressures across spatial and temporal scales remains poorly understood. Here, we address this by comparing the population-genomic signatures of root microbiome- and climate-associated loci in a natural Lotus japonicus population. abstract: Developments in the field of nanomedicine demonstrate that antioxidant-loaded nanoparticles (NPs) may improve targeted drug delivery. abstract: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is the most frequent primary antibody deficiency in adults. abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate how the soil substrate and harvest season influence the characteristics of multifloral honeys from the Alcarria region (Spain). abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous and aggressive hematologic malignancy associated with poor survival despite recent therapeutic advances. title: Transient species can increase resident metapopulation size by modifying local conditions and regional connectivity
abstract: Populations are regulated by processes operating at both local and regional scales. As a result, species can interact not only within local communities but also through regional-scale processes. However, the feedback between local and regional processes of species interactions in shaping metapopulation dynamics have rarely been tested experimentally. title: The Relationship Between Loneliness and Digital Addiction among Korean Young Adults Living Alone: The Mediating Effect of Depression and Anxiety and the Moderated Mediating Effect of Mental Well-being
abstract: Young adults living alone in Korea constitute a group in which limited social support, economic instability, and prolonged time spent alone converge, heightening relational deficits and compensatory reliance on digital devices. Based on the addiction syndrome model and the I-PACE model, this study examined whether depression and anxiety mediate the relationship between loneliness and digital addiction in this population and, on the basis of the complete state model of mental health, whether mental well-being moderates that mediating process. title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
abstract: Sp8 and Sp6 are closely related transcription factors expressed in the limb ectoderm, where they control proximo-distal and dorso-ventral patterning, yet their direct targets and molecular mechanisms have remained unclear. Combining genome-wide chromatin occupancy with transcriptomic profiling in vivo, we identify shared and specific targets and reconstruct the Sp8/Sp6 gene regulatory network, establishing Sp8 as its dominant, hierarchical node. Cologne Excellence Cluster on Cellular Stress Responses in Aging Associated Diseases

title: Scientific Insights into the Illegible and Discolored Red and Green Inks in Arabic Papyrus Protocols
abstract: Papyrus protocols are texts written on the outermost sheet of a papyrus roll, providing information relevant to its manufacture in a state-controlled facility. Arabic papyrus protocols constitute a key corpus of manuscripts that feature colored inks in early Islamic Egypt, with red and green inks used alongside iron-gall ink for writing the text. title: Synthesis Strategies and Photocatalytic Efficiency of Bi2O3 based Nanostructures: A Comprehensive Review on Recent Progress and Applications in Dye Degradation, CO2 Reduction and Hydrogen Generation
abstract: Bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) based nanomaterials have emerged as promising visible light driven photocatalysts for different applications like wastewater treatment, CO2 reduction and hydrogen generation. This is possible due to their suitable band structure, strong visible light absorption and chemical stability. This review presents a critical assessment of recent advances in the synthesis, modification and photocatalytic applications of Bi2O3 nanostructures for the degradation of organic dyes, pharmaceutical residues and other emerging pollutants. institutions: Centurion University of Technology and Management

title: From Past to Present: Rediscovering the Legacy of Chemical Analyses of Metals and Glass in the South Caucasus, Georgia
abstract: Soviet and post‐Soviet scholars (ca. 1921–2000s) produced a substantial body of archaeological science data on the South Caucasus, much of it published in Georgian and Russian and largely inaccessible to the international research community. These legacy datasets, detailing the volumetric and spectroscopic properties of metals and glass, offer valuable insight into material composition, production techniques, and metallurgical practices from Early to Late Bronze Age (ca. 3500–1500 bce ), and glass production from Late Bronze Age to Medieval period. title: Amplified Spontaneous Emission and Carrier Dynamics in Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion–Jacobson Quasi‐2D Perovskite
abstract: Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) quasi‐2D perovskites exhibit disparate chemical bonds and structures due to distinct organic spacer cations, endowing them with distinctive physical properties. A more far‐reaching investigation of the fundamental structure–physical relation, including the carrier dynamics, is expected in these layered perovskites. title: Enhanced microalgal biomass cultivation on anaerobic digestate depends on species selection, media characteristics and ammonium concentration
abstract: Microalgae cultivation on anaerobic digestate can contribute to the recovery and reuse of nutrients, but special attention is needed to achieve optimum digestate pre-treatment to support algal growth. Assessing culture performance based on feedstock dilution factors as the sole pre-treatment overlooks temporal variability in digestate composition, leading to poor performance reproducibility and potential operational failure at large scale. To address this, we implemented a one-variable approach to systematically isolate and evaluate the effects of key growth-limiting factors across digestates
journal: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology

title: TUBB2A as a Candidate Therapeutic Target for Alzheimer’s Disease: Orotidine-Mediated Metabolic Mechanisms and Druggability
abstract: As the most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, Alzheimer's disease (AD) poses a pressing need for novel therapeutic targets. This study was designed to address this gap by screening and validating druggable genetic targets nominally associated with AD through an integrative multi-omics approach. Mendelian randomization (MR) screened the druggable genome. GTEx eQTL data and differential expression analysis identified core candidates. SMR, GSMR, and cross-tissue eQTL validation assessed putative causal effects and cross-tissue generalizability. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dissected

title: Identification of Leading Factors Responsible for Solar Rebound Effect Among Residential Prosumers
abstract: Today, world economies have been facing many issues that contribute to environmental changes. Energy consumption is a major issue among all, as it is one of the largest carbon footprint producers. Growth of solar energy as a renewable resource is promoted to address the depletion of conventional energy sources and their harmful impact on the environment. The household sector is looked upon as major users of electricity and an increasing rate of solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption among them can speed up the transition towards sustainability. title: Air transport networks and urban economic activity: Dynamic relationships across major global airports
abstract: This study examines the dynamic relationships between air transport network structure and urban economic activity across the world’s top 50 airports by passenger volume in 2024, using monthly data from 2014 to 2024. As the aviation indicator, we adopt the Global Airport Connectivity Index (GACI), a composite measure of network measurements; as the economic indicator, we use Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Nighttime Lights (NTL), providing a globally consistent, high-frequency proxy for urban economic activity. journal: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice

title: Habitat filtering and species-specific spillover of forest gastropods across forest-open fen boundaries
abstract: Forest–open fen transitions represent sharp ecological boundaries for soil-dwelling fauna, but the extent to which forest species cross them depends on dispersal capacity, source habitat proximity, and environmental conditions. We examined forest gastropod occurrence along a forest–fen gradient to assess whether their presence in treeless calcareous fens is determined primarily by forest proximity or local habitat conditions. We integrated site-scale analysis of forest–fen transects in 17 Western Carpathian spring fens with a continental-scale analysis of 500 European calcareous fens. At the s

title: Carbonized rice husk–peat substrate improves irrigation water productivity in greenhouse tomato under reduced irrigation–fertigation
abstract: This study evaluated how cultivar and substrate modify greenhouse tomato responses to simultaneous reductions in irrigation water and nutrient supply. ‘Rambo F1’ and ‘Río Grande’ were grown under 100% or 50% crop evapotranspiration (ETc) in carbonized rice husk + peat, cattle-manure compost + peat, or vermiculite + peat (1:1, v/v). The factorial experiment lasted 212 days, with six biological replicates per treatment combination for most variables and three for proline. journal: Journal of the Saudi Society of Agricultural Sciences
institutions: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza

title: Multimodal Optical Anti‐Counterfeiting and Information Storage via Trap Manipulation Strategy in NaGdGeO 4 :Tb 3+ Long Persistent Luminescence Phosphors
abstract: In response to the growing demand for information security, the development of multimodal optical anti‐counterfeiting and information storage technologies is of paramount importance. In this context, long persistent luminescence (PersL) phosphors have attracted extensive research interest due to their unique luminescent properties. Herein, a series of Tb 3+ ‐doped NaGdGeO 4 PersL phosphors were successfully synthesized and exhibited the typical emission of Tb 3+ . title: Transcriptomic modulation of biofortified spinach through foliar application of lemon-derived vesicles and nanoencapsulated selenium
abstract: Selenium biofortification of crops is an effective strategy to address micronutrient deficiencies, although its efficiency is often limited by suboptimal uptake and phytotoxicity. In this study, we investigated the use of lemon-derived vesicles as nanocarriers for the foliar delivery of selenate in spinach ( Spinacia oleracea L.), aiming to enhance selenium accumulation while determining its effects on plant physiology. Plants were treated with free or nanoencapsulated selenate, and physiological, metabolic, and transcriptomic responses were evaluated. Nanoencapsulation of selenium in vesicles
institutions: Centro de Edafología y Biología Aplicada del Segura

title: Enamel thickness in the stem hylobatid Kapi ramnagarensis (Primates, Hylobatidae)
abstract: Enamel thickness has been extensively investigated in extant and fossil hominids, yet comparable data for hylobatids remain scarce. Existing studies are limited to Symphalangus syndactylus , Hylobates lar , and Hylobates muelleri and are based on relatively small samples. These studies have characterized enamel thickness as thin in Symphalangus and Hy. lar and intermediate‐thin in Hy. muelleri . The polarity of these conditions within Hylobatidae also remains unresolved because stem representatives of the clade have only recently been discovered. institutions: New York Consortium in Evolutionary Primatology

title: PILOT EVALUATION OF A SEMIAUTOMATED VERTICAL SYSTEM FOR HYDROPONIC OAT FODDER PRODUCTION
abstract: A forragem hidropônica permite produzir biomassa fresca em ciclos curtos e em estruturas compactas, mas o desempenho de sistemas verticais depende de uma distribuição adequada de água e da disponibilidade de luz. Este estudo piloto projetou e implementou um sistema semiautomatizado de quatro níveis para a forragem de aveia (Avena sativa L.) e comparou seu desempenho ao de uma estrutura de referência, operada simultaneamente com irrigação manual. Cada sistema continha 12 bandejas, cada uma com área de cultivo de 0,1326 m². A unidade semiautomatizada integrou reservatório de 30 L, bomba de 0,5 h

title: Structuring Firms' Alignment With the Sustainable Development Goals: ESG and Broader Corporate Performance Indicators
abstract: The literature on ESG indicators highlights the relevance of corporate contributions to sustainable development. However, fragmentation and a lack of standardized indicators limit alignment between corporate performance and global sustainability goals. This study examines how the literature has addressed the relationship between Corporate Performance, the SDGs, and ESG indicators in recent years, identifying prevailing approaches, measurement strategies, and reported findings. We conduct a systematic literature review complemented by bibliometric and content analyses. Results suggest a marked

title: Anxiety phenotypes accompany reduced Htr2a expression in prelimbic parvalbumin neurons following chronic heat exposure
abstract: Extreme heat is an increasingly important environmental stressor, but the neural alterations associated with sustained heat exposure remain poorly understood. Here we show that chronic heat exposure (36 °C, 4 h/day for 60 consecutive days) is associated with anxiety-like behaviors and altered local field potential and single-unit activity in the prelimbic cortex of male C57BL/6 mice. Optogenetic activation of parvalbumin-preferentially targeted prelimbic neurons ameliorates several behavioral alterations. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling indicates reduced Htr2a expression. institutions: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

title: IMPSA y WEG: : mercado eólico y energía industrial de Argentina y Brasil (2000-2019)
abstract: This article examines and compares the trajectories of two wind technology companies, WEG of Brazil and IMPSA of Argentina, in the context of the energy transition. The analysis covers the period 2000–2019 and considers a range of indicators relating to the broader economic environment, renewable energy support policies and instruments, and industrial policy. institutions: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

title: Antiviral activity of Clinacanthus siamensis Bremek ethanolic extract against dengue virus serotype 2 infection
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) infection causes dengue fever and can progress to severe, life-threatening diseases. Currently, no specific antiviral therapy is available, and although vaccines exist, their variable efficacy across DENV serotypes raises safety concerns. Therefore, the identification of effective antiviral agents remains critical for reducing disease severity and limiting viral transmission. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of the Thai medicinal herb Clinacanthus siamensis against DENV infection. title: Impacts of traditional and industrial approaches to oil palm cultivation on bird biodiversity and conservation in a West African rainforest landscape
abstract: Agricultural expansion threatens tropical ecosystems worldwide. Oil palm is cultivated primarily in Southeast Asia, but production in West Africa (its native range) is increasing rapidly. Here, oil palm is cultivated under traditional and industrial management, and the impacts on native West African ecosystems are poorly understood. title: Particulate matter induces apoptotic death of brain vascular endothelial cells in association with oxidative damage, DNA damage response, and MAPK/NF-κB signaling
abstract: Particulate matter (PM) is associated with cerebrovascular and neurological disorders, but the responses of brain vascular endothelial cell (BVEC) to PM remain incompletely understood. PM10 reduced BVEC viability and increased cell death, TUNEL labeling, and cleaved caspase-3 and PARP, accompanied by increased intrinsic and death receptor-associated apoptotic proteins, DNA damage response markers, MAPK/NF-κB signaling components, and lipid and protein oxidation markers. title: Barbed microneedle patch with programmable CO release for long-term and stage-specific therapy of chronic infected wounds
abstract: Chronic infected wounds are difficult to heal because bacterial colonization drives persistent inflammation, which further impairs tissue regeneration. This dynamic pathology requires stage-specific intervention, with rapid bacterial suppression followed by sustained inflammatory regulation. Carbon monoxide (CO) has concentration-dependent antibacterial and immunomodulatory activities, but on-demand and temporally programmed local CO release remains challenging. title: Neotropical lizard egg survival is related to predatory ant activity but not leaf litter depth
abstract: Accumulation of leaf litter and detritus on the forest floor is important for the detrital food web but may be affected by human-induced changes to climate and habitat. Long-term declines in leaf litter depth have been correlated with terrestrial lizard and frog population declines in the neotropics, but mechanisms driving this relationship remain uncertain. One possible mechanism is that reduced litter depth may drive changes in predator-prey relationships. title: Genetic Structure and Exchange of Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici Populations in China
abstract: Wheat powdery mildew caused by the obligate airborne biotrophic pathogen Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici ( Bgt ) is one of the most important diseases in wheat production in China. Understanding the genetic structure and genetic exchange in Bgt populations in China is important to understand epidemics and develop management strategies for wheat powdery mildew. title: Tracing Traditional Vestiges in Contemporary Mosaic Practice: A Study on the Mosaics of Gazanfer Bayram
abstract: This article examines the mosaic works of Macedonian artist Gazanfer Bayram, one of the leading figures of contemporary Balkan-Mediterranean mosaic art with a career spanning more than four decades, from thematic, iconographic, and stylistic perspectives. Bayram reinterprets the Early Christian and Byzantine Ravenna tradition through a contemporary idiom, and his works are examined comparatively against ancient and late antique examples using E. title: New insights into the biodiversity and taxonomy of the Capparis spinosa complex (Capparaceae) from Iran: integrated EST-SSR and morphological markers
abstract: Background and aims – Capparis sect. Capparis (also known as caper bush) comprises a group of perennial species within the Capparaceae family that grow across tropical and subtropical regions of Europe, Africa, and Asia, extending to Australia and Oceania. Despite the multiple social, ecological, and economic values of this group, its taxonomy has been controversial, probably because it represents a complex of closely related species. institutions: Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement

title: Photocatalytic activity of green-synthesized PANI/ZnO nanocomposite under solar irradiation: Water remediation applications
abstract: A morphologically modified PANI/ZnO NCs was synthesized using Solanecio gigas (S. gigas) leaf extract as a reducing and capping agent for the photocatalytic degradation of Crystal Violet (CV) under sunlight irradiation. PANI and ZnO NPs were synthesized via a green synthesis route, and the resulting nanomaterials were characterized using UV–Vis, FT-IR, SEM, and XRD. title: The Staphylococcus aureus Superantigen TSST-1 Directly Impairs Endothelial Migration and Vascular Regeneration
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus causes invasive infections characterized by extensive tissue injury and impaired healing. Although staphylococcal superantigens are best known for immune activation, emerging evidence suggests that they also directly disrupt vascular repair. This study investigated how toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 (TSST-1) affects endothelial migration and angiogenic remodeling. Immortalized human aortic endothelial cells were evaluated using viability and proliferation assays, cell-exclusion assays and live-cell imaging, actin staining, and proteomic profiling. title: Gümüş Nanopartiküller: Bitki Kaynaklı Yeşil Sentez, Karakterizasyon ve In Vitro Antikanser Aktiviteleri
abstract: Gümüş nanopartikülleri (AgNP), hastalıkların teşhis ve tedavisinin yanı sıra kozmetik, ilaç, sağlık, tarım ve gıda gibi birçok sektörde yoğun ilgi görmektedir. journal: Black Sea Journal of Engineering and Science

title: Effects of IRM 902 aging on the mechanical thermal and chemical properties of injection molded and extruded thermoplastics
abstract: This study investigates the aging behavior of injection- and extrusion-processed polypropylene impact copolymer (PP), polyethylene of raised temperature (PERT), and an impact-modified polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) grade formulated for pipe fabrication. Specimens were immersed in IRM 902 reference oil at both room temperature (RT) and 95 °C. title: Habitat type shapes the restructuring of peatland dragonfly communities over two decades
abstract: Climate warming is restructuring insect communities, and its effects are uneven among species. Understanding which species gain, which decline and why requires long‐term data on community composition, interpreted through the traits of the species involved. Peatlands hold isolated populations of cold‐adapted odonates at the southern margin of their ranges, yet long‐term data on how their assemblages are changing remain scarce. title: CFD-guided aerodynamic redesign of an electric bus for lower drag and energy demand
abstract: Electric buses face range and battery-temperature limits, and aerodynamic drag is a major part of their energy demand at higher speeds. This study examines how three features of an electric bus, the windshield inclination, the ground clearance and the roof transition angle, affect its aerodynamics, using steady computational fluid dynamics simulations of a 1:10 model of the BYD K9. Each feature was varied in turn, and the final combined design was simulated directly. title: Comparative One-Step Activation of Zhundong Coal Using KOH and ZnCl2: Hierarchically Porous Adsorbents for Malachite Green Adsorption
abstract: Although abundant in reserves, Zhundong coal is prone to severe slagging when combusted due to its high sodium content. Converting this coal into functionally designed carbon materials offers a sustainable strategy for clean utilization. This study compared hierarchically porous adsorbents prepared from Zhundong coal by one-step activation with ZnCl2 or KOH (denoted as ZnCl2@coal and KOH@coal, respectively) in terms of their pore structures and malachite green (MG) adsorption behavior in model aqueous solutions. title: Pareto-based screening of modified high-volume fly ash concrete formulations: Strength, environmental and economic trade-offs
abstract: Modifiers can improve the 28-day strength of high-volume fly ash (HVFA) concrete, but additional materials and processing may offset the environmental and economic benefits of cement replacement. This study assembled a harmonised literature database of 62 formulations, comprising 50 single-modifier HVFA mixtures, seven combined-modifier mixtures and five ordinary Portland cement (OPC) references. title: A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation
abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are central post-transcriptional regulators of bacterial gene expression, yet their evolutionary dynamics remain difficult to resolve due to limited sequence conservation. While sequence-homologous sRNAs can retain or diverge in function, unrelated sRNAs may independently evolve to regulate similar biological processes, making functional conservation invisible to sequence-based approaches. title: Butterfly diversity and community composition in a forest landscape restoration context in the tropics
abstract: Ecosystem restoration has become a global priority in tropical regions where land degradation, biodiversity loss, and climate change pose major challenges. In Rwanda, restoration activities are largely implemented within the framework of forest landscape restoration (FLR). However, the extent to which restored landscapes support biodiversity remains poorly understood. This paper examines butterfly diversity across different land cover types in Western Rwanda, where tree-planting restoration activities are widespread. title: Performance, Combustion, and Emission Analysis of a Ternary Hybrid Ethyl Ester Blend and Its Impact in a Single-Cylinder Compression Ignition Engine
abstract: Heavy-duty diesel engines significantly contribute to environmental degradation, motivating the search for sustainable alternatives like plant-derived biodiesel. This study investigates the performance and emissions of a novel ternary hybrid biodiesel blend made from shea butter, neem oil, and waste kitchen oils (40.41:19.73:39.86 w/w) in a direct-injection, four-stroke, single-cylinder diesel engine. title: Investigation of population dynamics in CO2-fixing bacteria associates plasmid expression loss to the expression of the genes of a heterologous production pathway
abstract: Introducing heterologous pathways into industrial hosts enables sustainable, cost-effective production of renewable chemicals. Plasmid-based expression ensures higher gene copy numbers than genomic integration and, greater production potential. However, imperfect plasmid inheritance makes the evaluation of production robustness essential for determining process viability. Stable strains are critical for maintaining consistent production, prolonging cultivations, ensuring reproducible titers, and minimizing byproduct formation. title: Responses of multi‐year plant–pollinator networks to temperature and drought variation across continents
abstract: Climate change is shifting species' distributions, activity periods and abundances, with consequences for species and interactions. Plant–pollinator interactions play a crucial role in maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, but it remains unclear whether responses to climatic variation are consistent across systems or depend on local ecological context. Here, we synthesize 12 multi‐year plant–pollinator network datasets from four continents to examine how interannual variation in temperature and drought shapes pollinator assemblages, floral resources and their interactions. title: Multilayer electrodeposition of functionally graded Cu–Al₂O₃ composite tubes: Effect of reinforcement architecture on microstructure and multiaxial mechanical behavior
abstract: The influence of reinforcement architecture on the multiaxial mechanical behavior of metal-matrix composite tubes remains insufficiently understood despite its importance for pressure-containing components. In this study, Cu-Al₂O₃ functionally graded material (FGM) tubes were fabricated by multilayer electrodeposition and compared with pure Cu and homogeneous Cu-Al₂O₃ composite tubes. SEM–EDS analysis confirmed uniform particle dispersion within individual deposited layers and the successful formation of the designed through-thickness compositional gradient. title: Discrepancies between airborne BTEX exposure, clinical outcomes, and risk perception in informal waste management setting, Indonesia
abstract: Open dumpsites are persistent sources of airborne pollutants. However, BTEX exposure, clinical outcomes, and perceived health risks remain insufficiently characterized. This study investigated discrepancies between airborne BTEX exposure, objective health indicators, and risk perception in an informal waste management setting. Ambient BTEX concentrations were quantified from 56 air samples collected across multiple landfill zones, while health outcomes were evaluated through clinical examinations and spirometry. Risk perception and self-reported symptoms were assessed using structured question

title: Baseline Diurnal Activity and Seasonal Patterns of the Critically Endangered Tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis Heude 1888) and Co-occurring Mammals in a Strict Protection Zone
abstract: Mammal activities are influenced by temperature and foraging opportunities particularly in the tropics which highlights the importance of understanding diel patterns and seasonal variations for evidence-based conservation. However, in the Philippines, behavioral studies on mammals remain scarce particularly for the critically endangered tamaraw Bubalus mindorensis (Heude, 1888). title: Bedrock-driven segregation is the main factor shaping local genetic structure of Dryas octopetala in the Western Carpathians
abstract: The genetic structure of temperate alpine plants is strongly influenced by historical factors, mainly connected with Pleistocene climatic oscillations. Less is known about how these broad-scale processes interact with local environmental heterogeneity, such as microclimate, substrate type and topography, to shape genetic structure at smaller spatial scales. The Western Carpathians, with their diverse habitats, varied bedrock, and the highest elevational gradients in the Carpathian chain, provide a relevant study area. title: Developing Pre‐Service Language Teachers' Critical‐Oriented Intercultural Awareness Within a Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Framework
abstract: Recent studies have posited that social justice‐ and critical pedagogy‐oriented concerns have called forth a diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) framework to use in considering critical issues related to language‐teacher education. While DEI offers a comprehensive approach with which to treat such issues, one perhaps can consider various subordinate critical perspectives as effective operators or agents of DEI. title: Determinants of Household Food Security among Smallholder Vegetable Farmers in the Oromia Region of Ethiopia: The Case of Adamitulu Jido Kombolcha and Dugda Woredas
abstract: This case study examined the determinants of household food security among smallholder vegetable farmers in the Oromia Region of Ethiopia. The study was conducted in six kebeles of Adami Tulu Jido Kombolcha, and Dugda woredas using a cross-sectional quantitative survey of 359 vegetable-producing households selected through multistage sampling method. title: Identifying Critical Fortification Node Sets for Directed Service Paths via Minimum Node-Cut Optimization
abstract: Maintaining end-to-end connectivity under disruption is a central problem in systems resilience. This study examines how limited protection resources can increase the minimum node-removal cost required to disconnect a specified service. Mission-Path Cut Fortification (MPCF) models a directed service as a functional graph and treats protection as a finite increase in node-removal cost. title: This study examined post-harvest losses (PHL) and their implications for food availability among smallholder fruit and vegetable farmers in Ethiopia's Oromia Region. The study was conducted in six kebeles of Adami Tulu Jido Kombolcha and Dugda woredas using a cross-sectional quantitative survey of 359 fruits and vegetable-producing households selected through multistage sampling method. Data were collected using structured questionnaires administered through KoboCollect App from December 2023 to March 2024. We assessed farm-level post-harvest loss (PHL) using the Aggregate Self-Reported Method, in which farmers reported quantities lost during harvesting and handling, transportation, storage, and marketing; we calculated percentage loss relative to the initial harvested quantity. The estimated producer-level losses were 11.84% for tomato, 8.62% for kale, and 13.81% for papaya. Regional-level PHL estimates were extrapolated by applying the farm-level loss rates estimated in this study to Oromia Region’s annual fruit and vegetable production data for 2013-2022. A deterministic 25% PHL-reduction scenario was used to estimate the quantity of produce that could theoretically be recovered and converted, using a dietary consumption benchmark into annual fruit-and-vegetable person-year supply equivalents. The analysis estimated cumulative fruit and vegetable PHL of 724,071.91 tons over the 2013-2022 period. Under the 25% PHL-reduction scenario, the estimated quantity of produce that could potentially be recovered varied across the study years. In 2022, the recovered quantity was equivalent to the annual fruit-and-vegetable consumption requirement of 832,444 people for one year (832,444.34 person-year equivalents), representing the highest annual estimate during the study period. When the annual estimates for 2013-2022 are summed, they amounted to approximately 3.31 million person-years. This cumulative estimate represented the aggregate annual food-supply equivalent generated over the ten years, expressed as the number of one-person annual fruit-and-vegetable consumption requirements that could theoretically be met by the recovered produce in each respective year. The findings indicated that reducing producer-level PHL could increase the quantity of fruit and vegetables potentially available for consumption, highlighting the importance of improved harvesting, handling, storage, transportation, and marketing practices among smallholder farmers. Key words: Post-harvest loss, smallholder farmers, fruit and vegetables, food availability, Ethiopia

abstract: This study evaluates the use of terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) for non-destructive estimation of above-ground biomass components in apple orchards. The research aimed to quantify leaf, wood (trunk and branches), and fruit biomass and analyze their correlations with key soil parameters. Eighteen apple trees from a semi-intensive orchard in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, were scanned using a Leica ScanStation C10. abstract: La productividad constituye uno de los fundamentos esenciales del crecimiento económico sostenible y un factor determinante para comprender las diferencias en los niveles de desarrollo entre las naciones. title: Ethnobotanical study of wild edible plants used by the Loi community of Manipur, India
abstract: Manipur is well known for its rich traditional food culture and indigenous cuisines, with a large proportion of rural communities relying on wild edible plants (WEPs) for nutrition, livelihoods, and cultural practices. The present study aimed to systematically document WEPs diversity, traditional cuisines, and their ethnobotanical significance among the Loi community of Phayeng village, Imphal West District, Manipur, India. title: Phosphate-modified ZSM-5 catalyst converting beverage wastewater to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and electrochemical upgrading
abstract: Converting sugars in beverage wastewater into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) provides a sustainable waste valorisation pathway. A heterogeneous phosphate-modified ZSM-5 catalyst was examined as an alternative to the conventional homogeneous sulfuric acid catalyst for selective 5-HMF production from beverage wastewater under hydrothermal conditions. Treating ZSM-5 with KH2PO4 introduces surface phosphate species while preserving zeolite crystallinity and the coexistence of acidic and basic active sites. title: Floristic and ecological diversity of vascular plants in the Cherat region, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
abstract: This study investigated the floristic and ecological diversity of vascular plants in the Cherat region of Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Seasonal field surveys were conducted from November 2023 to September 2024 across ecologically contrasting habitats, and collected specimens were identified using standard taxonomic references and herbarium protocols. title: Paul Vageler (1882–1963) and His Pivotal Role in Germany's “Colonial Soil Science”
abstract: This essay examines the role and activities of the German–Brazilian soil scientist Paul Vageler (1882–1963) in Germany's colonial policies and ambitions between 1909 and 1945. It highlights his scholarly achievements during the German Empire (with colonial possessions), the Weimar Republic (colonial revisionist thinking following the loss of those possessions), and the “Third Reich” (large‐scale colonial planning). title: Family Firms’ Productivity in Complex Regions
abstract: Prior studies suggest that regional contexts shape family firm performance, yet evidence remains mixed, often attributed to heterogeneity among family firms and regional characteristics. Less attention has been paid to how regional economic complexity influences family firm outcome. Using a panel of more than 90,000 Swedish firms over 25 years, we examine the relationship between regional economic complexity and family firm labour productivity. abstract: Mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) processing generates large quantities of shell byproducts that are typically discarded despite their potential as a renewable source of bioactive polysaccharides. In this study, polysaccharides were extracted from mung bean shells using cellulase-assisted extraction (MbSP-1) and hot-water extraction (MbSP-2), purified by ethanol precipitation, papain deproteinization, dialysis, and freeze-drying, and characterized by total sugar analysis, HPSEC, monosaccharide profiling, NMR, FTIR, XRD, SEM, and TGA. abstract: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines have emerged as an integrated framework since the early 2000s, reflecting their collective importance for addressing contemporary educational, economic, and societal challenges. Despite widespread use of the term in education, and in governmental policy initiatives promoting “STEM education,” the cognitive and developmental mechanisms that might link these disciplines remain largely un-investigated or un-tested. title: Alginate hydrogel co-loaded with phellodendron bark extract and HucMSC-exosomes for combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-repair acne effects
abstract: Acne vulgaris is a common inflammatory skin disorder involving follicular hyperkeratosis, Cutibacterium acnes proliferation, and aberrant inflammation, often leading to scarring. Current antibiotic treatments face resistance and limited repair capacity. Here, we developed an alginate-based hydrogel co-loaded with Phellodendron bark extract (PBE) and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (HucMSC-Exo) (PE gel). title: Late Holocene sediment dynamics in a mesoscale fluvial catchment from Upper Franconia (SE-Germany): Bayesian age-depth modelling based on OSL-chronologies
abstract: : Chronological frameworks are fundamental for reconstructing sedimentary processes and quantifying environmental change. Yet translating geochronological data into reliable sedimentation rates remains a major challenge, particularly when based on age-depth relationships. In fluvial systems, where deposition is episodic and stratigraphically incomplete, both the uncertainties of dating methods and the assumptions inherent to Bayesian modelling complicate the interpretation of sediment dynamics. title: Alkali-catalyzed transesterification of coconut and sunflower oils for biodiesel production
abstract: Introduction: Biodiesel represents a promising renewable energy source because it is biodegradable, environmentally friendly, and can reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Coconut and sunflower oils, with their relatively high oil content and availability, are potential renewable feedstocks for biodiesel production. Materials and methods: Coconut and sunflower oils were converted into biodiesel through alkali-catalyzed transesterification using NaOH as the catalyst and methanol as the transesterifying agent at an oil-to-methanol volume ratio of 5:1. title: A Method for Integrating Second-Home Populations into the Planning and Management of Services
abstract: Second-home (SH) growth and increased awareness of its negative impacts raise pressure on municipalities to enhance their role in planning SH-development (SHD) and SH-use. This paper addresses concerns shared by destinations worldwide and presents a collaboratively developed method primarily grounded on publicly accessible data to assess how SHD affects the demand for services – a key aspect for meeting the needs of visitors and residents and supporting local economies. Findings show that SH-users create opportunities for expanding commercial services but also exert pressure on public services

title: Spatio-temporal clustering of dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca. title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects a substantial proportion of individuals with major depressive disorder, posing a significant clinical and societal burden. Among emerging interventions, tractography-guided Subcallosal Cingulate Deep Brain Stimulation (SCC-DBS) shows promise as a treatment for TRD. However, despite the use of connectome-based targeting methods, clinical outcomes remain variable across individuals. title: Time-series modelling and forecasting of acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) in the Gaza Strip before and during the war in October 2023
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the temporal consistency and plausibility of manually collected data on acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) consultations reported by UNRWA staff based in Gaza and Cairo relative to the historical surveillance baseline. Further, the study aims to show the impact of the war in the Gaza Strip that began in October 2023 and the massive forced displacement of the Gaza population from Rafah governorate on the shape of the AWD curve. abstract: Acalypha pilosa Cav. is an underexplored medicinal species traditionally used in Mexico for the treatment of chronic wounds and skin lesions, although its phytochemical composition remains poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effect of Instant Controlled Pressure Drop (DIC) pretreatment on the recovery of phenolic compounds and antioxidant capacity from A. pilosa leaves as preliminary indicators of its potential application in cutaneous regeneration. abstract: Electrocatalytic reduction reaction of nitrate to ammonia (NO 3 RR) has emerged as a promising strategy that couples nitrate pollutant remediation with sustainable NH 3 production. Practical nitrate-containing industrial wastewater usually presents a wide pH distribution range, which puts forward an urgent requirement for pH-adaptive NO 3 RR catalysts with high ammonia selectivity. abstract: Ethiopian naked barley (Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum) represents a vital traditional cereal crop adapted to diverse and challenging highland agroecologies. Despite its agronomic and nutritional significance, high-density, genome-wide genetic characterization of this germ plasm remains limited. abstract: Sesquiterpene ozonolysis contributes to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation by producing Criegee intermediates (CIs) via primary ozonide (POZ) decomposition. abstract: Ageing associates with obesity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired glucose homeostasis. Previously, we documented that succinic acid (SA) treatment improves mitochondrial function and adiposity; however, the effects on ageing are unknown. Therefore, we determined the effect of SA treatment on metabolic health in 19 aged male mice (Age; 16 months), randomized to receive vehicle (Veh, n = 8) or SA (n = 11) and compared to young controls (Young; 6 months) (n = 24). abstract: This research explores the formulation of cisplatin tablets utilizing microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) derived from coconut coir as a sustainable matrix material. title: Uneven Progress in Urban Air Quality: Evidence From the Greater Bay Area and Implications for Metropolitan Management
abstract: Improving urban air quality requires attention to both regional trends and persistent differences between cities. This study examines how these patterns inform urban environmental management across the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. Official observations from 23 monitoring stations across 11 cities during 2019–2025 were analysed using city comparisons, a continuity-screened sample of 18 stations, and monthly regressions with seasonal controls and heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent covariance estimates. title: The mediating role of individual entrepreneurial orientation in the relationship between perceived organizational support and employee performance in the manufacturing sector
abstract: This study examines the influence of perceived organizational support on employee performance by incorporating individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) as a mediating variable in the manufacturing sector. The study addresses how employees’ perceptions of organizational support can stimulate entrepreneurial-oriented behavior that contributes to improved performance. title: Beyond Chapter VII: A quantitative analysis of how the Security Council moderates the legal value of its resolutions
abstract: The Security Council is considered the only organ within the United Nations that can issue legally binding decisions for states. With over two thousand resolutions adopted, the UNSC has developed a practice of formalistic legal language. However, the conditions under which resolutions are considered binding are controversial. title: Carbon sequestration in concrete: Emission gaps, material opportunities, and a decision framework for net-zero pathways
abstract: Carbon capture and utilisation in concrete is projected to contribute substantially to decarbonisation, yet few routes have progressed beyond demonstration stage. This review argues that the commercialisation gap persists because CO 2 uptake is treated as the primary measure of success, though it indicates little about overall viability, and no means exists of comparing pathways on a common basis. title: Aloe vera-mediated green-synthesized silver nanoparticles enhance physiological performance and yield in bread wheat
abstract: Green-synthesized silver nanoparticles (GS-AgNPs) have emerged as promising nano-biostimulant for improving crop productivity; however, their physiological effects under field conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study synthesized Aloe vera-mediated GS-AgNPs and characterized them using UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, DLS, zeta potential, XRD, SEM, and EDX analyses. title: Distinct Probiotic Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 in a Rat Model of Spleen qi Deficiency Syndrome
abstract: Spleen qi deficiency syndrome (SDS) is characterized by chronic fatigue, gastrointestinal dysfunction, and systemic metabolic disturbances and has been associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and chronic inflammation. This study evaluated the effects of two probiotic strains, Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 (LFP) and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 (BAP), in an SDS rat model. title: Fused Filament Fabrication of Soda-Lime Glass Feedstocks
abstract: Additive manufacturing methods are rather seldom used for the fabrication of glass parts. In this work, the knowledge gained from glass injection molding and ceramic fused filament fabrication (FFF) was extended to the usage of the FFF process chain covering the individual process steps compounding, 3D printing and thermal post-processing for the realization of soda-lime glass parts. abstract: The hyporheic zone (HZ) performs important filtering functions contributing to the reduction of pollutants from surface waters. It can be important in areas where the watercourse is subjected to strong human pressure. The study aimed to identify the hydrochemical conditions of the potential HZ of a spring watercourse in an area subjected to strong settlement pressure in the suburban area of Łódź. abstract: Banks' bond holdings expose them to interest rate risk, and the 2023 bank failures in the United States renewed attention to how market risk capital charges are computed. abstract: Given the Philippines’ susceptibility to hydrometeorological hazards associated with extreme rainfall, a reliable and accurate monitoring system is critical for protecting lives and property. However, current extreme rainfall monitoring tools often rely on static rainfall thresholds applied uniformly across all areas, failing to account for regional variability. title: Potential cost and combinatorial effects of commensal gut microbes on survival of individual honey bees
abstract: Gut microbiota can provide substantial benefits to their hosts, but maintaining microbial communities may also impose physiological costs. How these costs and benefits emerge from interactions among microbial species remains poorly understood. Using a gnotobiotic honey bee system, we here systematically examined the effects of all 32 possible combinations of the five core gut bacterial species on host survival. title: Surgical treatment of extratemporal epilepsy in children: seizure outcomes, complications and patterns of relapse
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extratemporal resections are increasingly performed in children with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but contemporary pediatric-only cohorts are scarce and reported seizure freedom has been modest. title: Alternative states and savanna conservation: Responding to woody encroachment in Guinean savannas
abstract: Woody encroachment in humid African savannas is often interpreted either as degradation of an open ecosystem or as a transition toward an alternative forest state. This distinction has direct conservation consequences, but it does not by itself define what should be conserved. As restoration ecology has long recognised, such decisions depend on explicit goals, history and values as much as on ecological evidence. abstract: The ecological balance and urban resilience of urban forests rely heavily on the attitude and participation of the community, and the sustainability of the forest is essential. abstract: Synthetic pigments and heavy metals released into urban water systems are a persistent concern for aquatic ecosystems. Textile effluents have been widely studied, but tattoo ink residues remain an almost unexamined source of discharge. title: MXenes-based heterostructures versus carbon-based anodes for metal-ion batteries: performance benchmarks, commercial viability, and translation challenges
abstract: MXenes and MXenes-based heterostructures have emerged as promising anodes for metal-ion batteries because of their high electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, and layered structures. abstract: Valorizing construction and demolition waste within a circular economy framework offers a promising strategy for sustainable wastewater treatment. We carried out a multi-year study of 200 accessions (natural inbred lines) of Swedish Arabidopsis thaliana using local field sites and a combination of common-garden experiments that measured adult survival and fecundity, and selection experiments that measured fitness over the full life cycle. abstract: Multi-LiDAR sensor configurations enhance perception for autonomous tasks in robotics compared to single sensors, but they require precise extrinsic calibration. abstract: Timely reporting of zoonotic infectious diseases allows for rapid response and mitigation by health authorities. title: Mechanistic heat-transfer model for predicting skin and feather temperatures in broiler chickens
abstract: Broiler chickens undergo rapid physiological and morphological changes throughout the rearing period, resulting in marked changes in thermal requirements and heat-exchange mechanisms. Young chicks are particularly sensitive to low environmental temperatures and often require supplemental radiant heating, whereas older birds increasingly depend on cooling systems to dissipate metabolic heat. This study developed a mechanistic heat-transfer model to predict skin-surface and feather temperatures throughout broiler growth and to simulate thermal responses under different environmental conditions.

title: Malaria burden and care in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon during the COVID-19 pandemic: A mixed-methods study
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with reported disruptions to healthcare delivery and malaria control activities in remote, malaria-endemic indigenous communities with limited access to healthcare. Such communities in the Peruvian Amazon may have been especially vulnerable due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. We investigated malaria burden, healthcare access, and community perceptions during the COVID-19 pandemic in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru. Methods A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conduct

title: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
abstract: Monitoring forest canopy water is essential for understanding drought response and interception losses under climate change. At short timescales, canopy water is partitioned among internal plant water storage ( S p ), rainfall interception ( S i ), and dew ( S d ), which together regulate plant functioning, canopy evaporation, and precipitation partitioning, yet are rarely observed simultaneously. GNSS transmissometry (GNSS-T) has recently emerged as a low-cost, continuous, stand-scale method to observe L-band vegetation optical depth (VOD) from signal attenuation. However, interpreting GNSS-T

title: Participatory action research for heritage-driven adaptation
abstract: Locally-led adaptation (LLA) has been proposed as a response to the limitations of top-down climate change adaptation (CCA), which often overlook local needs and lack sustainability. Yet, enabling LLA in communities affected by fragmentation and trauma poses significant challenges. This study explores a heritage-driven LLA framework, centred on trust-building, local empowerment, and co-design, as a pathway to foster hope, strengthen social cohesion, and build resilience in vulnerable, post-conflict settings. Focusing on Elandskloof, South Africa, we draw on lessons from a qualitative, Particip

title: Valorization of banana plant corm: Optimization of starch extraction using response surface methodology and development of biodegradable packaging film
abstract: Banana plant corm, a starch-rich residue left in the field after fruit harvest, has received little attention as a feedstock for bio-based materials. This study is the first to use response surface methodology (RSM) to optimize starch extraction from banana corm and link the optimized starch directly to biodegradable packaging film production. Using a face-centered central composite design, sodium metabisulfite concentration (1–3%) and soaking time (60–180 min) were varied to maximize starch yield and lightness. The optimized conditions yielded 16.05±0.17% starch with a lightness of 82.32 ±0.1
institutions: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology

title: Decreasing Circles, Sharper Triangles, Fewer Squares: Evolving the Academic Dress of the University of Sussex, 1963-2023
abstract: The determinedly modernist outlook of the University of Sussex impelled a radical reimagining of its academic dress. This article follows directly from the first partof the study, and concludes the vibrant history and complex gestation of Norman Hargreaves-Mawdsley’s colourful scheme, detailing the protracted debates concerning his designs, the installation of the chancellor, and the emergence of a completely new system of AD for the twenty-first century. For all researchers of the University’s history, The Keep, Brighton, is an indispensable archive. This investigation completes the explorati

title: Multifunctional Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate/Cuprous Oxide Nanocomposites in MEX 3D Printing: Rheological, Thermomechanical and Antibacterial Metrics
abstract: To address the critical need for robust and self‐sterilizing materials for challenging environments, this research introduces the use of cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O) nanoparticles in weatherproof acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA) through material extrusion (MEX) 3D printing to produce multifunctional nanocomposites with improved mechanical, rheological, and antibacterial properties. A range of ASA/Cu 2 O compositions (0.5–3.0 wt.% filler loading) was compounded and extruded into filament, and then specimens were fabricated using MEX 3D printing. institutions: Foundation for Research and Technology Hellas

title: From Polls to Persistence: Examining Coordinated Political Discourse Outside the Philippine Election Period on Facebook
abstract: Influence operations (IOs) on Facebook have shaped the Philippine political landscape since the 2016 elections, intensifying not only partisan divisions but also online political discourses. Building on literature on IOs in Philippine elections, we ask: How do patterns of coordinated behavior on Facebook persist during the non‐election period in the Philippines? Drawing on affordance theory through a socio‐cultural assemblage framework, we examine how coordinated political communication operates between partisan mobilization and IOs. We conceptualize coordinated behavior as a socio‐cultural as

title: Hepatic MCJ Silencing by GalNAc‐conjugated siRNA Attenuates Post‐Burn Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Intrinsic Apoptosis in Young and Aged Mice
abstract: Severe burn injury induces hepatic ER stress and apoptosis. MCJ (DNAJC15), a mitochondrial complex I repressor, is a therapeutic target in liver injury, but its role post-burn remains unknown. We tested whether hepatocyte-directed GalNAc-siMCJ attenuates post-burn hepatic ER stress and intrinsic apoptosis in young and aged mice. Young and aged female C57BL/6 mice received a 15% TBSA scald burn or sham, followed 1 h later by subcutaneous GalNAc-siMCJ (10 mg/kg) or vehicle. At 48 h, hepatic injury, MCJ, ER stress proteins, Bcl-2 family proteins, fraction-specific cytochrome c, caspase-9, and TUN

title: Revising the imposter phenomenon: a social perspective on the development and manifestation of the imposter phenomenon among medical students
abstract: Imposter Phenomenon (IP) describes the internal experience of perceived intellectual insincerity, marked by fear of exposure as an intellectual fraud. Research underscores a high prevalence amongst medical students. To date, IP has largely been recognised as an internal, psychological experience. This study expands this perspective by exploring the complex social environments that shape the development, manifestation, and perpetuation of IP. It offers a novel dimension to understanding IP within the context of medical education. A mixed methods approach was employed, combining quantitative dat

title: Local mechanical invariance in a recycled biobased vitrimer – evidence from the vibrational density of states
abstract: Biobased vitrimers represent a promising class of recyclable thermosetting polymers due to their dynamic covalent networks. In this study, the local mechanical properties of a vitrimer system based on glycerol triglycidyl ether and a vanillin-derived imine hardener are investigated before and after recycling. Using inelastic neutron scattering, the low frequency vibrational density of states is analyzed, focusing on the Boson peak (BP) as a sensitive probe of local elasticity.
