institutions: Federal Institute For Materials Research and Testing

title: SÍNDROME DE BURNOUT EN DOCENTES: ESTUDIO DE REVISIÓN SOBRE FACTORES ASOCIADOS, CONSECUENCIAS Y ESTRATEGIAS DE PREVENCIÓN
abstract: La presente investigación tuvo como objetivo analizar estudios relacionados con el síndrome de burnout en docentes, identificando los principales factores asociados a su aparición, las consecuencias emocionales y físicas derivadas del desgaste profesional, su repercusión sobre el desempeño docente y las estrategias de prevención planteadas dentro del ámbito educativo. El estudio se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cualitativo de tipo descriptivo-analítico mediante revisión documental de investigaciones científicas. Los hallazgos evidenciaron que factores como la presión laboral, la carga administrat

title: Forage grasses improve nutrient cycling and stabilize production in tropical no-till systems
abstract: Sustainable intensification in tropical agroecosystems requires production systems that enhance nutrient cycling, improve soil fertility dynamics, stabilize yields, and increase system-level resource use efficiency over time. However, integrated long-term evidence from tropical no-till systems remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of four off-season land-use strategies in a 12-year field experiment conducted in Brazil from 2006 to 2018: fallow, second crop, cover crop, and forage grass-based systems under no-till management. The experiment was arranged in a randomized complete bloc

title: Stressful Life Events, Rumination, and Psychological Harmony Among College Students in an Ethnic Minority Region of China: The Moderating Role of Sense of Coherence
abstract: A culturally grounded indicator of quality of life in Chinese populations, psychological harmony reflects the balance between one’s inner mental life and social surroundings. Although research on this construct has expanded in recent years, the processes by which stressful life events weaken it are not well understood. Guided by the diathesis–stress model as an overarching framework, with response styles theory specifying the mediating mechanism and salutogenic theory the protective resource, we tested whether rumination mediates the association between stressful life events and psychological
journal: Applied Research in Quality of Life

title: Nematode assemblages under maize‐ Grevillea intercrop systems
abstract: Background Integration of trees into agro‐ecosystems provides important ecological benefits compared with monoculture systems. Maize– Grevillea cropping systems are common in smallholder farms in Kenya, but their influence on soil nematode assemblages remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the influence of maize– Grevillea intercropping and maize and Grevillea monoculture systems on nematode assemblages in Embu, Kenya, using high‐throughput sequencing. Results A total of 64 genera were detected across the three systems. There were no significant differences in the alpha and beta diver

title: Tree size and thermal patterns in the public right-of-way: An empirical assessment of four mid-latitude U.S. cities
abstract: Urban street trees are widely promoted as a heat-mitigation strategy, yet it remains unclear whether municipal inventory metrics correspond with street-level air-temperature patterns. We examined associations between street-tree structure and evening air temperature across four mid-latitude U.S. cities—Portland, OR; Washington, DC; Philadelphia, PA; and Boston, MA—using NIHHIS Heat Watch observations and municipal street-tree inventories. We used complementary spatial framings: a heat-centric approach, characterizing trees within 50 m of temperature observations, and a tree-centric approach, c

title: Chemically modified agricultural-waste adsorbents: a critical review of leaching, toxicity, regeneration, and end-of-life risks
abstract: Chemical modification (acid or alkaline treatment, metal-oxide impregnation, magnetization, oxidation, and surface functionalization) improves the adsorption performance of agricultural-waste adsorbents, but better performance does not establish environmental safety. This critical narrative review synthesized 54 sources, identified through targeted searching and citation tracking, around three questions: which modifications create leaching or toxicity risks, how adequately these risks are assessed, and what hazards arise during regeneration and end-of-life management. Risk claims were classifi

title: Chromatin Remodeling of RasGRP3 Underlies Temozolomide Sensitivity in Glioblastoma Organoids
abstract: Acquired resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) constitutes a formidable clinical barrier in the management of glioblastoma (GBM). GBM organoid models (GBO) that faithfully mirror the parental tumor phenotype serve as powerful research instruments to overcome the limitations in this field. We established GBOs derived from primary glioma patients and their TMZ low-sensitivity counterparts. To unravel the intricate molecular underpinnings of this process, we performed an unbiased, integrated multi-omics analysis encompassing epigenomic, 3D genomic, and transcriptomic profiling, coupled with dual CRISP
institutions: The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

title: The Effect of News‐Based Measures of Biodiversity Exposure on Corporate Green Revenue Disclosure
abstract: Biodiversity loss has emerged as a significant challenge for firms. As firms face increasing pressure from stakeholders to address nature‐related risks, green revenue disclosure has become a potentially important strategic means of communicating environmentally oriented business activities. Using 12,055 firm‐year observations from S&P 1500 firms from 2005 to 2023, this study examines whether and when a firm with biodiversity exposure (defined as a news‐based measure of biodiversity exposure risk based on textual analyses of 10‐K statements) is associated with green revenue disclosure. The stud

title: Experimental Study on Compressive Strength and Freeze–Thaw Response of RCCP Containing Nano-Silica and Air-Entraining Agent
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study on roller-compacted concrete pavement (RCCP) containing nano-silica (NS) and an air-entraining agent (AEA). Eight mixtures were prepared: one control mix, three mixes with NS only, three mixes with AEA only, and one combined mix with 4.5% NS and 0.7% AEA. The NS mixtures needed more mixing water, and their water-to-binder ratio was 0.33–0.36, compared with 0.29 for the other mixtures. journal: International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology

title: Increasing Housing Stock of Intermediary Cities Through a Guided Practical Private–Private Partnership Approach: The Case of Bamenda, Cameroon
abstract: Cameroon’s formal housing delivery system, implemented through Société Immobilière du Cameroun (SIC), Mission d’Aménagement du Territoire Urbain et Rural (MAETUR) and Crédit Foncier , concentrates heavily in Douala and Yaoundé. Intermediary cities like Bamenda continue to experience shortfalls in residential, commercial and mixed-use space. Landowners who hold strategically located Central Business District (CBD) parcels but lack construction capital resort to outright sale, permanently alienating family patrimony and forgoing long-term urban economic participation. title: Experimental crossbreeding reveals ongoing, mosaic speciation in Akodon cursor (Rodentia, Cricetidae)
abstract: Akodon cursor (Winge, 1887) is widely distributed across more than 2500 km of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest and shows diploid numbers (2 n = 14, 15, 16) associated with the recognized phylogeographic clades (North, Central, and South), but unevenly distributed among populations, suggesting that A. cursor may comprise more than one taxon. We used experimental crosses to investigate how reproductive barriers emerge and accumulate in a geographically structured and chromosomally polymorphic taxon. We estimated reproductive success (RS), litter size (LS), and gestation length (GL) based on 300 int

title: Climate extremes, soil moisture, and agricultural production in Somalia: evidence from national annual data
abstract: Using 50 national annual observations for 1974–2023, this study examines short-run associations between agricultural production, drought severity, excess-rainfall intensity, soil moisture, agricultural land, and rural-population growth in Somalia. Production is measured by the FAOSTAT Agriculture Gross Production Index; climate and soil-water indicators are derived from monthly TerraClimate data. The analysis combines ARDL bounds testing, a mixed-order dynamic regression, robustness checks, bootstrap cointegration testing, and stability diagnostics. title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of thrips (Insecta : Thysanoptera) in olive orchards in Batna province (Northeast Algeria)
abstract: From 2015 to 2019, we surveyed thrips at six olive growing sites in Batna province, Northeast Algeria. A total of 7974 specimens representing 37 species were collected on two olive varieties, Sigoise and Chemlal, including 21 phytophagous species. Sigoise hosted all species, whereas Chemlal harbored 20. The abundant and dominant species were Trybommiella claricetis (2543 individuals: first report from Algeria), Frankliniella occidentalis (1279 individuals), and Thrips tabaci (722 individuals), accounting for 31.73 % on Sigoise and 32.33 % on Chemlal. title: Effect of plant-based compost on the growth and biochemical responses of ornamental cabbage under salt stress in peat-based growing media
abstract: Soil salinity is one of the major abiotic stress factors limiting the growth, ornamental quality, and performance of ornamental plants. This study investigated the effects of different compost application rates on plant growth, morphological characteristics, phytochemical composition, and antioxidant defense mechanisms in ornamental cabbage ( Brassica oleracea var. acephala ‘Pigeon Red F1’) under salt stress. The experiment was conducted as a two-factor factorial design consisting of three compost rates (0, 20, and 40%) and four NaCl concentrations (0, 25, 50, and 75 mM). Morphological traits,

title: Experimental thermal performance of a low-cost solar water heater with a serpentine CPVC collector under high-andean climatic conditions: A case study
abstract: The search for accessible and efficient solar water heating systems is critical in rural and high-Andean areas with limited access to conventional energy sources. This study experimentally evaluates the thermal performance of a low-cost solar water heater incorporating a 1.2596 m2 serpentine CPVC collector under high-Andean climatic conditions in Peru. A prototype featuring a 1.2596 m2 horizontal serpentine CPVC collector was designed and monitored over 30 consecutive days using an Arduino system with four temperature sensors. Thermal efficiency was evaluated under three usage scenarios: dayti
journal: Energy Sources Part A Recovery Utilization and Environmental Effects

title: From barriers to breakthroughs: Navigating success drivers of women entrepreneurs in China
abstract: Despite the adolescence stage, the past 30 years have evidenced the proliferation of mainstream academic research for the most interesting and emerging phenomenon, ‘Women Entrepreneurship’. To further shed light on the above-stated phenomenon, this study aims to explore the success drivers and challenges of women entrepreneurs in the specific context of China. abstract: Placental hypertrophy is a major cause of pregnancy failure in somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) animals, with metabolic-epigenetic crosstalk proposed as a key regulatory node, yet its molecular mechanism remains elusive. Isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (Idh2) is a critical mitochondrial metabolic enzyme that controls the production of α-Ketoglutarate (α-KG), a central regulator of epigenetic modifications. title: Enhanced oil recovery via foams featuring various nanoparticle and polymer formulations
abstract: This study comprehensively investigated how various additives affect the stability of nitrogen (N 2 ) foam at 25, 60, and 90 °C, focusing on both the fundamental mechanisms that influence foam behavior and its practical applications in enhanced oil recovery (EOR) processes. The methodology utilized involved silica nanoparticles (SiO 2 -NPs) and Polyethylene Glycol (PEG). To determine the most effective approach for enhancing foam stability, two stabilization methods were assessed. institutions: Islamic Azad University, Science and Research Branch

title: Nanoparticle Arrays for Efficient Organic Light‐Emitting Diode Emission Management
abstract: OLEDs are increasingly applied in illumination and displays because they offer excellent color quality, are mechanically flexible, and are self-emissive. However, their usage is limited by low external quantum efficiency (EQE) and efficiency roll-off at high driving voltages. These limitations, together with demands for smaller pixels and device sizes in emerging technologies, motivate innovations that increase efficiency and allow replacing external optical elements with embedded solutions. title: Spatial Determinants of Community Well-Being: A Geographically Weighted Regression Analysis of U.S. Counties
abstract: There are two challenges facing community economic development scholars and practitioners: the chaotic number of factors associated with community well-being, and the heterogeneity of places that requires a local lens on these associations. In this study, we build on (Isserman, Feser, and Warren, 2009) and construct a community well-being index from four beyond-growth indicators for 3,100 contiguous U.S. counties. title: Structural, morphological, and electrical properties of citric acid-crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol)/chitosan blend films for alkaline polymer electrolyte application
abstract: Alkaline polymer electrolytes need a host combining low crystallinity for hydroxide transport with a cohesive network, but the contributions of blending and crosslinking remain unresolved in KOH-doped PVA/chitosan systems. Partially hydrolyzed PVA (87–89 mol%) films with 0–50 wt% chitosan were cast, the blends crosslinked with 5 wt% citric acid. Undoped companion films were characterized by XRD, FTIR, and SEM; impedance spectra of three independently cast, 6 M KOH-doped films per composition were analyzed. title: PGAM5 dephosphorylates LCLAT1S410 to trigger cardiolipin oxidation-driven ferroptosis in cadmium-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represents a prevalent, steadily increasing metabolic liver disease characterized by steatosis and liver injury, with disease progression influenced by environmental risk factors. Cadmium (Cd), a ubiquitous environmental metal toxicant, has been epidemiologically associated with MASLD progression. Although mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative lipid damage contribute to MASLD pathogenesis, whether and how Cd disrupts mitochondrial lipid homeostasis to initiate lipid peroxidation-associated injury remains elusive. title: Factors Associated with Labor Productivity in Central and Eastern Europe and the MENA Region
abstract: This study examines within-country associations between institutional quality, human capital, demographic structure, resource dependence, and labor productivity in 11 Central and Eastern European and MENA countries. The descriptive dataset covers 2010–2022, while the principal first-difference model uses observations for 2011–2021 because oil-rent data end in 2021. The analysis applies year fixed effects and country-clustered standard errors, supplemented by lagged first-difference, regional interaction, variable exclusion, and sensitivity specifications. title: Resilience and Adaptation Among Ukrainian Refugee Children in Estonia: An Ecological Perspective
abstract: This qualitative study explores how Ukrainian refugee children in Estonia adapt to post‐migration life through the lens of resilience and ecological systems theory. Semi‐structured interviews with 10 children (aged 13–17) revealed that adaptation is a dynamic and relational process shaped by personal strengths, family warmth and community inclusion. Children demonstrated agency, emotional coping, and hope while families and schools provided safety, structure and belonging. title: Evaluating UAV-based pesticide application as a low-carbon pathway through life cycle greenhouse gas assessment across diverse cropping systems
abstract: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture requires technologies that replace or improve conventional field operations. This study compared GHG emissions from pesticide application by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and conventional ground sprayers (boom sprayers, air-blast sprayers, and mist blowers) in Korea, including energy use and pesticide manufacturing. title: Associations of protected area residence with nutritional status and nutrient intake among school-aged children in northeastern Cambodia
abstract: This study assessed nutritional status and nutrient intake among 500 children aged 6–12 years living inside and outside protected areas in northeastern Cambodia. Adjusted models showed no significant association between residence in protected areas and anthropometric Z-scores. However, wild food collection was negatively associated with height-for-age Z-scores (HAZ) and body mass index-for-age Z-scores (BAZ), while household size was positively associated with HAZ. title: Physics and Chemistry of Molecule-Based Strongly Isotropic Lattices: Hidden Frustrations, Flat Bands, Chirality, and Electrochemical Control
abstract: Strongly isotropic lattices are geometrically constrained networks in which all bonds connected to a common vertex are topologically equivalent. Only the honeycomb, diamond, and K4 lattices satisfy this condition, giving rise to characteristic electronic structures such as Dirac cones and Dirac nodal lines. In this Award Account, we describe our efforts to construct molecule-based strongly isotropic lattices and to explore emergent phenomena arising from the interplay of topology and molecular degrees of freedom. title: Moss is more: The moss Physcomitrium patens as an ideal chassis for plant synthetic biology
abstract: Physcomitrium patens, commonly known as the spreading earthmoss or Physco, has gained increasing attention as a chassis for synthetic biology in plants. This review explores its advantages over flowering plants traditionally used more often for biotechnology, such as Arabidopsis thaliana and maize, including shorter life cycles and ease to handle experimentally, being haploid, and much higher efficiency for integration of transgenes into its genome by homologous recombination. title: Energy, exergy, and drying kinetics of beetroot under electrohydrodynamic-assisted hot-air hybrid drying
abstract: Drying of agricultural products with minimum energy consumption and preserving their quality remains a major challenge in food processing. This study investigated beetroot drying in an electrohydrodynamic (EHD)-assisted hot-air method at 50–60°C and 15–30 kV by evaluating drying kinetics, effective moisture diffusivity, energy and exergy performance, thermal response, color, and ImageJ-based microstructural properties. title: Immune functions of vascular structural cells are endothelial communication, smooth muscle transdifferentiation and lymphatic immune regulation
abstract: The vascular wall maintains structural integrity, regulates blood flow, and supports tissue functions and homeostasis. Evidence also shows that its structural cells participate in immune sensing, inflammation and tissue remodeling. Vascular endothelial cells (ECs), vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), and lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) encounter different combinations of inflammatory, metabolic, mechanical, microbial, tissue and intracellular immune-derived signals. title: A pilot implementation study of a community-led integrated malaria elimination model in Busoga, Uganda: protocol for a mixed-methods implementation research study
abstract: Introduction Malaria remains one of the leading public health challenges globally, with over 95% of the disease burden occurring in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). In 2023, approximately 263 million malaria cases and 597,000 deaths were reported worldwide, most of them in Africa. Uganda continues to experience a high burden of malaria, particularly in transmission hotspots such as the Busoga sub-region in Eastern Uganda, where children under five years and pregnant women are disproportionately affected. title: Solving the location of the camp of Legio X Fretensis in Jerusalem
abstract: One of the enduring mysteries of ancient Jerusalem concerns the location and appearance of the camp of the Legio X Fretensis , established following the Roman destruction of the city in 70 CE. Although Flavius Josephus explicitly places the camp on the western side of Jerusalem, close to three monumental towers, its precise location has perplexed scholars since the nineteenth century. This study presents hitherto unpublished architectural remains dating to after 70 CE, uncovered by Magen Broshi during excavations in 1975–1978 along the western Old City wall, south of the present-day Citadel. title: Facilitation, Exploration and Exchange: The Asiatic Society of Japan in Late Nineteenth-Century British Scientific Networks
abstract: Founded in 1872, the Asiatic Society of Japan (ASJ) formed part of a vast international network of knowledge production and exchange through practices of membership, publications, and references. Papers published in the society’s Transactions heavily focused on cutting edge scientific research and through the participation of Japanese authors, society members and connections with groups such as the Meirokusha (Meiji Six Society), they integrated British scientific discourse with their Japanese counterparts. title: Assessing the range expansion of a generalist carnivore by a novel approach combining questionnaires to experts and dynamic occupancy models
abstract: Despite the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, the geographic ranges of many mesopredators are expanding, largely driven by their generalist life histories and the decline of apex predators. Quantifying these expansions and identifying their underlying drivers remain challenging and require innovative methodological approaches. We aimed at quantifying the factors driving the recent spatial expansion of the Egyptian mongoose ( Herpestes ichneumon ) at the European edge of its range. title: Neuronal cell line expressing full-length mutant huntingtin displays alteration of proteasome activity
abstract: Polyglutamine diseases are incurable genetic neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of extended polyglutamine fragments-containing mutant proteins, which are prone to the formation of poorly soluble aggregates. The adequate cellular model is crucial in uncovering the pathological mechanisms responsible for neurotoxicity in Huntington’s disease (HD), screening for therapeutic molecules and elucidation of the molecular mechanisms impacted by particular compound. title: Chitosan in Mitigating Saline Stress in the Morphophysiology and Production of Solanum melongena L. in a Semi-Arid Area
abstract: Objective: Evaluate the effect of foliar application of chitosan on mitigating the deleterious effects of irrigation water salinity on the gas exchange, growth and production of eggplant cv. Preta Comprida grown under semiarid conditions. Methods: The experiment was conducted in a greenhouse using a randomized block design in a 5 × 2 factorial scheme, consisting of five levels of electrical conductivity of the irrigation water (ECwi) - (0.4, 1.4, 2.4, 3.4, and 4.4 dS m -1 ) and two chitosan concentrations (0 and 0.50 g L -1 ), with four replicates. title: A transparent and auditable framework for selecting rural study sites in water governance research: application to Chile
abstract: Background Rural site selection in place-based research is often influenced by convenience and operational constraints, yet the procedures used to select study locations are not always explicitly documented. This can limit transparency, auditability, and comparability across studies. Objective To develop and empirically illustrate a transparent and auditable framework for selecting rural study sites for water-governance research using publicly available indicators and documentary evidence. Methods This was an exploratory methodological framework-development study with an empirical application.

title: Mapping Taliks Beneath Water Tracks Using Ground‐Penetrating Radar Grids
abstract: Permafrost is degrading, raising concerns about its impact on global climate. Taliks, year‐round unfrozen layers of ground in permafrost environments, affect hydrological and carbon dynamics and contribute to permafrost degradation. Despite their importance, they are seldom studied because of the difficulty in identifying them. Water tracks (zones overlying permafrost concentrating water flow) have an important role in controlling catchment hydrology, yet their contribution to talik formation remains poorly understood. title: Balancing productivity, soil health and estimated greenhouse gas emissions in diversified cereal–legume cropping systems
abstract: Reconciling productivity and environmental performance remain challenging in semi-arid tropical agriculture. A two-year randomized complete block experiment on one farm in Karnataka’s eastern dry zone evaluated twelve cropping systems with three replicates per treatment. Rainy-season sole crops and intercrops were followed by mung bean, with finger millet–fallow system as the benchmark. title: Exploring the Role of Cultural Capital in the Navigation of Religion-Based Stigma in the Workspace
abstract: Drawing on a study of 32 skilled Muslim humanitarian migrants, I show how cultural capital is discursively leveraged to navigate perceptions of religious stigma in the British workspace in a contested social process. Highlighting how the strategies used to navigate stigmatising connotations attached to religion (asserting worth, differentiating, aligning and minimising) are inscribed in embodied and institutionalised forms of cultural capital, I illustrate how stigma and privilege can coalesce in skilled individuals’ self-constructions. title: Sustainable pest management in Africa: Biological control strategies, emerging technologies, and case studies across major crops
abstract: Background : Integrated pest management (IPM) and biological control have become fundamental components of sustainable crop protection in Africa, where invasive and endemic insect pests continue to threaten agricultural productivity, food security, and rural livelihoods. This review synthesizes recent advances, implementation strategies, and emerging technologies associated with biological control and IPM across major African agroecosystems, with emphasis on key pests affecting staple, horticultural, and citrus crops. Methods : A comprehensive review of the scientific literature was conducted

title: Why Whistleblowing Does Not Deter Collaborative Tax Evasion
abstract: Does whistleblowing deter rule violations when such violations are believed to be common? We examine this question in an online experiment about collaborative tax evasion. We vary whether subjects can blow the whistle on their partner in crime and introduce a high-evasion environment by framing the social norm such that evasion is expected to be common. Our findings show that giving partners in crime the option to blow the whistle on their partner does not significantly deter collaborative tax evasion. title: “DEVEMOS SER MELHORES”: visões sobre Grécia antiga e masculinidade através da série de jogos God of War
abstract: Através da série de jogos God of War é possível observar mudanças culturais no tocante à visão histórica sobre a Grécia antiga e como interpretações sobre esta na atualidade inspiraram noções contemporâneas de masculinidade. Baseado nos estudos de Recepção da Antiguidade de Lorna Hardwick, busca-se abordar como uma versão idealizada da Grécia como berço e ápice da civilização alimentou uma fantasia de poder masculino na saga God of War. title: Regional governance of the energy transition: A comparison of spatial policies in Germany
abstract: The energy transition is a multifaceted and spatially differentiated transformation process that requires effective governance across multiple policy levels. While national and local energy governance has been widely examined, the regional level remains comparatively understudied despite its crucial role in translating strategic objectives into local implementation and in mediating between policy scales. title: Analysis of coupled prevention and control strategies for slope stability and hydrogeological conditions in coal mine fire-affected areas
abstract: The Zhundong Basin is a typical arid desert region in Northwest China characterized by abundant coal deposits. The widely distributed low-metamorphic Jurassic coal seams are prone to spontaneous combustion disasters. High-temperature burning of these coal seams has formed pyrolytic rocks that have altered the structural composition of original rock formations and groundwater distribution patterns, creating a unique hydrogeological pattern of "local fracture enrichment and belt-like water conduction and storage" specific to arid mining areas. title: Moderating role of religiosity in islamic banking intentions and behaviours within the decomposed theory of planned behaviour
abstract: While Islamic banking is becoming more important in Türkiye its market share is still small compared to many other Muslim majority countries. This gives rise to a big question as to how religiosity affects individuals’ intentions and behavior use of Islamic banking services. Therefore, this study investigates the moderator role of religiosity on the individuals’ intentions and behaviors towards Islamic banking in the Decomposed Planned Behavior Model. title: The structure of Poland's water footprint in 2010, 2015 and 2020: Structural path analysis of sectoral roles and supply-chain depth
abstract: Water governance typically targets abstraction sites, yet most national water footprints are embodied in inter-industry supply. This study unpacks the freshwater withdrawal embodied in Poland’s final demand in 2010, 2015 and 2020 using a 32-sector environmentally extended input-output model, structural path analysis, a tier-resolved decomposition of change, and a source-sink-conduit typology. title: Magnetic bentonite–keratin and bentonite–wool bio-composites as sorbents for magnetic dispersive micro-solid phase extraction of Pb(II) and Cd(II): Optimization and mechanistic insights
abstract: A comparative study was conducted to evaluate two bentonite-based magnetic composites incorporating keratin (magnetic bentonite–keratin) and wool fibers (magnetic bentonite–wool) as sorbents for dispersive micro-solid-phase extraction of Pb(II) and Cd(II) prior to ICP-OES determination. Both composites were successfully synthesized, thoroughly characterized, and systematically optimized using response surface methodology. title: Beyond Predatory Publishing : The Case for Verifying Journal Identity in Indian Higher Education - A Policy Perspective
abstract: Purpose : This perspective examined why cloned (hijacked) journals create a verification problem that differs from conventional predatory publishing, and what policy response suits Indian higher education after the UGC-CARE list was discontinued in 2025. Design/Methodology/Approach : The paper is a policy perspective and is based on published research, UGC regulations and notices, and two illustrative incidents of deceptive publishing from editorial practice in 2026, using signaling theory and information asymmetry as the lens. title: Hydrogen production and fuel-cell technologies: a review of operating principles, applications and sustainability challenges
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cell technology is a possible avenue for sustainable energy production and greenhouse gas reduction. This paper provides a detailed overview of hydrogen fuel cell such as their principle of operation, key types, hydrogen generation processes, technological advancement, application, problems and future possibilities. Fuel cells use electrochemical reactions to turn the molecules in hydrogen into electricity, and they do this with greater efficiencies and lower emissions than traditional power production systems. title: Ant dominance may mask effects of tree diversity on carcass decomposition
abstract: Tree diversity promotes the diversity of organisms at higher trophic levels and associated ecosystem functions. Tree diversity may thus also influence communities of insect decomposers and thereby accelerate the decomposition of animal carcasses. To test this, we placed 864 dead mice and measured their decomposition over two days across 96 plots in a forest biodiversity experiment (BEF-China) during the monsoon season in subtropical China in 2024. title: Proton conducting Cicer arietinum L starch electrolyte doped with NH4SCN for electrochemical double layer capacitors
abstract: A chickpea starch–agar biopolymer electrolyte plasticized with glycerol and doped with NH 4 SCN was successfully developed for symmetric electrochemical double-layer capacitor (EDLC) applications. FTIR confirmed the interaction between NH 4 SCN and the biopolymer matrix, while XRD revealed increasing amorphous character with salt addition. The optimized CSA5 electrolyte exhibited a maximum ionic conductivity of 1.1 × 10 − 3 S cm −1 , a low bulk resistance of 43.60 Ω, an ionic transference number of 0.89, an electrochemical stability window of 1.8 V, and good thermal stability. title: Temporal variation and chemico-biological profiling of bioactive metabolites from Pinus wallichiana : experimental and computational mechanistic insights
abstract: Seasonal GC-MS/NMR profiling of Pinus wallichiana needle oils revealed phytochemical shifts and anti-tubercular/anti-helminthic activity. Docking, 100 ns MD and MM/GBSA support potential dual inhibition of DprE1 and Tubulin-TUB015. A portion of the graphical abstract was generated using Google NotebookLM.

title: Phonon-Modulated Momentum-Space Geodesic Response Probed by Second-Harmonic Sidebands
abstract: The quantum metric of Bloch states endows electron dynamics with a Riemannian geometric structure. However, probing its dynamical signatures is severely hindered by the entanglement with ubiquitous band dispersion and topological responses. In this work, we propose a dynamical approach to isolate the momentum-space gravitational analog by investigating the interplay between strong-field driven electrons and coherent optical phonons. title: Anatomical Compartmentalization in Chickens Drives Divergent H9N2 Influenza Evolution Toward Human Receptor Binding and Immune Escape
abstract: Avian influenza A(H9N2) viruses pose a pandemic threat, having acquired preferential binding to human receptors and the ability to evade immunity in chickens. However, the selective forces driving these traits remain unclear. Here, we show how anatomical compartmentalization within chickens shapes hemagglutinin (HA) evolution. Using deep mutational scanning coupled with in vivo studies, we find that pre-existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, thereby imposing strong selection on viral diversity. title: Hongos micorrízicos arbusculares nativos en agroecosistemas tropicales: Evidencia agronómica, potencial bioeconómico y brechas de investigación en Ecuador
abstract: Los consorcios nativos de hongos micorrízicos arbusculares (HMA) se proponen como bioinsumos para suelos tropicales de baja fertilidad. Esta revisión sistematizada examinó la evidencia agronómica, ecológica y económica sobre su uso en agroecosistemas tropicales y qué brechas lo limitan en Ecuador. Se consultaron Scopus, Web of Science y PubMed (2005–2026) y listas de referencias; la selección se reportó con PRISMA 2020 y la calidad, con listas del Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI). title: String-breaking statics and dynamics in a (1+1)D SU(2) lattice gauge theory
abstract: String breaking is at the core of hadronization models of relevance to particle colliders. Yet, studies of string-breaking dynamics rooted in quantum chromodynamics remain fundamentally challenging. Tensor networks enable sign-problem-free studies of static and dynamical properties of lattice gauge theories. In this work, we develop and apply a tensor-network toolkit based on the loop-string-hadron formulation of an SU(2) lattice gauge theory in 1+1 dimensions with dynamical fermions. title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots
abstract: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability. Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online. title: Universal scaling of brine migration in ice
abstract: Sea ice hosts mobile brine inclusions whose migration influences salt redistribution, microstructure and transport within the ice. Although their motion under temperature gradient is commonly described as a diffusion-limited process, experimental evidence has remained rare and insufficient because migration is slow and controlled inclusion seeding is challenging. Here we introduce an experimental method to trap and monitor hundreds of inclusions in ice under controlled temperature gradients. Using four solutes, three imposed gradients and two order of magnitude in initial concentration, we qua
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: KuroshioVis: Hypothesis-Driven Discovery of Mesoscale Air-Sea Interaction through Coarse-to-Fine Exploration
abstract: Mesoscale air-sea interaction occurs throughout strong sea surface temperature fronts such as the the Kuroshio Extension, but its strength is highly non-uniform and can be resolved only in kilometre-scale coupled simulations. The response of any single eddy is weak relative to synoptic variability, so evidence supporting a hypothesis of systematic air-sea coupling must be accumulated across many eddies rather than inferred from individual cases. title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
abstract: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. title: Route Optimization Under Port Congestion and Carbon Reduction: An NSGA-II Approach
abstract: Maritime shipping simultaneously faces the dual challenges of escalating port congestion and increasingly stringent decarbonization mandates. The large-scale anchorage of vessels at hub ports inflates unit transport costs while simultaneously producing significant additional CO₂ emissions from idling auxiliary engines. This study develops a multi-objective routing optimization framework that jointly incorporates time, transport, and carbon emission costs under congestion-dependent generalized cost functions. A variational inequality (VI) model is formulated to characterize network equilibrium

title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. title: Wasserstein Target Diagram for Model Evaluation
abstract: The target diagram is often used in geosciences, which provides a visualization tool for model evaluation and shows the temporal or spatial matching of data. However, its construction requires paired data of equal sample sizes, limiting its application to model comparisons involving unpaired samples or probability distributions. In this study, we propose the Wasserstein target diagram based on the 2-Wasserstein distance from optimal transport. title: RevealLO: Global-Scale FWI Including Long-Period Major-Arc Surface Wave and Multi-Orbit Body Wave Data
abstract: Global full-waveform inversion (FWI) has matured significantly in recent years, but resolution in the southern hemisphere often remains limited due to sparse receiver coverage. To address this problem, we constructed RevealLO, a global-scale FWI model that updates its predecessor REVEAL by expanding the inversion time window from 1 hour to 3.5 hours. title: A place for stabilization alongside tipping cascades: The AMOC–cryosphere system
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and cryosphere are central to climate tipping point research, where their interactions are typically framed as pathways for cascading transitions. Here, I review evidence that stabilizing dynamics operating within and across these components can also oppose change, affecting its magnitude and timing or, in some cases, whether a transition occurs at all. title: A Hierarchical View of Ecological Encounters
abstract: Encounters between individuals, or between individuals and entities like vehicles, are central to understanding a host of topics in ecology and related fields. Problems of mate-finding, predator-prey interactions, pathogen spread, and animal interactions with infrastructure all hinge on encounters. Historically, however, encounters have been difficult to observe at scale, and the relevant theoretical frameworks---which ultimately derive from the ideal gas law---have been badly mismatched to the underlying biology. title: OmniFish: A Bioinspired, Modular, Reconfigurable Soft Robotic Fish Enabling Multi-Modal Swimming
abstract: In this work, we introduce OmniFish, a bioinspired modular soft robotic fish designed to emulate the full spectrum of body and/or caudal fin (BCF) locomotion modes within a single robotic platform. The design combines morphology averaging across representative fish species with a tendon-driven compliant segmented spine whose effective stiffness can be reconfigured through progressive mechanical jamming. title: Sub-Ice: semi-automated mapping of basal channels from ice shelf surface elevation data
abstract: Basal channels, troughs carved into ice shelf bases by buoyant plumes, modulate basal melt and can weaken ice shelves. Through hydrostatic adjustment they have a surface expression, yet their geometry is largely mapped manually, limiting the number of channels studied and the consistency between mappings. We present Sub-Ice, a semi-automated tool that maps basal channels from surface digital elevation models. title: Tendex Lines and Short-Time Deformation: The Geometry of Lunar Tides
abstract: Tendex lines and the stretchlines and squeezelines of Lagrangian coherent structure theory share a geometric construction: they integrate eigenvector fields of symmetric tensors. We connect their dynamical interpretations through the short-time deformation of particles released with zero initial velocity relative to a freely falling reference in an autonomous gravitational field. title: Grid Trouble in Paradise: Uncovering Vulnerable Distributed Energy Resources and Their Grid-Level Risks
abstract: Grid-connected solar distributed energy resources (DERs), such as solar inverters and monitoring platforms, have been deployed at unprecedented scale over the past few years, with global solar capacity more than doubling since 2022. To support monitoring and control, many of these systems are Internet-connected and configured by installers or end users, yet the real-world scale of their Internet exposure and the implications for power grid operation remain poorly understood. title: Real-Space Theory of Nonequilibrium Orbital Magnetization in Inhomogeneous Solids
abstract: We put forward a real-space linear-response theory of orbital magnetization induced by a dc electric field in bulk materials lacking translation invariance. title: Carbon-made Lobachevsky surfaces
abstract: Carbon-made surfaces of constant negative Gaussian curvature realize portions of the Lobachevsky plane in the laboratory, with motivations ranging from analogue gravity, where the elliptic, Beltrami and hyperbolic pseudospheres correspond to the three static phases of the Bañados--Teitelboim--Zanelli black hole, to water desalination. title: A Bayesian approach to technological emergence, climate variability, and demographic stability in northern South America
abstract: Human communities produce technology in almost every environment, but the conditions that enable technologies in the tropics are not well understood. We test two competing hypotheses---that technological emergence is triggered by environmental stress and that technology tracks growth in effective populations---by integrating Holocene archaeological and paleoclimate evidence. We use archaeological derived radiocarbon dates from Colombia as a proxy for human activity, including dating plant management, pottery, metallurgy, and raised fields. title: Multi-Band Galaxy Novel-View Synthesis with Radiative Gaussian Fields
abstract: We propose a novel view synthesis tool for galaxies based on Gaussian Splatting (GS). Unlike RGB data, where GS has achieved success, galaxy observations consist of multi-band signals from a massive number of bodies, contain complex patterns of cross-band interactions, and capture light propagation in highly heterogeneous media. As a result, the underlying physical process poses great challenges in model representation and optimization, which have not been investigated in existing research. title: ScoutCache: Efficient Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Conditional Readout and Selective Caching
abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient long video generation, but inference still incurs substantial computational costs from repeated denoising and KV cache operations. Existing acceleration methods reduce parts of this overhead, while historical KV reading and cache construction remain costly across video chunks. title: Sensitivity analysis in real options studies: systematic review and recommendations
abstract: Real options (RO) modeling provides a powerful framework for valuing managerial flexibility under uncertainty in capital-intensive investments across various industries, including climate, energy, and transportation. However, the transparency and usefulness of such models depends heavily on sensitivity analysis (SA). This study reviews over 100 peer-reviewed RO journal articles to examine the extent and quality of SA practices. title: Meme Coin Factories: Uncovering Large-Scale Manipulations on pump.fun
abstract: Once complex, creating and deploying a new cryptocurrency has become trivial. Coin launchpads now allow users to generate a new coin with merely a few clicks, at a minimal cost. Launchpad popularity has grown in tandem with the rise of "meme coins," which usually do not offer any novel technological properties and are purely created for fun. The most prominent coin launchpad, pump.fun, has gained significant traction, grossing over 100 million USD in daily trading volume. title: How Much Does Saliency Accuracy Matter for Saliency-Guided 360-degree Image Compression?
abstract: Saliency-guided coding allocates bits to the regions viewers are most likely to attend, but accurate 360-degree saliency prediction is computationally expensive, an obstacle for low-latency immersive streaming applications such as robot teleoperation. We quantify how much saliency-prediction accuracy actually translates into compression gain. title: A Serious Game for Training Civil Participation in Flood Crisis Management
abstract: Floods are among the most frequent and destructive natural disasters, requiring citizens to make critical decisions under rapidly changing conditions. Most serious games related to flooding emphasize awareness, preparedness, and education in flood management, but there is still a research gap on how to train citizens to act under pressure, uncertainty, and stress. In this paper, we position Virtual Reality (VR) serious games as a promising approach to addressing this gap by providing experiential and immersive training opportunities for citizens. title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning
abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. title: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
abstract: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. title: The Partially Saturated Cells Method for Complex Moving Geometries in Turbulent Flow Conditions
abstract: We present four application cases to test and validate fluid-structure-interaction models based on the Lattice Boltzmann and the Partially Saturated Cells method (PSM) for turbulent flow conditions. For a flow around a stationary sphere we compare the PSM with direct mapping boundary conditions and achieve good agreement to reference data for Reynolds numbers up to one million. title: Nonlinear long extensional waves in an elastic layer with irregular free surfaces
abstract: The propagation of nonlinear long extensional waves in a compressible hyperelastic layer with irregular free surfaces is studied within the framework of finite elasticity. The free surfaces are traction-free and symmetric with respect to the middle plane, and their irregularity changes the local thickness of the layer by a finite amount over distances long compared with the wavelength. title: Estimation-Aware Control on Quadrotor State Manifolds via Anisotropic Covariance Filtering
abstract: Conventional nonlinear flight controllers operate under the implicit assumption of reliable, high-confidence state feedback. During transient sensing degradation or partial unobservability, state estimation uncertainty is frequently misinterpreted as physical tracking error, triggering aggressive and parasitic corrective inputs. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose a generalized Estimation-Aware (EA) control framework that directly incorporates real-time estimator confidence into control execution. title: Threat Evasion and Information Propagation in Cognitive Flocks
abstract: Information sharing, threat perception, and collective evasion highlight the advantages of swarm intelligence. Here, we study the behavior of flocks of cognitive agents, based on numerical simulations of the augmented inertial spin model, with an explicit predator. Each agent on the predator-facing side of the flock perceives the threat, triggering collective turns through local interactions. title: Spatial patterns of transportation choice in Niterói
abstract: Characterizing how people move through a city requires spatially and temporally fine-grained data that are often costly and difficult to obtain. Here, we introduce a computational framework that uses macroscopic, aggregated, and static urban data to construct a microscopic, dynamic, and spatially detailed representation of urban mobility. Building on an existing activity simulator, the framework combines a synthetic population, the built environment, and transport networks to generate daily trips and assign walking, car, or public transit. title: Can Vision-Language Models Truly Understand Images? A Benchmark Beyond Commonsense Bias
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance on a wide range of vision-language tasks. However, it remains unclear whether their predictions are grounded in the visual content itself or are largely driven by statistical co-occurrence patterns and commonsense correlations learned from large-scale image-text corpora. title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
abstract: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. They were selected through an exploratory stakeholder consultation and 3 co-design workshops with audiovisual professionals and participants from organizations supporting people with visual or hearing impairments. title: Global analysis of the $ρ$ resonance in lattice QCD
abstract: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $ρ$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. title: Detection of CH$_2$NH on Titan
abstract: Saturn's moon, Titan, presents a chemical environment where abiotic synthesis of organics essential for life -- including amino acids and nucleotide bases -- may naturally occur. The assessment of Titan's organic content begins with characterizing its atmospheric chemical inventory, where many predicted molecular species remain unidentified. Here, we present the definitive spectroscopic detection of CH$_2$NH (methanimine) on Titan from observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. abstract: Integrated aircraft design combines models of aerodynamics, propulsion, mass, and mission performance in one design loop, so that the disciplines can be traded against each other from the earliest stage. abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. abstract: We present the measurement of the cosmic ray muon seasonal variation using single-muon events with the ProtoDUNE single-phase detector located at the CERN Neutrino Platform, using data collected from December 2018 to July 2020. Cosmic ray muon runs recorded during this period are analyzed to determine the muon rate as a function of time. The results show a seasonal modulation of the muon rate, with a significance of 4 σ relative to the null hypothesis of no seasonal variation. The observed muon rate reaches a maximum during the winter, consistent with measurements from other surface experiment

title: TRACE: Trajectory Synchronization for Training-Free Resolution Extension in Video Generation
abstract: More text-to-video models are available, but many remain limited to low resolutions. Training them for higher resolutions is costly, while existing training-free methods still struggle with fine detail, scene structure, and efficiency. We propose TRACE, a training-free method that synchronizes low- and high-resolution generation trajectories. During early denoising, TRACE aligns predicted scene content at corresponding noise levels. title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to improve an agent using its own task experience. Its practical value depends on whether performance gains justify the full cost of self-improvement and task execution. We evaluate this trade-off on continual task streams, scoring each task before its feedback is used for subsequent updates. We define the \emph{RSI Tax} as the token cost of the self-improvement process and include it alongside task-execution costs in end-to-end evaluation. title: Software-Defined Internet Integration of Satellite Networks (SDISN)
abstract: This paper proposes SDISN, a software-defined Internet integration of satellite networks. It facilitates the transmission of IP traffic from user terminals (UTs) or Internet nodes over a satellite network with inter-satellite links (ISLs). Gateways (GWs) together with Points of Presence (PoPs) support the transition between the satellite network and the Internet. UTs and GWs connect to the satellite network via serving satellites (SrvSats). As the satellites orbit the Earth at high speed, UTs and GWs frequently change their SrvSats. title: RADISH: A Robust Covariate-Adaptive Trial Design with Historical Control Borrowing
abstract: Incorporating historical controls into randomized clinical trials can improve statistical efficiency and alleviate enrollment challenges by reducing the need for concurrent controls, particularly when their recruitment is ethically or logistically challenging. These gains depend on comparability between the historical and concurrent controls. Many dynamic borrowing methods assess compatibility for the overall study populations and apply the same borrowing decision to every participant, even when comparability varies with participant covariates. title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
abstract: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $δf$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). title: MSTT: A New Multisensor Time Series-Triggered Intelligent Communication Framework for BeiDou Satellites
abstract: Existing BeiDou satellite channels are characterized by high packet loss rates and low communication frequencies, limiting the reliability and efficiency of multisensor data transmission. To address this issue, we present a multisensor time series-triggered (MSTT) intelligent communication framework for BeiDou satellites to improve information transmission by deep-sea networks. Specifically, we establish a new BeiDou satellite communication protocol. title: Airborne and marine microplastics in the Northern Indian Ocean: decoupled pathways traced by black carbon
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have been detected in both marine and atmospheric particulate matter, but their sources, transport, and air–sea exchange remain poorly constrained in remote marine regions. We investigated airborne microplastics (AMPs) and marine microplastics (MMPs) during a 1-month campaign at the Maldives Climate Observatory Hanimaadhoo and in adjacent coastal waters. Airborne particles were collected with a deposition box, and seawater was sampled at coastal sites. title: Lessons learned from UAV surveys over drifting sea ice at high latitudes
abstract: In this study, we provide an overview of the challenges encountered when using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), or drones, for mapping high-latitude Arctic pack ice. A major challenge when generating void-free orthomosaics and Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) of ice floes is their drift, which can easily exceed 0.5 m s −1 in the central Arctic Ocean. To address this issue, we developed and evaluated a novel approach for conducting autonomous grid missions at high latitudes, incorporating ice-drift correction during both the pre-flight planning and post-flight processing stages. title: TARS: a framework for marine oil spill triage using AIS anomaly detection and SAR browse imagery
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can observe oil on the sea surface in all weather, but operational pipelines are built around Level-1 Ground Range Detected (GRD) products of roughly 0.7–1 GB per scene. This paper presents TARS (Timely Anomaly Response System), an event-driven framework in which Automatic Identification System (AIS) telemetry decides where to look, and the Sentinel-1 browse (quicklook) image, about 3,400 times smaller than the GRD product, is classified at that location. title: Quality Control and Substantiation of Health-Related Claims for Processed Berry Products Entering the U.S. Market
abstract: Processed berry products often reach the United States with labels, dossiers, and sales practices shaped by foreign rules, where a product may be registered as a functional food and sold in recommended courses. This review examines quality control and the substantiation of health-related claims as part of the evidentiary chain for such products. title: Quantitative evaluation of the fate of TNT in controlled photic and aphotic zones: Implications for environmental risk assessment of underwater munitions
abstract: The kinetic behaviour and environmental fate of 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT) under controlled marine conditions remain poorly understood. This study quantifies TNT dissolution, adsorption and photodegradation in controlled seawater systems representing photic (≤200 m) and aphotic (≥1000 m) zones. Cylindrical TNT charges (bare) of mass range (1.17 g – 1.45 g) were incubated in 15 L of synthetic seawater (pH 8.1, salinity 35 ppt, 6–8 °C) within a closed recirculating seawater system and sediment consisting of sterilised sand for both photic and aphotic conditions respectively. title: Herb MaRS Guided Identification and Prioritization of Chemical Markers in Marketed Herbal Products for Rheumatoid Arthritis
abstract: Standardization of herbal products is a challenging area because of complexity in raw material identification and quality, extract consistency and diverse nature of phytoconstituents in them. The use of chemical markers in standardization is an important approach for overcoming the problems with raw materials to finished products in various stages of development. This study is aimed to identify and prioritize suitable chemical markers for medicinal plants used in rheumatoid arthritis herbal products marketed in India, with the objective of supporting product standardization and quality control

title: All at Sea? The United States and the International Governance of Deep-Sea Mining
abstract: In 2025, US President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing his administration to accelerate the development of mineral resources on the deep seabed. The executive order framed such action as necessary to secure robust domestic supply chains of critical minerals.1 The move was part of a broader effort by the second Trump administration to open federal lands to resource extraction, to reinvigorate domestic mining, and reduce the United States’ reliance on international supply chains.2 However, the executive order differed from other measures in stating that efforts to promote deep-se

title: Understanding the ocean as energy: the ITLOS Advisory Opinion on Climate Change as an earth systems provocation
abstract: This article contends that the 2024 Advisory Opinion of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea marks a subtle but significant ontological shift in the legal construction of the ocean under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). title: Climate Change and Multisystem Disruption of Diabetes Care: A Climate-Health System
abstract: Climate change increases the need for health systems to prepare for extreme weather events that threaten continuity of chronic disease care. This narrative review examines the clinical and health system implications of flooding for diabetes care in Southeast Asia, using the November 2025 Hat Yai floods in southern Thailand as a case study. We synthesized evidence from disaster medicine literature, regional epidemiological studies, and current diabetes guidance. title: State‐Controlled Fact‐Checking During COVID‐19: A Case of Thailand's Anti‐Fake News Center
abstract: Fact‐checking is among the most common responses to fake news. In authoritarian countries, particularly in Southeast Asia, state‐controlled fact‐checkers are common, but it remains unclear whether efforts to control fake news are driven by genuine concerns for information integrity or by attempts to control information flows and suppress dissent. To investigate the roles of these organizations, this paper employs content analysis to compare patterns in reports produced by the state‐controlled Anti‐Fake News Center (AFNC) and the independent AFP Fact Check (Thailand) during COVID‐19. abstract: The Roman mosaic of the Sea Centaur of Conímbriga (Condeixa-a-Velha, Condeixa-a-Nova, Portugal) was discovered in 1939. The Centaur is represented in a triumphal posture, as an abbreviated representation of a procession in honor of Neptune.This figurative panel is imbedded into the center of a pavement, the field of which presents a decorative program including other marine subjects, in a geometric composition of sixty tangent crowns, reminding the continuous wave movement of the water. title: Combinatorial Selection of Multi-Pass ICESat-2 ATL24 Calibration Tracks for Sentinel-2 Satellite-Derived Bathymetry
abstract: ICESat-2 ATL24 data provide along-track shallow-water depths that can serve as spaceborne calibration information for satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). A study area is usually crossed by multiple passes, but the tracks differ in quality, depth coverage, and spatial coverage. Existing studies still mainly pool all tracks, use a single pass, or refine the data point by point, and no systematic method yet exists for selecting among large numbers of candidate-track combinations. AusTemp: new thermal stress and marine heatwave monitoring tools for Australia
abstract: Context Recurrent marine heatwaves (MHW) across Australia’s marine region highlighted the need for expanded near real-time sea-surface temperature (SST) monitoring to support event responses and track ecosystem impacts. ReefTemp Next Generation, which supplied Great Barrier Reef heat stress data from 2012 to 2024, has been decommissioned. Aims To implement AusTemp, a new remote sensing application replacing and upgrading ReefTemp with near real-time marine heat stress and heatwave tracking across the Australian region (96–174°E, 8–48°S). title: Sinking Utopia: seasteading and religious infrastructures of time and space
abstract: The early twenty-first century has witnessed a resurgence of colonial dreams of frontier living, now at sea. Efforts to inhabit the ocean as a means to create new societies, known as ‘seasteading’, unabashedly draw on the rhetoric of nineteenth-century U.S. settler colonialism to frame contemporary forms of techno-capitalism and libertarianism. Driven by grandiose fantasies to open radically new political possibilities by enabling mobile, choice-based marine societies, seasteaders proudly frame their endeavours as utopian. title: Characteristics of multiple-trip echoes observed by EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar
abstract: Observations from the EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar (CPR) frequently contain spurious cloud signals caused by mirror images, multiple-scattering (MS) tails, and satellite mirror images (SMIs). These multiple-trip echoes are produced when transmitted radar pulses follow longer-than-nominal propagation paths and return within the reception window of subsequent pulses. title: Peroxidase-immobilized polycaprolactone/poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether electrospun nanofibers for colorimetric detection of hydrogen peroxide in seawater
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a key reactive oxygen species in marine systems, serving as an indicator of photochemical activity, organic matter transformation and environmental stress. Its determination in seawater is therefore relevant for assessing water quality, tracking pollution and understanding the biogeochemical processes that influence marine ecosystem health. In this study, nanofibers (NFs) were fabricated from poly-ε-caprolactone (PCL) and poly(ethylene glycol) diglycidyl ether (PEGDE) by electrospinning. title: An age calculator for high-latitude Quaternary foraminifera using amino acid racemization
abstract: Dating deep-sea cores from polar regions is challenging because sedimentation rates can be variable and oxygen-isotope stratigraphy can be ineffective, making amino acid racemization an important alternative. We calibrated the rate of racemization in Neogloboquadrina pachyderma , the dominant high-latitude planktic foraminifer, using 140 independently dated samples from 21 Arctic, Nordic Seas, North Atlantic, and Southern Ocean sites spanning 2 ka to 1.4 Ma. title: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
abstract: As the global biodiversity crisis accelerates across terrestrial and shallow marine systems, the extent of this collapse remains unknown within the deep sea. Despite encompassing most of the ocean, deep-sea ecosystems remain the planet's final frontier. Within this vast realm, the mesopelagic zone represents a critical yet poorly understood habitat, particularly in terms of its conservation status. title: Bilary PAH metabolites in Baltic Sea fish as indicators of spatial and temporal contamination trends
abstract: Background Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are priority pollutants of high environmental relevance. In fish however, they are quickly degraded into stable metabolites excreted via fish bile. To monitor PAH exposure of marine fish, these bile metabolites are used. The present study gives insight into two PAH metabolite concentrations in 850 samples in three fish species at nine locations in the Baltic Sea fish from 2011 to 2023. title: Recent thermohaline shifts in the Adriatic Sea and their potential consequences
abstract: The Adriatic Sea has warmed and salinified rapidly over the past two decades, and the changes are not uniform with depth. We combine 33 664 quality-controlled shipboard and Argo temperature and salinity casts from 1950–2025 into two climatologies, test the individual casts for regime shifts, and use the Argo profiles from the Southern Adriatic Pit to quantify the vertical structure of the changes. abstract: Measurements of aerosol size-resolved chemical composition and source contribution of carbonaceous aerosols provide a unique opportunity to characterize continental outflow over the sea. Studies at coastal sites usually show an interesting mix of continental and marine aerosol sources. However, few data exist on the size dependence of the aerosol chemical composition and isotopic source apportionment of organic carbon (OC). title: Marine guideline values for the oil dispersant Slickgone EW
abstract: Chemical dispersants are widely used in marine oil spill response, yet robust guideline values (GVs) for many products remain lacking. This study derived both acute and the first chronic marine GVs for Slickgone EW using a species sensitivity distribution (SSD) approach consistent with Australian and New Zealand guidance. New toxicity data for seven tropical marine species were combined with seven existing datasets, representing 14 species across nine taxonomic groups. title: Mugil cephalus as a Bioindicator of Coastal Ecosystem Health: Integrating Contaminant Bioaccumulation, Biomarkers, Multi-Stressor Toxicity, and Seafood Safety
abstract: Mugil cephalus, commonly called the flathead grey mullet, lives in rivers, estuaries, lagoons, and coastal seas, and feeds on detritus and sediment-associated matter. These habits make it one of the most widely used sentinel fish species for coastal pollution monitoring. This review brings together recent literature, mainly from 2015 to 2025, on four connected topics: contaminant bioaccumulation, biological biomarkers, multi-stressor toxicity, and seafood safety in M. cephalus. abstract: Low temperature is a major environmental stressor that severely affects the physiology and survival of marine fish. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying cold stress responses in spotted sea bass Lateolabrax maculatus remain poorly understood, particularly from a multi-omics perspective. Here, integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to systematically investigate hepatic responses to acute cold stress (8 °C). title: The Spatially Displaced Security Dilemma: Early Militarization and Crisis Stability across Indian Ocean Chokepoints
abstract: The security-dilemma literature usually assumes that rivals build up capabilities in the same place, so that each side’s deployments are visible to the other. This article argues that the assumption does not hold in the contemporary Indian Ocean, where states arm, garrison and survey chokepoints in peacetime, long before any crisis, and where rival capabilities often sit at different but functionally connected nodes of the same sea lines of communication. title: How decision‐makers perceive and assess risk is key to scaling up coastal restoration
abstract: Understanding how government decision‐makers perceive and assess risk is essential to scaling up coastal restoration. We examined risk perceptions associated with oyster reef restoration and reintroduction of tidal flow by interviewing 17 permitting officials across Queensland, New South Wales, and Commonwealth agencies. Participants identified a wide range of risks, often shaped by uncertainty, novelty, and regulatory frameworks designed primarily to prevent harm rather than enable restoration. abstract: The use of Earth Observation data for monitoring of aquatic and coastal ecosystems has expanded significantly, yet gaps remain in the spectral and thermal capabilities needed to detect and characterize liquid discharges. This study evaluates the potential of simulated pre-launch CHIME and LSTM observations, integrated with operational Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 data, for water-quality anomaly detection across diverse aquatic environments, demonstrating that the simulated datasets are sufficiently realistic to reproduce key water-quality and thermal indicators and support pre-operational applic

abstract: Background and Aims: The implementation of the International Maritime Organisation’s (IMO) IMO 2020 sulfur cap and subsequent regulatory amendments to MARPOL Annexe VI have markedly reshaped environmental compliance behaviour across the global shipping industry, directly influencing air quality and operational practices. IMO 2020 reduced the permitted sulfur content in marine fuel from 3.5 % to 0.5 % outside emission control areas, with even stricter limits within designated zones, driving widespread adoption of very low sulfur fuel oil and emission control technologies.Methodology: This study

title: Review: Toxicity Profile of Sea Cucumbers (Holothuroidea) and Its Implications for Cosmetic Product Safety
abstract: Sea cucumbers (Holothuroidea) have drawn growing interest from the cosmetic industry because of their rich bioactive compounds, including saponins, chondroitin sulfates, and antioxidants, which are thought to support skin rejuvenation and slow the signs of aging. Despite this growing use, scientific understanding of their safety and potential toxicity in cosmetic formulations remains incomplete. title: Alternative Marine Fuels: A Pathway to Carbon-Neutral Shipping
abstract: Shipping decarbonization requires fuel-selection decisions that account for emissions across the full fuel lifecycle as well as machinery adaptation, economic feasibility, shipboard safety and bunkering availability. This study evaluates liquefied natural gas (LNG), methanol, ammonia, hydrogen and advanced biofuels using a seven-criterion weighted-sum multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), supported by a structured technical literature synthesis. title: Unlocking the Seaweed Value Chain: Constraints and Possible Solutions in the Understudied Coastal Areas of Mainland Tanzania
abstract: Seaweed is a vital food and livelihood resource in Tanzania, with potential to strengthen and diversify food systems. It enables the production of high‐value products while delivering environmental benefits. Tanzania has witnessed promising research and advances in the seaweed value chain (VC), particularly in Zanzibar. However, critical gaps remain, including weak value chain mapping, limited analyses of constraints and potential solutions, poorly understood value distribution and insufficient attention to gender‐differentiated outcomes. title: 3D geometric documentation of cultural heritage sites at risk: Cross-environment workflow and hazard-related applications
abstract: Climate and geohazard pressures increasingly threaten cultural heritage, creating a need for transferable cross-environment approaches to 3D geometric documentation and stronger linkage to risk-oriented analyses. title: Inter-population connectivity of southern elephant seals and the likely intra-species transmission pathways of high pathogenicity avian influenza
abstract: High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has spread beyond birds to affect seals across the Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic region, with southern elephant seals ( Mirounga leonina ) particularly devastated. The virus, likely introduced via spillover from infected migratory birds, has killed tens of thousands of adult seals and pups throughout most of their range. title: Estado actual del sistema de aseguramiento de la calidad y el régimen de acreditación en la educación superior en Chile
abstract: This paper is aimed at characterizing the current quality assurance system for higher education in Chile. We discuss the main implications that the Chilean model of accreditation has brought to the country’s higher education system by presenting and analyzing official data. Results show that, although the Chilean model has permitted a more orderly and coherent growth of the higher education system as a whole, there are still several limitations and challenges yet to be addressed.

abstract: Although Yarrowia lipolytica has been extensively studied in industrial and genetically engineered strains, environmental isolates may harbor distinct genetic and functional traits that broaden our understanding of the species metabolic diversity and biotechnological potential. Here, we investigated Y. lipolytica LMS 24 B, a marine-derived strain isolated from zoanthids and previously reported to emulsify hydrocarbons and grow in the presence of kerosene, by combining genome mining with enzymatic assays under different carbon-source conditions.
