abstract: This study analyzes fishers' compliance with and perceptions of licensing documents at the Marine and Fisheries Resources Surveillance Office (PSDKP), Takalar Station, which operates within the working area of PSDKP Bitung. The objectives were: (1) to describe fishers' compliance with the procedures for issuing licensing documents and (2) to describe fishers' perceptions of licensing documents through an assessment of service quality. abstract: Fish Landing Bases (PPI) play a strategic role in supporting capture fisheries, improving fishers' livelihoods, and strengthening coastal economic development. This study aimed to analyze the implementation of the policy on the utilization of the Lonrae Fish Landing Base (PPI) in Bone Regency using the policy implementation framework proposed by Van Meter and Van Horn. title: Comparative effectiveness of soil and foliar application of different silicon sources on wheat productivity in coastal soils of the Ganges delta
abstract: Silicon (Si) has emerged as a beneficial nutrient element for increasing crop resilience under various stresses; however, limited information is available regarding the comparative performance of different application methods and sources for wheat production in coastal areas of the Ganges delta. A field experiment was conducted during two consecutive winter seasons of 2024–25 and 2025–26 in Patuakhali district of Bangladesh, to examine the effects of different Si sources and application methods on growth, yield, Si uptake and economic performance of wheat in coastal soil. title: Contrasting ecological patterns across deglaciating Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords revealed by soft-sediment benthic assemblages
abstract: Antarctic fjords are natural laboratories for assessing how global change and glacier retreat reshape marine benthic ecosystems, yet comparative studies integrating multiple components of soft-sediment assemblages remain scarce. Here, we assess three glacier-influenced fjords of the Western Antarctic Peninsula: Marian Cove, Börgen Bay and Sheldon Cove. title: Sustainable Precast Concrete Technologies for Climate-Resilient Buildings and Infrastructure in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Saudi Arabia’s is big country that require concrete systems that can endure severe heat, chloride-bearing coastal conditions, intermittent intense rainfall and long service periods while reducing embodied emissions. This critical integrative review examines sustainable precast concrete technologies through the combined lenses of climate exposure, material performance, factory quality control and whole-life environmental accounting. abstract: Estimates of outmigration timing of Atlantic salmon smolt ( Salmo salar ) have become crucial inputs for predictive models that quantify effects of anthropogenic impacts. Recent reviews indicate that choice of method may impact estimates of migration timing, demanding an evaluation of the various monitoring tools in tandem. Here, we compared the migration behavior of smolts tagged with PIT tags or acoustic telemetry tags with smolts monitored with river transects of underwater video systems in two rivers in western Norway for three consecutive migration seasons (2019–2021). title: Reluctant Conformity: Volunteers’ Faith in, and Expectations of, Law when Performing Maritime Search and Rescue Work
abstract: This article examines how Search and Rescue (SAR) volunteers think of and narrate their experiences of the law in the course of their work and assesses the legitimacy of the actions of coastal states when responding to refugees making sea crossings. This article argues that a narrative schema of “reluctant conformity” explains how SAR volunteers practically reconcile the faith they demonstrate in law with their operational reality, in light of multiple, competing obligations. abstract: Coastal island settlements face interconnected challenges of electricity supply, building energy demand, and indoor environmental quality. This study examined the comparative performance of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and coastal adaptive architecture within a renewable energy village framework for Panjang Island, Banten. abstract: Small urban mangrove remnants may undergo substantial spatial reorganization that regional land-cover products or endpoint area change alone poorly represent. title: First observations of aerosol mass fluxes over open water using a large-aperture scintillometer
abstract: Near-surface aerosol mass exchange over water remains poorly constrained because direct flux observations are scarce and conventional point measurements have limited spatial representativeness. This study presents the first application of a large-aperture scintillometer (LAS) to retrieve path-averaged aerosol mass-flux magnitudes over open-water-dominated environments, based on four field campaigns at an inland lake and a coastal bay in eastern China. title: Single-blind controlled release testing of vehicle- and aircraft-based methane measurement systems at the TADI facility
abstract: Accurate methane emission quantification is critical for climate mitigation efforts in the oil and gas industry. This study evaluates the performance of five academic methane measurement systems through single-blind controlled release testing at the TotalEnergies Anomaly Detection Initiatives (TADI) facility in France during June and September 2024. abstract: In September 2026, El Niño was strengthening, with positive temperature anomalies across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. The El Niño‐Southern Oscillation is monitored by satellites, moorings, ships, coastal gauges, and autonomous floats. Operational centers turn these observations into indices, maps, analyses, and forecasts. abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a major staple crop worldwide and improving grain yield (GY) through the identification of superior genotypes and yield-contributing traits is essential for sustainable production. This study evaluated genetic variability, character association, path coefficients and genetic diversity among 64 lowland rice genotypes under transplanted conditions using a randomised complete block design (RCBD) with two replications. abstract: Advanced aerosol measurements at high-altitude observatories are scientifically valuable but operationally demanding, and the established standard procedures, such as those of WMO/GAW and ACTRIS, were developed largely for near sea level stations. This technical note sets out operating procedures for advanced aerosol instruments at high-altitude sites, with an emphasis on tropical observatories, and is intended to complement rather than restate those guidelines. title: Beyond Knowledge Transfer: Non-Human Embodiment for Environmental Education
abstract: Effective conservation education must communicate ecological facts while also making distant environmental threats personally meaningful. Virtual reality (VR) may support this goal by allowing learners to experience such threats from a non-human perspective, yet it remains unclear whether embodied interactive VR primarily improves factual learning, affective engagement, or both. We present EcoShift VR, a dual-ecosystem experience in which users embody either a Sunda pangolin facing pollution and poaching or a blue shark facing pollution and bycatch. abstract: Protecting populations and genetic diversity within them is critical to conserving the resilience and adaptive potential of species. Fisheries management has long had the ambition of managing species at the population level, but mainly define “fish stocks” based on geographical limits, which can lead to overfishing of sensitive populations in areas where many different populations coexist. title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. title: Towards an Integrated Maritime Court System in Indonesia: Realizing Fair, Efficient, and Low-Cost Justice in Maritime Disputes
abstract: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic nation and has significant economic opportunities in its ocean-based industries. However, the legal framework governing maritime activities is fragmented across multiple disconnected areas. At present, maritime disputes fall under the jurisdiction of different institutions: the Maritime Court, District Court, Fisheries Court, and National Transportation Safety Commission. title: She Sails Scholar: A Structural Model of the Educational Experiences of Female Maritime Students
abstract: The maritime industry remains heavily male-dominated, creating an empirical research gap regarding how individual, socio-cultural, and institutional factors influence the educational outcomes of female maritime cadets. This study quantified and analyzed the educational experiences of female maritime students and evaluated the relationships among self- and career-related factors, social and cultural influences, institutional and onboard climate, and overall student performance and persistence. title: Digital Islam and the Rise of Minority Interest Parties in Europe: Assessing DENK’s Electoral Strategy and Muslim Youth Mobilisation in the Netherlands
abstract: The rise of right-wing populism across Europe has placed immigrant Muslim communities at the centre of increasingly hostile political discourse. From Geert Wilders in the Netherlands to Marine Le Pen in France, populist politicians have systematically framed Muslim minorities as threats to national identity, culture, and social cohesion, treating immigrant communities not as democratic constituencies but as problems to be managed. abstract: Memecylon umbellatum, is a versatile ethnomedicinal plant that is indigenous to Indian forests and belongs to the family Melastomataceae. It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic and Siddha systems of medicine. The study examines the phytochemicals present in the leaves and stem of Memecylon umbellatum and investigates their antibacterial potential. title: Beyond Resource Dependence: Human Ecological Perspectives on Angola’s Sustainable Development Challenges
abstract: Human ecological concerns in Africa have become increasingly urgent as nations struggle to balance economic growth with environmental sustainability. Angola, a leading oil-producing country, presents a critical case for examining the complex interplay between natural resource exploitation, ecological degradation, and human well-being. abstract: In May 2026 the United Nations Environment Programme released a working paper finding that solar radiation modification (SRM) is not currently a viable climate response, while framing continued research under globally coordinated oversight as the prudent course. title: Community-Based Fisheries Downstreaming through the Development of Natural Fish Stock Powder: Evidence from Usaha Mandiri Consumer Cooperative, Belitung, Indonesia
abstract: Coastal fishing communities often depend on selling fresh catches, limiting opportunities to increase product value through processing. In Tanjung Binga, Belitung, this highlights the need to strengthen Koperasi Konsumen Usaha Mandiri (KUM) 's processing capacity. This community service programme aimed to develop skills in producing natural fish stock powder and support the cooperative’s product development capacity. abstract: The escalating production of engineered nanomaterials has raised concerns about their environmental impact. However, conventional short-term, high-dose ecotoxicity studies inadequately reflect realistic exposure scenarios. This study evaluated the long-term, low-dose toxicity of bare zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) and four representative silane-modified ZnO-NPs in the marine diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana. We analysed monitoring data from Jingjiang, 240 km upstream of the river mouth (2002-2017; 519 effective surveys; 10,560 measured individuals), combining size-based catch indices, environmental-window analyses and otolith Sr/Ca profiles from 115 Japanese grenadier anchovy Coilia nasus. title: Carbon monoxide utilization by Thermanaeromonas species and description of Thermobium azorense gen. nov., sp. nov.
abstract: Syngas fermentation by carbon monoxide (CO)-utilizing acetogens offers a sustainable route for converting gasified waste materials into value-added chemicals. In this study, we isolated a novel thermophilic CO-utilizing bacterium, strain AZ2, from marine hydrothermal sediment collected on the island of São Miguel, Azores, Portugal. Strain AZ2 is an obligately anaerobic, spore-forming bacterium. title: Chemical characterization, antibacterial activity, in vitro cytotoxicity, and selectivity of the lipid extract from Sargassum filipendula against multidrug-resistant bacteria
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria necessitates new therapeutic alternatives, and marine macroalgae represent an underexplored source of bioactive lipids. This study characterized the lipid extract (LE) of Sargassum filipendula and evaluated its antibacterial and cytotoxic profiles against MDR hospital isolates. LE composition was determined by GC-MS, and its thermal behavior by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). title: Intercomparison of nighttime aerosol optical depth retrievals from both reflectance-based and city light-based methods using VIIRS DNB data
abstract: Using observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Day/Night Band (DNB), two different nighttime aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieval methods were evaluated and inter-compared. The first approach is a lunar reflectance-based retrieval method, using reflected moonlight in a manner similar to daytime retrievals. title: DFlee: a scalable agent-based framework for simulating flood-induced population displacement across multiple flood scenarios
abstract: Natural disasters displace millions of people each year, and effective disaster response requires accurate models of population movement. This study presents DFlee, an agent-based model for flood-induced evacuation built on the Flee framework for conflict-driven displacement. abstract: A horizontal schematic begins with a fungal finding in the source or water phase. It emphasizes that water-phase sampling alone may provide only a snapshot, may miss hidden surface or biofilm reservoirs, and may be misleading when release is intermittent. abstract: The decapod fauna of The Netherlands has changed markedly in recent decades, driven by natural dispersal of non-indigenous species (NIS) and human-mediated range expansions of invasive alien species (IAS). Thirty-five years have passed since the last comprehensive assessment of brachyuran crabs in The Netherlands and for the remaining decapods this gap extends to 40 years. abstract: The high cost and inconsistent availability of imported inputs constrain broiler production in Sudan. Since April 2023 these constraints have been aggravated by conflict, disruption to domestic and international trade, Red Sea and Suez Canal shipping difficulties, higher freight costs, and depreciation of the Sudanese pound against the US dollar. The selected four Croton species were Croton aromaticus L., Croton caudatus Geiseler, Croton persimilis Müll.Arg. and Croton zeylanicus Müll.Arg. abstract: Beginning in the late 2000s, coyotes ( Canis latrans ) colonized the barrier islands of the Outer Banks of North Carolina, USA, where they depredate protected shorebird and sea turtle nests. abstract: Subject of study. abstract: Hospital wastewater from medical, nursing, laboratory, pharmacy, and sanitation activities may contain organic matter, suspended solids, chemical compounds, metals, and microorganisms that pose environmental and public health risks if not properly managed, making treatment and regular effluent monitoring essential for pollution control. abstract: Islands occupy a privileged position in human imagination and in the geography of the real world. As circumscribed, ecologically distinct, and often isolated territories, they concentrate geographic diversity into bounded spaces that invite exploration, narrative, and control. abstract: Climate models struggle to accurately represent polar regions, largely due to the difficulty in modeling clouds. The uncertainty budget of polar radiation is dominated by cloud and cloud-aerosol interactions, but challenges in maintaining robust field observations mean that even basic knowledge such as cloud occurrence is not well known. abstract: Pore-pressure prediction has been a critical concern for the oil and gas industry for many decades. abstract: Accelerated Arctic warming may remobilize legacy radioactive contaminants preserved in the cryosphere, increasing the need for reliable historical baselines. abstract: Municipal wastewater is a significant pathway for the transport of pesticide residues into aquatic environments, particularly in rapidly urbanizing and agriculturally intensive regions. title: Diachronic analysis of food culture and butyrate production potential in the Kyotango region, Japan: from the Jomon period to the present
abstract: Kyotango City, Kyoto Prefecture, has roughly three times the national centenarian rate and a gut microbiota notably enriched in butyrate-producing bacteria ( Roseburia spp., Faecalibacterium spp., and relatives). Yet the historical and cultural origins of this distinctive microbiome have not been examined systematically. Using a large language model (LLM) as the literature-integration tool, we conducted a narrative integrative review that synthesizes food culture evidence from six temporal cross sections spanning the Jomon period to the present. title: Annual sampling frequency and false-negative probability in water-quality threshold-exceedance detection: an exact conditional analysis of the Buranhém River, Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Routine monitoring captures conditions present during sampling, so sparse schedules may fail to encounter threshold exceedances recorded at other times in the same year. Using 106 Class 2 freshwater campaigns from five Buranhém River sites during 2015–2024, the analysis examined seven water-quality parameters and a composite any-exceedance outcome within site-years. Exact finite-population probabilities were calculated for each positive annual reference set to determine whether hypothetical schedules of one to four campaigns would include at least one recorded exceedance. title: Liquid crystal monomers and organic light-emitting materials in alpine soils and vegetation from the Tibetan Plateau: levels and distribution behavior
abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs) and organic light-emitting materials (OLEMs) are emerging contaminants widely used in electronic displays, yet their environmental behavior in remote alpine ecosystems remains poorly understood. Here, 44 LCMs/OLEMs were investigated in soils and alpine vegetation from the Tibetan Plateau (TP). C Σ44LCMs+OLEMs in soils ranged from 28.5–2437 pg/g dw and followed the trend of Nyingchi > Lhasa > Ngari, indicating enhanced deposition in humid monsoon regions. title: A Wavelet-Change-Point framework for sequence-stratigraphic controls on reservoir quality and geomechanical evaluation: a case study of the Asmari-Ghar succession, SW Iran
abstract: The Oligo-Miocene Ghar-Asmari interval of the Dezful Embayment (SW Iran) is a proven reservoir, but its field-scale sequence-stratigraphic framework is poorly documented. We apply a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) multi-resolution analysis (Meyer wavelet, detail levels D1-D4) to gamma-ray logs of four wells in the Bahregansar and Hendijan fields. title: Aerosol Cross‐Boundary‐Layer Transport and Its Microphysical Impacts on Stratiform Clouds: Insights From Two‐Case Aircraft In Situ Observations
abstract: Aerosol‐cloud interactions represent one of the largest uncertainties in climate forcing estimates, particularly for stratiform clouds whose extensive coverage and low cloud bases render them highly susceptible to planetary boundary layer (PBL) processes. However, observational constraints on how diurnally varying PBL dynamics modulate aerosol vertical transport and cloud microphysical responses are limited. title: Digging deeper: Plant sedimentary ancient DNA in archaeobotanical studies
abstract: The analysis of plant sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) is increasingly being applied in paleoecology and is now gaining relevance in archaeobotany and archaeology. This review outlines the practices involved in sedaDNA sampling, extraction, and analysis, emphasising contamination prevention and methodological considerations. Various genetic methods (metagenomics, metabarcoding, and target enrichment) are discussed concerning their strengths, limitations, and suitability for specific research questions. title: Influence of Oxide Nanoparticles on Mechanical Performance and Freeze - Thaw Resistance of Rigid Pavement
abstract: Globally, rigid concrete pavements suffer premature deterioration when repeated traffic is combined with moisture and temperature fluctuations, as capillary water ingress and freeze-thaw cycles cause internal microcracking, loss of stiffness and a reduction in the modulus of elasticity. In Peru, this problem is critical in high Andean areas, where sub-zero temperatures and high humidity accelerate internal damage and increase road maintenance costs. title: Updating Analytical Methods for Cyanobacteria and Their Metabolites
abstract: Key Takeaways Cyanobacteria blooms pose significant water quality challenges. A multi‐tiered monitoring approach, in‐field and in‐laboratory, is essential. Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater offers guidance on monitoring of algae and cyanobacteria. Future method updates will continue to expand monitoring options for utilities.

title: Post-depositional geochemical transformations of aerosol impurities in EPICA Dome C ice core: dissolution, mineral neoformation, and immobilization revealed by CFA-sp-ICP-TOFMS
abstract: Aerosol-derived impurities in deep Antarctic ice cores provide high-resolution records of past climate and atmospheric variability. However, post-depositional englacial geochemical processes driven by impurity remobilization through ice metamorphism can perturb the originally deposited signals, challenging the interpretation of deep ice records. title: Sanitation, Hygiene, and Supply Management Practices Among Fish Vendors in Bongao Public Market, Tawi-Tawi, Philippines
abstract: This study assessed sanitation and hygiene practices, supply management, and operational challenges among fish vendors at Bongao Public Market, Tawi-Tawi, Philippines. Using a descriptive cross-sectional case study design, 50 vendors were selected through quota sampling. Data were gathered through structured questionnaires, supplemented by interviews and direct observations, and analyzed using frequencies, percentages, and weighted means. title: Food ration affects mRNA processing, translation, proteostasis and cytoskeletal responses during heat shock in Mytilus californianus
abstract: Despite a likely role in setting stress tolerance limits, food ration has received limited attention as an ecological factor affecting the cellular stress response (CSR). To study the interactive effects of food and temperature on the proteomic heat shock response, we acclimated intertidal mussels (Mytilus californianus) to four combinations of nearshore (low) and aquaculture (high) phytoplankton levels, combined with low (20°C) and high (30°C) aerial temperatures during daytime low tides. title: Late Habsburg Colonial Masculinity. The ‘Boxer’ War (1899–1901) and its Memory in the Museum of Military History in Vienna*
abstract: This article examines the memory and representation of the Habsburg Empire’s colonial involvement in the ‘Boxer’ War (1899–1901), as presented in the Museum of Military History (Heeresgeschichtliches Museum) in Vienna. Drawing on exhibition analysis and a gender-historical perspective, the contribution explores how the museum’s permanent naval exhibition constructs narratives of Austria-Hungary’s colonial past. title: Stormy Petrel: The rise and fall of Royal Navy submarine ace Alastair Mars
abstract: Thanks to a pair of entertaining war memoirs that have been in print for more than sixty years, Alastair Mars has long been among the most recognised British submarine commanders of the Second World War. He is also notorious for being court martialled and dismissed seven years after the conflict ended; an outcome which remains quite controversial. title: Spectral Co-Design of Ship Rudder Geometry and Heading Autopilot for Energy Efficiency and Manoeuvring Safety
abstract: Rudders determine the manoeuvring safety of a ship and permanently consume propulsive power through profile drag, weather helm and autopilot action. Because rudder geometry and course-keeping controller are designed separately and the energy cost of steering requires long stochastic simulations, their joint trade-off between energy efficiency and safety has remained unquantified. This paper proposes a spectral co-design method that optimises rudder area, span and section thickness together with the parameters of a PID heading autopilot. title: Physicochemical, Nutrient and Microbiological Characteristics of Water from Selected Waterfronts in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria
abstract: Water quality assessment is important in waterfront communities where surface waters support domestic activities, fisheries, transportation and other livelihoods. This study assessed selected physicochemical, nutrient and microbiological characteristics of water from Adiabo, Nsidung and Ikang waterfronts in Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Water samples were analysed for pH, temperature, turbidity, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids (TDS), colour, salinity, total hardness, nitrate, nitrite, phosphorus, ammonia, faecal coliform count (FCC) and total coliform count (TCC). title: The Impact of Water Supply on the Tourist Experience in Del Carmen, Surigao Del Norte
abstract: This study assessed water supply conditions and their relationship with tourist experience in Del Carmen, Surigao del Norte, Philippines, and identified existing water scarcity mitigation strategies. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed, involving 200 tourists selected through criterion sampling and 20 purposively selected tourism stakeholders and local government personnel. title: Eco-productive performance and managerial perception in environmentally certified companies: A mixed-methods study in Sinaloa, northwestern Mexico
abstract: Voluntary environmental certification constitutes an instrument that promotes corporate ecoefficiency practices; however, examining its relation with the eco-productive practices of companies and the perceptions of their managers is necessary. Objective: This study analyzed the self-reported eco-productive performance and managerial perception of environmental management in companies certified by the Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection in Sinaloa, Mexico, through a mixed-methods design with quantitative priority. title: Abiotic Stressors and Infectious Disease in Aquaculture: Emerging Evidence for Environmental Contaminants as Hidden Disease Drivers
abstract: Infectious disease in aquaculture is shaped by interactions among pathogens, hosts and the surrounding environment. Temperature, salinity and other physicochemical conditions are established modifiers of several aquatic diseases, whereas environmental contaminants have been studied predominantly for their direct toxic effects. Whether contaminant exposure also alters subsequent infection has received much less integrated attention. abstract: Flooding is a primary riparian disturbance, yet the short-term biogeochemical consequences of rare, extreme floods remain poorly characterized in karst floodplains. After a 1-in-50-year flood in a karst reach of the Qingshui River (Guizhou, China), we compared soil physicochemical properties, carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) contents, and potential extracellular enzyme activities between three flood-affected locations covered by freshly deposited silt and three adjacent reference locations. abstract: Mussel adhesive proteins (MAPs) are promising bio-adhesives, but recombinant production faces challenges in yield and post-translational DOPA modification. Here, a fusion protein Pvfp-5P, comprising Perna viridis foot protein 5β and a preCol-P fragment, was expressed in Komagataella phaffii GS115 with and without co-expression of Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase, generating a catechol-modified form (Pvfp-5P(D)) and an unmodified tyrosine form (Pvfp-5P(Y)), respectively. title: Patterns of species richness and endemism in bee and plant communities in California
abstract: Effective conservation priorities require understanding species distributions and endemism patterns. Despite their vital pollination services, California's native bee distribution patterns remain largely unexplored. We analyzed bee species richness and endemism and their concordance with plant distributions. Bee and angiosperm richness hotspots coincided across large swaths of California, whereas endemism hotspots coincided over much smaller areas. title: Chromosome-level assembly and population-scale genomics in an intensively monitored wild bird, the Seychelles warbler
abstract: Understanding evolutionary processes is greatly facilitated by high-quality data on genetic variation. We report the development of a genomic toolkit for a recently bottlenecked, long-term studied species, the Seychelles warbler (Ptimerl dezil; Acrocephalus sechellensis). This toolkit comprises a reference genome assembled into 31 chromosomes, together with functional annotations and reference-panel-free imputation of whole-genome sequences from 1,935 individuals. title: Determination of organophosphate flame retardants and their diester transformation products in rice using a modified QuEChERS method coupled with UPLC-MS/MS
abstract: Residues of organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) and their diester transformation products in rice have raised concerns due to their widespread occurrence and potential for human exposure. Herein, a practical ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed and validated for the simultaneous quantification of 15 OPFRs and their 5 diester transformation products in rice. title: Seafood MSME Performance in Export-Linked Supply Chains: Implications for Local Trade Policy in Panay Island, Philippines
abstract: This study looked at how micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in the seafood sector on Panay Island in the Philippines are performing in their role within the export-bound supply chain, and what these effects might be on local trade policies. The study used a quantitative research design and data were collected from 421 seafood MSMEs in the provinces of Aklan, Antique, Capiz, and Iloilo using a purposive sampling method, where all respondents were part of the supply chain of seafood products exported from Panay Island. The performance of these MSMEs was calculated using 8 metrics

title: Organizing Ecological Sustainability Policy: The Craft and Professional Norms of Policy Professionals
abstract: Despite numerous national and international goals, public policies often prove unsuccessful in stopping sustainability crises. Policy professionals are central in formulating and implementing sustainability policy. To understand how these policies come to be, and why they often fall short, it is also important to understand the craft and professional norms that constitute the professionalism of policy professionals working on ecological sustainability policy. abstract: Currently, the philosophy of technology tries to emphasize technical thinking and contrast it with humanitarian thinking. There may be certain reasons for this, but an appeal to the history of technology and art shows that science developed in parallel with art and artistic imagination greatly contributed to the development of science and technology. abstract: This descriptive-developmental study assessed multi-tiered reading comprehension interventions and home-school partnerships among Grade 6 learners at Canjulao, Lo-ok, and Timpolok Elementary Schools in District 7, Schools Division of Lapu-Lapu City, during School Year 2026–2027. It aimed to establish an empirical basis for an Integrated Literacy Development Plan. Using purposive stratified sampling, the study involved 99 respondents: nine intermediate English teachers, 45 parents or guardians, and 45 struggling readers. title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa lasR is a keystone gene in polymicrobial cultures
abstract: The airways of people with cystic fibrosis (CF) are often co-infected by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and a variety of other co-habiting microbes; these infections are polymicrobial. P. aeruginosa isolates from the CF airways are also known to commonly acquire mutations in the quorum sensing regulator, lasR. In this work, we show that loss of lasR function has a profound impact on the stability of inter-species interactions in a polymicrobial ecosystem, and in particular, on the dynamics of a common CF-associated fungus, Candida albicans. title: Impact evaluation of the SunSmart Dermoscopy for Victorian General Practice Program on dermoscopy skills, confidence and skin cancer prevention practices in Australia
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Skin cancer is a major health concern in Australia. Early detection and accurate diagnosis in general practice are key to improving outcomes. This study evaluated the 2020-2023 SunSmart Dermoscopy for Victorian General Practice Program's impact on skin cancer diagnosis, prevention and management in general practice. title: Measurement report: Tethered balloon observations of vertically resolved aerosol size distributions during the U.S. DOE ARM CoURAGE and BNF campaigns
abstract: The vertical distribution of aerosol particle size is important for aerosol transport, atmospheric mixing, and surface air quality, yet vertically resolved aerosol size-distribution observations remain limited. Here, a miniature scanning electrical mobility spectrometer (mSEMS) was deployed aboard the U.S. Department of Energy Atmospheric Radiation Measurement (ARM) Tethered Balloon System (TBS) during the 2025 CoURAGE and Bankhead National Forest (BNF) campaigns. title: An adjustable-rate user-printable rain gauge calibrator
abstract: Accurate precipitation measurement is essential. However, calibration of field-deployed rain gauges remains a challenge. Many methods require laboratory conditions, costly commercial equipment, or instruments designed for specific rain gauges, which cannot accommodate smaller-diameter gauges. We introduce the Adjustable-Rate 3D Printed Rain Gauge Calibrator (AR3D) , a low-cost, open-source device designed for in situ calibration of rain gauges. abstract: We present the first radiographic ageing framework for common dolphins ( Delphinus delphis ), based on ossification and epiphyseal fusion patterns in the pectoral flipper, demonstrating higher reliability for chronological age estimation than currently available epigenetic approaches for this species. title: Integrated Seismic interpretation for reservoir characterization and petroleum system evaluation of the Khatatba Formation in the El Obayed field of the Northern Western Desert Egypt
abstract: The El-Obayed Field is one of the major hydrocarbon-producing fields in Egypt's Northern Western Desert. Located on the western flank of the Matruh Basin, the field contains significant gas accumulations within the Jurassic Khatatba Formation, particularly the Lower and Upper Safa Members. This study integrates geological, petrophysical, and seismic interpretation data to delineate hydrocarbon-bearing intervals, evaluate reservoir geometry, and improve understanding of the petroleum system within the study area. title: Solar-Powered Shrimp Aquaculture: Advancing Energy Efficiency, Shrimp Health and Sustainable Production
abstract: Shrimp aquaculture depends on a reliable supply of electricity for aeration, pumping, feeding, and water-quality management. In intensive systems, interruptions in the power supply can rapidly affect the dissolved oxygen (DO) levels and other culture conditions, thereby increasing physiological stress and the risk of production losses. abstract: In South Asia, the nuclear factor is the primary intervening variable that the May 2025 military engagement between Pakistan and India lasted for not more than four days and both states agreed to the ceasefire out of caution against inadvertent escalation. title: Correlates of extinction risk dynamics of mammals
abstract: Mammals continue to face increasing extinction risk, largely driven by escalating human pressures. However, the drivers of change in extinction risk remain poorly understood. We used an ordinal modeling framework (cumulative link mixed models) to test the correlation between biological traits, ecological characteristics, anthropogenic threats, and trends over time to analyze changes in extinction risk for 4,992 mammal species assessed by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List of Threatened Species. title: Birdwatching ecotourism potential in Shirvan and Gyzylaghaj wetlands
abstract: The aim of this study is the comparative assessment of the birdwatching ecotourism potential and opportunities of green economy of Shirvan and Gyzylaghaj wetlands in Azerbaijan. The research makes use of a multi-source data set, which brings together official information from institutions, expert-based scoring, data from Avibase checklist, and data from Ramsar-based wetland indicators along with the summaries of bird observations from eBird and Protected Planet metadata. title: Assessment of Metal Contamination and Human Health Risks in the Amapari River, Brazilian Amazon
abstract: The contamination of water by heavy metals is a great concern for many countries worldwide because of their potential to harm human health and biota. Although bordered by a mosaic of conservation units, the Amapari River (Brazil) is impacted by legal and illegal mineral exploitation. However, data on metal concentrations and related risks remain scarce. abstract: The utilization of locally sourced raw materials plays a strategic role in strengthening the sustainability of fishery-based micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). This study examined Gerai Panglima in Samarinda and its network of 20 partner MSMEs to understand how the adoption of appropriate fish processing technologies and local resource utilization contribute to product development and socio-economic empowerment. abstract: Background: Climate change threatens population health through temperature extremes, air pollution, and altered infectious disease patterns. Emergency departments (EDs) are sensitive indicators of climate-related health impacts; however, comprehensive multicenter investigations integrating meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease surveillance across different health care provision levels remain scarce in Germany, particularly in maritime climate regions. abstract: Background Preterm birth (PTB) is a primary global public health concern and the leading cause of infant mortality. Monitoring temporal trends and territorial inequities in PTB is essential to guide equitable perinatal and maternal health strategies. Objective To analyse the characteristics, rates, trends, and geographical inequalities in preterm births in Ecuador from 2015 to 2023, using altitude as a geographic equity stratifier. abstract: The existence of mineral deposits, with the expanding use of nuclear science in agriculture, medicine, and industry in Tanzania, has raised the need for operational public protection and environmental radiation monitoring frameworks. This review synthesizes the existing status of Tanzania’s monitoring and protection schemes, with a focus on the roles of the Tanzania Atomic Energy Commission (TAEC), institutional capacity, national legislation, collaborations and partnerships between scientific groups, and scientific research outcomes. abstract: In this study, multiple linear regression and principal component regression (PCR) methods were applied to predict the albumen index of Star-53 French–Pekin duck eggs based on external egg quality traits. abstract: Urinary mercury is read as a marker of inorganic exposure, and urinary elimination of dietary methylmercury is treated as negligible. Whether urine carries a measurable seafood signal in children is unresolved, and national programs rarely draw blood from young children. abstract: The native pinewoods of Scotland are acknowledged to be an important ecological resource, both for their biodiversity value and as a cultural and amenity resource. Due to the unique nature of the habitat and its limited range, it plays a critical role as an early warning system for broader environmental issues. In the late 1960s and 70s, increased concern was expressed regarding a decline in the status and management of the pinewoods. abstract: This study focused on developing a powdered mouthwash incorporating extracts from mangosteen peel and mango leaves. abstract: Indonesia continues to struggle with the collection, disposal, and recovery of pack- aging waste. title: Multifunctional Bioactive Compounds from Medicinal Plants: Antioxidant, Antimicrobial and Corrosion Inhibition Perspectives
abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides and essential oils. Phytochemicals extracted from medicinal plants find application in different biological systems due to their varied biological activities. Rising environmental concerns along with requirement for sustainable substitutes have gained interest in multifunctional compounds from plants. abstract: This study investigates trends in annual maximum flood (AMF) data from 362 stations across Australia using complementary statistical methods, including Mann–Kendall, modified lag-1 Mann–Kendall, seasonal and regional Mann–Kendall, Sen’s slope, Sen’s innovative trend analysis, and partial Mann–Kendall tests. abstract: Elevated operating temperature limits photovoltaic (PV) performance in hot climates, even where solar irradiance is high. This study evaluated passive air, front-surface water, and combined air–water cooling for 100 W monocrystalline PV modules under outdoor tropical conditions in Kampala, Uganda. abstract: The invasive round goby Neogobius melanostomus (Pallas, 1814) has advanced eastward through the state of New York and provinces of Ontario and Quebec over the past two decades and is approaching Lake Champlain, one of the largest lakes in North America. abstract: We present a phylogeny and taxonomy of Poa in Turkey, focusing on 20 bulbous species endemic to Western Eurasia and North Africa and their relationships. abstract: Pandora multi-axis retrievals in the boundary layer provide continuous observations of formaldehyde (HCHO) vertical distribution, yet validation of these retrievals against independent measurements remains limited. abstract: OBJECTIVE: Osteoarthritis-like rheumatoid arthritis (OA-like RA) is a clinical phenotype characterized by suppressed joint destruction and radiographic features mimicking OA, despite an underlying RA diagnosis. title: Driving Social‐Ecological Supply Chains Toward Circularity: A Delphi Study on Microfoundations of Transformative Capabilities
abstract: To remain competitive in turbulent business environments, modern supply chains must undergo radical and systemic transformations, such as moving toward circular supply chain configurations. abstract: COVID-19 pandemic has had far-reaching global impacts, prompting extensive research on its economic, social, technological, and health consequences. abstract: BACKGROUND: Sonication of explanted implants has improved microbiological detection in implant-associated infections. title: Innovación: Gobernabilidad y cambio institucional en la Universidad Autónoma de Nayarit durante el periodo 2000-2008
abstract: This paper is aimed at analyzing the process of change implemented at the Autonomous University of Nayarit resulting from the institutional reform undertaken in recent years. It places particular emphasis on the effects of this process in the governance of the institution. It brings to light the existing implications of change from a neo-institutionalist framework, and thus deals with power relations, conflict and institutional arrangements that were made in the study period. title: Entropia pós-colonial no Zumví Fotográfico (Salvador, Bahia)
abstract: This article examines the material and curatorial history of Zumví Fotográfico, a Black community archive in Salvador, Bahia. Drawing on fieldwork (2019–2025), 22 interviews, and visual analysis, it asks how the archive survived structural neglect. I develop “postcolonial entropy” to describe the cumulative material disorder produced when preservation depends on sustained improvisation rather than institutional support. title: Struggle for Freedom in Tiruchirappalli - A Historical Study
abstract: This article examines the role of Tiruchirappalli in India's freedom struggle during British rule. It highlights the contributions of local Congress leaders, political activists, students, and ordinary people in promoting the national movement. The study discusses important events such as the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Civil Disobedience Movement, the Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha, and the Quit India Movement of 1942. title: Development and Performance Evaluation of a Timer-Controlled Solar- Powered Drip Irrigation System for Smallholder Farmers
abstract: This study developed and evaluated a timer-controlled solar-powered drip irrigation system for smallholder farming. The system used an ESP32 microcontroller and DS3231 real-time clock to schedule irrigation across a 70-day cucumber growth cycle. Hydraulic performance was assessed using coefficient of uniformity (CU), emission uniformity (EU), coefficient of variation (CV) and flow variation (FV). Timer performance was evaluated across four growth stages by comparing actual and programmed irrigation durations. title: La calidad de las universidades públicas estatales en México desde la perspectiva de un multi-ranking
abstract: This paper develops a multi-ranking for public state universities in Mexi­co, it is elaborated blending three different rankings. This exercise conclu­des that is appropriate to advance in ins­truments to complement the institutional forms of evaluation. Using a multi-ran­king for university evaluation decreases the adverse effects of rankings as it asso­ciates purposes, methods, indicators and stakeholders in higher education. The multi-ranking works as an average of the rankings involved.

title: Bio-inspired nanotechnology for dengue vector control: Progress and prospects
abstract: The global resurgence of dengue fever due to Aedes aegypti has necessitated the development of innovative and potentially sustainable vector control strategies. Conventional methods that were initially effective now pose significant challenges, causing nuisance to the environment and public health with the resurgence of the vector. To overcome these challenges, the combination of natural products with nanotechnology offers a promising green alternative. title: Spatial Distribution and Phytoaccumulation of Lead in Soils and Plants Adjacent to Mining Areas in Surigao Del Norte
abstract: This study assessed the spatial distribution of lead (Pb) in soils and its accumulation in Saccharum spontaneum adjacent to a mining-affected area in Mainit, Surigao del Norte, Philippines. Using a quantitative field approach, soil and plant samples were purposively collected at 0, 50, and 200 m; Pb in soil extracts and roots, stems, and leaves was quantified using atomic absorption spectrophotometry. title: Modelling the excess mortality associated with heat waves in Hong Kong: 2014-2023
abstract: Background Heat waves have become increasingly frequent, and prior studies have linked them to elevated mortality risks in Hong Kong. However, estimates of the total excess mortality burden attributable to heat waves in Hong Kong remain limited. This study aimed to estimate excess mortality associated with heat waves in Hong Kong from 2014 to 2023. title: Effect of Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL) on Student’s Academic Achievement in Ecology Concepts in Gumel Education Zone Jigawa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the effect of Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL) on students’ academic achievement in Ecology concepts in Gumel Education Zone, Jigawa State, Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pretest and posttest control-group design was adopted. The study involved 146 SS II Biology students from two public co-educational secondary schools. title: Mobilizing in difficult times: student contention in post-2010 Turkey
abstract: This article examines how Turkish student movements have been reconfigured under deepening authoritarianism. Against the backdrop of a longer history of student activism, it focuses on the post-2010 period, tracing two sub-phases and the transition between them: an early-2010s reconfiguration of student contention and its resurgence in the early 2020s, when political repression and economic precarity intensified together. title: Saltbush ( Atriplex spp .), a Climate-Resilient Future Food Resource: Nutritional Potential, Functionality and Emerging Food Applications
abstract: Climate change, soil salinisation, and freshwater scarcity increasingly constrain conventional crop production, driving demand for climate-resilient food resources suited to marginal and saline land. Halophytes offer an untapped solution, and saltbush (Atriplex spp.), a genus of over 300 species with a history in Indigenous Australian and traditional diets, is emerging as a promising candidate for functional food development. title: Balancing nutrients and metal contaminants: sustainable land application rates for livestock manures in Ireland
abstract: Livestock manures are valuable nutrient sources for crop production, but variable composition and inappropriate application rates can cause nutrient imbalance, phosphorus accumulation and trace-metal loading, increasing the risks to water quality and the wider environment. This study evaluated manure-specific application rates by considering nutrient and trace-metal composition, crop requirements and soil phosphorus status. title: Beyond escape: psychological restoration, nostalgia, and meaning-making in domestic rural tourism destination in Indonesia
abstract: Understanding domestic tourists’ motivations for rural tourism requires moving beyond conventional Push-Pull Theory, which often treats motivations as static, decontextualized variables. Such approaches may overlook how tourist motivations are shaped by personal memory, identity, social relationships, and cultural contexts. Addressing this limitation, this study investigates how domestic tourists in Indonesia construct and experience their motivations for visiting rural tourism destinations and how internal and destination-based factors interact. title: An Indole‐3‐Acetic Acid‐Amido Synthetase, GmGH3.2, Negatively Regulates Salt Tolerance in Soybean
abstract: Soil salinization severely restricts soybean growth and productivity. Therefore, uncovering salt‐tolerance genes and their regulatory mechanisms is critical for breeding salt‐tolerant soybean varieties. In this study, a genome‐wide association study (GWAS) was conducted across four environments, and 7 quantitative trait locus (QTLs) associated with salt‐tolerance traits were identified. abstract: Trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh giữa các điểm đến du lịch, việc xây dựng thương hiệu điểm đến trở thành một yêu cầu chiến lược nhằm nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh và khẳng định vị thế điểm đến. title: Translation Pathways and Cultural Imagery Transmission of Plant and Animal Knowledge in Chu Ci: From the Perspective of Transknowletology
abstract: Transknowletology is an analytical perspective conceptualizing translation as the cross-linguistic processing, restructuring, and re-dissemination of knowledge. Within this framework, this paper explores the English translation pathways and cultural imagery transmission of plant and animal knowledge in Chu Ci. title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth's surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. title: Medical doctors’ perspective on the causes and measures to reduce medicine wastage in private clinics
abstract: Medicine wastage in private clinics constitutes a healthcare, economic, supply chain, and environmental challenge. This study explores private medical doctors’ perspectives on the causes of medicine wastage in Hong Kong clinics and identifies contextually relevant measures for reducing it. A qualitative design was adopted, comprising semi-structured interviews with eight private medical doctors, and the data were analysed thematically. title: Narrating Veteran Trauma, Suicide, and the State: From the Korean War to the War on Terror
abstract: Since 1980, when posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) was included for the first time in the third edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-III), stigmatized notions of shell shock and combat fatigue have given way to broader and more nuanced clinical understandings and greater public awareness of veterans’ mental health struggles. title: Multi-season evaluation of red rice accessions for resistance to the rice leaffolder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis) and associated oviposition preference and larval leaf-folding behaviour
abstract: The rice leaffolder, Cnaphalocrocis medinalis (Guenee), is a major foliar pest of rice that can cause considerable yield losses, highlighting the need to identify stable sources of host plant resistance for its effective and sustainable management. Therefore, in the present study, 50 red rice accessions and two standard checks, TKM6 (resistant) and TN1 (susceptible), were evaluated for resistance to C. medinalis under field conditions across 3 seasons (kharif 2022, kharif 2023, rabi 2023–24). title: “They Are Not Here for the Camera”: Community-level strategies for building climate‑resilient health systems in response to floods in Uganda
abstract: Climate-related shocks pose challenges to community health systems. Limited evidence exists on how to build resilience in these systems, especially regarding governance and community engagement and involvement (CEI). This study examined how communities in flood-prone Uganda enhance community health system resilience. title: Detection and Statistics of Large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the heliospheric current sheet (HCS), heliospheric plasma sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the SBCross catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1076 SBC events derived from in situ observations spanning more than 30 yr (1995–2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. title: Transcriptomics of C3+CAM Peperomia species reveals potential initial steps toward a CAM pathway
abstract: The genus Peperomia (family Piperaceae) is the only known lineage with Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) in the Magnoliids. Previous studies have demonstrated C 3 +CAM in multiple Peperomia species, yet there are ~ 1,600 species in the genus and very few have been assessed for CAM. Further, no studies have used genomics to understand CAM evolution in the Magnoliids. title: Stakeholder perspectives on incentives and misalignments in prospective sustainable ship recycling: The Finnish maritime cluster
abstract: Ship recycling can recover substantial material and component value from end-of-life vessels, but responsible dismantling also requires strict environmental, safety, and waste management standards. These requirements may improve sustainability performance while increasing the costs and risks borne by the actors responsible for end-of-life decisions. abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important cause of preventable stroke in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic and treatment gaps may limit screening effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate AF screening in LMICs as a screening-to-anticoagulation pathway, focusing on reach, equity, diagnostic confirmation, anticoagulation uptake, and health-system capacity. abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the physicochemical and microbiological quality of honey marketed in the urban commune of Macenta (Guinea). A total of twenty-six (26) honey samples were collected and analyzed using standardized methods. Physicochemical results showed that moisture content ranged from 14.09% to 17.95%, generally complying with the recommended limit (<18%), indicating good storage stability. abstract: Water use efficiency (WUE) links carbon assimilation and water loss and is an important indicator of ecosystem functioning under changing hydroclimatic conditions. Process-based land surface models (LSMs) provide a framework for simulating carbon-water interactions, but their ability to reproduce ecosystem-scale WUE across contrasting climates remains insufficiently evaluated. abstract: Driven by the imbalance between nutrient discharge and availability of natural resources, there is a growing need for sustainable strategies for managing wastewater. Nutrient recovery from domestic wastewater through struvite crystallization presents one such efficient and circular technology for recovering nutrients and producing fertilizer. title: Bacteriological and Physicochemical Quality Assessment of Drinking Water from Water Storage Tanks of National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), During Pre-Monsoon and Monsoon Seasons
abstract: Water is essential for life, but it is being polluted at a significant rate. The current study aimed to assess the drinking water quality in storage tanks at the National University of Sciences and Technology in Islamabad, Pakistan over six months, including pre-monsoon and monsoon seasons. Various physico- chemical parameters were tested including residual chlorine, total dissolved solids (TDS), total suspended solids (TSS), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, turbidity, alkalinity, hardness and electrical conductivity (EC). title: The Effect of Fermented Monosodium Glutamate Waste as a Feed Supplement on Feed Efficiency. Growth. and Survival of Tilapia Fingerlings (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is a freshwater commodity with high economic value; however. its growth performance is often constrained by low feed efficiency. One potential approach to improve feed utilization is the supplementation of fermented monosodium glutamate (MSG) waste. which contains protein and amino acids and can be classified as a single-cell protein (SCP) source. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of fermented MSG waste supplementation on feed utilization efficiency and growth rate of tilapia fingerlings. title: The Cameroon Anglophone Crisis and the Dynamics of Internally Displaced Anglophone Population in the City of Douala (2016–2024)
abstract: One of the tragedies of the peaceful protest by lawyers, teachers, and university students in the Anglophone Northwest and Southwest regions of Cameroon that started on October 12, 2016, has been the displacement of people from both urban and rural areas within the two regions in crisis, to the Francophone regions of the country. title: Development of Guidelines for Organizing Youth Basketball Competitions in Qinghai Province, the People’s Republic of China
abstract: Background and Aims: The main problem in organizing youth basketball competitions in Qinghai Province is the lack of an integrated, effective management system. Compared with more developed regions domestically and internationally, where public–private collaboration, coach evaluation systems, and school–club networks are well established, Qinghai faces shortages of qualified coaches, inadequate infrastructure, limited funding, and fragmented management. title: Real-time embedded control and performance evaluation of BLDC motors for electric vehicle applications
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are central to modern electric vehicle (EV) drivetrains, yet achieving high efficiency and stable torque under dynamic conditions remains a significant engineering challenge. This study presents the design and real-time embedded implementation of a motor control system realised on the STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller, together with a hardware-parameterised performance characterisation used to evaluate and cross-validate its behaviour. abstract: Validated age-based life history traits are crucial towards understanding the biological complexity of the natural world. The blue sucker Cycleptus elongatus is a migratory freshwater fish of the family Catostomidae native to North America. For decades, there has been conservation concern for the species across much of its range, including populations with skewed size distributions indicative of recruitment bottlenecks. abstract: Since the early 1990s New Zealand has seen law reforms and new legislation to improve the rights of LGBTQIA+ New Zealanders. title: Performance evaluation of face mask: from textile filtration determination to air leakage minimization
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic emphasized the critical role of face masks in preventing the transmission of respiratory viruses, especially in medical settings. Respiratory viruses, including SARS, influenza, and adenoviruses are primarily transmitted through the respiratory pathways, making face masks the primary barrier for protection. This study aims to evaluate and compare the filtration efficiency and pressure differentials of different face masks to contribute to the development of a comprehensive test bench for medical textiles. title: Economic deprivation, mental health, and educational justice: challenges of an open educational model for all in university students from vulnerable areas of Los Cabos, Baja California Sur
abstract: This study analyzes the structural barriers faced by university students from vulnerable areas of Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, when entering higher education. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research examines how economic deprivation, reflected in insufficient income, precarious employment, and technological gaps, severely affects young people’s mental health, generating anxiety, stress, and critical levels of self-efficacy that compromise their academic performance and retention. title: Characterizing clinical heterogeneity by whole-genome sequencing of 591 patients with Hemoglobin H disease
abstract: Hemoglobin H (Hb H) disease, caused by the functional loss in three of the four α-globin genes, exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity that is not fully explained by primary α-globin genotypes. abstract: In this interview with Kalli Anderson and Eleanor McDowall, they explain the reason for their new project called A Library out of Air. abstract: Amidst a global landscape characterised by the convergence of geopolitical risks and green trade barriers, CATL has overcome geopolitical barriers through its Light Asset technology licensing model, built compliance competitiveness through zero-carbon and smart manufacturing, promoted collaborative global expansion across the industrial chain, and achieved deep localisation. abstract: The evolution of Kurdish politics in Turkey reveals a significant shift through the post-na tionalist and intersectional strategy adopted by the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP), which positions itself within a broader democratic and inclusive movement. Rather than reinforc ing ethnic or national divisions, the HDP has sought to transcend them by forging coalitions with left-wing, feminist, ecological, and minority-based movements. abstract: This study investigates the feasibility of using bamboo powder as a partial replacement for fine aggregate in paving block production. Bamboo powder was incorporated at replacement levels of 0%, 30%, 35%, and 40% by weight of sand. abstract: This study provides an in-depth analysis of the evolution of the Moroccan educational system through the lens of Education for Sustainable Development. title: Rebel Governance and the Limits of Statebuilding: Civilian-based Legitimacy in Turkey’s Kurdish Cities
abstract: How do civilians sustain rebel legitimacy under repression? Using interviews and digital ethnography in Turkey's Kurdish cities, this article develops a dual-pathway framework of civilian-based legitimacy. Legitimacy emerges from ideational (feminism, resistance, Kurdish identity) and institutional (municipal services, organizations) pathways. title: Kū and Lono, Neither One nor Many: Divine Identity and the Hard Case of Cook in Hoʻomana Hawaiʻi
abstract: In January 1779, Hawaiians are reported to have received Captain James Cook as Lono, a god said to return each year from a distant homeland. Scholars have argued for decades over what actually happened there and what Hawaiians believed while it was happening. This article sets that historical question aside and asks a different one: what would it mean for a claim like "Cook is Lono" to be true at all? title: Identidades cruzadas: género, sexualidad y religión en el Derecho internacional contemporáneo. Necesidad de una comprensión holística
abstract: La libertad de pensamiento conciencia o creencias como pilares fundamentales del marco internacional de los derechos humanos debe reconocerse a las personas LGTBIQ+. En ese acceso a la espiritualidad, las autoridades religiosas, Estados, gobiernos y demás instituciones tienen la responsabilidad de garantizar que la religión no constituya un instrumento de justificación de la violencia y la discriminación «justa» bajo los postulados tradicionales. Las identidades de género, sexual y religiosa deben integrarse y equilibrarse como un todo en el derecho al desarrollo de la personalidad y dignidad

title: Food system sustainability and agricultural water-related constraints in arid Central Asia: A multidimensional country-level assessment
abstract: The contributions of agricultural water-related indicators to long-term food system sustainability remain insufficiently quantified in arid Central Asia. This study assessed national-scale food system sustainability in the five Central Asian countries during 2000–2023 using a 22-indicator environmental–economic–social framework integrating global entropy weighting, additive index decomposition, and obstacle degree analysis. abstract: The Qimeigan area in the southwestern Tarim Basin contains multiple potential source intervals and records multistage hydrocarbon charging followed by tectonic modification. This study integrates biomarker data from five Carboniferous source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1 and two from Well Qiqian-2), 11 Qipan Formation source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1, three from Well Qiqian-1, and five from Well Kuntan-1), and three Kangkelin Formation reservoir-rock extracts from Well Shatan-1. title: Impact of artificial gravity on spaceflight-induced skeletal deterioration in male mice
abstract: Spaceflight-induced bone loss may increase the risk of fracture during long-duration missions. Exposure to artificial gravity (AG) of 1 G by centrifugation has been shown to prevent spaceflight-associated bone loss in mice. However, whether lower levels of AG can prevent skeletal deterioration during spaceflight is unknown. Young adult (11 weeks) male C57Bl/6 J mice were exposed to microgravity (µG) or AG (0.33 G, 0.67 G, or 1 G) via centrifugation during a 30-day mission on the International Space Station ( n = 5-6/group). abstract: Although higher education institutions (HEIs) in Uganda are supposed to be the heartbeat of national transformation by serving as nursery beds for innovations, testbeds for policies, hubs for technology development and training grounds for both prospective public servants and in-service civil servants, they are challenged for being unresponsive. abstract: The phrase “Do it for the plot” was recently coined by the actress and influencer Serena Kerrigan in a viral TikTok video where she urged viewers to remember that “if something works out, great, and if it doesn't, it's for the plot.” She explained that: “Do it for the plot” is an extension of the idea of being the main character of one's life (…). abstract: This paper aims to elaborate on a philosophical split between two explanatory strategies in Cognitive Semantics: Semantic Gestalt Theories (SGT) and Usage Statistical Models (USM). abstract: Vegetables co‑products, such as leaves and stems that are discarded in the field or during early processing, represent underexplored food sources, with relevant potential for plant‑based fermentations. This study evaluated the ability of a set of lactic acid bacteria and yeast, including strains selected based on the autochthonous microbiota of the plant substrates, to grow on plant‑derived substrates under different salt conditions (0.3-1.0%), namely on co‑products collected across three production and processing stages: primary production, primary processing, and minimal processing. title: Analytical quality by design for electrochemical nanostructured screen-printed sensor development: uric acid detection in saliva for diagnosis and monitoring of chronic diseases
abstract: The aim of this study is to develop an electrochemical sensor to determine uric acid levels in saliva, with the ultimate goal of designing a rapid, sensitive and non-invasive diagnostic device. To this end, easy-to-manufacture, disposable graphite screen-printed electrodes (GSPEs) were used as transducers, as they can be easily applied for a rapid, in situ analysis. title: Genome-wide association analyses reveal genomics basis for frizzled feather and candidate genes associated with growth traits in Yuexi frizzled feather chicken
abstract: BACKGROUND: Yuexi Frizzled Feather Chicken (YFC), an indigenous chicken breed in Western Guangdong of China (Yuexi region), is well known for its great adaptability and excellent tolerance to the high temperature and high humidity climates due to its frizzled feather characteristics. In order to investigate the genomic structure and genetic markers of frizzled feather in YFC, we conducted a genome wide analysis study (GWAS) for feather types using the whole genome resequencing data from 356 YFC and 85 non-frizzled feather chickens. title: Modified white LEDs spectra alter tomato seedling quality and post-transplant responses
abstract: This study evaluated tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) seedling responses to three white-light-emitting diodes (LEDs) spectra and assessed post-transplant performance in a commercial greenhouse. The treatments were normal white light (NW), normal white light supplemented with red light (NWR), and a specific white-plus-red spectrum (SWR). All treatments delivered 275 ± 5 µmol m −2 s −1 for 20 d, with blue emission peaks at 450 nm in NW and NWR and 436 nm in SWR. title: Facile Chemical Reduction Synthesis of Cu/Cu₂O Nanostructures: From Spherical Nanoparticles to Anisotropic Nanorods
abstract: Copper nanostructures are promising inexpensive substitutes for noble-metal nanomaterials. However, controlling their phase purity and morphology is challenging due to the facile oxidation of metallic copper during synthesis and storage. In this work, the effect of the amount of reducing agent on the phase composition and morphology of the copper nanostructures prepared by chemical reduction was investigated. abstract: Excipient functionality influences tablet quality, dose consistency, drug release, and the potential affordability of medicines. Green banana starch (GBS) has favorable hydration and swelling properties, whereas natural gums can provide binding and contribute to the mechanical strength of the tablet. However, each material has limitations when used alone for direct compression. abstract: Most of the population globally lives in areas exceeding prior and current WHO guidelines for fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), highlighting the persisting need for implementing emission reduction strategies. Given the complex transport and transformation processes that airborne species undergo in the atmosphere, chemical transport models can aid in designing and prioritizing air pollution mitigation actions. title: Tracing the Evolution of Dalit Consciousness under Hindutva Politics: A Comparative Study of Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat
abstract: The state of Gujarat described as “Laboratory of Today’s India” by Jaffrelot presents an intriguing puzzle wherein it has championed economic liberalization while simultaneously witnessing the rise of political illiberalism. Despite its historical association with entrepreneurial success and economic modernization, developmentalism and secularism have receded. Rather being a constitutionally secular state, its subjective practicality gave rise to right wing politics. title: Portland Limestone Cement for durable low carbon infrastructure concrete
abstract: Portland Limestone Cement (PLC), designated as Type IL under ASTM C595/C595M and Type GUL under CSA A3001, is now a mainstream clinker-reduction strategy for concrete infrastructure. Because the performance of commercial PLC containing up to 15% limestone is already well established, the principal question is no longer whether such cements can replace Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) under routine conditions, but how durability specifications, higher-limestone formulations, and multicomponent systems should evolve without sacrificing service life. title: Statistically Based Determination of Partial Safety Factors for FRP Bars
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) bars used as internal reinforcement in concrete structures have gained renewed interest in recent years, primarily due to their high durability, particularly in aggressive environmental conditions. The adoption of FRP bars as an alternative to steel reinforcement effectively mitigates corrosion-related deterioration; however, it also raises concerns regarding the reliability and safety assessment of nonmetallic reinforcement systems. title: Kinematics of the Eastern Kunlun Fault Revealed by Viscoelastic Earthquake‐Cycle Deformation Modeling Constrained by InSAR and GNSS Observations
abstract: The eastern Kunlun fault (KLF) accommodates significant deformation and the seismic gap around the Maqin–Maqu poses substantial seismic hazards, yet its slip rates and locking depths, thus the earthquake potential, remain controversial. We integrate InSAR and GNSS observations to construct a horizontal surface velocity field in a regional‐average local reference frame. abstract: Los costos de no calidad reducen la eficiencia de las empresas bananeras al convertir fruta cosechada en pérdidas dentro de la empacadora. Este estudio estimó los costos de no calidad por fallas internas en tres fincas de San Felipe S.A. abstract: Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. abstract: The paper gives an overview on escalating limitations on freedom of assembly and freedom of speech in Germany, starting with the COVID pandemic. Broad and massive limitations on freedom of assembly during the pandemic found a ‘follow-up’ in the policing of Palestine protests since October 7, 2023 until to date. abstract: The 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, ZB, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. abstract: In this study, it is aimed to evaluate the phytochemical properties and antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities of the methanol extract obtained from the roots of Astragalus aureus Willd., as well as the hexane, chloroform, ethyl acetate, and aqueous methanol fractions. Additionally, the phenolic components of the most active fraction were characterized using the bioactivity-guided approach with LC–MS/MS, and the amount of Astragaloside IV was determined using the HPTLC method. abstract: BACKGROUND: Pooled DNA genotyping has gained increasing attention in recent decades due to its potential to substantially reduce genotyping costs and its applications in identifying trait-associated DNA markers and estimating parental contributions to pooled offspring samples. However, accurately estimating parental contributions from pooled offspring genotype data remains a major challenge in selective breeding. title: VIOLENCE AGAINST HAZARA IN PAKISTAN: HISTORICAL PERSECUTION, INTERNATIONAL IDENTITY, AND SOCIO-POLITICAL VULNERABILITIES
abstract: The Hazara community, an ethnic group often marginalized and oppressed, has experienced ongoing violence and discrimination due to their unique physical features that distinguish them from the majority populations in Quetta and Pakistan. Over the past century, the Hazara people have endured severe persecution, particularly during the atrocities of the 1890s in Afghanistan and the Taliban's widespread violence in the 1990s. title: Histopathological and Immunological Impact of Glutaraldehyde Fume Inhalation on the Lungs of Albino Rats
abstract: Glutaraldehyde is widely used as a high-level disinfectant for heat-sensitive medical instruments and as a tissue fixative in histopathology, and the workers who handle it can inhale its fumes. Evidence on how prolonged inhalation affects the deeper lung remains limited. This study evaluated the histopathological and immunological effects of glutaraldehyde fume inhalation on the lungs of albino rats across increasing exposure durations.
