abstract: In the high-andean zone of Peru, the concrete structures are exposed to adverse conditions that can affect its durability and resistance, due to the fact that they tend to deteriorate over time; therefore, it is necessary to periodically perform a quality evaluation of the material with the purpose to guarantee the safety in the service requests. title: First assessment of population size, population dynamics, and carrying capacity of free-roaming dogs in Karaj, Iran
abstract: Dogs (Canis familiaris) were the first animals domesticated by humans, likely in Eurasia between 20,000-40,000 years ago, and remain deeply integrated into human societies. However, in many countries, free-roaming dog populations have expanded due to uncontrolled reproduction, abandonment, and widespread supplemental feeding. In Iran, scientific assessments of these populations are scarce despite growing ecological, social, and public health concerns. title: Nutritional profiling of turmeric rhizomes and development of a ready-to-mix curry powder
abstract: The development of functional foods from nutrient-rich turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) requires the identification of superior genotypes with enhanced bioactive compounds and validated health benefits. This study evaluated 10 elite turmeric genotypes for 16 biochemical traits, including proximate composition, mineral nutrients, curcumin content and antioxidant activity. The study was conducted at the Horticultural Research Station, Lam, Guntur District, Andhra Pradesh, during the year 2022–23. title: Electrified nutrient manufacturing from waste streams
abstract: Nutrient recovery from wastes is commonly judged by removal or mass-recovery efficiency, but these metrics do not establish that the recovered material is a safe, consistent, agronomically effective fertilizer that displaces a conventional product. Electrified nutrient manufacturing is developed here as a product-first framework that links heterogeneous waste streams with selective separation, concentration, conversion, finishing, qualification, agricultural use, and verified substitution. title: Log-To-Leak: Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents via the Model Context Protocol
abstract: LLM agents increasingly access external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), but the natural-language metadata used to describe those tools creates a prompt-injection surface. Within this established tool-poisoning surface, we study Log-To-Leak, an additive post-hoc logging attack that induces a separate attacker-controlled call after the final legitimate call. title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $σ$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
abstract: Safety benchmarks for computer-use agents (CUAs) place the harm either in the intent of the task or on a single screen: a malicious instruction, an injected command, a phishing page. An agent that checks the task and each screen in isolation can pass them, so they do not test whether it combines facts seen on different screens. Yet in delegated work, harm often arises exactly this way: a fact about a person on one screen, a fact about an item on another, and a legitimate task that binds them. title: Can you make models believe false facts in the prompt?
abstract: Making LLMs believe false facts is useful for alignment evaluations and for building model organisms. Previous work explored doing so with Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF). But SDF requires fine-tuning one new model for each set of injected false beliefs. To enable larger scale SDF-powered alignment evaluations, we attempt to produce a single model that believes any fact placed in a tag in the prompt. title: Decisions at the end of the world
abstract: International treaties are often described as tigers without teeth, failing to secure compliance or change outcomes. Cooperation also depends on how states maintain the rules they have already made -- especially where no sovereign stands above the states. Here we map more than six decades of decision-making under the Antarctic Treaty, linking submitted proposals to recorded responses and tracing how instruments act on earlier ones. title: PixelBench: Evaluating Language Models for Pixel-Art Creation
abstract: Pixel art is widely used in games and digital content creation, requiring readable forms, coherent spatial relationships, and harmonious colors under limited resolution and palette constraints. Language models show growing promise in visual creation, yet their pixel art creation capabilities lack systematic evaluation. We introduce PixelBench, formalizing text-to-image generation and instruction-guided editing for pixel art and providing a benchmark for these tasks. title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Plücker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. title: Evaluating safeguarding in multi-turn conversations with AI assistants
abstract: Conversational AI assistants are now used for personal and emotional support. Developers report improvements in how new models respond to sensitive conversations, yet users and civil society continue to raise concerns about their behaviour in real-world, repeated interactions that safety evaluations rarely capture. Often, evaluations present signs of distress clearly and in a single message, even though people may reveal their struggles gradually in otherwise ordinary conversations. title: AMISS: An Integrity Framework for Magnetic Navigation
abstract: Magnetic Navigation (MagNav) is a promising alternative to traditional systems like Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), offering resistance to jamming or spoofing attacks to which the latter are vulnerable. MagNav matches scalar magnetic measurements over time against a known map of Earth's magnetic anomaly in order to position a vehicle. MagNav is therefore sensitive to the quality of these maps, especially to errors in the survey data that the maps are derived from. title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases
abstract: Ice-cloud retrievals from polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter radiometry commonly assume random orientation, horizontal alignment or a prescribed flutter angle. We link the orientation dynamics of ice crystals to their scattering. Fluid-inertial torque turns small settling crystals broadside on, and turbulent velocity gradients turn them away, so their orientation depends on the dissipation rate. title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring
abstract: Remote wildlife monitoring increasingly depends on high-fidelity cameras and sensors deployed far from grid power and terrestrial networks. Low Earth orbit satellite links can provide connectivity in these settings, but their high power draw and variable bandwidth, combined with intermittent on-site solar harvesting, make continuous backhaul infeasible. abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
abstract: To find a $k$-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all $2^n$ subsets of the $n$ vertices, although only the subsets of size $k$ can be answers. title: The ratio of gradient-flow scales $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ in $2+1$ flavor lattice QCD
abstract: We determine the ratio $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0$ of gradient-flow scales in isospin-symmetric $2+1$-flavor QCD at the physical point and in the continuum limit. Our analysis uses CLS gauge ensembles at five lattice spacings and combines Wilson and Zeuthen flow data to constrain the continuum extrapolation at the flavor-SU(3)-symmetric point. We obtain $\sqrt{t_0}/w_0=0.8264(26)$ in the Edinburgh consensus scheme, corresponding to a precision of about $0.31\%$. title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied. abstract: Consensus lets institutions decide without a central authority, but a record of agreement reveals neither its basis nor its credibility. We model support, standing aside and veto as responses to a proposal. A proposal can pass without active support, and the member least willing to allow passage limits what can be adopted, however many members oppose the proposal. title: Cleaning the NTP Pool: Detecting and Mitigating NTP-sourced IPv6 Scanning
abstract: The ephemeral and random nature of IPv6 client addresses presents a practical challenge to attacks that depend on Internet-wide scanning or reconnaissance – the adversary must first find the client's IPv6 address. While a well-positioned passive adversary can potentially harvest some active IPv6 client addresses, such power is typically reserved for e.g., large CDNs or Internet exchange points. In contrast, prior work has shown the ease with which a low-power entity can join the volunteer-based NTP Pool and harvest large quantities of active IPv6 client addresses. title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. title: FinVerify: A Verification Framework for Financial Agents
abstract: Financial agents produce numerical claims that can be wrong even when their calculations execute correctly, due to mismatched reporting periods, unsupported sources, incompatible units, or incorrect financial definitions. We introduce FinVerify, an evidence-grounded framework for verifying financial agents' numerical claims. title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
abstract: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_η(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-η_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. title: A statistical study of ionized outflows in low-mass galaxies from DESI DR1
abstract: We present a statistical analysis of ionized gas outflows in a large sample of low-mass ($\mathrm{log(M_{*}/M_{\odot})\lesssim10}$) galaxies at $z<0.45$ from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). title: Calibration of LHAASO-WCDA Energy Scale using Cosmic Ray Moon Shadow
abstract: Cosmic-ray particles in the TeV range, originating outside the solar system, are partially blocked on their way to Earth by the Moon, producing a deficit in their flux known as the Moon shadow. This work presents a precision measurement of the westward shift of the Moon's shadow using 3.4 years of data from LHAASO's Water Cherenkov Detector Array (WCDA). abstract: The tripolar ORCA family of ocean model grids, widely used in the NEMO community, employs a semi-analytic curvilinear coordinate system north of approximately 20° N to avoid the geographic polar singularity. abstract: The ocean supports the biosphere and human well-being but is increasingly threatened by global change. abstract: Shipping is the primary source of underwater noise pollution, yet its impacts on marine biodiversity remain unquantified in Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA). This study presents the first framework for quantifying the regionalized impact of ship noise on marine mammal biodiversity within LCIA, demonstrated for European Seas. Ship noise data from the NAVISON project for 2019 were combined with species-specific sensitivity thresholds for marine mammals to derive spatially explicit Potentially Affected Fractions (PAF). abstract: Atmospheric and oceanic phenomena in the Pacific Ocean, such as the North Pacific Gyre Oscillation (NPGO) and the Victoria Mode (VM), have significant implications for global climate variability through their linkage with temperature variability in the Central Pacific (CP). title: Abrupt Shifts in Subpolar Gyre Deep Convection Under Pre‐Industrial Climate Conditions
abstract: Recent observations indicate two distinct drivers of interrupted winter convection in the Labrador Sea: anomalous atmospheric forcing and the advection of freshwater anomalies. Here we test whether these mechanisms arise spontaneously under stationary pre‐industrial climate conditions using six medium to high‐resolution CMIP6 control simulations. abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Seabirds feed on prey patches structured by physical and biological oceanography, foraging alone or in groups. However, it is unclear whether habitat selection varies with the degree of sociality. abstract: We study a random chemostat modelling the growth of the gut microbiome, in which the microbiota is split into a planktonic (luminal) and a wall–attached (mucosa–adherent) compartment, nutrient uptake follows a Monod response, and dead biomass is remineralised in a mass–consistent way. title: Historical and projected changes in tropical North and South Atlantic indices under different emission scenarios
abstract: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability in the Tropical North Atlantic (TNA) and Tropical South Atlantic (TSA) plays a critical role in regulating regional climate systems, atmospheric circulation, and hydrological extremes. However, uncertainties remain regarding the representation of tropical Atlantic SST variability and future warming patterns in CMIP6 climate models. This study investigated historical and projected SST anomaly characteristics over the TNA and TSA using NOAA ERSSTv5 observational data (1982--2014) and seven CMIP6 models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios (1967--2099).

title: Chemical Recycling of Acrylonitrile–Butadiene–Styrene (ABS) via Nitrile Reduction and Imine Vitrimer Formation
abstract: As plastic consumption accelerates, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) remains a major waste contributor because of its widespread use and limited recyclability. Here, we report a closed-loop chemical recycling strategy in which a boron catalyst selectively reduces ABS nitrile groups to generate amine-functional ABS (AFABS), followed by dynamic imine cross-linking with glutaraldehyde to form an imine-based vitrimer (v-IBS). title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
abstract: Whether the recent poleward migration of tropical cyclones (TCs) reflects anthropogenic warming or natural variability remains unresolved. title: A Scenario-Based Probabilistic First-Tier Screening of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
abstract: Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. title: Licensing the future: Petroleum regulation in a time of climate breakdown
abstract: This article examines petroleum licensing in the United Kingdom as a regulatory practice through which fossil fuel futures are modified, perpetuated, and deferred in a time of accelerating climate breakdown. Amidst demands for an end to oil, the UK government’s support for oil and gas extraction has remained ambivalent. title: Sulfur photochemistry traces mantle redox states of rocky planets
abstract: Volatile outgassing from planetary interiors controls the composition of rocky exoplanets' secondary atmospheres. title: Economic viability of floating offshore wind in Portugal with varying market conditions and financial support mechanisms
abstract: This study assesses the economic viability of commercial-scale floating offshore wind farms in Portugal under a range of contract for difference (CfD) mechanisms. A techno-economic model simulated financial revenues using synthetic time wind and spot price data, under varying CfD mechanisms and metocean conditions for 36 sites off the Portuguese coastline. abstract: Auditory masking, where the perception of a target sound is reduced by the presence of another, non-target sound, occurs when both sounds fall within the same critical band. In other words, the masking sound falls within the auditory filter bandwidth that is centered on the target sound’s frequency. abstract: Reconciling economic development with aquatic wildlife conservation remains difficult in heavily urbanized rivers. abstract: Mesoamerican seasonally dry tropical forests (SDTFs) are floristically differentiated, spatially discontinuous and affected by Quaternary climatic change; yet, effects on long‐term suitability, refugial persistence and environmental connectivity remain unresolved. We assessed whether climatic oscillations over the last 800 ka altered the extent and connectivity of suitable SDTF areas more strongly than core position (areas of high climatic suitability). abstract: The Heinrich Stadial 1 (HS1) interval (18–14.6 kyr BP) is regarded as a pivotal window for exploring the underlying temperature dynamics. abstract: Whether extreme climate events reflect intrinsic threshold behaviour of the climate system remains uncertain, in part because most terrestrial archives integrate multiple climatic signals and lack simultaneous constraints on temperature and hydroclimate. abstract: Offshore wind-to-hydrogen production is one of the key technologies for China to achieve deep decarbonization. The various stakeholders within the offshore wind-to-hydrogen production chain (wind power companies, hydrogen producers, and government policymakers) form a highly complex multi-stakeholder collaborative system. title: Influence of crack width on corrosion of steel fibres in cracked shotcrete tunnel linings
abstract: Fibre Reinforced Shotcrete (FRS) is widely used to construct linings for ground support in both civil tunnels and mines. Many linings incorporate steel fibres as reinforcement to provide tensile strength across cracks that may form in the linings as a result of, for example, drying shrinkage, ground instability, or frost heave. abstract: The global warming trend of near-surface temperature varies at regional and temporal scales. abstract: Freshwater diatom diversity remains unevenly documented across the Neotropics, limiting assessments of regional biodiversity and biogeographic patterns. abstract: Recorded in Flores, the Azores’ westernmost island and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, this fieldwork recording explores imaginaries of nature through listening. abstract: L'érosion côtière peut être abordée à travers l'évolution mesurée du trait de côte et la perception qu'en ont les riverains. abstract: O propósito deste boletim é disponibilizar as principais informações hidroclimáticas atualizadas sobre as principais variáveis que influenciam no padrão climático no Estado do Amazonas. abstract: This paper extends and formulates the Green’s Functions Differential Transform Element Method (GFDTEM) for the static analysis of linearly elastic axially non-uniform beams and piles modeled according to Timoshenko beam theory on spatially varying Winkler foundations. abstract: Under what conditions can middle powers translate control over strategic resources into political influence? This article examines Australia's uranium diplomacy between 1973 and 2013, integrating middle-power theory and economic statecraft to distinguish diplomatic influence, institutional influence and behavioural leverage. A high-purity germanium (HPGe) γ-ray spectrometer and scintillation-cell radon detector were adopted to measure the activity concentrations of 232 Th, 40 K and gaseous 222 Rn in granite, surface sediment and ambient air across 11 sampling sites covering crater core, crater rim and outer rim zones. abstract: This paper presents a newly discovered Cypro-Minoan inscription incised on the rim of a Cypriot pithos from Pyla-Kokkinokremos, a short-lived harbour settlement dated to the end of the 13th to the early 12th cent. abstract: Balanced nutrient management is a major concern in the present-day scenario, especially in soils of arid regions, which are low in soil fertility; hence, supplementation of sulphur (S) helps in plant growth and maintenance of soil health. The use of amino acids as biostimulants has gained widespread importance in recent times. abstract: Thermal pollution from industrial activities has become an important environmental problem. In order to evaluating potential environmental impacts, a one-dimensional advection-diffusion model was developed. The transport behavior of thermal pollution in the Brisbane River under different seasonal conditions is investigated. abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionization (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilization. abstract: This paper presents an optimal control framework for nonlinear systems with noise using Hamiltonian-based discretisation to enhance the approximation of stochastic differential equations. abstract: The total electron content observations during the Artemis‐II Lunar mission revealed rare ionospheric perturbations occurring at three different occasions. abstract: Context Alpine ecosystems are highly vulnerable to climate change, with rising temperatures and altered precipitation posing increasing challenges to cold-adapted mountain ungulates. How these species adjust their behaviour to cope with short-term adverse weather conditions remains poorly understood. title: International transport corridors and entrepreneurial dynamics: A quasi-natural experiment on the China Railway Express
abstract: A central question for transport policy is whether major transnational infrastructure can generate transformative economic impacts beyond its core logistics function. This paper examines the China-Europe Railway Express (CERE) as a quasi-natural experiment to assess its role as an external enabler of urban entrepreneurship. abstract: La humanidad enfrenta problemas bien conocidos derivados del cambio climático: sequía, calor extremo, pérdida de suelos y ecosistemas y enfermedades. abstract: Este artículo analiza cómo los orígenes del cumplimiento específico han determinado que haya sido irrazonablemente marginalizado, estableciendo limitaciones que socavan los intereses de la parte acreedora. abstract: This paper examines the film Odyssey (2026) by British filmmaker Christopher Nolan, analyzing the role of adapting a classic literary work for high-resolution, technically complex cinema. It discusses the filmmaker's creative freedom to interpret the original work, adapting it to the social context of his time and his own unique vision of the classic text. abstract: We present three multi-week, disc-integrated James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) campaigns monitoring HDO and SO2 absorption in Venus’ upper mesosphere at altitudes of approximately 80–110 km. We investigated the spatial and temporal distribution of the exotic spider Oecobius navus in relation to physical, trophic, and microclimatic variables in a Neotropical limestone cave. title: Cluster roots enhance phosphorus acquisition and may reduce fertilizer requirements through grafting and intercropping
abstract: Upon low phosphorus (P) availability, some plants develop specialized cluster roots that enhance P acquisition. Yet, the extent to which cluster roots contribute to plant P uptake and reduce external P fertilizer requirements remains poorly understood. This study mapped and analyzed surface displacement using differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR). abstract: Saliva is a readily accessible, non-invasively collected biofluid, increasingly recognized as a potential liquid biopsy for the diagnosis and monitoring of oral diseases. However, reliable assessment of disease biomarkers remains challenging, as their concentrations often lie at or below the analytical detection limits, and available volumes may be insufficient for accurate analysis. abstract: The article examines the textual contents, composition and historical background of a Latin–Low German Ex quo vocabulary manuscript preserved in the Tallinn City Archives. It aims to reconstruct the process of its compilation, identify its distinctive textual features, and assess its function within the religious and educational landscape of late medieval Estonia. title: The Limit of Nature: Thucydides and the Politics of Theory
abstract: This article reconsiders Thucydides’s role as a foundational theorist of human nature. abstract: Sugar production was one of the most significant industrial activities in eastern Andalusia during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. abstract: Stress influences memory not only for the stressful event itself but also for neutral events encoded nearby in time, with important implications for eyewitness testimony and clinical contexts. Previous research has generally assumed that stress uniformly affects temporally adjacent information. abstract: This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. title: The compressible-incompressible CAO problem introduced by Lions, Temam and Wang
abstract: We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. In this article, we prove for the first time the strong well-posedness of the coupled compressible-incompressible system both locally and globally for small initial data.

title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method for Mean Field Games on Scattered Point Clouds
abstract: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. title: Network-based modeling of cocaine trafficking flows and displacement effects
abstract: The worldwide cocaine market is undergoing an extraordinary surge. Insights on how cocaine is trafficked from production countries to consumer markets are limited, and often based on observed trafficking routes (e.g., seizures) alone. In this paper, we introduce a network-based model of actual transnational cocaine flows, beyond flows seized. In this model, cocaine is routed through an international transportation network of land and sea connections, where each link is assigned an interception risk metric for containerized transport. title: Decision Stability and Model Reduction for Hamilton--Jacobi Navigation in Multiscale Flows
abstract: Autonomous vehicles plan time-optimal routes through flow fields that are known only through reduced, finite-resolution models of an underlying multiscale flow. Classical Hamilton-Jacobi homogenization concerns convergence of the value function as the fine scale vanishes; but what a vehicle commits to is a route, and value accuracy need not imply route accuracy. We study this gap for a fixed-resolution reduction rather than in the homogenization limit. The committed route's dependence on the model-reduction error splits into two regimes. title: Constraining Accretion Heating in Neutron Stars with Carbon Instability and Quiescent Cooling
abstract: In accreting neutron stars, different heating depths can produce similar quiescent cooling when the heating strength and core temperature are adjusted. For KS 1731-260, we compare thermal histories with accretion heating either in a shallower region that overlaps the carbon fuel layer or in a deeper region below it. Without the carbon instability condition, the two histories fit ten quiescent Chandra spectra nearly equally well. title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
abstract: The two-phase Volume-of-Fluid solvers of OpenFOAM overpredict the horizontal water velocity near the crest of a water wave, and the error grows as the wave propagates. Part I of this series removed the spurious air velocities caused by the gravity term but left this error unchanged. Here we show that it is caused by the momentum convection term. Its mass flux is computed in the interface advection step from the velocity at the start of the time step, whereas the convected velocity is taken at the end of the step, because convection is discretised implicitly. title: Cross-experiment tests of the atmospheric-muon excess
abstract: High-energy cosmic rays produce atmospheric muons through cascades of hadronic interactions, yet simulations often underestimate the muon content of extensive air showers. Whether the same problem affects energetic atmospheric muons, which probe a different part of the cascade, is less clear. Here we compare published atmospheric-muon measurements from four experiments with reference predictions based on a shared choice of hadronic interaction model and primary cosmic-ray flux. title: Non-thermal emission from molecular clouds illuminated by continuous cosmic-ray accelerators: application to the stellar cluster W43
abstract: Context: Cosmic rays escaping from their accelerators produce gamma-ray emission through interactions with ambient gas. While the scenario of an impulsive injection of cosmic rays has been extensively studied, that of a continuous injection in time has received comparatively less attention. The latter scenario is particularly relevant for stellar clusters, which may contribute to a non-negligible fraction of Galactic cosmic rays. title: Zero to Four Views: Unified Panorama Generation and Preference RL for Unobserved Regions
abstract: Panoramas can serve as shared scene backgrounds for multi-shot video generation, but most existing panorama generators take text alone or a single input image. We present a single model that generates a full equirectangular panorama from a text caption and K in {0,...,4} perspective conditioning views taken by a four-camera rig at one viewpoint. We fine-tune a pretrained text-to-image rectified-flow transformer in two stages. title: Mapping the Design Space of Feature Sampling for Optical Flow
abstract: The computation of correlation features is crucial for optical flow estimation. Existing methods (e.g., RAFT) perform fixed-radius lookups on a cost volume, yielding a set of correlation features for each position; alternatively, WAFT performs single-point feature indexing, yielding one correlation feature vector per position. None of them designs a suitable correlation feature sampling scheme for each position according to regional characteristics. Our insight is that not every position requires the same sampling scheme. title: Spatial Price Formation in Transport Networks: A Variational Approach
abstract: This paper formulates a model of spatial price formation in a closed regional economy, with finitely many production nodes and finitely many demand nodes embedded in a continuous geographic domain. Transportation costs depend on the geometry of the region and on an underlying network of feasible connections. Prices are modeled as a spatial field constrained by arbitrage and transport feasibility. The equilibrium price system is characterized by a variational problem. title: A State-Level Assessment of Space Weather Impact on the Virginia Power Grid: From Vulnerability to Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Contemporary methodologies exist for assessing the nationwide impacts of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs), such as the Coupled Space Weather Impact Model (C-SWIM), which links power grid vulnerability with economic losses. Yet regional mitigation requires adapting the national model to the local transmission network so operators and planners can identify substations at risk and evaluate economic and population consequences and protective actions. title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
abstract: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. title: Balancing-based model reduction for output-constrained optimal control of switched linear systems
abstract: We develop a balanced-truncation (BT) framework for model-order reduction of optimal control problems governed by switched linear systems, with quadratic tracking costs, convex input constraints, and Moreau--Yosida-regularized output constraints. For general Petrov--Galerkin reduced models, we derive an a posteriori bound for the error in the optimal value function, and combine it with BT-based estimates of the dynamical-system reduction error. title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
abstract: We present a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so the gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, which is the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. title: Speedup-Aware Rounding for Scheduling Malleable Tasks with Precedence Constraints
abstract: We study the scheduling of malleable tasks with precedence constraints on $m$ identical processors to minimize the makespan, assuming that the processing time of a task does not increase and its work does not decrease with the number of processors, and that the work is a convex function of the processing time. The standard two-phase method solves a linear program, rounds the fractional processing times to allotments, caps the allotments at a threshold $μ$, and runs list scheduling. title: Monopole catalysis with massive fermions: the fate of the twisted sector
abstract: In the massless limit a fermion scattering on the minimal $SU(5)$ monopole in the lowest partial wave produces an outgoing state with half-integer fermion number in every flavour. This state lives in a twisted sector of the Hilbert space and is now understood as an ordinary fermion attached to a topological line running back to the monopole. In the Standard Model fermion masses and confinement destroy the line at distances greater than the inverse mass scales, causing the twisted state to decay into physical asymptotic states with integer fermion numbers. title: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands
abstract: High-energy outbursts from magnetars may be associated with crustal failures or quakes. The magnetoelastic modes of the star can be excited to large amplitudes in such a framework, providing a natural explanation for the quasi-periodic oscillations observed in the X-ray tails of some events. However, previous calculations of torsional modes have been carried out assuming an intact crust without accounting for the failure itself. title: Superlattice Stabilization of the Topological Quantum Hall Ferromagnet in Graphene
abstract: Competition between spin and valley orders makes graphene a versatile platform for engineering correlated topological phases in the quantum Hall regime. We show that a tunable superlattice potential reorganizes this competition, and stabilizes the ferromagnetic quantum Hall topological insulator at charge neutrality without requiring a large in-plane magnetic field or strong dielectric suppression of Coulomb interactions. title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO
abstract: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has detected photons with energies up to 3.7 PeV from the binary system Cygnus X-3 during a flaring episode. The combination of such extreme photon energies and the large source distance provides a sensitive probe of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV). In superluminal LIV scenarios, high-energy photons can become unstable and rapidly decay, resulting in a sharp spectral cutoff. title: Locking-free numerical methods for poroelasticity optimal control problems with minimal regularities
abstract: We study distributed optimal control of a linear poroelastic system in a total pressure formulation, with displacement and fluid-pressure tracking and box constraints on the source control. A mechanical Schur complement gives well-posedness at zero storage for each fixed finite Lamé parameter, without estimates that grow like the inverse storage coefficient. title: Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. abstract: This study experimentally investigates the compressive behavior, progressive deformation mechanisms, and energy-absorption efficiency of additively manufactured re-entrant auxetic lattices featuring multi-directional (vertical and diagonal) functional grading. Using an implicit volumetric modeling framework, continuous strut-thickness variations were parameterized and sampled through a structured parametric design-space exploration, yielding 12 grading scenarios realized as 30 polylactic-acid (PLA) specimens (12 vertically graded, V1–V12; 18 diagonally graded with upright and inverted V-core o

title: PFAS Occurrence and Bioaccumulation in Marine Organisms and Implications for Coral Reef-Associated Food Webs and Biomonitoring
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been measured in diverse marine organisms, but differences among compounds, sample matrices, food webs, and analytical methods complicate interpretation of their environmental significance. This targeted, literature-based comparative review organized evidence from 29 distinct peer-reviewed primary studies published from 2011 to 2026 for which full-text articles were available. title: Governing Brisbane 2032: Reframing Urban Impact Assessment Beyond Project-by-Project Approaches
abstract: With less than a decade remaining until the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, a critical urban policy question emerges: can existing project-based assessment systems adequately govern the cumulative, cross-scalar and long-term impacts of mega-event-led urban transformation? This article argues that Queensland’s dominant project-by-project assessment framework is not well suited to address metropolitan-scale sustainability pressures, distributive equity concerns, and enduring legacy obligations associated with the Games. title: Digital heritage ecologies in Oman: institutional archives, grassroots media, and community archive-making in musical intangible cultural heritage
abstract: This article examines how Omani musical intangible cultural heritage is safeguarded through the interaction of institutional archives, grassroots archivists, musicians, audiences, and digital platforms. It argues that Omani traditional music is best understood not as material preserved in a single repository, but as part of a plural digital heritage ecology in which preservation, circulation, interpretation, and transmission are distributed across formal and informal archival spaces. title: The evolutionary history of brackish specialization from marine ancestry in the seagrass Ruppia sinensis
abstract: Ruppia sinensis, a unique seagrass species that originated in the marine environment yet successfully colonized extreme inland habitats, offers a rare window onto how plants cope with major habitat shifts and clarifies the mechanisms of adaptive evolution during marine-to-brackish transitions. We assembled a chromosome-level genome, conducted comparative phylogenomic analyses, assessed salinity tolerance through physiological experiments, and analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 103 individuals representing 19 coastal and inland populations. title: Synergizing Local Culture And Religious Values For Inclusive Human Resource Development: Evidence From Muslim-Majority Organizations in Southeast Asia
abstract: Religious organizations in Southeast Asia face increasing challenges in preserving local cultural and religious identities while developing human resources capable of responding to globalization, digital transformation, and growing demands for organizational inclusivity. Although cultural and religious values are widely recognized in human resource management research, they are often treated as contextual factors rather than as core resources shaping organizational practices. title: Depth-Dependent eDNA Abundances across Ecosystems Inform Deep-Sea Sampling Strategies
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) surveys are increasingly used to assess marine biodiversity and inform deep-sea environmental decision-making, including mineral resource management and fisheries oversight. Yet standard low-volume protocols inherited from coastal work may be inadequate at depth, and recent findings indicate that depth- and productivity-aware sampling, often requiring high-volume in situ filtration, is needed. title: The coastline and the line of occupancy: risks of urbanization in the coastal area of Macaé
abstract: Coastal zones perform essential ecological functions and concentrate a significant portion of the world’s population, although they are increasingly affected by urban pressure and coastal erosion. This study analyzed the relationship between unplanned urban occupation and coastal erosion in the Special Zone of Social Interest (ZEIS) Fronteira, located in Macaé (RJ), Brazil. The research employed CBERS-4A satellite imagery, the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), and five perpendicular transects to monitor shoreline changes between 2020 and 2024. title: A decade of acoustic telemetry in a Marine Protected Area reveals multispecies connectivity throughout the Northwest Atlantic
abstract: In the Northwest Atlantic, acoustic telemetry is widely used to assess aquatic species movements and habitat use within and among conservation areas. We examined the contribution of acoustic telemetry to research and monitoring in St. Anns Bank Marine Protected Area (MPA) off Cape Breton Island (Mi’kmaq: Unama’ki), Nova Scotia. Acoustic telemetry receivers have been deployed within the MPA since 2015 (26 to 46 receivers per year), with tagging of Atlantic cod, Atlantic halibut, and Atlantic striped wolffish. title: On the Eastern Shores of Mare Nostrum: Sea, Fishing, Fish and Marine Iconography in the Mosaics of Antiocheia ad Orontem, Daphne, Seleucia Pieria, Alexandretta
abstract: Representations associated with the sea are especially prominent in the Roman period villas of Antiocheia ad Orontem, Daphne, the port citys of Seleucia Pieria and Myriandros-Alexandretta. A total of 33 mosaics featuring marine and freshwater themes have been identified in Antiocheia ad Orontem. These include depictions of fishing Erotes, Tethys, Oceanus and Tethys, Thalassa, the marine thiasus, Nereids, Tritons, Nymphe, fishing scenes, the Birth of Aphrodite, Arethusa, the Abduction of Europa, and the Navigium Isidis, as well as other mythological themes. title: Governing Marine Genetic Resources in the Digital Era: Bridging Policy, Science, and Industry Perspectives
abstract: Marine genetic resources (MGR) hold enormous promise for scientific innovation and commercial development, but their governance remains marked by significant uncertainty, especially during the operationalization of the Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. In response to these gaps, this study aims to gain a deeper understanding of the evolving MGR landscape. abstract: Efficient data transmission in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) using the 6G edge communication is vital for battery-operated devices. This paper presents a cooperative transmission strategy using an Unmanned Vehicle to collect sensory data and recharge sensor nodes for data transmission. This study introduces a UWSN with Blockchain-Based Energy Trading and Fairness based Power Allocation (UWBEFP) that combines secure energy management, intelligent routing, and efficient relay selection. title: Population genomic evidence of northern and southern subspecies of western Pacific abalones around Japanese archipelago
abstract: Subspecies can be formed as a consequence of an adaptive response to local climatic conditions, potentially exhibiting specific environmental requirements. However, limited examples exist of genomic and adaptive differentiation among the subspecies of marine organisms. title: Navigating the Sea of Reviews: Unveiling the Effects of Introducing AI-Generated Summaries in E-Commerce
abstract: AI-generated review summaries are reshaping how consumers access product information, but their influence also extends to consumers who write reviews. Examining Amazon’s rollout of AI-generated review summaries, we find that these summaries encourage more review contributions and richer content. Consumers discuss product attributes absent from the summaries and elaborate on topics already covered. title: Coupled layer-building and seawater ageing effects on axial compressive response of CFRP tubes
abstract: Layer build-up improves the axial resistance of circumferentially wrapped CFRP tubes, but its influence on seawater sensitivity depends on both wall deformation and material ageing. This study compares one- to four-layer tubes after 12 months in laboratory air or threefold-concentrated artificial seawater. Eight parent tubes provided 40 valid short-section compression records, which were analysed together with deformation photographs, SEM, FTIR and same-batch companion moisture-uptake and DMA measurements. title: Scaling Laws and the Fair‐Use Proviso on Urban Territory
abstract: Debates about land‐use policy and neighborhood change must be informed by rights to territory. We plausibly have limited rights to occupy and control our local territory. One or both rights might justify local (i.e., municipal or neighborhood‐based) control over land‐use policies. Following many theories of (national) territorial rights, I'll argue that this is the case only if such policies satisfy a fair‐use proviso on appropriating territory. title: Optimizing the Management of Indonesian Archipelagic Sea Lanes to Support the Development of Special Economic Zones in Maluku Province
abstract: Introduction: Article 53 of the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea establishes the obligation of an archipelagic State to designate archipelagic sea lanes. Indonesia has implemented this obligation through Government Regulation No. 37 of 2002, which designates the Indonesian Archipelagic Sea Lanes (ALKI). In this context, the designation of ALKI IIIA, IIIB, and IIIC, all of which pass through the Banda Sea west of Buru Island, has significant strategic implications for the development of the Southern Buru region as a Special Economic Zone. title: Stakeholder-derived research priorities to improve small-scale fisheries governance in the Azores oceanic archipelago
abstract: Small-scale fisheries involve complex interactions between ecological dynamics, governance arrangements, markets, and social dimensions across multiple spatial and institutional scales. Deciding how best to develop research agendas in the face of such complexity is a challenge, yet it must also account for diverse stakeholder priorities to avoid weakening the relevance and legitimacy of management. This paper utilizes issue division and linkage theory to analyze potential pathways for cooperation. It explores the creation of narrowly defined ‘mini- zopa s’ across key functional areas: Sovereignty, Security, Energy, Fisheries, Sea Lanes, and Conduct. title: Developing Vocal Skills Through Coastal Folk Song Traditions in Central Vietnam
abstract: Background: Coastal folk singing in Central Vietnam brings together vocal phrasing, diction, rhythmic coordination, leader-chorus exchange, and culturally situated expression. Its potential for university vocal education cannot be understood by treating songs as isolated melodies or assuming one technique applies across local traditions. Objective: This article identifies pedagogically relevant vocal competencies within selected coastal performance practices and develops a framework for their responsible use in higher music education. title: Taxonomically standardized iNaturalist records reveal broad-scale patterns in documented polychaete diversity across U.S. coastlines
abstract: Citizen-science platforms are increasingly used to document biodiversity, but their value for taxonomically difficult marine invertebrates remains uncertain. Polychaete annelids are diverse, ecologically important, and often difficult to identify from photographs alone, raising questions about how community-science records should be interpreted. Here, we evaluated research-grade iNaturalist observations of Polychaeta across the continental United States. title: Bycatch, Capture Mortality, and Release Condition in the Cypriot Pelagic Longline Fishery: A Multi-Year Observer-Based Assessment from the Levantine Sea
abstract: This study assessed bycatch composition, nominal catch rates, capture mortality and release condition in the Cypriot pelagic longline fishery targeting swordfish and albacore tuna. Observations covered 142 fishing days across 16 vessels during 2018–2024 and 335,340 hooks, recording 643 bycatch individuals from 23 species. Bycatch comprised 10.7% of the total catch biomass, with pooled rates of 1.92 individuals and 14.20 kg per 1000 hooks. title: Blue Justice for Small‐Scale Fishers in South Africa: Shifting From Co‐Management to Co‐Governance
abstract: This article critically examines the impact of the Policy for the Small Scale Fisheries Sector in South Africa on small‐scale fishers (SSFs). It centres SSFs’ lived experiences, structural barriers to participation, and opportunities for more just and sustainable ocean governance. By recognising small‐scale fisheries as relational systems embedded in community, place, and tradition, the article challenges narrow economistic framings prevalent in dominant blue economy discourses. title: Rooting, flourishing and cultural exchange of Chinese ancestors along the South Seas Maritime Silk Road before the Qing Dynasty
abstract: The Maritime Silk Road of the Chinese ancestors was characterized by the establishment and the flourishing and rooting of Chinese settlements across various regions, and by the long-term practice of cultural exchange and mutual learning. Its background lay in the continuous advancement of navigation and shipbuilding knowledge from the Han to the Song dynasties. title: INTEGRATION OF THE SEA-HORSE OPTIMIZER WITH THE ANALYTIC HIERARCHY PROCESS: AN ASSESSMENT OF CONSISTENCY AND ACCURACY
abstract: This study integrates the Sea-horse Optimizer (SHO) with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to examine whether metaheuristic post-processing of the priority vector improves the consistency and accuracy of AHP weights. title: First substantiated record of the twobar seabream Acanthopagrus bifasciatus (Forsskål, 1775) from Greek waters, with a critical update of Mediterranean occurrences
abstract: The twobar seabream, Acanthopagrus bifasciatus , is native to the western Indian Ocean and Red Sea and is regarded as a rare non-indigenous fish in the Mediterranean Sea. Here, we document a single individual photographed after being speared off Trypiti Beach, Gavdos Island, southern Greece, on 28 August 2026. The fish was reportedly captured at approximately 10 m depth and was photographed only after scaling and evisceration. title: A brackish, muddy, wave-dominated embayment depositional model for the La Colonia Formation (Maastrichtian–Danian) in the Cañadón Asfalto Basin, Argentina
abstract: The La Colonia Formation (LCF) is a Maastrichtian to Danian mud-dominated succession cropping out in northern Patagonia and considered part of the post-rift stage of the Cañadón Asfalto Basin. The unit is world-famous for its wealth of terrestrial (mostly) and marine fossils. Prior depositional interpretations were inconsistent, proposing diverse marginal marine systems, while dedicated sedimentological studies remained absent. title: Implementing Islamic Economic Principles for Fishermen Empowerment
abstract: This study addresses the persistent challenges faced by fishing communities in Muara Sabak Timur, where unstable income, reliance on middlemen, and limited access to formal financing continue to hinder economic resilience. The primary objective is to analyze the implementation of Islamic economic principles in empowering fishermen through the fisheries sector and to identify supporting and inhibiting factors. journal: Zabags International Journal of Islamic Studies.

title: Knowledge and Training Exposure in Safety Risk Management Among Third-Year Marine Transportation Cadets: A Descriptive-Comparative Study
abstract: Safety Risk Management (SRM) is essential for seafarers, yet few studies measure how well pre-immersion cadets grasp SRM concepts or how training exposure relates to that knowledge. This study assessed SRM knowledge and training exposure among 80 third-year Marine Transportation and Marine Engineering cadets at a Philippine maritime institution before shipboard immersion. abstract: This article explores emergent cosmologies of climate change in a predominantly Dalit Hindu community in the Sundarbans of West Bengal, India. In recent years, my interlocutors have begun to link changing weather patterns to human activity, often through reference to divine and demonic beings. This article considers how public performances generate such cosmological shifts. abstract: Frequent river health assessments are critical to track ecological change in freshwater ecosystems, but traditional monitoring is costly and difficult to scale. Ecoacoustics could become an alternative low‐effort method to monitor rivers, but current analyses remain focused on biotic activity, with no framework for simultaneously assessing biotic and abiotic components of freshwater health. title: Climate Change and Crisis of Multilateralism: Why do States Struggle to Cooperate on Shared Global Threats?
abstract: Climate change is a shared global threat that requires coordinated action among states, yet international cooperation remains slow, fragmented, and insufficient. This paper examines the crisis of multilateralism in global climate governance by asking why states struggle to cooperate despite the growing severity of climate impacts. abstract: The XPRIZE Carbon Removal, a competition launched in 2021 and concluded in 2025, awarded US$100 million in cash prizes to teams that demonstrated carbon dioxide removal (CDR) at a kilotonne scale. abstract: Nature restoration has evolved from focussing mostly on ecology to include societal aspects, yet it is unclear how this is reflected in the academic literature. In this article, we investigate the social and ecological dimensions of published frameworks and principles that guide nature restoration. We further assess how socio‐ecological concepts can be used to broaden and strengthen the discipline of nature restoration through an interdisciplinary analysis. abstract: In this wide‐ranging interview conducted for the Journal of Sociolinguistics, Emi Otsuji speaks with Alastair Pennycook about the trajectory of his scholarship across more than four decades in applied linguistics and sociolinguistics. abstract: Bangladesh is a developing country with limited resources and several climate disasters. title: Global threats and conservation strategies for temporary ponds based on expert opinion and scientific evidence
abstract: Temporary ponds are dynamic aquatic habitats found in all global biomes. Because they seasonally or intermittently dry out, they often support specialist flora and fauna including many endemic species. Although numerous studies report their decline, there is little consensus on their primary threats or effective mitigation strategies. abstract: This paper explores the role that soundscapes play in the uses and abuses of heritage in selected tourism spaces. abstract: This study highlights the pedagogical effects of drawing prompts as a classroom strategy to promote creative drawing practice and imagination among basic (primary) school learners at a selected school in Winneba, Ghana. abstract: Despite growing attention to global agendas in education systems, limited empirical research has examined how these agendas are translated into community-based adult education. This study investigates how Taiwanese community colleges reinterpret global educational agendas through locally situated educational practice. abstract: A delivery agreement creates a legal relationship between the shipper and the carrier, thus giving rise to rights and obligations for both parties. abstract: Regional development is increasingly challenged by climate and demographic change, technological transformation, and growing uncertainty, requiring planning approaches that extend beyond short-term decision-making. abstract: Chinese monopoly in processing and supply chains of rare earth and critical minerals have become instrument of great-power competition. This article gives an insight that how that dynamic has reached Balochistan, Pakistan’s largest and least populous province, which holds the Reko Diq copper-gold mine, the producing Saindak mine, and potential of rare earth elements. abstract: This article examines the sport and other pastime activities in which members of the British forces engaged during the South African War (1899–1902). abstract: Este artículo presenta la incoherencia normativa como un problema de justificación del reproche penal en la medida en que pone en cuestión los fundamentos que lo sostienen. title: Health-seeking behaviour and treatment preferences among women reporting symptoms suggestive of female genital schistosomiasis in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa: A facility-based cross-sectional study
abstract: Female Genital Schistosomiasis (FGS), a neglected manifestation of Schistosoma haematobium infection, affects 20-56 million women in sub-Saharan Africa and is associated with elevated HIV risk. In a Schistosoma haematobium-endemic area of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, 32% of girls aged 10-12 years reported a history of genital symptoms, yet awareness is low, and the proportion seeking appropriate care is undocumented. title: The inherent viciousness of American football fandom
abstract: American football fandom is many things. It’s normal (in America). It’s a multibillion-dollar industry. And, as the author argues in this paper, it’s vicious. While there’s much literature about the ethics of American football and dangerous sport more generally, as well as about sport fandom, there’s significantly less about the ethics of American football fandom. This paper takes a virtue ethical look at American football fandom, arguing that whatever else we think about American football or sport fandom more generally, American football fandom is vicious. title: Corporate Governance Failures and Their Influence on Liquidation Outcomes and Business Rescue in Nigeria
abstract: Corporate governance determines whether a company in difficulty can be saved and, if it cannot, how much of its value survives the process of winding up. The Nigerian literature examines the first of those propositions closely and the second hardly at all. This article addresses the second. title: The Island Equity Paradox: Capability, Governance, and Educational Reform in Peripheral Contexts
abstract: This study examines how China’s common prosperity reforms reshaped educational equity in two island counties of Zhejiang Province between 2020 and 2025. Addressing the dominance of cross-sectional approaches, it draws on a six-wave longitudinal qualitative study conducted from 2020 to 2025 with a 54-member core cohort of teachers and parents. abstract: Urban degrowth and shrinking cities are two research fields that have gained increasing attention in recent years. The intersection of the two fields is likewise attracting growing interest due to their potential synergy: shrinking cities research provides empirical evidence of degrowth-oriented planning, while urban degrowth research offers in-depth analysis and critique of growth-oriented planning that may prove useful for shrinking cities research. title: Application of bivalve shells for the removal of trace levels of micropollutants from wastewater under continuous flow conditions
abstract: Advanced nature-based systems such as METland® efficiently remove contaminants of emerging concern from municipal wastewater, yet a residual mixture of compounds often persists. This study evaluated bivalve shells as a low-cost polishing step for METland® effluent in two steps: preliminary fixed-bed adsorption experiment comparing the performance of whole clam shells, pyrolyzed clam shells and pyrolyzed oyster shells; a large-scale fixed-bed removal experiment using raw clam shells, calcined clam shells and a shell mixture, integrating LC-MS/MS multiresidue analysis and ecotoxicological assays

abstract: The continuous resource consumption and ecological externalities associated with the depreciation of China’s fixed assets pose systematic, yet often invisible, threats to biodiversity. abstract: This paper analyses Margaret Atwood's The Testaments (2019) through posthuman ecofeminist theory to demonstrate how the novel transforms feminist ethical principles past human-focused survival and agency models. This essay examines the Atwood’s The Testaments through the lens of the ecological dimensions of posthuman feminism. title: Promotion of energy from renewable sources and ensuring business respect for human rights in the EU
abstract: The article is devoted to the green transition and the European Union’s perspective on external energy engagement. The aim of the article was to analyze the European Union’s strategic and legal framework for promoting energy from renewable sources, identify key principles and approaches that guide these processes, and assess the interconnections with the EU priorities of ensuring business respect for human rights. title: Remaking the periphery: An urban political ecology of housing-environmental activisms in São Paulo
abstract: At the fringes of São Paulo’s macro-metropolis, precarious housing often meets fragile environments. In these peripheral neighbourhoods, grassroots groups have been reinventing the housing-environment nexus and remaking the peripheries on their own terms. This paper conceptualises these struggles as housing-environment activisms. abstract: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is increasingly faced with erga omnes (partes) claims that request reparation “in the interest of the injured State or of the beneficiaries of the obligation breached” (collectively referred to as the “others”), as foreseen in Article 48(2)(b) of the 2001 ILC Articles on State Responsibility. title: Historical narratives and populist power: Identity continuity and ontological security in political rhetoric
abstract: Populist leaders frequently use historical narratives to construct national identity and legitimize political authority, yet the social psychological processes through which these narratives may help sustain populist power remain underexplored. Drawing on social identity theory and research on identity continuity and ontological security, this study examines how historical narratives operate within populist rhetoric. abstract: William Wordsworth is considered the poet who made nature the central topic of English Romantic poetry. Wordsworth's celebration of nature is not merely decoration. It is a method of thinking about memory, moral development, imagination and the common life of ordinary people. This paper analyzes how Wordsworth represents nature in his major poems and prose, and what impact this representation had on English literature and Romantic poetry. Currently, the audit organizations is faced with the challenges of assessing the reliability of sustainable development information. abstract: Despite the traffic engineering efforts of cloud providers to reduce latency for cloud services, both researchers and practitioners observe that circuitous routing persists and that substantial opportunities for improvement remain. abstract: This paper brings discussions about far-right political economy into dialogue with the history of ideas by examining the economic thinking of the radical right intellectual movement known as the European New Right (ENR). abstract: Conflicts, political unrest, persecution and some other conditions from which people have to escape made the issue of refugee protection more pressing. When refugees flee from their home countries, they often face a number of challenges over their safety, housing, health, education, employment, as well as legal status. abstract: El incremento de la longevidad suele ingresar al debate previsional como un desafío de sostenibilidad: más años de retiro, mayor gasto y una relación demográfica menos favorable entre población activa y personas mayores. abstract: El término acquihires describe un conjunto de operaciones empresariales dirigidas principalmente a la adquisición de talento humano que pueden plantear ciertos riesgos para la competencia, tanto en los mercados de productos como en los laborales, y paralelamente importantes retos para los sistemas de control de concentraciones. abstract: Farm succession in Australian agriculture extends beyond a business transition; it encompasses social and cultural aspects that can significantly impact farming families and communities. The traditional rural idyll continues to influence succession practices; however, modern challenges including gender equity, climate change, and globalisation can create conflicting pressures on farming families. Working towards new means for reconciling wind power and reindeer husbandry through collaboration in Northern Finland
abstract: As formal governance and planning processes struggle to address energy transition related conflicts, there is a growing need for approaches that help parties understand emerging tensions and identify mutually acceptable solutions. In this paper, we present a case study from Finland where wind power developers and reindeer herders have established a collaborative arrangement to address conflicts and develop shared practices for communication and negotiation. abstract: This study examined traditional wedding discourse in Biqueli Village, Timor-Leste, as a culturally organised form of social action. It focused on speech acts, the organisation of the wedding ceremony, interpersonal relations, cultural values, and the exploration of distributed declarative force. abstract: During the real estate downturn, the Taishun merchant community has encountered a systemic predicament characterized by breakdowns in capital chains and an eruption of private lending disputes. abstract: Although Plasmodium falciparum is the most prevalent and highly virulent species in Sub-Saharan Africa, non-falciparum species are increasingly recognized as a hidden burden. Generally, infections caused by non-falciparum species occur with low parasite densities and often present as co-infections with P. falciparum. abstract: The absence of an operational mechanism for compensating landholders whose land contains water resources exploited by third parties creates legal uncertainty and social conflict. abstract: Sustainable finance is usually presented as a neutral body of technique: taxonomies, ratings, green bond principles and disclosure rules. This article reads it instead as a custom. abstract: In this article, we propose the Quartile-Adjusted Skewness Intensity Weighting (QASI-W) method for multi-criteria decision-making. We use a cross-country healthcare system evaluation to illustrate the applicability of QASI-W relative to conventional objective methods. institutions: Vignan's Foundation for Science, Technology & Research

title: El nuevo diseño de la instrucción en España, a la luz de los estándares europeos
abstract: La Exposición de Motivos del Anteproyecto de Ley por la que se modifica el EOMF, de 2025, afirma que la atribución de la instrucción del proceso penal al Ministerio Fiscal es coherente con nuestra pertenencia al espacio normativo de libertad y justicia de la Unión Europea. Por su parte, la Exposición de Motivos del Proyecto de Ley Orgánica de Enjuiciamiento Criminal, también de 2025, mantiene que dicho modelo es el generalmente aceptado en los países de nuestro entorno y el que puede considerarse parte del acervo jurídico característico de la Unión Europea. title: Elite Capture and Control in Participatory Budgeting: Evidence from a Sri Lankan Municipality
abstract: This study aims to examine how elite capture and elite control shape PB practices in a Sri Lankan local government, with a focus on how accounting mediates these practices. In particular, this explores how political and administrative elites utilise the PB process to dominate in the field during their respective leadership periods. To achieve the study’s aims, a qualitative case study was conducted in a Sri Lankan municipality, one of the earliest adopters of PB in the country. Data were collected through 24 semi-structured interviews with elected and administrative officials, complemented by
journal: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance

title: CS3D and private enforcement: the journey from international jurisdiction obstacles to the omnibus structural enforcement gap
abstract: This contribution traces the evolution of the CS3D’s private enforcement mechanism from the 2024 Directive to Omnibus I, focusing on how private international law rules have shaped its effectiveness. Under the 2024 framework, the Directive provided for overriding mandatory civil liability rules, but it did not ensure access to Member State courts. The paper argues that the EU principle of effectiveness supported an implicit forum legis—a lesson relevant for future EU instruments with lois de police. title: Formulation and Evaluation of Polyherbal Anti-Inflammatory Gel Containing Pyrus Pashia (Kainth) Fruit Extract
abstract: Inflammation represents a vital protective response to tissue injury; however, uncontrolled or chronic inflammatory cascades can cause substantial pain, edema, and tissue damage. Conventional treatment with oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) is severely restricted by systemic complications, including gastrointestinal ulceration, hepatotoxicity, and renal stress. To overcome these limitations, the present study developed and evaluated a topical polyherbal hydrogel incorporating the bioflavonoid-rich fruit extract of Pyrus pashia Buch.-Ham. ex D. journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Property rights after flooding: post-disaster land policy in Türkiye and Germany
abstract: Flood recovery involves not only rebuilding but reorganizing land, property rights, and long-term development. Yet the role of land policy in post-flood reconstruction remains underexplored. This paper compares responses to the 2021 floods in Türkiye and Germany to examine how land policy priorities – land-use regulation, and property protection – shape reconstruction, showing that outcomes hinge on how land-use decisions (allocation) align with ownership and compensation (distribution). title: La construcción jurídico-pública de la persona consumidora
abstract: El presente trabajo analiza la construcción jurídico-pública de la persona consumidora desde una perspectiva constitucional, tomando como eje el artículo 51 de la Constitución Española. A partir de un estudio sistemático de la evolución del concepto de persona consumidora, de la configuración de sus derechos y del desarrollo legislativo experimentado desde 1978, se examina el intenso proceso de expansión normativa que ha configurado un verdadero enjambre normativo en el ámbito nacional y europeo. El trabajo sostiene que el artículo 51 CE ha superado su tradicional consideración como principio

title: Atravesando la afasia
abstract: A lo largo de la obra de Beckett, las numerosas referencias explícitas e implícitas de la afasia desencadenan una lectura “contaminada” (a la vez literaria, lingüística, filosófica, ‘trágica’ y neuronal) que subraya y desestabiliza el concepto de intencionalidad.

title: LEGAL ETHICS AND PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY OF JUDGES IN CLIMATE CHANGE LITIGATION
abstract: Climate change litigation has become an important legal response to inadequate climate governance, corporate emissions, environmental degradation, and rights-based claims. This study examines the role, ethics, and professional responsibility of judges in climate litigation through the seven values of the Bangalore Principles: independence, impartiality, integrity, propriety, equality, competence, and diligence. Using qualitative doctrinal research and an integrative literature review, it analyses scholarly literature, judicial ethics instruments, Indonesian positive law, and selected global an

title: Stanislavsky and the Question of Truth
abstract: Konstantin Stanislavsky’s pursuit of truth in acting remains central to contemporary actor training, and this paper examines how his evolving understanding of truth can be read alongside wider philosophical and cultural debates of his time, particularly those concerning belief, authenticity, and the performer’s experience of the self as transformative. It explores Stanislavsky’s notion of truth in performance in relation to late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century discussions on embodied expression and the ethical dimensions of artistic practice.
