title: Probabilistic resilience mapping to flooding of urban multi-infrastructure systems
abstract: Because they are highly interdependent, most infrastructure systems are vulnerable to disasters such as severe floods. A vast amount of data has been made available with which to better anticipate the impact of severe floods and enable areas prone to flooding to become more sustainable and resilient. However, integrating these data sources and modelling the impact of floods remains challenging. In this study, we develop a transferable, fact-calibrated, weakly supervised, physically constrained probabilistic modelling framework designed to address this issue. We estimate the facility level floo
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: Política, ideología y Derecho en las leyes simbólicas
abstract: El trabajo describe y analiza, desde un punto de vista crítico, la llamada legislación simbólica, es decir, aquellas leyes que tienen un contenido esencialmente volitivo, ideológico o retórico y con ninguna o pocas prescripciones verdaderamente operativas o aplicativas desde el punto de vista jurídico. Son normas en las que el poder legislativo no regula, crea o extingue situaciones jurídicas exigibles o ciertas (no crea derecho ni vínculos jurídicos) sino que expresa sus opiniones o deseos, o expone un relato o narración, o regula meras aspiraciones sociales sin pretensión o posibilidad real

title: Production and Characterization of PLA/PBS Composites With Added Olive Leaf Powder
abstract: In this study, composites were produced by extrusion melt mixing and injection molding methods by adding olive leaf powder (OLP) to a PLA/PBS polymer blend matrix at weight percentages of 10%, 20%, and 30%. SEM analysis showed that at low OLP ratios, the additive was well distributed in the matrix, while at high OLP ratios, void and crack formation increased, and a more heterogeneous morphology was formed because of weakened interfacial interactions. title: Liberal nationalism and the protection of majority cultures
abstract: When the state acts to protect the language and culture of the national majority, it appears to violate the liberal principle of equal treatment by conferring a privileged status on the majority and turning cultural minorities into ‘second-class citizens’. Liberal nationalists argue that national cultures are public goods, and also that state neutrality in the cultural sphere is impossible. Moreover cultures are multi-stranded and flexible, and leave space for sub-groups to practice their own cultures in the private sphere. journal: Critical Review of International Social and Political Philosophy

title: La protección de la marca no registrada y la función del Derecho de la competencia desleal
abstract: Spanish trade mark law is built on the principle that rights are acquired through registration, so that the exclusive right arises from a valid entry in the register. Alongside this principle, however, a varied set of mechanisms protects signs that are used in trade but have never been registered. These include the protection of well- known marks under Article 6bis of the Paris Convention, the remedies against bad faith filings and, above all, unfair competition law, which prohibits acts of confusion, unfair imitation and the undue exploitation of another trader’s reputation. journal: Revista propiedad intelectual e innovación digital

title: La protección urbanística del caserío vasco: las limitaciones normativas y su impacto en la rehabilitación del patrimonio rural
abstract: Este trabajo analiza el régimen jurídico aplicable a la rehabilitación del caserío vasco y las limitaciones que condicionan su adaptación a las necesidades habitacionales actuales. A partir del estudio de las Directrices de Ordenación Territorial, la Ley 2/2006, de Suelo y Urbanismo del País Vasco, el planeamiento municipal de Oiartzun y diversas resoluciones judiciales, se examina la tensión entre la protección del suelo rural y la conservación efectiva del caserío como espacio habitado. El análisis normativo y jurisprudencial, complementado mediante un estudio de caso, evidencia una aplicaci

title: El veto presidencial en el sistema constitucional e institucional de los Estados Unidos: ventajas e inconvenientes en tiempos de división partidista
abstract: El veto presidencial es uno de los instrumentos más destacados que posee la Presidencia en Estados Unidos y una pieza central del sistema de frenos y contrapesos. Este artículo sostiene como hipótesis que, en contextos de creciente polarización y de Gobierno Dividido, el veto deja de operar principalmente como mecanismo constitucional de corrección y negociación interinstitucional para convertirse, con mayor frecuencia, en una herramienta de bloqueo y competencia partidista. A partir del análisis de su regulación, modalidades y práctica reciente —incluida la presidencia de Joe Biden y los veto

title: An Early Hispanist and Pioneer of Portuguese Studies: Norman Jones Lamb (1916–2014)
abstract: This article discusses an influential Hispanist and pioneer of Portuguese Studies. A student of E. Allison Peers, Norman Lamb completed his MA thesis at Liverpool University just as the Second World War started. He taught in the Spanish Department at Glasgow University before being called up in 1940 for army service overseas. He returned to Liverpool University in 1946 where he was lecturer, then senior lecturer in Spanish and Portuguese, but concentrated on developing Portuguese Studies. title: The Right to Have Rights as a Legal Test for the Rohingya in Bangladesh
abstract: Hannah Arendt described the condition of the stateless as the loss of a “right to have rights”; the right to belong to a community in which one’s actions and opinions count. This article turns that idea into a legal test and applies it to the Rohingya in Bangladesh. The test has three cumulative thresholds: recognition (being legible to the legal order as a person), standing (being able to bring a claim and have it heard) and agency (being able to act with legal effect). journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: From public relations to cognitive defense: Indonesian government digital communication as infrastructure in cognitive warfare
abstract: This study reconceptualizes Indonesian government public relations (PR) as cognitive defense infrastructure within the information environment. Drawing on Niklas Luhmann’s social systems theory and Susanne Holmström’s reconstruction of PR as society’s evolutionary learning mechanism, it proposes that government digital communication can be interpreted as a systemic device for stabilizing meaning under informational entropy. institutions: LSPR Institute of Communication and Business

title: Design for battery-cartridge longevity in cordless power tools: Modular standardization via LCA to end-of-life management and circularity
abstract: Proprietary battery systems in cordless power tools cause premature obsolescence, resource inefficiency and barriers to end-of-life management. This study quantifies the benefits of standardization and modularization through a comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) of three representative cordless-drill battery designs (36 V, 18 V and 18 V nominal/20 V max) under three standardization scenarios: proprietary, partially standardized, and fully standardized modular. institutions: Iran University of Science and Technology

title: Association of antiretroviral regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy with all-cause mortality among adults on ART in a high-mobility primary care setting in Northwest Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the association of antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) with all-cause mortality among adults on ART at a primary health center in a high-mobility setting in Northwest Ethiopia. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: This study was conducted from October 31, 2013 to October 31, 2024 in Northwest Ethiopia, Chagni town. This town serves as a delivery point for a population characterized by mobility, including seasonal and migrant workers, and main route to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. institutions: Amhara National Regional State Public Health Institute

title: Traducir para dos continentes: coedición de Fin de fiesta, de Juan Goytisolo en Grove Press y Weidenfeld & Nicolson (1962-1966)
abstract: Este artículo examina el proceso de coedición de la novela Fin de fiesta, de Juan Goytisolo, entre Grove Press (EE. UU.) y Weidenfeld & Nicolson (Reino Unido) entre 1962 y 1966, a partir del análisis crítico y contextualizado de documentación inédita de archivo, como correspondencia editorial, informes de lectura y contratos. La metodología adoptada combina herramientas de la historia cultural del libro con una perspectiva filológica orientada al estudio de la mediación editorial y la traducción. title: Los acuerdos de estandarización de la sostenibilidad y su exención en el Derecho Europeo de la Competencia
abstract: El trabajo analiza el tratamiento de los acuerdos de estandarización de la sostenibilidad entre empresas competidoras en las Directrices europeas sobre la aplicabilidad del artículo 101 del TFUE a los acuerdos de cooperación horizontal, de 21 de julio de 2023. Las Directrices pretenden ayudar a discernir cuándo se pueden admitir esos acuerdos desde la perspectiva antitrust, adoptando una posición favorable, que se manifiesta a través de dos instrumentos fundamentales. title: Energy crisis management in small isolated energy systems
abstract: The oil crises of the 1970s led governments to adopt immediate measures to limit fuel consumption, such as rationing, driving bans and speed limits, and to create new institutions including the International Energy Agency (IEA) and strategic oil reserves. The 2022–2024 energy crisis triggered by the war in Ukraine shifted the European Union towards a different mix of responses centered on energy savings, diversification of suppliers, accelerated deployment of renewables and storage, and extensive financial support for consumers and businesses. Building on lessons from these episodes, this pape

title: Dimensiones jurídicas del fenómeno Incel. Igualdad de género y derechos humanos en la era digital
abstract: Se busca identificar cómo debe enfocarse jurídicamente —con justicia y eficacia— el fenómeno Incel en las sociedades contemporáneas para determinar sobre qué aspectos debe aplicarse su regulación constitucional y secundaria frente a la problemática actual de la misoginia digital. El argumento central es que dicha regulación debe enfocarse en conductas y contenidos concretos, y no en la etiqueta identitaria Incel. El fenómeno adquiere una enorme relevancia jurídica en especial por su potencia simbólica y por su función de vector ideológico aunque no debe desestimarse nunca su creciente magnitud

title: The right to belong-childhood statelessness in Australia: international and domestic legal measures to reduce statelessness at birth
abstract: To be stateless—that is, without any legally recognised nationality—is a multi-faceted phenomenon impacting millions of children—including those born in Australia—worldwide. There has been little academic analysis of childhood statelessness, however, in Australia. Little is understood about statelessness within the Australian legal and policy sectors, and indeed, more broadly. Without nationality, stateless children can face difficulty in accessing essential human rights. Australia has shown a strong commitment to reducing childhood statelessness by ratifying the two key international treaties

title: Pallas, Tarpeia, and Virgilian Reception in Dionysius of Halicarnassus
abstract: This article examines Pallas and Tarpeia in Virgil’s Aeneid alongside variant traditions preserved in Dionysius of Halicarnassus’ Roman Antiquities. Although direct Virgilian influence on Dionysius cannot be demonstrated, Dionysius preserves mythographic traditions that illuminate Virgil’s treatment of genealogy, homonymy, and conflicting accounts of Rome’s early past. Particular attention is given to the tradition of Pallas, the prematurely deceased son of Hercules and Evander’s daughter Launa/ Lavinia, and its possible relevance to Virgil’s doomed son of Evander. title: Towards a gender responsive framework to guide social marketers in designing campaigns featuring social media influencers
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how gender norms shape the experiences of social media influencers (SMIs) and consumers when engaging in pro-social initiatives and to develop a conceptual and practical framework to guide social marketers in designing gender responsive campaigns that feature SMIs. This is important because SMIs operating in the pro-social domain face gendered marginalisation that can undermine both campaign effectiveness and SMI safety, yet practical guidance on how to address these dynamics remains limited. title: Clos(ur)e to professionalism? An international comparison of the effect of occupational closure on the income of adult educators
abstract: The development of professionalism among adult educators is widely regarded as essential for ensuring the quality and effectiveness of adult learning and education (ALE) in the face of major societal challenges. However, employment conditions and institutional structures in the field remain heterogeneous and fragmented across Europe. The study investigates whether occupational closure – defined as the formal regulation of access to a profession – is associated with income differences among adult educators. institutions: German Institute for Adult Education – Leibniz Centre for Lifelong Learning

title: Institutionalizing Folk Literature: Anthologies, Journals, and Disciplinary Boundaries in Mainland China
abstract: A prominent study of the founding journals of Chinese folkloristics after 1949 argued that Zhong Jingwen’s definition of folk literature as the “oral creation of the laboring people” served both to establish political legitimacy and to exclude traditional Chinese opera (xiqu 戏曲) and professional storytelling (shuochang 说唱) from the discipline. title: Composition gradients in sub-Neptunes: K2-18 b and TOI-270 d as case studies
abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18,b and TOI-270,d. We compare purely adiabatic models with distinct layers against models that include composition gradients and stable non-convective regions. title: Study Abroad for Climate Justice: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Sustainability Engagement in International Education
abstract: This study explores discourses of sustainability (dis)engagement across 22 study abroad websites under different US higher education institutions. Utilizing Critical Discourse Analysis and a novel analytical framework– “Study Abroad for Climate Justice” (SACJ)– the research examines how textual and visual representations of study abroad support and/or belie climate justice. The SACJ framework identifies four categories of discourses: Status Quo, Awareness, Leadership, and Reconstruction. journal: Frontiers The Interdisciplinary Journal of Study Abroad

title: ¿Puede un menor de edad ser juzgado por jurados? Aproximaciones desde el sistema procesal penal santafesino
abstract: El presente trabajo tiene por objeto analizar la aplicabilidad del juicio por jurados respecto de personas menores de edad a quienes se les atribuye la comisión de delitos graves comprendidos dentro de la competencia de dicho instituto. En tal sentido, el estudio no se orienta a evaluar la necesidad o conveniencia de esta implementación, sino a determinar, en una primera aproximación, si el modelo constitucional de juicio por jurados admite que personas menores de edad puedan quedar comprendidas en el ámbito de aplicación de las distintas legislaciones provinciales que regulan esta forma de ju

title: How Religious Leaders Become Nonbelievers: A Four-Stage Model of Deconversion
abstract: This article introduces a four-stage model of clergy deconversion (ontological secularization) based on grounded theory analysis of The Clergy Project, a global community of religious professionals who have lost their faith in the supernatural. Drawing on 59 in-depth interviews and surveys with clergy from 24 countries and multiple religious traditions, along with analysis of more than 300 autobiographical profiles, the study employs a netnographic approach combined with grounded theory to examine how deeply committed practitioners transition from a supernatural to a naturalistic worldview. institutions: Defense Language Institute Foreign Language Center

title: Mapping grey areas in international legal approaches to the failure of cryptoasset firms
abstract: The failure of cryptoasset firms, including FTX, Celsius and Voyager, has exposed a fundamental tension between the operational realities of cryptoasset markets and their legal characterisation. These cases demonstrate that centralisation does not eliminate insolvency risk; rather, it can obscure where that risk materialises and against whom claims may be brought. Insolvency law must therefore engage with firms that present as decentralised or borderless whilst retaining identifiable corporate structures, assets and creditor relationships. title: Between the hammer and the anvil: Collaborative states, MNES and development
abstract: Most governments continue to attract MNE investment as the optimal means of achieving economic development. However, MNEs have had a patchy record in addressing inequalities. Contemporaneously, the zeitgeist over the last decade has leaned toward greater state interventionism as part of inward-looking domestic policies, where the state is the main actor shaping economic development. We argue that successful developmental outcomes require neither the hollowing out of the state nor heavy-handed interventionism, but rather a collaborative state that strategically coordinates the MNE-state nexus.
institutions: Instituto Centroamericano de Administración de Empresas

title: Costos de Fricción del Comercio en América Latina
abstract: The barriers that arise in international trade are the costs that countries assume to export and import. These costs are called friction costs. They can be tangible, such as geographic and administrative barriers, and they can be intangible, such as institutional and cultural barriers. title: Castle tourism: A six dimensional (CoGVAT) planning model
abstract: This study conceptualises castle tourism as a specialised form of cultural heritage tourism and presents a six-dimensional theoretical framework to address its fragmented scholarship. Previous research has largely focused on isolated case studies or thematic approaches, neglecting the connected processes linking preservation, management, and regional development. title: The evolving role of educators in university: Navigating workloads and student mental health challenges
abstract: Purpose: This study examined the mental health and well-being of university teaching staff at a large Canadian university and how they are impacted by increasing student mental health (SMH) challenges. Design: Using mixed methods, we collected data from 48 university teaching staff of all ranks and across all disciplines. Quantitative scales evaluated teaching staffs’ mental health, well-being, stress, and their perceptions and experiences about SMH. title: Land, Law, and Debt: The Geography of U.S. Military Infrastructure Finance in Korea
abstract: Recent geographical research has emphasized the co-production of military and civilian space, particularly through urban processes. Research in geographies of militarism has included analysis of military base conversions and analysis of shuttered military lands as vehicles of capital accumulation. Focusing on the case of Korea, this article posits military infrastructure finance as a generative research area in geographies of militarism. title: Stress Levels and Teaching Performance of Secondary English Teachers in Bantayan, Cebu Province
abstract: This study examined occupational stress and teaching performance among 100 secondary English teachers from 14 schools on Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, during the 2024-2025 academic year. A descriptive-comparative and correlational research design was employed. Data were collected using a perceived work stress questionnaire and existing Classroom Observation Tool ratings. The findings indicated a moderate overall stress level, with work overload and role ambiguity emerging as prominent workplace concerns. journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

title: Food insecurity is associated with increased food environment interactions and lower dietary adequacy among peri-urban Tanzanian households
abstract: Africa is disproportionately burdened by food insecurity and HIV, yet few tools examine how food environments influence diets. Understanding urban food acquisition patterns is essential for designing targeted interventions, particularly in rapidly urbanizing East Africa. This observational study (2019–2020) examined associations between food insecurity, household food purchases, and dietary adequacy among 312 adults living with HIV in peri-urban Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. title: Towards A Greener Planet: International Legal Mechanisms for Sustainable Energy Technologies
abstract: Given the fact that there has been a sudden shift in the climate, there is an urge for the world to adopt sustainable energy practices. This article aims to examine the role of the international legal mechanism in promoting the usage of sustainable energy and its widespread implementation. Aside from that, this article also analyzes some significant agreements, such as the Paris Agreement and other relevant multilateral agreements that hold the purpose to promote the use of energy that can meet current energy needs without jeopardizing future resources and energy supplies. journal: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science

title: La arquitectura jurídica del derecho de huelga: entre la garantía y la restricción
abstract: El trabajo analiza la reconfiguración del derecho de huelga como manifestación inherente de la libertad sindical y la negociación colectiva, a partir de los pronunciamientos más recientes en el seno tanto del sistema universal como del sistema europeo de derechos humanos. title: Functional role of CatSper channels and opioid receptors in acrosome reaction and apoptotic-like processes in ram spermatozoa
abstract: The Cation/calcium Channel of Sperm (CatSper) and opioid receptors play critical roles in mammalian fertilization, yet their characterization and precise functions in ram spermatozoa remain not fully understood. This study aimed to determine the presence, membrane domain distribution, and functional roles of CatSper subunits (1-4) and μ-, δ- and κ-opioid receptors in ram spermatozoa. title: The Moderation of the Hybrid Function of the Cooperative in the Relationship between Structuring Organizations and Intercooperation
abstract: There are research gaps regarding the involvement of key stakeholders in cooperative relations, as well as aspects involving intangible advantages generated by intercooperation. Thus, the present study aimed to identify the influences of structuring organizations on intercooperation. For this reason, a qualitative research was carried out through data collection through documentary research and semi-structured interviews conducted with cooperatives in Brazil and Spain, which were analyzed using the content-analysis technique. title: Entre la norma y la realidad: la aplicación de los MASC como requisito de procedibilidad en distintos procesos judiciales
abstract: La introducción de los Medios Adecuados de Solución de Controversias (MASC) como requisito de procedibilidad por la Ley Orgánica 1/2025 constituye una de las reformas más transformadoras del proceso civil. Su objetivo es promover la resolución consensuada de conflictos y reducir la carga de trabajo de los tribunales. Sin embargo, el artículo pone de manifiesto que esta profunda modificación no ha ido acompañada de una adaptación coherente del resto de instituciones procesales, generando importantes lagunas, contradicciones e incertidumbres interpretativas. title: Human rights due diligence and corporate human rights litigation
abstract: The present paper examines whether human rights due diligence (HRDD) litigation improves access to remedy for victims of cross-border corporate human rights violations by addressing the legal barriers traditionally associated with more general corporate human rights litigation. title: The Care-ful Work of Climate Litigation: A Study of Women Climate Defenders
abstract: Climate litigation, often led by women, requires demanding work with little acknowledgement or support. The article argues that this work is a form of caring labour aimed at reproducing human society as well as the environment within which we are enmeshed. Rethinking care as including the environment draws from Indigenous ideas of ‘care for Country’, ecofeminist conceptions of our relationality with the rest of nature, and some versions of social reproduction theory. title: The Conservation of Absence: How Dead Elephants Animate the Living in Malaysia’s Nature Reserves
abstract: The origins of wildlife conservation in Malaysia are usually presented as part of a narrative about British imperial environmental consciousness that ushered in the formation of game reserves, wildlife sanctuaries and national parks worldwide. However, these spaces are more than just protected sites; they are also layered cultural landscapes that embed complex stories of inter-species interactions. title: Ley aplicable a la propiedad de los meteoritos: Estudio crítico de Derecho internacional privado
abstract: El presente trabajo aborda las múltiples, poliédricas y caleidoscópicas vicisitudes de la aplicación de la regla lex rei sitae a la propiedad de los meteoritos. title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Spodumene Processing Routes for Battery Grade Lithium Hydroxide Production in Australia, China and Finland
abstract: The increasing demand for lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for sustainable and resilient supply chains for battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM). This study presents a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of three hard-rock spodumene-based LHM supply routes: the conventional Australian–Chinese route (BASE), integrated Australian production (I-AUS), and integrated European production in Finland (I-FIN). title: The Place of Ecological Themes in Bulgarian Philosophy and Civic Education: Curriculum Analysis, Interim Teacher Survey Findings and a Plan for Follow-up Teacher Interviews
abstract: Environmental challenges are not only scientific and technological problems. They are also ethical, civic and educational questions concerning responsibility, justice, human action and the conditions of shared life. This article presents an interim stage of an ongoing doctoral study examining the place of ecological themes in philosophy and civic education in Bulgarian secondary schools and the conditions under which teachers of these subjects might foster ecological reflection. title: Biometría y privacidad en la seguridad aeroportuaria: estándares, límites y dilemas en perspectiva jurídica transnacional
abstract: La biometría se ha incorporado al transporte aéreo para acelerar la identificación de pasajeros y reforzar el control fronterizo. Cuando el rostro, la huella dactilar o el iris se convierten en credenciales de acceso, la seguridad entra en tensión con la vida privada y derechos fundamentales. title: Indoor microclimate shapes resting patterns of Anopheles funestus in south-eastern Tanzania
abstract: Indoor resting patterns of malaria vectors are changing, potentially driven by housing design including roofing materials, wall construction and associated indoor thermal and humidity-steered microclimates. This study quantifies how microclimatic gradients shape the resting choices of Anopheles funestus in southeastern Tanzania, testing whether different indoor zones create distinct thermal and humidity niches that influence mosquito microhabitat selection. abstract: Central Asian countries’ economic integration into world trade has recently been reoriented by regional integration schemes or investment plans supported by China and Russia. Predominantly, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is expected to ease infrastructure development in the region. However, the reduced effectiveness of past trade regionalisation attempts has recently hindered intraregional trade growth. abstract: Background/Purpose Organizations increasingly depend on operating in digital environments, where planning and implementing technical security and protective measures alone is not a sufficient prerequisite for business effectiveness. The aim of this paper is to clarify the concept of security culture and to explain how it emerges and functions in organizations. title: Swedish teachers’ perceived professional action competence in sustainability and climate change education
abstract: This study aims to explore how in-service school teachers in Sweden perceive their professional action competence (PAC) in Sustainability and Climate Change Education (SCCE). Drawing on data from an exploratory survey involving 202 primary and secondary school teachers in Sweden, the study examines three core dimensions of PAC in SCCE: professional knowledge, self-efficacy, and willingness to teach. title: The Pathogenic Episteme: Addressing Public Health Underdevelopment in Africa
abstract: Background: Health and disease are socially constructed phenomena, shaped by the interplay of knowledge and power that determines the distribution of social determinants of health. The underdevelopment of public health in Africa is rooted in both historical and contemporary injustices. Racist policies, founded on beliefs in racial and cultural superiority, established frameworks of moral inclusion and exclusion that designated African people as “outsiders” and subjected them to exploitation. title: Opening doors and sustaining pathways: A policy architecture for embedding gender diversity in corporate leadership
abstract: This article examines how gender quotas interact with social welfare systems to shape women’s pathways to corporate boardrooms. Through a comparative analysis of Norway and Iceland, where long-standing quota mandates operate alongside extensive parental leave and accessible childcare, and Ghana and South Africa, where welfare provision is uneven despite constitutional and voluntary commitments to inclusion, the study evaluates the durability of board diversity reforms. title: Does Policy Capacity Influence Environmental Policy Outcomes in Developing Countries?
abstract: Empirical evidence on the impact of policy capacity on environmental policy outcomes remains limited in developing countries. This study addresses this gap by proposing a governance‐based policy capacity measure, using the World Governance Indicators, that captures the governance and institutional conditions associated with policy capacity development and mobilization at the organizational and systemic levels. title: The Afrotropical Lepidostomatidae (Trichoptera)
abstract: The Afrotropical Lepidostomatidae are reviewed and classified into six species groups: Lepidostoma turkum group, L. sjoestedti group, L. scotti group, L. bilobatum group, L. brunneum group, and L. nudatum group. title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. title: Blind tests of a simple-body model of submarine target strength on open benchmarks
abstract: Finite-element and boundary-element models of a submarine's sonar echo need a mesh and a solver, and their cost grows quickly with frequency. SSR-Sim takes an analytical route. The hull is cut into a few simple bodies, the echo of each is a closed-form result of geometrical acoustics or of the Kirchhoff approximation, the surface enters through a plane-wave reflection coefficient, and the echoes add in energy. title: Ionospheric bow waves during Starship Flight 14: coupling through vented propellant
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations of Starship Flight 14 show clear bow-shaped waves in detrended total electron content (dTEC), including during motor-off coast. These observations raise a coupling problem because the spacecraft hull is small compared with the thermospheric molecular mean free path. Sustained visible release in flight video motivates the hypothesis that vented, unburned propellant supplies a much larger interaction region capable of producing a fluid response. title: HybridQC: Hardware-Grounded Simulation of Tightly Integrated Hybrid Quantum-Classical Systems
abstract: Hybrid quantum–classical performance depends on how quantum processors share classical compute, controllers, memory, and communication links. Circuit simulators and provider measurements expose kernel and job behavior, but leave topology-level questions about controller bottlenecks, quantum capacity, and mixed-workload contention unanswered. abstract: Large-eddy simulations (LES) of the convective atmospheric boundary layer (CBL) are used to investigate velocity variance statistics in turbulent sheared convection. The thirteen simulations span conditions from weak convection with longitudinal rolls to free penetrative convection with no mean wind. abstract: Powerful generative models including large language and vision models have demonstrated success across a wide range of content generation, editing and manipulation tasks via end-to-end prompt-based generation. However, current assessment of the quality of generative content manipulation remains subjective, limiting scientific understanding of model capabilities. title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. abstract: EmbeddingGemma-300M is a small open embedder, and used as released it finds the right passage first for 60.8% of the Kazakh Belebele retrieval questions. abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. abstract: Summary The Critically Endangered Fiji Petrel Pseudobulweria macgillivrayi is one of the rarest and least studied bird species globally. title: Reef resilience and demise on the NW shelf of Australia during the warm Miocene
abstract: During the Miocene, sea surface temperature (SSTs) and CO 2 exceeded modern levels. abstract: Benthic communities form the foundation of food webs in coastal and shelf seas worldwide. However, these communities face severe threats from anthropogenic bottom-disturbing activities. abstract: Baited remote underwater video stations (BRUVs) are widely used to survey fish assemblages, but their application to freshwater mammals remains poorly explored. abstract: This study aimed to investigate the integrated in vivo impact of progressive high altitude on metabolic, inflammatory, and vascular adaptation pathways and to assess their modulation by biological sex and anthropometric profile. abstract: Marine botany was one of the natural history ‘crazes’ in nineteenth-century Britain, the field particularly attracting many women from various social backgrounds. abstract: The Quindío department covers a small area, yet it harbors a high proportion of Colombia’s bird species. abstract: The taxonomy of the native New Zealand blue mussel has long been debated and is presently unclear. title: The Evolution of British Army Adventurous Training: 1960-2008
abstract: From the early 1960s Adventurous Training (AT) was seen as good training for active service and was encouraged in the British Army. In 1973 it was decided that AT should be delivered on a joint service basis with each service delivering the AT relevant to that service. In 2002 Army AT was centralised under the Adventurous Training Group (Army). This article examines the evolution of British Army AT and AT Policy in the period 1960 to 2008.

abstract: The Greater Male Region, (consist of Male, Hulhule, Hulhumale, Villingili, Gulhifalhu and Thilafushi) is the most densely populated urban cluster in the Maldives. Capital City Male' is one of the most densely populated City in the world. abstract: Influential strands of Island Studies have spent decades moving from the island as a bounded object towards relational, processual and generative islandness. This paper turns that critical achievement back upon itself by asking what work islandness is now being made to do. It situates this question within a wider orientation of contemporary thought, in which calls to ‘world the world otherwise’ increasingly seek critical purchase through relationality, attentiveness, immersion, care, opacity, fugitivity, and more-than-human responsiveness. title: A historical review of translocations of native bird species in Australia: the good, the bad and the perverse
abstract: The Australian bird fauna has undergone many changes since European colonisation in 1788. This review focuses on the role of translocations in these changes. Translocations began in the 1830s and have been undertaken for reasons that have varied over time. Many early translocations were done for utilitarian reasons, as foibles, or were the result of aviary escapes or release of captive birds. title: Blessings in Blue and White: An Iconological Study of Blue Jiaxie Bridal Textiles
abstract: Blue Jiaxie, an indigo clamp resist dyeing tradition in southern Zhejiang, China, combines opera imagery and auspicious motifs on bridal textiles. Although previous studies have documented its techniques and symbolic meanings, the relationship between pictorial organisation and marriage customs remains insufficiently explored. This study applies Panofsky’s iconological framework to examine how material form, motif combinations and bridal use shape interpretation. title: OUTDOOR SCULPTURES AS SYMBOLS OF IDENTITY AND SOURCE FOR HISTORICAL DOCUMENTATION: REFLECTION ON FIVE SELECTED SCULPTURES IN SOME TOWNS IN YORUBALAND, SOUTHWESTERN NIGERIA
abstract: The early histories of most ancient Yoruba towns in Southwestern Nigeria are derived primarily from oral traditions that have been transmitted across generations. These histories are deeply embedded in the people's folklore, praise poetry, and oral narratives. However, the reliability of oral tradition as a historical source has long been questioned because the transmission of information across successive generations may introduce distortions and inaccuracies. title: The Southern Route of the Great Silk Road in the Kushan Period: Archaeological Evidence of Trade Relations from Northern Bactria
abstract: This article examines the archaeological evidence for long-distance trade along the southern route of the Great Silk Road in Northern Bactria (present-day Surkhandarya region of Uzbekistan) during the Kushan period, 1st–3rd centuries AD. Drawing on published material from Old Termez, Kampyrtepa, Dalverzintepa, Zartepa and Ayrtam, the study analyses four groups of sources: coin finds, imported goods (Indian ivory, Roman and Mediterranean glass, Chinese mirrors and silk), ceramic assemblages, and Bactrian, Greek and Kharoshthi inscriptions. title: Wealth and Its Manifestations in the Traditional Culture of Alaska Natives Before and After the Onset of European Colonization
abstract: The subject addressed in this article has not yet received detailed scholarly attention, and the article aims to fill this gap. Conceptions of wealth and their embodiment in material objects and symbols were characteristic of all Alaska Native peoples—Aleuts, Indians, and Eskimos. title: Cognitive effects of first- and third-person perspectives on navigational safety and efficiency in ship operation learning
abstract: Remote ship operation involves analysing information from various perspectives. However, a standardized educational approach for training remote ship operators is lacking. This study addresses the challenges posed by the cognitive attributes of individuals using remote ship operation and monitoring systems by investigating how different perspectives (first-vs. third-person) impact skill acquisition in ship operation. title: A Two‐Stage Constant‐Voltage Wireless Power Transfer System and Its Design Method for Robotic Manipulators
abstract: To address the problems of limited motion range, cable wear, and reduced reliability caused by conventional power cables during continuous rotation of robotic manipulator joints, this paper proposes a two‐stage constant voltage wireless power transfer system based on a cascaded LCC‐S compensation topology and its design method. The system transfers electrical energy from the transmitter to two receivers through magnetic coupling, enabling simultaneous power supply to multiple joint loads of the manipulator without physical cable connections. title: Phylogenomics and taxonomic revision of Macropeplus (Monimiaceae, Laurales) reveal a remarkable hidden species and its unique habitat
abstract: Macropeplus is endemic to Brazil and found above 1000 m elevation in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado . Until this work, the four recognised species M. dentatus , M. friburgensis , M. ligustrinus and M. schwackeanus were initially separated by morphology and geographical distribution, with allopatric ranges. However, increased specimen collection and digital data have since revealed overlapping traits and sympatric distributions, making species delimitation challenging. title: Marvelous flowers of the arctic: resisting the taxonomic gaze in Hannimari Jokinen’s Mirabilis L.
abstract: This article examines Hannimari Jokinen’s installation Mirabilis L. as a critical intervention into the intertwined histories of colonial botany and Nordic racial science. We argue that the work made the mobility and circulation of colonial ideas spatially and affectively tangible by staging classification as a relational field shaped simultaneously by observation, resilience, and vulnerability. title: Checklist of the lichenised mycobiota in Aotearoa / New Zealand
abstract: Aotearoa / New Zealand has a diverse lichenised mycobiota, but the national flora treatment, now nearly 20 years old, has become increasingly outdated following taxonomic and nomenclatural changes, the description of new species, discovery of additional records, reassessment of historical records, and application of molecular phylogenetics. Subsequent national threat assessments have incorporated many of these changes, but were prepared for conservation assessment rather than as formal taxonomic checklists. abstract: This article examines the relationship between colonial conquest, territoriality, and identity reconfiguration in the historical trajectory of the Payayá people, associated with the Sertão das Jacobinas, a colonial zone of shifting boundaries in the centre of the captaincy that encompassed areas now associated with Chapada Diamantina and its Piemonte region in Bahia. abstract: This study examines how English-language online media in Indonesia frame the hantavirus crisis involving MV Hondius and how such framing is relevant to tourism marketing communication during a transnational health crisis. Using qualitative content analysis and framing analysis, the study analyzes 16 unique and relevant news articles archived from Jakarta Globe and The Jakarta Post between 4 and 31 May 2026 with the keywords “MV Hondius”, “hantavirus”, and “Andes virus”. title: Atmospheric Borders
abstract: What kinds of atmospheres do borders produce? And what kinds of bordering are produced by atmospheric conditions? This paper introduces the concept of ‘atmospheric borders’ as a way of conceptualising the ephemeral but sometimes overbearing elemental capacities of bordering processes. We build upon the abundant critical scholarship that has theorised borders as processual, spatially distributed and always in the process of being made an unmade. title: The Activities of Asinius Pollio in 40 BC: Venetia, Salona, and Brundisium
abstract: The article examines the activities of Gaius Asinius Pollio from the Perusine War to the conclusion of the Treaty of Brundisium in 40 BC, with particular attention to his role in Venetia, his alliance with Domitius Ahenobarbus, and his activities on the eastern Adriatic coast and at Salona. title: Von Rhönbussard bis ASW 28. Eine diachrone Korpusanalyse offizieller Namen von Segelflugzeugen
abstract: This article provides the first systematic analysis of the official names of sailplanes. It is based on a diachronic corpus of 405 name families from various countries covering the period from 1920 to 2000, compiled primarily from works by Martin Simons and official sources from manufacturers and institutions. The analysis examines linguistic name bases, semantic domains of reference and naming, and name-formation processes. title: Against the Archive: Decolonial Historical Fiction and Indigenous Representations in Micheliny Verunschk’s O som do rugido da onça
abstract: Historical fiction provides a powerful platform to challenge hegemonic narratives and amplify marginalized voices excluded from the archives. However, little attention has been paid to how Indigenous perspectives can reshape understandings of colonialism and capitalism within this genre. This article examines the decolonial historiographical metafiction O Som do Rugido da Onça (Micheliny Verunschk, Brazil, 2021), which recounts the story of an Indigenous girl taken from Brazil to Munich in the 19th century for scientific exhibition. title: Strategic Restraint to Punitive Deterrence: Indian Doctrinal Shift and its Implications for Pakistan
abstract: This research examines India’s shift from strategic restraint to punitive deterrence and multi-domain coercion, focusing on its implications for Pakistan’s security and South Asia's strategic stability. It analyzes the drivers of India’s doctrinal transformation, including terrorism-related threats, military experiences, domestic nationalism, technological modernization, and regional competition. The study examines India’s crisis behavior since 2016, particularly the use of cross-border strikes, airpower, precision weapons, information operations, and emerging cyber and maritime capabilities.

abstract: Este artículo propone emplear la noción económica de «falla de mercado» como criterio dogmático —operado a través de la teoría de las cláusulas generales— para reforzar la comprensión del contrato y, de manera más intensa, en la protección del consumidor. title: Burn the Ships: How History Made a Metaphor
abstract: At some point while scrolling through social media, you have probably come across the motivational phrase “Burn the Ships.” It represents a commitment to move forward without the security of a backup plan, to face challenges, and to step out of one's comfort zone. But this phrase is more than just a motivational slogan; it carries a wider historical narrative behind it. America's Sardanapalus: Byron, Delacroix, Orientalism, and Citizen Kane
abstract: Orson Welles's film Citizen Kane (1941) illustrates thirst for power and the destruction of a larger‐than‐life but flawed man. The movie is filled with historical allusions, and among these, we introduce the idea here that Citizen Kane suggests the tragic demise of the acquisitive, ancient Assyrian ruler Sardanapalus. Aspects of the film relate to the legendary Sardanapalus, especially to the text of the well‐received Sardanapalus: A Tragedy (published 1821) by English Romantic writer Lord Byron. title: Beyond Contested Logistics: “Prelogistics” and the Industrial Limits of Combat Power
abstract: The upstream industrial capacity to produce war materiel, a gap the authors term “prelogistics,” is a constraining determinant of American combat power. Contested logistics addresses sustaining forces under active interdiction. This “prelogistics” framework instead analyzes the industrial base and its ability to regenerate capabilities at wartime rates as the primary constraint on warfighting endurance. title: Biduk Kajang: Navigating the Musi River toward Evening and Its Decline
abstract: Biduk Kajang was a traditional watercraft associated with riverine trade and domestic life in South Sumatra, particularly among communities in Kayuagung, Ogan Komering Ilir. This study examines its historical development, decline, and significance in the changing relationship between riverine communities and the Musi River network. Using the historical method, the research draws on archival images, published literature, semi-structured interviews, and field observations, with attention to source criticism and triangulation. title: Liminal Spaces and the Search for Identity in Washington Black
abstract: Canadian writer Esi Edugyan’s Washington Black traces the ourney of Washington Black, an enslaved black boy, and depicts the fluidity of his identity and his psychological trauma within liminal spaces. Drawing on Victor Turner’s theory of rites of passage, this article examines three dimensions: the confinement of the enslaved identity in the separation stage, the struggle of the marginal figure in the liminal stage, and the failure of social incorporation and the resulting uncertainty about identity in the absence of the aggregation stage. abstract: The Great Lakes region in Africa is an ethnic-geopolitical “hornet’s nest” burdened with serious problems at the meeting of several worlds. The three francophone countries that emerged in the former Belgian (or in the case of Rwanda and Burundi, German for a few decades before) colonial territories are usually classified by some divisions as part of the Central African region, which also includes Chad, the Central African Republic, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon. abstract: The purpose of this article is to offer a new overview of the biography of the German-Bohemian bandmaster, journalist, and composer Josef Sawerthal, while also providing an account of the extent and significance of his documentary estate held at the National Museum – Czech Museum of Music in Prague. Josef Sawerthal (1819, Polepy – 1893, Litoměřice) came from a peasant family in Polepy and was one of the first pupils of Josef Kail at the Prague Conservatoire. abstract: Background The genus Bartonella has gained increasing attention due to the growing number of newly described species and the identification of novel reservoirs and vectors. This is particularly relevant for public health, as several Bartonella species have zoonotic potential. Rodents are key reservoirs, harboring high richness and prevalence of Bartonella species, and numerous rodent-associated Bartonella have been linked to human disease. title: Localizing Twelver Shi‘i Clerical Authority in East and West Africa: Contrasting Prophetic and Academic Genealogies
abstract: How do Muslim leaders claim Islamic authority in different geographical contexts? This article presents comparative ethnographic case studies of Twelver Shi‘a in East and West Africa who take divergent approaches to following a dominant marja‘ , a supreme religious-juridical authority. Efforts in Senegal to pave an indigenous Shi‘i path independent of traditional, geographically situated religious power structures are contrasted with Tanzanian links to Ayatollah Shirazi, who is outside the Shi‘i mainstream. title: Individual songbirds call and answer each other during natural nocturnal migration
abstract: Nocturnal songbird migration has long been pictured as solitary, yet migrants call in flight and the airspace they cross is dense with the calls of others. Flight calls are almost always recorded from the ground, from unseen birds of unknown identity, age, and sex, so what a single bird does vocally across a night has been unknown. We radio-tagged Swainson’s thrushes ( Catharus ustulatus ) with microphone transmitters and followed them by vehicle through entire nocturnal migratory flights, recording the calls of known individuals over 34 h aloft by eight birds. title: Fitness to Fly: A Comprehensive Review of Air Travel in Patients with Chronic Respiratory Diseases
abstract: Commercial air travel exposes passengers to hypobaric hypoxia, reduced barometric pressure, and limited access to emergency medical support. While these physiologic changes are well tolerated by healthy travelers, individuals with chronic respiratory diseases often have reduced ventilatory or gas-exchange reserve, placing them at higher risk for in-flight hypoxemia, symptom exacerbation, and barotrauma. abstract: This paper constructs a comparative historical framework for analysing the origins, expansions, and long-term trajectories of Eurasian steppe nomadic societies. Focusing on four major nomadic traditions—Indo-European, Turkic, Mongolic, and Tungusic—it traces their emergence from the Bronze Age through to the early modern period, with particular attention to patterns of migration, political formation, and imperial continuity across Inner Eurasia. abstract: The Quaternary Eifel volcanic fields are among Central European intraplate volcanic systems, with eruptions as recent as ∼11 ka and ongoing evidence for magmatic activity, yet detailed lithospheric structure and magma migration remain poorly constrained. Here, we present high‐resolution receiver function images from the Eifel Large‐N experiment, which reveal Variscan lithospheric structures modified by Cenozoic volcanism. abstract: Religion is known to be one of the common factors of conflicts in contemporary world. The introduction of religious sects and denominations in many parts of Nigeria compounded the causes of conflicts that trickled down to Goemailand and become one of the major problems that is bedeviling the area. The paper studied religious superiority and fundamentalism in Goemailand and interrogated the views that a particular group holds that their belief is the only absolute truth and superior faith that must be accepted. abstract: We report on the first detection of a gamma-ray ground-level enhancement (GLE) that occurred on 2025 November 11 (designated as GLE # 77), using ground-based gamma-ray detectors deployed at the Antarctic and Arctic stations. The event was associated with an intense X-class flare, a fast coronal mass ejection, and a strong solar energetic particle (SEP) event. title: Assessing climate change impacts on Eucalyptus productivity in Brazil using high-resolution CMIP6 models
abstract: Climate change threatens global forestry, including plantations of Eucalyptus, the world’s most widely planted forest genus. As the largest global producer, Brazil has plantations in climate-sensitive regions where climate change impacts are expected under future climates. This study assessed the impacts of climate change on Eucalyptus productivity in Brazil using the Agroecological Zone Model (AZM-FAO). abstract: Digital transformation in Social Studies learning needs to be accompanied by local wisdom integration to ensure contextual and meaningful learning experiences. This study aimed to explore students’ learning experiences in using local wisdom-based digital learning materials in Social Studies education at SMP Negeri 15 Sijunjung. A qualitative case study design was employed. title: The Sino-Soviet Border Conflict of March 1969: Escalation, Command, and Intelligence on the USSR’s Far Eastern Front
abstract: This article uses the March 1969 Sino-Soviet border clashes at Damanskii (Zhenbao) Island to explore the dynamics of military escalation, intelligence, and command and control. Drawing on recently declassified Soviet and Chinese archival documents and memoirs, the article reveals that Soviet leaders were deeply worried about escalation, at least initially. title: India-Pakistan Nuclear race and its Impacts on Regional Security (1998-2022)
abstract: India-Pakistan nuclear competition has been a defining element of South Asian geopolitics, influencing regional security dynamics. Using the conceptual frameworks of the balance of power, deterrence, mutual assure destruction and security dilemma, this study focuses on the India-Pakistan nuclear race and its impacts for regional security. title: Negotiating green dreams with a spectral state: Struggles over public housing and ecological tending in waterfront redevelopment at the urban-Southern frontier
abstract: Following 20 years of waterfront redevelopment in Sant'Elia, a public housing neighbourhood in Cagliari, Sardinia, this paper asks how struggles over public housing can work against the post-politicisation of sustainability discourses enacted by entrepreneurial green urbanism. I show how, in Sant’Elia, municipal green development discourses articulate an apolitical salvific future of landscape restoration that reproduces dichotomies between worthy and unworthy subjectivities and materialities. abstract: The Neotropical tailed caecilians of the genera Epicrionops and Amazops (Rhinatrematidae) remain poorly known. Here, we examined their morphology, distribution, and molecular phylogenetic relationships using specimens from Ecuador. Our review of museum collections expands the empirical basis for understanding variation in these genera and reveals broader geographic and morphological diversity than previously recognised. title: Tracing the Evolution of Anti-Kremlin Communication and Audience Engagement on Telegram During the Russia–Ukraine Conflict
abstract: During Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Telegram became an important platform for both state-aligned communication and opposition-oriented discourse. Over time, anti-Kremlin Telegram channels emerged as prominent venues for dissent amid increasing restrictions on independent political expression. This study examines how anti-Kremlin communication and audience engagement evolved across seven phases of the conflict. title: Revitalizing the Akhoykoy Folklore to Solve Ecological Conflicts of Indigenous Papuans
abstract: Akhoykoy is an oral tradition of the Sentani Indigenous community in Yokiwa Village, Papua, that functions as a medium of musical communication, a repository of collective memory, and a local knowledge system representing the community's social, ecological, and spiritual relationships. However, previous studies have primarily examined Akhoykoy as an object of folklore, performativity, or social function, leaving its ecological and communicative dimensions largely underexplored. title: Provisioning secure and sustainable food systems: a consumption processes perspective for researching and addressing global food insecurities
abstract: Drawing from over a decade of research and community engagement in the Caribbean, the article argues that a ‘consumption processes’ perspective adds novelty to the body of work seeking to design secure and sustainable food systems globally. Travelling with the conceptual resources of the sociology of consumption from the Global North to the Anglo-Caribbean, we see that the food insecurities faced are negotiated and can be further resolved when seeing the problem from the point of view of consumption rather than production as a starting point in the research process. title: ‘Time to Go’ where: on Margaret Atwood’s reimagining of ageing in Stone Mattress
abstract: In Stone Mattress, Margaret Atwood examines the plight of older adults influenced by consumer culture in late-capitalist Western societies and links their struggles to the development of Canadian literature. Drawing on Jameson’s critique of late capitalism and Baudrillard’s explication of consumer society, this essay untangles how anti-ageing culture commodifies the ageing body, transforms longevity into a consumable ideal and reinforces the imperative to transcend bodily decline. title: Modelling symbols among the first-sedentary communities: Emergence of clay figurines in Epipaleolithic Southwest Asia
abstract: The emergence of clay technologies and their use in symbolic practices marks a momentous techno-symbolic innovation for human societies. While in North Africa, Europe and East Asia, this innovation was sporadically attested during the Upper Palaeolithic, in Southwest Asia, it has been commonly believed to emerge in full much later, as one of the innovations associated with Neolithic agricultural societies. title: The novum at the margins: Vernacular modernity and Assamese Kalpabigyan (1937–2017)
abstract: Scholarship on Indian science fiction still concentrates on Bengali, Hindi, and English-language writing; the Assamese tradition of kalpabigyan, active since 1937, remains almost absent from international research. This article offers one of the first sustained accounts of it in English—not as a survey, but as a set of paired close readings that ask what Assamese kalpabigyan does as literature. It begins from the poetics of the genre developed in Shantanu Tamuli’s editorial introduction to his 2017 Sahitya Akademi anthology, and reads four of the stories he canonised in two pairs. title: Encrucijadas. Las emociones y los campos magnéticos en las metodologías nómadas
abstract: Este artículo propone una reflexión metodológica sobre el papel de las emociones en la investigación nómada, y parte de la experiencia del proyecto Brasilien am Main, una investigación sobre la diáspora brasileña en Fráncfort del Meno. Frente a los modelos de investigación planificados y orientados a objetivos predefinidos, la investigación nómada en Brasilien am Main propone una apertura a los encuentros fortuitos, las sensaciones y las emociones que surgen en el trabajo de campo como fuentes legítimas de conocimiento. title: The Effects of Crown–Noble Conflicts on Fifteenth‐Century Scottish Towns
abstract: Historians are starting to more readily appreciate that, during the fifteenth century, towns became important players in national politics within Scotland. This article contributes to the growing body of work on Scottish towns by examining instances in which they were the victims of noble violence, committed at various points by leading aristocratic families including cadet branches of the royal house of Stewart, the lordship of the Isles and the earls of Douglas. title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
abstract: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation. We first train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relations, and scene structure without paired robot-motion supervision. title: Exposure and remediation in the French maritime sector: a passive measurement of 129 organisations
abstract: Maritime transport and ports are essential entities under the EU NIS2 directive, but there is little public data on the external exposure of the sector in France. In March 2026, after physical attacks on Western interests in the Middle East raised the risk of cyber retaliation against French maritime operators, we assessed the internet-facing attack surface of 129 organisations: 103 French companies and 26 international operators active in French waters. title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
abstract: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. title: Cross-scale interactions of ocean circulations in the Northwest Pacific in a submesoscale-permitting model
abstract: Ocean circulations strongly interact with each other and transfer energy across horizontal scales. These cross-scale interactions regulate the ocean energy budget and drive variability of large-scale circulations and climate. The Northwest Pacific features rich multi-scale circulations due to interactions among the Kuroshio, eddies, and bottom topography. title: THE SEA AS A CINEMATIC ARCHIVE: MARITIME MEMORY, COASTAL EPISTEMOLOGIES, AND THE POLITICS OF BLUE BELONGING IN TAMIL FILM MANDAADI
abstract: This research paper provides an exhaustive theoretical examination of Mathimaran Pugazhendhi’s landmark 2026 Tamil film Mandaadi, conceptualizing it as a transformative text that reconfigures South Asian film studies through the critical paradigm of the Blue Humanities. Historically, Indian commercial and art cinema has maintained an overwhelming terracentric orientation, framing agrarian struggle, urban migration, and terrestrial land rights as the primary sites of subaltern agency and socio-political contestation. title: Mobilization of Geogenic Contaminants Induced by Seawater Intrusion in Coastal Aquifers Globally
abstract: Seawater intrusion deteriorates freshwater quality in coastal aquifers, threatening billions of people worldwide. While its impacts on freshwater scarcity and salinization are well documented, the associated mobilization of geogenic contaminants remains unclear. This study critically reviews the current knowledge on the global distribution, underlying biogeochemical mechanisms, specific triggering scenarios, management implications, and predictive modeling advances of seawater-intrusion-induced contaminant mobilization. title: Security dilemma and strategic hedging: policy challenges of U.S. Asia-Pacific alliances in the East Sea
abstract: This article explores the security dilemma in the Asia-Pacific, particularly in the East Sea, where one nation’s effort to enhance security often provokes insecurity in others. It emphasizes U.S. alliances with Japan, Australia, and the Philippines as China rises in power. These allies are crucial for containing China and ensuring access to Southeast Asia, but they struggle to balance ties with both Washington and Beijing. title: Never Empty
abstract: Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in the Roya Valley on the French-Italian border following a climate disaster, this text discusses listening and composing as practices of multispecies attunement. These practices, inspired by the Deep Listening method as developed and defined by Pauline Oliveros, help access the sounding world beyond the languages and stories told by human interlocutors. title: Juvenile coral assemblages reflect adult coral composition after a marine heatwave on the Great Barrier Reef
abstract: Coral reefs on the southern Great Barrier Reef experienced widespread bleaching during the 2024 marine heatwave, but the structure of juvenile coral assemblages following this event remains poorly resolved. We surveyed juvenile and adult scleractinian corals across 14 lagoonal patch reefs at One Tree Island in July 2025 to quantify post-disturbance juvenile abundance, taxonomic composition and life-history strategy representation. title: Mosaics with Marine Representations from the Archives of Rome: Revisions and Updates
abstract: Numerous documents, sketches, drawings, and photographs are preserved in the Archives of Rome, depicting archaeological discoveries made during excavations carried out between the late 1800s and the early decades of the 1900s, as part of the urban development of Rome, the capital of Italy. title: Coordinated Scheduling of Hydrogen Production and Flexible Loads in Offshore Wind-Powered Underwater Data Centers
abstract: Offshore wind-powered hydrogen production is increasingly recognized as an effective pathway for improving renewable energy utilization and facilitating the decarbonization of energy systems. However, the lack of flexible, high-demand local consumption scenarios limits the effective integration of offshore wind energy. In this context, underwater data centers (UDCs), characterized by high energy demand and operational flexibility, constitute a promising solution as controllable loads to support hydrogen-based energy systems. abstract: The lead-up to the Great Oxidation Event (GOE; between 2.5 and 2.2 Ga) was arguably as consequential as the event itself, yet substantial uncertainties remain regarding the timing and magnitude of oxygen rise in early Earth’s oceans. title: INTERPOL’s Role in Fighting Human Trafficking in Southeast Asia: Exploring the Cultural Aspects of International Police Coordination
abstract: Human trafficking, a form of transnational crime still present throughout the world, especially in Southeast Asia, threatens regional security and human rights. This paper examines INTERPOL’s role in facilitating cooperation among countries to combat this problem through communication systems, global criminal databases, joint operations, and other tools that help law enforcement entities collaborate more efficiently. title: The evolution of the marine ’nitrostat’ across the Great Oxidation Event
abstract: The bioavailability of nitrogen and phosphorus is tightly coupled in the modern ocean, a concept known as the ’nitrostat’. Phosphorus is considered the ultimate limiting nutrient on geological timescales, while nitrogen supply is biologically modulated via nitrogen fixation and denitrification. This balance maintains relatively constant N:P ratios in seawater. title: Assessing the potential distribution of the endangered coral Polycyathus chaishanensis in Taiwan using environmental DNA metabarcoding
abstract: The scleractinian coral, Polycyathus chaishanensis , first discovered in the Chaishan region of southern Taiwan, is an endangered species covered by the Taiwan Wildlife Protection Act (2017). At present, its population continues to decline due to environmental pressures. To develop and implement effective conservation strategies, better understanding of the distribution of this species is essential. title: Temperature dependence and coupling of dissolved oxygen and pH in coastal habitats
abstract: Coastal waters experience daily fluctuations in oxygen (O2), carbon dioxide (CO2), and pH driven by respiration and photosynthesis, processes that are highly sensitive to temperature variations. As global temperatures continue to rise, both photosynthetic and respiratory rates are increasing, with respiration accelerating more rapidly. title: Impacts of combined ambitious marine and terrestrial carbon dioxide removal on major ocean stressors
abstract: Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation are major stressors impacting marine ecosystems. While Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) is necessary to meet climate targets, its potential to mitigate ocean stressors under realistic future scenarios remains understudied. Here, we use two Earth System Models to simulate ambitious deployments of Afforestation/Reforestation (AR) and Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) under the high emissions scenario SSP3-7.0. title: MacroTraits: a global trait data and information system for marine benthic ecology
abstract: For a long time, biological trait data have been a bottleneck in biodiversity research. Constraints of data unavailability and challenging analytical implementation are still obstacles to the investigation of functional biodiversity patterns. This is especially true in marine zoobenthic ecology where the use of biological traits became common much later than in terrestrial and freshwater ecology. Additionally, most of trait-based marine studies have dominantly been conducted in European waters while large gaps remain in other areas of the world. title: Mythological Depictions of Marine Themes in Hispano-Roman Mosaics: The Prominence of the Marine Thiasos
abstract: The sea was of great significance to the Romans and many mythological representations in a marine setting are documented in Roman mosaics. Some of the most important include the triumphal voyage of Neptune and the birth of Venus, accompanied by a marine thiasos composed of Nereids, Tritons of different varieties, sea creatures, and fantastic hybrids. On some mosaic floors, however, participants in a marine thiasos are the protagonists of the composition, apart from a divinity or main figurative scene. I will devote special attention to new finds made in recent years.

abstract: The integration of Southeast Asian countries into the global value chains (GVCs) of the fast fashion industry reveals structural inequalities between lead firms and suppliers in developing countries. This study aims to analyze how the formation of governance typologies and degrees of power asymmetry within Uniqlo's (Fast Retailing) production networks in Vietnam, Indonesia, and Cambodia affect productivity, supply base capabilities, upgrading opportunities, and labor conditions. title: Harmonizing Islamic Social Finance and National Food Security: A Regional Legal Perspective on Waqf Crowdfunding in Southeast Asia
abstract: Food insecurity in Southeast Asia is shaped by availability, access, utilization and stability, while Muslim communities may also require halal assurance throughout food value chains. Waqf crowdfunding is a potential complementary source of finance, but donation-based waqf, investment and securities crowdfunding confer different rights and are governed by different laws. title: The Social Ecology of Human Trafficking: A Theoretical Synthesis with Evidence from Southeast Asia
abstract: This study investigates the structural factors driving human trafficking patterns across four Southeast Asian countries—Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand, and Singapore—using a quantitative comparative analysis of data from 2014 to 2024. Drawing on secondary data including international tourist arrivals, GDP per capita, gender inequality indices, female vulnerable employment rates, and detected trafficking victims, the research reveals significant regional variations. title: Cementation Processes of Cenozoic Reef Carbonates: Insights from Well NK1, Nansha Islands, South China Sea
abstract: Carbonate cements record critical information about diagenetic fluid properties and environmental evolution. Carbonate successions in Well NK1 penetrate a depth of 997.7 m, located at Meiji Reef in the Nansha Islands, South China Sea, providing an ideal archive for studying cement characteristics and cementation processes. abstract: Environmental degradation has encouraged scholars to explore more integrative approaches that connect religion, governance, and sustainable development. This study examines how structural da'wah is implemented through public policy in coral reef conservation in the Selayar Islands Regency, Indonesia. title: eDNA Metabarcoding and Population Genomics of Commercially Important Marine Fish for Biodiversity Assessment and Sustainable Fisheries Management Along the Pakistan Coast
abstract: The northern Arabian Sea along Pakistan's 1,001 km coastline represents a biologically productive yet increasingly threatened marine ecosystem, supporting over 500 cataloged fish species of substantial commercial and ecological importance. Escalating anthropogenic pressures, including overfishing, illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, habitat degradation, and the intensifying Arabian Sea Oxygen Minimum Zone (OMZ), have severely altered fish community structures and precipitated declines in key commercial stocks. title: RNA virus‐induced metabolic reprogramming in a bloom‐forming marine diatom
abstract: Diatoms are a widespread group of phytoplankton that disproportionately influence the global carbon cycle through substantial contributions to primary production and carbon export in the ocean. Marine viruses are major drivers of host metabolic reprogramming and mortality, and it is increasingly clear that RNA viruses, which primarily infect eukaryotes, are abundant and distributed throughout the global ocean. title: Atlantic salmon marine survival and distribution inferred from six decades of scale-derived growth: temporal trends and growth consistency among sea ages
abstract: Across its range, the survival and maturation dynamics of Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) are dependent on growth, energy reserves, and predation pressure. This study examined growth of one-sea-winter (1SW) and two-sea-winter (2SW) salmon using archived scales collected from the Miramichi River, Canada, spanning 59 smolt migration years (1958-2016). Marine sediments accumulating at the bottom of the ocean serve as the only continuous archive of Earth's climate history spanning tens of millions of years. title: A porosity threshold shifts rare-earth element uptake mechanisms in deep-sea bioapatite
abstract: Deep-sea bioapatite is a major sink for rare earth elements and yttrium (REY), which serve as key paleoenvironmental proxies, yet REY uptake mechanisms remain elusive. title: Human Exploration of Extraterrestrial Oceans: A Perspective from Hyperbaric and Aerospace Medicine
abstract: The discovery of liquid environments beyond Earth, including the methane–ethane seas of Titan and the subsurface oceans of Europa and Enceladus, raises the possibility of future human operations in extraterrestrial aquatic environments. Unlike conventional space exploration, these settings combine hypobaric, hyperbaric, cryogenic, and reduced-gravity conditions, creating unprecedented physiological and engineering challenges. title: From Sea to Serve: An Integrated Situation Analysis of Oman’s Fisheries Sector
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive situation analysis of Oman’s fisheries sector, which remains under-researched despite its strategic importance for economic diversification under Oman Vision 2040. Adopting an integrated PESTEL-SWOT framework, the research evaluates the political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal dimensions of the sector to identify systemic constraints and development opportunities.
