abstract: Scholarship on Indian indentured labour has examined colonial political economy, plantation exploitation, diaspora formation and women’s migration. Literary studies have read gender and maritime mobility in Amitav Ghosh’s Sea of Poppies (2008), and GaiutraBahadur’s Coolie Woman (2013) has aimed to recover women’s lives through family history and colonial records. title: Part of a project or partners in the project? Moving from tokenism to true collaboration in marine research and restoration with Australian First Nations people
abstract: First Nations Australians have cared for marine environments for over 60,000 years and sustained balance because of their deep ecological knowledge and management practices. Since colonisation, however, marine environments have been increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures including overfishing and over harvesting, pollution, invasive species, habitat loss and climate change. title: Impact of Climate Change on The Blue Economy: An Appraisal of Bengal
abstract: Climate change is fundamentally reshaping the blue economy in the Bengal region, where coastal and marine resources reinforce livelihoods, food security, and trade. This paper appraises the impacts of rising sea levels, salinity intrusion, and intensifying cyclones on fisheries, aquaculture, mangrove ecosystems, and port infrastructure in Bangladesh and West Bengal. institutions: Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Institute of Science and Technology

title: The “Oceanic Head” in Mosaic: Origin, Iconographic Variations and Polysemy of a Roman Motif
abstract: The “oceanic head” motif depicts a bearded male head featuring aquatic appendages, such as crustacean claws. This motif would enjoy a long legacy in Roman décors, particularly within the repertoire of mosaicists. title: A methodological approach for determining sea turtle responses to vessel traffic using passive in situ monitoring
abstract: Vessel strikes are an important cause of sea turtle morbidity and mortality in some coastal areas. abstract: The biometric parameters and organismal condition of marine bivalves are strongly influenced by environmental conditions such as temperature, food availability, and anthropogenic disturbance. Using biometric parameters, the condition index (CI), and weight-length relationships (WLR), this study evaluated spatial variation in the organismal condition of Modiolus capax at coastal sites with contrasting environmental conditions in the Gulf of California, Mexico. abstract: Underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) requires light sources with low optical attenuation, high quantum efficiency, and robust environmental stability. title: Combating Communalism: Tracing the Spirit of Hindu-Muslim Unity in the Literary Oeuver and Selected Life Events of Kazi Nazrul Islam
abstract: The world is presently undergoing a period in which human thought is being influenced deeply and allencompassing, singular human identities are being established by populism, ultra-nationalism, and religious fanaticism. This paper argues that the Hindu- Muslim aspects of Kazi Nazrul Islam’s personal life events and literary works may serve as a guiding force in the global struggle against communalism, in the purest sense. title: Ground-truthing the application of compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids to planktic foraminifera tests from Santa Barbara Basin
abstract: Planktic foraminifera form shells that are preserved in ocean sediments and are used in a variety of paleoproxy and biostratigraphic applications. However, species-specific ecology can complicate the interpretation of planktic foraminifera-based proxies, and limited options exist for examining the ecology of extinct species. Here we apply test-bound compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids (CSI-AA) to examine the trophic ecology of extant planktic foraminifera. title: Modal Sosial dan Restorative Justice sebagai Strategi Resolusi Konflik Nelayan
abstract: Horizontal conflicts between mobile Bagan Lampu fishermen and traditional fishermen posed a serious challenge to good governance of coastal waters in Pinrang Regency, South Sulawesi. This study analyzed the conflict dynamics, the patronage structure, and social capital and restorative justice as strategies of the Head of Waetuoe Village to achieve good governance at the village level. title: Bioclimatic and habitat signals in Pleistocene fluvial microvertebrate assemblages from the Middle Dnipro region, Ukraine
abstract: Fluvial microvertebrate assemblages are important but underexplored archives for reconstructing Quaternary environments, particularly in regions lacking karstic and cave deposits. We analyse late Middle and early Late Pleistocene small‐vertebrate assemblages from the Middle Dnipro region, Ukraine, to compare two interpretative frameworks: habitat‐weighting analysis and bioclimatic spectra. title: Pange lingua gloriosi: Himnos en la colección de partituras de las Misioneras Agustinas Recoletas, Cali, Colombia (1903–1970)
abstract: The study of women’s conventual music in 20th century Colombia shows a historiographic vacuum that limits the understanding of sonic practices within cloisters and their relationship with the urban environment. This article analyzes the music score archives of the Augustinian Recollect Sisters in Cali, residents of the Convent La Merced, who over nearly seventy years consolidated a significant musical corpus. title: Molecular phylogenetics reveals contrasting evolutionary trajectories in Trinidadian worm lizards (Amphisbaena)
abstract: This study provides the first genetic confirmation of Amphisbaena fuliginosa and A. alba from the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago. Using multilocus molecular data and divergence time estimates from samples spanning Brazil, Colombia, Guyana, Panama, Peru, and Trinidad, we investigated the phylogenetic relationships and biogeographic history of these two worm lizard species. Our analyses support an Amazonian and Dry Corridor origin for both species. title: Variations in Genesis Locations and Typhoon-Induced Precipitation Intensity of Typhoons Impacting Northeast China: 2000–2025
abstract: Global warming poses persistent challenges to human societies worldwide and is accompanied by an increasing occurrence of intense and anomalous extreme weather events, including those affecting Northeast China. Apart from destruction of infrastructure, these severe weather phenomena are also a threat to food security and livelihoods, and have started attracting attention among climate scientists. Under ongoing climate warming, more tropical cyclones travel northward into Northeast China and produce heavy rainfall. title: Potentially Toxic Elements in Bed Sediments from Urban and Agricultural Watersheds in Brazil: Concentration, Fractionation Patterns, and Ecological Risk
abstract: Urban and agricultural watersheds are increasingly exposed to contamination from multiple human activities, raising concerns about sediment quality and ecological risk. Bed sediments act as long-term archives of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) at the watershed scale. In this study, riverbed sediment samples were collected from two Brazilian coastal watersheds with contrasting land uses (urban and agricultural) during dry and wet seasons. title: Hipnose terapêutica como tratamento para o estresse acadêmico: uma revisão bibliográfica
abstract: Introduction: Academic stress is a prevalent issue in the university setting, affecting student performance, mental health, and retention. Therapeutic hypnosis has emerged as a complementary intervention with a growing body of evidence. This research aims to synthesize the scientific literature on the effectiveness of hypnosis in managing academic stress, with a focus on findings from Cuba and the rest of the world. abstract: Background: Northern coastal communities surrounding MacKay Medical University have experienced substantial population aging, yet regional data on chronic disease prevalence, healthcare utilization, and associated medical expenditure remain limited. Methods: We conducted a population-based descriptive study using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database from 2018 to 2024. Environmental DNA captures ecological communities' dynamics along natural and anthropogenic gradients in a mediterranean lagoon ecosystem
abstract: Mediterranean lagoons are vital ecosystems that provide essential services such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and habitat support. Despite their high ecological and socio-economic value, transitional waters naturally experience strong environmental variability, including atmospheric phenomena like sea level rise and temperature fluctuations, and are vulnerable to human pressures such as invasive species, pollution, and human activities, emphasising the need for effective conservation strategies. title: A 100‐Year Record of Mineralogical Variations in Northeastern Greenland Ice‐Core Dust: Insights From Individual Particle Analysis
abstract: Reconstructing mineral dust deposition on the Greenland Ice Sheet provides crucial insights into atmospheric circulation and climate variability. However, understanding spatial and temporal variations in Greenland ice‐core mineral sources during the Holocene is challenging due to low dust concentrations. Here, we present the first continuous, high‐temporal‐resolution record of size, composition, and source variability of mineral dust from a northeastern Greenland ice core (EGRIP S3) covering 1910 to 2013 AD. title: Irradiated Atmospheres. VII. Effect of Mixing Energy Flux on Atmosphere–Interior Coupling
abstract: Highly irradiated, underdense rocky planets such as puffy Venuses may host strong coupling between their atmospheres and magma-ocean interiors. Previous studies have mainly treated this coupling through radiative transfer and chemical equilibrium, leaving the role of vertical mixing unclear. title: Holdfast-associated macroinvertebrate assemblages of stipitate kelps from a natural reserve in the SE Pacific
abstract: Introduction: Stipitate kelp forests formed by Lessonia trabeculata are important subtidal habitats supporting high biodiversity and providing key ecosystem services within the Northern Humboldt Current System (HCS). Despite their ecological importance, the macroinvertebrate assemblages associated with L. trabeculata holdfasts remain poorly described, particularly in populations near their Northern distribution limit. abstract: Chloride-induced corrosion of reinforcing steel is a major durability concern for reinforced concrete structures, especially in marine, coastal, and salt-affected areas. A common passive corrosion mitigation method is the use of conventional epoxy-coated reinforcement; however, its durability is often degraded by coating imperfections, microcracking, inadequate adhesion in humid environments, and the progressive ingress of water, oxygen, and chloride ions. title: Adaptive Energy Management System for Reverse Osmosis Desalination: Modelling Fuzzy Logic Control for Hybrid Solar PV, Battery and Grid Systems
abstract: The demand for fresh water in coastal regions has increased the energy demand for desalination systems. This study models a hybrid solar PV, battery, and grid energy system for reverse osmosis desalination under realistic solar conditions in Mombasa, Kenya. An adaptive system that responds to real-time irradiance data is modelled in MATLAB R2025a using a five-year hourly solar irradiance dataset from NASA POWER, an internet database with renewable energy datasets. title: Gas Chromatography-High Resolution Mass Spectrometry Spatiotemporal Screening of River Rhine Suspended Particulate Matter (2005–2022): An Early-Warning Tool for Contaminants of Concern
abstract: Environmental monitoring of archived suspended particulate matter (SPM) provides a basis for retrospective assessment of emerging contaminants in river systems. This study used yearly resolved SPM samples from two sites in the River Rhine, Koblenz and Weil am Rhein, to generate and prioritize gas chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (GC-HRMS) data within an early warning system (EWS). The aim was to identify potential contaminants of emerging concern (CEC) showing increasing temporal trends. abstract: The occurrence of Biffarius biformis (Biffar, 1971) and Fragillianassa fragilis (Biffar, 1970) in the Southwestern Atlantic is based on previous literature record from Pernambuco. Here, we question this report due to the physical absence of all lots reported in the original publication as deposited in the Museum of Zoology, University of São Paulo (MZUSP). title: Influence of natural and anthropogenic forcings on western US winter fire weather and the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires
abstract: Winter fire weather is shaped by interactions between anthropogenic climate change and natural climate variability, yet how the combination of human and natural forcings influences winter fire weather conditions remains poorly quantified. This study uses a multiple linear regression framework that removes long-term CO 2 -related trends to examine the influence of natural modes of variability on the December–February monthly fire weather index over the western United States (WUS), with the January 2025 Los Angeles (LA) fire risk as a motivating case study. title: Digital Transformation in Online Public Service Delivery at Commune Level: The Current Situation in Hai Thinh Commune, Ninh Binh Province, Vietnam
abstract: Online public services are the most visible output of digital transformation in public administration, and in Vietnam they are now delivered mainly at commune level after the introduction of the two-tier local government model on 1 July 2025. This paper analyses the current situation of digital transformation in online public service delivery in Hai Thinh, a coastal commune of Ninh Binh province formed by merging Thinh Long township and the communes of Hai Chau and Hai Ninh. The study applies a descriptive case design that combines document analysis of national, provincial and commune sources

title: Argentinean Wetlands Through Time: A Chronicle of 100 Years of Botanical History in Buenos Aires Province
abstract: Wetlands are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, facing pressure from land-use change, hydrological alterations, and biological invasions. Historical vegetation records provide a valuable resource for assessing long-term changes in these environments. In this study, we evaluated the conservation status of wetlands in the province of Buenos Aires using vascular plant occurrence records, spanning more than two centuries of information (1819–2025). title: Postpartum intrusions are associated with child and maternal mental health
abstract: Intrusive thoughts of infant-related harm are a common postpartum experience, yet their relationship with maternal and infant mental health is understudied. The current analyses utilized data from 267 participants ( M = 32.2, SD = 4.6) across Australia, the UK, and the US who took part in the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) study. abstract: This article investigates the presence of Central European literary tradition in South Africa over the last five decades, which has so far remained largely un- or under-recognised. Coetzee, Stephen Watson), as well analysis of previously unpublished works and a series of interviews conducted with selected South African poets (e.g. Douglas Reid Skinner, Robert Berold, Fiona Zerbst), this article claims that the identification with Central Europe has produced a distinct kind of modernism in South African literature – one that involves the valorisation of ce

title: Patterns of occurrence of the Portuguese man-of-war Physalia spp. along the Brazilian coast
abstract: The Portuguese man-of-war Physalia spp. is a pleustonic siphonophore responsible for severe stings globally and widely documented on digital platforms. This study analyzed over 1000 occurrence reports extracted from social media and online news along the Brazilian coast between 2020 and 2024. We investigated whether sea surface height (SSH) variability at 14°S, serving as an integrated proxy for the southern branch of the South Equatorial Current (SSEC) bifurcation, is associated with the temporal and spatial patterns of colony occurrence. title: Roman Occupation of the Area Around the Bay of Lagos
abstract: From the 19th century to the present, archaeologists produced knowledge about the Romanized communities settled around the Bay of Lagos, in the extreme southwest of Europe, facing Atlantic North Africa and the Gulf of Cádiz, a territory staggered in amphitheater between the Monchique mountain range and the sea. In this paper, we intend to contextualize the relatively frequent occurrence of mosaic panels in the contexts of the Roman imperial period in this territory. title: Drivers of seasonal variability in sediment composition and accumulation rate in varve-forming Lake Gorzyńskie, central Europe
abstract: Biogenic varves provide valuable annually resolved archives of environmental change. Yet their palaeoenvironmental interpretation requires a detailed understanding of the processes that control seasonal sedimentation. We integrated 3 years (2021–2024) of limnological monitoring, hydrochemical measurements, phytoplankton analyses, and sediment-trap observations to investigate the mechanisms of modern calcite–diatom varve formation in Lake Gorzyńskie (western Poland), a eutrophic hardwater lake preserving an almost continuous varved sediment record spanning approximately the last 13,250 cal yr B

title: Combined Methodological Approach to Examine Genotoxicity of Biocolourants Dermocybin and Dermorubin
abstract: Dermocybin and dermorubin are natural anthraquinone dyes which can be extracted from bloodred webcap (Cortinarius sanguineus) fungus. These biocolourants are suitable as textile dyes for several materials. The toxicity data related to these anthraquinones is limited which has hindered their wider use. title: Prekmurski vojaki v vojaškoorganizacijskem sistemu Avstro-Ogrske monarhije med prvo svetovno vojno
abstract: The article focuses on the presentation of soldiers from Prekmurje and their role in the structures of the Austro-Hungarian Army during the First World War. The research draws on the combined analysis of available archival material, field research results, and secondary historical sources. These are further supported by visual elements that add to a more accurate reconstruction of the operational history of soldiers from Prekmurje and their ranking in the Austro-Hungarian Army.

title: Two Episodes of Au and Ag–Pb–Zn Mineralization in the Kangshan Deposit, the Southern Margin of the North China Craton: Constraints from C–O–S Isotopes and Sphalerite Rb–Sr Dating
abstract: Polymetallic deposits are significant repositories of both bulk commodities and critical metals. However, determining the ages of multiple mineralization events in these deposits remains a persistent challenge. The Kangshan Au-polymetallic deposit, located in the southern margin of the North China Craton, exhibits distinct mineralization zonation, transitioning from deep-seated gold mineralization to shallow Ag–Pb–Zn mineralization, making it a natural laboratory for investigating composite mineralization processes. title: Gentamicin-loaded nanoformulations: From passive carriers to infection-responsive delivery systems
abstract: Gentamicin has been in clinical use for over 60 years, and to this day it remains a challenge to replace. It is bactericidal in a concentration dependent fashion, effective against aerobic Gram-negative pathogens and cost effective, making it a good first line of choice in resource limited countries where newer agents are not available. The primary limitations are nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and resistance—with biofilm tolerance representing the most difficult of these. abstract: Depletion of Nb and Ta relative to the light rare earth elements (LREE) is widely regarded as a characteristic feature of subduction-related magmatism. However, similar trace-element signatures also occur in basalts from non-subduction settings, raising questions about their tectonic significance. abstract: Research on environmental contamination, ecological health effects, and historical disease processes often uses large datasets and simple exposure–outcome models. These approaches are essential but can mislead when outcomes depend on rare combinations of environmental conditions, host physiology, pathogen state, chemical exposure, location, and history. abstract: This paper analyzes examples of applied safeguarding methodologies for ancestral knowledge, often termed Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), implemented between 2004 and 2024. Drawing on a non-exhaustive review of international initiatives, the study focuses on Latin America, contrasting processes with references from other continents. title: Re-examinando al volcán El Chichonal: prosopopeya de un lugar sagrado
abstract: The Chichonal volcano eruption (Chiapas, 1982) generated significant and immediate socio-environmental impacts, as well as constituting a turning point in the lives of the Zoque People, who attributed to it new meanings as a sacred place or enchantment symbolically associated with the spirits of the deceased people and ancestors. title: Mineralogical and geochemical fingerprinting of Lower–Middle Eocene carbonates at Umm Russeies area, north Galala Plateau, Egypt
abstract: The Lower–Middle Eocene carbonates of Egypt’s Northern Galala Plateau preserve a critical, yet geochemically underexplored, archive of southern Tethyan paleoenvironmental change. This preliminary integrated mineralogical and geochemical screening study of the Minia, Gebel Hof, and Observatory formations in Umm Russeies reveals a dynamic depositional history. abstract: This article critically examines the conduct of Canadian soldiers from the 4th Canadian Armoured Division in Sögel, a small town in northwestern Germany, during the Second World War. Drawing on an array of archival materials, including local records and Canadian war diaries, the study scrutinises allegations of civilian complicity in German counterattacks, subsequent punitive actions by soldiers, and incidents of misconduct. abstract: This paper has been written as part of an ongoing collaboration between Jade, a community researcher, artist and activist and Kate, a practitioner researcher at the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. We draw on archival images to recall past impressions of the collection, galleries and building and to reflect on experiences of recent museum projects and initiatives. title: Misreading Détente: Australian and New Zealand Labo(u)r Government Diplomacy with the People’s Republic of China, 1972–75
abstract: Internationalist Labo(u)r governments took office in Australia and New Zealand in December 1972. One of their most celebrated achievements was diplomatic recognition of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Despite the scholarly attention given to this, the quality of their bilateral relations with the PRC has not been evaluated against the archival record. This article undertakes a comparative analysis of the Whitlam and Kirk Labo(u)r governments’ diplomacy with the PRC from 1972 to 1975. title: Juventudes y mujeres en la Confederación Mapuche de Neuquén
abstract: This paper aims to contribute to the study of the sociopolitical processes that took place in the province of Neuquén between 1969 and 1983, shaped by social conflict, political violence, and state repression. It focuses on the role of Mapuche youth and women in the emergence of supracommunal Indigenous organizations, with particular attention to the Confederation of the Mapuche of Neuquén, as key actors in the reconfiguration of organizational forms, the transmission of knowledge, and the production of Mapuche political perspectives. title: Subjects of Suspicion at the Imperial Crossroads: British Indians on the Russian Periphery
abstract: This article examines mobility along the Russo-British paper frontier between the 1880s and 1910s. Drawing on a transimperial archive of petitions, passports, and consular records, it traces how South Asians moved through a landscape governed by kaghaz bazi (paper game), a contest of moves and counter-moves under rules unevenly known and applied. title: The Mesolithic Double Burial of Öland, Sweden
abstract: Mesolithic double burials in Scandinavia are rare. Half a dozen has been found in Sweden and equally many in Denmark. In many cases, these contain one adult and one child or were initially intended for single burials where an additional individual was later deposited. On Öland, Sweden, a double burial containing two men was discovered in 1948. The men were buried simultaneously and placed as if they were holding hands. title: Feather-based biomarkers link geography, physiology and reproduction across the annual cycle in northern pintails
abstract: Conditions that individuals experience during the nonbreeding season can have subsequent effects on breeding performance (i.e. carry-over effect), with implications for population dynamics. We used feather biomarkers from breeding female northern pintails (Anas acuta) to evaluate whether body condition and timing of nest initiation were related to prior moult and nonbreeding locations as estimated by both band recoveries and stable isotopes (δ2H, δ15N, δ13C, δ34S). title: Las infancias en la historiografía uruguaya: desafíos y aportes desde la noción de agencia infantil
abstract: The present work will address how the notion of children's agency enables new perspectives on childhood in Uruguayan historiographic studies. It will reference the historiographic production on childhoods from its initial approaches with historical conceptions of children as incomplete beings, without voice or in development processes, made possible since the late 19th and early 20th centuries. title: Building Macroeconomically Relevant Climate Indices via the Assemblage VAR
abstract: What should a macroeconomically relevant climate index contain? The composition is inherently ambiguous, and aggregation choices affect structural inference. We introduce the Assemblage VAR, which jointly estimates nonnegative aggregation weights and VAR parameters by maximizing the system likelihood-gain criterion, effectively outsourcing aggregation to observed macroeconomic dynamics. title: Crystal-Rich Picrites from Margi, Cyprus, Evidence Melt Diversity, Magma Mixing and Crystal Accumulation within the Troodos Ophiolite
abstract: The area near Margi, Cyprus, contains a well-characterised volcanic sequence which forms part of the Upper Pillow Lava (UPL) unit of the Troodos ophiolite. This sequence consists of olivine-phyric and aphyric basalts and basaltic andesites, along with several small, unusually olivine-rich (typically >40 vol.%, 1-20 mm grain size) picritic bodies. title: Jupiter, Medea and Triton, October 1778: new evidence
abstract: In 1778 HMS Jupiter and HMS Medea engaged the French Warship Triton. abstract: In the autumn of 1938, the men’s magazine Adam was launched as a Swedish version of the U.S. magazine Esquire, featuring its popular airbrushed pinups. While cultivating a modern masculinity according to Esquire’s formula, where readers were positioned as societal “leaders” and thus an affluent consumer group, the editorial staff also maintained close contacts with the German legation in Stockholm. title: War, Sovereignty, and Institutional Restructuring: The Abolition of Mount Lebanon’s Autonomy During World War I
abstract: The governance of autonomous regions within a central state under wartime conditions poses a fundamental political and administrative problem. The abolition of Mount Lebanon’s autonomy during World War I provides a historical laboratory for examining this problem. This study analyses the institutional tools through which the Ottoman Empire sought to establish sovereignty in the region following the abolition of autonomy. title: Iron Spin Crossover in Ferromagnesite (Mg, Fe)CO 3 and Its Contribution to Lower‐Mantle Seismic Heterogeneity
abstract: Carbonates host oxidized carbon in subducted slab and play a key role in controlling the distribution and seismic signatures of deep‐mantle carbon. Ferromagnesite, (Mg, Fe)CO 3 , is the stable carbonate in the lower mantle, yet its thermoelastic properties across the iron spin crossover (SCO) remain poorly constrained, limiting predictions of its seismic visibility. title: Environmental Impact Evaluation of Batik Production through Gate-to-Gate Life Cycle Assessment: Quantitative Evaluation of Energy, Water, and Emission Hotspots in Textile Dyeing
abstract: This study presents a gate-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of traditional batik production in Sri Lanka, aimed at quantifying environmental impacts and identifying process-level hotspots. title: Deportation and Forced Migration to the Swedish Province of Ingria During the Seventeenth Century
abstract: This article examines forced migration to the province of Ingria, part of the Swedish Empire from 1617 to 1704. The main purpose is to study to what extent deportations did occur during the Swedish rule and what other forms of forced migration existed. Previous research has strongly promoted the notion of Ingria as a site for deportation. However, there are no comprehensive studies on the topic. Consequently, this study also analyses the development of this deportation narrative. title: Entre fe y resistencia. Las asociaciones femeninas en Amozoc, Puebla (México): prácticas religiosas durante la Guerra Cristera, 1926-1929
abstract: This article argues that the coordination of lay women’s organizations in the municipality of Amozoc, Puebla (Mexico), between 1926 and 1929 enabled the continuation of religious life despite anticlerical policies implemented by the post-revolutionary state and the measures imposed by the high Catholic hierarchy. It examines the religious practices and organizational structures of women’s associations in Amozoc as forms of resistance during a turbulent period in the history of the Mexican Republic: the Cristero War. abstract: This article examines the potential biologically active compounds of Khiva milkvetch (Astragalus chivensis), a representative of the genus Astragalus L. associated with the flora of Central Asia. Particular attention is given to the phytochemical characteristics of the genus, including flavonoids, saponins, polysaccharides, phenolic compounds, and other secondary metabolites. title: Ecocide as a Mode of Genocidal Violence in Gaza: A Green Criminological Reading of Environmental Destruction, Conditions of Life, and State Harm
abstract: This article argues that the destruction of Gaza's environment should be understood not merely as collateral damage or a tragic by-product of war, but as a mode of genocidal violence that attacks the material conditions of collective life. The argument is criminological rather than narrowly doctrinal. It does not pretend to replace a final judicial determination on genocide. title: Sensing the Past: Memory, Identity, and Belonging in Monique Truong's Fiction
abstract: This This paper examines Monique Truong’s “The Book of Salt” and “The Sweetest Fruits” through memory, forgetting, and identity formation. Truong portrays memory as a continued process through which displaced individuals experience belonging, loss, and selfhood across cultural and geographical boundaries. Food functions as a sensory archive preserving personal and collective histories. abstract: Background: Indonesia's B40 mandate (40% palm oil-based fatty acid methyl ester [FAME] blended with petroleum diesel), which took effect in January 2025, extends to fishing fleets that operate older engines and purchase subsidized fuel at a fixed price. abstract: This study assessed residents’ awareness of proper waste disposal in Dapa, Surigao del Norte, focusing on waste segregation using the 5Rs, household waste management, composting, and challenges encountered in implementing appropriate practices. abstract: This article theorizes how distinct world-making projects intersect and come into tension with each other through extended urbanization. It draws on archival and field research on the remnants of the Port Hedland immigration detention center in the Pilbara region of Western Australia. abstract: Vannamei shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) is an important aquaculture commodity and a potential source of bioactive peptides with diverse health benefits. title: Improving Tsunamigenic Source Models through Interseismic Coupling Approach in Stochastic Slip Distributions: Insights from Large Chilean Earthquakes
abstract: Chile is one of the most seismically active countries in the world, having experienced three major earthquakes exceeding Mw 8.2 in 2010, 2014, and 2015. These tsunamigenic events provide critical observational constraints for developing realistic coseismic slip models. title: Ivan N. Nazarov: A Bright Meteor in the Sky of Organic Chemistry
abstract: The Soviet chemist Ivan N. Nazarov (1906-1957) is widely known for the inventions in chemistry of vinylethynylcarbinols, divinyl ketones, and steroids. His biography presents a striking contrast: a peasant boy from a rural background who, through years of determination and education, rose to the highest levels of academic achievement. Infection may result in diarrhoea, anaemia and death, especially in young animals. abstract: Dangerous goods (DGs) in loose form are a major problem and challenge when it comes to handling at maritime ports because of the risk of leakage, contamination, and regulatory non‐compliance. This is a study on the effectiveness of loose dangerous goods management practices at Port Klang, the port authority's main seaport in Malaysia, looking at the factors of dangerous goods regulatory adherence, staff training and competency, standard operating procedures (SOPs), infrastructure and technological support, and coordination between required agencies. title: Ecology, population structure, and habitat vulnerability of Trachomitum venetum s. l. in the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve, Romania
abstract: Trachomitum venetum is an endangered plant species in Romania. Overgrazing and associated trampling pressure represent the main identified threats to the species. The distribution area of this species is very limited in Romania, as it is found only on the Perișor sandbank in the Danube Delta. title: Relevancia de la investigación sobre consciencia ambiental dentro del ámbito de la educación
abstract: Education is fundamental to raising consciousness about environmental problems and possible solutions. The aim of this article was to describe the production of literature related to environmental consciousness in the field of education. A systematic review was conducted using two international scientific databases, focusing on the period from 2004 to 2025 and using the PRISMA methodology and analysis with Natural Language Processing. This research was based on a classification of criteria that served as the basis for the structure of the results, including grouping data into homogeneous sets.

abstract: This article examines the consequences of an environmental mobilization against a hydroelectric project in southern Chile, which was unique in that it included both Indigenous and non-Indigenous communities. abstract: This research aims to understand how organizational culture has become a determining factor in the development of organizational innovation. abstract: The objective of this study was to develop a model for environmental planning, assessment and monitoring through a structured causal diagnosis based on territorial indicators for El Salvador, by applying the Driving Forces-Pressure-State-Impact-Response framework to the period 2000-2024. title: Antimicrobial Activity of Selected Essential Oils from the Myrtaceae Family
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an important global problem affecting health care and leading to the inability to treat infections caused by pathogens. The increasing resistance and limitations of the number of antimicrobials increases the demand for new potential drugs from various sources. AIM: The purpose of the review article is to present knowledge about essential oils of the Myrtaceae family as possible alternatives to address AMR. title: Contaminación plástica en la hidroponía: un desafío emergente para la producción agrícola sostenible
abstract: Hydroponics is a production system that is efficient in terms of water and space; however, its reliance on plastic materials leads to the release and accumulation of microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) within nutrient solutions. This review analyzes MP and NP contamination in hydroponic systems, covering emission sources, plant uptake mechanisms, physiological consequences, and implications for food safety. title: Impacto de la disbiosis del microbioma vaginal en la patogénesis del parto pretérmino espontáneo
abstract: Spontaneous preterm birth (SPTB) is the leading cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. This study thoroughly analyzes the impact of vaginal microbiome dysbiosis on the pathogenesis of SPTB, detailing its molecular, immunological, and clinical mechanisms. Using a systematic review based on the PRISMA statement, we evaluated studies published between 2021 and 2026 retrieved from PubMed, SciELO, LILACS, MEDES, and the Trip Database. title: Programas televisivos educativos para adultos mayores en Latinoamérica: Una revisión sistemática
abstract: Context: In Latin America, population aging has become a challenge for education systems; in particular, the design of television programs for older adults stands out. This is a matter of interest because, given television's mass reach, it acquires relevance as a tool for non-formal education in this age group, but research on its potential is still insufficient in the region. abstract: Introduction: the problem of substance use disorder (SUD) has a high global prevalence; the literature seems to suggest that there is an influence from the gender and education of users in the patterns of seeking help in specialized establishments. Objective: the aim is to analyze the effects of schooling and sex on the amount of time it takes people to seek help in treatment centers. title: Species of the Genus Plantago L., Growing in the Territory of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
abstract: The present study was carried out during 2024–2025 in different floristic regions of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. The research focused on the taxonomic composition, ecological characteristics, distribution patterns, altitudinal ranges, and economic significance of species belonging to the genus Plantago L. occurring in the regional flora. title: Community-initiated co-creation in the Global South: Does the government just watch?
abstract: Co-creation has increasingly gained traction as a means to search for innovative solutions to wicked problems, including in the pursuit of the green transition. Whereas several contributions on the forms, determinants and successful outcomes of co-creation for the green transition focus on the Global North, experiences from the Global South – where non-state actors often drive local green co-creation – are increasingly drawing attention. title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
abstract: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). title: Regional differences in nutritional composition and lipid metabolism gene expression in wild male mud crabs (Scylla paramamosain)
abstract: This study compared morphological traits, tissue color, proximate composition, fatty‑acid and amino‑acid profiles, and lipid‑metabolism gene expression in wild adult male Scylla paramamosain from four regions (Nansha, Sanmen, Ca Mau, Jawa Barat). Morphometric analysis showed significant regional variation in body size and indices, with Ca Mau and Jawa Barat larger. title: Vojna struktura Palanke Tuzla u prvoj polovini 18. vijeka
abstract: In the literature at large, the term palanka is most often understood in its popular sense, denoting a small settlement located at some distance from a larger urban centre. In Ottoman military terminology, however, the term refers to a specific type of fortified structure established for the defense of the settlement in which it was situated. From a military standpoint, the distinction between a fortified palanka and a fortress lies primarily in the materials used for construction. abstract: Background: Community participation is central to dengue prevention, but evidence for educational promotion of live marigold and fermented ovitraps is heterogeneous. Objective: To critically synthesize available educational, laboratory and field observations and propose appropriately matched environmental-health indicators. Methods: A focused, purposively assembled mixed-evidence narrative review considered 15 categorized sources; database searches and selection counts were not documented, and no meta-analysis was attempted. title: Characterizing multiple dimensions of climate hazards for conservation planning: a case study of estuaries in the Pacific Northwest
abstract: Incorporating the complexities of climate change into conservation planning can be challenging. Climate change is projected to change the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation, and change dynamics of extreme events of many climate variables globally. These changes will all have compounding effects on ecosystems worldwide, affecting species distributions, seasonal timings, and population dynamics. title: Inclusión y alteridad en la educación rural
abstract: Rural education and inclusion processes aimed at diverse populations have historically faced significant segregation, leading to fragmentation and inadequate, ineffective support—whether in pedagogical practice, research, or educational policy, all of which have traditionally prioritized urban settings. title: Pedagogical trade-offs in sustainability integration in Indonesian primary-oriented EFL contexts
abstract: The integration of sustainability themes into English language teaching (ELT) has increased in response to global Education for Sustainable Development initiatives. However, limited research addresses how teachers interpret and adapt these themes within language-focused classrooms. This qualitative study analyzes written reflections from fourteen Indonesian English teachers who responded to environmental visuals from a primary-level textbook series. abstract: Nonsyndromic cleft lip and/or palate (NSCLP) is the most common congenital craniofacial malformation worldwide, with significant aesthetic, functional, and psychosocial implications. Scientific evidence suggests that individuals with NSCLP may be exposed to social, familial, and personal circumstances indicative of child abuse; however, this issue remains insufficiently documented. abstract: The ABO and Rh blood group systems constitute the most clinically relevant erythrocyte markers in transfusion medicine and immunohematology, serving a crucial role in ensuring immunological compatibility between donors and recipients. The objective of this review article was to examine and discuss the antigens of the Rh blood group system. abstract: Purpose: Green finance has proved to be a critical instrument in aligning financial systems with environmental sustainability and long-term economic growth. abstract: The study investigated the role of library and information services in the development of blue economy in maritime institution in Southern Nigeria. Five research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted descriptive research methodology. Population of 104, comprises academic librarians and lecturers in maritime institutions in Sothern Nigeria. Questionnaire was used as instrument to elicited data. title: Origins of brines in the Kłodawa salt dome, central Poland, Europe – a study based on selected isotopic analyses
abstract: Brines in salt mines may have diverse origins, and therefore provide valuable information on the conditions controlling their chemical and isotopic compositions. Depending on the nature of the deposit and local hydrogeological conditions, such brines may also pose water hazards of various severity. In order to investigate possible origins of brines flowing in the Kłodawa Salt Mine and to enhance our understanding on the processes forming their chemical and isotopic compositions, water sampling was conducted at selected locations during two sampling periods (April and October, 2022). title: Escalas de actitudes hacia la inclusión universitaria: Revisión sistemática
abstract: Assessing attitudes toward educational inclusion is essential for understanding and improving practices that promote more accessible and equitable university environments for diversity. Therefore, the objective of this research was to analyze scales published between 2015 and 2025 that assess attitudes toward educational inclusion in the university setting. title: FOOD PRESERVATION BY COMBINING ESSENTIAL OILS AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES. REVIEW
abstract: The growing global demand for fresh food emphasizes the need for effective preservation methods. Widely used traditional processing methods ensure microbiological stability of foods but often reduce their nutritional value. The aim of this study is to review the results of combining plant-based essential oils with innovative technologies, including nanoencapsulation, edible coatings, modified atmosphere packaging, and modern non-thermal processing methods. title: Climate change and public health: its impact on communicable and non-communicable diseases in Indonesia
abstract: Climate change has become a global issue with significant impacts on various aspects of life, particularly public health. This study aims to examine the impact of climate change on public health conditions in Indonesia through a literature review approach. The literature search was conducted using five relevant scientific articles from reputable databases, focusing on infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and health system adaptation to climate change. title: Gender determination using anthropometry: Exploring its potential in Western UP population
abstract: Background : Forensic identification often relies on sex estimation, especially when fragmentary or disfigured remains are involved. When traditional procedures are not accessible, anthropometric characteristics of the hand and foot offer straightforward, non-invasive alternatives. Aims and Objectives : This study aimed to evaluate the utility of hand and foot measurements—specifically index finger length (IFL), ring finger length (RFL), their ratio (IFL/RFL), hand and foot indices, and the Heel-Ball (HB) index—for gender determination, and to compare their efficacy as forensic tools. title: Cornulitid tubeworms from the Upper Ordovician Agüeira Formation of northwestern Spain
abstract: Two cornulitid species are described herein from the Late Ordovician of Spain. These specimens support the view that there is no reliable evidence for free-living tentaculitids in the Late Ordovician of Spain. The Spanish cornulitids are best classified as secondarily free, solitary, soft-bottom dwellers. The prominent annuli of the Spanish cornulitids presumably had a stabilizing function, helping them maintain their preferred position in soft sediment. title: Greenland ice sheet retreat intensifies the African monsoon through a polar-tropical atmospheric teleconnection
abstract: Global climate forcing drives major changes in the North African summer monsoon (NASM), yet how high-latitude cryospheric changes influence tropical hydroclimate through atmospheric dynamics remains unclear. Integrating paleoclimate proxy evidence with coupled climate-model simulations, sensitivity experiments, and idealized atmospheric modeling, we show that Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) retreat acts as a dynamically important amplifier of NASM rainfall. title: Melochia nodiflora Sw. (Malvaceae): A new distributional record from Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Melochia nodiflora Sw. (Malvaceae) is a shrub or undershrub, native to tropical and subtropical regions, with a limited distribution record in India. During the recent floristic and ethnobotanical studies in Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, natural populations of M. nodiflora were encountered at Aragonda Hill, near Ardhagiri Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Madhavaram and Peddakappalle. title: Mapping the applications of stable isotope analysis in rodent ecology: Protocol for a scoping review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rodents (order Rodentia) are the most diverse and geographically widespread order of mammals, occupying virtually all terrestrial ecosystems and playing key ecological roles in food webs and ecosystem functioning. Stable isotope analysis has become a tool for investigating trophic ecology, resource use, habitat use, and movement across spatial and temporal scales. abstract: From its earliest adoption as a tool by early human species more than 1.5 million years ago to its continued use in jewelry, shell has a historical reach unrivaled by any other gem material. As the first global currency, cowrie shells fueled industries that shaped humankind and left a lasting impact on various cultures. Native Americans created their own shell-based currencies that were still in use during the colonial period. title: Suicide in former reserve UK Armed Forces personnel, 1996–2018: A whole population cohort study
abstract: "Reserve Personnel", who serve voluntarily, comprise around a fifth of the UK Armed Forces (UKAF). Little is known about their suicide risk, or factors associated with suicide in this population. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of suicide in reserve personnel who left the UKAF between 1996 and 2018 by linking national databases. We examined the risk of suicide in this group of veterans compared to the general population and identified the factors most strongly associated with suicide after discharge. title: Kinship on the Keen: Relations With(in) Place Through Creative Practice
abstract: Inspired by the idea that we know places through their weather, I used diffractive methodology to explore more-than-human kinship on the Keen of Hamar in Unst, Shetland, through film-making, creative writing and embodied return to place. The Keen is a distinctive hillside of serpentine debris exposed to extreme weather and home to tiny, rare plants. title: Off the boat and into the bank: direct market channels and seafood sales
abstract: Direct seafood markets provide small-scale fishers channels to sell source-identified, sustainably harvested products. While the economic impacts of direct marketing are well studied in agriculture, analogous research in seafood systems has been limited by data scarcity. Consequently, little is known about how direct marketing strategies; such as direct-to-consumer (DTC), direct-to-retail, and direct-to-foodservices; impact seafood harvesters’ revenue. title: Wetland restoration for climate change mitigation and biodiversity recovery
abstract: Introduction Wetland restoration is increasingly promoted as a strategy to mitigate climate change and recover biodiversity in Europe, yet its outcomes and key drivers remain poorly understood across wetland types. Objectives We quantify restoration effects on carbon stocks, greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes, and biodiversity indicators in European bogs, fens, and salt marshes. title: To tip or not to tip
abstract: Tipping points have become a buzzword in Earth sciences, but ambiguous or overly narrow definitions of tipping are causing confusion around the concept. Agreeing on what tipping means, and whether a system tips or not, is important for robust science and communicating tipping risk. Based on a critical evaluation of existing tipping definitions, we propose a revised, general definition that characterizes a tipping event as a persistent nonlinear transition in forced systems. abstract: In this study, the geotourism potential of the Wolin municipality on the southern Baltic coast was analysed, combining expert assessment with the perspectives of the local community. Existing and potential geosites were identified through field inventory, literature review, cartographic analyses, pilot survey, and interviews with local stake-holders. abstract: Purpose This study evaluated the effects of WECARE (Women’s Education Program for Climate Change Adaptation in Reproductive Age), a 4-week intervention based on Roy’s Adaptation Model, on oxidative stress biomarkers and psychosocial adaptation outcomes among women of reproductive age. title: Climate change perceptions and risk awareness: causes, consequences and responses
abstract: Climate change is one of the major challenges of modern society, affecting the environment, human health, the economy, and social stability. In addition to examining its causes and consequences, understanding how citizens perceive climate change is important for developing effective approaches to climate risk management. abstract: The deployment of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs) and dual-use fuel strategies for aviation and ground transportation requires a detailed understanding of the hydraulic properties governing fuel injection-system behavior. This study presents a dynamic methodology for determining fuel density, bulk modulus, and speed of sound directly from rail-pressure, back-pressure, and injection-rate signals acquired during real common-rail injection events, eliminating the need for dedicated acoustic characterization equipment. abstract: Green ammonia is increasingly considered a low-carbon energy carrier for industrial demand centers. abstract: This study explores the influence of the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO), Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO), and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) on tropical cyclone (TC) genesis, strength, track curvature, and spatial distribution in the Northwest Pacific (NWP) from 1977 to 2016. abstract: The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

title: Divergent species responses to warming: insights from long‐term reproductive phenology monitoring in the Oroarctic
abstract: Climate warming is driving shifts in reproductive phenology of Arctic plants, yet long‐term studies focus on the timing of phenological events, while far less is known about how warming influences reproductive effort. Linking phenology with reproductive effort over decadal timescales is essential for understanding how Arctic vegetation will respond to climate change. abstract: Eruption-caused volcaniclastic mass flows were a significant feature of the four-month-long 2023 eruption of Shishaldin Volcano in Alaska. The volcano supports a nearly continuous cover of glacier ice and snow on the flanks of its upper edifice, and the emplacement of pyroclastic density currents over this snow and ice cover led to the generation of meltwater and lahars. Pyroclastic density currents that formed during the eruption were long and narrow in map view and did not develop marginal levees. title: Experimental evolution of yeast reveals trade-offs between early and late stationary phase
abstract: Stationary phase in yeast and other microorganisms begins when a limiting nutrient in the environment is exhausted and cell division ceases. Most cells subsequently enter quiescence and then lose viability. However, even in spent media, metabolism continues, and the environment can change over time, causing the relative fitnesses of genotypes to differ over the course of stationary phase. For yeast, how such fitness varies and what genotypes might be favored at what points in stationary phase is largely unknown. title: Seismic Attenuation Tomography of El Hierro: Insights Into Magmatic Processes in the Canary Islands
abstract: Recent eruptions in the Canary Islands highlight an increase in volcanic activity and provide an exceptional data set to investigate subsurface processes. We present the first 3D seismic attenuation model for the 2011–2012 eruption on El Hierro, using the coda normalization method and a large seismic data set. Our results complement previous 3D velocity models, improving constraints on crustal structure, magma pathways, and intermediate storage zones. title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026
abstract: We previously described GapMind, an automated web-based tool for annotating amino acid biosynthesis pathways in bacterial and archaeal genomes. We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. We confirmed the activity of ten of the proposed enzymes by using cross-species complementation assays. title: Tropospheric Scintillation on L-Band Signals Using Mountaintop-Based Radio Occultation Measurements
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric scintillation-induced amplitude and phase fluctuations in Global Positioning System signals at L1, L2, and L5 frequencies. Data were collected at the summit of Haleakalā, Hawaii, using mountaintop global navigation satellite system (GNSS) monitoring station with a side-facing horn antenna and a zenith-pointing antenna connected to Septentrio PolaRxS receivers, combining observations from both antennas. journal: NAVIGATION Journal of the Institute of Navigation

title: Evaluation of agronomic traits, yield, and nutritional quality of seven quinoa varieties under arid environmental conditions in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is a climate‐resilient, nutrient‐rich crop with potential to enhance agricultural diversification and food security in arid and semiarid regions. This study evaluated the agronomic performance, grain yield, and nutritional composition of seven quinoa varieties grown at Al Kharj Agricultural Experimental Station, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Agronomic traits, yield components, grain yield, proximate composition, bioactive compounds, and mineral contents were assessed. abstract: The genus Agarna Schioedte & Meinert, 1884, is reviewed and rediagnosed. The female, male and transitional stages of Agarna cumulus (Haller, 1880), the senior synonym of the type species, are redescribed based on the newly designated lectotype and additional material collected from the Caribbean parasitising doctorfish, Acanthurus chirurgus (Bloch, 1787), blue tang surgeonfish Acanthurus coeruleus Bloch & Schneider, 1801, and barber surgeonfish Acanthurus bahianus Castelnau, 1855. title: Enigmatic mid‐Cretaceous amber‐preserved flowers with remarkable stellate trichomes show affinities with early‐diverging angiosperms
abstract: The study of Cretaceous flowers is crucial for elucidating the early evolution and diversification of angiosperms. Approximately 100-million-year-old Kachin amber from Northern Myanmar is well known to preserve flowers in life-like fidelity. Here, we describe new flower inclusions that share a dense indumentum of stellate trichomes and re-evaluate the structure and affinities of similar fossils placed in the genera Antiquifloris (magnoliids), Eophylica (Rhamnaceae), and Electrophycus (green algae). title: Metabolism, Metabolic Regulation and Nutritional Requirement of Iron in Aquaculture Species: A Critical Review
abstract: Iron is an essential cofactor for oxygen transport, electron transfer, DNA synthesis, and Fe‐S cluster enzymes, with its redox cycling between Fe 2+ and Fe 3+ , underpinning both its biochemical utility and cytotoxic potential via ROS generation, requiring tight homeostatic regulation across all organisms. In contrast to terrestrial vertebrates, aquatic organisms acquire iron not only from dietary sources but also directly from the surrounding water through the gills. title: Diasporas of Sefarad and al‐Andalus: Intellectual and Literary Creation Across Early Modern Europe and the Mediterranean
abstract: Most scholarship on the early modern Sephardic and Andalusi diasporas has developed within separate disciplines. This special issue is a step in bringing research on these two Iberian diasporas into closer conversation. This introductory article reviews essential questions in the histories of the two diasporas and explores how theorizations of the concept of diaspora provide a framework for connected studies. title: Fish Oil Mitigates Ozone-Induced Lung Inflammation by Restoring Oxylipin Homeostasis
abstract: Background and Aim: Ground-level ozone threatens respiratory health by inducing pulmonary inflammation. Although fish oil has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties, its protective mechanisms against ozone-induced lung injury remain unclear. This study investigated fish oil efficacy in modulating oxylipin homeostasis and mitigating pulmonary toxicity induced by ozone exposure in a mouse model. title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract: Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. title: Bioluminescent bacteria: benefits and challenges of producing bioluminescent bio-concrete for clean and sustainable lighting
abstract: The global energy matrix is still largely dependent on non-renewable, polluting fossil fuels, while energy demand is projected to rise significantly by 2040. Bioluminescent bacteria present a promising alternative for clean, renewable, and accessible lighting, particularly for low-income communities. This review explores their potential use in civil construction through the development of bioluminescent bio-concrete, a sustainable material that incorporates genetically modified bacteria carrying the luxoperon from species such as Aliivibrio fischeriand Photobacteriumphosphoreum. title: Distinct Methane-Cycling Pathways Drive Variable Surface Flux in Freshwater Wetlands
abstract: Freshwater wetlands are the largest natural source of methane (CH4), representing a third of global emissions. Both CH4 production and oxidation are microbially mediated, yet the metabolic controls governing CH4 cycling across wetland types remain poorly resolved. Here, we investigated six hydrologically and geochemically distinct wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region of North America. title: FROM GULF PORTS TO BRAZILIAN BUYERS: A DECISION FRAMEWORK FOR ASSESSING THE EXPORT FEASIBILITY OF TEXAS AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS IN BRAZIL
abstract: Brazil is both one of the world's largest agricultural exporters and a structural importer of wheat, genetics, specialty foods and other agricultural products, which makes it a difficult but not closed market for Texas suppliers. This white paper proposes a five-gate decision framework for assessing the export feasibility of Texas agricultural products in Brazil: product–market matching, regulatory mapping, logistics and landed-cost modeling, quality and traceability, and a commercial go/pilot/no-go decision. title: Ammonia excretion dynamics of the silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) during the juvenile-to-adult grow-out phase, under different body sizes and stocking densities in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS)
abstract: The Chilean silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) is an endemic freshwater species with emerging potential for aquaculture and conservation-oriented production. However, key bioengineering parameters required for system design and biomass management remain poorly defined. This study evaluated how body size and stocking density affect total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) excretion rates in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) under controlled conditions. abstract: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to comprehensively investigate the exposure-integrated risk prioritization of legacy and emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in domestic freshwater networks, specifically the Geum River basin, South Korea. This was achieved by integrating the targeted analysis of 39 PFAS with high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)-based suspect and non-target screening (SNTS) and quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR)-based hazard prioritization. title: Skin and gut bacterial assemblages show differential responses to prolonged heat exposure and cooling in zebrafish ( Danio rerio )
abstract: Rising water temperatures can disrupt host-associated microbial communities important to fish metabolism, immunity and pathogen defence; however, the effects of prolonged thermal exposure and subsequent recovery remain poorly understood. We examined skin and gut bacterial assemblages of juvenile zebrafish under four temperature regimes: T1 (28°C for 60 days), T2 (28°C for 30 days followed by 34°C for 30 days), T3 (34°C for 30 days followed by 28°C for 30 days) and T4 (34°C for 60 days). title: First record of Clerodendrum chinense (Lamiaceae) in Algeria
abstract: Biological invasions significantly drive global biodiversity change, and early detection of newly established alien plant species is crucial for evaluating invasion risks. Here, we report the first documented natural establishment of Clerodendrum chinense (Osbeck) Mabb. in Algeria. This ornamental species, native to tropical and subtropical Asia, was first recorded in 2022 as having escaped cultivation in two locations in the Annaba region. title: Color pattern evolution in the threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus): a review
abstract: Studies of animal color patterns have provided important insights into evolution, particularly the genetic and developmental bases of adaptation, natural selection’s role in molding both nuptial and nonbreeding traits, and sexual/social selection’s role in ornament evolution. Here we review these topics for the threespine stickleback, a leading evolutionary model. Concerning genetics, we find that melanic characters are the best elucidated, with one to multiple genes indicated. Red coloration appears polygenic and candidate genes include ttc39b, but manipulations using CRISPR-Cas9 are needed.

title: Atmospheric water generation technologies: comprehensive analysis, economic payback and climate suitability for applications in Malaysia
abstract: Global water shortage has been one of the issues that has remained prevalent over the decades, with no viable solutions. Despite efforts and mitigation measures proposed by multiple international institutions and researchers, progress remains inadequate at present. Atmospheric water generation (AWG) emerges as one of the alternatives to the water shortage problem, offering sustainable water production from the ambient air while preserving natural water sources such as groundwater. title: ENZYMATIC HYDROLYSIS OF BROWN SEAWEED POLYSACCHARIDES: CHARACTERIZATION OF THE MAIN SUBSTRATES AND ENZYMES
abstract: Brown seaweed is a widely used raw material for the production of food, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals. First and foremost, macroalgae of the Phaeophyceae class are considered a source of unique polysaccharides with a wide range of physiological activities. The following main carbohydrates are isolated from algae: alginic acids and their salts – alginates, fucoidans and laminarans. The polysaccharide content can reach 56.4% of the dry weight of brown seaweed biomass. title: Narratives of salmon production and care in indigenous hatchery programmes
abstract: Amidst global biodiversity declines, human‐assisted reproduction programmes such as salmon hatcheries are the focus of a highly technical and often fraught debate due to concerns about genetic and ecosystem impacts. Indigenous Peoples in some parts of North America have a vital relationship with salmon, deeply connected with governance, self‐determination, and Treaty rights. title: Hydroclimatic evolution under changing westerly–monsoon influences in northeastern China since the Late Glacial
abstract: Hydroclimatic variability in the transition zone between the East Asian summer monsoon and mid-latitude westerlies reflects the combined influence of these two circulation systems. Understanding how their relative influences have changed over time is essential for interpreting long-term regional moisture variability. Here, we reconstructed regional hydroclimatic changes since 14.3 ka BP using a continuous lacustrine sequence from Aranji Nur, a closed lake on the southwestern margin of the Hulunbuir Grassland in northeastern China. title: Context-dependent dispersal directionality in a headwater stream salamander
abstract: Background Dispersal is an integral component of population dynamics that comes with both fitness costs and benefits. Behavioral adaptations that minimize dispersal costs, such as non-random directionality, occur across taxa. However, most studies on directionality focus on single-risk (or single-benefit) systems even though organisms are likely subject to multiple co-occurring risk factors that may influence directionality in different ways. title: Naming the empire: The legacy of the revolt of 1857 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
abstract: The place names do not just indicate a location, but can also serve as a memory of political power, history, and evolving notions of identity. In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the colonial naming, the colonial power, and the colonial memory of resistance in South Asia is an important case study. After the Revolt of 1857, the British in 1858 established a penal settlement at Port Blair, the islands became an important place of Colonial punishment, surveillance, labour and exile. title: Characterising the longer-term impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks prior to 2020 on wild bird populations
abstract: Since 2020, there has been a global escalation of the impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) on wild bird species. However, the population-level consequences of this disease remain poorly understood, despite repeated outbreaks affecting wild birds over the past two decades. To address this, we collated population counts and mortality data from 40 historical cases where HPAI mass-mortality occurred in wild bird populations prior to 2020. title: Narrating Against Forgetting: rivers, dams and environmental amnesia in Elif Shafak’s novel There Are Rivers in the Sky
abstract: The aim of this article is to read Elif Shafak’s novel There Are Rivers in the Sky (2024) as a narrative that combats environmental amnesia by focusing on stories in which the colonization of water and by means of water are a central theme. The novel connects the practices of colonial control and processes of environmental degradation, particularly through its engagement with the damming and culverting rivers. abstract: The intensive use of antibiotics in pig farming contributes to the emergence of antimicrobial resistance, thereby encouraging the search for alternatives such as algae-based feed supplements including Algo-Bio®. title: Uncovering Cultural Heritage Buildings in Luwu
abstract: This study explores the architectural features and historical significance of selected cultural heritage buildings in Palopo City, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the research investigates nine heritage structures, including the Istana Datu Luwu, Masjid Jami Tua Palopo, and Gereja Pniel, to uncover their original functions, structural transformations, and cultural symbolism. title: Window(s) to the World(s): Windows, Libraries, and Transgression in Gothic Literature
abstract: This essay argues that the windows and libraries of the buildings in Emily Brontë’s Wuthering Heights, Daphne du Maurier’s Rebecca, and Bram Stoker's Dracula function as borders between the physical and spiritual, different races and classes, life and death. title: Laboratory-based assessment of quantitative PCR to describe Arctic fish assemblages in surface water affected by acid rock drainage
abstract: Permafrost thaw has been identified as a cause of metal mobilization from acid rock drainage and transport to Arctic rivers. Elevated metal concentrations and precipitation of Fe(III) minerals (i.e., rusting) in surface waters deteriorates water quality and raises questions about ecosystem effects, especially to the health of fish species. title: Fossil Leaf Impression of Cecropia (Urticaceae) from Cenozoic Travertines at Presa Damují, Cienfuegos, Cuba
abstract: Cuba alberga un registro diverso, pero poco estudiado de plantas fósiles, preservadas en una variedad de contextos sedimentarios y diagenéticos. A pesar de esta riqueza, los fósiles macroflorísticos diagnósticos del Neógeno-Cuaternario siguen siendo escasos y, a menudo, poco documentados. title: Judicial Strategies in Adjudicating Climate Change Disputes, or What International Tribunals Can Learn from Domestic Apex Courts
abstract: This article discusses the judiciary’s role in settling environmental disputes. The initial argument is that national and international courts can be divided into two main groups: the first, which is more limited and that operates through “traditional” or self-restraining judicial concepts; and the second, which is more elaborate and driven by the climate agenda. title: Freshwater Ornamental Fish Trade in Tanzania: Species Composition, Trade Practices and Conservation Risks
abstract: The ornamental fish trade is one of the fastest‐growing sectors of the global aquatic animal industry, involving more than 7900 fish species. Global demand for ornamental fish has increased substantially over the past few decades, with millions of fish traded annually to supply the expanding aquarium industry. The industry in Tanzania is also expanding rapidly, yet information on traded species, trade practices and associated conservation risks remains limited. abstract: Background: Paediatric gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) may persist beyond infancy despite conventional management. From a traditional acupuncture perspective, reflux beginning in infancy may reflect disruption of foundational regulatory systems, including but not limited to the Ren Mai. abstract: This article examines a Nilotic scene discovered in the apse mosaic of the late antique bishop’s church inDoliche, a city situated in present-day southeastern Türkiye. While Nilotic imagery has long been associatedwith Hellenistic and Roman decorative traditions, its integration into Christian liturgical spaces is less wellunderstood. title: Diet and digestive traits associated with crab digestion in the crab-eating frog (Fejervarya cancrivora)
abstract: Despite the mechanical resistance of chitin-rich exoskeletons, how anurans with limited chewing capacity utilize crustacean prey remains poorly understood. The crab-eating frog ( Fejervarya cancrivora ), which inhabits mangrove and brackish-water environments and feeds on crustaceans, provides a suitable model system for addressing this question. abstract: Purpose Cultural approaches that aim to shift people's worldviews toward environmental sustainability have gained attention, but most remain small-scale or experimental. This study examines the nationwide implementation of cultural approaches through Japan's integration of animistic stories into elementary school language textbooks. title: New palaeointensity results during 300–1300 CE from Khao Kuram and Yarang Ancient City, Thailand
abstract: SUMMARY There have been few archaeomagnetic studies performed in Southeast Asia despite the potential of data from this region to provide valuable insights into low-latitude field variations. title: Bayesian Inference of Global Land Plant Diversification Dynamics Across the Phanerozoic
abstract: The patterns and potential drivers of land plant diversification remain puzzling, particularly over deep time and at the global scale. Here, we reconstruct land plant diversification dynamics using an updated time-calibrated phylogeny comprising 30,278 extant species and 39,857 fossil occurrences within the Bayesian birth-death framework. title: FROM COCONUT FIBER (Cocos nucifera L.) TO EDIBLE SALT: PHYSICOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF AN INNOVATIVE PRODUCT
abstract: Coconut fiber (Cocos nucifera) is an abundant, inexpensive agricultural by-product with high potential for value-added processing. However, it is undervalued. In this context, the aim of this study is to determine the physicochemical characteristics of an edible salt obtained from the ash of this fiber. To do this, coconut fiber from the West Africa Tall (WAT) cultivar, immature with gelatinous almonds (NIGA) and mature with hard almonds (NMHA), was used. abstract: Primary European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) forests represent fundamental sources of information regarding natural stand dynamic processes, disturbance regime, as well as abiotic and biotic stressors that shape the structure, functioning and biodiversity of conspecific forest ecosystems across the continent. title: Debasement and the production of copper-alloy coins in ninth-century Northumbria
abstract: The production of copper-alloy coins in the kingdom of Northumbria during the ninth century AD represents a unique move away from silver coinage in early medieval western Europe. While differing explanations for this debasement have been proposed, few consider non-numismatic evidence. The compilation and analysis of available ninth-century gold and silver objects found in Northumbria, presented here, sheds new light on the change in coinage. title: Studying invasive species by non-invasive methods: Real-time qPCR successfully detects protected vertebrate species in raccoon scats
abstract: Invasive alien species pose a major threat to biodiversity, particularly through predation on rare and endangered species. In Europe, studies on the impacts of invasive mammalian predators such as raccoons remain scarce, and existing diet analysis methods often fail to detect such predation events. This study therefore evaluates the suitability of real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) as a sensitive method for detecting predation on rare species.
