abstract: This paper examines the changing relationship between the Viking Age settlement beneath present-day Aarhus and regional landscapes from the 7th to the 11th century. A local landing site is documented below Aarhus from the late 8th century, while regional evidence extends back to the 7th. A fortification was constructed after the landing site’s destruction in the early 10th century, but activity within it remained limited for decades. abstract: This article examines industrial wastewater as liquid waste in motion across the Czechoslovak–Austrian frontier in the 1970s. Using bilateral commission protocols, related correspondence, official treaty material and contemporary Austrian fisheries reporting, it reconstructs how recurring sugar-beet pollution, bacteriological uncertainty and oil spills transformed the Danube, Morava and Dyje into monitored environments. abstract: Plastics are everywhere in modern environments, and smaller plastic particles, known as microplastics (MPs, 1 µm-5 mm), have raised increasing concerns regarding indoor air quality and potential human exposure. Given that people spend more than 80% of their time indoors, understanding potential indoor sources and the distribution of MPs is important. abstract: Mean ages and diversification rates of lineages in biological assemblages are widely employed as indicators of large-scale evolutionary dynamics. Bryophytes have been hypothesized to have originated under temperate climates and to have later expanded into tropical climates. This temperate niche conservatism hypothesis predicts higher mean genus ages but lower diversification rates of bryophyte assemblages in areas with temperate climates than those with tropical climates, but this remains untested. title: Catch-Size Composition of Mud Crab (Scylla serrata) Landings in Two Villages on Belitung Island, Indonesia
abstract: Approximately 65% of mud crabs (Scylla serrata) landed by fishers on Belitung Island had carapace widths greater than 12 cm, whereas 35% measured 12 cm or less. This study assessed the size distribution of mud crab catches based on the 12 cm carapace-width criterion in Sungai Padang Village, Belitung Regency, and Mentawak Village, East Belitung Regency, Indonesia. abstract: Accurate stream flow measurements, especially during floods or at ungauged sites, are essential to progress hydrological understanding. Quantitative Image Velocimetry (QIV) helps to address this need using video-based flow measurements. title: Crusader towns of the military orders: from the Levant to the Baltic
abstract: This paper examines the archaeology, urban plans, and history of towns founded by military orders in the Levant and the Baltic regions. First, the analysis compares the 13thcentury development of Templar Atlit (Israel) and Teutonic Elbląg (Poland). These two towns are shown to have developed in an almost identical way. title: Effects of Gelatin and Corn Syrup Addition on the Physicochemical and Sensory Characteristics of Wedang Pokak Jelly Candy
abstract: Wedang pokak jelly candy is a diversified product derived from the traditional herbal beverage wedang pokak, developed to enhance its appeal and consumer acceptance. Gelatin serves as a gelling agent, while corn syrup acts as a anti-crystallizing agent that plays an important role in determining the characteristics of jelly candy. title: Ontogenetic development of digestive enzymes in the crayfish Procambarus acanthophorus
abstract: Mexico boasts a great diversity of decapod crustaceans, including crayfish known locally as acociles. Within this group, Procambarus acanthophorus stands out as an important species for regional fisheries and has high aquaculture potential because it adapts quickly to captive conditions and develops directly without larval stages, giving it a significant advantage in growth and survival over other crayfish species. However, its digestive and physiological capabilities, which could inform the development of aquaculture technologies and enhance its aquaculture potential, remain largely unknown.

abstract: This study explored the socio-semiotic dimensions of the Nāga and the Bakunawa, two significant serpent figures from Thailand and the Philippines, respectively, and investigated how these figures generate meaning and become woven into collective memory, identity, social values, and the relationships among humans, nature, and the sacred. title: Investigating the antibacterial effects and modes of action of two endophytic fungal extracts from Annona muricata seeds against resistant Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Introduction and objective: Antimicrobial resistance in Staphylococcus aureus represents a major public health concern, highlighting the need for new antibacterial agents. Endophytic fungi associated with medicinal plants are promising sources of bioactive secondary metabolites for this purpose. This study therefore aimed to evaluate the antibacterial activity and investigate the modes of action of two ethyl acetate extracts of endophytic fungi isolated from Annona muricata seeds, against a resistant strain Staphylococcus aureus NR-46003. abstract: Filamentous fungi are a valuable source of bioactive metabolites. abstract: Recent debates addressing plant consumption by lizards challenge classical ideas about morphological and physiological adaptations to herbivory that require large body size and active thermoregulatory behaviour as major requirements related to ingestion of this type of food. title: A Sacred Geoheritage Site: Integrating Indigenous Knowledge and Geoconservation in Ado-Awaye’s Suspended Lake, Nigeria
abstract: Ado-Awaye’s Iyake Lake in southwestern Nigeria represents a rare geomorphological feature and a culturally significant landscape, recognised as one of the few known suspended lakes globally. Despite its scientific and cultural value, the site remains underrepresented in geoheritage and geoconservation scholarship. This study examines Iyake as a sacred geoheritage site, analysing how geomorphological distinctiveness and indigenous belief systems interact to shape its conservation. abstract: Water quality deterioration poses substantial environmental and socioeconomic challenges for agricultural communities dependent on contaminated surface water resources. This study assessed the implications of Manchhar Lake water contamination for vegetable production, food-chain exposure, and farming livelihoods in Sindh, Pakistan. An integrated approach combining laboratory analysis with a structured field survey of 50 farmers was employed. abstract: Objective/context: This article analyzes the narrative practices, actions, and charitable sensibilities of school-aged children and youth in Chile from 1878 to 1935 to examine their participation in charitable and philanthropic culture during this period. abstract: The main goal of this study is to inventory and describe the geological characteristics of local and regional types of rocks that were applied in secular and sacral architecture of the Sandomierz Upland. Field reconnaissance of leading historical stone masonry centres in the regarded area and evaluation of their resources in the investigated objects in relation to architectural style were carried out. This socio-legal study analyzes civil losses under the law on unlawful acts and the payment’s effect on civil rights. abstract: Antecedente. Los profesionales de la salud enfrentan múltiples estresores, entre ellos el síndrome de quemazón (SQ). abstract: This exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial investigated whether a nocturnal pressurization intervention, designed to simulate altitude reduction during sleep, was associated with changes in multi-system physiological responses in male workers with chronic intermittent high-altitude exposure. Twenty-four male workers were randomized to a Pressurization group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 12); Over a 5-week protocol, the Pressurization group slept at the simulated altitudes while both groups worked at 3500 m. abstract: Soil viruses are increasingly recognized as components of microbial communities with the potential to alter ecosystem functioning, yet the frequency and functional distribution of virus-encoded metabolic genes in soils remain poorly understood. abstract: Decentralized rural domestic sewage treatment facilities in China often emit ammonia-rich odours. Conventional media are costly and have poor microbial affinity. abstract: Most histories of science fiction trace the genre from Europe to America treating speculative writing from colonies as late or borrowed. abstract: Understanding the economic impacts of drought remains challenging, particularly in identifying causal effects and accounting for regional heterogeneity. abstract: The research aims to evaluate the policy of developing tourist areas in Boalemo Regency based on the CIPP evaluation method. abstract: Este artículo examina la transformación de las filmotecas ante el giro digital, desde su función histórica de conservación del cine analógico hasta los retos actuales de la preservación digital. abstract: Purpose: This study examines the impact of carbon farming on economic growth and investigates whether the Emission Trading System (ETS) moderates this relationship across countries. abstract: This paper explores the relationship between information practices, creativity, and sustainable cultural development within localized cultural ecosystems. Drawing on perspectives from cultural studies, information behavior research, and heritage studies, the study examines how culturally embedded forms of information seeking, sharing, interpretation, and reuse contribute to creative expression and the continuity of local cultural identity. abstract: Over the years, Plastic materials have become indispensable in contemporary urban life because of their affordability, versatility, durability and convenience. However, the rapid growth in the consumption of single-use plastics, coupled with inadequate collection, sorting, recycling and final disposal systems, has created significant environmental and urban-management challenges in Nigeria. abstract: The anti‐racist dimensions of Guarani rap remain under‐examined in scholarship, with existing research primarily focusing on the genre's cultural and linguistic hybridisation, and its role in bridging distinct contexts and expressing social critique. This article investigates how Guarani rappers in Brazil mobilise the genre to counter racial discrimination. title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
abstract: Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. title: Printing powerful soft robots on a desktop
abstract: Soft robots can achieve complex behaviors with simple control strategies. One promising approach is to embed fluidic control circuits directly into the structure of a soft robot without electronics. Automated additive manufacturing offers a route to consistently fabricate such integrated robotic systems without labor-intensive manual assembly. However, previous soft robots fabricated using this approach relied on control circuits that operated at low power, limiting their practical utility. title: Haloarchaeal and enzymatic bioprocessing of shrimp waste for sustainable production of chitin and chitosan
abstract: Shrimp processing waste is an abundant source of chitin and chitosan; however, conventional extraction methods rely on chemical treatments that may compromise the quality of the resulting biopolymers. This study evaluated two biotechnological approaches, namely enzymatic hydrolysis using an alkaline protease (ECOENZYME–ALKP) and haloarchaeal fermentation using Halococcus dombrowskii , for producing chitin and chitosan from Pacific white shrimp waste. title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
abstract: Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. title: Trend Analysis of Non - Revenue Water using Mann-kendall Test and Sen's Slope Estimator: A Case of Sumbawanga Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Authority
abstract: Non-Revenue Water (NRW) remains a critical challenge for urban water utilities in sub-Saharan Africa, where system losses frequently exceed the International Water Association (IWA) benchmark of 20%. This study investigates monthly NRW trends at the Sumbawanga Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Authority (SUWASA) in Rukwa Region, southwestern Tanzania, over six years (2019–2024) using two robust non-parametric statistical techniques: The Mann-Kendall (MK) trend test and Sen's Slope Estimator (SSE). title: Cassava root rots in the humid tropics: fungal niche inversion and early-warning threshold in West Africa
abstract: Cassava ( Manihot esculenta Crantz) root rots, caused by soil-borne fungi, constitute a major constraint in the West African humid tropics. However, their combined effects with topography, altitude and plant age remain insufficiently documented. This study evaluated these effects via the Disease Severity Index (DSI) across 192 plots and 1,920 plants aged 8–25 months, in three contrasting regions (Tonkpi, Guémon, Cavally) of the mountainous west of Côte d'Ivoire. journal: Journal of Plant Diseases and Protection

title: Succession of coast pine barrens to northern hardwoods in a lacustrine sand dune system
abstract: The Grand Sable Dunes is a perched lacustrine dune system within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, USA, on Lake Superior. Wind provides disturbance which has continually influenced the successional pathways of these dunes. The objectives of this study were to identify the relationships between forest stand age, successional processes, and overall forest development by categorizing forest type and regeneration patterns, mapping the dendrochronological sequence, and quantifying coarse woody debris (CWD) accumulation in the Grand Sable Dunes. title: Challenges in the sustainable management of archaeotourism: insights from Ireland
abstract: Purpose The sustainable management of archaeotourism sites involves reviewing existing practices to develop more effective strategies that benefit the site, the host community and the tourism industry. This paper examines the challenges faced by stakeholders involved in the management of a range of archaeotourism sites in Ireland. New insights reveal interconnected challenges essential for sustainable archaeotourism management. abstract: Background : The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an educational module regarding the alternative birthing practice of water birth on the knowledge of pregnant mothers. Objectives : The objectives were to assess the pre-test knowledge of pregnant mothers regarding water birth, evaluate the effectiveness of the educational module in improving their knowledge, and determine the association between pre-test knowledge scores and selected demographic variables. title: Thrombo‐Occlusive Vasculopathy and Dual‐Excipient Granuloma Secondary to Subcutaneous Injection of Crushed Codeine Tablets
abstract: Skin popping refers to the subcutaneous injection of drugs, including crushed oral tablets modified into injectable solutions. Pharmaceutical excipients such as microcrystalline cellulose and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) are deposited into the tissue, provoking foreign body reactions. A 44-year-old man presented with bilateral painful ulcerated lesions on the extensor forearms. He was otherwise healthy with no history of renal impairment. title: Ecologies of Gendered Vulnerability in South Asia: Displacement, Disaster, Resource Conflict, and the Cultural Politics of Ecologies of Violence
abstract: Environmental disruption in South Asia is closely associated with gender inequality, displacement, livelihood insecurity, and violence. Floods, cyclones, droughts, riverbank erosion, heat stress, water scarcity, and resource extraction affect populations differently because access to land, income, mobility, social protection, and political institutions is unequal. Women and girls may face heightened risks due to gendered labor divisions, insecure property rights, care responsibilities, mobility restrictions, and exclusion from environmental decision-making. title: Traditions and experiments in contemporary jewelry art education
abstract: The article examines the methodology for training future jewelry artists, which is based on artistic-technological experimental research activities. The relevance of the study is due to the need to combine traditional hand techniques of artistic metalworking with the experimental application of new materials, technologies and design-engineering solutions. The methodology is presented through the example of students developing a collection of jewelry based on the artistic heritage of the Maya civilization. title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Preventive Practices among Communities Living Near a Tobacco Processing Factory in Morogoro Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Background: Tobacco processing factories contribute to environmental pollution through the release of smoke, dust, and chemical pollutants that may negatively affect the health of nearby communities. Despite increasing concerns regarding environmental health risks associated with tobacco processing activities, limited information exists on the knowledge, attitudes, and prevention practices of communities living near tobacco processing factories in Tanzania. title: Operational Performance in Global Maritime Freight Transport: A Multi-Criteria Analysis of Selected Countries
abstract: A general review of the literature reveals that performance in maritime freight transport is examined from various dimensions, such as port efficiency, transport costs, trade volume, operational times and infrastructure characteristics. Whilst econometric studies highlight the economic impacts of performance, multi-criteria analyses enable the integrated assessment of various indicators. journal: Journal of Decision Science and Applications

title: Geographic Spillover of Merger Effects Within Retail Chains
abstract: This study examines the role of downstream retail chains in shaping the effects of upstream mergers. Focusing on PepsiCo's bottler acquisitions, I present evidence that the merger effects spilled over within retail chains to stores outside the territory of acquired bottlers. I find that the acquisitions reduced PepsiCo product prices by 4.3% for these outside‐territory stores, with varying magnitudes depending on retail chains' exposures, and by 7.8% for retail chains operating solely inside the territory. title: Structure–fermentation–function relationships of prebiotics: linking molecular features to clinical outcomes
abstract: Prebiotics are dietary modulators of the gut microbiota with demonstrated links to human health; however, existing literature remains largely descriptive and lacks integration of how molecular structure determines functional efficacy. This review provides a mechanistic synthesis of structure–fermentation–function relationships across established and emerging prebiotics, emphasizing degree of polymerization, glycosidic linkage type, and branching architecture as determinants of microbial utilization and metabolic outcomes. title: Evaluating Tree Diversity and Carbon Sequestration in Kandyan Home Gardens: Implications for Climate-Smart Agroforestry and Carbon Mitigation
abstract: Agroforestry systems are increasingly recognized for their dual capacity to sequester carbon and sustain biodiversity, yet fine-scale assessments of tropical home gardens remain limited. This study quantified species composition, above- and below-ground biomass, and carbon storage across four Kandyan home garden sites in Sri Lanka, encompassing 500 trees from 21 species. Total carbon (TC) ranged from 25,629 to 33,030 kg C per site. title: Digitalization of Cooperative Governance in Indonesia: Legal Adaptation to Electronic General Meetings and Electronic Voting
abstract: This study examines the legal adaptation required for digital cooperative governance in Indonesia, focusing on electronic General Meetings and electronic voting. Using doctrinal legal research, it analyzes the Cooperative Law (Law No. 25 of 1992, as amended in relevant part by Law No. 6 of 2023), the Electronic Information and Transactions Law (Law No. 11 of 2008, as amended by Laws No. 19 of 2016 and No. 1 of 2024), and Government Regulations No. 7 of 2021 and No. 71 of 2019. journal: Boletín de la Asociación Internacional de Derecho Cooperativo

title: Gaze Behavior in Pedophilia and Hebephilia: How Task Instruction and Sexual Interest Shape Viewing of Prepubescent and Pubescent Stimuli
abstract: Visuospatial attentional processes are central in eye-tracking research of deviant sexual interest, yet it remains unclear to what extent task instructions modulate early (time to first fixation; number of first fixation) and late visuospatial attention (relative fixation time). We examined gaze behavior in individuals with pedophilic, hebephilic, and teleiophilic sexual interests while viewing prepubescent, early pubescent, and adult stimuli under free-viewing and forced-choice (attractiveness rating) conditions. title: Moon Watching Quiets the Ego: Implications for Death Acceptance
abstract: Although research on natural environments has focused largely on terrestrial settings, little is known about the psychological effects of celestial nature. We propose that moon watching fosters a quiet ego, a balanced, less defensive orientation toward the self and others, and thereby promotes death acceptance. Across seven studies involving 1,437 participants and 15,806 social media posts, we combined natural-language analysis, laboratory experiments, recall tasks, cross-cultural samples, and a field experiment. title: Temporal Wayfinding in Built Environments of Power: "Understanding" and "Exploration" in Villa Pisani and Villa Valmarana
abstract: This interdisciplinary qualitative study examines wayfinding in historically layered environments by extending the Preference Matrix (Kaplan et al., 1998, p.13) beyond its original spatial framework to include a temporal dimension. Integrating insights from Azaryahu and Foote (2008) on spatialized historical narratives, this study conceptualizes meaning as emerging from visitors’ present moment experience while walking through space, as perceptual understanding and exploration unfold in situ. title: A postmortem effect plays an important role in mineral formation
abstract: Igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary forms of the mineral genesis of main mineral-rock types are mature categories in terrestrial mineral lithology. In recent decades, the presence of a further large category, biomineralization, has been outlined. Questions regarding small-scale mineral assemblages have been partially answered by the processes found in large-scale sedimentary ore deposits. title: The ‘Herodotus Museum’: student engagement, object-based learning, and innovative design in a second-year undergraduate unit
abstract: This article examines the design, implementation, and outcomes of an exercise in object-based learning we came to refer to as ‘the Herodotus Museum’: a physical representation of objects and themes from Herodotus’ Histories. It discusses the rationale and learning context of this exercise, and explores the way in which it contributed to the learning outcomes of the course of which it was part. I show how engaging in this exercise helped students to make sense of the world Herodotus created in the Histories in new ways. title: In-situ Gamma Spectrometric Assessment of Terrestrial Gamma Radiation Dose Rates and their Geological Controls in the Pindiga Formation, Gombe State, Nigeria
abstract: This study presents a radiological assessment of the Pindiga Formation, North-Eastern Nigeria, based on in-situ measurements of terrestrial gamma radiation dose (TGRD) rates as well as activity concentrations of 238U, 232Th and 40K across 37 locations. The objectives were to establish lithological controls on dose distribution, and estimate associated health risks to residents. title: Comparative Assessment of Biochemical Composition and Nutritional Value of Two Freshwater Fishes, Channa striata and Catla catla
abstract: Fish is an important source of high-quality animal protein and contributes valuable lipids and other nutrients to the human diet. The biochemical composition of fish muscle varies among species and is influenced by biological characteristics, feeding habits and environmental conditions. The present study was designed to compare the biochemical composition and nutritional characteristics of two freshwater food fishes, Channa striata and Catla catla. title: Geopolitical Consequences of Geologic Hydrogen for the United States
abstract: The potential rise of geologic hydrogen as a prominent primary energy source might trigger geopolitical consequences that would be significant enough to warrant robust analysis and preparation.

title: How to Evaluate Participant Demographics in Citizen Science: Design Guidelines for Ethical and Inclusive Best Practice
abstract: Who participates in citizen science influences a project’s impacts. Lack of inclusion risks exacerbating environmental and social injustices or creates unrepresentative or biased datasets. However, many projects fail to gather information on participant demographics, and there is a lack of guidance for citizen science researchers on conducting demographic surveys, as our literature review demonstrates. title: Myroides odoratimimus clinical outcomes biofilm formation environmental surveillance and in vitro evaluation of novel antimicrobial agents
abstract: Myroides species are emerging opportunistic Gram-negative pathogens increasingly associated with healthcare-associated infections and poor clinical outcomes. This study investigated the clinical characteristics, antimicrobial resistance, biofilm formation, and in vitro activity of ceftazidime/avibactam, cefiderocol, and aztreonam–ceftazidime/avibactam against clinical M. odoratimimus isolates. A total of 44 Myroides odoratimimus isolates recovered between January 2023 and April 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. title: The Criminal Panopticon: Armed Power, Surveillance, and The Transnational Expansion of the PCC and CV
abstract: This article presents the concept of the Criminal Panopticon as a theoretical and conceptual tool to understand the forms of power and surveillance exercised by Illegal Armed Groups (IAGs) in Brazil, which are increasingly assuming transnational dimensions. Inspired by Foucault and Mbembe, and in dialogue with the literature on IAGs and drug trafficking within the field of Critical Security Studies, the study demonstrates that the power of groups such as the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho (CV) stems from the selective presence of the State. title: Whose Village, Whose Art? Decolonizing Rural Institutions Through Indigenous Visual Knowledge in South Asia and Latin America
abstract: What does it mean for a community to lose the right to define its own knowledge? This paper exhibits how indigenous visual traditions in South Asia have been systematically misread by metropolitan art institutions that claim to celebrate them. Drawing on Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement (2016) and Jungle Nama (2021), Mahasweta Devi’s “Douloti the Bountiful,” and Gabriel García Márquez’s No One Writes to the Colonel (1961), the paper argues that the same structural failures Ghosh identifies in literary culture are reproduced in the visual art world. title: A Green Reduced-Alkali Hydrothermal Route for the Valorisation of Indian Coal Fly Ash into Zeolitic Aluminosilicates: Structural, Morphological and Textural Characterisation
abstract: Coal combustion in India generates over 270 million tonnes of fly ash annually, much of which remains stored in ash ponds. Converting this waste into zeolitic aluminosilicates is scientifically promising, as fly ash possesses significant silica and alumina content comparable to conventional zeolite precursor materials. However, most synthesis methods require concentrated alkali, high temperatures, or alkali-fusion pre-treatment, raising environmental and economic costs. title: Valorization of methanotrophic bacterial biomass as a sustainable protein source for aquaculture: A case study with juvenile rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
abstract: Methanotrophic bacteria convert methane, a potent greenhouse gas, into protein-rich biomass. A Type II methanotroph, Methylocystis sp. MJC1, was cultivated in a gas bioreactor, yielding biomass with a crude protein content of 53.86% protein on a dry cell weight basis, and 2.3 kg was produced in three large-scale batch fermentations. This methanotrophic bacterial protein (MBP) was evaluated as an alternative to fishmeal (FM) in juvenile rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). title: Terrestrial protected areas have not been effective in mitigating human pressure on biodiversity
abstract: Global biodiversity is declining rapidly and protected areas are a major conservation measure aiming to reverse this negative trend by limiting pressures on biodiversity in particular locations. There are increasing calls to protect larger areas, but also growing evidence that an increase in area alone is insufficient. At least as important is the effectiveness of existing and new protected areas. title: High-damage-threshold metasurfaces with apertures exceeding 100 mm fabricated by spatiotemporally shaped femtosecond laser
abstract: Metasurfaces offer powerful capabilities for light field manipulation, yet their practical deployment in high-power laser systems remains limited by low laser-induced damage thresholds (LIDTs), small apertures, and low absolute conversion efficiency (ACE). Here, we demonstrate a circular Airy-like beam generator and a quarter-wave plate with high LIDTs and large apertures, which are realized through spatiotemporal and polarization co-shaping femtosecond-laser processing. title: Alkali Metal Potassium-Synergistically Driven Dual-Phase High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide/Spinel Heterostructure for Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: The sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis for hydrogen production and its heavy dependence on noble metal catalysts restrict the large-scale application of green hydrogen energy. title: Species-agnostic tools for Influenza A H5 antibody and NP antigen detection in dairy cows, chickens, and humans
abstract: High Pathogenicity Avian Influenza (HPAI) A (H5N1) circulates in wild birds, causing outbreaks in domestic poultry, but recently became enzootic in the United States spilling over into various mammals, including cattle. The zoonotic potential of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b emphasizes the need for tools for surveillance in mammalian and avian species. title: Microbial Resurgence in Degraded Soils: Early‐Stage Recovery of Biological Quality by Legume Cover Crops in Alluvial Gold‐Mining Areas
abstract: Artisanal and small‐scale gold mining in the southeastern Amazonian department of Madre de Dios, Peru, has caused severe soil degradation characterized by extreme sand dominance, nutrient depletion, and disrupted microbial communities. Conventional restoration approaches have often resulted insufficient, highlighting the need for evidence‐based strategies. This study evaluated five legume cover crops— Stylosanthes guianensis , Pueraria phaseoloides , Canavalia ensiformis , Centrosema macrocarpum , and Crotalaria juncea —and a control as nature‐based solutions for soil health recovery. abstract: The present study was conducted in the Chillavaripalli and Ellutla Reserve Forests of Ananthapuramu District, Andhra Pradesh, India, to assess the diversity and composition of herpetofauna, comprising amphibians and reptiles, in the study area. The field investigations were carried out over a two-year period, from October 2024 to September 2026. abstract: OBJECTIVES: Tobacco and nicotine are known to alter the oral microbiome, thereby promoting dysbiosis. The impact of new nicotine forms, such as electronic cigarettes (e-cigs), on oral dysbiosis remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the microbial biofilm composition and carbohydrate presence in e-cig users' saliva. title: Intermodal Competition and Balance Between Transport Modes
abstract: The article examines competition and the economic balance between transport modes in Uzbekistan, focusing on freight flows, cost structures, service characteristics, and the role of transport and logistics in national economic development. It considers road, railway, air, and pipeline transport and explains how their relative advantages depend on distance, cargo characteristics, delivery time, reliability, and infrastructure costs. title: Societal Norms and Risky Sexual Behaviour among Undergraduate Students in Nakuru County, Kenya
abstract: This study examined the association between societal norms and risky sexual behaviour among undergraduate students in university town campuses in Nakuru County, Kenya. The study adopted a descriptive correlational approach and collected quantitative and qualitative data. The target population comprised 1,161 third-year undergraduate students from Egerton University, St. Paul’s University and Kabarak University. title: Redescription, with molecular information, of Trinigyrus peregrinus (Monogenea: Dactylogyridae) from the invasive Pterygoplichthys pardalis in southern China
abstract: Pterygoplichthys pardalis, an invasive fish native to South America, has established feral populations worldwide and poses substantial ecological risks. In this study, we identified and redescribed Trinigyrus peregrinus infecting P. pardalis from three localities across southern China. title: ( IM ) POSSIBLE REALISM : A counterpoint (Part Two)
abstract: Part One of this dialogue—a discussion of ethnography, photographs, film, spectral reality, and heterotemporality—appeared in VAR 41:2. Part Two engages the “conjunctural history” and articulation politics of Stuart Hall, whose thinking has been pivotal for Clifford and Mollona. It continues with a discussion of “decolonization” in ethnographic and art museums and stresses the interventions of Indigenous artists. It concludes with summary comments on the (im)possible realism that is needed to account, nonreductively, for the confusions and possibilities of the present moment.

title: HEALTH CONDITIONS IN THE EASTERN SAHARA: THE ZIBAN REGION AS A CASE STUDY (1700-1900)
abstract: This study examines an important aspect of the modern history of the Eastern Sahara and the Ziban. It focuses on health conditions as a reflection of the social and economic difficulties experienced in the region. The study seeks to identify the principal diseases and epidemics that affected local communities. It also considers forms of medical treatment that became widespread in the area. Particular attention is given to their effectiveness and to the ways in which residents responded to these treatments.

title: Fermentation Time and Proximate Composition of Pedek from Ranai, Natuna: A Bioprocess Engineering Review
abstract: Pedek is a traditional fermented anchovy (Stolephorus sp.) product from Ranai, Natuna Regency, processed with salt and kandis acid in an airtight container. Although designated a regional flagship product, its processing remains spontaneous, with fermentation ranging from three days to two weeks and quality varying among producers. This review synthesises evidence on how fermentation time shapes the proximate composition of pedek and analogous fermented fish products, and proposes a process window for standardisation. title: Self-organized fractal architectures driven by motility-dependent chemotactic feedback
abstract: Complex organization in living systems often emerges through self-organization driven by local interactions. During processes such as vasculogenesis and epithelial remodeling, cells both generate and respond to self-produced chemical cues to coordinate collective behavior. Here, we introduce a minimal agent-based model in which agents deposit a chemical only while moving and subsequently bias their motion up local chemical gradients through a saturating chemotactic response. title: Frustration in the middle: emotional strain in the vice-principalship
abstract: Vice-principals face multiple structural and relational challenges in their work, yet frustration in this role has received limited scholarly attention. This study examines how high school vice-principals understand, interpret, and articulate frustration in their professional lives. Using a qualitative design, in depth interviews were conducted with 16 Israeli vice-principals. title: Prevalence of depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and stress and associated factors among Palestinian nurses in the Gaza Strip during the war
abstract: BACKGROUND: The ongoing war in the Gaza Strip has profoundly affected the psychological well-being of healthcare workers, particularly nurses, who provide frontline care amid continuous violence, displacement, and resource scarcity. Understanding the mental health consequences of these extreme working conditions is essential for developing targeted interventions and institutional support mechanisms. title: Sustainable Eco-Tourism Potentials of Mt. Kabalalaan in Barangay Badak, Datu Odin Sinsuat Maguindanao Del Norte, Philippines
abstract: Eco-tourism promotes appreciation and local heritage, traditions, and cultural diversity. Mount Kabalalaan, renowned for its rich biodiversity, scenic landscapes, and cultural heritage, presents significant potential for eco-tourism development. Yet, despite these natural and cultural assets, the area remains underutilized due to the absence of a structured framework for sustainable eco-tourism. abstract: This study examined the dynamics of United States strategic engagement in the Middle East between 2001 and 2025, focusing on its military, diplomatic and security dimensions. It investigated how American strategic interests, regional alliances, energy security, geopolitical influence and emerging security threats have shaped United States foreign policy towards the region. abstract: Community-based forest management plays an important role in promoting sustainable forest management, enhancing local participation in forest governance, conserving biological diversity and improving the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities. In Cameroon, the introduction of the concept of community forestry under Law No. 94/01 of 20 January 1994 to lay down Forestry, Wildlife and Fisheries Regulations was intended to decentralize forest management by granting local communities access to and responsibility for managing forest resources. abstract: Hamath, a Syrian kingdom of Neo‑Hittite origin, may have played a role of mediation and, therefore, transmission towards the Israelite world of some elements of the rich Hittite cultural tradition. title: Beyond Border Delays: Explaining Cross-Country Variation in Road Freight Transit Time Along East Africa’s Northern Corridor
abstract: Efficient road freight transit is essential for regional trade integration, supply-chain reliability, and the competitiveness of landlocked economies served by East Africa’s Northern Corridor. However, freight movements may be delayed by administrative and regulatory stops, including police/security checks, customs inspections, weighbridges, and border-post procedures. abstract: Dreams lie between the realms of memory, emotion, subconscious thought and imagination, between realities and illusions, between logic and chaos, between fear and freedom of mind. abstract: La terminal de aguas profundas DP World Posorja, la de mayor volumen de contenedores en Ecuador, sustenta el control de accesos y movimientos en el sistema TOS Navis N4 y en el sistema automatizado de puertas Camco GOS, lo que genera una vulnerabilidad operativa crítica ante fallas informáticas. abstract: The Teaching and Research Farm of the Faculty of Agriculture, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, is a source of crop trials, teaching and soil science research, but the horizon-level information of its soils is lacking. This study characterized and provisionally classified three pedons (P1, P2 and P3) selected across the farm’s soil–landscape units. title: Taking Diplomacy to the Field: Conservation Diplomacy in the Belizean Chiquibul Borderlands and Beyond
abstract: Conservation diplomacy has predominantly referred to bilateral treaty-building to safeguard biodiversity. This raises the following question: What does conservation diplomacy entail in complex transboundary environments? This article explores the diplomatic endeavors of conservationists who straddle tense international relations in the Belizean Guatemalan borderlands. title: Nutritional Quality of Pearl Millet-Based Breakfast Gruel (Ogi) Substituted with African Catfish Powder
abstract: Ogi is a fermented cereal slurry that is steamed until it becomes a paste. In Nigeria, this is a traditional dish that is loved by both adults and children. Nonetheless, a significant amount of nutrients are lost throughout the ogi production process. These losses come from the different unit operations that it experiences. title: Silicate Solubilizing Microorganisms as Drivers of Soil Fertility and Plant Nutrition: Mechanisms, Plant Benefits and Critical Research Gaps
abstract: The majority of silicon (Si) in soil is immobilized into poorly soluble silicate minerals, despite the fact that Si reinforces plant tissues, promotes growth, and aids crops in enduring biotic and abiotic stress. Silicate-solubilizing microorganisms (SSMs) are capable of releasing Si along with related cations such as K, Ca, and Mg in forms that can be taken up by roots. abstract: Background: The Zanryu Koji (残留孤児), Japanese children separated from their families during the 1945 Soviet invasion of Manchuria and raised in northeastern China, constitute one of East Asia's most historically complex diasporic communities. Resettled in Osaka from the late 1970s, this population negotiates a distinctive double displacement: culturally Chinese yet legally Japanese. abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) are among the most clinically significant symptoms of schizophrenia, yet they vary widely in subjective experience, ranging from elementary auditory phenomena to complex dialogues, and from internally located voices to experiences perceived as externally imposed. This heterogeneity limits clinical assessment and treatment planning, because hallucinations are still often approached as a unitary symptom. abstract: Founded in 2020, the Sanseitō party surprised Japanese society with its success in the national elections. In the House of Councilors, it gained its first seat in 2022 and seven in 2025. Despite their significant social and political impact, little scientific analysis has been conducted on their rapid rise to power. What is the Sanseitō ? What is its history ? title: The Elegance of Survival: French Perfume Houses, Logistics and the Politics of Continuity, 1940–1945
abstract: While the Second World War severely disrupted the French economy, the perfume industry maintained both its activity and prestige. Between 1940 and 1945, leading firms devised ingenious logistical strategies to overcome shortages, blockades, and surveillance through material substitution, recycling, parallel trade, and chemical innovation. Supported by the Vichy regime and regarded as a vehicle of national prestige, the sector adapted to supply chain breakdowns through a mix of circumvention and compromise. abstract: In Ghanaian Theatre for Development (TfD) practice, the use of indigenous languages, including Fante, Twi and Ewe, alongside or in place of English is commonly framed as a pragmatic measure for ensuring community accessibility and engagement. abstract: Web 2.0 has expanded the public circulation of science, making social media increasingly relevant to educational practice. abstract: 1. Las especies exóticas invasoras (EEI) son organismos que se expanden rápidamente fuera de su área de origen y generan impactos ecológicos, económicos y sociales. abstract: Background: North Central Vietnam preserves diverse traditions of visual expression, from Dong Son bronze-drum decoration to textiles, folk paintings, and royal enamelwork. Their use in contemporary applied arts offers opportunities for distinctive products but also risks reducing situated cultural practices to detachable ornament. title: Environmental short-term risk assessment in 66,651 cases of urgent hospital admissions among patients with IBD in Poland
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) incidence is rising worldwide, yet evidence on short-term associations between environmental exposures and urgent IBD hospitalisations remains limited in population-based evidence, particularly in Poland, a country at the stage of emergence. abstract: This essay reviews 25 years of contemporary practice by the architect Marie Andreé Soundy Escobar, rooted in Central America’s vernacular traditions. abstract: Workplace relationships and collaborative performance are key factors in organizational effectiveness, and many organizations still rely on siloed, single-discipline strategies that don't fully account for the multidisciplinary nature of the modern workplace. abstract: The research focuses on the impact of domestic politics on India’s China policy from 1991 to 2004. abstract: Global change is altering fire regimes worldwide, exposing fire-sensitive ecosystems such as Patagonia’s to unprecedented fire sizes and frequencies, which can result in irreversible soil degradation. abstract: Every trait in an organism reflects the formation of a particular phenotypic state jointly shaped by genotype, environment, and the intrinsic dynamics of a developing system. abstract: The Tumbu Tanah Dance is an intangible cultural heritage of the Arfak Tribe community in Manokwari, Papua. This research aims to examine the Tumbu Tanah Dance comprehensively with an ethnochoreogralogical approach, focusing on the documentation and analysis of the components that make up the dance, including history, goals, movements, formations, accompanying music, musical instruments, accessories, and the values contained in it. abstract: Diaporthe is a large genus of ascomycetous fungi comprising plant pathogens, saprophytes and endophytes. In 2016, on Buxus sempervirens ornamental plantings in Krasnodar, Russia, shoots bearing dead straw‐coloured leaves with abundantly developed ascomata were observed and collected. abstract: Cameroon’s decade-long Anglophone Crisis has largely been analyzed as a conflict between the Anglophone minority and the majority-Francophone state. abstract: Photochemical mechanisms are core components of air quality models, yet differences among them can introduce substantial uncertainty in tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) simulations. abstract: The present study tries to evaluate the predictability of academic performance related tosome income indicators in students attending the career of Medicine. The investigation design was cross-sectional and retrospective of students who entered in the course 2005-2007. The variables used were: academic index in high-school, overall average in income tests, age, gender, place of birth and overall average of the first four semesters of career. abstract: Shifts in predator-prey interactions in response to environmental change can affect population dynamics and community structure, but have received relatively little attention in the climate change literature. abstract: This article examines waiata pakanga as living literature through four compositions connected to Māori experiences of world war: Te Ope Tuatahi, Arohaina Mai, Hitara Waha Huka and Tomo Mai. title: ‘Better emulate the Irish resistance’: Influences of the Irish literary revival on Taiwanese literature and politics during and after the Japanese occupation
abstract: The Irish Literary Revival emerged in response to centuries of cultural suppression and linguistic marginalisation in Ireland under British rule, alongside disillusionment with the Home Rule movement. It sought to define Irishness, revive the Irish language, and construct a distinct national literature, ultimately contributing to the Easter Rising of 1916 and the formation of the Irish Free State. This movement resonated in colonial Taiwan under Japanese rule (1895–1945), where Irish nationalist writing was widely read and discussed, shaping anti-colonial intellectual currents and independence

abstract: The mountains of Central Asia are a major region of global biodiversity, but the flora of this area remains understudied relative to other temperate biodiversity hotspots. (subtribe Nepetinae) is one of the most species-rich genera in Central Asia. title: Subaltern Macedonian Heritage in Northern Greece: A Model for Inclusive Heritage Use and Sustainable Peace
abstract: Greece is largely based on a narrative of a homogeneous nation. When it comes to heritage, the application of an Authorized Heritage Discourse leaves little space for subaltern identity expression. Such is the cultural and linguistic heritage of the local Macedonians (dopii), ethnic Macedonians and other people that identify with non-dominant Slav cultural expressions which have been hierarchized in the process of Greek nation-building and deemed dissonant and unwanted, under the fear of irredentism. abstract: Microalgae are a promising feedstock for producing fuels and chemicals, but biodiesel production from their oil remains constrained by reliance on n-hexane, a toxic, fossil-based solvent. Furthermore, improving the technical and economic performance of microalgae-based biofuels requires an energetically efficient oil extraction step. title: Forest cover and coexistence modulate wolf nocturnality and temporal human avoidance across southern Europe
abstract: Understanding how wolves adjust their temporal activity in response to human presence is essential for managing coexistence in increasingly human‐dominated landscapes. We analysed diel activity patterns of wolves across four southern European study areas in Portugal and Croatia, which differ in levels of human coexistence, forest availability, and human activity intensity. title: Pensar la traducción en América Latina desde el archivo. Sujetos, genealogía y experiencia colectiva
abstract: La traducción es una experiencia vital en la cultura impresa y sus dinámicas, y ha sido un eje de la producción cultural y la historia intelectual en América Latina y el Caribe. El acto traductor es un acto ético situado histórica y políticamente y un espacio de producción de discurso. abstract: The mentoring teacher plays a fundamental role in supporting future physical education (PE) teachers during their teaching practicum in schools. Therefore, the objective of this study was to understand the perceptions of mentoring teachers regarding the support they provide during the teaching practicum of future physical education teachers in the school context of a region in south-central Chile. abstract: Recognising the challenges that international students face in integrating the Portuguese Education System, NOVA University launched a semester-long Foundation Program in 2017. Within this program, we introduced the Ideas Club course in 2020 to promote students’ engagement and facilitate long-term academic success. abstract: The aim of this study was to study the floral biology and pollen quality of 4 hazelnut cultivars ('Romavel', 'Vâlcea 22', 'Uriaș de Halle' and 'Tonda Gentile delle Langhe' ('TGDL') cultivated in Leleasca area, Olt County, Romania. abstract: The production of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by the gut microbiota has garnered attention due to its potential role as a driver of gut-brain axis signaling. However, mechanisms regulating microbiota-derived GABA under physiological conditions remain unclear. abstract: The objective of the study was to assess the maturity period, physico-chemical and biological properties of composts made from water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), an aquatic weed from Lake Victoria, Kenya. A randomised complete block design (RCBD) experiment with three treatments, replicated three times, was set up in the Lake Victoria basin, Kenya. title: Screening Tools and Interventions Used by Healthcare Professionals to Identify and Support Victims of Coercive Control: a Scoping Review
abstract: Purpose Coercive and controlling behaviour can have long-term consequences for victims and often precedes physical violence or homicide. Due to its subtle presentation and the normalisation of abusive behaviours, it frequently goes unrecognised. Healthcare settings provide an opportunity to identify abuse, enabling earlier intervention and potentially better long-term outcomes. abstract: This article examines how ecological citizenship is differentially enacted by residents in Singapore through everyday waste practices. It argues that household waste management is a key site through which the state governs environmental conduct by framing waste routines as civic responsibility and mobilising residents to sustain a highly engineered sociotechnical regime. title: Host trophic strategy decouples microbial and arthropod community assembly in sympatric tropical pitcher plants
abstract: Community assembly in natural ecosystems reflects the interplay between environmental filtering, resource inputs, and dispersal processes. We tested whether host trophic strategy and spatial position act as environment and resource filters structuring microbial and pitcher-associated arthropod communities in sympatric Nepenthes pitcher plants. abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across the spectrum of surgical risk, substantially improving symptoms and clinical outcomes. abstract: This article reads Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña’s La casa lobo (2018) through the figure of the counterfeit editor, which Fred Botting identifies in the Gothic novel as the voice that vouches for a found manuscript. The film passes itself off as an instructional reel rescued from the shelves of a German colony in Chile modeled on Colonia Dignidad, and its prologue rewrites, almost phrase by phrase, the sleeve note of a record the colony released in 1969. abstract: This research explores the fundamental elements of social harmony within three major indigenous communities in Bangladesh: the Chakma, Marma, and Garo. As global interest in inclusive policy intensifies, there is an urgent need to understand how these cultures sustain social cohesion through unique rituals, values, and communal practices. title: Apta-photonic biosensor based on cholesteric liquid crystal network nanoarchitectonics for the visual detection of thiamethoxam
abstract: In this study, we present a cholesteric liquid crystal network-based (CLCN) apta-photonic biosensor for the selective and real-time detection of thiamethoxam, a widely used neonicotinoid pesticide. The biosensor utilizes aptamers for target recognition, coupled with the optical photonic properties of CLCNs to produce visible color changes in response to pesticide binding. abstract: This essay examines Isaac Julien’s multiscreen installation Lina Bo Bardi–A Marvellous Entanglement (2019) as an atmospheric encounter between moving images, architecture, and the cultural imagination of public space. Through Julien’s cinematic traversal of Bo Bardi’s buildings in São Paulo and Salvador, the article explores how montage, screen arrangement, choreography, and the use of elemental agents produce a relational environment. title: Cuerpos que retornan del archivo. Los mutilados de la Guerra del Pacífico y sus reapropiaciones desde las artes visuales. Mario Soro y Luis Montes Rojas
abstract: Este artículo examina las reapropiaciones contemporáneas de las imágenes de mutilados de la Guerra del Pacífico (1879–1884) en las artes visuales chilenas, a partir de las obras de Mario Soro y Luis Montes Rojas. title: Comitative constructions in Southern Mansi
abstract: The article describes the comitative markers of the extinct Southern Mansi language — two postpositions (jitəl and jortəl) and the suffix -nat/-nät — on the basis of corpus data and compares them with those of Northern Mansi in terms of Stassen 2000, Stolz and Stroh and Urdze 2006, and Arkhipov 2009. The analysis shows that all the comitative markers under consideration occur in genuine comitative constructions (ComCs), such as ’go with someone’. The postpositions are also used in ComCs with polyadic predicates (e.g., ’fight with’) and in coordinating ComCs (with the structure “X Y-com V.pl”).

abstract: This article investigates factors associated with self‐reported Indigenous‐State treaty understanding among caregivers of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander youth. abstract: The integration of digital technologies into agriculture has encouraged the use of drones as tools for precision farming, with the potential to reduce operating costs and improve processes. abstract: El principio de parsimonia consiste en elegir la explicación más simple y menos compleja de un fenómeno. title: Displacement-in-place: Waiting, immobility, and the cinematic grammar of absence in Hakim Belabbes' Boiling Dreams (2011)
abstract: This article examines Hakim Belabbes’ Boiling Dreams as a migration film organized around the woman who does not migrate. abstract: En els darrers anys, la llengua catalana ha despertat un interès creixent arreu del món, i la Xina no n’és una excepció. abstract: The brain has long been studied as a self-contained organ, and environmental microbes have long been studied as agents of ecosystem function and disease. abstract: Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is a pseudocereal crop valued for its nutritional composition, particularly its relatively high protein content. abstract: La investigación sobre el trauma temprano vincula el maltrato infantil con diferencias neurobiológicas, dificultades en la regulación emocional y determinados rasgos de personalidad. abstract: Waxes in cultural heritage are not a single chemical class but a group of hydrophobic, low-melting organic materials that may function as original binders or modeling media, use-related surfaces, protective coatings, or later conservation and restoration materials. abstract: In 2025, Brazilian democracy celebrated its fortieth anniversary. abstract: This study was initiated alongside an investigation of a heritage artifact illustrating the confluences of Baroque within a space predominantly shaped by Catholicism in the eighteenth century. However, Baroque is not merely a style associated with the Counter-Reformation and the post-Tridentine world; it also manifested within the Orthodox sphere. Accordingly, this research seeks to explore the artistic universe shaped by Zaharija Orfelin’s creations, aiming to identify the stylistic elements adopted by Romanian painters from this master, recognized as a foundational figure of Serbian Baroque.

title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
abstract: Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers' mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. In response, disaster mental health professionals from across Japan were mobilized on an unprecedented scale. abstract: The Manisa Great Mosque occupies a significant place in the development of Anatolian mosque architecture through its multi-support plan scheme, domed bay before the mihrab, and courtyard arrangement. Together with the adjacent madrasa and tomb, the complex reflects the architectural characteristics of the Seljuk and Principalities periods and represents one of the most important architectural ensembles of fourteenth-century western Anatolia. abstract: Reconstruction was the American state's first sustained peacetime intervention into local communities, and the Freedmen's Bureau was its most important component. What was the social impact of this program? Using an original data set on Freedmen's Bureau operations, we link the distribution and duration of Bureau offices to local socioeconomic outcomes. abstract: While the positive effects of rhizobia on legume performance are well understood, it remains unclear how these effects scale up to plant-plant interactions and community assembly. This scaling is complicated by the fact that plant-rhizobia interactions depend on nitrogen availability, which is spatially heterogeneous and increasing due to anthropogenic inputs. abstract: This article examines the state of the British contingent of the Palestine Police Force (PPF) during the ‘Jewish Revolt’ of 1944 to 1948. Faced by constant attacks by the Irgun and Lehi—Zionist groups using armed violence in an attempt to bring British rule in Palestine to an end—British colonial policemen found themselves unprepared to encounter or fight back against such extreme violence. abstract: Carinata ( Brassica carinata A. Braun) and camelina ( Camelina sativa L. abstract: En las últimas décadas, las reformas educativas neoliberales han transformado profundamente el trabajo docente, especialmente en contextos donde estas políticas han sido implementadas con fuerza y persistencia. abstract: Este artículo examina críticamente la tendencia a interpretar dificultades cotidianas e interpersonales mediante el lenguaje de los trastornos mentales. abstract: Conventional separation-based water treatment can reduce microplastic loads but generally transfers polymer-derived carbon to secondary residual streams. abstract: Introduction Herbivory by wild animals poses a significant challenge for revegetation projects in the arid southwest. Reactive silicon (Si) may prove a promising alternative, as it is frequently induced in plants as a chemical defense against herbivory and is well associated with improved plant and soil health. abstract: Helichrysum nuratavicum Krasch. is a narrow endemic species, found only in the Nuratau Mountains of Uzbekistan. However, its molecular characteristics and phylogenetic position remain poorly understood. abstract: Deep coalbed methane (CBM) exploitation plays a vital strategic role in energy transition and energy structure optimization. Field exploration has verified widespread high enrichment of deep CBM in China, whereas its formation mechanism remains poorly understood, which severely restricts commercial extraction efficiency. This study focuses on the Daning–Jixian Block of the Ordos Basin. title: Building E-Government at the Grassroots under Vietnam's Two-Tier Local Government Model: Current Status and Solutions from Lai Thanh Commune, Ninh Binh Province
abstract: Since 1 July 2025, Vietnam has operated a two-tier local government model in which the commune has become the main point of contact between the state and citizens for most administrative procedures. This shift places e-government at commune level at the centre of public administration reform. This paper examines the current state of e-government at the People's Committee of Lai Thanh commune, Ninh Binh province, a rural commune formed from three former communes of Kim Son district. abstract: Orchidaceae is one of the most diverse plant families globally and is threatened by habitat loss, degradation and unsustainable collection. This study aimed to assess and document the orchid diversity in Jukethali Community Forest, Lalitpur, a relatively poorly documented area near Kathmandu. Systematic field surveys, specimen collection and morphological examination were conducted for species identification and taxonomic assessment. title: Iatrogenia digital en la primera infancia: una propuesta conceptual sobre los efectos no intencionados de las pantallas en la crianza
abstract: Este artículo es un ensayo teórico, sustentado en una revisión narrativa de la literatura, que propone la categoría de iatrogenia digital para describir los efectos adversos no intencionados que pueden derivarse del uso de pantallas como recurso de crianza en la primera infancia. title: From the Electronic Babylonian Literature Lab 54-56
abstract: Three new fragments from the Electronic Babylonian Literature project are presented. BM.109141, a large Old Babylonian tablet, restores several passages of Atram-ḫasīs Tablet II, including Atram-ḫasīs ’s river-bank prayer, Ea’s messengers, the drought famine, and Enlil’s accusation against Ea (no. 54). Four fragments of the 76-11-17 consignment join or duplicate BM.32255+, a Late Babylonian manuscript of the Cuthaean Legend of Narām-Sîn (no. 56).

abstract: Purity culture, a socioreligious framework promoting strict sexual abstinence, has been qualitatively linked to sexual shame and distress. title: Incidence and determinants of malaria recurrence in Andabiet district, Northwest Ethiopia: implications for malaria elimination
abstract: Malaria remains a significant public health burden, with recurrent infections posing challenges for control and elimination efforts. Evidence on the incidence and determinants of malaria recurrence in Ethiopia is limited. This study assessed the incidence of malaria recurrence and its contributing factors among patients in the Andabiet district, Northwest Ethiopia. title: Zombis y espectros: Representaciones indirectas del migrante en el arte contemporáneo
abstract: In the context of intensified forced displacement caused by armed conflicts, economic crises, and ecological collapses, contemporary art has developed strategies of representation that move away from direct testimony and the humanitarian paradigm. This article analyses how various artistic practices resort to indirect forms of conflict (ruins, objects, silences, and altered cartographies) to construct an aesthetic of precariousness, in which the migrant appears as a spectral or zombified figure: present and absent at the same time; alive but politically suspended. title: The Role of Local Artisans in the Architecture and Ornamentation of Masjid Darkhana Wali, Multan
abstract: Islamic architecture is ornamented and filled with symbols. The early mosques were very simple and plain, and emphasis lay on collective worship. In time, however, mosque architecture developed to integrate a great variety of ornament, such as geometric patterns, arabesque motifs, calligraphy, and elaborate surface decoration. The added elements not only added to the beauty of the religious structures, but also represented to Islamic believers the concept of paradise and the spiritual attributes of Islamic beliefs. abstract: Many insurance loss models, such as lognormal and Pareto I distributions, are special cases of the log-location-scale family. title: Trade Openness and Bilateral Trade Relations Between India & Sri Lanka: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: The paper will analyze the extent to which India and Sri Lanka rely on one another with respect to the trade based on trade openness (bilateral trade as a share of GDP) during 2006-2025. The findings indicate that there is a drastically skewed relationship. abstract: El envejecimiento de la población trabajadora constituye uno de los principales desafíos para la salud laboral. La creciente esperanza de vida, el retraso de la edad de jubilación y la coexistencia de varias generaciones en las organizaciones obligan a desarrollar estrategias que integren la edad como variable clave en la prevención de riesgos laborales. title: The Hidden Footprint of Hydrogel Adsorbents: Residual Monomer, Crosslinker and Nanofiller Leaching and the Ecotoxicity of Treated Water – A Critical Review
abstract: Hydrogel adsorbents are currently among the most investigated materials for the removal of colours, metals and medicines from water. Most articles evaluate them by capacity, speed and number of reusecycles . Hardly anybody asks what the gel leaves in the water that it has just cleansed. This review tackles that hidden footprint. abstract: Caecilians (Gymnophiona) are the least studied of the three extant amphibian orders, yet their predominantly fossorial or aquatic habits position them as potentially important predators within soil and freshwater food webs. Although over a century of scattered dietary observations exists, no synthesis of caecilian diet had previously been undertaken. title: Team diversity and radical green innovation: a patent-based analysis of gender, geographic, and institutional effects
abstract: Achieving ambitious climate goals hinges on radical green innovation, yet how inventor-team composition shapes the radicalness of green patents remains largely unexplored. abstract: Oil palm needs warm temperatures and a steady water supply, so climate change may affect its yield. This study examined whether long-term climate conditions were related to oil palm yield in Ecuador between 1975 and 2022, using Brazil as a comparison. Yield data from FAOSTAT were combined with temperature and rainfall data from the CRU TS 4.07 dataset. abstract: This article presents the preliminary findings of a research project on the experiences of Ottomans of African origin—referred to as Afro-Ottomans in this project—focusing on the Harem Ağalar Teavün Yurdu (The Eunuchs’ Mutual Aid Society), a mutual aid association founded by former harem eunuchs of African origin who remained free individuals in the late Ottoman and early Republican periods. Practitioners of “biospiritual” cultivation—exercises for nourishing qi , essence ( jing 精), and spirit ( shen 神)—also claimed that one’s inner spirit became radiant when properly nourished. abstract: Denne del er udarbejdet af Knud Vohn fra Det Kongelige Bibliotek og indeholder en bibliografisk oversigt over nyere bøger og publikationer inden for moderne historie og statskundskab. abstract: By the early 1620s, Morisco intellectuals in Tunisia were producing a notable corpus of religious texts in Spanish. title: From Khmer Independence to Act East Policy: Civilizational Narratives, Cultural Diplomacy, and the Transformation of India-Cambodia Relations
abstract: This article chronicles the evolution of India-Cambodia relations from Cambodian independence to the implementation of India's Act East Policy. abstract: Este artículo examina la representación del Quilombo de Palmares, centrando su atención en el papel del archivo colonial como fuente de inspiración para la imaginación poética del siglo XIX. abstract: This paper examines historical efforts to calculate the health manpower needs of the United States from 1950 to 1980, highlighting how perceived physician shortages justified efforts to maximize the effective utilization of existing medical labor. While federal and philanthropic investment was largely directed to increasing physician supply, research on how physicians might improve their productivity through delegating tasks to allied health personnel has received less attention. abstract: Electronic mediation has been retained as a permanent option in the Religious Courts after the Covid-19 pandemic through Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) Number 3 of 2022 to realize simple, fast, and low-cost justice. abstract: Assessing the energy efficiency of buildings and minimizing their operating costs are essential for reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: Community colleges are pivotal in expanding access to both science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and career and technical education (CTE). abstract: Episodic memory is grounded upon a spatiotemporal framework that binds discrete event details into a coherent structure. However, the neural mechanisms that construct this scaffold and their potential for memory enhancement through cognitive training have yet to be investigated. abstract: This paper presents the findings of a qualitative study carried out with young people aged 18 to 22 in Uruguay, which sought to examine the criteria, resources and strategies they use to assess media trust and the credibility of political news. abstract: La castración química voluntaria como condición de preacuerdo penal para agresores sexuales en Colombia es el objeto de este artículo. abstract: This paper examines the possible effect of women's representation at three organisational levels, including the boardroom, senior management and the workforce, on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions using an unbalanced panel of FTSE350 firms over the period 2010–2020. abstract: This essay examines the legal autonomy of Canon Law in relation to State Law, considering its configuration as the internal legal order of the Catholic Church. abstract: Anaemia is common in pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Data from western Libya are limited, and the role of vitamin D status is unclear. abstract: Precursory slow slip holds potential for reliable earthquake forewarning, yet the conditions conducive to it remain elusive. While quite a number of large earthquakes on smooth megathrust faults are preceded by precursory slow slip, laboratory experiments suggest such slip is inhibited on smooth faults. title: A New Species of Dendroseius (Mesostigmata, Digamasellidae) From Vineyard Soils in Southern France, With an Identification Key to the World Species
abstract: A new species of Dendroseius Karg (Digamasellidae) is described based on female specimens collected from vineyard soils in southern France. This finding represents one of the few records of the genus in Western Europe and expands the current knowledge about digamasellid diversity in the region. The new species is illustrated and diagnosed based on morphological characters of the adult female. In addition, an updated identification key to the world Dendroseius species, based on females, is provided.

abstract: Global warming and climate change have emerged as critical environmental challenges, threatened agricultural sustainability and increasing the pressure on already limited water resources. Therefore, practices that improve irrigation water use efficiency and alleviate water deficit stress, such as ascorbic acid (AsA) application, are essential for sustainable crop production. abstract: This extended abstract examines the principal tendencies in the development of Uzbek terminology during the period of national independence, with particular attention to the influence of globalisation, international communication, scientific and technological progress, economic reforms, and changes in the political and social organisation of Uzbekistan. abstract: The efficacy of effective microorganism products in aquaculture covers multiple aspects that act directly on fish, such as improving resistance to fungal, bacterial, and viral infections, reproduction, feed efficiency, and overall growth performance, or indirectly through improved water quality. abstract: This article examines Helen Keller's The World I Live In (1908) as a sustained challenge to compensatory models of sensory disability. Rather than treating touch, smell, and vibration as deficient substitutes for sight and hearing, Keller's writing constructs perception as a relational process in which bodily sensation, language, memory, imagination, environment, and encounters with others participate in the production of knowledge. abstract: This study examines the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on sustainable firm performance (SFP) through the mediating roles of green innovation and corporate image in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) manufacturing firms in Vietnam. abstract: Feed costs constitute a major component of total production costs in dairy farming enterprises. In this study, ration optimization was performed using linear programming (Simplex method) based on field data obtained from dairy farms in Niğde province. abstract: The international protection of environmental defenders remains fragmented, insufficient, and unevenly applied across regions. title: Wind of Change? Ukraine's Place in Jewish Studies Amidst Russian Invasion
abstract: This article examines how the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 reshaped the place of Ukraine within Jewish Studies. Using the lens of cultural decolonization, it interrogates how long-standing imperial frameworks have influenced the field and how they are being reconsidered. abstract: Reproductive losses undermine reproductive efficiency, threaten productivity and cause significant negative economic impacts on cattle industries in most of Africa. Though reproductive wastage of cows occurs in Cameroon, there is dearth of information on its extent and economic impact in the country. The study was done to determine the prevalence and associated economic losses due to the slaughter of cows and foetal wastages in the Bamenda municipal abattoir, Cameroon. title: Continuous and Episodic Metal Exposures Disrupt Aquatic Insect Drift, Emergence, and Larval Survival
abstract: Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with benthic macroinvertebrate communities to compare the effects of continuous and pulsed exposures to dissolved copper and zinc on larval drift, adult emergence, and benthic survival. Our goal was to evaluate how different exposure regimes alter in situ survival relative to the downstream movement of invertebrate prey resources and their dispersal to terrestrial consumers.

abstract: The development of wool follicles is considered a complex biological process that is regulated by the coordination of metabolic, molecular, and genetic processes during animal growth. abstract: Hypnos, personnification du sommeil, n’occupait pas une place ma-jeure dans la religion grecque, et les témoignages cultuels directs à son sujet restent extrêmement rares. abstract: Verdina Shlonsky (1905–90) was not only an original composer and an accomplished pianist but also a prolific writer. abstract: Background: Young adults increasingly rely on the internet for medical information. abstract: Armed conflicts generate profound environmental degradation and public health risks, yet direct environmental assessment is often severely constrained during the early stages of active hostilities. This study examines the potential environmental and public health implications arising during the early phase of the 2026 Iran conflict through an integrative review and an evidence-informed predictive framework.
