abstract: Este artículo analiza la construcción de una memoria cultural del pasado peruano y su articulación con una determinada representación de la peruanidad en Quipus. title: Bacterial Causes of Ovine Mastitis in Iraq: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Sheep constitute one of Iraq’s most numerous livestock populations, and their milk is marketed both raw and in processed dairy products. Mastitis is the principal mammary disease affecting ewes; however, published Iraqi evidence concerning its bacterial aetiology has not been systematically consolidated. This structured narrative review examines the microbial causes, epidemiology, pathogenicity, antimicrobial resistance, diagnostic approaches, and treatment of ovine mastitis in Iraq. title: Relationship Between Environmental Factors and Plant Distribution and Diversity in the North African Sahara Region: The Case of Tunisian Senghar‐Jabess National Park
abstract: The environmental factors influencing plant community composition in North African deserts are still not well described. This study evaluates the impact of environmental variables on vegetation structure in Senghar‐Jabess National Park (2804 km 2 ), a protected area situated in the hyper‐arid Sahara of southern Tunisia. abstract: Z jakich tradycji akademickich wywodzą się polscy ekonomiści? abstract: Despite decades of reform and the adoption of regulatory frameworks modeled on international best practices, Nigeria’s regulatory state continues to grapple with persistent inefficacies, operational misalignments and public skepticism. This article explores the phenomenon of “organ rejection syndrome” in the Nigerian regulatory context, in which externally introduced institutions and policies are resisted, distorted or rendered ineffective by local political, economic and social dynamics. abstract: This paper examines the development of Latin and the influence of spoken Dalmatian Romance in the early medieval epigraphic record. abstract: Objetivo: describir la evidencia sobre el láser de baja potencia como coadyuvante del movimiento dental ortodóntico, en el contexto de los métodos de aceleración, sus mecanismos y sus aplicaciones clínicas. abstract: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are non-enveloped double-stranded DNA viruses that cause a wide range of typically mild, self-limiting infections in humans, but are associated with high morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised individuals. abstract: This study examines the historical development of detached housing in Russia and the relationship between changing residential needs, spatial organisation and structural systems. abstract: How do you robustly evaluate a citizen science project, capturing long-term value, such as participant agency and community ownership, which frequently emerge only after formal funding ends, without excessively burdening participants? abstract: Driven by the construction of a unified national market and the rural revitalization strategy, the performance of rural property rights transfer and transaction markets has become a key issue in improving the allocation efficiency of rural factors. abstract: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 requires a strategic integration of cross-border infrastructure investment to bridge persistent energy gaps and uneven development along the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). abstract: Supplier concentration can facilitate coordination but increase dependence on critical upstream partners. abstract: La resiliencia académica constituye un recurso psicológico relevante para afrontar las adversidades asociadas con la formación universitaria. abstract: The importance of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors has been steadily increasing, and their integration into corporate operations is now widely recognized as one of the key drivers of long-term value creation and competitive advantage. abstract: Ethnographic fieldwork remains central to understanding the fragmented and uneven realities of an archipelagic Philippines. Drawing on a retrospective analysis of a 2023 undergraduate anthropology field school in a Philippine island municipality, this paper proposes precarious ethnography as a conceptual orientation and methodological condition for inquiry under political uncertainty. title: Agromorphological diversity and yield performance of sorghum [Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] accessions at West Belessa, Amhara National Regional State, Ethiopia
abstract: Sorghum [ Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench)] is a drought-tolerant cereal crop that plays a critical role in food security in Eth​iopia and other semi-arid tropics of Africa and Asia due to its adaptability to moisture stress and marginal soils. This study eval​uated agromorphological diversity and yield performance of 147 sorghum (Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench) accessions collected from different regions of Ethiopia under rainfed conditions at West Belessa, Amhara Region, Ethiopia. The experiment was conducted using an alpha lattice design, and both quantitative and qualitative traits were recorded.

Prabowo’s improbable 8 percent target growth by 2029 will require substantial improvements in productivity and much higher foreign investment. Prabowo’s centralised, state-led, universalist, and impatient approach to programs and institutional change lacks planning and prioritisation. title: Micropropagation of Tamarindus indica L. - An underutilised tree: A critical review on methods and challenges
abstract: Tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.) is a tropical, multipurpose fruit-bearing tree that remains underutilised despite its nutritional, industrial and economic benefits, as well as its agroforestry value. Micropropagation offers a viable alternative to conventional propagation methods to derive true-to-type plantlets of elite tree species on a large scale. title: Astral Deities and Disease in Dūnhuáng: Death, Malevolent Spirits, and Ritual Control
abstract: This paper explores the link between Dūnhuáng’s astral deities and disease, death, and malevolent spirits via Dūnhuáng manuscript P.2713, which contains the Incantation of the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions (廿八宿神咒), as well as the transmitted Procedures for Distinguishing the Movements of the Stars According to the Seven Planets (七曜星辰別行法). title: Ancestral Distance and the Cultural Foundations of State Capacity
abstract: This study investigates the role of long‐term population relatedness in shaping global variation in state capacity. It argues that longer periods of ancestral separation are associated with greater divergence in intergenerationally transmitted civic norms governing voluntary compliance with state institutions. Ancestral distance may also hinder the international diffusion of effective state institutions, contributing to persistent cross‐country differences in state capacity. journal: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics

title: ADAPTATION OF THE TNI AD'S CAVALRY EDUCATION AND TRAINING SYSTEM TO THE CHARACTER OF MODERN WARFARE
abstract: The changing character of modern warfare has expanded the competencies required of Indonesian Army Cavalry personnel, particularly in responding to UAS and counter-UAS threats, electronic warfare, networked command and control, and combined-arms and multidomain operations. This study aims to analyze the adaptation of the Indonesian Army Cavalry education and training system, identify remaining gaps, and formulate relevant directions for improvement. title: Perception Towards Bees in Rural Schools in the Sierra de Huautla, Morelos, Mexico
abstract: This article examines the perceptions and attitudes of students from nine rural schools in a Protected Natural Area, analyzing variations in attitudes toward conservation and bees by age, gender, grade level, and social context. A questionnaire combining semantic differentials, four open-ended questions, and a sociodemographic survey was administered to 257 elementary, middle, and high school students. title: Trazabilidad cognitiva e ignorancia deliberada: reconstrucción epistémica del no-saber
abstract: La ignorancia deliberada constituye un fenómeno normativo definido por la evitación consciente del conocimiento debido. Este trabajo no discute esa caracterización general, sino que aborda una cuestión distinta: cómo reconstruir ex post el trayecto epistémico que conduce al vacío cognitivo generado y gestionado por el propio sujeto. Para ello se propone la trazabilidad cognitiva como regla metodológica destinada a interpretar la postura epistémica del autor sin recurrir a ficciones sobre su conocimiento. title: Edible Oils and Cardiovascular Health: An Evidence-Based Review
abstract: Edible oils are the primary dietary sources of fat, providing concentrated energy and essential fatty acids. They encompass a wide range of plant-derived oils, including olive, sunflower, soybean, canola, coconut, palm, and mustard oils, which differ in fatty acid composition and physicochemical properties such as smoke point. Their cardiovascular effects are largely determined by their fatty acid profiles. abstract: O presente artigo objetiva examinar instrumentos que possam contribuir para a prevenção do estado de crise econômico-financeira empresarial e, por conseguinte, da própria decretação do estado falencial. Considerando o importante papel desempenhado pelas empresas e empresários no tecido social, bem como os vários riscos a que estão submetidos no exercício de suas atividades, busca-se refletir acerca de medidas que possam auxiliar a gerenciar estes riscos e, assim, evitar o estado de insolvabilidade. title: Illiberal gateways and hubs: Chinese push and European pull in Hungary and Serbia
abstract: In this article, we examine how Chinese economic engagement positioned Hungary and Serbia within US–China network competition from 2013 to 2025. Drawing on the network-centrality thesis, we apply a push–pull framework across infrastructure, digital technology, production and finance. On the push side, Chinese firms sought markets, production sites and natural resources, channelled domestic overcapacity outward and internationalised the renminbi. title: Escribir, resistir, politizar: La (re)creación del archivo como dispositivo feminista en ¿Por qué volvías cada verano? y Donde no hago pie de Belén López Peiró y El invencible verano de Liliana de Cristina Rivera Garza
abstract: Las obras ¿Por qué volvías cada verano? y Donde no hago pie de Belén López Peiró, junto con El invencible verano de Liliana de Cristina Rivera Garza, construyen un archivo de la memoria y la conciencia feminista que cuestiona al archivo institucional — garante del discurso histórico-político — frente a las violencias patriarcales. Desde una epistemología y crítica feminista, y en el contexto del “giro del archivo” y el “giro documental” que enmarcan parte de la actual literatura latinoamericana, este artículo propone mostrar cómo estas obras crean un contra-archivo que no solo registra las vio

title: Exploring the impact of multidimensional complexity interplay on the success of mega infrastructure projects
abstract: Complexity is an inherent characteristic of mega infrastructure projects (MIPs), playing a crucial role in determining their success. While existing research has explored the effects of individual complexity factors, the interplay of multidimensional complexities and their collective impact on MIP success remains underexamined. This study systematically identifies complexity factors from both internal and external dimensions, leveraging the TOE framework and grounded theory, and empirically investigates their dynamic interactions. title: Cinema From the Ottoman Empire to the Republic: A Comprehensive Reading of Hüseyin Rahmi Gürpınar's Novels
abstract: The primary aim of this article is to examine and evaluate the value of a prominent Turkish author's works as a source for the history of Ottoman‐Turkish cinema. Hüseyin Rahmi Gürpınar, who wrote popular novels, continuously from the 1890s, when cinema first entered the Ottoman‐Turkish region, through the 1930s, produced texts that incorporate everyday life and the common person into his narrative, with a strong emphasis on contemporary relevance; these texts possess the capacity for testimony and representation within the context of cinema history. title: The gender pay gap during conflict: evidence from farm workers in Myanmar
abstract: Rising global conflict increasingly destabilizes food systems and labor markets that underpin livelihoods and food security. Conflict-driven shocks—such as male outmigration or shifts toward manual, gendered tasks—can fundamentally reshape the structural inequalities that determine how men and women are compensated. However, quantitative research on gendered agricultural labor markets remains rare, particularly in conflict settings. title: Consenso mexicano de cáncer mamario. Manejo del cáncer de mama en poblaciones especiales
abstract: El cáncer mamario en poblaciones especiales (mujeres jóvenes, de edad avanzada, en embarazo o lactancia, hombres) requiere de consideraciones especiales de manejo sistémico, quirúrgico y radioterapia.La décima actualización del Consenso Mexicano Sobre Diagnóstico y Tratamiento del Cáncer Mamario (Colima, enero de 2023) es publicada por sus autores en diferentes artículos.El presente artículo incluye la actualización relativa al manejo de cáncer de mama en poblaciones especiales.La difusión de este consenso contribuye a la actualización y homogeneidad de criterios de manejo del cáncer.

abstract: Although concentrations exceeding theoretical requirements may enhance microbial activity, the effects of such concentrations on cattle grazing tropical pastures remain unclear. This study assessed the influence of excess rumen-degradable protein (RDP) on feed intake, digestibility, and weight gain in heifers grazing tropical pastures. title: Prevención de riesgos laborales y discapacidad: del marco jurídico a la gestión del SGSST
abstract: La prevención de riesgos laborales (en adelante, PRL) es un aspecto esencial al que no se le suele dar la suficiente importancia en la inclusión laboral de las personas con discapacidad. El presente artículo analiza el marco jurídico español que vincula la discapacidad y la gestión de la PRL y examina cómo trasladar las obligaciones derivadas a la práctica de un sistema de gestión de la seguridad y salud en el trabajo (en adelante, SGSST). abstract: Cobalt enrichment in iron oxide–copper–gold (IOCG) systems is widely recognised, yet the processes controlling its mineralogical distribution remain poorly constrained. This study integrates mineral chemistry, textures, and in-situ trace element data from IOCG, iron sulphide–copper–gold (ISCG), and ISCG-skarn deposits in the Cloncurry District, Australia, to investigate cobalt behaviour during magmatic–hydrothermal evolution. abstract: This article critically reviews the literature on JAK/STAT pathway biology, its roles in myeloproliferative, inflammatory, and neoplastic diseases, and advances in targeted pharmacological inhibition. The evidence reviewed indicates that cytokine-mediated JAK/STAT activation regulates essential cellular functions. Several inhibitors, including ruxolitinib, tofacitinib, and baricitinib, have demonstrated clinical efficacy in specific approved indications, such as myelofibrosis and rheumatoid arthritis. title: Declining soil organic matter as a dominant control on agricultural nitrogen loss
abstract: Nitrogen (N) losses from agricultural soils that pollute water and air and threaten biodiversity are often assumed to result from excessive fertilizer and manure applications. Yet, soil organic matter is the largest pool of N in agricultural systems and its contribution to environmental N loss remains poorly quantified. title: Confiance, risque et paiement dans l’intention d’achat de billets en ligne : le modèle conceptuel CRP-Ticket et son programme de validation au Maroc
abstract: Studies of online purchasing of transport and event tickets rely mainly on the technology acceptance model (TAM) and UTAUT2. In the corpus examined, they treat trust as a single-target belief, do not measure the fear that a ticket will not grant access to the service, and overlook the availability of payment means. title: Transición y Bono Demográfico en Venezuela: Desafíos ante la Emigración Internacional Masiva
abstract: En el presente artículo se analiza la evolución de la transición demográfica y la dinámica del bono demográfico en Venezuela, considerando los posibles efectos de la emigración interna­cional. Se realiza un análisis descriptivo e interpretativo basado en las proyecciones de pobla­ción del Centro Latinoamericano y Caribeño de Demografía (CELADE, revisión 2024, variante media) y en los datos sobre migración mundial de la División de Población del Departamento de Asuntos Económicos y Sociales de las Naciones Unidas (UNDESA por sus siglas en inglés). title: Human-made structures as nesting sites for hummingbirds across the Americas: insights from citizen science
abstract: Urbanization can negatively affect nesting and reproductive behaviors of birds. Even so, certain species can survive in abundance despite its negative impacts, due to their ability to use alternative human-made structures as nesting sites. There are several studies focusing on hummingbirds’ floral resource use in urban environments, however, little is known about their reproduction and nesting in these areas. title: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines on the investigation of suspected liver disease in adults
abstract: Chronic liver disease is increasingly prevalent yet often undiagnosed. The British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) published guidance on the investigation of abnormal liver blood tests in 2000, and this was comprehensively updated in 2018. Since then, significant developments including the adoption of new nomenclature for steatotic liver disease (SLD), advances in non-invasive fibrosis assessment and expanding strategies for early detection in primary care have necessitated further revision. title: Hebrew Writing on National Music 1880–1930: An Anthology in Translation
abstract: This project presents an anthology in English translation of Hebrew-language writings on music by four authors—Zvi Nissan Golomb, Abraham Ber Birnbaum, Abraham Zvi Idelsohn, and Aharon Leib Bisko—published between the 1880s and the 1920s. Emerging during the revival of Hebrew as a modern language, these writings offer a distinctive perspective on the relationship between music, language, and Jewish national identity. title: Bridge: Database-Grounded Interactive Disambiguation for Text-to-SQL
abstract: Ambiguity remains a persistent challenge in text-to-SQL, where an underspecified natural-language question may admit multiple plausible SQL interpretations. Recent work attempts to recover the user's intended interpretation through iterative clarification, but typically relies heavily on LLM parametric knowledge for ad hoc reasoning, leading to limited ambiguity-resolution effectiveness and high LLM cost. title: Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
abstract: We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

title: Persistent Metric-Semantic Maritime Scene Memory from Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs
abstract: Three-dimensional scene graphs (3DSGs) can provide robots with persistent metric-semantic representations for spatial reasoning, but the existing methods have primarily been developed for indoor and terrestrial environments. In this paper we investigate how a representative outdoor open-vocabulary method transfers to maritime environments and which adaptations are needed. title: Helicity conservation for compressible barotropic Euler flows: regularity criteria and a momentum-based approach
abstract: In this paper, we study helicity conservation for weak solutions to the compressible barotropic Euler equations. Using generalized Constantin-E-Titi-type commutator estimates that fully exploit the kinetic energy, we derive new sufficient conditions for helicity conservation across a broader range of regularity exponents. These conditions reveal the interplay between temporal, spatial integrability and differentiability of the velocity and density, as well as the influence of velocity-density coupling on helicity conservation. title: Knitting the Ising Transition: Statistical Physics as a Tool for Stochastic Knit Design
abstract: Textile designs are typically based on biperiodic, deterministic patterns. However, hand and machine manufacturing are not restricted to periodic patterns. Instead, the entanglement topology can be chosen for each base unit cell of the textile. Non-deterministic processes, such as stochastic realisations of physical systems, can then serve as design tools for creating original patterns. In this Proceedings, we present a proof of concept for stochastic design by generating knitted fabrics from Ising model spin patterns. title: Mechanical acclimation of bacterial growth and division across generations
abstract: Bacteria frequently encounter mechanical confinement in natural and engineered environments, yet how an abrupt change in mechanical conditions reorganizes growth and division across generations remains poorly understood. Using single-cell time-lapse microscopy, we tracked Escherichia coli across generations following transfer from liquid culture to glass-attached or glass-gel-confined conditions. title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots
abstract: Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power. Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware. title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
abstract: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. title: Self-similarity of axisymmetric Marangoni flows on a deep viscous subphase
abstract: Local gradients of surface tension caused by inhomogeneous distributions of surfactant molecules are known to generate Marangoni flows, the mechanics of which have important consequences in various areas of science and engineering. In this paper, we investigate the deposition of insoluble surfactants on the surface of a deep, viscous subphase, which propagate axisymmetrically without diffusing. title: A Game of Throngs: How Spotlight Tourism Reshapes Local Economies
abstract: In July 2017, San Juan de Gaztelugatxe, a modest chapel in the Basque Country, appeared as "Dragonstone" in Game of Thrones, transforming a locally known site with limited tourism activity into a global tourist destination overnight. We exploit this exogenous spotlight shock to estimate its causal effects on the local economy using a novel administrative dataset and a Synthetic Control approach. We find an abrupt increase in tourism activity, far exceeding the effects documented in the literature. title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
abstract: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. abstract: We study a stylized single-vehicle replenishment-routing problem in which the cities of a national logistics network are both demand points and supply points: a vehicle of limited capacity delivers to every city once, and when its load is insufficient for the next city it must detour to a city already served that can still supply goods. abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. title: A conditional quadrature method of moments for populations of oblate spheroidal particles
abstract: Non-spherical particle populations are encountered in numerous industrial processes, where particle size, shape, and velocity jointly influence transport, breakage, and classification dynamics. The resulting coupled distributions of geometric and kinematic particle properties evolve within a high-dimensional phase space whose accurate representation remains a significant challenge. abstract: Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. abstract: A generalized Renard-Deck (RD) drag decomposition is developed for spatially developing compressible turbulent boundary layers over rough surfaces. Derived from the locally resolved, time-averaged momentum equations, the formulation accounts for both viscous friction and pressure drag without requiring spatial averaging at the roughness-element scale. title: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
abstract: Terrestrial free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) provides a flexible complement to fiber-based networks, but its deployment over long horizontal paths in dense metropolitan environments remains challenging, as atmospheric turbulence, demanding pointing and tracking requirements, and operational constraints can substantially increase system complexity. We experimentally demonstrate the operation of a decoy-state BB84 system over an 18.9~km free-space link across a densely populated urban area in the metropolitan region of Barcelona using an aviation-compliant optical architecture. title: ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
abstract: We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. title: The Shape of the Strongly Coupled MQM Ground State
abstract: We study a surprisingly efficient family of variational ansatze for the ground state of bosonic matrix quantum mechanics at large $N$. These are ansatze whose norm-squared probability distributions are themselves matrix integrals with single-trace actions, and so have their own independent `t Hooft expansions. They are efficient in the sense that optimizing over a small number of parameters produces many digits of accuracy for the energy, single-trace moments, and connected correlators. title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. title: Verification of coastal enhanced weathering by tracking the dissolution of alkaline minerals: theory and laboratory tests with olivine
abstract: Coastal Enhanced Weathering (CEW) is a marine Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) method that adds ground alkaline minerals to shallow regions of the ocean in order to increase seawater alkalinity, i.e. its capacity for storing atmospheric CO 2 as bicarbonate. While CEW is promising with regard to cost and scalability, it is an uncontained, “open-system” style of CDR, and presents significant challenges to effective measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) of the process. title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
abstract: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. title: Educational Design for Scaffolded, Interactive Simulation-Based Learning: SeaVarinv, an Open-Source GUI for Paleo-Sea-Level Reconstruction in Geoscience Education
abstract: Sequence stratigraphy asks students to reason in both directions along the model chain: forward, from sea level to strata, and backward, from strata to sea level. The backward direction is an inverse problem—ill-posed, non-unique, and dependent on regularization choices that textbooks describe but rarely let students feel. title: Performance of restored microfragments of Orbicella annularis and Orbicella faveolata during the 2023–2024 marine heatwave in the Mexican Caribbean
abstract: Introduction: Coral reef ecosystems are declining worldwide due to the combined effects of climate-driven marine heatwaves and local anthropogenic stressors, leading to widespread loss of reef-building corals and degradation of carbonate frameworks. In the Caribbean, these impacts are intensified by recurrent thermal anomalies, disease outbreaks, and declining water quality, with massive corals such as Orbicella spp. among the most affected. title: Communication Strategies of the Malabero Coastal Fishermen’s Group in Responding to the Decline in Fish Catch
abstract: This study aims to identify and explain the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group in Bengkulu City in dealing with the decline in fish catches. This study employed a qualitative method with a case study approach. The research informants were selected using purposive sampling and consisted of the group leader, senior members, and active fishermen. title: Evaluación y seguimiento del blanqueamiento coralino 2023 en el Parque Nacional Sistema Arrecifal Veracruzano, suroeste del golfo de México
abstract: Introduction: In 2023, the fourth mass bleaching event caused by a heatwave was recorded. This event affected virtually all of Mexico’s coral reefs. The bleaching began in August in the Veracruz Reef System National Park (PNSAV). For the first time, a bleaching event of this magnitude was recorded and monitored in the southwestern Gulf of Mexico. Objective: To estimate the extent and prevalence of bleaching in the corals of the PNSAV, as well as to monitor its progression. Methods: Two-minute videos were recorded at a constant depth and speed, with the camera positioned 1 m above the seafloor.

abstract: Developing advanced amphibious adhesives that perform well in both dry and underwater environments is critical yet challenging for unlocking diverse underwater applications. title: Reproducible event‐bed correlation with uncertainty: pyCoreRelator
abstract: Stratigraphic correlation is fundamental to Earth science, yet conventional approaches rely heavily on subjective visual data matching. Automated algorithms such as dynamic time warping (DTW) provide reproducibility, but when sequences are subdivided into clearly defined stratigraphic units, DTW alone struggles to explore a vast range of correlation possibilities among these units and evaluate the optimal alignment. title: Co‐Creating the Predefined: Participation and Epistemic Tensions in EU Coastal Research
abstract: EU research and innovation frameworks increasingly promote co-creation while simultaneously requiring projects to deliver predefined policy objectives and solutions. This article examines the tensions arising between these ambitions, using nature-based solutions as an empirical lens. Drawing on six transition coastal labs in the Horizon Europe project EmpowerUs and Aristotle’s distinction between episteme, techne, and phronesis, we examine how universal scientific knowledge, institutional requirements, and contextual forms of knowledge/experiences interact in co-creation processes. abstract: The yield of major crops is declining steadily due to increasing salinity intrusion in the coastal regions of Bangladesh. Mushroom production offers a viable alternative for improving the socio-economic conditions of coastal communities, as it is unaffected by field salinity and can be cultivated within household environments. abstract: Herbivory is one of the most important ecological interactions globally. Herbivores, among which arthropods predominate, play key roles in fundamental ecological processes, and may profoundly affect plants. Invasive alien plants (IAP) may influence herbivory in varied ways, including by supplying additional resources, yet, few comparative studies have assessed how IAP impact herbivory, particularly on heavily invaded oceanic islands. abstract: The article identifies stages in China’s space tracking ship program and changes in the functions of these specialized platforms within national space and missile infrastructure. It draws on Russian scholarship, official Chinese materials and open sources on recent launches. Historical-genetic, institutional and functional methods are used. abstract: Transport exposes fish to considerable stress, threatening their health, well-being, and overall farming productivity. Assessing fish welfare requires a deep understanding of physiological and molecular stress responses. While plasma cortisol is the standard biomarker, blood collection itself induces stress. institutions: Instituto de Ciencias Marinas de Andalucía

abstract: The research paper reports on the use of social media by foreign tourists coming to Terengganu, Malaysia, as a case study. The researchers were trying to know the factors that trigger the intention of tourists to use social media for the purpose of travel planning and decision-making. The quick growth of digital technology has completely changed the tourism business, and one of the major reasons for this change is that eventually, tourists have started to count on social media more for destination info, sharing experiences and trip planning. title: Ultraviolet instruments on the Habitable Worlds Observatory: considerations and capability trades on the multi-object, integral-field, and high-resolution modes of a potential ultraviolet instrument
abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is NASA’s next-generation astrophysics platform, delivering transformative capability in the search for life and study of the origins of the universe. Among the instruments under consideration for HWO is a multipurpose ultraviolet spectrograph and imager that provides a deep toolbox for some of the most pressing science investigations of the next several decades. title: Likelihood estimation of an interpretable early-warning sign of critical transitions
abstract: A critical transition is a sudden, abrupt and potentially unforeseen change in the state of a complex system often associated with catastrophic collapses and irreversability. Here we introduce a novel, interpretable early-warning signal of bifurcation-induced critical transitions. The proposed indicator can be readily computed from timeseries observations by maximum likelihood estimation and it has the advantage of providing immediate insight on the state of the system. We showcase its applicability by assessing its performance using models of ecosystems and ocean circulation collapse.

abstract: Breaking waves play a major role in wave-energy dissipation and air–sea exchange, but their short duration and complex dynamics make direct measurements difficult. Passive acoustic measurements appear to provide a valuable source of information about wave-breaking processes. While detection of breaking waves can be achieved using one of the existing methods, estimation of breakers energy dissipation is a more complex task. title: Shrinking reefs, shrinking minds? Reef complexity and social rank shape damselfish cognition
abstract: Environmental complexity is positively correlated with enhanced cognitive abilities across a range of vertebrate taxa, driven by cognitive plasticity within an individual's lifetime. Coral reefs are among the most environmentally complex ecosystems, yet they are degrading rapidly due to global and local anthropogenic stressors. This progressive loss of complexity may reduce the cognitive abilities of reef-dependent fish, potentially affecting their capacity to respond behaviorally to environmental change. title: Large deformations of Oldroyd-B drops in a steady electric field
abstract: Viscoelastic drop deformation under electric fields plays a key role in applications such as microfluidics, inkjet printing, and electrohydrodynamic manipulation of complex fluids. title: Icons as a Tool to Connect Water Practices, Functions and Values across Space and Time: A Second Attempt
abstract: Humans have shaped water systems for millennia, creating complex networks of physical structures, institutions and cultural practices. These systems reflect locally embedded yet globally influenced values that evolve over time. From infrastructure and landscapes to rituals and laws, human engagement with water is both tangible and intangible, deeply influenced by societal preferences, climate conditions and historical choices. abstract: Background Nutrient resorption is an important nutrient conservation strategy in mangroves. Nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE), defined as the proportion of nutrients withdrawn from senescing leaves before abscission, reflects plants’ ability to recycle internal nutrients under nutrient-limited saline conditions. abstract: Maternally derived antibodies transferred across the placenta are hypothesized to protect infants against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in early life, but placental malaria may impair this transfer and alter the subsequent development of infant immunity. To test whether maternally derived and infant antibody responses are associated with protection from infection and clinical malaria, and how malaria exposure during pregnancy and infancy shapes these responses, we enrolled a birth cohort of infants in a birth cohort nested within a randomized trial of chemoprevention in Tororo, Uganda. title: Estimation of wet radome and rain induced attenuation in cloud radar observations
abstract: Estimation of the properties of ice clouds above rain from ground-based cloud radar observations is affected by the wet radome, rain path, and melting layer attenuation. In this study, we present a method for estimating wet radome and rain attenuation using collocated disdrometer observations. abstract: In late 2024, an avian H5N1 influenza virus derived from clade 2.3.4.4b was isolated from a severe human infection in British Columbia (A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024), revealing a rare combination of substitutions E190D and Q226H as minor variants in the receptor-binding site (RBS). title: Flicker Fusion Camouflage: A Mechanistic Framework for Motion‐Induced Concealment
abstract: Flicker fusion camouflage (FFC) challenges the view that movement necessarily compromises camouflage by proposing that rapid movement can render contrasting patterns perceptually blurred. FFC emerges from interactions among pattern geometry, locomotion, observer visual processing, and environmental context. This framework provides testable predictions for determining when motion can enhance rather than compromise animal concealment.

abstract: CD45-positive erythroid cells represent a distinct erythroid population described in mice and humans, but their molecular characteristics in the adult spleen remain incompletely defined. abstract: This study assessed the awareness of rice farmers in Nueva Ecija regarding Super El Niño and their preparedness practices using a descriptive-correlational research design involving 75 respondents. Results showed that farmers were moderately aware of its nature and characteristics but highly aware of its agricultural effects and recommended preparedness measures. title: Development of Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) Models in Python to Optimize Last-Mile Distribution Routes in an SME
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that produce perishable food often plan last-mile distribution reactively, which raises fuel consumption, extends working days and forces vehicles to return to the plant for additional product. This study develops and evaluates vehicle routing problem (VRP) models implemented in Python for a family-owned cheese SME located in Apaxco de Ocampo, State of Mexico, which serves about 35 commercial destinations per day with more than 900 kg of product using two light trucks of 600 and 800 kg. abstract: This article critiques the persistent marginalisation of investigative journalism as an alternative Knowledge relative to scientific research, particularly in the context of rigorous evidence synthesis. title: Development of an Oral Subunit Vaccine to Protect Rainbow Trout Against Infectious Hematopoietic Necrosis Virus (IHNV)
abstract: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) is a highly virulent pathogen of salmonids that causes severe mortality in aquaculture, particularly during early developmental stages. Current vaccination strategies rely mainly on injectable DNA vaccines, which are labour-intensive and unsuitable for large-scale immunization of juvenile fish. In this study, we developed and evaluated two recombinant nanostructured subunit vaccines based on the IHNV glycoprotein: IHNV NP and IHNV-IFN NP , the latter incorporating interferon-gamma (IFNγ) as an immunomodulatory adjuvant. abstract: The Garnet Valley deposit in the Damara Orogenic Belt of Namibia hosts both alaskite-hosted and skarn-hosted uranium mineralization, forming a distinctive uranium metallogenic system. abstract: Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. abstract: Elang Ular Bido (Spilornis cheela) merupakan salah satu raptor dilindungi yang memiliki peran penting dalam ekosistem, tetapi informasi mengenai distribusi, lokasi perkembangbiakan, dan kesesuaian habitatnya di Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta (DIY) masih terbatas. title: Effect of mycorrhizal fungi inoculation, phosphate fertilisation and gypsum percentage on the uptake of nutrients in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L.)
abstract: This study examined the individual and interactive effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) inoculation, phosphorus (P) fertilisation and gypsum levels on nutrient uptake and growth of Sorghum bicolor L. in gypsiferous soils under pot conditions. A factorial experiment was conducted with two gypsum levels (5 % and 25 %), four P rates (0, 80, 160 and 240 kg P ha-1) and two AMF treatments (with and without inoculation). title: Design of Sustainable Formulations for Nanodosing: Insight into Fatty Acid Profile Modulation in Tenebrio molitor Larvae
abstract: In the context of sustainable insect production,Tenebrio molitor larvae (TML) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional livestock systems. Their rich nutritional profile is characterized by high protein content and favorable lipid composition. Herein, we developed nanovectors based on exopolysaccharides derived from Neocyanospira capsulata(Es) or olive pomace (O), combined with egg yolk phospholipids (E) to deliver oils obtained from the seeds ofPerilla frutescens L. title: Fusing the Civil-Military Sphere: Total Defence and Maritime Security Governance
abstract: European governments increasingly turn to total defence and whole-of-society approaches in response to hybrid threats. Despite their policy prominence, the practical operation of such approaches remains insufficiently examined, particularly within the complex maritime infrastructural domain. This article investigates the functioning of maritime total defence through an empirical study of the Norwegian total defence model in the maritime domain in the aftermath of the 2022 Nord Stream sabotage. abstract: Angkutan Sungai, Danau dan Penyeberangan (ASDP) berperan penting untuk menjangkau daerah yang belum terlayani prasarana jalan, termasuk penyeberangan Sungai Barito antara Banjar Raya (Banjarmasin) dan Tamban (Kabupaten Barito Kuala). title: Genetic diversity and nutritional profiling of Moringa oleifera Lam. half-sib progenies
abstract: Moringa oleifera Lam. ("Miracle tree") is a multi-purpose tropical bioresource valued for combating malnutrition. However, systematic evaluations monitoring proximate principles and mineral concentrations across wild genotypes during early nursery establishment remain limited. This study evaluated the nutritional profiles, proximate principles and biomass determinants of 35 half-sib genotypes collected from wild populations across five sub-Himalayan Indian states after one year of nursery growth. title: Development and Validation of a LEGO®-Based Texture Analyser for Tensile Testing Using Gelatine-Based Films with Different Glycerol Concentrations
abstract: Texture analysis is important for evaluating the mechanical properties of biobased plastics, providing valuable insights into their performance, durability, and suitability for various applications. However, conventional texture analysis is often expensive and complex, limiting its accessibility in academic research. Hence, this study employed a cost-effective alternative using a LEGO®-based texture analyser developed with Visual Studio Code, Arduino IDE, and MINDSTORMS EV3, adhering to ASTM D6882-12 (2012) to evaluate the mechanical properties of bio-based films, such as gelatine-based films.

title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
abstract: Radical glycosylation offers versatile strategies for carbohydrate synthesis, yet the development of accessible glycosyl radical precursors compatible with stereoselective coupling remains challenging. Here we report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis. title: Construction of a signal peptide library in Escherichia coli and its application in guiding protein secretion expression
abstract: Expression of extracellular proteins in Escherichia coli is crucial for boosting recombinant protein production, but single signal peptide use is restricted by its targeting and efficiency limitations. This study integrated endogenous E. coli signal peptides, exogenous microbial signal peptides, and atypical signal peptides to build a library of 30 signal peptides for protein secretion in E. coli . title: Generalized approach to relaxation time of magnetic nanoparticles with interactions: From superparamagnetic to glasslike freezing
abstract: A generalized expression for the relaxation time of dipolar-interacting magnetic nanoparticles is derived by extending the Kramers-Brown escape-rate theory within the Tsallis statistical framework. A coarse-grained microscopic motivation is developed for the fluctuation-dominated superdiffusive regime, whereas the subdiffusive regime is treated as an effective phenomenological description of configurationally confined relaxation in strongly interacting assemblies. title: UPLC–QTOF/MS-based metabolomic profiling of Lespedeza species for marker selection and monoamine oxidase inhibitory activity
abstract: Monoamine oxidases (MAO)-A and MAO-B are key enzymes involved in the regulation of monoamine neurotransmitters and are closely associated with various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, the MAO-A and MAO-B inhibitory activities of methanol extracts from Korean native Lespedeza species were compared and related to metabolite profiles using ultra-performance liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC–QTOF/MS)-based metabolomics combined with in silico prediction of central nervous system distribution. title: Evaluating maternal pod variability and early growth dynamics in Moringa oleifera progenies
abstract: Moringa oleifera is an important crop globally, but there is limited characterisation of maternal pod traits and progeny seedling performance. In this study, growth patterns of 10 accessions (MO-11 to MO-20) and their half-sib progeny (P-11 to P-20) were evaluated to select the best germplasm. Maternally, MO-11 exhibited largest pod dimensions and weight, and MO-16 had the highest 100-seed weight (19.14 g). title: Cation‐Directed Supramolecular Design of Luminescent Hybrid Liquid Crystals Based on A 2 Mo 6 Cl 14 Ternary Salt (A = Li + , Na + , K + , Cs + , NH 4 + )
abstract: Red NIR emissive hybrid liquid crystals (LC) are obtained by combining A 2 Mo 6 Cl 14 ternary cluster salts and a mesomorphic dimer containing a hexaethylene oxide complexing center. The complexation induces a large broadening of the LC range around 0°C ± 20°C. Photophysical studies demonstrate the influence of the cation/cluster anion interactions on the emission properties of the salts and of the hybrid compounds, which show quantum yields in the LC state close to 30% and excellent photostability, with a loss of less than 10% of intensity after 3 h of continuous irradiation. title: A new subspecies of Teucrium montanum (Lamiaceae) from northern Albania
abstract: Morphological and anatomical variation within Teucrium montanum was examined in 322 individuals from 33 populations, representing the two currently accepted subspecies, subsp. montanum and subsp. helianthemoides, as well as three populations of a morphologically distinctive group from northern Albania. A total of twenty-two morphological and twenty-three anatomical quantitative characters were analysed using univariate and multivariate methods, and a further analysis was conducted of the qualitative traits of habitus, indumentum and corolla colour. title: Kerangka ketangguhan iklim PLTMH dan ketahanan energi di hulu DAS Kabupaten Bogor
abstract: Pembangkit listrik tenaga mikrohidro (PLTMH) tipe aliran sungai bergantung langsung pada debit, sedangkan penapisan awal tapak umumnya memakai debit rata-rata yang tidak memperlihatkan perilaku pada tahun El Niño. Artikel konsep metodologis ini merumuskan kerangka lima langkah untuk menapis ketangguhan iklim PLTMH dengan neraca air bulanan F.J. title: Painted architectures, embedded salts: A scientific look at the murals of Navalcarnero (Spain)
abstract: A comprehensive multi-analytical approach was applied to evaluate the materials and conservation state of three mural paintings located in Navalcarnero (Madrid, Spain), attributed to the artist Alberto Pirrongelli. In-situ analyses using portable Raman, XRF, and FTIR spectroscopy were combined with laboratory techniques, including μ-EDXRF mapping and Raman imaging on cross-sections, and ion chromatography. title: Cripto-tribunales y arbitraje: problemas de calificación legal en la resolución de disputas descentralizada
abstract: En los últimos años, la expansión de mecanismos de resolución de disputas basados en blockchain y contratos inteligentes ha impulsado la noción de un supuesto “arbitraje descentralizado” o de los llamados “cripto-tribunales”. title: “I wouldn't use it here, that's what they call it”: Dialect acquisition and attitudes in two Irish-born Chicagoans
abstract: This study examines the lexical familiarity and dialect attitudes of two Irish-born immigrants who have lived most of their lives in Chicago, Illinois. Drawing on research in second dialect acquisition, dialect familiarity, and perceptual dialectology, this case study explores how long-term exposure to American English has shaped participants’ lexicons and perceptions of regional variation. title: Development of a grassland condition index for assessing hydrocarbon pipeline disturbance in the magellanic steppe
abstract: Assessing the ecological condition of grasslands requires indicators that integrate floristic and structural attributes sensitive to anthropogenic disturbances. The objective of this study was to develop and evaluate a Grassland Condition Index (GCI) to characterize differences between an area disturbed by a buried hydrocarbon pipeline and an adjacent reference area in a Festuca gracillima-dominated grassland of the Magellanic Steppe. title: On the rediscovery and resurrection of Pachyiulus pluto Verhoeff 1910 (Diplopoda, Julidae) in Sicily, Italy
abstract: The Sicilian diplopod fauna is a mosaic of endemic species and taxa that have followed multiple colonization routes. In Sicily, the species of the genus Pachyiulus have faced several taxonomic changes and are known by three taxa: P. flavipes, P. oenologus, and P. (oenologus) humicolus. A fourth taxon, P. cattarensis pluto, has a complex and taxonomically unresolved history. title: Target speech norms and short‐term study abroad: The development of sociolinguistic competence in L2 French
abstract: This study examines the role of short‐term study abroad (SA) in the development of second language (L2) sociolinguistic competence, or knowledge about the L2 that incorporates culturally and socially appropriate language use. Speech data from 12 French learners participating in a 4‐week SA program in Lyon, France, were analyzed for the acquisition of a high‐frequency sociolinguistic variable in informal French: the use of the third‐person singular pronoun on “one” in place of the first‐person plural pronoun nous “we” (i.e., variable on vs. nous ). title: Kinetically controlled boron carbide composite sub-micrometer particle formation pathways during continuous-flow laser melting in liquids with high-power lasers
abstract: Monodisperse, spherical sub-micrometer particles with clean, smooth surfaces are key materials used as composite reinforcements, abrasives, and tribological additives, but remain synthetically challenging to produce. Pulsed laser melting in liquids (LML) is an environmentally friendly, emerging route for producing such particles. However, demonstrations have so far been limited to batch reactors, which are difficult to scale up to industrial production. title: Efficacy, tolerability, and adverse events of tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis: A real-world study at Khyber Teaching Hospital, Peshawar, Pakistan
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the effectiveness, tolerability, and safety profile of tofacitinib in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Methodology: A retrospective observational cohort study using routine clinical records from May 2, 2023 to December 31, 2025. Adults meeting the 2010 American College of Rheumatology and European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria were included. Effectiveness was assessed by change in DAS28 disease activity category and by remission or low disease activity at follow-up. Paired category changes used Wilcoxon signed-rank and marginal homogeneity tests.

title: Non-Thermal Plasma-Assisted CH4–CO2 Co-Conversion: A Reservoir of Surface Species is the Key to Selective Liquid Product Formation
abstract: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) catalysis enables the direct co-conversion of CH4 and CO2 into thermodynamically limited liquid products under mild conditions. However, achieving high selectivity toward liquid products and clarifying the role of the catalyst in steering product distribution remain significant challenges. Here we uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism governing selectivity in plasma catalysis: the formation of a reservoir of strongly adsorbed surface species that evolves during reaction and dynamically controls liquid-product formation. title: How care divides and connects: On forest conflicts and transformations in a German upland region
abstract: Forest conflicts require analysis in relation to diverse human–forest relationships specific to local contexts. We examine local forest conflicts from a critical care perspective, conceptualising care as deeply ambivalent and entangled with power. The analysis draws on empirical material from a case study in a German upland region, focusing on different practices of actively shaping and engaging with the forest. institutions: Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre

title: Factors associated with Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses in Europe (2022–2025)
abstract: BACKGROUND: Equine granulocytic anaplasmosis (EGA) is caused by Anaplasma phagocytophilum and mainly transmitted by Ixodes persulcatus complex ticks, particularly I. ricinus in Europe. The study aimed to investigate factors associated with PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses. METHODS: Equine samples from across Europe submitted to a laboratory between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. title: The Electromagnetically Isolated Global Signal Estimation Platform (EIGSEP)
abstract: The Electromagnetically Isolated Global Signal Estimation Platform (EIGSEP) is a new instrument designed to measure the global 21-cm signal from Cosmic Dawn and the Epoch of Reionization, redshifted to frequencies below 250 MHz. To reduce spectral structure in the antenna beam associated with ground scattering, EIGSEP uses a shaped bowtie antenna suspended in a canyon, designed to keep terrain and conducting structures about 100 m away. title: RESPONSE OF MUNG BEAN [Vigna radiata (L.) WILCZEK] VARIETIES TO BLENDED NPS FERTILIZER IN SOUTHERN ETHIOPIA
abstract: Mung bean is an important cash crop and source of protein rich food for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia. However, it is a relatively new crop in the southern part of the country. Hence, a field experiment was conducted in Borda sub-site of Areka Agricultural Research center during the 2019 main cropping season to identify the most adaptable variety (V) and determine the optimum and economically feasible rate of NPS fertilizer (F). A field experiment was conducted using three mung bean varieties (Rasa, NVL-1 and Shewa robit) and four rates of blended NPS fertilizer (0, 50, 100 and 150 kg ha-1)
journal: International Journal of Agricultural and Natural Sciences

title: Effect of topramezone herbicide on weed suppression, crop safety and productivity in chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.)
abstract: Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) productivity is often constrained by severe weed infestation, particularly during early growth stages, necessitating efficient and safe weed management strategies. The use of post-emergence herbicides is limited due to potential crop phytotoxicity, highlighting the need for alternative options. A field trial was undertaken at Sriniketan, West Bengal, during the rabi seasons of 2021–2022 and 2022–2023 to study the performance of topramezone at different application rates as a post-emergence herbicide in chickpea cultivation. title: Marco tecnológico para un repositorio de recursos digitales en la UNAM: arquitectura, clasificación y diseño de la interfaz gráfica
abstract: En los últimos años, la integración del material digital en el ámbito universitario ha fortalecido las habilidades tecnológicas de la comunidad; sin embargo, aún es necesario trabajar en la difusión de información sobre el funcionamiento, los alcances, las ventajas y las desventajas de estas herramientas. En este contexto, se desarrollan repositorios digitales con el objetivo de concentrar y divulgar recursos digitales generados por la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México acerca de temas orientados al procesamiento de lenguaje natural, la visión artificial, el análisis de información y la a

abstract: Anodic outer-sphere oxidation of olefins to cation radical intermediates that undergo spontaneous reactions has potential synthetic utility but is often limited by low selectivity in the absence of catalysts. In this computational work, we investigate the hypothesis that the competing kinetics of nucleophilic attack and deprotonation pathways of cation radical intermediates can be modulated by tuning water microenvironments, leading to higher reaction selectivity. title: Agronomic Evaluation of Alternate Furrow Irrigation Under Different Furrow Lengths and Inflow Discharges for Sunflower on Heavy Clay Soil
abstract: Improving irrigation water productivity is essential for sustainable crop production in water‐limited environments where surface irrigation remains widely used. This study evaluated alternate furrow irrigation (AFI) and continuous furrow irrigation (CFI) across different furrow lengths and inflow discharges under heavy clay soil conditions. A 2‐year field experiment was conducted during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 sunflower seasons in central India using a split‐split plot design with three replications. abstract: We present next-to-leading-order calculations of heavy-quark contributions to the deep-inelastic scattering structure functions $F_4$ and $F_5$ within the Aivazis-Collins-Olness-Tung scheme, implemented in the open-source library APFEL++ and evaluated using CT18NLO parton distribution functions. title: Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
abstract: Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. title: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
abstract: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition
abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling of linear systems, such as Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity, is described by the bosonic Hopfield model, and gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition (SRPT). Modulating the magnetic field alone has been predicted to enhance the cycle-averaged coupling and induce a Floquet SRPT. We develop an exact theory of periodically driven Landau polaritons. title: Ultrafast imprinting of fused ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic skyrmions
abstract: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are promising topologically protected entities for robust storage and THz transport of information. Their generation has so far relied on slow techniques or on specific magnetic structures, which limit their integration into spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate the imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions within a few picoseconds in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer with a thermal laser pulse. title: Evidence for MeV Radiation from a Large-Amplitude Crystalline Undulator
abstract: We report evidence for MeV radiation from a large-amplitude crystalline undulator in which 35 GeV/c positrons channel along periodically bent Si(110) planes. Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors produce ten periods with $λ_u = 334~μ$m and midplane amplitude $A_u \simeq 1.85$ nm (XRD-validated modeling). title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
abstract: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
abstract: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. title: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
abstract: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
abstract: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. title: SignAligner: Dual-Granularity Span Generation for Sign Language Alignment
abstract: Large sign-language corpora benefit from temporal labels at two scales: subtitle spans for subtitle alignment and word spans for sign spotting. Sign spottings already locate words in time at corpus scale, but training subtitle alignment jointly on subtitle and word spans remains underexplored. We present SignAligner, a prompt-conditioned visual-language span generator that maps a sign-language video and a subtitle-sentence or target-word query to a textual start/end frame interval. title: The Distributed Run Manager A C++ Library for Distributed Processing
abstract: The DistributedRunManager (DRM) is a C++ library for distributing a computing task among a number of computer systems for parallel processing on a network. The library was originally designed to accelerate synthetic image production for tomographic images, but is also a general solution for distributing a software task across diverse, multiple hardware platforms. The DRM self-configures using a novel C++ class, the ElectionManager. This class selects a server cooperatively at runtime and eliminates the need for a priori distribution configuration.
